Ambitious, visually impressive dishes are the German chef’s hallmark and his detailed creations show a memorable array of flavour and texture contrasts. Choose between the tasting menu or an upgraded ‘Premium’ experience with caviar, truffle and cheeses. Warm, engaging service helps to create a relaxed experience.

Name: 1887 by André
Address: Raffles Hotel, Lobby Level, 1 Beach Road, 189673, Singapore
Description: The ornate bubble chandelier and emerald-green Belle Époque punkah fans befit the centennial dining room dripping in heritage. In the kitchen, chef André Chiang leads a young team to reinterpret French classics with a unique Singapore spin. Diners can devise their own 4- or 5-course set menu or opt for the 7-course tasting menu. The chef’s papillote de bouillabaisse seduces with seafood umami and fragrant fennel and saffron.

Name: 7132 Silver
Description: Dutchman Marcel Koolen is at the helm of the kitchen at this stylishly urban restaurant (housed in 7132 Hotel, a heritage building that is a magnet for design and architecture fans). With the support of his international team and executive chef Matthias Schmidberger, he proposes highly creative cuisine that features pleasing contrasts and accentuates the natural flavours of the wonderful ingredients. Dishes are pared down to the essentials with stunning results. Take, for example, the hake, cooked on a binchotan charcoal grill and accompanied by the characteristic earthiness of a stuffed morel, a buttery morel cream and a drizzle of herb oil. The "Menu Surprise" also comes in a vegetarian version. Wine or house-made alcohol-free pairings are available. The excellent wine list is dominated by Swiss, Italian and French labels – the Bordeaux picks are a real highlight. The selection of perfectly aged vintages is certainly worth exploring. The front-of-house team is professional, charming and always on hand. The chefs, too, join in with serving, and talk you through their creations. A thoughtful touch: small cards on the table present each dish. An aperitif is served in the kitchen, allowing diners a fascinating peek behind the scenes.

Name: 8 ½ Otto e Mezzo Bombana
Address: 6-7F, Associate Mission Building, 169 Yuanmingyuan Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The third restaurant under the aegis of chef Umberto Bombana stars a glitzy cocktail bar and jaw-dropping balcony views, without forgetting an equally eye-catching glazed wine cellar with amazing selections, both by the glass and the bottle. Globally sourced ingredients and modern techniques result in elegant Italian flavours. The lunch set menus are great value, but for a full-on experience, go for the truffle feast or the 8-course tasting menu.

Name: A
Address: 4F, Building 2, Diamond Towers, Shin Kong Mitsukoshi, 282, Section 3, Zhongxiao East Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan Region
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Flower displays add splashes of colour to the pristine white interior in a gallery-like setting that provides the backdrop for chef Alain Huang’s contemporary French score. Underpinned by classic Gallic sauces and Asian accents, the tasting menus showcase an interplay of colour, flavour and texture. Top-notch ingredients are meticulously crafted and artfully plated. A specialty is the mushroom cappuccino and doughnut creation titled “Umami”. From amuse-bouches to petit fours, the meal impresses from start to finish.

Name: A. Wong
Address: 70 Wilton Road, Victoria, London, SW1V 1DE, United Kingdom
Description: Andrew Wong’s inspiration comes from across all of the Chinese provinces; join him for a three-hour culinary voyage around the country with the ‘Collections of China’ evening menu, where he presents his own unique interpretations of regional dishes, which demonstrate extraordinary sophistication, creativity and depth of flavour. Start with a drink downstairs in the Forbidden City, or come at lunch for outstanding dim sum – they even have a dim sum tasting menu. Clued-up service adds to the overall experience and dishes are explained with obvious pride.

Name: ACQUOLINA | Nuova Cucina Mediterranea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Just steps from Piazza del Popolo, the elegant First Roma welcomes guests with courteous, impeccable hospitality before leading them into a dining room of understated design, in keeping with contemporary taste, yet with tables still set with style and attentive service described as “dynamic” by its own team. At center stage is the cuisine of Daniele Lippi, who interprets the Mediterranean in its broadest sense, reaching well beyond national borders. Two tasting menus are offered: Periplo, dedicated to the aquatic world, and Anabasi Catabasi, which incorporates meat as well. Both conclude with a generous selection of desserts, the perfect finale to a gastronomic journey that is as intriguing as it is indulgent. Equally noteworthy is the wine offering, enhanced by an extensive list and the expertise of sommelier Francesco Aldieri.

Name: AIRA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This striking restaurant sits near the Royal Djurgården – a lush, historic island that was formerly a royal hunting ground and is now part of the City Park. The boathouse-inspired design employs Corten steel, wood and glass, and its light-filled interior is complemented by a lovely waterside terrace perfect for pre-dinner drinks. The generous cooking is precise and harmonious, offering the likes of scallops with white asparagus, crème crue and caviar or lamb with green asparagus, marjoram and mint. Opt for the wine pairing or the creative non-alcoholic option featuring ingredients from the garden.

Name: ASAHINA Gastronome
Description: Satoru Asahina pursues a gastronomy of ‘traditional heritage with modern innovation’. He delves into the history of French cuisine to reconstruct ancient recipes with his own interpretations. The prix fixe meal begins with a colourful amuse-bouche and proceeds to plates adorned with multi-layered culinary creations. Consommé pressed through a siphon with a flourish and desserts paraded on trolleys catch the eye. Classic cuisine tuned up to point to the future.

Name: ATAMA by Martin Stopp
Description: In a chic space, Martin Stopp, who made a name for himself at LOUIS in Saarlouis, presents two exceptionally interesting set menus: "Menü für die Seele" ("Menu for the Soul"), which is pared back and ingredient led, and the creative, somewhat more playful "Menü für die Sinne" ("Menu for the Senses"). The former, for example, impresses with a perfectly cooked saddle of fallow venison with an exquisite black pudding crust and fresh cranberries, finished with a wonderful dense and intensely flavoursome shiso Rouennaise sauce. The other boasts exciting combinations such as veal and unagi, pea ash, myoga and mint. Both set menus are available in five-, six- or seven-course formats. The exceedingly friendly and professional service aligns perfectly with the sophisticated setting – even the chef and his team serve up dishes. Alternatively, there is the "Bar Menu" comprising nine amuse-bouches. At lunchtime, you can opt for the three-course "Stammtisch-Menü" or a five-course version of the evening fine dining set menu.

Name: AUGUST
Description: A place that lives, sleeps and breathes art! Not only is there the special cachet of the listed Haag Villa (1877), there is also Christian Grünwald's cooking, the likes of which you would be hard pressed to find anywhere else. More than 35 years on, his creativity and distinct signature, delivered through a nature-inspired set menu featuring superlative ingredients, remain compelling. The names of his dishes mirror their inventive character – as seen in "Im Blätterwald" ("In the Leafy Forest"): venison loin sourced from the villa's own hunter in the Altmühltal, pan-fried in rosemary butter and briefly charcoal-grilled, is accompanied by a sour-cherry-infused jus, toasted beechnuts, intense beetroot, lightly glazed porcini slices and crisp, caramelised parsley root. Various amuse-bouches served beforehand are first class. Dinner is served on illuminated "display window" tables in exceptionally stylish rooms. The atmosphere is pleasingly relaxed, warm and personal – Christian Grünwald himself is also on hand to shed light on his creations. Practical for motorists: Parking spaces are available on the grounds.

Name: AURA by Alexander Herrmann & Tobias Bätz
Description: In their modern and elegant fine dining restaurant, well-attuned chef duo Alexander Herrmann and Tobias Bätz deliver regionally inspired cuisine with a distinctive signature. For their set menus (one of which is vegetarian), they use the finest ingredients Franconia has to offer to create imaginative, intensely flavoursome dishes, some of which are very intricate. A standout example is the fabulous wild eel, glazed with soy sauce, grilled over binchotan charcoal and served with braised leek and Tropea onions, radicchio and plum jam, and a green strawberry vinaigrette with eel oil and green pepper. The wine list is devoted to Franconian labels. Service of the set menu starts at 6pm sharp. Always on hand, the front-of-house team is exceedingly friendly and adept, and the chefs also frequently present their dishes in person. The small cards with information about the ingredients, prepared and preserved in Future Lab ANIMA, are a nice touch. For overnight stays, the Herrmann family's long-established Posthotel has genuinely lovely, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Aan de Poel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The view of De Poel lake is simply breathtaking – and the restaurant's large windows and chic designer interior allow you to fully appreciate the charm of the setting. Stefan van Sprang's creations are a perfect match for these beautiful surroundings. He likes to add the finishing touches to his dishes tableside and personally introduce the regularly changing lunch menu. There is also a choice between the signature menu featuring Aan de Poel classics and the more frequently changing "Chef's Menu". This skilled craftsman deftly combines diverse influences and uses his creativity to put his own spin on classic recipes. The herb garden behind the restaurant provides inspiration for the aromatic nuances he weaves into his cooking. His eye for top quality is evident, for example, in hand-cut steak tartare with briny caviar, a grilled langoustine cooked to perfect translucency and a delicate wasabi emulsion. The captivating interplay of familiar flavours and original accompaniments elevates the core ingredient and the food is a treat for both the palate and the eye. It is complemented by an exclusive wine list that the sommeliers are happy to help you explore. And when the friandises trolley arrives to round off your meal, it is yet another reminder that no detail is overlooked when it comes to spoiling guests.

Name: Acquerello
Address: 1722 Sacramento St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
Description: With its signature A-frame ceiling and luxuriously warm furnishings, this dining room has been Chef Suzette Gresham’s home since 1989. The cooking remains top rate, promising finesse and bold flavors in equal measure. Handmade pastas like their rabbit marubini in a prosciutto brodo are a particular highlight here, as are dishes like Spanish mackerel with asparagus. Sweets are a notable strength, down to the very last few bites when one of the best mignardises carts in town rolls up stacked with chocolates, pâtes de fruits, and caramels rolls. Speaking of bests, friendly sommeliers are essential guides for navigating one of the deepest Italian wine and Champagne cellars in the country.

Name: Agli Amici
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Agli Amici is one of the finest examples of contemporary Friulian cuisine, a restaurant that uses food to showcase the many facets of a border region, rich in cultural influences and extraordinary ingredients. The menu centres on two tasting menus, one of which is dedicated to plant-based dishes, complemented by a selection of ‘favourite dishes’ that trace the restaurant’s history through some of its most iconic creations, each accompanied by the year they were first created. It is, however, in the tasting menus that Emanuele Scarello’s gastronomic vision is most accomplished, based on constant research and a deep understanding of the local area. The pastures, vegetable gardens, woods and mountains of Friuli-Venezia Giulia serve as a source of inspiration for refined and distinctive dishes, often enhanced by ingredients from other regions in a harmonious blend of tradition and openness. Among the most memorable dishes are the variation of tender shoots and courgette flowers served with the rare centrolofo, presented both raw and cooked, and the elegant take on Kvarner scampi, enhanced by a delicate layer of rhubarb and lard on a raspberry cream base, rounded off with a delicious shellfish crème brûlée. In the dining room, Michela leads a close-knit team that stands out for its professionalism, warmth and genuine sense of hospitality, helping to ensure that the experience lives up to the restaurant’s name: making guests feel truly among friends.

Name: Agli Amici Rovinj
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant enjoys a splendid seafront position along the elegant promenade of the modern Marina. A charming setting, enhanced by a spacious terrace – where dinner opens with refined finger food – and a breathtaking view over the blue sea dotted with lush green islets. As evening falls, the illuminated silhouette of the Church of St. Euphemia adds further charm to the atmosphere. The kitchen is helmed by Simone De Lucca, under the supervision of Emanuele Scarello, chef of the renowned two-Michelin-starred Agli Amici in Udine. The menu offers two tasting menus, Rovinj and Istria, dedicated respectively to the sea and the land, alongside an à la carte selection. In every proposal, great attention to the quality of the raw material and a precise, considered approach to its preparation are evident: few ingredients, each with a well-defined role, often celebrated in their entirety so as to ennoble even the less conventional parts. Among the most memorable dishes for our Inspector: the mussel and saffron risotto, rich in aromas, creaminess and fragrance, and the amberjack, courgette and saffron, played out through elegant contrasts of texture and flavour. For the wine pairing, it is well worth placing oneself in the hands of the knowledgeable sommelier, who can guide you through a selection of Croatian and international labels or suggest specially created original cocktail pairings.

Name: Akasaka Kikunoi
Description: To spread the joy of Kyoto cuisine beyond the ancient capital, Kikunoi opened a Tokyo branch. Guests are warmly greeted with cheerful calls of ‘Oide-yasu!’, a traditional welcome in the Kyoto dialect. While located in central Tokyo, the mood, taste and feel of the restaurant are pure Kyoto. Yearly events are woven into the menu, and eye-catching dishes served on brilliantly decorated plates. Western ingredients are included too, expressing contemporary flavours. An attractive feature is the choice of tatami mat or counter seating, combining the charms of ryotei and kappo.

Name: Alain Ducasse at Morpheus
Address: 3F, Morpheus, City of Dreams, Estrada do Istmo, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Water, glass and mood lighting are combined dramatically to create a unique space that is both stylish and intimate, as befits its striking host hotel. The 6-course signature menu can be broken down with a minimum of 3 courses. Every dish is the quintessence of flavour, balance and high-flying gourmet technique. Those familiar with other restaurants headed by renowned French chef Alain Ducasse around the world will recognise his inimitable hallmark.

Name: Alchemist
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: There’s no restaurant in the world quite like Alchemist, so you’ll have to invest plenty of time securing a reservation months in advance. An immersive and perfectly choreographed six-hour-plus experience, eating here is a highly theatrical affair divided into ‘Acts’ and set across several locations, including a spectacular planetarium-like dome. Dishes are technically complex and highly creative with dramatic, provocative and sometimes even startling visuals. Every course is a social commentary from the chef: dip into a cod-eye jelly pupil modelled on the chef’s own eye to reveal a core of caviar, blue mussels and razor clams (surveillance) or break open a confectionery bar in the shape of a coffin (child labour).

Name: Aleia
Description: A dual experience that fuses haute cuisine and architecture? You'll find few more interesting options, as this restaurant is located on the first floor of the famous Casa Fuster (now Hotel Casa Fuster), a jewel of Catalan Modernisme designed in the early 20th century by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. In its luminous and elegant dining room, with large columns flanking the incredible window and an undulating ceiling that reminds us of the titanium plates of the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao, you can enjoy a unique tasting menu with a contemporary-creative style, with the option of food and wine pairings. Jerez-born chef Rafa de Bedoya, always under the guidance of the award-winning Paulo Airaudo (Amelia by Paulo Airaudo, in Donostia-San Sebastián), brings coherence and flavour based on local, seasonal products. Outstanding dishes? We loved the Garrucha red prawns with piriñaca and the spectacular scallop with cava and Figueres onion soubise. A truly excellent selection of wines, all served by the glass!

Name: Alevante by Ángel León
Address: Amílcar Barca, Chiclana de la Frontera, 11130, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The luxury Gran Meliá Sancti Petri hotel’s gourmet restaurant boasts a bright, elegant and minimalist design – the only thing adorning the walls of the dining room are the silhouettes of shoals of fish and curtains made from sailing rope. Given that this is the offshoot of the extraordinary Aponiente restaurant in El Puerto de Santa María, guests can savour (via the Gran Menú Alevante) many of the dishes that have led to acclaimed chef’s Ángel León’s reputation as “The Chef of the Sea”. The experience (overseen by chef Cristian Rodríguez) begins with enticing appetisers accompanied by wines from the Cádiz area in the bar at the entrance and continues in the dining room, where the best maritime fish and seafood (sea urchin, mackerel, tuna, dogfish etc) take centre stage. The menu, which includes extraordinary dishes such as shrimps cured in Manzanilla or "Sea Soy", comes with the “Alevante Crew” book, as the common thread here is a journey by boat to discover the ingredients used.

Name: Alex Dilling at Hotel Café Royal
Address: 68 Regent Street, Soho, London, W1B 4DY, United Kingdom
Description: In a discreet, intimate environment inside the grand Hotel Café Royal, the eponymous chef has the perfect canvas in which to showcase his impressive and accomplished cuisine. Dilling's dishes are exquisite in appearance and, like a seasoned orchestra, everything on the plate adds its own note of flavour to produce something harmonious and exhilarating. Whether Kaluga caviar, Scottish lobster or Peruvian chocolate, the kitchen knows how to bring the best out of its exquisite ingredients.

Name: Alinea
Address: 1723 N. Halsted St., Chicago, IL, 60614, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Not shying away from performance and theatrics, Chef Grant Achatz’s flagship restaurant continues to be one of the city’s most immersive experiences. Combining scented vapors, hidden ingredients and tableside service, dinner is a constant mix of whimsy and surprise. Signatures like the black truffle explosion or bourbon-maple cured Arctic char are woven in with a series of small, at times diminutive, courses that involve a number of unexpected ingredients and preparations. Dessert offers pure, childlike delight, starting with an edible helium balloon and ending with a nitro-fueled, Pollock-esque creation that’s sauced, splattered, cracked and glittered directly onto the table.

Name: Alliance
Description: Between the Left Bank and Boulevard St Germain, this dinky restaurant celebrates the alliance of Shawn and Toshi, respectively in charge of the dining room and the kitchen, and partners in this culinary adventure. Chef Toshitaka Omiya prefers authenticity to fancy frills. His cooking, which revolves around fine seasonal ingredients, hits the spot every time, regaling both the eye and the tastebuds, as he rolls out disarmingly, yet stunningly simple, subtle recipes. His surprise menus, which are practically made to measure for each of the establishment’s 8 tables, are a treasure trove of imagination as he enhances green asparagus from Erhardt, scallops from the Bay of St Michel or Racan pigeon. The pared-back interior dotted with discreet nods to Japan is cosily snug and affords a fascinating insight into the action in the kitchen. Shawn Joyeux’ stylish service and gracious welcome add the final touch to this portrait.

Name: Alois - Dallmayr Fine Dining
Description: Dallmayr is a name that has always been synonymous with good taste and excellent ingredients, and the same can be said for Alois. Head through the bar to a staircase that leads you up to the first floor of the iconic delicatessen. This is a chic and elegant setting in which to savour Rosina Ostler's cuisine, which skilfully blends classic French and Nordic styles with her Bavarian roots. This gives the array of 15 - 17 dishes on the menu a unique hallmark: cleverly devised, thoughtfully structured and at the same time delicate creations. Allow plenty of time in order to immerse yourself completely in this experience – dishes such as "lobster tail, dark beer, chanterelles" or "roe deer, wild fig, Swiss chard – malt brioche & port wine butter" don't disappoint! The quality of the produce is second to none. At Midday on Fridays and Saturdays, in addition to the full menu, there is an 8-course business lunch. Seek out Julien Morlat for judicious recommendations from a wine list that leaves nothing to be desired, especially when it comes to "Old World" wines. The charming waitstaff is supported by the chefs, who talk diners through their dishes, making for a refreshingly relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Amazing Chinese Cuisine (Changning)
Address: B5 Villa, 1665 Hongqiao Road, Changning, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A Chaoshan native, the chef sources items from his hometown, such as teal and sun-dried shrimps. Must-try classics include steamed fourfinger threadfin served chilled. Seasonal offerings embrace produce picked at the peak of its flavour. In summer, try the braised fish maw with chanterelles in a dried seafood broth, slow cooked for 5 hours and drizzled with balsamic vinegar. There are just five private rooms in this villa, so reservations are a must!

Name: Amelia by Paulo Airaudo
Address: República Argentina 4, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20004, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Argentine chef Paulo Airaudo’s flagship restaurant has set a new course following its move to the iconic Hotel Maria Cristina (one MICHELIN Key), which boasts over a century of history, elegance, and distinction. Here, at the mouth of the Urumea River and practically across from the Kursaal, the Amelia restaurant aims to continue growing through a contemporary-creative cuisine where flavour takes centre stage and, above all, leaves no one indifferent. The approach, rich in nuances, draws inspiration from the Cantabrian Sea, its primary source of inspiration, featuring an open kitchen and a special focus on the bar, as they advocate for a close connection between the chef and the diner. It also evolves into what the chef defines as an ‘Italian omakase’, where his transalpine roots find the perfect counterpoint when combined with Japanese flavours. The experience revolves around a single seasonal tasting menu, with a pairing option (the harmony can be alcohol-free).

Name: Ammolite - House of Light
Description: Part of Hotel Bell Rock, this beacon of gastronomy at Europa-Park is located in a lighthouse. The decor is refined and timelessly elegant – sheer organza curtains in shimmering gold and warm tones lend the circular room an intimate feel and a sense of calm. Seated in stylish armchairs at exquisitely set tables, diners enjoy attentive and adept service provided by a well-coordinated team. Chef Peter Hagen-Wiest presents two eight-course set menus: "Around the World" and the vegetarian "Green Forest". Both reflect his cosmopolitan outlook and, at the same time, his ties to the region. Dishes such as "Arctic char, barley, bacon" or "Breton red mullet, foie gras, lemon" reveal complex and beautifully balanced compositions unlike those encountered every day. The quality of the ingredients is beyond question. Well-curated wine selection and interesting pairings.

Name: Andrea Aprea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: On the top floor, reached by lift, of the Fondazione Luigi Rovati, within a magnificent historic building that also houses a highly refined art museum, chef Andrea Aprea is entirely at home: a space of great impact, entirely oriented towards the open kitchen, with the walls of the central dining room clad in bucchero (the characteristic black ceramic with which the Etruscans crafted their jars). The gastronomic offering centres on three tasting menus: Contemporaneità, the most concise, with four courses dedicated to Aprea’s latest inventions; Partenope, a six-course journey in which the Neapolitan chef (though now a long-adopted Milanese) revisits certain Campanian classics; and Signature, eight dishes that retrace some of Aprea’s defining creations. In the secret green courtyard of the palazzo at Corso Venezia 52, the Caffè Bistrot is also to be found, where from breakfast to dinner the classic flavours of Italy may be savoured.

Name: AnnaLena
Description: You won't find white tablecloths or a formal atmosphere at AnnaLena, but you will find one of Vancouver's most polished—and delicious—dining experiences. Effortless service, expertly prepared cocktails and astute wine pairings are all part of the magic, but of course it's the seasonally inspired tasting menu that really steals the show. This globally accented cuisine marries precise technique and top-flight ingredients. Peak-season Sungold tomatoes with house-made XO sauce and caramelized buttermilk infused with Thai green curry; and fresh pasta with charcoal-roasted asparagus and sauce vin blanc poured tableside are merely two examples of Chef Michael Robbins’ focused creations displaying exceptional clarity and depth of flavor.

Name: Anne de Bretagne
Address: Port de Gravette, 163 boulevard de la Tara, La Plaine-sur-Mer, 44770, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: On the south bank of the Loire estuary, this imposing contemporary building overlooks the small port of Gravette. Talented chef Mathieu Guibert, a local lad from the Retz region and a farmer’s son, has forged solid ties founded on respect with producers from the region who share his passion for the ingredient. It is no surprise that seafood plays a star role here. Depending on the catch of the day, you may sample locally caught red mullet marinated in basil and a slightly jellied fish soup; risotto of haddock with thickly sliced carpaccio of langoustine; lobster spiked with verbena and a shellfish and vin jaune bisque… Slick, cheerful service by Claire Bâcle. What’s not to like?

Name: Anne-Sophie Pic at Le Normandie
Address: 5F, Mandarin Oriental, Bangkok, 48 Soi Charoen Krung 40, Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A new chapter unfolds in Bangkok’s dining scene as Anne-Sophie Pic brings her celebrated French artistry to the city. Working alongside her trusted Japanese head chef, Tamaki Kobayashi, the menu highlights Pic’s signature creations, including her renowned lobster dish and the thoughtfully curated Voyage menu. Set in a beautifully renovated space overlooking the Chao Phraya River, it blends elegance with quiet refinement.

Name: Antica Corona Reale
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated between the Langhe and Monviso, this historic restaurant was founded in 1815. Run by the Vivalda family for five generations, it started out as a dairy farm before gaining a well-earned reputation for its cuisine. Owner-chef Gian Piero Vivalda creates top-quality menus featuring expertly prepared, colourful and aromatic dishes. Popular with food-lovers from Italy and abroad, Antica Corona Reale is also a point of reference for many local businesses who supply it with capon, guinea fowl, veal, Carmagnola peppers, porcini mushrooms and much more besides. The menu offers an array of enticing flavours, with modern dishes featuring alongside classic favourites, including a delicate raviolo of bagna càuda served with the restaurant’s legendary bouillabaisse, which has made a reappearance on the menu after guests’ insistent requests. In summer, dine alfresco in the shade of a beautiful pergola, while two small private rooms are available for intimate dinners, one of which is in the wine cellar surrounded by legendary bottles of wine. There’s also a charming garden with an English-style rose garden and other beautiful flowers, which are often used in the delicious desserts, as demonstrated by the superb rose tart.

Name: Antica Osteria Cera
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Regarded as one of the most popular destinations for seafood lovers, the restaurant offers an extensive menu that combines classic dishes with modern creations, fine-tuned season after season. The atmosphere here is elegant, modern and minimalist, purposely distanced from the idea of a traditional “osteria”, with a section called “Solo Verde” dedicated specifically to vegetarians.The kitchen focuses on raw seafood and charcoal-grilled dishes, the restaurant’s real strengths. The highlight among the starters is the cold spaghettino with essence of molluscs, along with references to Venetian tradition, such as “cicchetti crudi” (raw fish or meat appetisersi) and, in season, fried “moeche” (green crabs). For those who love shellfish, “la catalana” is a classic plateau not to be missed, while the “risotto della laguna” precisely interprets the taste and identity of the territory.

Name: Antiqvvm
Address: Rua de Entre Quintas 220, Porto, 4050-240, Portugal
Description: There are places in the world that, simply by their location, exert a particular pull. Such is the case of Antiqvvm, set in a singular building beside the Museu Romântico, and boasting a pleasant garden where you can enjoy a meal… with one of the most idyllic views over the Douro! In its elegant rooms, which combine classic and contemporary details with undeniable good taste, chef Vítor Matos champions creative cuisine with elegant dishes of “only apparent” simplicity that conceal an ode to the product (scarlet prawn, red mullet, caviar, wagyu, black truffle…). In his own words, the chef seeks to "promote the values of a natural, cultural, evolutionary, social and artistic cuisine” and proposes two tasting menus: Orgânico (vegetarian) and Ensaios Sensoriais (Sensory Rehearsals) with incredible dishes such as Violet Prawn & Moqueca and the Sea Bass & Curry. The experience also includes a showcooking station, where guests can observe the preparation of the snacks served at the beginning.

Name: Aquavit
Address: 65 E. 55th St., New York, NY, 10022, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Aquavit remains one of the city’s most polished expressions of contemporary Scandinavian cooking, set within a sleek dining room anchored by a striking open kitchen under Chef Emma Bengtsson. The tasting menus lean heavily into Nordic sensibilities, balancing pristine seafood, preserved elements, cultured dairy and bright seasonal produce with elegant restraint. Dishes may include beautifully cooked Norwegian langoustine with Meyer lemon sabayon and crisp shellfish tuile, or halibut paired with salt-baked celeriac and smoked whey beurre blanc. Desserts continue the restaurant’s refined style, weaving subtle herbal, citrus and licorice notes into compositions that feel thoughtful without becoming overly heavy.

Name: Aramburu
Address: Vicente López 1661, Buenos Aires, C1018ABA, Argentina
Description: Original snacks, maritime-inspired light bites teeming with flavour and delicacy, surprising dishes that establish a dialogue with seasonal produce, an egg with rainbow trout tartare that, in its shell, features a painting from the chef himself.... This is what the culinary experience at Aramburu is all about! Located in the heart of the Recoleta district, with access via the pleasant Pasaje del Correo. This is one of those places that everyone is talking about thanks to its high levels of cuisine. Here, chef Gonzalo Aramburu, who can often be seen from the dining room working the stoves alongside his team, focuses on a single surprise tasting menu that aims to combine innovation, technique and aesthetics through the use of the best Argentinian ingredients. For dessert, coffee and a post-dinner cocktail, guests need to head to the adjoining chillout room, a lounge/bar-type space filled with bottles and comfy chairs. Haute cuisine with an Argentinian soul!

Name: Arbane
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: After many years at Le Parc des Crayères, ‘Meilleur Ouvrier de France’ Philippe Mille has set up shop in this stylish abode dating back to 1874. In a contemporary interior done out in natural shades and strewn with references to the vineyards of Champagne, the chef from Sarthe finetunes a culinary vision that is rooted in the Champagne terroir. He cooks over vine branches and draws inspiration from the seven grape varieties (including Arbane), to which he adds first-class seafood ingredients (monkfish, turbot, lobster etc). He signs dishes of breathtaking precision demonstrating standout talent when it comes to pepper and exquisitely discreet hints of refreshing citrus fruit. The champagne list is naturally of interest, and the plush upstairs lounge sports a sculpture by a famous Reims-based master glassmaker.

Name: Arbor
Address: 25F, H Queen's, 80 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Japanese and Nordic cuisines enjoy a natural affinity as they both boast a subtractive form of cooking that focuses on subtle, natural flavours. Through precise execution and the insistence on using top quality ingredients, the two come together in the form of balanced and intriguing set menus at this understatedly stylish restaurant. The chef’s Finnish background is reflected in the lingonberries that accompany the pigeon and the horseradish that accentuates the scallop and peas.

Name: Arnolfo
Address: Viale della Rimembranza 24, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With sharp lines created by the use of iron and glass, this modern building is especially designed to allow guests to admire the views from wherever they’re sitting. To the rear of the dining room, the large open-view kitchen framed by a superb yellow Siena marble wall is home to chef Gaetano Trovato (Mentor Chef Award 2024) and his team. Although there are three tasting menus available, one of which is vegetarian, any of the courses can also be chosen à la carte style. We could say so much about Arnolfo’s cuisine, but we’ll limit ourselves to mentioning the bread (which has been central to this chef’s work from the very beginning), duck, Chianina beef, Valdarno chicken and the ice-cream which always features among the desserts. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the delightful amuse-bouche with which guests are welcomed, the caponata with Taggiasca olives and basil, and the mullet served with white asparagus, peas and mint. The wine list is impressive, both for its quality and for the extensive selection of wines not only from Italy and France but also from other countries around the world – 7,000 different labels in total.

Name: Aska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Aska remains one of New York’s most distinctive dining experiences. Hidden inside a dark, intimate space in South Williamsburg, Chef Fredrik Berselius draws on his Swedish heritage and the ingredients of the Northeastern United States to create a highly personal tasting menu. The room is centered around an open kitchen, where a small team prepares a procession of dishes rooted in preservation, foraging, smoke and seasonality. Shellfish, wild herbs, berries and carefully sourced seafood appear throughout the meal, reflecting a Nordic sensibility without feeling dogmatic. Highlights often include pristine langoustine, beautifully prepared fish and inventive desserts that balance dairy, flowers and fruit. Thoughtful service and a singular point of view continue to make Aska one of the city’s most compelling destinations.

Name: Atelier
Description: This remarkable restaurant in Hotel Bayerischer Hof is reminiscent of an artist's studio – chic grey dominates the colour scheme, and everything is tastefully done, down to the last detail. This understated luxury provides the backdrop, courtesy of Axel Vervoordt's interior design. The young, experienced waitstaff are exceptionally personable, attentive and eager to please. There has been a change in kitchen leadership, with Kevin Romes (known from Skin's – the restaurant, in Lenzburg) now at the helm. His dishes are based on outstanding ingredients and executed with remarkable precision, revealing his penchant for acidity and heat, both of which he incorporates with great skill. A six- or seven-course set menu is available, with the option of adding two standout dishes. The wine list comprises some 300 labels.

Name: Atera
Address: 77 Worth St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Atera offers one of the city’s more polished counter dining experiences, with a spacious U-shaped counter that allows guests to settle comfortably into the rhythm of the open kitchen. The room is dark and sleek, while an occasionally playful soundtrack keeps the atmosphere from becoming overly formal. The tasting menu moves fluidly through globally influenced compositions rooted in precision and balance. Dishes like Hokkaido scallop with pickled kiwi and lemon verbena, or halibut with peekytoe crab and brown butter champagne foam, showcase a style that is refined without excess, where luxury ingredients and technical detail remain carefully calibrated.

Name: Atomix
Address: 104 E. 30th St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Junghyun Park and his wife Ellia are global ambassadors for contemporary Korean cooking, but all roads lead back to their Murray Hill brownstone. Sporting dark finishes and soothing earth tones, the room unfolds into a chic bar and subterranean dining counter that is as warm and as inviting as the servers. This is one of the city’s most coveted reservations – and for good reason. Black banana is topped with monkfish liver, puffed buckwheat and perilla leaves, while langoustine from Norway is grilled, then set over truffle gel and honey nut squash foam. The menu is ever evolving, but the team's commitment to Korean traditions prepared with finesse and flair is steadfast.

Name: Auberge de l'Ill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The Auberge de l'Ill is much more than just a restaurant. It embodies the Alsatian inn in all its glory – an inviting and friendly place, untouched by the passage of time, where every customer is welcomed like a member of the family… It is an institution in the region, but also renowned throughout France and beyond! Since it was established in 1882 (between Sélestat and Riquewihr), the restaurant has made a name for itself thanks to its matelote with riesling and dishes based on local game. Marc Haeberlin, grandson of the founders, now serves the classical repertoire (foie gras terrine served by the spoonful, frog’s leg mousseline, salmon soufflé) alongside more modern creations. The legend lives on.

Name: Aubergine
Address: L'Auberge Carmel, Monte Verde at 7th Ave., Carmel-by-the-Sea, CA, 93921, USA
Description: Easygoing luxury and refinement strike a harmonious note within L’Auberge Carmel, where every element seems designed to delight. Chef Justin Cogley balances classic technique with a sleek, modern aesthetic, and his cooking captures a sense of place that feels wholly his own. Products of spectacular quality are prepared skillfully and painstakingly presented with an artistic eye, as in a surprising "cabbage" taco filled with shallot jam, Madeira-braised treviso, Kaluga queen caviar and cabbage chips. The hits keep coming, like the rice roulade with Dungeness crab finished in a white dashi and butter sauce or the triple-seared dry-aged ribeye brushed in wagyu XO. Fabulously accommodating sommeliers are ever present to help navigate a wine list of real distinction.

Name: Azurite
Description: When a passionate and experienced figure on the Dutch culinary scene such as Mario Ridder expresses himself so personally through his cooking, diners can expect something special. He welcomes you in the heart of Delft, where Azurite immerses diners in a tasteful blend of glass, concrete and wood. The atmosphere is robust and natural yet warm, with premium produce on display providing a striking focal point. During your meal, the chef takes you up to the wine loft, where he shares his enthusiasm for wine amid literally thousands of bottles. This is also where you'll find the vintage whisky and digestif bar. The service is elegant, understated yet attentive, and the sommelier provides excellent wine pairings. With the scene set, Ridder can showcase his expertise in classical cooking and his love of Dutch ingredients.His three set menus – vegetarian, signature and caviar – distil his wealth of experience with finesse. He needs no frills to get to the heart of each ingredient, often adding an invigorating touch of spice. For example, impeccably fresh kingfish, briny razor clams, herbs and a vibrant buttermilk sauce come together in a dish of remarkable depth. Mario Ridder reveals himself through his cooking, making for a genuinely emotional experience.

Name: Baan Tepa
Address: 561 Ramkhamhaeng Road, Hua Mak, Bang Kapi, Bangkok, 10240, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: At Baan Tepa, Chef Chudaree Debhakam elevates her farm-to-table ethos with a polished seven-course Thai tasting menu. The experience begins in the kitchen, immediately drawing guests into the restaurant’s thoughtful sense of place. For each course, the team presents trays of featured ingredients, from seasonal fruits to vegetables and herbs, offering a vivid glimpse into the produce that shapes the menu. Traditional curries, flavours and techniques are reimagined with deft precision, creativity and harmony throughout. She remains committed to mindful gastronomy, from thoughtful local sourcing to minimising kitchen waste.

Name: Bao Li Xuan
Address: 3F, Chamber of Commerce Shanghai, Lane 108, North Shanxi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestling in an adjacent century-old building and appointed with six private rooms inspired by Bvlgari jewellery, this restaurant of Bvlgari Hotel blends the elegance of historic Shanghai with modern twists. Under the stewardship of chef Fu, solid technique, spot-on precision and refinement mark Cantonese classics like roasted suckling pig that boasts bubbly, crispy, fat-free skin, served with eponymous lotus leaf buns.

Name: Bardal
Description: Some people call Ronda the “city of dreams”. But without drifting off into reverie, we are indeed talking about one of the most beautiful towns in Andalucia, where Bardal, not far from the impressive bridge over El Tajo de Ronda, is now a flagship of the local restaurant scene. Here, chef Benito Gómez, a Catalan by birth who has made the region his home, cooks up creative cuisine, steering clear of gimmickry and labels, while the recognisable flavours in his cooking have a connection to local tradition and are transformed into a subtle interplay of contrasts and textures. Diners are given a choice of two tasting menus with different numbers of courses (Bardal and Gran Menú Bardal). Both come with wine-pairing options and a trolley with a large selection of cheeses prior to dessert. One section of the menu we especially liked was the monkfish in Andalusian marinade, roasted and finished with a layer o "Lagrima del Maresme" peas.

Name: Bartholomeus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Bart Desmidt, his right-hand man Philip and gracious Sandra invite you to sample a banquet of flavour in Bartholomeus, a swanky restaurant with Japanese overtones. It is a treat to watch the cheerful chefs seamlessly and humorously working together in the open kitchen. The 18 seats around the counter are reserved for connoisseurs of high-flying cuisine. The single set menu rolls out several courses which reveal the chefs’ passion for fish and seafood, while Sandra can be relied upon for judicious wine-food pairings, drawn from a splendid cellar. The cast of exceptional ingredients stars the likes of turbot, truffle and Polders hare, all of which are crafted with consummate know-how. Creative, bang-on cooking designed to showcase the ingredient, courtesy of deceptively simple recipes. In an approach that errs towards minimalist, oysters, wagyu and lemon explode in a festival of flavour or bitter endive is paired with speculoos, mature Groendal cheese and a warm mandarin-laced vinaigrette. The chefs’ superlative technique and boundless creativity left us reeling – you won’t be disappointed by their carte blanche menu…

Name: Belcanto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Belcanto boasts a superb location in the Bairro Alto (Chiado) district popular with tourists, on a corner close to a former convent damaged by the large earthquake that devastated the city in 1755. In his culinary empire’s showcase gourmet restaurant, chef José Avillez offers a modern à la carte and a single tasting menu entitled Belcanto that takes guests on a journey of gastronomic discovery in a dining room divided into different spaces, alongside a chef’s table in the kitchen. Avillez explains that all his dishes are influenced by Lisbon’s different light, its maritime shoreline and its distinct districts: in the words of this celebrated chef, “cooking is our very own fado, and our own form of expression”. He recreates recipes that recall our childhood memories, such as the classic “sweet eggs and citrus” (doce de ovos e citrinos), which boasts a sublime delicacy and a truly special flavour. Interestingly, the napkin provided for dessert is in the shape of a sleeve, recalling the way the chef once wiped his mouth on his sleeve as a child!

Name: Birdsong
Address: 1085 Mission St., San Francisco, CA, 94103, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Live fire is of the essence at this high-ceilinged and elegantly appointed dining room. Chef Christopher Bleidorn's skill lies in his ability to combine the rugged appeal of flame-kissed meats with a delicate touch and palpable sense of whimsy. Look no further than the lacquered quail with grilled Parker House rolls and crunchy pickles to be assembled à la Peking duck. His team's impressive variety of techniques wring out every fleck of flavor from such pristine ingredients as creek trout, presented as roe with kelp kombucha sabayon; or "tail end" lox served on crispy skin.The playful and spontaneous spirit carries on until the end—with the possible arrival of tart blueberries and crème fraîche hidden beneath lemon mochi bites and a bee pollen-dusted tuile.

Name: Blackswan
Address: 1F, Luohong Art Museum, 89 Capital Airport Road, Shunyi, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: On a swan theme, feather motifs and graceful arabesques abound in the spotless white room of this restaurant, set in an idyllic spot overlooking a pond where swans and koi swim. As for the food, French chef Vianney Massot champions a unique take on traditional Gallic fare using seasonal ingredients. The slow-roasted, wild-caught turbot boasts firm, juicy meat with two sauces that complement its intense briny flavour.

Name: Blanc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: After making a name for himself at Passage 53, Shinichi Sato has settled here beneath a corolla vault of interwoven wooden slats in a plush yet minimalist circular dining room. The starting point is top-quality produce, which is enhanced by means of high-flying technical skill, an almost surgical attention to detail and zero compromise: caramelised Roscoff onions and restructured Bellota chorizo or Galician beef cooked over embers and paired with cecina… A Burgundy-centric wine list and an impressive lineup of whiskies, that can be sampled at the softly-lit, hushed bar, complete the picture.

Name: Blue Bay Marcel Ravin
Address: 40 avenue Princesse-Grace, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: After moving from Martinique to Monaco and from Alsace to Belgium, Marcel Ravin, who exhibits a distinct culinary personality, signs off on creative cuisine that transports us to the West Indies. With flawless technical prowess (superb sauces), he recounts his personal history, including his happy youth spent in Martinique. He references the dishes cooked by his grandmother (calalou, blaff, "next day's bread"), which he reinterprets with panache, incorporating the fine ingredients of these parts: poultry and veal from Piedmont, fish from the Mediterranean, vegetables and aromatic herbs from the kitchen garden. An appealing cuisine bursting with West Indian flavours, nicely rounded off by the fruity and spicy creations of pastry chef Floriane Grand. Sit back and enjoy this culinary experience in the lavish setting of the Monte Carlo Bay Hotel and Resort, on the edge of the Larvotto Peninsula, with a superb terrace opening out onto the sea.

Name: Blue Hill at Stone Barns
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The passion of Chef Dan Barber is at the core of everything here, where a meal is a true experience that uniquely knits together his vision of improving our foodways, the grit of utilizing the land to provide sustenance, and luxurious touches like crisped linens and fine crystal.A procession of dramatically presented, farm-fresh seasonal produce kicks off the meal and may include freshly plucked radishes with browned butter, Hakurei turnips dressed with poppy seeds, and morsels of dried honeypatch squash. While the focus is plant-based, heartier compositions may reveal roasted, retired dairy cow plated with root-to-leaf celeriac. The meal may end celebrating how this operation began; as a dairy, with a tower of milk crumbs, milk jam, panna cotta and ice cream to dress poached quince.

Name: Bo Innovation
Address: 1F, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: The spacious room pays tribute to Hong Kong’s vibrant and long-standing pop culture with wall designs inspired by the iconic red-white-blue nylon canvas bag. Similarly, the playful menu adds a new spin to the city’s nostalgic repertory courtesy of modern techniques. The single dinner tasting menu is full of surprises and regularly changing themes. Witty puns, bespoke serving vessels and theatrical presentation make for a fun-filled, immersive experience.

Name: Bo.TiC
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in a quite village in the Baix Empordà region, this restaurant is remarkable both in terms of its setting in an old carriage factory and its ongoing quest to delight guests. Behind the attractive garden are two minimalist-style dining rooms, one overlooking the kitchen (including a “chef’s table”) the other, which is cosier, laid out within the stone walls of what used to be the carpentry workshop. Here, chef Albert Sastregener offers two set menus (Degustación and Del Chef) plus a concise à la carte featuring dishes from the former. These abound with imaginative and technically sophisticated creations that are respectful of Catalan tradition without excluding international influences. As an example, one of his local “zero-miles” growers (Hidenori Futami) supplies him with vegetables and shoots native to Japan. We particularly enjoyed visiting the kitchen as well as savouring the snacks that feature on the menus here. The extensive wine list includes an impressive number of small producers and wines by the glass.

Name: BonAmb
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A unique restaurant, where each season finds inspiration in a different theme.Occupying a restored country house in beautifully landscaped surroundings, the setting is as appealing as the menu. The latter comes courtesy of Alberto Ferruz, who also runs Casa Pepa in Ondara. This is a chef who always turns to the Mediterranean and Alicante's Marina Alta for his magnificent fish and seafood, which take centre stage alongside produce from his bountiful vegetable gardens, and herbs from the Montgó mountains. The new proposal revolves around the Fragmentos (9 courses) and Caleidoscopio (12 courses) tasting menus, as the chef makes an ode to the constant transformation of ingredients, techniques and experiences, so that we can enjoy multiple perspectives. The chef himself comments: they would be those ‘fragments of the landscape of the Marina Alta, elements, ingredients and memories that, when you turn around, are transformed. Each dish is a different pattern: ancestral, familiar, but unexpected.’

Name: Bonheur by Matt Abé
Address: 43 Upper Brook Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 7QR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: It’s not easy taking over the site of a legendary restaurant – in this case, Le Gavroche – but Australian-born Matt Abé has already made this famous basement space his own. Colours and shapes inspired by the landscape of his home country have been used to lighten and brighten the room, while the service team are adept at putting all their guests at ease. But it’s Abé’s style of cooking, blending the classical with the contemporary, that makes dining here such a pleasure, exemplified by dishes like Herdwick hogget with courgettes and Cornish turbot with coastal herbs.

Name: Bottiglieria 1881
Description: Go for the ‘Full Experience’ set menu to really discover the range and depth of Chef Przemysław Klima’s intriguing and sophisticated cuisine. The terse menu descriptions give little indication of the creativity to follow, as he takes traditional Polish dishes and recipes and, through refinement and skilled technique, makes them his own. Highlights include pierogi with saffron, a sublime guinea fowl broth with calamari, and succulent loin of venison with aged veal. The room is smartly dressed and the service team are attentive and knowledgeable, although the atmosphere remains refreshingly relaxed.

Name: Bozar Restaurant
Description: Karen Torosyan is a genuine craftsman and an enthusiastic chef who, whilst respecting tradition, has developed his own culinary signature. In the company of his executive cheffe, Cassandre Ercolini, he raises ancestral culinary techniques to the rank of art. It is impossible not to be enthralled by his calm, high-precision gestures as he appropriates the mythical pâté en croûte and pithiviers recipe (by reservation only). This perfectionist seeks to communicate his emotions with each dish. His puff pastry creations are presented to the diner before going into the oven in this inclusive experience. Each bite is a moment of sheer bliss from the rich, crunchy pastry to the unctuous filling (for example, sweetbread, foie gras, Corrèze veal, cabbage and black trumpet mushrooms), further underscored by a harmonious jus. Searingly good food! Subtle interpretations that revive the classics of French and Belgian cuisine. Chef Torosyan aims for delicacy and reaches dizzying heights of intensity. Each dish is a masterpiece of artistry, with no detail left to chance, which is also the case of the interior. This magnificent restaurant is emblematic of Victor Horta’s Art nouveau architecture. Karen Torosyan has found his place at Bozar.

Name: Brooklands by Claude Bosi
Address: The Peninsula Hotel, 1 Grosvenor Place, Belgravia, London, SW1X 7HJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Peninsula’s rooftop restaurant is a celebration of the world of speed; it’s named after the famous Surrey racetrack and a scale model of Concorde hangs from its ceiling. When it comes to the kitchen, it’s clear there’s a high level of skill on board, as the team is run by the experienced Claude Bosi. Expect finely detailed, exquisite cooking that showcases the best British ingredients, like Lake District lamb and Cornish squid, in delicate yet rewarding dishes. The floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto a fantastic terrace.

Name: Brut172
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: Hans van Wolde has set up shop in the heart of the quiet Limburg countryside, having transformed a farmstead into an architectural gem. Diners are led through the different spaces, from the aperitif lounge to the cosy salon to the kitchen itself. The place has the feel of a luxurious chalet; the upscale modern design is extraordinary. This is art rather than architecture! Hans van Wolde takes you into his world, where you momentarily lose track of time. It is certainly worth considering the wonderful accommodation options in the lodges and mansion. But back to the food, which is made with top-quality ingredients and features deep, complex sauces. Hans van Wolde's culinary creations are playful and expressive, just like his character. For example, he presents perfectly seared langoustine on top of a roasted onion tarte Tatin alongside a delicate sweet-and-spicy som tam salad, as well as a savoury tom yum sauce that adds layered depth of flavour. Terroir and craftsmanship come together, resulting in cuisine that creates diverse impressions, ranging from the adventurous to the familiar. Then there is the obliging front-of-house team and a selection of wines from around the globe, as well as a range of delicious juices for alcohol-free pairing… Brut172 promises a captivating dining experience!

Name: Bulle d'Osier
Address: Clos Vauban, 1 place du Colonel-de-Grouchy, Langres, 52200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A former officers' mess, this mansion standing proud next to the Porte des Moulins is now a charming restaurant, designed and set up by chef Laurent Petit. Both the name and decor of this elegant property surrounded by a large vegetable garden pay homage to the tradition of basket-making in Fayl-Billot – the birthplace of this champion of ingredients from Lake Annecy. The carte blanche menu devised by Valentin Loison (the chef from the Jura previously worked at Le Clos des Sens and Mirazur) is creative and on point, drawing inspiration from foraging (polypody), garden vegetables, local livestock (matured Black Angus beef), Saône fishing (carp ventrèche, matured pike-perch, catfish) and hunting (roe deer). These fine, well-balanced dishes are enhanced by sommelier Anaïs (partner of the chef), who oversees things front of house with professionalism and warmth, dispensing judicious wine recommendations.

Name: CODA
Description: Don't be fooled by the unassuming-looking exterior of this Neukölln eatery – a very special take on fine dining awaits you inside. The atmosphere in the dimly lit interior is lively and laid-back. Dine either at the counter, with a view into the kitchen, or at one of the surrounding tables. If you're lucky, you'll be given a sneak peek into how one ingredient or another is prepared in the kitchen. The cooking style is quite unique: René Frank and his team apply patisserie techniques. Particularly refined examples include "buttercream with plum, walnut, and dulse" and "grilled peach with pointed pepper and coriander". Desserts are by no means the only focus, and refined sugar is completely avoided. The set menu comprises 13 to 15 small and larger dishes – these are always paired with a drink that is tailored to the flavours. In addition to the pairing drinks that accompany the tasting menu, there is also an optional wine flight or an alcohol-free zero flight. The wine list showcases a well-curated selection of German Rieslings, as well as an appealing range of sparkling wines and choice of sake. The service is relaxed and very cordial.

Name: Cabaña Buenavista
Address: Buenavista s/n - Urbanización Buenavista, El Palmar, 30120, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A culinary experience in every sense! From the moment you enter you are guided through a surprising sequence of flavours and sensations that include stunning appetisers in the garden and the Living Lab, a collaborative space in which the restaurant grows and revives native species that are almost extinct (’Ciezana’ aubergine, ‘Flor de Baladre’ tomato, cowpea, etc.). You then continue to the spectacular modern dining room with its surprising setting in a huge thatched hut. Here, you savour main dishes, with fantastic dishes such as Panaché of vegetables and langoustines (a wonderful tribute to the garden, with up to 18 types of vegetables cooked independently) or their powerful Red mullet with garlic and seafood.Chef Pablo González’s creative cuisine is showcased on two tasting menus (Olivo and Experience) that constantly reference regional recipes and stand out for their presentation. Dessert and coffee can be enjoyed on the terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Caino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The cuisine of Valeria Piccini is a declaration of love for the Maremma and for Tuscany; here everything speaks of territory and family, of warmth and memory. It is a vision of cooking that steers clear of artifice and strange pairings: one comes here to eat, and to eat very well, not to be astonished. Such is the case with the bread filled with extraordinary ricotta, the family’s own-produced oil, and, naturally, the dishes themselves. To name but a few: Angela’s tripe and the lampredotto sandwich (an extraordinary duo of starters), the ricotta gnudi with peas and Orbetello bottarga, the caciucco and the charcoal-grilled lamb. An astonishing cellar, with around 2,500 labels. And, staying on the theme of the local area, after dinner do not fail to visit the nearby castle square: romantic and picturesque, it is the heart of this small stone village.

Name: Campo del Drago
Address: Località Castiglion del Bosco, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Allow yourself to be guided along the evocative Tuscan white roads, immersed in lush vegetation and between orderly rows of vines that compose the landscape with an almost painterly harmony: the journey itself becomes an integral part of the experience. On arrival, guests are welcomed into a fascinating medieval hamlet, complete with tower and frescoed chapel, which is home to Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco – awarded Three Michelin Keys – and to one of the most interesting restaurants in the area. It is here that chef Matteo Temperini offers a personal and creative reading of regional cuisine, celebrating also the produce of the property’s kitchen garden. The offering extends across three tasting menus, with the option of choosing à la carte as well (minimum three courses). The dishes are served in a contemporary and elegant dining room, enhanced by a panoramic terrace. The wine list, with over 700 labels, favours the local area while opening up to the rest of Italy and some international selections. The by-the-glass offering is of interest, with a notable Montevertine 2020 deserving particular mention.

Name: Canton 8 (Huangpu)
Address: 63 Runan Street, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is the place to go for handmade dim sum and affordable classic Cantonese fare. With over 40 years of experience, Chef Mak from Hong Kong cooks up all-time favourites as well as painstaking recipes that you don't come by every day. Old-fashioned shrimp toast is coated in whisked egg and deep-fried until crispy. Deeply flavourful slow-boiled soups are made with top-notch ingredients. Ask servers about the varieties available that day.

Name: Casa de Chá da Boa Nova
Address: Avenida da Liberdade, 1681, Leça da Palmeira, 4450-718, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Rarely has the idea of "bringing the sea to the table" been so literal, so authentic, so wild… to the point where you can feel the waves crashing in the dining room. It is no coincidence that this unique building, declared a National Monument, rises from the rocks of Boa Nova Beach. Chef Rui Paula, with Executive Chef Catarina Correia at his side, based his offering on a verse ("Through seas never before sailed") by the illustrious poet Luís Vaz de Camões in his famous epic The Lusiads. The offer, presented on a concise menu and an excellent tasting menu entitled Cantos, allows you to choose six, twelve or twenty-one dishes. Focused on the marine world and marked by exceptional ingredients, the kitchen stands out with dishes such as Red Prawn/Broccoli/Kaffir Lime, "Chanel" Squid and John Dory/Endive, placing great emphasis on presentation, textures and flavours, as well as modern techniques that make the most of the extraordinary fish and seafood of the Atlantic.

Name: Casadelmar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Here in Porto Vecchio, everything revolves around the sea. The ancient Genoese city fought off the onslaught of barbarian invasions and is a symbol of pride for Corsicans. Another source of pride is this restaurant: a mecca for lovers of seafood. Don't be distracted by the enchanting view of the bay, nor by the location of this superb hotel – it is on the plate that the most remarkable things happen! Chef Fabio Bragagnolo's cooking is inspired by both Corsica and Italy, as can be seen in his John Dory confit in olive oil with red lentils, burrata and tomato water emulsion. Masterful from start to finish, the meal culminates in delicate low-sugar desserts, such as his composition with raspberries and Corsican pomelo, juniper ganache and rose-scented geranium.

Name: Castel fine dining
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in an independent wing of the hotel and with its own private entrance, the restaurant welcomes guests on the first floor with a dramatic open kitchen that immediately sets the tone for the gastronomic experience to follow. Beyond an elegant entrance salon, the dining room unfolds around just five tables looking onto broad panoramic windows, through which the gaze sweeps across the Val Venosta in a captivating 180-degree panorama. Chef Wiesner's proposal takes shape through a single tasting menu that selects high-quality ingredients without limiting itself to the regional confines. The cuisine is distinguished by a contemporary style, precise in its execution and consistently attentive to the balance of flavours. Among the dishes that best express his philosophy, the grilled wagyu fillet with peppers and potatoes stands out: a preparation that is only apparently simple, elevating an exceptional raw material through impeccable technique and a flavour that is full and deeply satisfying.

Name: Castor
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Purity is the name of the game at Castor. The elegant yet brutalist-looking cube on Kortrijkseweg is home to a modern interior of wood, glass and concrete. Stefanie sets the tone of the restaurant’s classy front-of-house style, while Maarten Bouckaert surprises the diner right from the appetisers. From the ingredients and the sauces to the savvy blend of exotic flavours, the chef unveils his talent at every step. Stints with culinary virtuosos of the likes of Peter Goossens enabled him to hone his skills, which he now deploys with tact and sensitivity. Examples: pork cheeks braised in Rodenbach beer and paired with tagliatelle of cuttlefish, cockles and mussels, together with a knockout gravy of briny cuttlefish, a reduction of beer and crispy tempura tentacles. A feast of culinary delicacies! Rather than fussy, gimmicky showmanship, Bouckaert’s characteristic hallmark remains distinctive and legible, particularly in the sauces. Save room for the lineup of desserts that are (almost) too exquisite to eat – the Bordeaux cannelé is downright addictive!

Name: Chapter One by Mickael Viljanen
Address: 18-19 Parnell Square North, Rotunda, Dublin City, D01 T3V8, Ireland
Description: Mickael Viljanen’s restaurant is a stylish, elegant spot decorated with eye-catching art, where superb service complements truly top-drawer cooking. Prime luxury ingredients – like Donegal lobster or Limousin sweetbreads – are the bedrock of the menu, prepared using classic French techniques combined with subtle modern touches. The chef’s creativity and personality shine through in perfectly balanced, immaculately executed dishes with sublime natural flavours and beautiful presentation. The 'Irish Coffee' is made in the dining room and is, like everything else, an experience to remember.

Name: Chef Tam's Seasons
Address: GF, North Esplanade, Wynn Palace, Avenida da Nave Desportiva, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
Description: As well as the main menu, the dining concept by chef Tam Kwok-Fung features two sets – one classic, one seasonal. New à la carte items pop up every month to showcase seasonal ingredients. The traditional appetiser ge zha, or deep-fried egg custard, comes in a hairy crab version in autumn - the velvety custard bursting with crabmeat flavour is enrobed in a crispy crust. Barbecued pork belly glazed with honey is smoky and aromatic.

Name: Chef's Table
Address: 61F, Tower Club at Lebua, 1055 Silom Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: At this sky-high restaurant on the 61st floor of Lebua, panoramic views form the backdrop to the elegantly designed space. The mood is calm and sophisticated, with tables angled to the skyline. An open kitchen takes centre stage, as chefs skilfully craft a sequence of hot and cold dishes. An expert sommelier curates pairings to enhance each bite; featuring both fine imports and artisan produce from a local farm, an impressive cheese trolley rounds off the meal.

Name: Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare
Address: 431 W. 37th St., New York, NY, 10018, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This famed address hidden in the back corner of a Hell’s Kitchen grocery store has entered a new era under Chefs Max Natmessnig and Marco Prins. The room is a box of luxury and sparkles as bright as ever under the spotlights, with most guests seated at a glossy walnut counter that wraps around a brigade of cooks who have nowhere to hide. The team works quickly, sending out a volley of delicate tarts and bites that showcase skill and refinement. Highlights have included a nicely crisped duck breast with foie gras and desserts like Fujisan bread accompanied by coconut sorbet. All the while, an excellent service team keeps close watch from all corners of the room.

Name: Christophe Hay - Fleur de Loire
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Christophe Hay's restaurant is housed in a 17C stone-built hospice on the banks of the Loire, overlooking the river that is his primary inspiration. Giving onto the kitchens, the elegant dining room is adorned with decor that evokes the chef's culinary world. He rolls out his repertoire, from signature dishes to original creations, which are notable for their lightness and flavour, but also their textures. Every plate is an ode to the Loire Valley, drawing on its Ossietra caviar from Sologne, wild-caught Loire perch, vegetables from the kitchen garden, Touraine guinea fowl, Chambord venison, Wagyu beef from the restaurant's own farm… A true ambassador for the region!

Name: Ciel Bleu
Description: Ciel Bleu lives up to its name. Here, you dine on the top floor of the luxurious Okura Hotel with a spectacular view of the blue sky and the Amsterdam skyline as a backdrop. The modern elegance of the restaurant and the superlative presentation of the dishes are equally pleasing to the eye. Arjan Speelman's cuisine is technically accomplished and creative. The seasoned chef deftly plays with French cooking techniques, Asian seasonings and spices. By focusing on the depth of his sauces, he ensures that each dish packs a punch. His marinated bluefin tuna tartare with yuzu, paired with a horseradish cream, egg yolk and briny caviar has duly earned its place as a signature dish. Every detail is precise, every bite a surprise. Dining at Ciel Bleu is intriguing. You will be served by one of the best front-of-house teams in the country, starring maître d' Francesco Simonelli. The extensive wine list and the alcohol-free options are another highlight. The sky really is the limit here!

Name: Cinc Sentits
Description: This enchanting restaurant has been designed to enhance the dining experience through different spaces that reflect the family roots and the culinary influences of chef Jordi Artal: the home-made vermouth and appetisers that welcome guests to the Faifó; the move from La Torre de l'Espanyol (Tarragona) to cosmopolitan Barcelona that is explained in the dining room; the Biblioteca Viva (Living Library) where they display jars of fermented products, garums, kombuchas... and, of course, the exclusive space set aside for the “chef's table” overlooking the kitchen. The cuisine here is this self-taught chef’s personal take on modern Catalan cuisine, which he bases around working with trusted small-scale producers and showcases ingredients with a strong Catalan DNA. Everything revolves around two delicate tasting menus: Light and Tasting (the comprehensive selection of wines and food pairings is complemented by a range of non-alcoholic pairing options).

Name: Cloudstreet
Description: In addition to naming his venture after the Tim Winton book, Sri Lankan chef Rishi Naleendra pays homage to Australia where he honed his skills. His food embodies balance and harmony, making the best use of top-quality ingredients and well thought-out flavours. Highlights include Sri Lankan curry with blue marron and coconut broth, and Murray cod with fermented bell pepper and almonds. The savvy front-of-house team delivers slick service and the perfect vibe.

Name: Coeur D'Artichaut
Description: This appealing "casual fine dining" restaurant is tucked away in a courtyard (with a fabulous terrace in summer), just a stone’s throw from the cathedral. Featuring a striking ceiling with densely packed pendant lights and an eye-catching open kitchen, the stylish dining area is almost reminiscent of a stage in a theatre – complete with a front-row view of the pastry section and "Chef's Table" seating. With consummate skill, French-born Frédéric Morel draws on his Breton roots and incorporates influences from his adopted home in Northern Germany, adding a touch of modern creativity in the process – his sauces and stocks are outstanding! When selecting his high-quality ingredients, he is mindful of the seasons and regional provenance. The "Morel's Tasting" set menu, which changes every month, is composed of six or eight courses.
