It is here that the Capri Palace, among the island’s most exclusive hotels, provides the introduction to its two-Michelin-starred restaurant, set within a spacious and elegant room that recalls a contemporary salon. In the kitchen, Andrea Migliaccio delivers a proposal that celebrates the Italian, and above all Campanian, tradition with great vitality, reinterpreted with a modern sensitivity yet always faithful to the generosity of its flavours and its vivid character. The dishes impress with intensity and precision, the first courses in particular, the true protagonists of the journey: from the pasta with reef fish to the richly constructed risotto al ragù napoletano. A deeply satisfying and joyful experience, which finds its natural complement in a stroll through the lanes of Anacapri or along the mule track leading to Villa Axel Munthe, perfect for immersing oneself in the island’s most authentic atmosphere.

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: Four Seasons George V, 31 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is established in this glazed extension in the courtyard of the George V hotel, graced by an amazing hanging porcelain sculpture of thousands of bougainvillea petals. The ingredients are superb, the cooking is surgically precise, as is the balance struck between the flavours. As for the remarkably light sauces, they subtly combine maritime or vegetable notes and manage to bring an element of surprise to each dish, while maintaining a leitmotif that creates structure. There's never a dull moment, backed up by elegant, discreet service.

Name: L'air du temps
Address: rue de la Croix Monet 2, Liernu, 5310, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: L'Air du Temps is in a world of all of its own and the square farmstead tucked away in the Namur countryside is a picture of present-day elegance. The stripped-back edifice blends in perfectly with the surrounding landscape and San Degeimbre’s immense cottage garden, where he finds much of his inspiration. A champion of the natural world, Degeimbre’s culinary repertory is coloured by his Korean roots. Fermentation and acidity are a common theme of his intricate recipes, as is his habit of serving each course in several small plates. For example, he may underscore Dieppe scallops with an intense roe sauce enhanced by citrus fruit notes. Another example is a large corn noodle rolled in green veggie sauce and a punchy creamy emulsion of roe on a bed of house XO loaded in umami flavours. Each mouthful and each detail reveal the chef’s philosophy and desire to create a global experience. The water menu, for example, and the wine-food and non-alcoholic beverage pairings, are emblematic of this approach. L’Air du Temps is the purest expression of the zeitgeist. Treat yourself to a night in one of the tastefully appointed elegant guestrooms to finish this amazing experience in style.

Name: LOUIS restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the restaurant of the tasteful boutique hotel LA MAISON, chef Sebastian Sandor and his team have forged a distinctive identity rooted in modern French cuisine infused with pronounced Japanese influences. Their seven-course menu, complemented by a succession of amuse-bouches, reflects meticulous craftsmanship through its interplay of numerous components, aromas and contrasts. One standout dish is the lightly smoked ikejime salmon trout, which is of exceptional quality, accompanied by swede prepared three ways – pickled, lacto-fermented, and grilled – and a superb beeswax and vanilla beurre blanc with a finely calibrated hint of kumquat. The service is professional and attentive yet pleasingly unobtrusive – wine recommendations come courtesy of sommelier Robert Jankowski. The chef also makes occasional appearances at the table to introduce a dish. The interior sees a stylish marriage of chic design features and a historical backdrop – the high-ceilinged room in the beautiful villa was once a courtroom. Interesting detail: On the way to your table, you glimpse the open kitchen encased in a yellow glass cube.

Name: La Boscana
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re looking for a special restaurant, La Boscana offers a culinary experience enhanced by its natural setting, with glass-fronted buildings overlooking pretty gardens, leafy groves and an idyllic lake, making this one of the most romantic places to eat in Spain! In its elegant dining room, bathed in natural light and embellished with designer details, enjoy innovative cuisine from Joel Castañé that has a strong emphasis on detail, both in terms of technique and presentation. Through his menus (usually one concise menu and a second, more extensive, seasonal option), the chef skilfully reworks the flavours of Lérida as he searches for the perfect symbiosis between his savoury dishes and the fruits that enhance them, the latter sourced from various fruit farms in the local area as well as from his own garden. His delicious pork and apple tartlet pays homage to two of Lérida’s most iconic ingredients.

Name: La Brezza
Description: This elegant place dedicated to modern cuisine is part of the impressive Tschuggen Grand Hotel, which is perched 1 800m above sea level. Young chef Marco Campanella and his team astound diners with aromatic dishes that frequently present as elaborate and playful, yet maintain depth of flavour and technical precision, striking a perfect balance between robustness and sophistication. The exquisite sauces demonstrate true artistry – take, for example, the wonderfully full-bodied and velvety bisque with delightful roasted notes, which elevates beautifully firm langoustine tail. Of the two set menus, "Inspiration" and "Moving Mountains", the latter is vegan and reflects the latest research in the field of nutrition. The service is always friendly and professional, and the wine list is excellent. During the summer season, Marco Campanella cooks at the restaurant of the same name in Ascona.

Name: La Chèvre d'Or
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Château de la Chèvre d'Or boasts an exceptional location: Perched high up on the flank of a rocky hillside in a medieval village, it commands jaw-dropping views of the Riviera hinterland to the rear and of the sparkling Mediterranean Sea to the fore. After feasting your eyes on your surroundings, it's time to sit down to dinner, courtesy of the chef and his brigade, which includes talented pastry chef Florent Margaillan. Previously chef of Granite, Tom Meyer, also a Meilleur Ouvrier de France, has replaced Arnaud Faye here. He demonstrates the solid qualities for which he is already renowned: masterful technique, beautifully intense jus and sauces, stylised plating. This dynamic cuisine keeps things interesting by alternating between notes of vegetables, herbs and seafood: Mediterranean mullet, grilled prawns and basil; cherry tomato, green melon, myrtle and summer purslane water; sardine, sea fennel, shades of green.

Name: La Cime
Description: Yusuke Takada unravels the mysteries of the classics while pursuing the modern. Takada is the author of a new French cuisine, one imbued with the essence of Japan. Takada’s aim in using traditional ingredients such as kudzu vine, tofu skin, miso and wasabi is to proclaim the goodness of foodstuffs grown and raised in Japan. Cultural elements from Osaka and his native Amami Ōshima weave together into a story that is unique and fascinating.

Name: La Côte Saint-Jacques
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This edifice on the banks of the Yonne is truly superlative! Founded by Marie Lorain in 1945, the establishment rose to fame in the hands of her son, Michel, and then later, when her modest, conscientious grandson, Jean-Michel, took over. The latter has entrusted his nephew, Alexandre Bondoux, with the task of composing the menu. Regulars can rest assured that the original, iconic dishes remain (lobster blanquette; calf sweetbread with ginger), now flanked by flashes of inspiration (cuttlefish tagliatelle with konjac in smoked-milk carbonara style; Wagyu beef grilled on the barbecue, Savora mustard condiment and pastrami jus). A symphony of flavours, high-flying craftsmanship and an exquisite repertory, underscored by slick attentive service.

Name: La Côte d'Or
Address: Le Relais Bernard Loiseau, 2 avenue Bernard-Loiseau, Saulieu, 21210, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This iconic institution of the Morvan region, which has seen so many generations of chefs and fine food lovers pass through its doors, has embarked on a new chapter. In the wake of its auspicious débuts with Alexandre Dumaine and Bernard Loiseau, chef Louis-Philippe Vigilant now rolls out up-to-the-minute cuisine founded on solid classical bases. He has added his hallmark to more personal recipes that star first-class ingredients. Nostalgic guests can travel back in time and sample some of Bernard Loiseau’s iconic classics, such as frog's legs with garlic purée and parsley juice. The lineup of desserts, which are the work of Lucie Vigilant, the chef’s wife, continues to star the emblematic orange-flavoured ‘roses des sables’ with pure chocolate ice cream together with a last-minute Saint Honoré made with chiboust cream (pastry cream lightened with meringue).

Name: La Fourchette des Ducs
Address: 6 rue de la Gare, Obernai, 67210, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Nicolas Stamm-Corby strikes the perfect balance between celebrating the classics and adding an inventive touch that hits the mark. Throughout the seasons, he treats diners to high-calibre dishes that spotlight top-drawer ingredients. In winter, for example, the Alsace venison served two ways with grand veneur sauce is a homage to the terroir. The same ambition is palpable when it comes to the desserts – the selection of petits fours (fruit tarts, kugelhupf, cherry financiers, lavender honey madeleines etc) is particularly memorable. Finally, the warm welcome provided by maître d' Serge Schaal deserves a special mention.

Name: La Grand'Vigne - Les Sources de Caudalie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from Bordeaux, this blissful property nestles in the vineyards of Château Smith Haut Lafitte, a Graves grand cru classé winery, whose iconic tower serves as a beacon to gourmets in search of excellence. Nicolas Masse is the chef of La Grand'Vigne, the hotel's fine dining restaurant. Masse strives tirelessly towards a single goal, which is to showcase the bountiful produce of Aquitaine, particularly its cornucopia of veg and wines from Pessac Léognan. As legible as it is pure, his refined cuisine aims to reveal the distinctive flavours of cherry-picked produce from southwest France. Nothing is too good, whether it be the front-of-house service or the wine tips. A truly mind-blowing experience!

Name: La Grenouillère
Address: 19 rue de la Grenouillère, La Madelaine-sous-Montreuil, 62170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Few chefs show such a strong culinary personality as Alexandre Gauthier in La Madelaine-sous-Montreuil. The story unfolds in a space with two tiered metal rooftops (designed by architect Patrick Bouchain) and views onto the verdant surroundings and the kitchens. This is the laboratory in which the chef cooks up "contemporary cuisine with French roots, liberated from its certainties and preconceptions". Like an alchemist, he teases out flavours in on-point dishes, each a vignette of creativity in which the ingredients sing the praises of the seasons. Artistic and experimental cuisine, to be savoured in this old farmhouse imbued with a luxury that remains close to nature.

Name: La Madia
Address: Corso Filippo Re Capriata 22, Licata, 92027, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Park in the surrounding streets and get ready for a culinary journey into the very heart of Sicily; thanks to Pino Cuttaia’s vision, Licata has, over the years, become a must-visit destination for food lovers from all over Italy and abroad. His cuisine, deeply rooted in the island, eschews any stylistic flourishes for their own sake, focusing instead on the essence of the ingredients and the memory of flavours, reinterpreted with extraordinary contemporary sensitivity. Examples include dishes such as pasta with a shellfish broth or Nebrodi black suckling pig with Sunday sauce. The two dining rooms, modern and minimalist, create an elegant and relaxed atmosphere, while the service, led by Vincenzo and his close-knit team, stands out for its professionalism, experience and genuine hospitality. The wine list is also of particular interest, featuring a carefully curated selection of wines and numerous large-format bottles, among which many outstanding Sicilian wines stand out – wines that, in the glass, reflect the very same regional identity that inspires the cuisine.

Name: La Merise
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This handsome Alsace establishment near Haguenau is a remarkable modern construction built out of old materials so as to seamlessly blend in with its rural setting overlooking the hills and orchards. It is the haunt of Christelle and Cédric Decker, who have patiently developed their property (adding a kitchen garden, orchard, chicken coop, etc.). Using premium ingredients from Alsace and elsewhere, the chef concocts his own intriguing take on classical, yet never boring recipes, enhanced by subtle and skilfully crafted house-made jus and sauces. Seamless, on-the-ball service.

Name: La Peca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: 2027 will mark forty years of business: a story made up of aromas, flavours and traditions, the story of the Portinari family, who have carved their name among the pillars of Venice's restaurant scene and beyond. Chef Nicola Portinari welcomes guests to La Peca with one clear goal: to give them pleasure, letting them choose freely from an extensive and inviting menu (for those who prefer a guided experience, there are three tasting menus, including a vegetarian option). Leafing through it, it is easy to be seduced by dishes that speak to the palate and the mind. His creations are technical, but never ostentatious: harmonies rich in flavour, without ever being contrived. It's always hard to choose because there's so much to tempt you: the ravioli filled with venison, wrapped in a delicate jelly, accompanied by mushrooms and completed with a clear, fragrant consommé, are unforgettable; for those who love game, the mallard is a tribute to the season, with variations that enhance its nobility. And then there is the dessert, which ends the journey with one last embrace: creme brulée and ancient citrus ravioli are the historic signature dish, but there are also surprising reinterpretations of classics such as the Sachertorte, made intriguing by peanuts and Ghital cheese ice cream, and the Mont Blanc, enhanced by a delicate hint of green tea. A monumental wine cellar with around two thousand labels and a generous selection of natural wines completes the experience.

Name: La Pyramide - Maison Henriroux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally a modest inn opened in 1822, this Vienne institution was made famous by the emblematic couple of Mado and Fernand Point in the early 20C. It was taken over by Patrick Henriroux in 1989 and has since continued to evolve on his watch: a designer decor in the dining area, the addition of a second restaurant (PH3), a charming hotel and a cocktail bar… As for the food, classical dishes are given a highly precise and pared-back contemporary twist: artichokes and European lobster, the Camus and baby varieties stuffed with meat from the claws, the tail with its coral ; milk-fed lamb with Provençal moussaka and confit and herb-smoked Chinese aubergine ; chocolate piano, grilled coffee-infused crème anglaise sauce. The breath-taking cellar book is a dizzying array of Côte-Rôtie and Condrieu, wines that go perfectly with this cuisine. It is worth noting that the lunchtime menu is a real bargain, and the slick, polished service upholds the time-honoured traditions of France's grand old establishments.

Name: La Scène
Description: Stéphanie Le Quellec makes no secret of her aim to "deconsecrate haute cuisine" courtesy of a generous gourmet ethos in which each dish tells a story. Her menus, which are comprised of varying numbers of courses, or "acts", may appear simple but every last detail has been endlessly puzzled over and her big-boned sauces are often enhanced by vintage sherry vinegar. Among her signature dishes is an iconic red mullet, the recipe of which she is constantly tweaking. The vibe is casual, both in the kitchen and dining room, and diners are invited to enjoy the present moment to the full. Warm seamless service from the on-the-ball front-of-house team. The unorthodox wine cellar features wines by the glass that are poured from a magnum, even a jeroboam bottle. At lunchtime, a tempting menu based on seasonal ingredients is served in the bistro.

Name: La Table Lionel Giraud
Address: Rond-point de la Liberté, 68 avenue du Général-Leclerc, Narbonne, 11100, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The place is named after Abbé St Crescent, who in the Middle Ages opened his doors to pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago. The arcades and bare stones may be a throwback to the distant past, but today the decor is ultra-modern, with finely crafted black and white polished concrete floors and sculptural one-piece seats. Lionel Giraud, son of a restaurant owner, is a strong advocate of locally sourced produce. An inventive chef, he honours ingredients from the most noble (Mediterranean red tuna) to the most modest (green beans) and everything in between, such as an authentic Corbières buffalo mozzarella. He is also a proponent of ikejime, the Japanese method of killing fish that maintains the quality of the meat and is argued to be more humane.

Name: La Table d'Olivier Nasti
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Ah, Kaysersberg! This small village on the Alsace wine route comes into view between two valleys – you can't miss the iconic red façade of Hotel Le Chambard, which houses La Table d'Olivier Nasti, Meilleur Ouvrier de France 2007. The chef's objective is to showcase the terroir and restore tradition in a series of creative, visually arresting, even playful dishes. To this end, no ingredients are off limits: game, morels from the Vosges, foie gras, truffles and even Arctic char. He has created a personal menu that takes the seasons into account and pays particular attention to sauces and decoctions. As for the wine, talented and enthusiastic sommelier Jean-Baptiste Klein is a mine of information. The Chambard's guestrooms are decorated in a chic, refined style, and let's not forget the gorgeous spa.

Name: La Table de Christophe Dufossé
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Christophe Dufossé has been thriving in his homeland, as his cooking illustrates. This pretty château set in leafy grounds sports a contemporary conservatory extension. Here, he champions organic, self-sufficient and sustainable surf and turf cooking centred on vegetables and produce from the North. Every dish is delicately yet generously crafted – and flanked by robust classic sauces. The dishes speak for themselves – monkfish gratin with a sabayon sauce and its ragout of clams, razor clams and cockles. Other highlights are the bread and sweets, particularly the incredibly lavish dessert trolley.

Name: La Table de Franck Putelat
Address: 80 chemin des Anglais, au Sud de la Cité, Carcassonne, 11000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The medieval city is emblematic of the time-honoured heritage of Carcassonne and its region… and the same could almost be said of Franck Putelat. Established at the foot of the city’s famous ramparts, this native of the Jura who has made the Aude his home, spins a succulent tale of land and sea in his contemporary, designer lair. Much of the produce comes from his large vegetable garden, as he cleverly reworks regional hits according to his mood and inspiration of the day. Attractive plating, lashings of flavour and suave finesse embody his spot-on repertory. Three examples that have become iconic: parmentier of sea fig (a marine animal); cassoulet with supreme of squab and pigeon leg sausage; bouillabaisse with duck foie gras. Pastry chef Alexis Pocinho crafts a particularly balanced repertory of sweet-toothed delights. Seven lovely guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: La Table de Maxime
Description: Welcome to Our, a picturesque Ardennes village nestling in peaceful countryside, that has become a beacon for savvy gourmets thanks to Maxime Collard. He has forged his own style back in his homeland, turning an old farmstead into a stylish, fashionable restaurant, whose many windows and mirrors seem to invite the countryside indoors. The establishment offers accommodation in the area to enhance the pleasure of a meal here. Chef Collard steers clear of showing off his extensive technical background, preferring to highlight the essence of a few premium ingredients, local whenever possible. Examples of the handiwork of this high-precision artisan include immaculately cooked turbot flanked by a punchy concoction of verbena and mussels. Courgette flowers stuffed with ricotta add a refreshing green note. The meal may end with a fluffy, light as a feather chocolate soufflé paired with ripe cherries and vanilla ice cream. Whether you have opted for lunch, the set menu or the à la carte lineup (the Anjou pigeon is to die for!), one thing is certain: you are in for an unforgettable experience. Aromatic cuisine, steeped in subtle nuances and generosity. A meal at Maxime’s is a moment of pure bliss!

Name: La Table de Pavie
Address: Hôtel de Pavie, 5 place du Clocher, Saint-Emilion, 33330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: In the world-famous village of Saint-Émilion, Yannick Alléno rigorously oversees the restaurant of this luxury hotel, once a convent, whose nuns offered sanctuary to pilgrims and travellers. Chef Sébastien Faramond and his team turn out finely tuned dishes that lean towards the Aquitaine terroir of Southwest France, enhanced by remarkably intense sauces and reductions: koji risotto cooked in Graves wine, grated aged Mimolette cheese and cockles au naturel; the signature dish of "pigeon soufflé et rôti au feu d'enfer, bec façon ortolan, filet au jus de presse en amertume d'oseille"; warm chocolate tart, Maury sauce and textured Tahitian vanilla ice cream… Needless to say, the superb wines of Saint-Émilion will accompany your meal.

Name: La Table de Yoann Conte
Address: 13 vieille route des Pensières, Veyrier-du-Lac, 74290, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Breton chef Yoann Conte discovered the meaning of brotherhood and the importance of food on the high seas. He is committed to creating "unpolished" and sincere dishes within the fine dining context. An extreme hiker in his spare time, his lakeside garden benefits from his herbalist know-how. His cooking is in his likeness: physical, down-to-earth, adventurous and with a wry sense of humour. Supported by a highly motivated team, he tirelessly refines two set menus with distinct themes: "Adopted Land" which highlights the Alpine terroir, "Native Brittany" which celebrates his homeland with precision. The savvy food and wine pairings devised by the chef and sommelier are emblematic of the establishment's sustainable ethos. The front-of-house team bring a good dose of humour to the lively service. There are 11 lovely guestrooms overlooking the lake.

Name: La Table des Amis
Address: Le Mas Les Eydins, 2420 chemin du Four, Bonnieux, 84480, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Christophe Bacquié greets diners like old friends in his gorgeous farmhouse set in peaceful countryside, surrounded by vineyards, olive groves and lavender fields. With his wife Alexandra and a closeknit, committed team, all of whom share his passion for Southern France and its produce and wines, Bacquié unfolds a single set menu with a strong Mediterranean identity. With flavour as his watchword, he crafts the finest ingredients simply and transparently and we were delighted to see some of his signature dishes, such as his modern aioli and his vision of iced Calisson, in pride of place on the menu. An authentic Provençal property and the guarantee of wholehearted hospitality.

Name: La Table du Lausanne Palace
Address: Rue du Grand Chêne 7, Lausanne, 1002, Switzerland
Description: Run by Franck Pelux and Sarah Benahmed, the Table of the lavish Lausanne Palace oozes refined elegance and bucket loads of intensity. A score in the zeitgeist, whose Gallic roots are nurtured by international techniques, BBQ cooking and expressive ingredient-led recipes starring top-drawer produce. Delicate, almost sensual sole meunière with a marinière-style celery pie; Breton blue lobster in a new take on couscous; crunchy farm-reared calf’s sweetbread finished on the BBQ with a medley of cabbage. On Wednesdays and Thursdays, the business lunchtime menu is just the ticket and the view over Lake Geneva, particularly from the window tables, is matchless. Before dinner, pop into the bar for an aperitif. Superlatively seamless, spot-on service.

Name: La Villa Archange
Address: Rue de l'Ouest, Le Cannet, 06110, France
Description: This handsome 18C provençal villa is perched up in the hills above Cannes. Take a seat in one of the small cosy lounges to sample chef Bruno Oger's cuisine. Breton by birth, he has adopted the Mediterranean as his home, concocting inspired seafood dishes drawn from Brittany and the French Riviera… Abalone from the island of Groix in a parsley herb sauce; roast turbot, celery, shallots and walnuts; a lemon-flavoured praliné and buckwheat dessert. His braised pork cheeks and razor clams with a black pudding tartlet illustrate his knack for meat dishes. A table d'hôte in the kitchen provides the opportunity to glean insights into the culinary process. The cheerful, attentive service further adds to the experience. You can’t go wrong with the lunchtime menu, available on Fridays and Saturdays, all the more so as it offers the chance to taste the same dishes as those on the more high-flying set and à la carte menus.

Name: La Voile - La Réserve Ramatuelle
Address: Chemin de la Quessine, Ramatuelle, 83350, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This exclusive luxury hotel, which blends seamlessly into its natural surroundings, is the HQ of talented Éric Canino, a chef influenced by his fruitful collaboration with Michel Guérard. Inspired by the master of healthy cuisine, Éric composes his own Provençal repertory, starring fruit and vegetables, fish and seafood (often cooked in sea water), enhanced with aromatic herbs and olive oil. Despite all that, his signature dish stars Bresse poultry and lobster. His impressive culinary talents range from a modern use of citrus fruits to textbook perfect sauces and reductions that add character and depth to each dish. Accomplished pastry chef Julien Coulomb (stints at le Cinq and Plénitude with Maxime Frédéric) signs creations that bear his hallmark delicate subtlety, embodied by his lemon and tarragon delight.

Name: La Yeon
Address: 23F, Shilla Hotel, 249 Dongho-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, 04605, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Stunning views are guaranteed from La Yeon’s position on the 23rd floor of The Shilla Hotel, but the quality of the food ensures your attention never strays far from the plate. There is a delicacy and lightness to the dishes, which take the time-honoured traditions of Korean cuisine and update them without compromising familiar flavours and textures. From crisp red mullet to tender, char-grilled Hanwoo bulgogi, the kitchen resists overcomplication and focuses instead on clean, precise flavours. The dining room is comfortable, and the service team is a delight.

Name: Lafleur
Address: Palmengartenstraße 11, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In a prime location in the Palmenhaus, adjacent to the Palmengarten, Andreas Krolik applies his personal signature to top-notch ingredients to produce highly sophisticated dishes with complex flavour profiles, such as tender braised Wagyu short ribs with a punchy truffle sauce, flavoursome autumn truffles and a fine corn purée, along with spicy paprika chutney and mildly sweet braised balsamic onions. In the evening, the "Grands Produits" and "Ethical Vegan Cuisine" set menus are served – the latter is testament to the chef's passion for plant-based cooking. At lunchtime, there are two appealing set menus, dubbed "Casual" and "Casual Green", each with three or four courses. The setting is stylish: the chic and elegant modern interior and the view of the Siesmayer-Blumenparterre are worth mentioning, as is the extremely cordial and professional front-of-house team headed up by restaurant manager Boris Häbel. The sommelier service is also excellent, and the wine pairing for the set menu is first-rate. In case you were wondering, the restaurant's name refers to the famous Château Lafleur vineyard near Bordeaux.

Name: Lai Ching Heen
Address: GF, Regent, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In this upscale hotel restaurant, the glitzy decor, expansive harbour views and Hong Kong's dazzling skyline don't outshine the familiar Cantonese flavours elevated to unprecedented excellence. Delicious golden-seared Hokkaido scallops, crispy deep-fried tofu, and umami-laden crab claw casserole with house-made XO sauce – this menu is all killer, no filler! Both the extensive wine list and the tea menu with some exceptional choices are well curated.

Name: Lakeside
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Come out of the lift on the seventh floor of the imposing The Fontenay hotel and you will find yourself in an airy, light-filled space. The bold interior design in elegant white is upscale and luxurious but still feels casual. The view over the city and the Outer Alster is simply sensational! Julian Stowasser's unique cooking style shines through in his modern seven-course set menu. He skilfully blends premium ingredients with an elegant restraint, as seen in the impeccably fresh, beautifully fragrant langoustine from the Faroe Islands, served with silky sour cream and a vibrant piel de sapo melon sauce. The entire experience is complemented by an outstanding front-of-house team led by Michel Buder, who stands out as a warm, professional and confident host. Astute wine recommendations. If you have an aperitif in the chic bar on the sixth floor before your meal, you reach the restaurant via a curved staircase.

Name: Lalique
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Château Lafaurie-Peyraguey is the epitome of special occasion indulgence: the lavish dining room is adorned with a Lalique (surprise, surprise!) crystal chandelier and the glazed extension commands a sweeping view over the vineyards. Chef Jérôme Schilling, MOF 2023, who boasts an enviable CV, describes himself as a "cook of the vineyards”. His dishes inspired by the Sauternes terroir bear names such as "Interpretation of the 2015 vintage" (colourful tomatoes, vanilla and stracciatella) or “Sarments of vines” (smoked blue lobster, verbena and kombu seaweed). This virtuoso score is served in Lalique crystalware and fine china tableware, taking table arts to a whole new level. Timeless and luxurious with stylish, razor-sharp cuisine, which aims to exalt the distinctive flavour profile of Sauternes that, needless to say, enjoys pride of place on the extensive wine list.

Name: Lamdre
Address: Room 04, 1F, Block 14, Courtyard 4, Gongti North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, 100000, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A skylight in the pitched roof bathes the main room in natural light, while the private rooms and balcony sport a cosy vibe. An inquisitive soul by nature, veteran chef Dai spent time in Japan studying plant-based ingredients. The menu follows the seasons and may feature the chef’s signature "porcini, green pepper and sea salt" dish with Yunnan mushrooms chargrilled to impart smoky aromas. Try the interesting wine or tea pairings.

Name: Landhaus Bacher
Address: Südtiroler Platz 2, Mautern an der Donau, 3512, Austria
Description: A true institution in the Wachau Valley, this place continues to impress with its charm and, first and foremost, the calibre you can expect here. Chef-patron Thomas Dorfer has maintained consistently high standards for many years. His cooking is based on the classics and replete with contrasts and creative touches. A prime example of a dish showcasing depth and purity of flavour is the wonderfully succulent Ramsau mountain trout, served with sweet-and-sour cucumber and medlar, sour cream mousseline, and a fresh, subtly buttery elderflower-citrus beurre blanc. Diners can choose from four set menus and an appealing lunch menu, with each dish also available à la carte. Signature creations by senior chef Lisl Wagner-Bacher, including breaded egg with caviar, also feature. There is a fantastic selection of wines. Excellent service is provided by the very attentive, professional and effortlessly charming team led by restaurant manager and sommelier Susanne Dorfer-Bacher. Dine in the elegant country-house-style dining area or out on the lovely garden terrace. Tastefully appointed, comfortable guestrooms are available for overnight stays. The restaurant also has a shop and offers a range of cookery courses.

Name: Lasai
Address: Largo dos Leões 35, Humaitá, Rio de Janeiro, 22271-020, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking
Description: (Temporarily closed due to the relocation to Avenida Vieira Souto, 460 – 21st floor, at the Sofitel Ipanema Hotel, from December 2026) Dining at this restaurant with just 10 seats is like attending a show, but with the best seats in the house! Although it starts out quietly, the kitchen comes to life as the chefs embark on the task in hand, with interesting interaction between chef Rafa Costa e Silva and his guests. The surprise tasting menu begins with a variety of appetisers in which vegetables take centre stage – displayed on a wooden tray illuminated by a spotlight on the counter – and served in different forms and textures. These are organically grown in line with the seasons and are mainly sourced from the chef’s gardens in Itanhangá and Vale das Videiras. A wine-pairing option, chosen by the experienced Maíra Freire, is also an option. “Lasai” translates as “tranquil” in Basque – the restaurant takes its name from the time the chef spent refining his skills in the award-winning Mugaritz (in Errentería, in Spain’s Basque country). You’ll need to book ahead and be punctual, as the experience starts at the same time for every guest.

Name: Lazy Bear
Description: This dining spot is firmly rooted as part of San Franciso's dining landscape. The nightly tasting menu is served in a swanky, bi-level warehouse decked out like a mogul's hunting lodge. The menu has a sweeping creative scope, drawing on both nostalgia and current culinary trends with a confident swagger.Highlights include a duo of oysters served two ways: one topped with a gooseberry mignonette and the second charbroiled with a grilled Jimmy Nardello glacage and finished with pickled biquinho peppers. Bold flavors presented with flair are a common thread, like in a buttery A5 Wagyu ribeye paired with a sweet-and-savory oxtail and sour cherry tart, perfect lattice crust, and all.

Name: Le Cerf
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The culinary centrepiece of the Wald & Schlosshotel Friedrichsruhe has an elegant style that verges on the opulent. Exquisite details such as fine fabrics, ornate wallpaper and crystal chandeliers are perfectly in keeping with the historical castle. The cuisine is a celebration of classic tradition but always features a sophisticated twist – such as the fruity, tangy passion fruit note in the chilled white tomato soup. Boris Rommel and his dedicated team bowl diners over with their precise technique, outstanding ingredients and attention to detail. There are two set menus (one vegetarian), from which you can also order à la carte. Service is both warm and highly professional, and the chef himself often visits tables to explain the ideas behind his dishes. Theatricality is also part of the experience, for example, when the Gugelhupf of non-force-fed foie gras is portioned at your table. The amuse-bouches are served in the form of imaginative plates arranged by Boris Rommel himself. The wine list is fantastic and includes some real gems to accompany the set menu. Tip: Kick off with an aperitif at the hotel bar.

Name: Le Chalet de la Forêt
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Pascal Devalkeneer’s chalet is magnificently set on the edge of the Sonian Forest and the chalet’s terrace makes the most of this fantastic natural environment. The restaurant overlooking the chef’s cottage garden oozes luxurious elegance to which you should add well-oiled, slick service and, above all, chef Devalkeneer’s personal stamp on each dish. His blend of classicism and creativity reveals surgical precision, as well as a quest for subtlety and generosity. He scours the countryside of Belgium and France for the best ingredients from Aveyron lamb to abalone from the Brittany coast and honey from his own beehives, with which he crafts an amazing floral dessert starter… He works with exceptional ingredients, flanking them with intriguing side dishes to create a felicitous festival of flavours. For example, he may delicately perfume seabass with bay leaf, adding green asparagus and black truffle, before adding the final definitive flourish, a vivacious dressing of confit shallots, a gutsy gravy and a last-minute hollandaise sauce. This high-flying craftsmanship unveils chef Devalkeneer’s talent, demonstrated by his deep-seated understanding of the role and impact of each ingredient which enables him to create combinations that intelligently enrich and exalt the original flavour. The sommelier is a fountain of insightful wine tips, with a preference for Burgundies. This chalet is a temple of superlative culinary art that never fails to surprise.

Name: Le Clarence
Description: This lavish 1884 private mansion just off the Champs-Élysées is graced with a luxurious interior that embodies the essence of French art de vivre. In the wake of Christophe Pelé, Andrea Capasso has embraced the house tradition of unfettered, yet disciplined cuisine strewn with bold notes. A keen surf and turf champion, the chef slips Italian twists into what he calls ‘satellite’ dishes, while savvily developing a single theme within each menu. The wine list is enough to make your head spin; one of its two sections is devoted to the owner's prestigious wines. The lounges on the upper floors are just the ticket for a relaxed drink before dinner or coffee afterwards.

Name: Le Corot
Address: Les Étangs de Corot, 55 rue de Versailles, Ville-d'Avray, 92410, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Much like the artist Corot, who painted the nearby ponds, Rémi Chambard turns to nature and produce from Île-de-France for inspiration when it comes to cooking. He devises a set menu that showcases the region by highlighting the different villages from which he sources his ingredients, from Montmorency to Crécy-la-Chapelle. He also personally undertakes what he calls his "urban harvest" in the King's Kitchen Garden in Versailles. This virtuoso chef still takes great pleasure in working with vegetables and plants (as well as other ingredients). Imbued with a certain purity, his dishes are striking in their freshness, lightness and aesthetic, not to mention the depth of his sauces and emulsions. Take, for example, the wild pike-perch from the Giverny area, enhanced by a remarkable sabayon with saffron and parsley, or the veal sweetbreads au gratin with Meaux mustard and a reduced jus with watercress and tarragon. The pared-back, plush, yet cosy interior provides the perfect foil to polished cuisine.

Name: Le Grand Restaurant - Jean-François Piège
Description: Welcome to Jean-François Piège's "laboratory of great cuisine", a sleek dining area whose sculptural ceiling is adorned in panes of glass that catch and reflect the light. The chef gives full expression to his extensive experience and know-how, executing timeless signature cuisine that finds its source in the annals of French gastronomy (the chef is said to own one of the finest cookery libraries of Paris). The score tours the regions of France and revolves around Piège’s "mijotés modernes". This consummate chef demonstrates his creative talent and ability to provoke culinary emotion and taste without falling foul of the temptation to craft purely visual masterpieces. He invariably surprises us with dishes that are the epitome of simplicity and flavour, such as his succulent veal sweetbread cooked on walnut shells. We also recommend one of his earliest desserts: the Mon Blanc à Manger – an upside-down île flottante.

Name: Le Jules Verne
Address: Tour Eiffel - 6 avenue Gustave-Eiffel, Paris, 75007, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Frédéric Anton presides over the fortunes of this emblematic restaurant on the second floor of the Eiffel Tower, accessible by a private lift. The magic of the venue, perched at a height of 125m, instantly bewitches diners, who are then entranced by the high-flying cuisine. Every day, the team pulls out all the stops to elevate premium produce as they craft delicate, spot-on dishes boasting flavour combinations that never fail to deliver. For example, ravioli of langoustine in parmesan cream and a delicate beetroot jelly, or grenobloise-style caramelised calf’s sweetbread, perfectly executed and free of unnecessary frills. The desserts are fully the equal to the rest of this lofty score. To bag one of the tables near the windows, be sure to book well in advance - the iconic view over Paris through the tower's iron fretwork is nothing short of spectacular. Polished welcome and suitably slick, seamless service.

Name: Le Neuvième Art
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: It was in the kitchens of Paul Bocuse and Régis Marcon, among others, that Christophe Roure learned the ropes. He holds three professional qualifications (in cookery, charcuterie and pastry-making, no less!) and was named Meilleur Ouvrier de France in 2007. Based in Lyon since 2014, his virtuoso culinary talent grows stronger by the day: subtly inventive, spot-on marriages of flavours, and of course cherry-picked ingredients. His shellfish and miller mushroom stew is a marvel of balance and finesse, in which the lemongrass-spiked hollandaise sauce teases out the seafood flavours and underscores the earthy mushroom notes. Finally talented Tanguy Nourrisson signs knockout desserts like a chocolate and iced coconut delight.

Name: Le Parc Les Crayères
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking
Description: Once Louise Pommery's mansion, this small château (early 20C) standing in superb grounds exudes classic elegance. Using premium ingredients, chef Christophe Moret concocts refined, approachable dishes that are as generous as they are delicious – spider crab infused with sea fennel, or glazed mallard duck with juniper and elder. Rosalie Boucher's desserts are cleverly devised for maximum lightness. These gems feature in the various set menus but also – an increasingly rare pleasure – on the à la carte menu. The wine list includes almost 900 champagnes. Superb guestrooms and suites.

Name: Le Pavillon
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Elegance and refinement run throughout the luxurious Dollenberg resort, set in an idyllic Black Forest landscape, and find their finest expression in the classically appointed fine dining restaurant. In his five- to eight-course set menu, Martin Herrmann places exceptional ingredients centre stage with precision, restraint and superb balance, while weaving in exciting modern touches. One fine example: perfectly cooked sea bass paired with tender squid rings and a fruity-tart shallot marmalade as a striking contrast, rounded off by a wonderful, lightly frothed paella broth – sauces are truly this chef's forte. The breathtaking natural scenery framed by the floor-to-ceiling windows provides a magnificent backdrop. The experience is taken up a notch by the charming, exceptionally courteous service with a personal touch. Special mention goes to Sabine Ritter and sommelier Christophe Meyer, two consummate professionals who are the face of the restaurant. The wine recommendations are spot-on, and the list itself is a serious affair – weighted towards the region and France, with some impressive rarities. Year after year, the team has upheld impeccable standards of consistency and quality. This is a family-run establishment in the best sense of the term – something that is lived and breathed here, and can be felt at every table.

Name: Le Pressoir d'Argent - Gordon Ramsay
Address: InterContinental Bordeaux - Le Grand Hôtel, 2-5 place de la Comédie, Bordeaux, 33000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: British-born Gordon Ramsay, world-renowned celeb chef and personality, signs Le Pressoir d'Argent's score. In the kitchen, chef Alexandre Koa breathes a hint of modernity into the classical lineup, savvily blending Aquitaine produce with house spice mixes and a few ingredients imported from Cameroon. French art de vivre is celebrated by the opulent, polished décor, super slick, seamless service and the solid silver Christofle lobster press that is moved from table to table. And let’s not forget the truly remarkable wine cellar of outstanding Bordeaux vintages!

Name: Le Pré - Xavier Beaudiment
Address: 3 route de la Baraque, Clermont-Ferrand, 63000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: "The Auvergne I want you to meet is the one we encounter and pick every morning in our mountains, meadows and forests." The words of local lad Xavier Beaudiment are far from platitudes. Le Pré celebrates the quintessence of its region through cuisine that is both instinctive and poetic. Frog’s legs, pike, foie gras and rabbit are lovingly and enthusiastically crafted and paired with some 200 plants and wild herbs picked at the foot of the volcanoes or in the establishment’s own herb garden. All of which is washed down with a knock-out wine list.

Name: Le Skiff Club
Address: Hôtel Ha(a)ïtza, 1 avenue Louis-Gaume, Pyla-sur-Mer, 33115, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In a 1930s neo-Basque hotel nestled in a pine forest near the legendary Pilat dune, with an interior by designer Philippe Starck, Le Skiff Club is a veritable haven, the cosy conservatory dining room decorated in the style of a yacht club. Captain Stéphane Carrade celebrates the Aquitaine region and its produce, adding his own personal touches. Delicate and original desserts by Alexandre Blay, like his Mexican vanilla, in the form of crème brûlée and jumbo grapes with JM rum, gavotte and caramelised almonds, ice cream and zephyr of grilled pods, are the icing on the cake.

Name: Le Taillevent
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This iconic establishment dating back to 1946 is the epitome of French classicism. Run by the Gardinier family (Les Crayères in Reims), Taillevent is nothing short of an institution. Here in the former private mansion of the Duke of Morny (19C), you are cocooned from the world outside. Tradition is honoured with some elements being prepared tableside, such as the meat or fish trolley served in two courses (veal chop, Pornic pigeon, the catch from small-boat fishing etc) or the classic crêpes Suzette, flambéed first with Grand Marnier and then with cognac. Last but not least, the superb wine list reads like a compendium of vintage tipples.

Name: Les Ambassadeurs by Christophe Cussac
Address: Hôtel Métropole Monte-Carlo, 4 avenue de la Madone, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Métropole Monte Carlo Hotel, an iconic Belle Epoque extravaganza (1886), has been entirely revamped by Jacques Garcia, including the luxurious restaurant that sports the graphic palette so dear to the interior designer (bronze, ivory, warm yellow and gold). At the helm, virtuoso chef Christophe Cussac (former disciple of Joël Robuchon) consummately slaloms between a pure-bred Gallic culinary line-up and more modern recipes, all of which with the Mediterranean as a common thread. High-flying, meticulous cuisine, expert seasoning, cooking and plating: lobster, tarragon, spinach and spianata lasagne; John Dory and artichoke in a coriander stock. Special mention for the incredible bread and dessert trolleys, and for the slick, seamless service. The epitome of special occasion dining!

Name: Les Cols
Address: Carretera de la Canya, Olot, 17800, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Ably assisted by her three daughters (Clara, Martina and Carlota) and her husband Manuel Puigvert, chef Fina Puigdevall builds her creativity around seasonality, sustainability (the family has its own vegetable garden which can be visited at the Casa Horitzó R&D centre in the Vall de Bianya) and the use of produce from the volcanic region of La Garrotxa – they are also staunch advocates of the “food that hasn't travelled” concept. Today, the old family farm is a building with a remarkably cutting-edge interior design that revolves around a relationship between its dining spaces and nature. This is especially noticeable in the events pavilion, which is visually ethereal and where hens roam freely! It offers an impressive single tasting menu: Horizonte, Naturaleza Viva & Mística (Horizon, Living and Mystical Nature) that starts with eye-catching aperitifs and appetisers in the garden (in fine weather) and includes unusual dishes such as “onion royale” and, in season, delicious grilled peas with black sausage (butifarra), bacon, snails and mint.

Name: Liath
Address: Blackrock Market, 19a Main Street, Blackrock, A94 V0D8, Ireland
Description: There's a slightly magical feel to this stylish, cosy restaurant. With just a handful of tables, it makes for a personal dining experience, with Damien Grey and his small team offering a genuinely warm welcome and explaining the dishes personally. First-class ingredients are present throughout the surprise tasting menu, which showcases bold, original dishes centred around the five tastes: salty, savoury, sweet, bitter and sour. Each precisely crafted creation brings together a range of these flavours in perfect harmony, such as aged parmesan with eel and marjoram.

Name: Locanda Sant'Uffizio Enrico Bartolini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In one of the most picturesque corners of Monferrato, within an ancient monastic building that has been converted into an elegant five-star hotel, a truly enchanting culinary experience takes shape. Under the guidance of multi-starred chef Enrico Bartolini, the kitchen is led by Gabriele Boffa, a Piedmontese chef with a solid international background, who is able to combine a deep understanding of the local area with remarkable technical skill. The menu features tasting courses that alternate between faithful interpretations of regional classics – the agnolotti del plin are particularly memorable – and more personal creations, all of which remain firmly rooted in local produce, flavours and traditions. Here and there, Latin American influences and bolder touches emerge, though they are handled with balance and restraint. The dining experience takes place in an elegant dining room with just a few tables, where attentive service accompanies a sequence of dishes brimming with character, from carefully crafted amuse-bouches to homemade baked goods, right through to dishes that showcase excellent ingredients. The wine list is also of a high standard, supported by a competent and close-knit front-of-house team.

Name: Louis Linster
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Louis Linster has added his own spin to the family restaurant. His mother, Léa, made it a first-rate fine dining establishment and her youthful successor is now leaving his own hallmark. The interior is the quintessence of casual luxury in a reworked vein with modern artwork on the walls and a knock-out terrace overlooking the rolling countryside. Chef Louis is upholding the establishment’s classical repertory, albeit with some lively, exotic touches.Don’t expect plates piled high in victuals, but rather creations that underscore the essence of each ingredient in a bid to let them enjoy the limelight. The sauces are quite simply out of this world. An example: trout salmon perfectly cooked at 40°C, flanked by chive oil, different textures of broccoli, sesame seed seaweed, and, above all, a beurre blanc of incredible depth, subtly enriched in dashi. Alternatively, how about barbecued scallops flanked by an intense onion sauce and a vin jaune emulsion?Louis Linster has found his path, and his partner and your hostess, Njomza, further enhances the venue’s elegance by her attentive service. Léa can be proud.

Name: Lu Shang Lu
Address: 2A01-2A03 / 2A05-2A13, 2F, Sunshine Financial Center, No.1 Tower, 33 Jinghui Street, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Shandong cuisine tops the bill here, starring Confucian cooking, sea cucumber and live seafood shipped daily from Jiaodong peninsula. This regional culinary score has no secrets for the chef, who hails from Yantai. Try his 45-day-old roast duck served with caviar, prawn crackers and Shandong pancakes in a knock-out mix of both Beijing and Shandong cuisine. The well-curated wine list, which shines the spotlight on Shandong, adds a special perspective to the experience.

Name: Lung King Heen
Address: 4F, Four Seasons Hotel, 8 Finance Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Quality produce is sourced from all over the world to make sophisticated Cantonese dishes. Dim sum lunch is a delight; so is their hearty double-boiled soups brimming with ingredients. On top of the main menu, seasonal offerings are also worth checking out. Enjoy the food with organic sparkling teas or ask the sommelier about wine pairings. The room commands panoramic harbour views and is popular among locals and seasoned travellers alike.

Name: Lycabettus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: The terrace of this restaurant, part of the Andronis Luxury Suite hotel, is one of the most photographed spots in Oia—and it’s no wonder, since it looks like a real-life natural balcony overlooking the Santorini caldera! After being escorted from the reception area by a hostess, you’ll be able to sample the creations of chefs Christos Karagiannis and Petros Brandenburg, who champion an elegant, contemporary cuisine built around local, seasonal ingredients, featuring highly refined techniques and French influences. The well-balanced service, with a choice between an à la carte option at a fixed price (some dishes can be included for a surcharge) and a tasting menu, features some truly memorable dishes, such as the original Squid with red mullet sauce (which resembles tagliatelle) or the Lobster with carrot purée. The experience is truly unforgettable, thanks to the charming service, creative cocktails, and a wine cellar with over 1,000 labels (which can be ordered by the glass).

Name: LÚ Cocina y Alma
Address: Zaragoza 2, Jerez de la Frontera, 11402, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Juanlu Fernández, a fan of slow cooking, defines his style as 'rearguard avant-garde', an expression that highlights his personal, somewhat crazy interpretation of cooking which is based around classic French cuisine but which also showcases the best Andalucian ingredients, with stews and traditional recipes.In his attractive restaurant, designed by architect Jean Porsche, he aims to personalise the experience by involving guests in the creative process (the kitchen is visible from the dining room) through two tasting menus offering different sensations: 'Duxende' (9 courses), which is described as the restaurant’s soul, and a more extensive 'Duxo' (12 courses), a journey across the senses, enabling guests to discover the region’s history and recipes. For their delicacy and depth of flavour, dishes like Choco a la cochambrosa (cuttlefish) and Marisco con chícharos (seafood with peas) were a cut above. Over 600 wines and sherries of Jerez take centre stage in the wine pairing options, many of which are old bottles or from wineries that no longer exist!

Name: M.B
Address: Maria Zambrano 2, Carretera TF 47, Guía de Isora, 38687, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In keeping with the Ritz-Carlton Abama, a spectacular resort boasting attractive gardens, palm trees and a whole host of leisure options and one that fully deserves its myriad plaudits, the M.B restaurant exudes the same essence of luxury and exclusivity that is reserved for the chosen few. It features a room used for welcome drinks and after-dinner coffee (including innovatively presented petits-fours) and cocktails, a contemporary-style main dining room with a predominantly white decor, and two glass-fronted galleries that are used as terraces in the summer months. On his meticulously prepared à la carte and a tasting menu, chef Erlantz Gorostiza faithfully recreates the amazing dishes devised by culinary maestro Martín Berasategui (including many of the latter’s iconic dishes), through dishes bursting with passion, technique and flavour that are based around the island’s best ingredients. We were particularly impressed by the “soldier shrimp” from El Hierro over an almond kernel with green gazpacho and shiso sorbet.

Name: MAZ
Address: 3F, Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho, 1-3 Kioicho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 102-0094, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This gustatory experience is a journey through Peru. The menu features the culinary traditions of the Andes and the ecosystem of the Amazon basin. Each menu item lists the producing region and, uniquely, its elevation. Taking these altitudes as a guide, the meal traces a route through sea, mountain and river, weaving a tale of diverse natural environments. Dried foods from Peru combine with Japanese ingredients to bring forth a cuisine that is richly imaginative.

Name: Ma Langue Sourit
Description: Wholehearted Cyril Molard aims to ensure that the diner enjoys their meal as much as a child devouring an ice cream! Each detail has been endlessly pondered over and then fine-tuned in this snug, trendy establishment. Creative side dishes set out to showcase the flavours of outstanding produce. The chef may add whoomph to a dish with subtle additions of tangy acidity. When he cooks asparagus, you can be certain it will be the best you have ever tasted. The fish is cooked to perfection and the succulent side dishes are paired with sauces that err towards the classical in a bid to shine the spotlight on the main ingredient. Examples include a broccoli and watercress juice that provides a perfect umami taste to pair with poached abalone, while a frothy succulent sabayon of beurre noisette blends scallops and different textures of parsnip in a match made in heaven! Molard and his team occasionally pop out to the dining room to see how diners our enjoying their meal and to chat with them in a casual, good-natured spirit. Apparently sticking your tongue out is an insider code that means you’re enjoying the meal!

Name: Madonnina del Pescatore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: It opened in 1984, but to call it a historic restaurant is misleading: Moreno Cedroni is one of Italy’s most innovative – as well as most talented – chefs. It was from this restaurant in Marzocca, a hamlet south of Senigallia, that ideas emerged which have found their way onto many dining tables across Italy and beyond. Today more than before, the Madonnina del Pescatore is a hotbed of innovation, which Moreno blends with extraordinary ease and good taste into the cuisine of the Marche region and his childhood memories, in a constant interplay between local traditions and gastronomic journeys, even as far afield as the Far East. The setting is a room overlooking the beach – home to the chef’s marine garden – and the sea, in an atmosphere of refined elegance. The service is orchestrated by the natural and gentle grace of his wife, Mariella, who creates an atmosphere of genuine well-being in the dining room, free from stiffness and formality – a place where you can relax and enjoy an extraordinary meal.

Name: Magdalena
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The motto here is "raw, rugged, regional." Chef Dominik Hartmann and his team delight diners with modern seasonal cuisine that strikes an impressive balance between natural simplicity and creativity, complexity and a pleasing sense of groundedness. Great emphasis is placed on regional sourcing, with a preference for small-scale producers. There is a fully vegetarian seven-course surprise menu, with the option to add two extra courses. The house-made bread with butter is extremely moreish, as is the interesting combination of beetroot – oven-baked and puréed – with fruity-tart fermented blackberries, slightly bitter radicchio and aromatic roasted hazelnuts, finished with a fresh beetroot and ginger broth. The surprise menu, which can be made vegan on request, is complemented by a fantastic selection of Swiss wines. The sleek, upscale interior has floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a magnificent view of the valley! The establishment boasts its own bakery with a terrace (open Thu-Sun, 7-11am).

Name: Magill Estate Restaurant
Address: 78 Penfold Road, Rosslyn Park, Adelaide, SA 5072, Australia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Magill Estate Restaurant boasts an unbeatable location at the base of the Adelaide Hills and overlooking the vineyards of the world-famous Penfolds winery. Chef Scott Huggins blends Australian products with precise technique in this tasting menu, where 10 courses may reveal the likes of sea urchin with snow peas and tarragon or Spring lamb Wellington with kohlrabi. The service and setting are warm and engaging, making guests feel right at home from the very beginning. Naturally, wine is an integral part of the experience here, and the Icon pairing allows diners the opportunity to experience the full range of what these winemakers have to offer. The tasting is complemented by sommeliers who deliver elegant, yet accessible service.

Name: Magnolia
Address: Via Pelliciano 35, loc. Montilgallo, Longiano, 47020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the refined Relais Villa Margherita, an eighteenth-century residence transformed into an elegant boutique retreat with a handful of rooms, parkland and a swimming pool, Magnolia represents its contemporary soul. The light-filled veranda dining room opens onto the landscape of the Romagna hills, the gaze stretching as far as the distinctive peak of San Marino, in a continuous dialogue between indoors and out. At the helm, chef Alberto Faccani lucidly interprets a gastronomic journey that alternates memory and exploration: alongside more classic dishes that tell the story of his professional career, room is found for original creations, the expression of a restless evolutionary drive. His style is elegant and measured, built on refined balances and pairings that are never predictable, as in the delicate harmony of coconut and milk that accompanies baby cuttlefish with caviar and peas, or in the intense signature dish of squid carbonara with black truffle. More exotic flourishes are not lacking, well integrated into the overall narrative, as in the lobster with peas, coconut and lemongrass, where freshness and fragrance meet with natural ease. The welcome is gracious, the service precise and engaging, while the broad and carefully curated wine list finds a capable interpreter in the passionate work of the sommelier.

Name: Maison Aribert
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Christophe Aribert is thriving in this handsome 19C house built against the hill, in the heart of Uriage Park. A nature lover, he has made eco-responsibility the backbone of his establishment: waste management, pellet heating system, organic cotton fabrics... Every aspect is examined and analysed in terms of its impact on the environment. In addition to singing an ode to freshwater fish, the chef's passion for herbs and roots from the surrounding mountains is becoming more pronounced than ever, alongside herbs and flowers from the kitchen garden, honey from bee hives and fruit and veg from local market gardeners. Finally, let's not forget the comfortable guestrooms – ideal should you wish to stay a little longer.

Name: Maison Benoît Vidal
Address: Sur-les-Bois, 79 route de Thônes, Annecy, 74940, France
Description: Benoît Vidal is the Catalan chef behind this restaurant done out in a slick contemporary style in the Annecy area. Having completed stints with Michel Trama and Michel Guérard, he has created a light, poetic brand of cuisine that is rooted in the culinary traditions of Savoie, his adopted home. He brings a sense of precision and his own personal style to bear on the rigorously sourced ingredients, elevating them with sound technical skill and elaborate presentations. The strength of this chef may well lie in his pared-down, apparently simple creations showcasing pike, trout and crayfish with understated elegance. Appealing vegetarian set menu ("Sentier à fleur d'eau") and wallet-friendly lunch menu.

Name: Maison Colette
Description: A wind of enthusiasm heralds Thijs Vervloet’s return to Tongerlo. This former doctor’s home has been entirely refurbished with alfresco dining in the garden and five deluxe guestrooms. Luxury is the bedrock of the high-end establishment from its Gallic poise and floor-to-ceiling windows that flood the interior in light to the cosily intimate drapes and made-to-measure porcelain tableware by Pieter Stockmans! A champion of the ingredient, Vervloet’s culinary signature seeks to place his classical background and training at the service of a demanding score underpinned by sensitivity and know-how. Everything is prepared on the spot, so, when he presents his emblematic dish of no less than four different versions of langoustine (including a shellfish consommé to die for!), you know that you are in for a festival of flavour. His melt-in-the-mouth suckling lamb with proper crackling and a creamy-crunchy gratin dauphinois, crisp green peas and a punchy gravy is in exactly the same delicious vein. This banquet ends on a similar high note, as your coffee is escorted by a trolley piled high with wickedly enticing sweet titbits. The variety of the à la carte menu is eminently noteworthy, as are the insightful wine-food pairings, and Lore’s attentive service. Maison Colette has clearly puzzled and pondered over every tiny detail.

Name: Maison Nouvelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: On the lively Chartrons market square, this pretty stone building is the newest and latest establishment of chef Philippe Etchebest, also behind Bordeaux’ Quatrième Mur. Guests are greeted like old friends and immediately feel at home in this tasteful, welcoming interior. Philippe’s unwavering commitment to good food and to working only with top local produce shines through and is clearly shared by his talented team. The tasting menu, entirely seasonal, features a few of his signature dishes, such as ravioles of mushrooms and sautéed foie gras, as well as some exquisite vegetarian recipes. Welcome to "Etxe Beste" ("new house" in Basque)!

Name: Maison Ronan Kervarrec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ronan Kervarrec signs a vibrant and indulgent homage to his native Brittany. The chef is going from strength to strength at Saint Grégoire to the north of Rennes courtesy of recipes that tell the tale of his childhood. In a cosy string of contemporary lounges that overlook a manicured garden, the chef rolls out a modern score that stars the premium produce of Brittany. An example: delicate tartare of Breton lobster with red seaweed and a sorbet of sea fennel or line-caught mackerel marinated in muscadet wine. In tribute to his father, who was a saucier chef at the George V Hotel (Paris), Kervarrec expertly executes a range of jus and sauces ranging from intense to subtle. Slick professional welcome and service from the chef's wife, Els, and her team. Guestrooms for overnight stays and a small delicatessen where you can purchase gourmet souvenirs.

Name: Maison Rostang
Description: Chef Nicolas Beaumann enthusiastically perpetuates the tradition of delicious food that has always been synonymous with this emblematic establishment, albeit while increasingly embracing the modern, as reflected in the newly refurbished dining room. The short à la carte menu and the tasting menus (one of which is plant-based) include poivrade artichoke "in a velouté of its leaves; caper and olive stuffing", their classic pike-perch quenelle with lobster cream, and Bresse chicken with salsify and a yellow wine jus. Pastry chef David Boudinet's sweets also make an impression – for instance, the lovely Madagascar 65%-cocoa chocolate dessert with crispy Gavotte biscuits, a fresh herb sorbet and a finely balanced bitter yuzu sauce. The plush decor, further to refurbishments, appeals to newcomers and regulars alike, with its glass partition between the dining area and the kitchen, Art Nouveau touches, art collection and, now, its exposed brickwork.

Name: Maison Wenger
Address: Rue de la Gare 2, Le Noirmont, 2340, Switzerland
Description: In his elegant lair, owner-chef Jérémy Desbraux quietly regales us with satisfying wholesome fare, crafted with textbook precision. Rather than fussy or contrived, everything smacks of crisp, legible regional flavours to the delight of discerning foodies. For example, the appetisers and petits fours use Swiss rice and local honey and the bread is made entirely from flour ground by a local mill. Even the table arts are a nod to the region from a bell jar that pays tribute to Tête de moine cheese to a huge watch case bearing the restaurant’s logo in honour of the local watchmaking tradition. The establishment’s trolleys piled high with refreshing aperitifs, after-dinner drinks and cheeses, which are, of course, produced by artisans, also catch the eye. A warm, professional welcome and a wine list worth writing home about. A word of advice: small groups should book the chef’s table near the kitchen for an extra-special experience.

Name: Mammertsberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The exclusive boutique hotel is just one aspect of this beautiful old establishment boasting a fabulous view all the way to Lake Constance. In the restaurant run by two MICHELIN-starred chefs, Andreas Caminada and Silvio Germann, the latter is behind the creative dishes. He uses the finest ingredients in elaborate but unfussy cuisine, pared down but imbued with real depth of flavour. A rather unassuming name such as "salmon – lettuce" belies a wealth of complexity: premium Lostallo salmon, delicately seasoned and flame-kissed, served with an emulsified buttermilk and lettuce broth, finished with an intense herb oil. In late autumn, be sure to try the house-made tagliatelle with white truffles. Over 1 000 different wines to accompany the fantastic food are stored in the chic, modern wine cellar. The service team is headed up by maître d' Giuseppe Lo Vasco, who is exceedingly attentive, charming and knowledgeable. The decor is an elegant blend of traditional and modern, and the terrace is wonderful. In summer, an aperitif in the garden is an absolute must!

Name: Maralba
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A family business that sums up what it has set out to do here in one punchy phrase: 'Manchego cuisine with glimpses of the Mediterranean'. In the elegant dining area with a glass-walled wine cellar, Albacete-born chef Fran Martínez, with a healthy dose of support from his wife Cristina Díaz, really knows how to showcase the region's cuisine and its produce; he gives his creations modern touches that make them stand out without disguising the peculiar names they bear, such as gachamiga, ajopringue, and mojete. The inclusion in the set menus (Alma and Fran Martínez's Gran Menú) of all kinds of fresh fish, even discarded fish (supplied daily by the fish market in La Vila Joiosa), and the option to add a wine pairing selected by Cristina, who also acts as sommelier and demonstrates extensive knowledge in this field, are all worthy of note. The bread, made by the restaurant itself, is unique and perfectly rounds off the experience!

Name: Marsan par Hélène Darroze
Description: The elegant interior provides the perfect foil to food embodied by the “special something” that depicts the cooking of Hélène Darroze, descended from a family of cooks. Namely, the ability to scour her homeland of southwest France for ingredients that nurture her culinary inspiration, paired with an unmistakable flair for artistic plating: Landes foie gras, roasted with sesame and buckwheat, blue lobster in tandoori spices (a signature dish), armagnac-drenched baba. Her rigour, insatiable curiosity and mixture of talent and intuition hit the spot every time. A stellar success.

Name: Masa
Address: 10 Columbus Circle, Ste. 401, New York, NY, 10019, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: There is nothing like an omakase in the care of Chef Masa Takayama. The commotion of Columbus Circle gives way to the calm, collected ceremony of a room anchored by a strikingly smooth hinoki counter. Everything is in place, as chefs and servers work with a kind of harmony that recalls ballet. Every decision, every move, is in the service of his distinctive style, which many have copied but none have mastered. Fragrant white and black truffles, pearly beads of Osetra caviar, and vibrant garnishes make for brilliant touches that straddle the line between luxury and excess. Few have both the imagination and the know-how to make foie gras nigiri, and few serve abalone so meltingly tender. It is a captivating experience that is singularly memorable.

Name: Meierei Dirk Luther
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elegant, modern setting with a Nordic feel and the magnificent view over Flensburg Firth are exceptionally inviting from the outset. The visual appeal is topped only by Dirk Luther's wonderful set menu. Your anticipation builds as you enter and get a glimpse into the kitchen through the viewing windows. The classically based dishes are well thought out, displaying both depth and finesse, and place top-quality ingredients centre stage – outstanding examples include turbot and lobster from Denmark!
