The set menu is available in six or eight courses; for the six-course format, there are two starters and two main courses to choose from. A vegetarian version can also be arranged with prior notice. Excellent service comes courtesy of sommelier Martin Kammann and his highly attuned, professional and attentive team. The wine recommendations from the superbly curated list are fantastic, backed by thorough and knowledgeable guidance. For those who wish to stay longer in this splendid Baltic Sea location, there is Vitalhotel Alter Meierhof.

Name: Meta
Description: Chef Sun Kim hails from Korea's Busan and his refined modern cooking combines Korean traditions and bold flavours with minimalist plating. The single tasting menu is dominated by seafood and vegetables, as seen in steamed Jeju abalone with gochujang seaweed risotto – the tender mollusc, creamy rice and crunchy lily bulbs feature contrasting textures. In addition to wine pairing, the non-alcoholic Korean drink flight is also worth trying.

Name: Mezzaluna
Address: 65F, Tower Club at Lebua, 1055 Silom Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: A talented Japanese chef reimagines French cuisine through the lens of his heritage, applying classic techniques from both traditions to top-notch ingredients from Japan, France and specialist producers across Thailand. Subtle Thai flavours weave through the refined, seasonal seven-course menu, where each dish is beautifully composed and full of nuance. Though the panoramic city views are striking, it's the balance of precision and creativity on the plate that makes the biggest impression.

Name: Michel Kayser - Restaurant Alexandre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Between Nîmes and Arles, in grounds planted with hundred-year-old cedars, Michel Kayser does what he does best: cooking from the heart to enhance the ingredient, while harnessing his extensive technical skill in a bid to trigger the emotions of good food lovers. There are few chefs who celebrate the Mediterranean with such precision, aplomb or enthusiasm: red mullet grilled under a salamander, ravioles with a tapenade of French olives (picholines), jus of roasted fish bones; Camargue Angus beef seasoned with fragrant marrow bone, a composition of umbellifers jazzed up with anchovies and a ‘Land of Camargue’ sauce. All the side dishes and other edible delicacies (like the bread made with red mullet scales – just the ticket to joyfully mop up the big-boned jus in the fashion of a bouillabaisse rouille) are specifically designed to underscore and enhance the main ingredient (which is used from top to tail, like chaud-froid quail). Utterly free of gadgets and gimmicks, everything tastes of something in this establishment devoted to flavour.

Name: Midsummer House
Address: Midsummer Common, Cambridge, CB4 1HA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In an idyllic location overlooking Midsummer Common, inside an equally beautiful Victorian house, you'll find this stylish, long-standing restaurant. Over 20 years into its lifetime, the dishes are continually evolving thanks to a kitchen which is not afraid to push the boundaries. Every course is packed full of personality and originality, especially the standout desserts like delicious lychee parfait with Jerusalem artichoke yoghurt, preserved rose and matcha tea. Luxury ingredients are generously used, flavours are measured and there’s an appealing range of different textures.

Name: Milka
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from the Austrian and Italian borders, overlooking a crystal-clear lake surrounded by mountains, Milka represents a magnificent gastronomic synthesis of the territory, interpreted with sensitivity and mastery by Chef David Žefran. His cuisine is built on local ingredients used in their entirety. The surprise menu unfolds naturally, marked by the rhythm of the seasons, while the kitchen brigade actively participates in service, presenting each course with detailed and passionate explanations. The culinary proposal is modern and creative yet doesn’t forgo intense and satisfying flavors, as in the spelt with Tolminc cheese cream, snails, and wild garlic, a dish that perfectly captures the bond between territory, technique, and taste. The desserts also merit special mention: they alternate delicate, fresh notes, such as Pearls of tomato water, basil, and sour milk, with more indulgent, enveloping creations, such as warm doughnuts with pork fat, hazelnuts, and apples. The wine list is a pleasure for enthusiasts: extensive and carefully curated, it reflects direct collaboration with numerous winemakers connected to the restaurant, eager to showcase their wines in a context of absolute prestige. For those wishing to extend the experience, refined hotel rooms are available.

Name: Miramar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This wonderful restaurant is the professional epicentre of chef Paco Pérez, who has proved unstoppable in taking his culinary concept from this small town out into the demanding international arena. His wife, Montse Serra, has played a key role in his career, working with him to take over this family inn overlooking the bay. After a major overhaul, it has become a renowned fine-dining hotspot and the perfect place to discover 21st-century Mediterranean cuisine, with the added bonus of a handful of guest suites.The concise à la carte features innovative dishes (half-plates are also available) that showcase his famous ‘surf and turf’ concept alongside two superb tasting menus: MAR, dedicated to the raw ingredients of the Mar d'Amunt, with its seaweed and some little-known products, as well as Memoria, Territorio y Cultura, more focused on the cuisine of the Empordà. They have a bakery where they sell freshly baked bread, pastries, jams, and even garums!

Name: Mitou
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: At Mitou, the prowess and ingenuity of chef duo Young-woon Kwon and Bo-mi Kim are showcased through authentic Japanese cuisine prepared with fresh, seasonal ingredients. Chicken, eggs, rice, and vegetables are carefully sourced from Chef Kwon’s family farm, ensuring consistent quality. A culmination of such painstaking effort, the dishes reflect the chefs’ shared values of sincerity, restraint, and dedication, shaped by their ongoing pursuit of culinary craft. It thus comes as no surprise that diners eagerly look forward to Mitou’s evolving menu every season.

Name: Miyamoto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: The crockery forms an essential part of the cuisine of Miyamoto. From a collection years in the making, each item is carefully selected to complement the item served on it. The arrangements remain simple to let this harmony shine, and there is a refreshing honesty in the chef’s unstinting use of ingredients. He honours the customs of Japanese cuisine yet cooks unbound by theory; he aspires to run a restaurant where he freely creates what is simply delicious. House-made udon is prepared according to the season. The purity of white rice cleanses the soul.

Name: Mizue
Address: 2F, Capella, 139 Dunhua North Road, Songshan District, Taipei, 105021, Taiwan Region
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Hinoki wood features prominently in this serene room, from the counter to the shelves and ceiling panels. Working under a mentor, Chef Katsunori learned his craft in Kanazawa, which explains the appearance of rare finds such as amaebi or koubako crab from that city in his 10-plus-course tasting menu. Exact items vary with the seasons but always include intricate sushi and refined cooked dishes made with ingredients from Kyoto and Shizuoka, Japan.

Name: Molino de Urdániz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The last thing you expect in an old stone mansion such as this, which has witnessed the passing through of pilgrims heading to Santiago de Compostela along the Way of St James over the centuries, is innovative cuisine that is well worth a break in your journey. Its interior is both rustic and contemporary in style, with two separate sections: the informal dining space at the entrance (Origen restaurant), where the only option is an affordable traditional menu, and the more refined gourmet dining room upstairs (with just three tables) where you can eat while watching the chefs at work. Chef David Yárnoz prepares sincere, creative cuisine that is highly appealing in terms of both its presentation and flavour, and always showcases the outstanding ingredients found in the Navarra region (pork from Lekunberri, vegetables from Tudela, trout from the Baztan area, game from de Errea, eggs from the Iza valley etc) and a strong commitment to the local region. This is demonstrated on a single surprise menu (Clásicos & Evolución) featuring the restaurant’s signature dishes, such as the legendary paprika candy with a Chistorra mousse, alongside its more recent creations.

Name: Molino de Urdániz
Address: GF, Hotel MVSA, 61, Section 1, Jianguo North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 10491, Taiwan Region
Description: Warm lighting, a stone wall and a wine cellar provide an elegant setting for a score inspired by Spanish landscapes and depicted by artful plating. The seafood-focused tasting menu blends Spanish culinary traditions with modern techniques, creating varied textures and layered flavours while preserving natural freshness. The signature “Molino”, drawn on the backyard of the original Spanish restaurant, transforms oyster, cucumber and herbs into a light, layered dish presented in vibrant shades of green.

Name: Mont Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant with a gastro-bar ambience that is becoming a must for every foodie in Barcelona. In this delightful setting featuring elegant decorative detail, you’ll find an array of traditional and contemporary dishes, all of which showcase high levels of technique, plus presentation that is so refined that it is hard not to take a photo! In keeping with the philosophy of the owners, who hail from the small village of Mont (in the Val d’Aran), the cuisine here is based around fresh, seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. The à la carte (you have to order a minimum of three snacks and two main courses) features inventive snacks, innovative tapas, and small sharing plates, always accompanied by impeccable and attentive service. We particularly enjoyed the superb seasonal suggestions (morel mushrooms, Reixago cheese and pork cheek, peas with vanilla, clams and hazelnuts, etc) but there are also dishes available all year round that are a must, such as the spectacular Iberian sobrasada mochi with Mahón cheese. For a more complete experience, try their Classic and Mont set menus!

Name: Mosu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Mosu delivers imagination, precision, and balance on each plate. Unpredictable flavours and intriguing textures create constant delight. Signature dishes like abalone taco, sesame tofu, and burdock tarte are deeply satisfying, the sourdough is especially delightful, and the fish dish is elegantly composed. Each floor of the restaurant provides a distinct ambience: the first offers a view of the passionate chefs at work; the second, a romantic sunset view. The attentive service and thoughtful wine pairing further add to the unforgettable dining experience.

Name: Mraz & Sohn
Description: A true institution on Vienna's fine-dining scene. Expect the unexpected: Markus Mraz and his son Lukas's menu is based on a surprise concept – only the ingredients are revealed in advance. The experience unfolds over 13 small, distinctive courses, far removed from the mainstream and typically centred on a single star ingredient, which forms the basis of the menu. A memorable example is the "kimchi börek", in which aromatic sika venison meets vibrant, tangy kimchi, elevated by fine shavings of Périgord truffle. The setting is chic, modern and relaxed. At the chef's table by the open kitchen, diners find themselves right in the middle of the action. Service is charming, attentive, and highly professional – with special credit to the sommelier, who maintains a terrific cellar and provides imaginative, beautifully balanced wine pairings. The terrace in the courtyard is another delightful bonus.

Name: Mudan
Address: 17, Lane 52, Siwei Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan Region
Description: When it comes to tempura, precision is the name of the game. With decades of experience in Japanese cooking, the head chef brings out the best in every ingredient with his keen sense for oil blend, oil temperature and batter consistency, sealing in the umami with an incredibly thin, crisp and light batter. The simple, cosy room is decorated with Japanese garden details. Reservations are mandatory, with only two sittings, at 12.30pm and 6.30pm.

Name: Mugaritz
Address: Aldura Aldea 20 - Otzazulueta Baserria, Errenteria, 20100, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Mugaritz is much more than a restaurant, offering food enthusiasts a very different dining experience. Here, absolutely everything is questioned, hence the focus on both individual and general tastes to the extent that, in the words of the chef, ‘the experience is as much playful as it is gastronomic.’The intentions of Andoni Luis Aduriz, who likes nothing more than breaking the rules, can be seen in a small glossary placed on your table, detailing terms defined by the chef, his staff and even his customers in a cooperative endeavour to add meaning to the dining experience. Dishes, many of which are eaten directly with the hands, do not follow a classic order and constantly aim to transcend borders through a single tasting menu. One particularly outstanding dish is called ‘Podredumbre noble’ (Noble Rot): a delicate and very flavourful cheese flan that’s presented as if it were mouldy on the outside, but has a soft, creamy interior with pleasant hints of blue cheese.

Name: Muromachi Yui
Description: Omakase dishes reflect the turning of the seasons; hassun platters convey the month’s events and customs. Dedicated to fresh-from-the-kitchen deliciousness, white rice is served the moment it’s cooked. A generous assortment of accompaniments, such as dried mullet roe, dried baby sardines with pickled plum and savoury seaweed paste, brings joy. ‘Yui’ is short for ‘yuiitsu-muni’, or ‘one and only’. Unique cuisine and unmatched décor captivate diners.

Name: Mère Brazier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking
Description: Eugénie Brazier (1895-1977), an exceptional chef who pioneered lyonnaise cuisine, was the first person to obtain six stars, three each in two different restaurants. It is in her Lyon establishment on rue Royale that Mathieu Viannay rolls out his version of the Brazier "myth". In a classy hybrid decor, 1930s stained glass windows and mouldings are blended with Saarinen Tulip chairs (a bold design move!) as the chef pays a vibrant tribute to past iconic dishes (artichoke and foie gras, Bresse chicken with truffles, crispy pike bread), infusing them with his talent and novel ideas. Be sure to try the lunch menu, which is excellent value for money. When it comes to desserts, the mind-blowing Grand Marnier soufflé, a house specialty, is available in different versions depending on the season or the chef’s whims.

Name: Mélisse
Address: 1104 Wilshire Blvd., Santa Monica, CA, 90401, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Since opening in 1999, Chef Josiah Citrin’s flagship has been a Santa Monica mainstay. Through its many evolutions, the restaurant has sought to offer a certain kind of fine dining experience that will never go out of style. Slip in through a discreet side entrance to enter the enclosed space that combines a vibe-y underground feel with classic luxury. One can expect the finest cutlery and plates, gorgeous presentations, plenty of tableside saucing, and a level of French decadence that borders on gratuitous. The results are indulgent. Truffles, wagyu, uni, and crab weave their way across intricate canapés and courses, ending with a signature finale of dry-aged duck “Rouennaise” that features a rich sauce made with the help of an antique silver press.

Name: Mühle
Description: Owner Marius Tröndle has a decidedly ambitious man at the helm in Fabian Obergfell. The chef delivers modern cuisine, cooking with great sensibility, finesse and consummate precision. Often he pares back his dishes to just a handful of components, and the result is a wonderfully harmonious balance of flavours – one highlight is the superbly roasted calf sweetbread with a crunchy, paper-thin crust and a creamy, melt-in-the-mouth centre, served on a vin jaune sauce with pointed cabbage and garnished with pickled grape halves and crispy pointed cabbage leaves as chips. The hors-d'œuvres whet the appetite for the seven-course set menu, which is accompanied by well-curated drinks pairings, including wine or alcohol-free options, some of his own creation. The service is pleasant and professional, the interior tastefully done out and truly cosy. The staff address diners informally, which also contributes to the relaxed atmosphere. Overnight guests are accommodated in very pretty guestrooms in this charming house dating from 1603 and served a superb breakfast, which you order the evening before. Top tip: the eggs benedict.

Name: NARA NIKON
Description: ‘Nikon’, meaning ‘live to the full in this moment’, was the principle advocated by Zen master Dogen Zenji (1200–1253). Every day in his kitchen the chef displays the sincere devotion to Japanese cuisine he has had ever since he began at the bottom of the ladder. He focuses above all on the right timing for handling his ingredients: when to prep, when to slice, and so on. Serving at just the right temperature is vital as well. This craftsman’s spirit of applying every ounce of effort in the present moment is reflected in the name of the restaurant.

Name: NARISAWA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Narisawa celebrates the culture of Japan’s ‘satoyama’, rural hillscapes, through the genre of ‘innovative satoyama cuisine’. The Japanese islands form a long arc from north to south, and most of the land is satoyama. In this geographical backdrop from foothills to plains, people have found ways to live harmoniously and sustainably with nature. This image of the satoyama informs the imagination of Narisawa’s cuisine. The restaurant uses traditional craftworks such as lacquerware and washi paper, harmonising diverse people and culture.

Name: NOBUO
Address: 8 Tai'an Street, Zhongzheng District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: With a Japanese façade and a Scandinavian-inspired interior, NOBUO embodies a combination of purity and simplicity. The single menu centres on seafood, complemented by seasonal local veg and tea. The precise use of modern techniques brings the ingredients’ natural flavours to the fore, resulting in dishes that are clean, mild and layered. The plating is in the same vein and white tableware highlights the harmony between ingredients and sauces. Insightful explanations of each dish enhance the overall experience.

Name: Nishiazabu Sushi Shin
Description: The movements are those of one immersed in the world of nigiri. On the fingertips of the left hand balances a piece of fish; clutched in the right, a fistful of sushi rice; the tip of the forefinger applies wasabi. Pushing, occasionally pulling, and scoring in delicate strokes, the single-edged knife crafts hidden incisions to help flavour soak in and heat travel through. Gracefully flowing motion, fine-tuned through daily practice, is the simplicity that holds countless truths. The spirit of nigirizushi is in capable hands with Shintaro Suzuki.

Name: Noi by Paulo Airaudo
Address: 5F, Four Seasons Hotel, 8 Finance Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chefs Airaudo and Troiano deliver a season-driven set menu that changes every two to three months. The 10+ courses feature a strong seafood slant with ingredients shipped daily from Japan. The signature dish on silky egg custard is infused with Ibérico ham consommé that imparts faint smokiness. The food nods to Italian traditions, but is updated with modern plating and cutting-edge technique. Excellent wine pairings elevate the whole experience.

Name: Nuance
Description: Thierry Theys’ cuisine is the pinnacle of “nuanced”. Despite his youth, he has already made a name for himself on the Belgian fine dining scene and owes his reputation to highly individual recipes. Right from the first bite, he unveils his high-flying precision and technical craftsmanship. Not afraid of challenges, each dish is rich in emotion. For example, he may prepare North Sea crab with finger lime, avocado and a subtle sweet-sour flavoured stem lettuce. He may enhance suckling veal, simply grilled, with a barigoule sauce and a gravy jazzed up by kimchi. This chef knows how to nurture and draw out the distinctive character and tiniest details of outstanding ingredients. Suave, delicate food that suits our modern tastebuds. The mind-blowing experience is further enhanced by a fantastic selection of wines, available by the glass, a decadent range of sweet titbits served with coffee and super slick service. A stylish interior, fantastic wine cellar and marble details set the scene in this exceptional establishment on a permanent quest for excellence.

Name: Numata
Description: The tempura fried by the chef as his heart dictates comes out refined. To bring the flavour of carefully selected ingredients, the main oil of choice is Taihaku sesame oil. The coating is infused with bubbles, giving it a light texture. In a distinctive presentation style, seafood and vegetables that work well together are served in alternating pairs. The final dish is the guest’s choice of tendon, tempura over rice; tencha, tendon steeped in roasted green tea; or tenmusu, onigiri filled with shrimp tempura. The chef does not neglect training the next generation, either, entrusting understudies with running his branch restaurants.

Name: OPUS V
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Shopping and fine dining under one roof? Head to the top floor of fashion retailer engelhorn Mode im Quadrat to investigate. A team headed up by Dominik Paul cooks up modern and creative cuisine. With flavours that range from bold and robust to low-key, subtle and highly elegant, the dishes bowl diners over. Made using excellent ingredients, everything is nicely pared down and wonderfully balanced. The carefully devised wine pairings are also impressive – there are alcohol-free alternatives, too. In the evening, you can choose between three set menus: the six-course "Urban Nature", four-course "Chef's Choice" and a three-course option, which is also served at lunch. All of the above can be supplemented by a few special recommendations such as "beef tartare, caviar, myoga" or "langoustine, shiitake, verjus". The sleek, contemporary interior with a Nordic feel is attractive, and there is an open kitchen. The highlight, of course, is the roof terrace with a view of the city! N.B. The restaurant also has a separate entrance.

Name: Obauer
Description: Restaurant closed.This lovely establishment dating back to the 15C is located in the heart of Werfen, known for its distinctive castle complex. It has been run by the Obauer family for decades and now brothers Karl and Rudolf are in charge. Their classic cuisine draws on modern influences and uses select ingredients, e.g. for dishes such as tur­bot and tip­sy char, toma­toes, peas, wild rasp­ber­ries. Choose between the two set menus or dine à la carte. At lunchtime, there is a moderately priced set menu, including tempting classics such as Wiener schnitzel with Pinzgau veal. Berthold Obauer represents the next generation to lead the friendly and attentive service team, Sommelière Magdalena Gleiss recommends the right wines with charm and profound expertise. The decor is modern and elegant in style, incorporating the historical architecture of the building. There is also a gorgeous terrace to the rear of the property. Overnight guests can look forward to comfortable guestrooms and a delicious breakfast.

Name: Obendorfers Eisvogel
Description: Sebastian Obendorfer has a real talent for delicate, intricate creations with skilfully incorporated details, and his own distinctive style. He carefully combines Japanese and regional elements with classical flavour profiles using ingredients of outstanding quality. The execution is exacting, the presentation highly precise – and the result is beautifully balanced dishes in which the individual components shine in their own right yet work wonderfully together. Take the scallop tartare encased in a wafer-thin avocado pocket and served with a vibrant, fruity and tangy sanbaizu-yuzu broth: freshness and lightness are superbly matched by intensity and umami. The set menu comprises six or seven courses, with optional wine or house-made alcohol-free pairings. The setting is modern and elegant, with the elliptical wine cabinet in the centre of the room providing a striking focal point. Large windows afford views of the rolling hills of the Upper Palatinate countryside – magnificent sunsets included! Service is professional, exceptionally friendly and discreet. Tip: Stay overnight at Hotel Der Birkenhof.

Name: Ocean
Address: Rua Anneliese Pohl - Alporchinhos, Porches, 8400-450, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This is an exceptionally special restaurant, bringing together all the ingredients for an experience that will linger long in the memory. The entrance, flanked by Murano glass, commands attention with its theatrical effect, leading into a dining room decorated in an elegant combination of gold, white and blue tones. The space astonishes with its impressive panoramic windows, offering breathtaking views over the coast and the seemingly endless Atlantic. After years spent travelling the world in search of the culinary traces left by the Portuguese across different continents, Austrian chef Hans Neuner bases his offering on the Essência (the name given to the menu) of Portuguese cuisine, drawing inspiration from dishes that embody local cooking and tradition and reinterpreting them from a more contemporary perspective. The menu features dishes such as the famous Francesinha, made with scarlet prawn, black truffles and chouriço, and piri-piri quail with warm tomato salad. The wine list is truly exceptional!

Name: Octavium
Address: 8F, One Chinachem Central, 22 Des Voeux Road Central, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: The smart minimalist dining room dotted in Italian furniture provides the perfect foil for elegant Italian classics, whose flawless craftsmanship showcases the head chef’s Sicilian roots and premium produce. To experience his culinary vision in all its glory, go for the 6- or 8-course tasting menu that changes regularly to reflect the seasons. The house-made pasta, like red prawn linguine, is simply unmissable!

Name: Odo
Address: 17 W. 20th St., New York, NY, 10011, USA
Description: A serene atmosphere awaits in-the-know diners at this secluded counter, closed off from the cocktail bar in front to foster a mood of intimacy. The service, like the ambience, is warm but unobtrusive, allowing focus to fall on the singular kaiseki menu on offer. Under the assured hand of namesake Chef Hiroki Odo, the cuisine skillfully blends tradition and creative personal touches for a meal that is anything but stuffy. Flavors are both vibrant and precise, with a depth and purity that attests to superbly sourced ingredients and careful preparation. From a refined but subtle soup with seared tilefish and house-made sesame tofu to springy house-made soba noodles with indulgently rich salmon roe, this is cooking that will linger in your memory.

Name: Ogata
Description: Bold, elegant cuisine, stripped down and pure, sets off works by Rosanjin and other artists. Avoiding piling element upon element, Ogata finds creativity in deceptively unsophisticated appearances. Technique is guided by intuition gained from each ingredient or inspired by seasonal expressions. Seasonal aesthetics are manifested through the choice of ingredients, revealing the natural vitality of each.

Name: Oimatsu Hisano
Description: The chef interprets the seasons through kaiseki, adding twists and tricks that make the cuisine his own. To express each season, appetisers are accompanied by leaves collected on hill and dale and a slim strip of paper is inscribed with a seasonal phrase. White rice, cooked in clay pots, is specially selected and treated. Rice grown in serpentinite soil, with its rich mineral content, is seasoned with salt and soy sauce to bring out umami and flavour. In a unique touch, scorched rice is served like a rice cracker. The basics of Japanese cuisine are safely guarded, yet imagination has room to run.

Name: Ois
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Combining tradition and modernity to wonderful effect, Mühltalhof is a lovely place to stay and, above all, to eat extremely good food. Ois has just five tables and a modern design dominated by chic black. Diners can watch as the 12-course set menu is prepared in the kitchen. Chef-owner Philip Rachinger pares his cooking back to the essentials, skilfully handling intense flavours. His abundant creativity is matched by a fine sense of balance and finesse. This is beautifully illustrated by a succulent pike-perch fillet grilled over binchotan for intense roasted notes, and served with lightly dried tomato, artichoke in various textures and fermented plum in a foamed broth. Service is excellent, not least thanks to the outstanding sommelier, whose charming, relaxed yet professional approach extends to recommending some very interesting wine pairings. The wine selection is first-rate. Alternatively, the second restaurant serves a four-course Carte Blanche menu.

Name: Opheem
Address: 48 Summer Row, Birmingham, B3 1JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Locally born and bred chef-owner Aktar Islam has fashioned a wonderful dining experience at this ever-developing restaurant. A spacious bar and sitting room are cleverly used as a space in which to enjoy snacks and a drink before heading to the dining room and its open kitchen. The series of flavoursome, excellently spiced and carefully balanced dishes are creative, modern takes on Indian recipes – such as the Lucknow-inspired 'Gajar' that showcases the extraordinary diversity of the humble carrot. Well-chosen wines from the excellent sommelier are on-hand to accompany.

Name: Ophelia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Elegance and sophistication permeate every inch of the fine dining restaurant of the Hotel Riva. It begins with the aperitif in the inviting lounge (also ideal for a digestif or coffee) and continues in the elegant restaurant. In the pretty Jugendstil villa dating back to 1909, Dirk Hoberg turns heads with his fantastic haute cuisine that is rooted in the classics. In the tasting menu, top-quality ingredients are combined in an extremely delicate and thoughtful way and finished with wonderful French-inspired sauces – the zander poached in oil on fresh Swiss chard and nut butter hollandaise is particularly exquisite. The chefs serve one or two of the courses themselves. The extensive wine list is excellent, featuring a particularly good selection of regional labels and sparkling wines, and the sommelier's recommendations are spot on. Tip: Book the "Kitchen Table" right by the pass to the open kitchen. Up to four diners can sit here with a clear view of the chefs at work. The terrace with a view of Lake Constance is also wonderful. And you might want to take advantage of the beautiful location for a walk along the waterfront promenade – the perfect way to soak up the lakeside atmosphere!

Name: Orfali Bros
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Three Syrian brothers run this ever-popular restaurant, now refreshed with elegant wood panelling and designer furnishings, while retaining its signature two-storey open kitchen and pastry workshop. Dining has evolved into tasting menus: the shorter OG highlights signature creations, while Voyage 2.0 reflects the brothers’ travels through dishes rooted in Syrian, Turkish and Armenian flavours, such as sea scallop with OB hot sauce, tamari and wagyu coppa. Thoughtful non-alcoholic pairings complete the experience.

Name: Oriole
Address: 661 W. Walnut St., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Guests enter this former warehouse through a converted freight elevator, a testament to Oriole’s unique brand of elegance, further exemplified by the striking ceiling collage above the spotless open kitchen. Chef Noah Sandoval and team execute a thoughtful tasting menu that blends French and Japanese elements. Small bites in the impressive bar are accompanied by a welcome drink and might include razor clam with ginger and sea buckthorn. Hudson valley foie gras with California fig, pink peppercorn and anise hyssop is served overlooking the impressive open kitchen watching the kitchen team in full flow. The capellini with black truffle is a highlight and a great lesson in culinary self-restraint. Service is polished, detailed and discreet.

Name: Oro
Address: Avenida General San Martin 889, Rio de Janeiro, 22441-015, Brazil
Description: One of those restaurants that every food-lover should get to know! The rapport formed between chef Felipe Bronze and sommelier Cecilia Aldaz works wonderfully well as can be witnessed in every single detail. In this charming and elegant restaurant one block from Leblon beach, the cuisine is a fusion of Brazilian roots and cutting-edge technique. This is reflected in the Afetividade and Criatividade menus (with two and four main courses, respectively) which pay homage to the different regions of Brazil. At the counter in front of the kitchen, with seats for just four guests, you can appreciate the synchronised movement of the chefs at work and their preparation of dishes on the grill – the restaurant’s core element. What impressed us first and foremost was the creativity of the starters, including the superb oysters with a guava “granizado” and a light touch of Biguinho chilli pepper, and the selection of appetisers to eat with your hands, some of which are crunchy, some Brazilian, and others inspired by Japanese cuisine.

Name: Oryori Hanagaki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: This house, surrounded by bamboo, welcomes only one party per day. The refined gate, elegant room and tasteful garden are all the work of the proprietor. Devotion is paid to every aspect of cuisine and service in the spirit that each meal is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter. Meals incorporate seasonal flavours from across Japan. To convey the proprietor’s feelings for the food directly, ingredients are brought to the table and sometimes even prepared before guests’ eyes. Western ingredients are also used, charming diners with creativity beyond Japanese cuisine.

Name: Oswald's Gourmetstube
Description: The culinary centrepiece at Hotel Oswald! This elegant fine dining restaurant is situated in the basement of the Landromantik Wellnesshotel Oswald located in Kaikenried, a Bavarian Forest village with a population of some 550 people. Thomas Gerber has been chef here since 2014, after holding a number of positions in renowned kitchens. His modern-inspired set menu comprises four to eight courses; classic in their foundations, the dishes are crafted with the utmost precision. The wonderfully fresh, perfectly glazed John Dory is a prime example of the subtlety with which he showcases top ingredients – covered with plenty of sliced Périgord truffle, the fish is accompanied by a light and airy celeriac purée and an intense Madeira sauce with a fine, perfectly harmonious sweetness. Choose a bottle from the nicely curated wine list and enjoy attentive, ultra-friendly service.

Name: Otagi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The shop stands in Takagamine, a hilly area in northern Kyoto. Out of affection for the land where he was born and raised, the chef makes a point of using the region’s produce. Vegetables come from a nearby field cultivated by an old friend. The juiciness of freshly harvested foods and the aroma of the good earth leap from every dish. The meal ends with white rice with one of a variety of toppings, such as raw egg and soy sauce, cooked egg, or hashed beef. Enjoyable and satisfying right to the very end.

Name: Ox & Klee
Description: "The Art of Taste" is the name of Daniel Gottschlich's new concept. In a six-course set menu, he creatively combines the tastes "salty", "sweet", "bitter", "fatty", "sour" and "umami", which are introduced in a "black box" with six small amuse-bouches served beforehand. This is imaginative cuisine that draws on regional specialities such as Halve Hahn (traditional Rhenish fare comprising rye bread and cheese). Another highlight is the "Mackerel" dish, inspired by Caesar salad and featuring a combination of tender yellowtail mackerel, sturgeon caviar, a tangy Reypenaer cheese cream, dots of fruity calamansi gel, and bread crisps with anchovy powder, served with a fresh and creamy salad dressing. The menu is also available in the form of the "Kitchen Experience" with a tour of the kitchen. Both menus have their vegetarian counterpart. On request, "Chef's Signatures" can be added as an upgrade, along with wine and alcohol-free drinks. Cool location in the middle Kranhaus 1 building, industrial architecture, a harbour view, plus great design. The laid-back atmosphere is typical of Cologne – lively chatter and lots of laughter. Charming and relaxed service.

Name: PAZ
Address: Doktara Jakobsens gøta 18, Faroe Islands, Tórshavn, 100, Denmark
Description: Having returned from Greenland, celebrated local chef Poul Andrias Ziska settled into his own restaurant in an unassuming Faroese hotel. Ring the bell at reception to initiate an immersive and memorable experience where the talented team deliver a series of spectacularly crafted dishes formed around produce from the surrounding land and sea, which pay homage to local traditions with outstanding reinterpretations of local recipes. The wine and non-alcoholic drinks pairings are a perfect match for refined dishes that are filled with personality, such as cod on cabbage mousseline with seaweed ‘tare’.

Name: PRISMA
Description: Standing alone in his kitchen, Tomofumi Saito engages with Italian cuisine in earnest. His attention to detail is relentless, from the cuisine itself to the music, flowers and other elements. Seating is limited to ensure each dish gets his undivided attention. When he creates new menu items, there are no prototypes: he pushes himself hard to create inventive cuisine found nowhere else. 'Prisma' means 'prism' in Italian and the high standards Saito demands of himself shine in a rainbow of culinary inventiveness.

Name: PUR
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The picturesque location on the Obersalzberg, at around 1 000m above sea level, affords a fantastic mountain panorama for diners to take in. But the fine dining restaurant of the luxurious Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden has plenty more to offer than the view. First, the chic interior with its elegantly pared-down and modern design draws on a colour palette of soothing dark tones. Then there are the culinary creations of Ulrich Heimann. His cooking is modern European in style, regionally influenced and shaped by high-quality ingredients from the Alpine region. The tasting menu consists of five or seven courses; a vegetarian version is also available. Service is very friendly and obliging. Tip: If you would like a little more privacy but still want to be in the thick of things, ask for "The Box" when booking. On fine summer days, the wonderful terrace is naturally a popular spot.

Name: Paco Roncero
Description: Displaying an elegant avant-garde aesthetic, this is a truly unique space... on the top floor of a nineteenth-century building!Here, where there is also a spectacular terrace, you can enjoy a culinary experience in the form of four menus, all with wine pairing options: Esencia laborables (available Thursday and Friday at lunchtime), Esencia (evenings and Saturdays, with the possibility of adding further dishes), the so-called Madrid, Madrid, Madrid and, finally, the so-called Gran Madrid. Chef Paco Roncero, who has an unwavering enthusiasm for olive oil, demonstrates his full creativity in his starters (his Filipino of foie gras with white chocolate is particularly noteworthy), and focuses his menu on more traditional cuisine, paying homage to the Spanish capital's bars (we loved his version of the calamari sandwich). The sweet finish, with a series of chocolates dedicated to the different neighbourhoods of Madrid, is a fun and surprising twist!

Name: Palace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Take in magical views over the harbour from the 10th floor of this modernist building, constructed in 1952 for the Olympic Games. Beautifully delicate modern dishes feature on a multi-course tasting menu packed with well-balanced flavours. These are presented both by the chefs and the top-notch serving team.

Name: Patrick Guilbaud
Address: The Merrion Hotel, 21 Upper Merrion Street, Dublin City, D02 KF79, Ireland
Description: This iconic restaurant has been thriving since 1981, thanks to both the eponymous restaurateur and the exceptional team he has around him. It sits hidden away within a Georgian townhouse and oozes sumptuousness and sophistication thanks to features such as a gilt barrel ceiling and hand-crafted marquetry. The accomplished cooking isn’t to be upstaged, however: it is French at heart yet has a restrained modernity and showcases some bold yet superbly balanced flavours. The Irish ingredients are certainly luxurious and the baba flambé with your choice of rum provides an inviting, classical way to finish.

Name: Paul Bocuse
Address: 40 rue de la Plage, Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or, 69660, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Paul Bocuse’s legend is as vibrant as ever. The “cook of the century”, as gifted in the kitchen as in business and an example for so many of today’s international stars of gastronomy, was no doubt the first modern chef. Faithful to this spirit, the high-flying kitchen brigade (two chefs and a maitre d’, all MOFs, and a world champion of iced desserts) endeavours to uphold this legacy, whilst anchoring the establishment firmly in the present. The master’s recipes have thus been lovingly and painstakingly reworked with a focus on seasonal creations in an updated menu. The performance staged in the dining room is equally dramatic, courtesy of tableside carving and flambées carried out with textbook precision, illustrated by a Dombes duckling served in two courses, lacquered with citrus fruits and flambeed. The decadent dessert trolley is both modern and wickedly addictive. At Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or, the story has far from reached its conclusion.

Name: Pepe Vieira
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: It is a miracle to find a restaurant of this standard in the middle of the countryside, but Pepe Vieira bucks this trend! In this spectacular restaurant surrounded by woods, gardens and pleasant terraces, chef Xosé T. Cannas takes a bold approach to everything, exploring new recipes and ingredients from elsewhere which he combines with superb local ingredients (particularly from the sea) on tasting menus (Romasanta, O Señor de Andrade and A Santa Elección) that take guests on a journey back to the roots of Galician cuisine which is described here as the “la última cociña do mundo”! Sustainability is the backbone of the experience, which begins with aperitifs in the garden before exploring the building’s different spaces and then moving to the dining room, which opens out onto nature via huge picture windows. A dish? The red mullet (citrus-infused stew with a creamy pine nut sauce) is absolutely delicious. Guests have the additional option of 14 individual cube-style bedrooms with an unexpected cutting-edge design that enables guests to experience their natural surroundings to the full.

Name: Piazzetta Milù
Address: Corso Alcide De Gasperi 23, Castellammare di Stabia, 80053, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: It would be impossible to describe this venue without beginning with the welcome, the authentic hallmark of the Izzo family: a warmth and attentiveness that transforms every visit into a memorable experience. Leading the gastronomic proposal is Maicol, who expresses his vision through a seasonal and surprise tasting menu in constant evolution: the number and sequence of dishes remain unknown, leaving space for a free narrative constructed in the moment.The experience unfolds across several different rooms in a dynamic itinerary that may vary throughout the year: it often begins in the kitchen, before moving to the evocative historic cellar, surrounded by bottles from around the world, where each guest has their own private table, and concluding in the dining room, with possible further interludes beside the chef.The cuisine fuses technique and creativity to remarkable effect, as in the tagliolini with cardoncelli mushrooms, butter and aged Parmigiano, finished with white truffle and accompanied by a curious “fake crumb” fashioned from the same mushroom. The experience is orchestrated with precision by Emanuele and Valerio in the dining room, while the cellar – broad and carefully selected – helps make the experience even more immersive. The portions, well judged in size, allow guests to navigate the entire journey with ease, arriving at the close entirely satisfied.

Name: Pic Beau-Rivage Palace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: After nearly a year's refurbishment, French chef Anne-Sophie Pic's luxurious Lausanne establishment now welcomes diners in an elegant and modern leather-clad interior overlooking the lake. This exquisite new setting is a perfect match for the light, expressive and almost ethereal creations of chef Jordan Theurillat. Once past the entrance to the restaurant, there is a table-bar where excellent mocktails and a lineup of appetisers are prepared, drawing on produce from the garden in particular. Dishes such as the ‘venison chop marinated and smoked with juniper berry and imperator root, flanked by end-of-summer tomato confit with mace’ are emblematic of this refined and daring vision of cuisine, paired with a strong regional slant. The evening menu comes in 7 or 8 courses, while the lunchtime menu features a choice of 4 or 5 courses – truffles can be added to all the dishes. A tip: the wasabi-flavoured mocktail is an excellent way to kick off your meal. Impeccable service.

Name: Pietsch
Description: An interesting modern dining concept. Guests arrive at 7pm, with service starting at 7.15pm. There is a single seven-course set menu (plus a starter and finale), with an international outlook, numerous Asian influences and clear, intense flavours. The excellent desserts also deserve a mention, such as a black garlic and dark chocolate mousse with roasted pecan, ice cream made from grilled banana and a fruity bergamot sauce with pandan oil – a beautifully balanced combination full of nuanced flavours and pleasing contrasts. Diners are seated at an 18-seat counter facing the open kitchen, giving them a clear view of the chefs at work. This is teamwork at its finest, with palpable enthusiasm from everyone involved, which creates a sociable, entertaining atmosphere that aligns with the trendy urban aesthetic. As well as fine wines, the expertly crafted alcohol-free beverage pairings are highly recommended! Zeitwerk, another restaurant by Robin Pietsch, is right next door.

Name: Pujol
Description: Chef/owner Enrique Olvera’s seminal dining room has long stood as one of the country’s most famous addresses. This breezy, contemporary space is a constant hive of activity, thanks to servers dressed in sharp, black suits and a crowd eager to dine here. Some come for the taco omakase, but the culinary heart of this restaurant lies in the seasonal tasting menu. Tradition and invention go hand-in-hand in the likes of scallop ceviche with egg salad or grilled Baja coast rockfish with butternut squash puree and sherry foam. The savory progression culminates with mole madre, an effort like no other that celebrates Mexican history and cuisine in the most profound way. The wine list features an impressive number of regional vintners, some of whom bottle exclusively for the restaurant.

Name: Py-r
Address: 19 descente de la Halle-aux-Poissons, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: Pierre Lambinon is nothing if not wholehearted! In this restaurant just a stone's throw from the Pont Neuf, he is making waves with his cooking. The meal begins with a festival of appetisers, bringing a foretaste of the flavours that will define the meal. The chef is at his most inspired when it comes to deftly preparing dishes based on herbs from the garden, fish and seafood and fine seasonal vegetables – intoxicating seafood aromas, grilled notes and the bitter overtones of vegetables. For example, line-caught hake from Saint-Jean-de-Luz and Pyrenean trout gravlax, broad beans and wild garlic in a big-boned pesto and citrus juice with concentrated honey. It's original, but he pulls it off! The vaulted, predominantly white interior is hung with eye-catching artwork by contemporary artists. The epitome of stylish!

Name: Quintonil
Address: Isaac Newton 55, Polanco, Miguel Hildalgo, 11560, Mexico
Description: This chic dining room from Chef Jorge Vallejo and his wife Alejandra Flores is named for an herb native to Mexico. A discreet facade belies the lively, engaging experience within, with a hip vibe that is anything but stuffy. The stylish cuisine utilizes local products — including a variety of insects, deployed with subtlety and then displayed for effect. These ingredients are combined with interesting techniques, both modern and traditional, while creativity produces unique compositions. The tasting menu shifts with the seasons but may include striking bites like a tartlet of guajillo-glazed mussels paired with a “seafood mole” made with dried scallops. A sense of playfulness and balance is evident in a dessert of coconut sorbet, caviar and plankton oil.

Name: R-Haan
Address: 131 Soi Sukhumvit 53, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: R-Haan celebrates the deep connection between Thailand's cuisine, its people and its culture. Begin with a delicious cocktail in the intimate lounge, then step into the dining room, where Thailand's diverse culinary heritage is showcased. The set menu opens with an elegant amuse-bouche. The main courses navigate between traditional family-style cooking and dishes with inventive modern twists. Highlights include the signature crab roe and yellow chilli dip, served with fresh vegetables and fruits, as well as the iconic tom yam presented in a siphon.

Name: RAUSCH
Address: Reuterweg 57, Frankfurt on the Main, 60323, Germany
Description: Jochim Busch has established RAUSCH on the premises that used to house Gustav, the restaurant in which he made a name for himself with his MICHELIN-starred cuisine. Here, he serves up accessible modern food. The bold dishes are notable for their contrasting flavours, always judiciously pared back, and the ingredients are of excellent quality. This approach is evident, for instance, in the super-fresh and tender raw marinated white prawns accompanied by an aromatic buttermilk emulsion enriched with crisp salted cucumber brunoise and the citrus aromas of grand fir tree. The chef serves up a four- or five-course set menu, with two additional dishes to choose from. From some tables in the chic and minimalist space, the open kitchen is visible. Service is laid-back and attentive, with staff always on hand and attentive yet pleasantly unobtrusive. The well-stocked wine list with a penchant for German and French picks is excellent.

Name: Racine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Here in the heart of Reims, there is definitely something interesting afoot. This small restaurant has a delightfully pared-back and contemporary interior with bay windows looking out onto a charming Japanese garden. The setting is in perfect harmony with the cuisine of Japanese chef Kazuyuki Tanaka. He crafts elegant and creative dishes that are rife with different flavours and influences, using aromatic herbs, vegetables, plants, condiments etc. Each one is a surprise, not only in terms of the exceptional quality of the ingredients (such as the langoustine or lobster) but also by their technical mastery and aesthetic appeal. An excellent wine list, including 250 champagnes.

Name: Ramón Freixa Atelier
Description: Haute cuisine in an exclusive setting? Here you can savour the culinary creations of renowned chef Ramón Freixa, who describes himself as Catalan but with a strong Madrid influence! With this luxurious establishment in the heart of the Salamanca district, the chef has taken a step further by diversifying his offering with two concepts that seek to satisfy different audiences. Atelier, a kind of clandestine speakeasy within the larger Tradición, has guests sit at a single U-shaped table, allowing the chef to come and go from the open kitchen and interact constantly with the customers (only 10 diners). Everything revolves around a single tasting menu called Origen (there is also a vegetarian option: Origen Vegetalia) which, based on truly top-quality produce, masterfully balances tradition and creativity, always serving dishes of the highest technical level. The bread service is particularly noteworthy, a heartfelt tribute to his parents and his roots!

Name: René et Maxime Meilleur
Description: Dad René, son Maxime and now Maxime’s children too, Oscar and Calixte, work hand in hand towards a common goal: shine the spotlight on their mountain terroir as they lovingly craft each ingredient, while seeking inspired new ways to prepare regional delicacies. Cheese, fish from the lake, as well as herbs and berries that René picks daily, are at the core of their “intelligent and legible” score. The entire family pitches in here: mum, daughter, daughter- and son-in-law all play a role too, waiting on tables or in the back office. Finally, should you wish to spend the night, book yourself into the next-door chalet and snuggle up in the exquisitely chic, alpine-styled rooms and suites.

Name: Restaurant 141 by Joachim Jaud
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the renowned Alpenresort Schwarz, this upscale modern restaurant is housed in the historic main building, which dates back to 1694. Joachim Jaud, who hails from nearby Telfs, completed his apprenticeship here before honing his skills at top-flight establishments. Since April 2024, he and his small kitchen team have been serving up a creative, seasonal set menu of five or seven courses. Nuanced and full of character, his cooking is skilfully pared back to the essentials. Classical French cuisine is combined with local and Asian influences to great effect. He uses only top-notch ingredients, which take centre stage in dishes such as scallop with ponzu or pigeon with truffle. The fine selection of wines includes numerous organic labels and a few rare gems. The service is exceptionally friendly, attentive and professional. In case you were wondering, the restaurant takes its name from the resort's street number, 141. Beyond the wonderful food, there is an extensive range of amenities for spa-goers, holidaymakers and golfers.

Name: Restaurant 212
Description: As soon as you step into this quintessential canal house in the centre of Amsterdam, Richard van Oostenbrugge and Thomas Groot draw you into their world. There is something theatrical about the sight of the chefs working meticulously in their open kitchen. There is an enchanting intimacy and luxurious comfort about Restaurant 212. Nothing is left to chance here, and that goes for the attentive service, too. With their inventiveness and classical know-how (those sauces!), both chefs put their own stamp on their creations. An ingredient will undergo the most surprising of transformations, and it all seems to happen with such ease – therein lies the chefs' originality. For example, crispy Jerusalem artichokes are hollowed out and filled with a mixture of spicy Belper Knolle, North Sea grey shrimp, Jerusalem artichoke cream, parsley and a garlic vinaigrette. Its simplicity is what makes it so ingenious! Nothing is overdone, and nothing is lacking. Premium ingredients including the finest local produce take centre stage in well-thought-out creations. The (Dutch) cheese board is outstanding, and there are some irresistible gems for wine lovers. The real stars of this show are the extraordinary produce and the talent of two friends.

Name: Restaurant Allen
Address: E205, 2F, Center field EAST, 231 Teheran-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06142, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: At Restaurant Allen, Chef Hyun-min Suh’s sensibility shines through in contemporary dishes accented with light French touches. The elegant yet comfortable dining room, paired with carefully chosen tableware and views into the orderly kitchen, enhances the experience. The cuisine is delicately constructed around seasonal local ingredients and reinterpreted throughout the year. A sourcing map in the menu highlights the origins and seasonality of the products used. The makgeolli-yeast sourdough, with its crisp crust and balanced acidity, is a standout. Warm, polished service brings the meal to a graceful close.

Name: Restaurant Andrew Fairlie
Address: The Gleneagles Hotel, Auchterarder, PH3 1NF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden away in the depths of the world-famous Gleneagles Hotel, this intimate restaurant has a luxurious classical elegance, courtesy of dark wood walls, clever lighting and colourful food-themed art. The philosophy and spirit of the late Andrew Fairlie live on in refined cooking with a French heart and a Scottish soul. Superb produce, much of it from the kitchen garden, is combined with exemplary classical technique – which is most evident in the outstanding sauces, from a punchy Bordelaise to a glossy lamb jus. The service brilliantly balances formality with friendliness.

Name: Restaurant Le Meurice Alain Ducasse
Address: Le Meurice, 228 rue de Rivoli, Paris, 75001, France
Description: Take an iconic luxury hotel opposite the Jardin des Tuileries and an incredibly gifted chef, Alain Ducasse, then add a sprinkling of luxury à la Versailles (white ceiling adorned with gilding, crystal chandeliers) and – voilà! – you get Le Meurice. This place has not failed to catch the imagination of wealthy foreign patrons, who come to soak up that Parisian je-ne-sais-quoi. The Ducasse brand is cultivated by executive chef Amaury Bouhours: the tasting menus featuring dishes served in small portions are both a tribute to French tradition and a showcase of the chef's creativity. High-profile pastry chef Cédric Grolet creates desserts, images of which do the rounds on social networks.

Name: Restaurant Papilio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: This elegant restaurant done out all in white and with a beautiful high groin-vaulted ceiling is truly chic – you would never guess this space was once the château's stables. In the open kitchen, Jan Knedla and his team prepare a set menu comprising eight or ten courses. Inspired by the chef's childhood, the dishes lean towards regional ingredients and are presented in a modern and creative style. Seats at the Chef's Table promise interesting glimpses of the action. Service is friendly and professional; the chefs mostly serve the dishes themselves and explain the idea behind them. They offer a very well-stocked wine list and the wines are presented charmingly and with profound knowledge. Also recommendable: national or international wine by the glass or the tea experience as a non-alcoholic option. In summer there is a nice terrace.

Name: Restaurant Parkheuvel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in Het Park and boasting a wonderful view of the Meuse River – the terrace is a must – this elegant Art Deco building is the ideal setting in which to be thoroughly spoiled. The spacious restaurant is supremely comfortable, with the open kitchen among its eye-catching features. Here you can watch Erik van Loo at work, a chef with a feel for classic finesse that comes through, for example, in a deeply flavoured sauce based on lobster bisque and enriched with saffron and Pernod, which elevates his well-known combination of Bresse chicken ravioli and langoustines. At Parkheuvel, it is the sauces that really blow diners away. The input of the chef's son Juliën brings even more detail and diversity, as well as a livelier approach to the ingredients. For instance, a dessert of wonderfully ripe cherries comes in various textures – as a compote and a tuile, or marinated in a rich rum-infused coulis – accompanied by a cream and a milkshake, both made with buttermilk and vanilla. The sommelier's expert recommendations and impressive wine collection are definitely the icing on the cake. Parkheuvel continues its tradition of fine dining with passion.

Name: Restaurant Pearl Morissette
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This 42-acre destination in the picturesque Niagara region is the full experience. A restaurant, winery, orchard, farm and bakery, Restaurant Pearl Morissette is a powerhouse. With great pride for Canadian ingredients and respect for the seasons, Chefs Daniel Hadida and Eric Robertson make the most of their surroundings to enhance their spontaneous tasting menu's dishes, as in roasted guinea hen with chanterelles, mokum carrot and fig. Yes, there is plenty of wine available, but don’t miss the accomplished juice pairing either. The meal may conclude sweetly with a deliciously creamy hogweed ice cream sandwich followed by terrific, freshly baked madeleines. Meanwhile, the warm team keeps the tasting moving at a friendly clip.

Name: Restaurant Sat Bains
Address: Lenton Lane, Nottingham, NG7 2SA, United Kingdom
Description: This restaurant has become quite the operation over the years, what with its main dining room, Tasting Room, Kitchen Bench, bedrooms, garden and even its own bees. Sat Bains has an unerring commitment to exceptional produce, both from his own garden and around the British Isles, and puts it to use in dishes that are as punchily flavoured as they are good looking. One course is taken in the greenhouse for a playful touch, while the 'Crossover' dish before dessert has become a brilliant signature. You're guided smoothly through the whole experience by the genial, well-versed service team.

Name: Restaurant Story
Address: 199 Tooley Street, Southwark, London, SE1 2JX, United Kingdom
Description: Story is a restaurant that continues to evolve rather than merely reinvent itself and its latest chapter saw the addition of a second storey which hosts a handsome private dining room. In the bright, open main restaurant, Tom Sellers’ talented kitchen team serve a surprise set menu, where luxurious ingredients – from langoustines to turbot – make up dishes that are as succulent as they are visually arresting; you can also expect updated versions of his signature constructions. The charming service team ensure the atmosphere is always warm and welcoming.

Name: Restaurant de Joël Robuchon
Address: MGM Grand, 3799 S. Las Vegas Blvd., Las Vegas, NV, 89109, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Leave behind the casino cacophony and settle in for a world-class dining experience at this sumptuous enclave on the ground floor of the MGM Grand. Fashioned to evoke an intimate salon with Art Deco panache, the opulent space is deeply carpeted and dressed up in regal aubergine velvet, gilded accents and sparkling crystal. Dinner here is an event; you'll progress through a series of courses driven by contemporary French cuisine and global inspiration, beginning with a tableau of house-baked breads and ending with a chariot of mignardise. Expect creations like crustacean gelée with crabmeat and caviar; crisped daikon with dashi; and roasted venison with red wine-poached pear. The menu is enhanced by an extensive and impressive wine list.

Name: Retiro da Costiña
Address: Avenida de Santiago 12, Santa Comba, 15840, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant that will be a pleasant surprise for guests, both in terms of its passion for hospitality, its use of the very best ingredients, and its small town location. Ably supported by his family, Manuel García strives for culinary excellence through his impressive tasting menu (a tribute to the history of the business which was founded by his grandparents in 1939). This “gastro-sensory” experience, which provides an insight into traditional Galician flavours and ingredients (sea bass, spider crab, locally reared chicken etc) from a creative perspective, evolves in stages in the Champagne “corner” on the ground floor followed by the bakery, the spectacular bodega, and the pleasant dining room on the first floor, before ending in the impressive lounge with its sofas and fireplace for a post-dinner coffee, delicious petits-fours and an extensive choice of spirits. In addition, the delightful design-inspired villas close to the restaurant are modelled on a typical Celtic “castro” settlement in the heart of nature. If you are staying here, don’t miss the stunning breakfast.

Name: Ricard Camarena Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This magnificent place is part of the refurbished Bombas Gens factory, which also houses an arts and culture centre. Here, there is a large foyer with a contemporary feel, a private bar where hors d'oeuvres are served, and the modern dining room at the back, with an open-plan kitchen where you can enjoy a final aperitif.Along with seven other chefs, Ricard Camarena was distinguished/commended with the Cocinero del Año award (Madrid Fusión, 2021) for his "green activism". His is a coherent signature cuisine solidly grounded in homegrown vegetables and a painstaking process of research. His set menus convey a clear commitment to sustainability, as he uses every last leaf of the vegetables to make his sauces or even the occasional beverage.

Name: Rote Wand Chef's Table
Description: Guests are treated to a very special culinary experience here in the exclusive Rote Wand Gourmet Hotel – formerly an inn housed in Zug's historic schoolhouse. After an aperitif and a selection of appetisers in the little parlour downstairs, you proceed upstairs to a chic dining area in which warm wood meets sleek design. Diners are seated on one of the comfortable high stools arranged around a horseshoe-shaped counter. The unique atmosphere owes much to the well-coordinated, charming team and their relaxed, engaging manner. Chef Julian Stieger showcases his distinctive style of cooking: highly modern and fairly complex, yet free of unnecessary frills. He skilfully incorporates familiar, pleasingly accessible flavour profiles, creating comforting dishes of the highest calibre, such as beef goulash with chanterelles and onion, or potato foam with egg yolk and caviar. The dry-aged duck, accompanied by an intensely aromatic, full-flavoured chive sauce, is also wonderful. A vegetarian version of the surprise set menu is available if ordered in advance. There are two sittings, at 4.30pm and 8pm.

Name: Row on 45
Address: 45th Floor, Tower 2, Grosvenor House Hotel, Al Emreef Street, Dubai Marina, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This gastronomic venture comes from acclaimed British chef, Jason Atherton. Its name combines the acronym for its “refinement of work” and its location on the 45th floor of The Grosvenor House. A penthouse-like setting with an open kitchen, this intimate culinary experience seats 22 guests and offers a 17-course tasting menu divided into three acts. The dishes feature fine Japanese ingredients prepared with French techniques, such as amebi and bafun uni. The full menu is sophisticated, refined and immaculately presented, delivering well-judged and complex flavours. If you’re going to opt for the four-seater chef’s table, be sure to book well in advance.

Name: Row on 5
Address: 5 Savile Row, Mayfair, London, W1S 3PB, United Kingdom
Description: The name of Jason Atherton’s flagship operation is short for ‘Refinement of Work’ – and indeed there is a great deal of refinement in every inch of this mightily impressive restaurant. The premises, on the iconic Savile Row, have been fitted out with no-expense-spared luxury, while the service is charming and attentive in equal measure. Chef Spencer Metzger leads the kitchen, taking outstanding British produce and adding depth of flavour with unerring skill – as in the sika deer with a sublime sauce flavoured with red fruit and beetroot. The wine list, as you may expect, is an oenophile's delight.

Name: Rozó
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Diego Delbecq and his pastry chef partner Camille Pailleau have channelled all of their energy and talent into this former printing works, turning it into a loft-style restaurant, with tables set out beneath the vast glass roof and its metal beams. Lovely hardwood floors, light-coloured walls and large kitchens separated by glass panes from the elegant dining area, which has a mezzanine on which hors-d'oeuvres are served with the aperitif during the evening service. The chef cooks up creative, inspired and delicate cuisine that shows a penchant for sauces, tangy and bitter notes, condiments and peppers – plus the obligatory nods to the cuisine of this northern region of France (eg endive, tarte au sucre). And he does so with a striking sense of balance when it comes to flavours. Friendly service.

Name: Ru Yuan
Address: 11 Yuquan Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Ru Yuan stands amid lush vegetation. Though the menu seems to feature familiar dishes like Xihu fish in vinegar sauce or sautéed shrimps with Longjing tea leaves, each one has been extensively fine-tuned and tweaked. The chef’s personal character shines through in the meticulous details. The gold medal braised pork exudes winey aromas; the pork is sliced thinly and shaped into a pagoda for perfect texture and exquisite plating.

Name: Ryuzu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The crown, ‘ryuzu’ in Japanese, is a vital part of a watch. Under the leadership of Ryuta Iizuka, the team moves like clockwork: chefs, patissiers, servers, and the sommelier working in perfect synchrony, like the gears of a precision timepiece. Foodstuffs from the chef’s native Niigata Prefecture, as well as vegetables from the Noto region of Ishikawa Prefecture, reflect the essence of each passing seasons. The passion of food producers is transformed into cuisine by the kitchen and conveyed to guests through graceful service.

Name: Ryō-shō
Description: The chef has made himself a master of old-school Japanese cuisine to take it to the next level. While respecting orthodoxy in wanmono and side dishes, he refers to French flameworking techniques for his grilled items and snacks. Masu salmon is served mi-cuit; beef is rested multiple times during grilling. The sukiya-style interior in a remodelled wooden townhouse is appointed with both antique and modern dishware. ‘Ryosho’ means ‘aspire to the heavens,’ and the sky’s the limit for the chef’s ambition and desire to better himself.

Name: Rùn
Address: 2F, The St. Regis Hotel, 1 Harbour Drive, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Hung has worked in many 5-star hotels and values food quality and shrewd techniques more than anything else. Seasonal ingredients from around the world are painstakingly prepared the traditional way and then plated with modern refinement. Wok-fried crab claw with dried shrimps, spring onion and layered bean curd sheet is exquisitely presented and loaded with umami. The wine and tea sommeliers, as well as the professional service team, make for a pleasant experience.

Name: SENNS.Restaurant
Description: Gusswerk – once a bell foundry – is an impressive location for a restaurant. Details of the old industrial architecture have been skilfully combined with chic, stylish modern furnishings. The centrepiece is the open kitchen, allowing you to watch the team led by Andreas Senn and head chef Christian Geisler at work. The cuisine is presented in the form of "The 5 Senses of Taste", a set menu that abounds with creativity and well-thought-out details, finely balanced textures and bold flavours, from the five savoury appetisers to dishes such as "Chilean sea bass, ajoblanco, tomato, Amalfi lemon", to the five sweet treats served at the end of the meal. It goes without saying that the quality of the ingredients is second to none. The service is top-notch, as are the wine recommendations. Ever wondered what goes on behind the scenes? The "Chef for a Day" programme gives you the opportunity to experience being part of both the kitchen and front-of-house teams for a night. Tip: The adjacent Senns.Bar serves cocktails, wines by the glass and dishes from the menu of the fine dining restaurant à la carte (open Tue-Sat from 6.30pm).

Name: STAY by Yannick Alléno
Address: One&Only The Palm Hotel, West Crescent Road, The Palm Jumeirah, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This elegant, high-ceilinged restaurant is exclusively set at the end of the Palm in a colonial-style property, which is breathtakingly opulent in design, with magical tropical gardens and a private dock. Inside, it’s luxurious without being stuffy, and service follows suit, with a team that are attentive and professional yet relaxed and personable. The cuisine is innovative, creative and intriguing, combining French tradition with modern culinary advances to create à la carte dishes and exclusive menus. The combination of flavours is harmonious, and dishes are cohesive, creating an unforgettable experience.

Name: SUIS
Address: Strucht 77, Schin op Geul, 6305 AH, Netherlands
Description: Ralf Berendsen is a perfectionist, and it shows in every dish that reaches your table, in cooking executed with split-second precision and in the finest details. Drawing on his considerable experience, he elevates familiar flavours with delicate nuances and judicious touches of international seasoning. His cooking is complex yet never convoluted. The sauces are an experience in themselves.For example, he serves Anjou pigeon in its entirety, preparing its intensely flavoured breast and confit legs with pistachio in three forms: crushed, powdered and as an intense cream. Then there is generous truffle-enriched mashed potato, chanterelles in a creamy poultry jus and a pigeon jus that brings even greater depth and dimension to the whole dish – a veritable feast. The chef's classics, available both as a set menu and à la carte, more than live up to the name.Soumia's approach as hostess is every bit as elegant as the overall experience at this chic restaurant. Personable, attentive and in tune with her guests, she sets the tone for the service. Berendsen, too, makes a point of greeting diners on arrival – a personal touch that rounds off an impressive display of culinary craftsmanship.

Name: Saga
Address: 70 Pine St., New York, NY, 10005, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Set atop a landmark Art Deco skyscraper in the Financial District, Saga pairs its dramatic setting with a surprisingly relaxed experience. Sweeping views surround a series of intimate dining rooms, where plush furnishings and polished service never feel overly formal. Chef Charlie Mitchell leads a seasonal tasting menu rooted in French technique, with a particular focus on seafood and vegetables and influences that range well beyond France. Excellent products anchor the experience, and the pastry team brings equal finesse to the closing courses.
