Address: Kuşçular Mahallesi, 8037. Sokak No:3, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ozan and Seray Kumbasar make a formidable team who put their heart and soul into their restaurant. Seray wins hearts with her love for regional wines, presenting them with expertise and surprising us, for instance, with a Chamlija Riesling, 2024, from Baglari. Her digestif trolley is nothing short of outstanding. Her love of the local terroir is shared by her chef husband, and he sources whatever he does not grow himself from nearby producers whenever possible. Every six weeks his set menu changes to keep pace with the seasons. This also fuels his creativity and shapes the direction of his sensual, refined cuisine, which has a strong sense of place.For instance, he cooks prawns to a perfect, still-translucent finish, allowing their delicate flavour to shine through. Okra and baby sweetcorn are grilled over a wood fire to unlock their full intensity, and a silky corn sauce brings these exuberant flavours together with a touch of sweetness. At Vino Locale, ingredients take centre stage in a set menu that strikes the right balance between meat, fish and plant-based foods (a vegetarian set menu is available; lunch is à la carte only). Every so often, subtle details betray his fondness for the cuisines of Italy and Asia – his gyoza are as wonderful as his sauces! The restaurant itself has something of a trattoria feel – the art-covered walls, cheerful atmosphere and romantic terrace make its appeal irresistible. Guaranteed to be a memorable dining experience.

Name: Virtus
Description: A stone's throw from the Marché d'Aligre, the navy-blue façade of this restaurant conceals a vintage interior strewn with Art deco details that is reminiscent of a Parisian apartment and which is the work of Argentinian architect Marcelo Joulia. A talented couple is at the helm: Frédéric Lorimier in the kitchen and Camille Gouyer who graciously supervises the front of house. After honing his talent with the greats (not least Arnaud Donckele in Saint-Tropez), the chef crafts a meticulous, almost surgical score. Think seasonal produce, virtuoso technique and exquisitely aromatic sauces, e.g. line-caught brill meunière, green pea ragout, stuffed morels and a vin jaune-laced sauce made with the peapods, or smoked chicken roasted in savory butter with a wafer-thin tartlet of confit legs, sautéed girolles and a punchy gravy.

Name: Vollmers
Description: Keep an eye out for the small sign hanging above the door of this discreet restaurant on a cobbled Old Town street, otherwise you might walk right on by. From the outside, its whitewashed walls give it something of a residential look, which is matched inside by an elegantly low-key dining room where seven linen-laid tables and comfy chairs set a homely tone. The surprise menu sees texture and acidity used to good effect in creative, sophisticated dishes; some are inspired by the owners’ childhood memories, such as the traditional pork, cabbage and lingonberry, which is elevated into a very personal dish.

Name: Voro
Address: Urbanización Atalaya de Canyamel, Canyamel, 07589, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in a separate building from the Cap Vermell Grand Hotel (two MICHELIN Keys), this restuarant exudes an unmistakable desire to explore global cuisine. And it’s no wonder: its name comes from a Latin term meaning ‘to devour’. In its attractive dining spaces crowned by high ceilings, you can discover the culinary philosophy of chef Álvaro Salazar, a man whose efforts revolve around a single idea: to create cuisine without constraints, with a commitment to the environment and to his Mediterranean roots. They offer a single tasting menu with a modern-creative flair (Devoro) that surprises diners both for the attention to detail and meticulousness of the presentations and with its attempt to tell a story through each dish, featuring nods to his hometown of Linares (Jaén), the island of Mallorca itself, and the Mediterranean Sea. The menu mixes seasonal dishes with some of Voro’s iconic signature classics (Patito 2019, Almendra y Caviar 2022, etc.), structured around three stages inspired by the sun (Dawn, Zenith and Sunset).

Name: Votum
Description: Regional culinary star Benjamin Gallein wows diners with subtly creative cuisine in the form of flavoursome dishes that pack a punch. The restaurant is on Platz der Göttinger Sieben, close to the Leine River. It is housed in the modern extension of the historical Leineschloss, a palace that is also the seat of Lower Saxony's state parliament. The name "Votum" is a reference to the choices to be made by diners: the order of the courses, optional upgrades, and wine pairings (standard or "premium") or alcohol-free alternatives. Their original signature dish, "Lobster, shellfish hollandaise, tarragon", is a real flavour sensation with a sharp, elegant aesthetic. The outstanding quality of the ingredients also shines through, for example, in the perfectly seared scallops or the Wagyu mille-feuille. The "Two Hours – Three Courses" set menu is also an interesting recommendation. Furthermore, this space with a glass façade provides a stylish setting, as does the lovely terrace overlooking the river. Attentive and professional service – the chefs come to your table to talk you through the dishes. V ANDY Bar is a separate concept, to be tried out Wed-Sat from 9pm. Restaurant Schorse im Leineschloss is also part of this food and beverage group.

Name: Vrijmoed
Description: Michaël Vrijmoed is light years from your run-of-the-mill chef. Committed body and soul, he harnesses his phenomenal creativity and extensive technical know-how to the service of fine food, combining pedigree Gallic techniques with traditional fermentation and exotic influences. His stellar reputation is also due to his unabridged passion for vegetables, which comes to the forefront in his vegetarian Purs menu, as he relentlessly coaxes the best out of each ingredient. Should he get his hands on white truffles, he proudly brings them to your table as he plies you with suggestions. You may be tempted by an invigorating yuzu sorbet with Timut and Sichuan pepper, before you tuck into pheasant from the Flemish Ardennes cooked whole and flanked by portobello mushrooms, stewed endives, cranberries, foie gras and celery. A powerful gamy gravy further underscores and heightens all these flavours. Such exuberant, occasionally complex harmonies are fully emblematic of the talent of chef Vrijmoed. You can rely on the sommelier for inspired and sometimes daring tips to enhance your dining experience in this stylish contemporary town house that blends elegance and Art nouveau details.

Name: Widder Restaurant
Description: In the chic fine dining restaurant of the luxurious Widder boutique hotel, chef Stefan Heilemann and his team skilfully bridge the gap between classic and modern, drawing on international influences. Thoughtful preparation and precise technique go into the elegant dishes. The set menu starts as it means to go on, with a veritable explosion of flavours, in the form of light bites such as a fluffy bao bun filled with pulled goulash and amuse-bouches including tender, delicately sweet Algarve prawns with a refined cauliflower foam and crispy frosted herb pearls. The culinary delight continues with the superb langoustine, perfectly cooked to a translucent finish and paired with tom yam, peanut and kaffir lime. Or with the sensational Balfego tuna, served as a delicate tartare. The quality of the ingredients is top notch – and that also applies to the restaurant's own produce. The set menu, as well as its vegetarian counterpart, is available in a four- to six-course format. In addition, you have the chef's recommendations available à la carte. The highly adept waitstaff impress with their pleasingly relaxed approach. Tip: Book the Chef's Table! They also open for lunch Thu-Fri. Widder Bar is one floor below.

Name: William Frachot
Address: Hostellerie du Chapeau Rouge, 5 rue Michelet, Dijon, 21000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This 19C former coaching inn bang in the heart of historic Dijon is the HQ of one of Burgundy’s most talented chefs. A local lad and son of restaurateurs, William Frachot, who is something of a globetrotter (England, Quebec), devises stripped-back dishes in his own image: serious and applied, juggling international flavours and regional produce. He adds just the right dose of inventiveness and energy, illustrated by his new take on eggs meurette and his steadfast commitment to freshwater fish (perch, black bass, pike, zander) depicted by brook trout, zander and river fish soup. Meals are served in a distinctive interior featuring light wood cladding, grape vine motifs and mustard yellow swivel Shark chairs - each design choice is a nod to Burgundy's heritage. Inspired and accomplished cuisine peppered with influences from near and far.

Name: Wing Lei
Address: GF, Wynn Hotel, Rua Cidade de Sintra, NAPE, Macau, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Equally suited to power lunches and friendly get-togethers, this strikingly lavish restaurant dominated by a frosted crystal flying dragon offers far more than just a treat for the eye. Cantonese classics and dim sum crafted with top-notch ingredients are what keep diners coming back. Besides the main menu, ask about their seasonal dishes such as clay pot rice and Dongshan goat in winter. Thoughtful service adds to the experience.

Name: Ying Jee Club
Address: Shop G05, 107-108, GF & 1F, Nexxus Building, 41 Connaught Road Central, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Rather than gimmicky promotions, the owner prefers to devote his energy and resources into sourcing quality ingredients and honing the chefs’ skills. The tasteful, modern room adorned with marble tables, velvet seats and metallic trim primes the diners for Cantonese classics with a delicate twist. Crispy salted chicken is silky and tender; sautéed lobster with sea whelk, water chestnut and crispy conpoy delivers umami and interesting textures.

Name: Ynyshir
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: For a truly unique experience, head for rural Wales and this matt-black house with an immersive approach and a mellow soundtrack. The evening starts early, which gives Chef-Owner Gareth Ward five hours to take diners on a playful culinary journey around the globe. He has a particular reverence for Japanese cuisine, with sashimi and A5 Wagyu beef likely to appear on the surprise menu of around 30 vibrant servings, all using outstanding produce prepared with superb craft. Regional sheepskins and handmade crockery show the team's pride in their Welsh locale, and you can extend your visit in one of the luxurious bedrooms.

Name: Yu Kapo
Address: 9-1 Sanmin Road, Songshan District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: The room sports a minimalist edge courtesy of light wood and slate grey hues. Chef Masa Chung deploys his deft craftsmanship and savvy skills, drawing on a 20-year career in Japanese cooking. He serves a single season-driven kappo menu. Chargrilling is his strong suit, but his uni and shiso tempura, as well as the famous kamameshi course are equally impressive. The meal unfolds like a page-turner, with compelling highlights and breathing spaces.

Name: Yu Zhi Lan
Address: No. 1, 24 Changfa Street, Qingyang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: This low-key private dining concept can dispense with signage. The owner-chef Lan Guijun is a local legend who raised Sichuanese cooking to the level of haute cuisine, so foodies always find their way here. The quaint rustic room is dotted with ceramic art and pottery made by the chef himself. The dishes of the elaborate, multi-course set menus depend on market availability, but you can specify food allergies when booking.

Name: Yugen
Description: Yugen means ‘mysterious profundity’, grace whose depths can never be plumbed. It connotes the depths of Japanese cuisine, a product of constant refinement through the ages. Keisuke Mifune puts on display the skills and instincts he honed at a ryotei. He pays attention to combinations of ingredients and dishware, expressing the changing of the seasons through his menu. A Fukuoka native, the chef furnishes the bounty of Kyushu in the form of seafood from the Genkai Sea and the Goto Islands.

Name: Yun Jing
Address: 70F, Raffles Shenzhen, T7, One Shenzhen Bay, 3008 Zhongxin Road, Nanshan, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
Description: This sky-scraper restaurant, whose name means cloud iridescence, aims to serve novel Cantonese fare against a backdrop of breathtaking 270-degree city and ocean views. Chef Guo strikes a balance between tradition and innovation, crafting a menu that covers all the bases from double-boiled soup and barbecue to poultry and seafood. Try his poached sunflower seed-fed chicken, or spicy sautéed mantis shrimp with basil and golden fried garlic.

Name: Yusokuryori Mankamero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: This long-serving restaurant was built as a general store and traded as a sake dealer before transforming into a ryotei. In continuous operation since its founding three centuries ago, Mankamero has preserved tradition by constantly changing. Heir to the tradition of ‘yusoku ryori’, banquet fare served at imperial court functions, the restaurant carries on the Ikama school of ‘shikibocho’, the ceremonial art of knife handling that unites cookery with etiquette—faithfully preserved to the present day. Seasons are reflected everywhere, from the elegant Kyoto kaiseki to the arrangements, serving vessels and even the leaves and other underlays beneath the food. A taste of history, handed down in unbroken tradition.

Name: akordu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: ‘Akordu’ is Basque for ‘memories’. Chef Hiroshi Kawashima invokes memories from his ingredients, encapsulating messages in his cooking. Each course in the prix fixe meal comes with a card; menu names are akin to story titles. Kawashima interprets the history and cultural topography of Nara through a modern Spanish sensibility cultivated in Basque country. Cuisine bursting with creativity, beautifully prepared and arranged.

Name: alla prima
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: alla prima's natural flavors of the ingredients are preserved, while the balance of herbs and vegetables adds an alluring aroma. The tasting menu is original without being overly complex or intimidating. The wide counter offers the best view of the the kitchen’s lively energy, while the calm, classic ambiance and softly lit dining room ensure that no detail has been overlooked in providing a truly comfortable meal.

Name: a|o|c
Description: Flanked by private members’ clubs, the 17th-century Moltkes Palæ sits in a quiet street close to Amalienborg Palace. Within its vaulted basement sits a|o|c, whose elegant, sophisticated design takes in handcrafted oak and leather chairs, soft designer lighting and a tasteful piano soundtrack. There’s a long bar for snacks, a cosy lounge for petits fours and, as befits a restaurant founded by a sommelier, an impressively stocked glass wine cellar. Finely wrought dishes showcase top-quality ingredients and come with subtle global touches, such as in the razor clam with kosho or scallop with wasabi and tare.

Name: d'Eugénie à Emilie
Address: place de la Résistance 1, Baudour, 7331, Belgium
Description: Éric Fernez inherited his love of cooking from his grand-mother, Eugénie, and he has passed on this passion to his daughter, Émilie. Premium produce, generous classical fare and the added dimension that wine can bring to a dish are the bedrock of this family’s values. Éric, a past master of old school cooking, crafts nostalgic food that reads like a culinary encyclopaedia. You can expect to sample traditional produce, like pigeon, pig’s trotters and sole (à la Fernand Point, no less!), courtesy of almost-forgotten recipes. The sauces are in a class of their own, illustrated by a consommé of beef tail that flanks trout, cooked medium rare, or the gutsy duck gravy that escorts duck breast and an amazing caramelised nougat. The jaw-dropping à la carte lineup of timeless dishes and seasonal set menus reveal the establishment’s desire to bend over backwards to please. This restaurant, in which legacy and intimacy go together like salt and pepper in a contemporary elegant interior, is the perfect place for a slap-up meal with all the trappings of tradition. The chef often pops out to greet and chat with diners, which further adds to the friendly vibe.

Name: daní maison
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: “A casa di Nino” is not merely an evocative name but a promise fulfilled: guests truly do enter the home of chef Di Costanzo, set among the hills of a quiet residential area of the island. Beyond the threshold, a path through the garden – tended with great care and dominated by Mediterranean scrub – captivates with its richness of plants and flowers; it is here, on milder evenings, that aperitifs and after-dinner drinks are enjoyed, in a setting of rare charm. Inside, beneath a typical vaulted ceiling, just a handful of tables ensure an intimate and personal experience, while those wishing to observe the kitchen up close may take a seat facing the stove, watching the chef at work. The dishes are notable for their complexity, technical rigour and inventiveness: the expression of a conceptual cuisine capable of surprising even on a visual level. The cellar merits a visit: interesting and well-stocked, ranging across historic labels and a selection of prestigious sparkling wines, with names such as Ferrari and Dom Pérignon.

Name: dede
Address: Customs House, Baltimore, P81 K291, Ireland
Description: This restaurant is temporarily closed and will reopen on 11th November.Chef Ahmet Dede’s warm, inviting restaurant in this West Cork coastal village is a masterful marriage between his Irish surroundings and his Turkish heritage. Superb local produce is the bedrock of the cooking, enhanced by skilful, judicious spicing which delivers multiple layers of authentic Turkish flavours while never overpowering the core ingredients – as with a refined take on a 'muhallebi' dessert that showcases superb Turkish hazelnuts. The charismatic Dede and his brigade deliver their dishes with pride, while the service team work with a friendly charm.

Name: etz
Description: Felix Schneider and his team take you with them into their very own world. Their responsible concept, consistently implemented, down to the last detail – is clearly reflected in the extraordinary seasonal set menu, which is brimming with their own ideas and a clear sense of purpose. They forage, grow, ferment… everything is made in-house, from the ham and butter to the miso and vinegar. The short tour of the experimental kitchen starts at 6.30pm, after which you will be served numerous courses of creative fare – "omnivore" (fish/meat) or vegetarian – over the course of four to five entertaining hours. Impeccable ingredient quality is evident throughout – from the aromatic, sweet heirloom tomatoes to the super-fresh, ikejime-slaughtered golden trout. And then there is the superb "Brotzeit": house-made charcuterie and fantastic oven-fresh sourdough bread. The excellent wine list is particularly appealing thanks to a remarkable selection of Silvaners from the region. The open kitchen makes for a friendly and relaxed atmosphere, and everything runs seamlessly and professionally. The chefs help serve the food and talk you through the dishes. N.B. The restaurant is tucked away in a courtyard off the street, which is accessed via Kirschgartenstraße 6.

Name: focus ATELIER
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is as exclusive as every other part of the luxurious Park Hotel Vitznau. In their six- or eight-course set menu, Patrick Mahler and his team combine classic, Japanese and Scandinavian elements in exciting and intricate ways. It all begins with fantastic appetisers – the halved oyster in its shell with roasted leek and caviar, for example, is delicious. Technically flawless preparation and a judicious, harmonious combination of ingredients underpin the particularly impressive langoustine – beautifully cooked, wonderfully tender, topped with a thin slice of lardo and fresh chanterelles, and accompanied by a robust vadouvan sauce with perfectly pitched heat to provide contrast. The signature dish of "duck liver rice, beetroot, beef tartare" also deserves a special mention. The quality of the ingredients is second to none. Boasting around 40 000 bottles of wine, and with an impressive range of vintages, the wine cellar is simply magnificent. The service, too, is top-notch, thanks to a well-coordinated and unflappable team; the chefs talk you through their dishes personally. Set in an elegant glass cube, the spacious, upscale restaurant commands a magnificent view of the lake. In the evening, the moonlight can lend the space a uniquely atmospheric charm. In summer, the terrace is simply idyllic!

Name: hide and fox
Address: The Green, Saltwood, CT21 4PS, United Kingdom
Description: Start your night with a cocktail at this delightful neighbourhood restaurant that was once the village shop. There is no small amount of skill on display from the chefs, with dishes that are exquisitely crafted and deliver fabulous flavours and textures, be it an exceptional raviolo or glistening turbot. The very best ingredients from Kent’s larder are a feature, while the wine list looks further afield to up-and-coming regions such as Georgia, Croatia and Macedonia. Service comes from a charming team who work with pride and passion.

Name: logy
Address: 39, Lane 258, Ruiguang Road, Neihu District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: logy moved to this location in 2025, whose handsome room is generously furnished in walnut wood. The over 10 courses omakase menu presents thrilling moments of creativity and pleasant surprises for an unforgettable experience. The kitchen seamlessly melds Japanese and Taiwanese elements, as illustrated by the ochazuke made with Taiwanese tea and Hokkaido rice that pairs expertly cooked Wagyu from Kyushu.

Name: minibar by José Andrés
Address: 855 E St. NW, Washington, DC, 20004, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A single door, with a host to match, marks the entrance to this culinary laboratory that goes far beyond its tiny name. Dinner begins in the all-white bar for a cocktail and inventive snacks before moving to the main room with a dozen seats at a wood-topped counter built around the kitchen (there's also an intimate table for small groups).Through a series of small bites and courses, whimsy and surprise are the driving forces. From trompe l'œil cauliflower with caviar and hazelnut oil, via a trembling jamón chawanmushi with soy caramel and sea urchin, to a perfectly judged squab pigeon and the closing crowd-pleasing fried ice cream donut, there is never a dull moment. Along the edges of the room, sharply suited servers ensure a seamless, sincere experience.

Name: roots
Description: This restaurant presents a compelling concept in a stylish setting near Basel Zoo. A personal, handwritten welcome at the table sets the tone for the cuisine of Pascal Steffen and his team, which combines classical foundations with modern creativity. The surprise menu spans seven to 10 courses – only the ingredients are disclosed in advance, and these are of exceptional quality, with an emphasis on regional sourcing. The dishes are plant-forward, but fish and meat also feature. Their signature "Gemüse Garten" showcases over 30 varieties of vegetables prepared using a range of techniques to create a diverse and engaging flavour profile. The cooking style is pleasingly pared-down, clean and accessible, with small but exquisite details skilfully incorporated. Many dishes are finished at the table, offering a great opportunity to see the chefs in action. Harmonious wine pairings by the glass or interesting house-made alcohol-free alternatives are available. Service is delightfully attentive and adept. An original upcycling idea: empty wine crates are used as bag storage for diners.

Name: sein
Description: Thorsten Bender serves creative cuisine at this small restaurant on a quiet residential street. His distinctive style shines through in technically accomplished, clearly structured dishes with judiciously incorporated Asian influences. Their intensity and depth of flavour impress just as much as their finesse and refreshing accents. Top-notch ingredients take centre stage – the very best the market has to offer. An absolute highlight is the perfectly seasoned, firm-fleshed Faroe Islands langoustine served with richly flavoured pumpkin, a robust foamed XO sauce and a delicate, aromatic hint of sudachi. The upscale interior has a chic, contemporary feel. Service is friendly and professional, with the chefs helping to serve the dishes. The evening set menu comprises six courses, with various optional additions. A vegetarian alternative is available if ordered in advance. On Wed, Thu and Sun evenings, diners can also opt for a four-course surprise menu. Much to guests' delight, the full experience is even available at lunchtime – something of a rarity among two-MICHELIN-Star restaurants. In addition to the four- to six-course set menu, a three-course surprise menu is served on Thu and Fri.

Name: the dune
Address: Paul-Ehrlich-Straße 9, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: The fine dining restaurant of luxury hotel The Florentin has an urban and cosmopolitan feel. Its upscale and thoughtfully designed interior provides the perfect backdrop for Niclas Nußbaumer's set menu, which is built around excellent international ingredients. His cooking focuses confidently on the essentials. Technically accomplished and refreshingly direct in style, his dishes impress with elegant, beautifully harmonious flavours, "sea bream, teardrop peas & vin jaune" and "Théo Kieffer squab, salsify & red cabbage kosho jus" being two cases in point. A vegetarian version is also available – ideally, please mention this at the time of booking. Service is very warm and professional: charming and approachable, yet polished, the team led by restaurant manager Lea Rupp ensures a relaxed evening.

Name: Ösch Noir
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Your curiosity will be piqued before you even reach your table, thanks to the glimpse into the open kitchen along the way. In this stylish and elegant fine dining restaurant housed in the luxurious Hotel Der Öschberghof, Manuel Ulrich skilfully incorporates just the right degree of modernity into his classic, French-based cuisine. The cooking impresses with its precision, harmonious flavours and exceptional ingredient quality. For example, an outstanding scallop is cooked to perfection – succulent and impeccably seasoned – and paired with a light, buttery lemongrass foam that provides a pleasing contrast, plus a broth of fermented carrot and tamarind that adds a distinctive note. The "Menu Noir" comprises up to seven courses, with a selection of additional dishes that can be added or substituted, as well as caviar specialities. Each course is presented on a little card – a thoughtful touch and a nice keepsake. A vegetarian set menu can also be arranged with advance notice. The well-coordinated and dedicated front-of-house team, led by sommelier Michael Häni, provides excellent service – and you can count on him for superb recommendations and the occasional surprise, thanks to the impressive wine list he has at his disposal.

Name: 't Amsterdammertje
Address: Rijksstraatweg 119, Loenen aan de Vecht, 3632 AB, Netherlands
Description: This revamped farmhouse is the place to come for a lively dining experience in a vibrant and trendy setting. Upbeat music plays in the background, large chandeliers hang from the ceiling, modern art adorns the walls… This restaurant is brimming with atmosphere, yet also has a romantic side thanks to the subdued lighting and dark colour scheme. Working in an attractive open kitchen, André Gerrits's vibrant creativity befits the setting. His cuisine has verve and knows no boundaries. In his diverse creations, he gives pride of place to vegetables from his own garden, along with other gems of Dutch produce. From the amuse-bouche onwards, the chef reveals his love of global influences, while showing equal mastery of the classics. Take, for instance, perfectly medium-rare chateaubriand wrapped in spinach leaf and puff pastry, placed on a creamy mushroom purée and paired with carrot seasoned with fermented garlic cream, a wonderful chilli sauce and grated summer truffle. 't Amsterdammertje is all about bold flavours and fun – all delivered with remarkable expertise. Be sure to check out their delicatessen, Marché.

Name: 't Fornuis
Description: Johan Segers has moved ’t Fornuis across the street. The 18th-century building possesses just as much character as his previous location—delightfully authentic and rustic, in an old-Flemish style. The godfather of Antwerp’s gastronomy remains true to himself here. Everything begins with his respect for the seasons, the produce, and the people behind it. His cooking is so traditional and unpretentious that it borders on the creative.Where else, for instance, would you find a croque monsieur made with gently cooked brains, served with a zesty tartar sauce? A real treat for any gourmet! And when he receives some pristine brill in the morning, he will poach the fish to perfection, accompanying it with a refined white wine sauce, a mousseline sauce with a delicate tang, a poached egg, and an elegant quenelle of caviar. It is so incredibly easy to enjoy oneself here. This craftsman has held a MICHELIN Star since 1986 and continues to captivate his guests with a compelling sense of nostalgia.

Name: 't Ganzenest
Description: 't Ganzenest will forever be associated with Harry Visbeen, who held a MICHELIN star for many years. Today, Erik Tas is writing a new chapter of this beautiful story. He has cultivated the authentic allure of the building and revamped the restaurant with just the right dose of elegance. A glance at the menu reveals that chef Tas is a fan and connoisseur of top-quality produce such as turbot, veal sweetbreads and wagyu. He enhances these ingredients with the perfect garnishes and expertly done sauces with great depth of flavour. Take, for example, the wonderful cream sauce with chanterelles and the rich veal jus that elevates a fillet of turbot to new heights. He showcases strawberries, for instance, in a beautifully airy soufflé, but also subtly macerated with a ball of super creamy vanilla ice cream and in an elaborate creation with a strawberry coulis brightened with a dash of vinegar. Erik Tas is an astute chef who knows how to get the best out of his ingredients, and understands that less is more. The produce is clearly the star of the show here – the enthusiasm with which the waitstaff present the wines and cheeses is infectious.

Name: 't Korennaer
Description: Edwin Van Goethem, who is always on the move, has been going from strength to strength since the opening of 't Korennaer in 1997. This gifted chef concocts cuisine, underscored by subtle international influences, ranging from Japanese seasonings to elements of North African culinary tradition. Thanks to trusted suppliers of the likes of butcher Hendrik Dierendonck and asparagus grower Els Vercauteren, the top-notch quality of the ingredients is guaranteed. The chef lets the natural flavours take front stage in dishes that are very much in tune with their era. First-rate produce, such as hop shoots and wagyu beef, is elevated with rich sauces, exotic aromas and fascinating sides that keep diners on their toes. For example, eel from the Eastern Scheldt River is cooked at a low temperature and enriched with a nine-spice green sauce, fries cooked in beef tallow and a fresh green salad in a masterful modern take on a pedigree Belgian classic. The sophistication of 't Korennaer is matched by the opulence of its stylish interior and alfresco dining area. A buzzy down-to-earth vibe nonetheless reigns throughout, and chef Van Goethem's enthusiasm is infectious.

Name: 't Lansink
Description: 't Lansink is a warm and welcoming haven for food lovers. Built in 1916, this charming house is located in the heart of the historic Tuindorp neighbourhood known for its romantic gardens. The dedicated front-of-house team makes it its mission to pamper you. A friendly chat, expert wine recommendations, or an explanation of their fantastic cocktails? They are here for you, serving up the delicious creations of the enterprising Lars van Galen with genuine pride. His tasting menus and à la carte dishes alike offer outstanding value for money. He puts the spotlight on local ingredients such as Twente asparagus and game from the region, adding thoughtful accompaniments and deeply flavoured sauces that showcase his culinary talent. Take the venison, for example: the loin is beautifully cooked pink, the leg glazed with the jus. The depth of flavour is accentuated by a garlic foam, asparagus served both lightly charred and as a flan, dots of sweet potato purée and a caramelised sauce that adds further character. At 't Lansink, the main ingredient is allowed to shine in visually appealing dishes. Why not enhance your culinary experience by booking yourself in for a thrilling spectacle at the chef's table or booking an overnight stay?

Name: 't Raedthuys
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Striking contemporary art adorns the walls inside this historical property dating back to 1863 – at 't Raedthuys, art and dining go hand in hand. The modern decor beautifully preserves the authenticity of the building's character. A window to the kitchen allows you to see the chefs and their team at work. On sunny days, the terrace at the front is the perfect spot for a romantic dinner for two. Hostess Anoeshka Lamers takes you under her wing, while sommelier Karina van der Kolk recommends her personally imported wine gems, which complement the culinary creations of Tom Lamers and Hans den Engelsen beautifully. They prepare an outstanding tournedos Rossini, for example, and know exactly how to cook black pudding until meltingly soft, before combining it generously with foie gras and a warm, cardamom-scented apple compote. However, they also have a modern edge, delighting diners with artistic plating and surprising textures. An amuse-bouche of finely sliced cabbage, red cabbage foam and balsamic ice cream is a fine example. You should definitely sample something from the cheese trolley, which boasts around 30 cheeses. Then comes the tea trolley laden with a tempting assortment of sweet treats? No doubt about it: the real artist is in the kitchen!

Name: 't Stoveke
Description: Daniel Antuna and his wife Petra have been pampering their guests from the warm welcome on the doorstep to the final goodbye as they leave with a smile on their lips since 2005. An open kitchen ensures that you won’t miss any crumbs of the culinary show in this restaurant, which is also home to a chef’s table, where you will feel both at home and as if you are a VIP guest. Chef Antuna deploys state-of-the-art culinary techniques without betraying his classical training. His unique sense of flavour is superlatively enriched by Asian influences. For example, he may pair the delicacy of exceptional scallops with a subtle interaction of caramelised chicory and shavings of chorizo, a crumble of chicory and a creamy miso and chorizo sauce. The chef manages to add a whole new dimension to familiar flavours and adores cooking veggies, as his mouth-watering vegetarian menu demonstrates. Intelligently inventive cooking designed to uplift the spirits.

Name: 11 Woodfire
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Industrial styling, intimate lighting and a laid-back feel are the hallmarks of this striking modern villa conversion in the residential suburb of Jumeirah – along with the huge open kitchen and grill which gives the restaurant its name. The variety and excellent quality of global ingredients are grilled to perfection over oak, hickory or hay, each of which impart their own distinctive flavour. The talented kitchen has the know-how to keep things simple, enhancing the skilfully cooked dishes subtly with well-judged seasoning.

Name: 114 Faubourg
Address: Le Bristol, 114 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honoré, Paris, 75008, France
Description: (Temporarily closed) Situated within Le Bristol, this brasserie is truly one of a kind! The interior will win you over at first glance: interspersed with imposing gilded columns, it has large luminescent dahlia motifs on its orange walls. At its heart, a grand staircase opens up, leading down to the lower level where tables rub shoulders with the open kitchens. Chic, shimmering, both bustling and intimate, this place hits all the right notes. As for the food, this is a discreetly original take on the French classics we know and love. Dishes are carefully presented and flavours are beautifully combined. This is a lesson in how things should be done.

Opposite Palais Rohan, an architectural masterpiece completed in 1741, this ‘1741’ is the quintessence of stylish, depicted by cosy, pleasantly hushed dining rooms and a counter that shines the spotlight on the consummate handiwork of the kitchen team and chef Jérémy Page. The chef, a former disciple of Robuchon, signs delicate, precise recipes, strewn with nods to Alsace. His creativity is particularly notable in sauces and jus: seaweed soup, curry-laced scallop stock or a Grand Veneur game sauce…

FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Here at 1789, chef Florian Stolte has carved out a niche for himself that perfectly complements the culinary portfolio of Hotel Traube Tonbach. He showcases his signature style in a pair of six-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. His approach is minimalist and modern, with contrasting Asian influences woven through the courses. He skilfully showcases the exceptional quality of the ingredients, allowing, for example, the distinctive flavour of the juicy, tender langoustine to shine by serving it raw as a classic carpaccio and using minimal seasoning. Another case in point is the grilled Wagyu beef fillet, the wonderful meaty aromas of which are brought to the fore by a mere sprinkling of salt. The restaurant itself is done out in an intimate, minimalist and yet chic and sophisticated style, the atmosphere is pleasingly relaxed, and the well-staffed front-of-house team is friendly and professional.

Name: 1804 Hirschau
Description: Chef Lukas Adebahr and his team adhere to the farm-to-table principle in this period building, which boasts an idyllic location in Munich's Englischer Garten – be sure to factor in a stroll in the park before or after dinner. The seasonal regional cuisine is made using excellent ingredients sourced from local farmers or grown on site, featuring dishes such as rooster with green asparagus and morels. Bavarian influences are also integrated in imaginative ways. Tempting dessert options include baba with rhubarb and soured cream. Two set menus are available: "Vom Hof" and the vegetarian "Vom Garten". Incorporating a tasteful blend of sleek design, wooden furnishings, glass fixtures and attractive decorative touches, the stylish interior has an Alpine feel.

Name: 1876 Daniel Dal-Ben
Description: At his chic and elegant little restaurant by the zoo, Daniel Dal-Ben serves up classic cuisine with a judicious flourish of creativity. In addition to Italian and French influences, the chef-patron also incorporates Japanese accents from time to time. A good example of interesting contrasts and harmonious balance is "Cannelloni, smoked eel, Caprese foam, pumpkin seeds". He is also partial to decorating his dishes with skilfully integrated herbs and flowers. The "Cicchetti 1876" starter has become a staple of the set menu. Allow plenty of time, as you may be treated to additional courses. Beyond the terrific food, the atmosphere is inviting and almost intimate. Attentive and well-trained front-of-house team.

Address: Torridon Hotel, Annat, By Achnasheen, Torridon, IV22 2EY, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the banks of Upper Loch Torridon with majestic mountains in the background and manicured gardens outside, this vibrantly decorated restaurant inside The Torridon hotel is in a truly stunning location. Exceptional Highlands produce is the bedrock of superbly balanced dishes that could be either classic or original in their make-up: from day-boat John Dory with a sublime roast chicken sauce, to the clever combination of white chocolate and rocket with preserved brambles. An extensive global whisky collection adds to the appeal.

Name: 1890 by Gordon Ramsay
Description: This intimate restaurant next to The Savoy's American Bar is named in honour of the year in which renowned French chef Georges Auguste Escoffier joined the hotel. It’s a comfortable and discreet space, with golden hues, art deco touches and just 10 well-spaced tables. The surprise tasting menu is in part inspired by Escoffier’s classics but prepared using modern techniques, resulting in dishes with elegance and poise, underpinned by high-quality ingredients such as Cornish Red chicken. The Fragola Melba dessert is an updated version of the original made in honour of Dame Nellie Melba.

Name: 1910 Gourmet by Hausers
Description: The fine dining restaurant of the Hotel Belvedere welcomes diners in a compact space with just six tables. In the kitchen, Hungarian chef Dávid Imre Rózsa runs the show. His technically modern and pleasingly pared-back style conveys emotions through its flavours, coming into its own in dishes such as dry-aged pike perch with Oscietra caviar from Frutigen – this also exemplifies the firm focus on using local seasonal produce, some of which they collect and plant themselves. Vegetarian dishes are the backbone of the menu, with one of the two set menus being completely vegetarian. There is a good wine selection with the option of ordering by the glass. The wine pairings to accompany the set menu comprise Swiss organic wines. The kitchen team provides back up to the friendly waitstaff.

FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Named after the birthday of chef Flavio Costa’s twin daughters, 21.9 reflects both his Ligurian origins and his deep ties to Piedmont. Set within a wine estate whose cellar dates back to the 15th century, with sweeping views over vineyards and rolling hills, the restaurant offers a creative cuisine at the crossroads of land and sea, marrying Piedmontese recipes and ingredients with those of Liguria, while also embracing more contemporary influences. All this is expressed through three tasting menus, with dishes also available à la carte. In season, a menu dedicated to game is also available.

FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: There aren’t many restaurants that can claim to have made it past their 40th birthday, but then 28+ isn’t just any restaurant. Passionately run since 1985, it sits in a historic building in one of the city’s most elegant neighbourhoods. Descend the stairs and you’ll find yourself in a romantically candlelit cellar, where you settle in to spend the evening over a tasting menu of timeless classics. Prime Swedish and Scandinavian ingredients are showcased in carefully executed, boldly flavoured dishes, which are accompanied by an exceptional cheese selection and an outstanding wine list.

Name: 2Monkeys
Description: There are some restaurants that exude positive energy – and this is, without a shadow of a doubt, one of them. The two monkeys after which it is named (and which are also depicted on the logo) refer, somewhat surprisingly, to the two chefs at the helm (Vítor Matos and Guilherme Spalk) and their approach to their work – at the same time as offering a high-quality culinary experience, they are also keen to entertain and have fun! This unique space, occupying the former wine cellar at the luxury Torel Palace Lisboa hotel, recreates, in stunning wood, the concept of a theatrical dining experience for just 12 guests built around a central island that provides the setting for the open kitchen. On the single, creatively focused menu, which includes some French-inspired details, guests can explore flavours from around Portugal (we particularly enjoyed the onion chawanmushi and the violet shrimp). The chefs interact constantly with their guests, who are not restricted to a fixed time schedule, enabling them to manage their own experience in more relaxed fashion.

Name: 311 Omakase
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: Located on the ground floor of a South End rowhouse, this intimate chef's counter is the vision of Chef Wei Fa Chen. Pale walls and light wood provide a blank canvas to show off the chef's seasonal selection of ceramic platters (from Kyoto and Asheville), custom-made tatami coasters and thoughtfully crafted cuisine.The chef's omakase features impressive nigiri showcasing high-quality product, much of it imported from Japan; and the range of fish could include fluke, striped beakfish and goldeneye snapper. Cooked items precede the sushi and highlight a particular cooking method, such as delicately crunchy fried longtooth grouper with ponzu sauce or a simmered bowlful of amadai and abalone in dashi.

Name: 33 The Homend
Address: 33 The Homend, Ledbury, HR8 1BP, United Kingdom
Description: You'll find an abundance of homespun charm at this sweet, cosy restaurant run by a husband-and-wife team. Elizabeth warmly welcomes you into the 18th-century, Grade II listed building, while her husband James works alone in the kitchen. His concise menu is a masterclass in naturally delicious cooking that is free of frippery. Ingredients are sourced from trusted suppliers and delivered with excellent complementary flavours, be it Salcombe crab with punchy romesco or in-season deer with a deep, intensely flavoured faggot.

Address: Bahnhofsplatz 1a, Limburg an der Lahn, 65549, Germany
Description: With a name like 360°, who isn't expecting a great view? The highlight of this sleek, modern restaurant on the third floor has got to be the roof terrace! But you can also enjoy the views over the city from the inside thanks to the large windows. Alternatively, you can watch Alexander Hohlwein and his team at work in the open kitchen as they prepare their creative set menu in the evening ("Weltreise"). Over four to eight courses, harmoniously balanced flavours are presented – such as exquisite Helgoland lobster with tomato, passion fruit and ponzu, or perfectly roasted Challans duck with coffee, hot banana sauce and parsley root. Heading up the front-of-house team is Rebekka Weickert, your cordial hostess who also offers expert wine recommendations – the selection of German labels is particularly noteworthy. A shorter set menu is served at lunchtime. A beehive on the terrace supplies the restaurant with honey. Note: The restaurant entrance is to the left of the main entrance of the WERKStadt shopping centre, with convenient parking available.

A pastel blue townhouse plays host to this series of intimate, elegant dining rooms, but many favour a spot in the striking glass-enclosed terrace overlooking the street. The multi-course menu opens with dishes inspired by the chef’s global travels, before moving on to offer refined versions of more local recipes. Beautifully presented, wonderfully flavoured Hungarian produce might include Danube salmon – accompanied by caviar, butter sauce and dill – or aged Mangalitsa ham with white asparagus, morels and chervil. Charming service and an impressive wine cellar add to the experience, as do the luxurious bedrooms.

Even after all these years, 5 is still bang on trend. This is primarily down to Alexander Dinter's modern cuisine. Since 2018, he has been the creative force at the helm, successfully incorporating his own original ideas into his seasonally inspired set menu. The location near the Schlossgarten, in what was Stuttgart's first ever railway station, is also unique. A laid-back urban vibe combined with an elegant lounge decor makes for a special atmosphere, which persists as you move from the stylish bar on the ground floor to the "casual fine dining" restaurant on the first floor. Here, guests sit on chic, individually designed chairs at bare tables to enjoy the excellent food and service, which includes expert wine recommendations. The parking garages in the immediate vicinity are convenient for those coming by car. The gourmet set menu is offered from Wednesday to Sunday in the evening. Reservation times: 18:30 and 19:15. At lunchtime and on Mon. and Tue. evenings there is a somewhat simpler, reduced offer.

Name: 64 Goodge Street
Address: 64 Goodge Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 4NF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Sister restaurant to Portland and Clipstone, this small bistro deluxe delivers intimate, relaxed surroundings in which to enjoy a menu based around classical French cooking. British Racing Green walls blend with simple polished wood, candle-lit tables and wicker chairs, while the semi-open kitchen brings a livelier atmosphere to one end of the room. Fine ingredients are used to excellent effect in bold, gutsy combinations that deliver simply delicious results; ensure you save room to finish with the greengage Tatin or the textbook Paris-Brest. Wine connoisseurs should look out for the 'Cellar List' and its many gems.

Name: 7 Adams
Address: 1963 Sutter St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
Description: Chefs Serena and David Fisher cook with confidence at this intimate tasting menu restaurant. The room is thoughtfully designed without feeling precious: a railway-style space with an open kitchen that moves with calm purpose, inviting diners to observe without distraction. The seasonal menu reflects a distinctly Californian sensibility, rooted in strong technique and an instinct for balance. Dishes arrive composed and deliberate: warm milk bread with house-made cultured butter, handmade pasta dressed in a deeply flavored sugo or carefully cooked fish paired with broths and sauces that support rather than dominate. Desserts, such as a refined take on a Mont Blanc, capture the kitchen's approach at its best, while service remains warm and attentive throughout.

Name: 7th Door
Description: Chef Kim Dae-chun’s cooking continues to diversify and deepen over time. The menu at this restaurant embodies the culinary direction he wishes to pursue, largely thanks to his modern Korean preparations. Under the theme of fermentation and aging, the essential attributes of Korean gastronomy, the chef prepares ingredients with care and expertise. The 7th Door symbolises a gastronomic entrance to “the seven tastes of food,” the first five being the five basic tastes; the sixth, the taste of fermentation and aging; and the seventh, the culinary sensibility of the chef.

Name: 8 1/2 Otto e Mezzo - Bombana
Address: Shop 1031, 1F, The Promenade, Galaxy, Avenida de Cotai, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This award-winning Macao outpost offers the same exquisite fine-dining experience as its Hong Kong flagship. A single set tasting menu focuses on Sicilian cuisine – the appetisers awaken the tastebuds with ingenious food combinations, the hand-rolled pasta is simply divine and the hazelnut soufflé with a runny centre an exquisite surprise. Caring service befits the quality of the food.

Address: 1052-1054 Charoen Krung 26 Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Named for the ratio of local ingredients to the chef's inspiration, 80/20 promises a dynamic seasonal tasting menu, featuring innovative delights from the first bite to the last. The concept extends to the design, using predominantly Thai materials in an industrial loft style. The chef employs traditional techniques to create contemporary interpretations of classic Thai dishes with Lao influences. Mains are paired with aromatic Yasothon jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan.

Name: A Casa di Mà
Description: (Temporarily closed) Lumio, a village of Haute-Corse, is the quintessence of light and flavour... The contemporary interior leads onto a pretty terrace, providing the perfect foil to sample pared-back cuisine drenched in the flavours of the Mediterranean and the land of Corsica. Friendly, attentive service. Prolong the fine dining experience with a night at the hotel overlooking the Bay of Calvi.

Name: A Cozinha
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This could be the icing on the cake during your visit to this beautiful city, with its medieval centre declared a World Heritage Site. The restaurant, in an unassuming building in the historic centre, features a charming dining room from which you can see the kitchen, separated by a glass wall. Chef António Loureiro, always loyal to the idea that “cooking is also about storytelling”, serves up his Equilíbrio (“Balance”) tasting menu (available in 6 or 9 courses) and a small menu with dishes taken from it, such as his excellent, tender and tasty veal with cauliflower. The balanced concept, brimming with sensitivity and modern touches yet grounded in a solid traditional foundation, emphasises a deep respect for raw ingredients. Curious details? On the upper floor, there’s a private dining room and... a small terrace filled with aromatic plants!

Name: A Cozinha do Paço
Address: Paço do Morgado de Oliveira, Estrada M527 - Km10, Évora, 7000-016, Portugal
Description: Haute cuisine in the heart of the Alentejo? This restaurant is located in the Paço do Morgado de Oliveira, a 14th-century building restored in full respect of its original structure and, in turn, set within the Fitapreta winery, surrounded by vineyards and meadows where cattle graze. Here, in an intimate yet sophisticated setting, the connection between the culinary world and that of viticulture is constant. Upon arrival, you are guided on an immersive journey while the story of the house is told, with aperitifs and stops both on the terrace and in the kitchen, a space that preserves the charm of former times. In the dining room, chef Afonso Dantas’s elaborate proposal takes shape in two contemporary tasting menus: Poda Longa and Poda em Vaso (both with wine-pairing option). Curious details? We were surprised by the bread moment, reserved for the very end, after dessert, and prepared in another room, encouraging lively conversation among diners.

Name: A Cut
Address: 2F, Fubon Liaoning Building, 177 Liaoning Street, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104105, Taiwan Region
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Diners are escorted past the open kitchen into an airy room bathed in natural light, perfect for power lunches or social gatherings. For a surcharge, all the à la carte steaks can be made into a set. Australian Mayura Full-blood Wagyu ribeye tastes milkier than typical grass-fed beef, and with the cut, you get to enjoy the robust flavour of New York strip and the even marbling of ribeye cap. Wine buffs should check out the rare vintages.

Name: A Tafona
Address: Virxe da Cerca 7, Santiago de Compostela, 15703, Spain
Description: There are personal goals that develop with learning, travel, effort... that personal evolution that can only be achieved by reaching your targets. This is the perspective from which we must take Lucía Freitas, a chef who is aware of food intolerances, tireless in her quest for a healthier cuisine and who, whenever possible, uses vegetables from her own garden. This charming restaurant with a contemporary atmosphere, where the stone walls and the wonderful skylight of the main dining room blend with a cosy private room, is the ideal setting to enjoy a modern, regionally based proposal, which is indebted to the magnificent Galician products (especially fish and seafood) but is also tasty, technical and feminine, constantly playing with colour. It offers two interesting tasting menus: Semente and Alborada de Gloria. Interesting facts: The beautiful tables, which are left as is... are all made with the original wood from authentic bateas!

Name: A Ver Tavira
Description: This house is located near the Moorish castle and was designed with heart, as a tribute to the city’s history; little wonder it has two terraces with spectacular views over Tavira and the Gilão River. The attentive couple who run it, with Cláudia Abrantes watching over everything in the dining room and her husband, chef Luís Brito, at the helm of the stoves, spare no effort to make the experience perfect. The concept, always seeking balance between vegetables and seafood, unfolds as a sensory and emotional journey through Portuguese flavours via two tasting menus: for lunch, A viagem do sabor (5 courses) and Entre momentos (6 courses); and for dinner, A viagem do sabor (6 courses) and Toda a viagem (9 courses), as well as a small à la carte menu. Curious details? The petit fours will surprise you, presented on a ceramic piece adorned with figures of animals, musicians and horsemen, echoing one found in an archaeological dig by the city walls.

Name: A'Barra
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: A'Barra is much more than a restaurant: Its contemporary offering revolves around premium products, such as Joselito Iberian pork and seasonal vegetables from La Catedral de Navarra. To a striking backdrop of a profusion of fine wood, a spacious layout and cutting-edge design, guests can choose between the elegant dining room, spacious private rooms, an exclusive table in the kitchen and what they call La Barra, a separate, sophisticated space that is ideal for a cocktail or an aperitif. Chef Sergio Manzano champions a concept closely linked to the finest ingredients, technique and raw passion, which is why both the à la carte menu (with the option of half portions) and the tasting menu invite us to discover traditional flavours from a contemporary perspective. Signature dishes here include the Huevo de Mos, with Joselito ham tagliatelle and smoked eel and the steak tartare. Let the superb sommelier Valerio Carrera guide you in your pairing from the extensive wine cellar.

Name: ADAM ALBIN
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: After more than a decade at their former address, chef-owners Adam and Albin moved to a handsome 19th-century building beside the opera and opposite the Swedish parliament. The interior features a seductive dark-wood panelled lounge with a curated art collection and a light, spacious dining room boasting an impressive wine cellar. Both the ‘Seasonal’ and shorter ‘Selection’ menus feature highly accomplished dishes cooked over open flames, such as squid with Noir de Bigorre lardo, white icicle radish, coriander blossom and green cardamom jus or blue-shelled lobster with fig, turnip and saffron.

Name: AKKEE
Address: 42/99 Mu 7, Pak Kret Bypass Road, Bang Talat, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This unassuming Thai gem delights with bold, regional dishes served in an immersive, dimly lit setting. Chef-owner Sittikorn's meticulous technique shines in his skilful updates of classic Thai recipes that change with the seasons. One notable feature is the traditional preparation in a no-frills kitchen, resulting in dishes with a rustic edge and distinct flavours. For the full experience, opt for the set menu, paired with selected Thai draft beers.

Name: ANIMA
Description: Janice and Heiko Lacher are the perfectly coordinated duo at the helm here. Working in an open, fully visible kitchen, the latter presents his creative set menu "Mit Leib und Seele" ("With Heart and Soul"), which comprises five to seven courses, plus aperitifs, bread and petits fours. Dishes such as grilled Breton lobster, pickled melon, lime kosho and gado-gado sauce, or Nebraska prime beef with glazed asparagus, chipotle jus and tarragon are technically outstanding and exceptionally rich in flavour. Skilfully integrated heat and delicate acidity create pleasing contrasts throughout. Their motto "Weltoffen – Produktverliebt" ("Open to the world – in love with produce") could not be more apt. Tip: Oysters and caviar are available as optional additions to the set menu. Your charming and highly organised hostess attends to guests while also assisting her husband in putting the final touches on the dishes. The sleek, modern dining space feels appealingly airy thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows. Capacity is limited, making for an almost intimate atmosphere. N.B. The set menu begins at the same time for all diners.

Name: APRON
Description: This tastefully designed restaurant is housed in Hotel Am Konzerthaus Vienna - MGallery, not far from the Stadtpark and the historical centre of Vienna. The open kitchen turns out precise modern cuisine replete with subtle contrasts. Made from high-quality ingredients, the internationally inspired dishes, such as "scallops, chorizo, cucumber, cabbage" or "rack of lamb, corn, pak choi, apple" take the form of a set menu comprising five or seven courses. A small selection of dishes can also be ordered as add-ons. The combination of stylish contemporary interior design and impeccable, attentive service makes for an appealing atmosphere. A few seats afford interesting views of the chefs at work in the kitchen.

Name: ARIA
Address: Via Loggia dei Pisani 2, Naples, 80133, Italy
Description: The ambience at this hushed and discreet restaurant couldn’t be more different from the hustle and bustle of the elegant district in which it is situated. The softly lit dining rooms are elegant and minimalist in style, with lamps creating pools of light illuminating the dishes conjured up by Paolo Barrale. Originally from Cefalù but now settled in Campania, the chef’s cuisine is inspired by the culinary traditions of both regions which he reinterprets with ease, occasionally creating more personalised dishes. Generous in every way, from the warm welcome to the cuisine right up to dessert, Paolo offers guests a top-quality dining experience ably assisted by his well-trained, professional staff.

Name: ARO
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Set in the old Østerbro machine factory on the edge of town, ARO upholds the theme of having skilled craftsmen in its workshop. The room has a modern, industrial feel, courtesy of exposed ducting and industrial lighting, and the stark walls and floors are punctuated by black wooden furnishings and sketches pinned to chipboard panels. The atmosphere, too, is pleasingly laid-back, with both the service team and the chefs looking after the guests. Choose either a three- or seven-course set menu, where the chefs get playful with wonderfully fresh produce to create some interesting dishes with a strong identity.

Name: ARREA!
Address: Subida al Frontón 46, Santa Cruz de Campezo, 01110, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: When you drive through small villages such as this one, what you least expect to find is a restaurant like ARREA!, where owner-chef Edorta Lamo takes guests on a fascinating cultural and gastronomic journey through the almost subsistence-like landscapes of the Montaña Alavesa region, albeit from a more contemporary perspective. Its three highly distinct dining spaces also come as a surprise, comprising the Taberna (the waiting area), the Kuadra (only offering the Mendialdea menu, featuring five market-inspired dishes and the traditional “putxero” stew), and the main dining room, with its homely rustic ambience, dedicated exclusively to the gastronomic menu. This magical menu comprises a fixed section entitled “ongietorri lunch” (pâtés, hams, preserves, rennet, tiny fried birds etc) which are explained individually, followed by what ARREA refers to as “passes”, based around different ways of preparing partridge, trout, ingredients from the orchard, pigeon, deer and wild boar. Different lichens, which are found in these mountain landscapes, also feature as an ingredient here.

Name: ARVI
Description: On bustling Third Avenue in the neighborhood of Limoilou, ARVI is the stomping ground of chef Julien Masia, a Frenchman from Lyon, who cut his teeth in kitchens in the French Alps. As for the decor in this open-plan space, urban edginess meets contemporary design (exposed brick and concrete). The chefs move between the kitchen and tables, as a trendy playlist sets the mood. Over the course of the set menu (available in "regular" and vegetarian versions), ingredients from Quebec's terroir enjoy their moment: scallops from the Magdalen Islands, lacto-fermented Jerusalem artichoke and local yuzu; sockeye salmon and a delicate beurre blanc with whitefish roe; textures of quince and sweet clover crème diplomate. The chef's signature dish of golden brioche, gravlax-style duck foie gras and birch syrup proves to be a real treat. This is refined modern cuisine in which each ingredient is given its due.

Name: AT
Description: A stone's throw from the banks of the Seine, this small, quietly unobtrusive restaurant sports a minimalist interior in line with today’s quest for authenticity rather than hot air! Chef Tanaka, formerly of Pierre Gagnaire, is a fan of fresh ingredients and precision. Armed with boundless creativity and imagination, he conjures up enticing dishes that keep us drooling right up to the very end. The vaulted cellar in the basement is home to a wine bar and delivers take-away meals. It is also nice to know that you will always be surprised here, because the single set menu changes regularly.

Name: AVANT
Address: 30F, Kimpton Maa-Lai Bangkok, 78 Soi Ton Son, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The Singaporean chef is renowned for his culinary approach, which combines traditional and modern techniques with meticulous attention to detail. Drawing on rich Japanese ingredients and modern European style, each passionately presented course reflects his mastery. Seated at the L-shaped counter, diners can soak up the energy of the kitchen, while the city view adds another dimension.

Name: AVERY
Address: 54 Saint Stephen Street, Edinburgh, EH3 5AL, United Kingdom
Description: When American chef Rodney Wages visited Edinburgh on holiday, he fell in love with the city so much that he decided to move himself, his family and his restaurant here. And that's how Avery, which once graced the streets of San Francisco, came to be located in a classic Georgian townhouse in Stockbridge. Rodney has wholly embraced his Scottish surroundings, taking the country's bountiful produce and treating it with a Californian lightness, while providing bold, distinct flavours – like Orkney scallop dressed with pineapple jus. The drinks flight combines wine, sake, sherry and, of course, a wee single malt whisky.

Name: Ababol
Address: Calderón de la Barca 14, Albacete, 02002, Spain
Description: Albacete, which has been known as the New York of the La Mancha region since the time when the Spanish writer known as Azorín coined the term in one of his poems, boasts an enticing gourmet focus thanks to the Ababol restaurant, which is the Spanish word for a type of red poppy. In its contemporary dining room, overlooked by the open kitchen, chef Juan Monteagudo conjures up dishes which showcase the traditional roots of La Mancha, select ingredients (many from its local farms), and sublime sauces that you’ll want to mop up on your plate! The French technical detail on display is influenced by the chef’s father (the artist Philippe André Georges Monteagudo) and is accompanied by a meticulous approach to presentation. The à la carte (half-portions are available) is complemented by two tasting menus (Tierra and Ababol) and a third dedicated to game during the hunting season. Everything on the menu is delicious but one dish that stood out for us was the “cauliflower with Iberian pork fat”.

Name: Abantal
Address: Alcalde José de la Bandera 7, Seville, 41003, Spain
Description: This elegant restaurant, the name of which is the linguistic predecessor of the Spanish word for apron ("delantal"), is enthusiastically run by a team that brings its full expertise, emotion, soul and intrinsic personality to the cuisine. Head chef Julio Fernández Quintero oversees everything that goes on here with the clear objective of transferring traditional Andalucian flavours to a more cutting-edge culinary approach, while maintaining the authenticity of local ingredients and produce and their seasonality. In the renovated dining room, the decor of which is more akin to that of a museum, choose between two tasting menus with different numbers of courses (one menu has nine, the other twelve) but both offering a wine-pairing option. For an even more intense and immersive dining experience, why not book the superb chef’s table in the kitchen, with seating for just ten guests.

Name: Abba
Description: In the heart of Milan's Certosa District, Abba is set in a former brush factory and welcomes guests with Nordic elegance: an open kitchen, only eight well-spaced tables, minimalist furnishings, and natural light streaming through large windows. In the kitchen, Abbattista offers two paths that tell his vision: excellent ingredients and modern techniques merge into delicious and surprising dishes. Among the must-tries, the tomato water risotto with parsley oil and mantis shrimp cream, or the whitefish, elegantly served on black lentils and turmeric. To end beautifully, the hazelnut soufflé is an indulgence not to be missed. The wine list is essential but carefully curated, with some natural and organic options. At lunch, there’s also a business lunch with selections from the menus.

Name: Abbruzzino Oltre
Address: Piazza Salvo d'Acquisto 16, Lamezia Terme, 88046, Italy
Description: A historic palazzo that once served military and ecclesiastical functions now presides over the main promenade with understated grandeur. Inside, minimalist elegance converses with modern art objects perfectly integrated into the setting, creating a refined space of contemporary character. Here, Luca Abbruzzino explores his Calabria with a personal, engaging vision: a vibrant, modern cuisine that showcases technique and sensitivity through dry-aged fish, well-balanced contrasts, and masterful use of local ingredients. Bergamot takes the lead in the dessert course, while savory highlights include amberjack and grouper, prawns with sea urchin, and an oyster risotto that merits unequivocal recommendation. The menu, however, is a surprise: one entrusts the day’s selection to the chef, confident he will captivate with fresh, coherent intuitions. Intimate spaces, impeccable service, and a naturally romantic atmosphere complete an experience uniting history, elegance, and a cuisine that looks to the future without losing its bond to the land.

Name: Abocar Due Cucine
Description: Among the streets of the city centre, one “approaches” – the meaning of abocar in Spanish – Mariano’s cuisine, where Argentine origins and a decidedly globetrotting spirit, shared with his partner Camilla, give rise to an original gourmet proposal, capable of fusing two cultures in a personal and harmonious gastronomic language. The choice ranges from a concise à la carte selection to tasting menus of varying length, dedicated either to fish – with adherence to the Hadria 37 project for sustainable fishing – or to meat; those wishing to create an individual journey may nevertheless freely choose any dish, including those featured on the menus. The dining room, with its contemporary atmosphere, is gracefully furnished: there is almost the feeling of eating in an elegant private home, an intimate setting that invites guests to slow down and allow themselves to be guided by the experience. In summer, those wishing to sit outdoors are advised to book well in advance.

Name: Accents Table Bourse
Description: "Accents tell us where someone is from and about their country, their region and their history. It is this idea of openness and discovery that I want to champion, a cuisine made up of encounters and exchanges," declares Ayumi Sugiyama, the Japanese owner and head pastry chef of this contemporary, Scandinavian-styled restaurant. Chef Romain Mahi's score is a combination of purebred classicism with more daring creations and subtle experiments with roasted aromas and smoky flavours: tartlet of aged caviar, fermented milk, nila oil; sweetbread, celery in vin jaune and morels. From start to finish, everything is balanced and precise, right through to the light, impressively crafted desserts: whipped creamy pear, lemon and Jerusalem artichoke ice cream with powder of dried lime. Warm, vibrant front-of-house team.

Name: Achilli al Parlamento
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Parliament building, this elegant restaurant’s origins as a wine shop are visible in the many wine bottles that line the walls of the dining room. Today, the restaurant offers elegant cuisine, divided into two tasting menus, one more traditional and the other more adventurous, as well as an à la carte menu featuring creative dishes such as the “Senza spaghetto alle vongole” and well-executed dishes inspired by the Campania region.Chef Gallo reveals a sure hand and remarkable skill in making the most of entirely plant-based ingredients, from which he conjures up interesting flavours and textures. There is a wide selection of wines by the glass, while bottled wines can be chosen directly from the wine shop’s shelves. At the entrance, there is a bistro that is also open for lunch, offering simpler dishes in an informal setting.

Name: Ackermannshof
Description: Housed in a lovingly restored printing house that dates back centuries, this chic and tastefully designed restaurant is run with great dedication by Eveline and Roland Tischhauser. Duc Tan Arrigoni, the Italian-born chef of Vietnamese descent, presents a modern tasting menu inspired by the flavours of the Mediterranean, available in five to seven courses. Dishes such as "I Plin Piemontesi – house-made ravioli with guinea fowl, Riesling sauce, parsley" and "Agnello Nostrano – Swiss lamb, ginger and carrot purée, Swiss chard, jus" are prepared using high-quality ingredients, sourced locally if possible. The menu is accompanied by carefully matched wines from an extensive selection, including an excellent choice of Champagnes. The stylish bar area is the perfect spot for an aperitif or nightcap. There is also a sheltered courtyard terrace.

Name: Acqua
Address: Via Filippo Corridoni 1, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Family tradition is renewed with a contemporary spirit at this venue overlooking the historic Ma.Ri.Na. The philosophy here is clear: exceptional raw materials, carefully selected and showcased by chef Menoncin and patron Davide Possoni. The latter enjoys sitting down with guests at the start of the evening to guide them toward offerings best suited to personal tastes: fish, crustaceans, and mollusks interpreted in original recipes, occasionally with pleasing spicy accents, always generous and elegantly plated. The crudo selection is unmissable – notably the sumptuous crustacean trio of scampi, impressively sized caramote prawns, and red prawns – while among the hot dishes, we highlight the seared red mullet with Tuscan kale velouté and gorgonzola gelato, sampled on our last visit and truly memorable. The wine list favors Champagnes, with numerous labels available by the glass. In summer, the outdoor terrace adds an extra touch of pleasure.

Name: Acqua Pazza
Address: Via Dietro la Chiesa 3/4, Ponza, 04027, Italy
Description: Arranged on a series of multi-levelled terraces, the tables at this restaurant boast breathtaking views of the semicircular port, as well as much of the island, extending out to sea as far as Gavi and Zannone – one of the most spectacular views in Italy! In business for over 30 years (20 of those with a Michelin star), Luigi Pesce and Patrizia Ronca delight guests with their fine cuisine which focuses almost exclusively on fish and seafood in classic, unfussy dishes which allow the ingredients to take centre stage (the selection of raw seafood dishes at the beginning of the menu is proof of the high quality), along with the surrounding scenery! An impressive wine list completes the picture.

Name: Acquerello
Description: The word “modern” sums up the cuisine here, although more than one word is needed to do justice to this restaurant. Housed in an old courtyard typical of Lombardy, Acquerello focuses on flavour rather than colour, with dishes created by a chef who enjoys being in the kitchen away from the spotlight. Although the restaurant offers an à la carte, our inspectors recommend the tasting menu with its fine balance of delicate flavours and original combinations that offer a hint of Eastern influence and pleasing contrasts in cooking methods and temperatures. The wine selection reflects the owner’s tastes: a slight emphasis on sparkling wines from the other side of the Alps, but also something for everyone.

Name: Acte 2 Yannick Delpech
