The initial idea behind it was to provide a place to rest and sustenance for pilgrims visiting the nearby 13C Andra Mari church, hence its name. This stunning building boasting superb views of the Ibaizábal river valley features a wine cellar in the basement which can be visited by guests, a bar area for a pre-dinner drink, and two dining rooms decorated in a rustic-regional style, both of which benefit from lovely views. The cuisine on its à la carte and tasting menus (Elexalde and Andra Mari) is firmly focused on the rural and maritime roots of Vizcaya and a modern reinterpretation of traditional Basque flavours, but always based around the very best seasonal ingredients and a continual connection with small-scale local producers (we absolutely loved the Veal sweetbread, coffe and vainilla dish). The brigade's uniform has quite a folkloric feel to it!

Name: Andrea Larossa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Across the Po from the city center, where ample, convenient parking invites a stress-free stop, a luminous dining room awaits, one that once hosted recreational gatherings and social events. Today it retains that same spirit of conviviality, marked by genuine smiles, attentive service, and measured professionalism. In the kitchen, Andrea Larossa demonstrates a deep command of Piedmontese ingredients and traditions, enriched by Southern Italian influences inherited from his family origins and a natural inclination toward contemporary creativity. Two tasting menus favor pleasure over ingredient rarity, free from the dogmas and rigidity of tradition. Both unfold in a generous sequence of small bites, almost a playful prelude that introduces the journey like a fan of appetizers.

Name: Andrea Monesi - Locanda di Orta
Address: Via Olina 14, Orta San Giulio, 28016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Situated in the historic centre of one of the most romantic lakeside villages in Italy, and offering a picture-postcard view of bygone days, this small building houses a contemporary-style restaurant with a small private dining room and three romantic outdoor terraces (book well in advance). The cuisine here is creative and precise, with a menu that features fish and seafood alongside top-quality meat from the Piedmont. Each recipe is personalised, often focusing on contrasting flavours and textures (don’t miss the unstructured elderberry crêpe with pollen and pan brioche). The wine list is overseen by an excellent sommelier who is happy to guide you through the superb wine list.

Name: Andreina
Address: Via Zona Industriale Brodolini, 2, Loreto, 60025, Italy
Description: More than sixty years after Nonna Andreina first opened her doors, this establishment continues to tell a family story deeply rooted in the region. In the elegant surroundings of a former farmhouse, the service stands out for its professionalism and discretion, while the cuisine reaffirms its identity through a focus on game, open fires and charcoal-grilling techniques. Here, the fireplace and the grill are not merely decorative features, but the very heart of the dining experience. The aromas of the spit feature in most of the dishes, enhanced by personal touches and ingredients, some of which are home-grown. There are two tasting menus on offer, ‘Fuoco’ and ‘Fumo’, featuring dishes that will surprise you and offer an original take on tradition. The wine list is well put together.

Name: Andreu Genestra
Address: Camí de Sa Torre, Km 8,7, Llucmajor, 07609, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Chef Andreu Genestra has begun a new, and much more mature, culinary venture within the walls of the luxurious and aristocratic Hotel Zoëtry Mallorca in the rural surroundings of the historic Sa Torre estate, which dates back to the 14th century and features a windmill and even its own church. In this restaurant, accessed via a beautiful patio that houses a romantic terrace, the aim is to create uncomplicated contemporary cooking with plenty of creativity, based around a small menu. We opted for two or three dishes, but there are also comprehensive tasting menus: Mediterranean (12 courses), Mediterranean Extrem (14 courses) and another, called Mediterranean Verde (12 courses), which focuses especially on the vegetable world. Standout dishes? We really liked the tuna belly with courgette tartare, ‘Fava Parada’ sauce and toasted butter for its fantastic balance and interplay of textures.

Name: Andō
Address: 1F, Somptueux Central, 52-54 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Born in Argentina but having honed his skills in Japan, chef-founder Agustin Balbi opened Andō to realise his culinary vision from his unique vantage point. His tasting menu takes diners on a personal journey by fusing his ancestral roots with strong Japanese influences. Don't miss the signature caldoso rice, dubbed "Sin Lola" – a homage to his grandma. The sommelier works closely with the chef, and his wine flight offers some inspired choices.

Name: Angelo Sabatelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In the maze of picturesque alleys of the historic center, housed in a 16th-century building with an elongated dining room under a vaulted stone ceiling, are a few tables and a fireplace. This is Angelo Sabatelli's niche, featuring his refined cuisine woven with Apulian inspirations and personal creativity. In the dining room, his son Daniele, an excellent sommelier, will guide you through one of the most extraordinary wine cellars in the region, spanning two volumes with approximately three thousand labels.

Name: Angle
Description: Located inside the Hotel Cram, but with a separate entrance, Angle is overseen by celebrity chef Jordi Cruz. Here, guests can enjoy an aperitif and appetisers in the foyer before heading up to the dining room on the first floor, a contemporary space that exudes elegance and serenity with its striking floor lamps, wooden fixtures and fittings and heavy curtains. In the kitchen, the award-winning chef’s modern, creative blueprint is followed to the letter without any unnecessary fuss, but with great care and attention and a sense of freedom. Based around market-inspired ingredients, the cuisine is showcased on a tasting menu that features dishes from the three-starred ABaC alongside others conceived in-house. However, everything is in keeping with the restaurant's mission to create “haute cuisine for everyday consumption”. We strongly advise saving space for the dessert menu, with its vast array of textures and flavours.

Name: Angler
Address: 3 South Place, Finsbury, London, EC2M 2AF, United Kingdom
Description: As the name suggests, it’s all about fish and shellfish here on the top floor of the South Place Hotel. Whether it’s Scottish cod with Jersey Royals and sea lettuce, or Cornish monkfish with roasted carrot, the kitchen knows how to cook prime seafood perfectly and make it the star of the dish. The ‘Taste of Angler’ set menu is the best way of sampling more of their specialities, while the wine list is global in its reach. The room is bright and comfortable, with a lovely terrace that's ideal for sunny days.

Name: Angler SF
Address: 132 The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA, 94105, USA
Description: Perched along the Embarcadero, Angler feels like a hunter’s cabin gone Nordic-chic. All eyes eventually drift to the gorgeous kitchen, where the cooks tend to a live fire. The touch of those embers can be felt everywhere, starting with embered oysters with smoked chili butter as well as a radicchio salad so formidable that it calls for a bib and a steak knife. Mains could include aged black cod, flanked by Parker House rolls with seaweed butter or potatoes with taleggio. There are no wrong choices. For dessert, end with a soft-serve sundae bathed in warm salted caramel and stuffed with cocoa nibs. The wine list is not to be ignored either.

Name: AngloThai
Address: 22 Seymour Place, Marylebone, London, W1H 7NL, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Rooted in Thailand, Uniquely British’ is the tagline of this joyfully run restaurant from John and Desiree Chantarasak – John is half-Thai, half-British, a duality that informs his cuisine. The exemplary ingredients – from crab to venison – are sourced from across the UK, including from Desiree’s family’s farm, but you can certainly expect more than British ingredients simply married with Thai flavours. There are reimagined and innovative dishes aplenty here too, such as Brixham crab with caviar and coconut ash cracker. Clever sourcing also extends to the furniture, with the tables made from Chamchuri wood by craftsmen in Chiang Mai.

Name: Angélica Cocina Maestra
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed
Description: This restaurant, the name of which pays homage to the mother of Nicolás Catena Zapata, showcases the authentic flavours of Mendoza from a modern perspective. The dining room, which is as imposingly impressive as the rest of the building, is part of the Catena Zapata winery in Agrelo (in the department of Luján de Cuyo), famous both for the quality of its wines and its design in the shape of a Mayan pyramid. Here, the duo of chefs at the helm, Josefina Diana and Juan Manuel Feijoo, boldly showcase their “Wine First” concept, where every aspect of their cooking revolves around wine, and not the other way round. They invite guests on a personalised tour of the facilities (a stroll through the winery and a glass of vermouth in the distillery room) before they seat you at a table where the focus is on an exclusive and creatively inspired tasting menu which evolves in various stages or courses and is centred on the full DNA of Mendoza (we thoroughly enjoyed the appetisers and dishes such as Trout-Carrot-Tomato). Other details that stood out included the free return transfer from our hotel.

Name: Aniar
Address: 53 Lower Dominick Street, Galway, H91 V4DP, Ireland
Description: 'Aniar' means 'from the west' and indeed the local area is a key inspiration for both the back-to-nature cooking and the chic, moody interior design here. The micro-seasonal menus are finalised based on the day's locally sourced produce, which is showcased in pure, delicate and well-balanced dishes such as a beautifully balanced combination of squid and nettle. The cooking cleverly blends traditional and modern techniques, while contrasts in texture, temperature and acidity are also a feature. Many courses are served by the chefs themselves, some with accompanying poems.

Name: Anima
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Housed inside the prestigious Milano Verticale | UNA Esperienze hotel in the Corso Como and Piazza Gae Aulenti district of the city, this restaurant is run by multi-Michelin-starred chef Enrico Bartolini. Minimalist elegance and design are the key words to describe the stylish decor here, inspired by Gio Ponti’s city of the second half of the 20C. Resident chef Michele Cobuzzi prepares dishes with a modern flavour, prepared using top-quality ingredients which are mostly sourced from his native region of Puglia. Given his origins, it’s no surprise that this chef is highly skilful in his preparation of vegetables and bread-making. The wine list is enhanced by an interesting selection of cocktails, including original and exciting drinks from around the world alongside more classic options.

Name: Animalón
Address: Carr. Tecate-Ensenada Km. 83, Ejido Francisco Zarco, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Many restaurants claim to be transporting, but how many deliver on the promise? Animalón certainly does. In season, this spot shines with an al fresco dining space under a centuries-old oak tree (during colder months, they move to a pop-up space). It's the very definition of tranquility, yet with owner Javier Plascencia at the helm, it's equally thrilling.The contemporary Mexican cuisine pulls influences from all over the country. The kitchen's vision is apparent in dishes like beer-braised barbacoa wrapped in a banana leaf, steamed and smoked in a pig's bladder, then served tableside for a dramatic presentation. Meanwhile, a tableside pour of tomato broth infused with chocolate clams is equal parts sweet, savory, and gently spicy.

Name: Anna Stuben
Description: Although many brilliant “Anna’s” have cooked in this family-run restaurant over the years, in recent times there has been a superb male chef – Reimund Brunner – at the helm. Since December 2024, the restaurant has occupied a new purpose-built dining room (next to the hotel entrance) – this modern Stube has a few round tables, large windows and a summer terrace overlooking the centre of the small town. The cuisine is inspired by the Alto Adige, yet also remains open to ingredients from further afield, including fish and seafood, in dishes which are lighter and fresh in style with a reduced use of butter and sugar. Our inspector particularly recommends the organic duck serve with late radicchio and black poplar mushrooms.

Name: Anne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Pavillon de la Reine, a magnificent residence in Place des Vosges, is named after Anne of Austria, Queen of France and wife of Louis XIII, who once lived here. The refurbished dining room sports a plush, sophisticated vibe, while the patio is idyllic in fine weather to sample a carpaccio of golden grey mullet or monkfish à la meunière. Their oeufs à la neige meringue extravaganza is out of this world.

Name: Anona
Description: In a lively, working-class enclave, this place serves good contemporary cuisine. Talented chef Thibaut Spiwack, whose CV includes Michelin-starred kitchens, finds original ways to showcase produce from the Paris region. The emphasis is on sustainable development and a desire to challenge the codes of gastronomy. Attractive set menu plus a few à la carte options at lunchtime; in the evening, a single set menu with several courses. A moment of gastronomic pleasure.

Name: Ansils
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This restaurant, located in a village in the Benasque valley, has been in business since 1984 and is run by the third generation of the family – it is now overseen by the niece and nephew of founder Pilarín Ferrer with Iris Jordán at the helm in the kitchen and her brother Bruno in charge of the dining room and wine cellar. Under their guidance, the restaurant has had a change of direction with a focus on contemporary cuisine that seeks inspiration from tradition through the culinary influences from the valley and a more modern perspective. Game and vegetables from their own garden take centre stage here, as they are keen to showcase time-honoured ingredients and revitalise the cooking techniques of bygone days (salting, curing, escabeches etc) but with elegance, personality and a lightness of touch. Choose between two tasting menus: Monte Bajo and Alta Montaña (the first offering five courses and the second seven, both accompanied by small welcome appetisers and two desserts at the end).

Name: Ansitz 12
Description: Located in the town centre by the Pfarrbrücke, Gasthof Goldener Stern (est. 1791) is home to David and Anita Senfter's restaurant. Diners enjoy a cosy atmosphere in charming rustic rooms beneath vaulted ceilings, with traditional stoves providing warmth in winter. After stints in renowned kitchens (with Heinz Reitbauer, Silvio Nickol, Vitus Winkler and Andreas Döllerer), the chef-patron now cooks up modern cuisine using regional ingredients – cooked over an open fire. A highlight is the grill-braised beetroot, which is packed with flavour, has a gentle smoky note and is served with pleasingly tart currants and cream. The intense sauces and stocks – the chef's trademark – are outstanding. There is a four-, six-, or seven-course tasting menu, as well as an à la carte selection, complemented by Austrian wines. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: Anthony's Kitchen
Description: Host and proprietor Anthony Sarpong runs an appealing restaurant-cum-cookery school. The Ghanaian-born chef is supported by a dedicated team, whose carefully considered dishes present a modern take on African culinary traditions. There are two set menus: "The Expedition" and the vegetarian "Green Journey", each available in a four-, five- or six-course format. Dishes such as "plantain, pear, savoy cabbage" or "suya kebab, fufu, peanut" are every bit as in tune with the times as the refined, stylish decor, the open kitchen and the easy-going atmosphere. The chefs serve the food themselves. After you have eaten, the dishes and ingredients are explained, encouraging an enjoyable dialogue between the kitchen team and the diners – Anthony Sarpong's passion for his concept is absolutely palpable.

Name: Antica Corte Pallavicina
Address: Strada del Palazzo Due Torri 3, Polesine Parmense, 43016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A fairy-tale setting for a property of almost castle-like aspect, originally built as a customs post on the River Po in the fourteenth century. Today Massimo Spigaroli, whose family were once sharecroppers on the surrounding land, is its owner and has transformed the complex into a complete destination: guest rooms, the Hosteria del Maiale bistrot and spaces for private events. Completing the experience are a visit to the Museo del Culatello and a ‘gastrofluvial’ cuisine deeply bound to the traditions of the local area. Among the historic dishes, the frogs’ legs stand out, golden with sweet garlic and parsley upon a velouté of sweet potato and saffron, while the more contemporary offerings also convince, among them a Carnaroli risotto with asparagus, peas, Parizzi snails and lemon zest: balanced and of refined harmony.

Name: Antica Osteria Nonna Rosa
Address: Via Laudano 1, Loc. Pietrapiana, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In the dining room one breathes the genuine warmth of a Campanian home of times past, enriched by personal touches such as the nativity scene that also depicts the chef alongside his grandmother Rosa. For those seeking a more intimate setting, two secluded alcoves accommodate as many tables, perfect for a private dinner. Among dove-grey walls and carefully designed lighting, the kitchen stands out for its originality and creativity, never losing its connection to tradition and to the produce of the Campanian region, often sourced from the restaurant’s own production. The offering is structured across four tasting menus that alternate chef’s surprises, great house classics and interpretations tied to the produce of the Montechiaro kitchen garden, to which one of the menus is dedicated. A vision well summarised in the words of chef-patron Giuseppe Guida: “An intriguing journey through flavours of times past, with forays into more imaginative territory, never renouncing its origins.”

Name: Antonello Colonna Labico
Address: Via di Valle Fredda 52, Labico, 00030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a scenically impressive setting nestling in the Vallefredda countryside and housed in an original, avant-garde building, this sophisticated restaurant serves carefully balanced and elegant dishes that underline its proximity to Rome and its close connection with Lazio’s rural traditions. Here, nature and modernity go hand in hand: the restaurant is home to large, almost museum-like rooms adorned with works of art and surrounded by parkland. The dishes, on the other hand, are classic in style, in deliberate contrast to the striking, contemporary backdrop in which they are served, and are inspired by many of Italy’s different culinary traditions. We highly recommended booking a table on the lawn under the mature chestnut trees in summer.

Name: Anvers Restaurant
Address: Anvers Wines, 633 Razorback Road, Kangarilla, SA 5157, Australia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Anvers, attached to a winery of the same name, occupies an enviable location. Set in the countryside of Adelaide Hills, the panoramic views from this modern restaurant are worth the trip alone, and Chef Connor Bishop's creative dishes are the ideal accompaniment to this inviting setting. Several menus are on offer, but the Long Story tells a tale of modern Australian cooking with products like Paroo kangaroo, Murray cod and flavorful damper bread taking center stage. It's all simple in the very best way, while Anvers wines complete the experience.

Name: Apdikt
Description: Crispy grey shrimps with a frothy espuma of cod and samphire: the signature appetiser illustrates the calibre of the experience you can expect in this former apothecary, which sports an authentic herringbone parquet floor and warm fabrics strewn in subtle industrial references. We won’t say more as chef Mathieu Van Wetteren voluntarily preserves the mystery, as is the case of his surprise menu. With a painstaking eye for detail, his creative streak refrains from falling into the trap of overworking his recipes and aims more for simplicity and purity, with the occasional Japanese accent. Cod is poached in butter at a low temperature and flanked by a cream of cèpes and a gutsy frothy sauce based on fish stock and fermented yeast. The menu rolls out a patchwork of big-boned, forthright flavours. This unorthodox chef never fails to surprise!

Name: Apicius
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Housed in a sumptuous 18C private mansion that calls to mind a small palace, Apicius is named after this Ancient Roman epicurean who is said to have written the first cookbook. Chef Mathieu Pacaud is keeping the flame alive at this legendary place with a magnificent terrace that amounts to a remarkably bucolic garden in the city. The dishes perpetuate fine bourgeois tradition and achieve a synthesis between classicism and creativity. Time passes, Apicius changes… but remains!

Name: Apicius
Address: Place du Marché-Saint-Pierre (à l'étage), Clermont-Ferrand, 63000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bang in the city centre, on the first floor of Saint Pierre Market, this swanky restaurant enjoys a lofty location. The stylish venue sports a series of beautifully appointed contemporary dining rooms and exquisite tableware. Chef Arkadiusz Zuchmanski, of Polish extraction, decided to move to France to fortify a vocation that took root in the kitchen of his forebears. He confesses an unbridled passion for noble ingredients and for Auvergne, which reminds him of the landscapes of his home city, Drzewica. The focus is on visually striking plating and honest, simply crafted ingredients, such as foie gras with hand-picked wild pepper or sautéed sweetbread with truffle parsnip.

Name: Apicius
Address: Van der Mijleweg 16, Castricum, 1901 KD, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Apicius is the culinary triumph of chef Thorvald and host Gaylord de Winter. The brothers have consistently held at least one MICHELIN star every year since 2003. Good taste is in their DNA, and their expertise shines through in the tiniest details – from the perfectly chosen Burgundy to pair with a fish dish, to the velvety pistachio ice cream complementing an exotic dessert. Chef Thorvald has a true knack for the classics. Exceptional ingredients are the foundation of his cuisine. He keeps fish preparation simple and straightforward: he sears it skin-side down – just long enough – and elevates it with refined finishing touches and a sauce that adds depth. For example, succulent sea bass gets a touch of acidity from a foam made from house-made pickles. Appealing presentations add a fresh twist, too. In the dining space, you are surrounded by art and floral decorations that add an air of elegance to the setting. Ask for a table by the kitchen if you want to watch the chefs in action.

Name: Apollo
Description: The name is a nod to the owners' deep-seated interest in NASA's famous programme. The space theme is also evoked through the elegant, dark interior, the atmospheric dimmed lighting and reprints of original photos from various missions, accompanied by captivating descriptions. The open "satellite kitchen" invites you to witness the culinary artistry unfold firsthand. Enjoy friendly and attentive service and soak up the atmosphere as head chef Thomas Huber and sous chef Sergiu Midori prepare bold modern dishes such as monkfish and calamaretti with bouillabaisse, sauce rouille and chorizo, or dry-aged Swiss char, Osietra caviar, daikon radish and shiso. The cuisine is predominantly Mediterranean, with Asian accents thrown in here and there. There is a choice of two set menus – one omnivore and one vegetarian – each comprising four to six courses. The restaurant is housed in Hotel Grischa, which boasts comfortable accommodation options and a chic bar for a nightcap.

Name: Apostelstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In beautiful Bressanone, the historic Hotel Elephant, housed in a building whose oldest section dates back to the late 15th century, is one of the city’s true icons. Managed by the same family since 1773, it is now in the hands of the eighth generation. In the intimate and exquisitely elegant dining room, with just four tables and the watchful eyes of the twelve apostles that, in the form of statuettes, observe you from the walls, Chef Mathias Bachmann presents a unique, extensive, and exclusive tasting menu. Drawing ingredients and techniques from around the world, with a special fondness for Japan, he reinterprets them with contemporary flair. Service is entrusted to Michael and Eleonora, whose expertise and innate warmth will also delight you with the incredible tale of the elephant that once passed through the city. In the warm season, aperitifs are served in the pleasant garden; during the colder months or inclement weather, they are offered in the elegant lounge, also on the first floor, just like the dining room.

Name: Aptos
Address: 147 Mount Barker Road, Stirling, SA 5152, Australia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Reservations are a must at Aptos, where something special is waiting. Ring the doorbell and you'll soon be invited to step inside this fully renovated former church. The warm, engaging staff is the first sign that this will be a memorable evening. Don't make other plans, as this is a meal to be cherished, enjoyed over three+ hours across three different rooms. Michigan-born Chef Justin James oversees this creative, product-focused tasting menu spotlighting native Australian ingredients and products. Eye-catching presentations (wild venison served in a deer's jawbone or smoked tuna and emu tucked inside folded seaweed) add to the experience.

Name: Aqua Crua
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few tables arranged in a simple, minimalist dining room, facing the open kitchen: the focus here is on chef Giuliano Baldessari and his creative culinary interpretations. There is a restricted selection of dishes available à la carte but, if you really want to enter his culinary world, opt for one of the surprise tasting menus, the first of which consists of ten dishes, served if you’re visiting for the first time, while the last comprises sixteen. Whatever you choose, you can expect sophisticated, imaginative cuisine of the highest standard.

Name: Ar Men Du
Address: 47 rue des Îles, à Raguenès-Plage, Névez, 29920, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Imagine wild moorland buffeted by the ocean with the rocky island of Raguenez glinting in the sunshine just a short distance away. Sustainable gastronomy is the name of the game here: the ingredients are strictly seasonal, harvested from the vegetable garden or sourced from small-scale producers, and the fish is caught locally. Comfortably seated with a view of the sea, diners enjoy Jérôme Gourmelen's dishes, characterised by well-defined flavours and careful presentation, eg his symphony of raw ikejime fish. Friendly service.

Name: Arabelle Meirlaen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Arabelle Meirlaen crafts a highly personal version of healthy food, guided by her intuition and a desire to shine the spotlight on veggies and spices. In fact, a large proportion of the fresh produce comes from her own garden, which boasts an exquisite terrace come summertime. Meirlaen merges an inventive streak with elegance and is unafraid of the odd bold touch, whilst steering clear of the trap of surprising us at all costs. You can expect an unusual array of light dishes, which are nonetheless packed in full-bodied generous flavours. Floral aromas are something of her hallmark. In addition to a vegetarian menu, she rolls out an “intuitive menu” in which she elegantly crafts meat and/or fish. An example: a fresh slice of salmon paired with artichoke, olives, a frothy sorrel-laced beurre blanc and a subtle shredded cabbage and sorrel to finish. Her fragrant signature desserts are to die for! How about a fruity floral mix of grapefruit and black pepper with strawberries and black sesame seeds? The excellent wine list of the owner-sommelier, who enjoys working around themes, brings an added dimension to the meal. To finish, take the time to explore the pretty country village of Marchin before or after (or both) your meal. The bright interior of the splendid restaurant provides the perfect foil to the natural instinctive character and cooking of this master chef!

Name: Araf İstanbul
Address: AG/E İç Kapı, 19 Mayıs Mahallesi Sümer Sokak Sümko N Blok No:1, No:2, Kadıköy, Istanbul, 34742, Türkiye
Description: Kenan and Pınar Çetinkaya welcome you warmly to their intimate restaurant, where capacity is limited. A seat at the counter offers the perfect vantage point to watch the chefs expertly tame the open fire (there are also a few tables in the conservatory). It creates a convivial atmosphere too – you'll almost certainly strike up conversations with your neighbours, and the chefs happily take the time to talk you through their dishes.What may at first glance look simple reveals remarkable depth once you taste it. The chefs focus on bringing out the true essence of their ingredients. They have a penchant for offal but can also conjure up a vegetarian dish with ease. The intensity of perfectly rosé-grilled kidneys, for instance, is balanced with fresh hummus. Melt-in-the-mouth lung pieces are elevated by a wonderful beef jus, a blend of spices, mint and a yogurt dressing, and served with pita bread. Fire is used with sensibility, proving that bold flavours can also be profoundly nuanced. Thanks to the smaller portions, you can sample and share a wide range of dishes – trust us, you wouldn't be the first to try something from your neighbour's plate.

Name: Araka
Address: Kapalı Bakkal Sokak No:8, Yeniköy/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: Here you’ll find it's easy to forget you're in the metropolis of Istanbul. You’re actually in the Yeniköy district, in the north of the city, just beyond the exclusive marina you pass on the way (taking the Bosphorus ferry over is a must). Behind its charming façade, this rural-style restaurant awaits with its cosy, romantic interior and a terrace to the rear where you feel cut off from the world. This enchanting spot perfectly suits Zeynep Pınar Taşdemir's highly individual style. Seasonal ingredients are showcased on the menu. The young chef likes to express her creativity with vegetables and herbs. Pumpkin puree is imbued with the potent freshness of za'atar and combined with pickled vegetables and warm olives in a spicy sauce. A robust dish that is full of character and pleasingly harmonious thanks to its subtle acidity. This chef is adept at balancing spicy, savoury flavours with tangy aromas. She creates exciting dishes that let the regional produce do the talking.

Name: Arakel
Description: Tucked away in one of Geneva’s liveliest districts, the sleek open kitchen of this dainty restaurant captures your attention right from the start, drawing you into the heart of the action. A blend of modernity and tradition, the score adds an innovative spin to a lineup of classics, illustrated by risotto of mussels, celery, saffron mousse, passion fruit gel or a carpaccio of giant red shrimps, subtly marinated in yuzu, lemon zest and fresh herbs and paired with stuffed carrot rolls and a slightly sweet carrot sauce. The small pavement terrace offers a chance to get a real feel for this delightful quarter. The young, enthusiastic and appropriately irreverent front-of-house team adds to the venue’s lively vibe.

Name: Araya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The creations of Chilean chefs Araya and Guerrero are deeply influenced by Araya's stints in Spain and Japan. Dishes, with a South Pacific theme, feature an eclectic mix of Chilean and Japanese produce. Expect the likes of Japanese cod milt jazzed up by Chilean aji amarillo, served with French caviar. The menus "Costa" and "Andes" pay tribute to Chile's coast and mountains respectively; the shorter "Celebrating Chile" menu showcases all-time classics.

Name: Arbore & Sens
Description: Assisted front of house by sommelier Océane (his partner), Clément Dumont, a young chef from the region with some solid experience, has made this restaurant not far from the Royal Citadel the new place to be. An inspired technician with a love of plants and the seasons, he cooks up creative, at times bold cuisine that is inspired by the village, Loire poultry and fish, and of course the goat's cheese, vegetables from his own kitchen garden, and herbs picked by small-scale grower Juliette Krier. One example is the starter based on white asparagus from the Richelais area, preserved egg yolk, elderberry and sake. A pleasant terrace in the shade of the wisteria.

Name: Arborescence
Address: 76 rue de la Gare, Croix, 59170, France
Description: Established in an early-20C textile factory on an entirely rehabilitated industrial wasteland, chef Félix Robert and his wife Nidta, after working for Alexandre Gauthier at La Grenouillère in Tokyo and then at Troisgros, now give free rein to their talents in a stripped-back, stylish interior. The chef's creative and personal repertory is dominated by seafood and vegetables and liberally scattered with nods to Japan and Asia – green curry, ponzu, shiso and saké are unveiled in set menus. One example is semi-cooked lobster with bisque-flavoured crackers paired with citrus fruit and Vietnamese coriander – throbbing with flavour! A restaurant whose resounding success is well deserved.

Name: Arc Restaurant
Description: This small, tastefully designed restaurant with its modern, minimalist aesthetic is deservedly much sought after. Thanks to the fully open kitchen, you can watch at close quarters how a 10-course pescatarian menu takes shape. The modern, creative dishes may seem simple at first glance, but reveal remarkable complexity and detail. A fine example is the lightly cooked, meltingly tender fillet of brook trout, served with mushrooms, fresh horseradish and artichoke purée, accompanied by a creamy, aromatic mushroom sauce. Fermented and preserved elements are also incorporated. The attentive team will gladly tell you all about each creation. Information about the carefully selected seasonal produce – sourced largely from the surrounding Hamburg region – is presented in the restaurant's "Freundebuch". A vegetarian version of the set menu is also available. It is certainly worth perusing the nicely curated wine list. The set menu can be paired with wines or house-made alcohol-free accompaniments.

Name: Arcane
Address: 3F, 18 On Lan Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Aussie chef Shane Osborn lets diners witness how quality ingredients are turned into artistic creations in the open kitchen. Simple recipes are executed with a refined edge that allows authentic flavours to shine through. Always save room for his yuzu and lemon posset – smooth, creamy and with balanced acidity. Ask the affable sommelier about the extensive cellar, which includes a lavish Burgundy selection and covers Europe, Oceania and the Americas.

Name: Archibald De Prince
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Archibald De Prince is going from strength to strength in the company of Rachel, who acts as your charming hostess. De Prince honed his skills as second chef to René Mathieu at La Distillerie as you will quickly realise. Vegetables take pride of place in his culinary score, but not to the detriment of meat and fish. The chef has a knack for sourcing outstanding local produce which he then enhances courtesy of a deft creative touch. He might craft a tartare of locally bred salmon trout with a subtle herby salad, adding a suave caper and parsley emulsion for a final flourish of contrast. The setting is equally stylish and adorned with modern works of art. Even better, book a pleasant room and stay overnight to do full justice to the talent of this gifted chef.

Name: Arco by Paco Pérez
Address: 33rd Floor, Olivia Centre, Aleja Grunwaldzka 472c, Gdańsk, 80-309, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Located way up on the 33rd floor of northern Poland’s tallest building, this restaurant affords views over Gdańsk and out to the Baltic Sea. The cooking is equally spectacular, underpinned by Polish produce, driven by Spanish flavours and incorporating a few Italian influences. The superb pumpkin risotto is a prime example, with a perfectly judged amount of melted liquorice drizzled over the top in a nod to the chef's childhood. The service is smooth and charming, while the wine list is a treasure trove for oenophiles.

Name: Arden
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning Ardennes landscape is the star of the show in this design-heavy restaurant located in a modern wing of the tastefully restored château de Vignée (Michelin key). Picture windows command a fantastic view of the countryside, while the peaceful patio overlooks the Lesse River. Nature is also the name of the game for chef Bosmans, who conjures up a high-flying culinary score courtesy of veggies grown on the property and regional produce. He might exalt the main ingredient with a spicy note in a bid to create fascinating combinations. An example: perfectly cooked seabass in a crispy skin is paired with crunchy squash, cream and shiso oil to further exalt the contrasts, together with a rich vegetable stock and a chewy, briny mussel. Chef Bosmans is known for his fondness for delicately tangy citrus-rich lemon, which he uses to underpin and exalt the flavours of other produce. A minimalist approach is not the only surprise you can expect to sample - make sure you ask to see the Wine ‘Bible’! Arden boasts one of the finest and biggest wine cellars of Wallonia!

Name: Ariete
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: You can settle in at a table in the dining room or on the patio and eat just as well in both. So goes the charm of Chef Michael Beltran’s Coconut Grove mainstay. Lush with greenery, this dimly lit restaurant immediately welcomes with a menu that weaves together new American and classic French influences to dazzling effect.First-timers should aim for the tasting menu, as it's the surest way to experience the chef’s talent for creative combinations and excellent sauce work. Highlights include fluke topped with conch escabeche and sided by fish chorizo and an earthy tomato ragout with beans and pickled chanterelles; or venison tartare and pickled mushrooms with a bone marrow sabayon. The seeded country bread served alongside the tartare is ideal for scooping up every last bite.

Name: Arkestra
Address: Etiler, Dilhayat Sokak No:28, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34337, Türkiye
Description: Cenk Debensason has travelled extensively over the years, and this has shaped his personality as a chef. In brief, he grew up in Istanbul, trained in France, and matured as a chef in the United States. You will notice those influences both in your glass (the cocktails are outstanding) and on your plate. The chef is particularly fond of vegetables, and effortlessly marries classical techniques with flavours from around the globe. His expertise is evident, for example, in the perfect balance between a snow-white fillet of shi drum, sweet Jerusalem artichoke, sharply dressed onion and a deeply flavoured green pepper and coriander sauce, a combination that allows the delicate fish to shine. The versatility of this cuisine will keep you on your toes throughout the entire meal. Choosing from the menu is no easy task! The vintage feel of this stylish 1960s villa is a perfect match for Cenk Debensason's personality. Be sure to visit the Listening Room on the upper floor before or after your meal to enjoy a delicious drink and the chef's carefully curated playlist – DJs also play sometimes. Or how about Ritmo (open at weekends only), the charming concept under the same roof where you can choose from a concise mezze menu? A visit to Arkestra is an experience you won't forget in a hurry.

Name: Armani Ristorante
Description: This restaurant is in an original location on the first floor of the Armani store in St-Germain-des-Prés (not far from the church). The interior is pure and elegant, in the designer's style, of course: a palette of beiges, banquette seating, glossy walls, subdued lighting… Might this be just another shopfront in all but name? On the contrary, this ristorante is one of the best Italian eateries in Paris. Chef Massimo Tringali, former sous-chef at Casadelmar in Porto-Vecchio, works with high-quality ingredients in the spirit of contemporary Italian cuisine. It is fresh, tasty and skilfully done: a fine piece of work.

Name: Arnaud Donckele & Maxime Frédéric at Louis Vuitton
Description: In the courtyard of a building that was once home to the village doctors and is now the White 1921 Saint-Tropez Hotel, this seasonal, alfresco restaurant is further testament to the talent of the Arnaud Donckele & Maxime Frédéric duo, here paired with an iconic luxury brand. The ingredients are chosen with the same superlative care as at La Vague d'Or, and crafted into globetrotting, Mediterranean dishes, flanked by gutsy sauces and jus: a velvety emulsion of coconut, lemongrass and kumquat enhances John Dory roasted in seaweed or coconut- and sweet pepper-laced leche de tigre on raw greater amberjack. The delicate desserts bear the same fresh, distinctive hallmark, illustrated by the wickedly tempting house signature: a profiterole-style iced chocolate wafer.

Name: Aroma
Description: From the ground floor, the lift leads to one of the city’s most evocative roof gardens: a terrace which, in winter, is enclosed and covered – thus usable in every season – directly overlooking the Colosseum. To your right unfolds the view of the Domus Aurea, in the distance a corner of the Altare della Patria can be glimpsed and, just beyond, the great dome of St Peter’s. The kitchen offers four tasting menus (of which one is vegetarian), with the option of also ordering individual dishes freely. Between classics of Roman tradition, Campanian influences and more contemporary creations unfolds the offering from chef Giuseppe Di Iorio, who draws on extensive experience here and in other prestigious hotel establishments – both in Rome and internationally. We are, indeed, guests of Palazzo Manfredi.

Name: Arrels
Description: If you were planning a trip to Sagunt to discover its heritage (castle, Roman theatre, Jewish quarter etc), there’s no excuse not to, as the town also boasts a fine-dining restaurant. This delightful eatery, occupying the former stables of the 16C Palacio de los Duques de Gaeta, features imposing stone arches that provide the backdrop for cuisine that is respectful of traditional Mediterranean flavours but with a contemporary twist and a strong focus on technique. Chef Vicky Sevilla, a cook with lots of determination (she opened the restaurant when she was just 25), showcases modern, personal cooking with a strong connection to the local area (in the Valencian language, Arrels translates as “roots”) which can be savoured on three menus: A la carte (weekdays, lunchtime only), Saba and Arrels (the latter two offer vegetarian options). The slightly elevated upper part of the dining room features an “island” where guests can enjoy dessert and watch the chef put the finishing touches to his dishes.

Name: Artichoke
Address: 9 Market Square, Amersham, HP7 0DF, United Kingdom
Description: At the centre of a picturesque market town sits this 16th-century red-brick house, where the interior blends historic touches and an inglenook fireplace with smart modern design. To start, sample the signature Chiltern Black ale bread, before dining from one of a variety of menus that showcase the experienced chef's accomplished cooking, where the well-measured flavour combinations have an understated complexity. Seasonality is to the fore, as evidenced by superb dishes like local lamb sweetbreads with first flush garden peas and morel mushrooms.

Name: Artis
Description: This restaurant located in the pedestrian area makes for an inviting eatery with its stylish interior done out in a palette of dark colours. Its surprise menu comprises four, six or eight courses. The modern and creative dishes are prepared using excellent international ingredients – a shining example of the first-rate quality of the ingredients is the hand-dived Norwegian scallops, flavoured and seasoned with daikon radish, wasabi, buttermilk and horseradish. Tip: Make a reservation at the chef's table to be seated right in front of the open kitchen!

Name: As Garzas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In a remote Atlantic location at the heart of the Costa da Morte, this restaurant is impeccably run by chef Fernando Agrasar, who works here alongside his wife (who runs the front of house), his eldest son (in charge of bread and desserts) and Eva Fares, head chef and the partner of one of their children. The gourmet cuisine on offer is showcased on a tasting menu built around seasonal ingredients which highlights in a contemporary way Galicia’s gastronomic bounty (we particularly enjoyed the red mullet with a seaweed pil-pil and teardrop peas from Coristanco), as well as an à la carte menu featuring time-honoured classics, daily fish specials, savoury rice options etc. Every table boasts a stunning vista, although we recommend that you book those closer to the picture windows in order to get an even better view of the cliffs and the swell of the ocean from this property that the chef romantically refers to as his refuge at the end of the world. Garzas also has a handful of attractive rooms for guests wishing to stay the night.

Name: Asador Alfonso
Address: Lot-3308, Barangay Road, Alfonso, Cavite, The Philippines
Description: About 80 kilometers from Metro Manila, this modern, minimalist property takes inspiration from Taal Volcano and sits on nine hectares of lush fields. Spanish chef Rodrigo Andres Osorio helms at the kitchen, ingredients sourced directly from Spain to deliver authentic dishes that balance rustic simplicity with remarkable depth and charact. Highlights include melt-in-your-mouth house-aged A5 Wagyu ham "Jamon de Wagyu" and the classic roasted suckling pig "Cochinillo", both showcasing the chef’s dedication to tradition and craftsmanship. Warm service, genuine hospitality, and a splendid atmosphere creates the perfect setting to escape the bustle of the city and immerse yourself in a truly memorable gastronomic journey.

Name: Asador O'Pazo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re unfamiliar with O’Pazo, one of Galicia’s most renowned restaurants for grilled cuisine, you’re long overdue a visit to dine in this unique space created by the Vidal brothers (with Óscar in the kitchen and Manuel in the dining room), where everything revolves around the wood-fired grill. This charming property located next to the main road boasts an elegant interior design featuring an abundance of dark wood, providing the backdrop for traditionally based cuisine that is mainly served as part of the Rescaldo tasting menu. Despite the apparently simple grilled approach to cooking, the end result is a gourmet experience of the highest level which showcases Atlantic fish and seafood, produce from the fields around Padrón and, above all, the native Rubia Gallega breed of cattle (don’t miss the superb steak, which is braised and filleted). The extensive wine cellar features some top-notch Spanish and international labels.

Name: Aska
Description: Two restaurants with Swedish names under one roof. In contrast to the original restaurant (Storstad), Aska is a compact sushi restaurant with a decidedly personal touch. The name translates as "ash", and the interior is accordingly dark in hue. Diners sit at the counter or one of the few booth tables to enjoy authentic sushi served just the way it is in Japan. You can choose between an eight- or 10-course set menu – with the option of additional courses. Having learned his craft in his hometown of Osaka, sushi master Atsushi Sugimoto now transforms premium ingredients into the best classic sushi to be found far and wide! The pleasant ambience is also largely down to the attentive and charming front-of-house staff, who will be able to recommend just the right sake to accompany your set menu. Plus there is a "flat rate" for all-you-can-drink mineral water and green tea – a highly unusual offer in Germany!

Name: Assa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Every morning ("assa" in Japanese), Anthony and Fumiko Maubert devise the daily menu together, drawing on locally sourced produce of impeccable quality. A range of Japanese seasonings and ingredients are seamlessly woven into their inventive dishes. Anthony, who worked alongside Arnaud Donckele (La Vague d'Or) for a long time, signs the savoury score, while Fumiko expresses her twin vocation of nutritionist and pastry chef, rolling out light, low-sugar creations. Splendid wine list with a soft spot for local Val de Loire vintages.

Name: Assonica
Address: Via Don Santo Carminati 9, Sorisole, 24010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the hills just beyond Bergamo, this smart, elegant and well-run restaurant has the Manzoni brothers (Alex and Vittorio) at the helm in the kitchen, where they create some of the most interesting cuisine in the region, while the capable Giovanna Danzo oversees the excellent service in the dining room. Creative and surprising, the dishes here are striking for their complex and original flavours, which combine vegetables with a clever use of herbs and spices without overwhelming the palate. The chargrilled veal sweetbreads (slightly crunchy on the outside and soft inside) are delicious, served with a selection of mushrooms and a fir extract that provides a hint of bitterness. There’s a strong focus on sourcing local ingredients in order to create cuisine which is both contemporary and sustainable at the same time.

Name: Asterales
Address: Hôtel du Golf, Les Ritons, 784 route du Clos-de-la-Balme, Corrençon-en-Vercors, 38250, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Poetically named after an order of flowering plants, this tasteful restaurant sports a low-key alpine style. Chef Ludovic Nardozza’s painstakingly crafted cooking showcases his favourite, first-class ingredients: roasted langoustines in marjoram butter, girolles and vin jaune bisque; John Dory lacquered in wild fennel, courgette flowers and grilled cuttlefish; apple like an upside-down pie with local honey and black cardamon… Service with a smile. Pleasant guestrooms make it an ideal basecamp to explore Vercors.

Name: Astrance
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Pascal Barbot and his partner Christophe Rohat took the gamble of setting up their restaurant in premises that are the stuff of legend – here, Joël Robuchon made a name for himself with Jamin! They have turned it into a slick, modern space, without for all that neglecting to pay tribute to the great chef with the "Salon Joël". With his passion for produce undiminished, the chef creates innovative cuisine in which nothing is out of bounds, with a particular predilection for Asian and plant-based dishes. His fans will be ecstatic to note that his famous button mushroom millefeuille with foie gras marinated in verjuice is still on the menu. The talented maître d' can be counted on to put his guests at ease… and to find them that rare pearl among the vintages that fill the superb glass wine cellar.

Name: Atalaya
Description: Located on the ground floor of an apartment block close to the marina, this restaurant features a space adjoining the wine cellar for aperitifs and appetisers, three welcoming Mediterranean-style dining rooms, plus a modern open kitchen enabling the team here to interact with guests.The pair of chefs at the helm, Alejandra and Emanuel, met in the kitchens of award-winning chef Martín Berasategui’s three-Michelin-star eatery in Lasarte-Oria, where they perfected contemporary techniques and understood the values of haute-cuisine. Here, you’ll find modern, creative cuisine with a strong emphasis on presentation, textures and a skilful combination of ingredients. Take your pick from the three set menus available (with a wine pairing option): Llaüt (not available on long weekends or bank holidays, or in July and August), Bergantin and Falutx. We loved their skate, with beurre blanc, lemon gnocchi and crispy collagen!

Name: Atelier
Description: The Ossola gastronomic atelier offers a safe harbour for lovers of good food and drink in the town centre. The Bartolucci family's tradition has soared thanks to dynamic chef patron Giorgio and entrepreneurial sister Elisabetta, joined by Katia, whose smile and professionalism are invaluable to guest comfort. In addition to the welcoming service, the cuisine beckons clientele from afar. The evening menu is packed with revisited Ossola citations (among others, gathered in the tasting menu "Flavours and Aromas of the Mountains") alongside contemporary Italian culinary nods. In certain occasional dishes you’ll find the fusion of meat and fish, cooked with such skill and experience that the - not easy - balance aligns perfectly. Such is the case with small local veal rolls stuffed with apple and scampi tartare. A splendid selection of wines is available by the glass, where pairing them with your dishes will be both a pleasure and a delight. At lunch, the Bistrot is open.

Name: Atelier Fischer
Description: It's a shame chef-patron Stefan Fischer's excellent cuisine isn't available all year round. The surprise menu comprises seven, eight or 10 very modern and creative courses, such as "Heloin char" with caviar, wild garlic, lovage, lemon balm, rosehip and spelt. Much of the pottery used to serve the food is made by Stefan Fischer himself. The friendly, highly skilled sommelier recommends interesting wine pairings, and alcohol-free pairings are also possible. Tasteful and intimate, the restaurant has just two tables accommodating a maximum of six diners, who receive attentive service. It occupies the first floor of a modern pavilion on the lakeside promenade – unsurprisingly, the terrace is much sought after! Thanks to the large windows, there are lovely views from inside, too. The same owners also run Papageno, a restaurant-café on the ground floor.

Name: Atelier Noun
Description: You will immediately feel at home in Bert and Sandra’s workshop. No sooner are you over the threshold, than you are greeted by a warm, snug interior done up in soft colours. The venue’s serene Japanese vibe is framed by the view of the pretty garden and the splendid summer terrace. This calm extends to the plate, although the deceptive simplicity hides a fiercely structured technical composition.Chef Castermans pays a highly personal homage to the ingredient. Free of fussy frills, his food is uncluttered, occasionally complex and often dotted with sensitively balanced umami nuances that are his personal hallmark. He may associate confit red beetroot, subtly smoked radish, plankton-flavoured beurre blanc and a tangy jelly in a fruity composition that triggers a host of impressions. He is however equally at ease with lamb, which he cooks medium rare, flanking it with a delicious cooking jus, wild garlic oil and a floral tomme cheese espuma.The menu, entirely renewed every six weeks, is always fascinating. One last tip: take a look at the alcohol-free pairings which add a genuine dimension to this delicate score.

Name: Atelier Sanssouci
Description: Atelier Sanssouci – the name alone sounds stylish, and this wonderful 18C estate certainly lives up to expectations! Not only is Hotel Villa Sorgenfrei, complete with a magnificent garden, a feast for the eyes from the outside, but the interior is also a sight to behold: The large dining room done out in an elegant Mediterranean style boasts remarkable chandeliers and a high ceiling. And the sophisticated cuisine is on a par with this romantic setting. First-rate ingredients are used to create a menu that successfully blends classic and modern dishes. Choose from the à la carte menu, which includes vegetarian options, or the four- to six-course set menu. The wine pairings are on point, and the team is attentive and knowledgeable. Tasteful guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Atempo
Description: This spacious and contemporary restaurant will surprise guests as soon as they walk through the door as they are accompanied to two kitchens, for hot and cold food respectively, in which they can try a pleasant array of appetisers and small snacks before being ushered into the elegant dining room.Chef Iñaki Aldrey offers his cuisine with the option of an à la carte menu and two tasting menus designed by celebrity chef Jordi Cruz (Atempo and Gran Atempo), showcasing contemporary cooking and techniques that aim to highlight the depth of flavours, something they succeed in here thanks to top-quality ingredients and highly consistent combinations. The interplay between the kitchen and the service in the dining room is particularly impressive, as the finishing touches to many dishes are added in front of the guests’ eyes. Try the Galician sea urchin with carabinero tartar and Ossetra caviar or the hare royale with a black garlic emulsion and roast pumpkin and white garlic cream – a French-inspired recipe combining both flavour and solid technique.

Name: Atlantic Restaurant
Description: The elegant Atlantic Restaurant is entirely in keeping with the Hanseatic flair of the luxe Hotel Atlantic by the banks of the River Alster. Using excellent ingredients, chef Fokke Mick proposes the set menu, "Identité", alongside its vegetarian counterpart, "Flora" – in both cases, diners choose from four to seven courses. In addition, there is a three-course menu for two people with the restaurant's classics, such as lobster bisque and whole sole. The appealing classic decor provides a perfectly fitting setting. Last but not least, the front-of-house team is experienced, extremely cordial and professional.

Name: Atlas
Address: The St. Regis Atlanta, 88 W. Paces Ferry Rd. NW, Atlanta, GA, 30305, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: When the night calls for a grand celebration, few places fit quite like Atlas. Snuggled inside the posh St. Regis Atlanta, this restaurant from London-born Chef Freddy Money is impossibly elegant. Fine art graces the walls — it's home to rotating installations in partnership with a local gallery, showcasing works from local, national, and internationally acclaimed artistsv — but it's not just the artwork that impresses. Order à la carte from this seasonal American menu with European influences or celebrate with the tasting menu for dishes like tender lobster plated with smoked paprika butter sauce and heirloom summer squash, and sherry-caramelized sweetbreads with delicately smoked potato espuma. Wagyu beef from Australia is a decadent end to the savory courses. Bespoke cocktails including original zero-proof options, a cheese cart and whimsical desserts complete the well-rounded experience.

Name: Atmosphères
Address: 618 route des Tournelles, Le Bourget-du-Lac, 73370, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: From Lamartine to Stendhal and Maupassant, many a French author has waxed lyrical about the atmosphere of Lac du Bourget and the view over Mt Revard. For his part, Chef Alain Perrillat-Mercerot has made the lake and mountains the splendid backdrop against which he serves his delicate, creative cuisine that fervently champions the Savoie terroir. Classically trained, his high-precision preparation of freshwater fish, local cheeses and wild blueberries is second to none – choose between two carefully composed single-choice set menus. The fantastic wine list fetes local grape varieties (among others).

Name: Attablez-vous
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Take a seat, as the restaurant’s name orders, and admire the ornamental tree that jazzes up the elegantly stylish contemporary interior, also home to an authentic cheese cave where all sorts of delicacies ripen slowly. Now let’s add attentive service and tips from the knowledgeable sommelier, who gets a kick out of suggesting unusual wines, and the scene is set. Chef Charles-Edouard Jeandrain mixes playful ideas with timeless classical flavours, conjuring up a fascinating repertory that demonstrates his respect for the ingredient and his quest for varied textures. He may prepare paella-style rice, adding stuffed txistorra squid, whose powerful flavour he offsets by deep-fried mussels and a coulis and purée of smoked paprika. Art-directed, intelligent plating contributes to whetting the appetite of diners and, even better, it is possible to mix and swap dishes from the different set menus. We recommend the Prestige menu, if you feel like splashing out and treating yourself to exceptional produce.

Name: Atto di Vito Mollica
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A few steps from the Duomo, within the Corte degli Imperatori of Palazzo Portinari, the historic former residence of the Salviati family, the restaurant occupies a setting of rare beauty, enriched by sixteenth-century frescoes by Alessandro Allori and the soothing sound of a fountain. An authentic Renaissance salon transformed into a refined dining room. The kitchen distinguishes itself through technical precision and elegance, bringing out the very best of the highest-quality produce in dishes that are creative yet always balanced and never contrived. Emblematic is the lightly seared langoustine, served over two mirror sauces – one sweet and aromatic with carrot and orange, the other more acidic and buttery with Champagne. Attentive and considered service accompanies the experience with expertise, from the wine pairing through to the final dedication to coffee.

Name: Au 14 Février
Description: Au 14 Février stands on rue du Bœuf, among the Renaissance mansions, cobbled streets and arcaded galleries in the heart of historical Lyon. A wonderful location in which to sample the surprise menu of chef Tsuyoshi Arai, whose talent and imagination are no longer up for discussion. Born in Kyoto, he belongs to the large family of Japanese chefs who have fallen for France's culinary heritage. He elevates exceptionally fresh ingredients (Miéral poultry, Wagyu beef) by playing on textures, bitterness and acidity: peas, broad beans and snow peas with tamarind, crab and caviar; beetroot tarte tatin with strawberries and foie gras; squab cooked over a cherry wood fire… At every meal, he enchants his clientele with his seasonal symphony. On top of that, the service is extremely obliging.

Name: Au 1465
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Drawing on his extensive experience in starred restaurants, Mariano Buda rolls out a modern score of classical inspiration dotted with Italian and alpine notes in his partially screened kitchen. The marbled fillet of beef in puff pastry, textures of chard, pistachio and marigolds is emblematic of his spot-on, flavoursome style. The à la carte and vegetarian menus star local produce, polished plating and light sauces. Housed in the swanky Au Club Alpin Hotel, the restaurant commands a stunning view over Champex-Lac and the peaks, that is even more jaw-dropping from the window tables. Before or after your meal, make a beeline for the hotel’s lovely bar, or indulge in a stroll around the peaceful lake…

Name: Au Coin des Bons Enfants
Description: Au Coin des Bons Enfants holds an important place in Maastricht's culinary history having received its first MICHELIN Star back in 1957. Driven by youthful energy, Timo Reichelt and sommelier Lino de Vrede are now writing a new chapter that pays all due respect to the past, maintaining the establishment's elegant and romantic ambience, including a fabulous secluded terrace. Chef Reichelt's cooking puts the produce centre stage. His style is rather classic, enhanced by his knack for drawing the very best out of quality ingredients and his talent for spectacular sauces. The deep flavour of a beurre blanc enriched with icewine, for example, perfectly ties together pan-seared North Sea turbot and a succulent cut of Livar pork. Or he pan-fries yearling venison the meat to a perfect medium-rare and finishes it with a glossy, rich sauce grand veneur and the sweet, vibrant tang of redcurrants. This is indulgent traditional fare prepared by a young chef with a sound grasp of flavours. The finesse of the dishes is accentuated by the wines. The sommelier delights in sharing his passion for Pinot Noir and wines from the Old World, which are also available by the glass.

Name: Au Crocodile
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The stuffed crocodile in the window, a souvenir brought back from Egypt by a Napoleonic soldier, underlines the historic character of this iconic Strasbourg establishment, which was the HQ of chef Émile Jung for many a year. The interior sports a stylish modern edge but has nonetheless preserved the venue’s period charm. Chef Romain Brillat, former second of Gilles Goujon and a distant relative of Brillat-Savarin, a famous French gourmet, has achieved a balance between classicism and sophistication. Examples include his original take on cherry-picked noble produce: Tarbouriech oysters, wild turbot, summer venison…

Name: Au Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Two enthusiastic partners, Ludovic Kientz and sommelier Sandie Ling, are at the helm of this venerable country inn set in a large garden. In this plush, snug interior, bathed in light, the chef takes obvious pleasure in crafting sauces and working with premium ingredients, including from his own garden, to deliver spot-on cuisine with a hint of classicism. Friendly, seamless service.

Name: Au Gré du Vent
Description: A meal at Au Gré du Vent offers a splendid opportunity to explore the magnificent Hainaut countryside. Stéphanie and Sébastien Thunus converted a former barn into a fantastic restaurant, whose floor-to-ceiling windows open onto a landscaped garden. The visitor is initially impressed by the venue’s elegance, before sinking into its all-embracing cosy cocoon. Chef Stéphanie Thunus is a perfectionist who aims to make each dish a work of art with a distinct fondness for local, seasonal produce, such as game from Ardennes. Her culinary creations are subtle, distinctive and generous and nothing leaves her kitchen that hasn’t been endlessly puzzled and preened over. For example, she prepares tomatoes grown by her local producer in different ways, further jazzing them up with a bittersweet fresh dressing or she may underscore melt-in-the-mouth Limousin veal with a punchy gravy, a sauce made out of broad beans and agnolotti stuffed with aubergine caviar that will set your tastebuds tingling. Stephanie’s parents' farm, which supplies the butter and cheese among others, is just opposite and Ms Thunus has inherited a farmer’s respect for the ingredient to which she adds her own distinctive culinary flair. Stéphanie and Sébastien also run the Au Fil de l’Eau Hotel, whose elegant guestrooms provide the perfect climax to this fine dining experience.

Name: Au Jardin
Address: The Warehouse@Hin Bus Depot, 125 Jalan Timah, George Town, 10150, Malaysia
Description: This distressed building clad in corrugated metal panels is housed inside a bus depot-turned art space. The low-key exterior is however a stark contrast to the modern, sleek interior. The tasting menu showcases creative, sophisticated European fare with subtle local twists. The signature hay-aged Penang duck uses 90-day-old local birds that offer leaner meat and a robust flavour. Homemade sourdough with tomato butter is another standout.

Name: Au Vieux Couvent
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Set near the flower-decked banks of the Brunnwasser, this inviting building catches the eye from afar with its earthy beige hue and traditional half-timbering typical of the Bas-Rhin. Alexis Albrecht's generous cuisine is in step with the seasons and makes the most of the terroir and local produce. As you might expect, fish from the Rhine and game from the Ried take pride of place here. He also draws on an abundance of vegetables and aromatic herbs from the family's kitchen garden, which he and his father cultivate.

Name: Auberge Chez Guth
Description: In the Villé valley, this old farmhouse in the upper reaches of the village of Steige provides the canvas on which chef Yannick Guth expresses his culinary creativity. His dishes draw on local produce, foraged ingredients (eg herbs and flowers from the surrounding fields) and freshwater fish (pike, zander, Arctic char). His sense of invention is sometimes surprising, but always confident and judicious. Make a beeline for the pleasant terrace, which offers sweeping views of the rolling landscape – the perfect spot for an aperitif or coffee. A friendly welcome and service.

Name: Auberge Frankenbourg
Address: 13 rue du Général-de-Gaulle, La Vancelle, 67730, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this small village perched in the foothills of the Vosges, this hotel-restaurant has been welcoming travellers since the start of the last century. The Buecher brothers, who took over the reins of this family business from their parents, preside with cheerful enthusiasm. The delicious and refined cuisine of the elder brother, Sébastien, showcases the best of the terroir in the form of a menu that is always changing. He puts a creative spin on traditional dishes, as exemplified by the veal chop, double ravioli and sauce ravigote with calf's foot. Most of the fruit and vegetables come from their own garden. Front of house, the younger brother Guillaume operates with poise, in a minimalist decor tempered by the warmth of wood panelling. There are pretty guestrooms.

Name: Auberge Grand'Maison
Description: This eminently hospitable inn upholds culinary traditions rich in textbook technique and indulgent, spot-on flavours. Christophe Le Fur, born at Cap Fréhel, is thriving in his homeland as he crafts bold, crisp dishes oozing in generosity. The chef, who cherry-picks his ingredients, demonstrates the full scope of his talents (particularly in the field of sauces, one of the house’s signatures!). Brittany lobster and sweetbread sautéed in butter with creamy morels in Noilly; poultry pie in a tarragon jus; without forgetting the flamboyant crêpe flambée to finish your meal on a high.

Name: Auberge Le Prieuré
Description: On the road between Bordeaux and Toulouse, in the heart of a tiny picturesque village near Agen, this country inn occupies a centuries-old stone house, whose terrace, shaded by ancient plane trees, faces a Clunisian priory founded in the 11C. A former consort of Michel Trama of Puymirol, chef Benjamin Toursel has forged his own distinctive modern style, scattered with bold, creative notes that frequently surprise the diner: mouth-wateringly juicy red tuna with a wasabi made out of roses, rhubarb and rose geranium; rack of veal, raw and cooked carrots and nasturtium-flavoured béarnaise. A priory devoted to fine dining…

Name: Auberge Pom'Poire
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This contemporary restaurant surrounded by orchards has a bright, welcoming, clean-lined dining area that looks onto the surrounding countryside. Full of verve and creativity, Bastien Gillet's colourful, zesty cuisine is as subtle as it is finely judged, both in terms of the aromas and the textures; his dishes, laden with top-notch farm produce from the region, are rife with flavours. And the detail to seal the deal: the dishes are served in delightful crockery that is handmade locally. The menu is liable to change daily, in accordance with the chef's inspiration. Suffice to say, this restaurant that pushes the boundaries with delicious fare has plenty to recommend it, so why not take a bite?

Name: Auberge Quintessence
Description: At the Col de la Couillole, a pass in the Mercantour National Park, this former refuge run by Pauline and Christophe Billau is a top destination for foodies. These two serve up a warm welcome and a single set menu that draws inspiration from the mountains and changes with the seasons. Diners can indulge in creamy local mountain nettle cappuccino, superb roasted white asparagus, whether tangy with candied citrus fruit or in a sabayon sauce, or lightly smoked Mediterranean tuna served confit-style and subtly counterbalanced by the herbal notes of oxalis. Dishes such as veal from the Plateau de Longon accompanied by confit shallots and a courgette flower filled with pine nuts and a herb cream are brimming with skilfully mastered flavours, while the cheeses are carefully matured. There's nothing superfluous or artificial about this place! A few prettily decorated guestrooms are up for grabs for overnight stays.

Name: Auberge Saint-Laurent
Address: 1 rue de la Fontaine, Sierentz, 68510, France
Description: This inviting 18C coaching inn with its long, flower-decked façade is an authentic and elegant local institution. Chef Laurent Arbeit presides over the kitchen, having honed his skills at Haeberlin and Ducasse. He continues the family tradition by working with Alsace's finest ingredients, such as duck foie gras, Sundgau pink trout, milk-fed veal chop and farm-raised squab. The delicate and harmonious cuisine of this proprietor who is very much in tune with the times is replete with well-balanced flavours. The guestrooms are decorated in Alsace style.

Name: Auberge Saint-Mathieu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed
Description: Located near La Mauricie National Park, on the shores of Lake Bellemare, this country inn surrounded by forest is picture postcard perfect. Chef Samy Benabed crafts exquisitely plated, locally sourced cuisine, harmoniously blending heroically vibrant flavours depicted by smoky BBQ aromas and preserved foods of Scandinavian inspiration (lacto-fermentation, dehydration, etc.) with Quebec spices and citrus fruits. A case in point is his trompe l’oeil dumpling (a steamed rabiole) stuffed with pork in a white miso stock with matsutake. Simpler fare (summertime only) at the Comptoir buvette and also a small grocery store. Book yourself into one of 10 cosy guestrooms - just the ticket to recharge your batteries.

Name: Auberge Saint-Walfrid
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the road from Metz to Strasbourg, this pretty little inn – once a farm belonging to the church in Welferding – has been run by the same family since the late 19C. Having taken over from his father who built up the auberge’s gastronomic reputation in the region, Stephan Schneider (fifth generation) is now at the helm here. Guests dine in a large, plush and warmly decorated dining room with old parquet flooring and cabinets laden with gleaming Sarreguemines earthenware. The chef is a staunch champion of tradition who works with local market gardeners (he also has his own kitchen garden) and buys whole animals that he prepares himself, including cured meats. Spacious guestrooms are also available.

Name: Auberge Sauvage
Description: This charming, rustic16C presbytery in the heart of a photogenic country village on the road to Mont Saint Michel is home to a restaurant flanked by a cottage garden. The latter provides chef Thomas Benady with plenty of produce (veg, fruit, aromatic herbs, flowers…) and inspiration for his single set surprise menu. Benady also works with small local producers and independent fishermen.
