Address: Via Ronco 1, Villa Zarri, Castel Maggiore, 40013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in Villa Zarri, a historic family residence where one of the most famous brandies in Italy was created, this restaurant is home to chef Agostino Iacobucci, who creates a culinary bridge between his native Campania and the Bologna region. His dishes include a delicious rabbit alla genovese, a type of Neapolitan stew, served with a scamorza cheese and herb cream and topped with shavings of local black truffle. The impressive wine list boasts a selection of vertical labels including prestigious wines such as Sassicaia and Tignanello, with over ten different vintages available. The villa also offers a convenient car park and a delightful garden which is perfect for a stroll either before or after your meal.

Name: Ibaya
Description: The gastronomic restaurant at the Sport Hotel Hermitage (which also boasts other dining options) is overseen by chef Francis Paniego, a leading Spanish chef with two Michelin stars whose brilliance is also on display at his El Portal de Echaurren restaurant in Ezcaray, and Jordi Grau, the resident chef.The cuisine here is based around two creative tasting menus: A Walk through the Incles Valley, and another, more extensive, called A Walk through Andorra. They strive to bring Andorran gastronomy and its flavours to the fore, paying tribute to the rural part of the principality where the raw ingredients come from, but always opening the door to some international touches (a good example is their fantastic mountain ramen). The experience starts in the reception area with a few insights into the chef, continues with appetisers (both in the ‘Chester’ sofa space, and the kitchen) and concludes in the dining room. The fun appetisers, with references to the seasons, feature a surprising interactive element!

Name: Icca
Address: 20 Warren St., New York, NY, 10007, USA
Description: Chef counters are a treat, but a seat in front of Chef Kazushige Suzuki feels like a best-kept secret. The room has a presence of its own, notable in scale and hidden away in the back past a cocktail bar. Friendly as ever and seemingly never in a hurry, the chef sources fish entirely from Japan and keeps his nigiri traditional with little more adornment than a brushing of nikiri.Other dishes that bookend the meal flex far more creativity and panache. Hokkaido hairy crab with capellini and shiso or snow trout marinated in koji for seven days are uniquely satisfying, while beef sourced from Japan makes regular appearances. At the meal’s end, disbelief may turn into wonder as guests dive into apple sorbet boldly topped with Yamazaki 12 whisky.

Name: Ich weiß ein Haus am See
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Somewhere between Berlin and Rostock, in the middle of nowhere... This idyllic spot is a place in which to slow down and unwind – the name of the road, Paradiesweg, is apt. Set beside a secluded lake, the small hotel offers far more than just a comfortable overnight stay. Raik Zeigner, head chef since 2005, excels in the classic culinary style that has long been a hallmark of the house. His four-course set menu is different every evening and showcases carefully chosen seasonal ingredients, from hot-smoked sea bass and exceptionally fresh turbot with fine roasted notes to flavoursome veal fillet. The location is equally appealing, combining lake views with elegant country-house charm. The impressive wood-burning stove at the centre of the dining room is just one of many attractive upscale details that create a welcoming atmosphere, complemented by the heartfelt enthusiasm of hosts Petra and Adi König. The owner – virtually a walking wine encyclopaedia – unfailingly recommends the perfect pairings. The next generation is also already involved in the running of this delightful family business.

Name: Ichiju Nisai Ueno Minoten
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: A Japanese restaurant at the foot of the Minoh mountains. The head chef weaves the turning of the seasons into his menu. Hassun platters are arranged on large plates using several small dishes, then garnished with leaves gathered on the mountainside. Tempura, prepared with rice oil, is light in texture. If you reserve a seat on the ground floor, the tempura master will fry each piece right before your eyes. Dine with relish on the bounty of nature, serenaded by the murmuring Minoh River.

Name: Idylio by Apreda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In an elegant dining room decorated in shades of blue and orange, Francesco Apreda’s cuisine takes shape: a gastronomic narrative that weaves together Asian influences and Italian tradition, the result of the chef’s experiences in the East. The offering unfolds through clear tasting menus: ‘Iconic Signature’, dedicated to the dishes that have defined his career; ‘Eco dal Mare’, centred on the marine world; and the vegetarian ‘Green Butterfly’. Alongside these is ‘Idylio’s Butterfly’, a four-course menu that allows you to choose from a range of great classics and new creations, offering the utmost freedom of choice. The wine list is well-curated and extensive, with particular emphasis on the wines available by the glass.

Name: Iggy's
Address: voco Orchard, Level 3, 581 Orchard Road, 238883, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: A picture window in this elegantly furnished room gives diners a front-row view of the kitchen team in action. The tasting menu served at dinner features multiple courses that showcase top-notch produce from Japan and France, such as Miyazaki Wagyu and Bresse pigeon, deftly crafted with European techniques. There is also a plant-based menu for vegans. With thousands of labels from Burgundy, the wine list is worth perusing.

Name: Ikaro
Description: Nestled in the heart of Logroño, Ikaro is unique and has undoubtedly become one of the most exciting establishments on the La Rioja culinary scene—a must-visit if you want to understand avant-garde cuisine in the region. The duo in the kitchen (Carolina Sánchez and Iñaki Murua) have successfully developed their own unique fusion style, one that blends her Ecuadorian roots, his Basque heritage, and, of course, that magnificent selection of locally sourced ingredients that speaks volumes about this region. Seasonal produce takes centre stage here, featuring in both the à la carte menu and the set menus (Corto, Descubrir and Ikaro), with standout dishes such as the red prawn salpicón with salad and smoked tomato water—a wonderfully harmonious dish that masterfully encapsulates the restaurant’s philosophy. The experience is rounded off with a carefully curated selection of wines, showcasing how the great wines of La Rioja complement other international wines.

Name: Il Bavaglino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant now occupies new premises in an old building once used for salting fish, its style of cuisine (featured on three tasting menus, “Storie e passioni”, “Mura di Casa”, and the vegetarian “Erba Terra Foglie”, from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style) remains unchanged. Inspired by regional traditions, chef Giuseppe Costa creates personalised and imaginative dishes that are influenced by local flavours and his past culinary experience, proving himself to be equally at ease with fish and meat options. Our inspector particularly recommends the local purple prawns, served raw with caviar and olives and a lemon and ginger coulis.

Name: Il Bocconcino by Royal Hideaway
Address: Avenida Virgen de Guadalupe 21, La Caleta, Adeje, 38679, Spain
Description: If you’re looking for an Italian restaurant with a difference, this dining space in the Royal Hideaway Corales Suites hotel won’t disappoint thanks to its superb terrace (which we highly recommend for lunch or dinner in fine weather) and its re-creation of Italian recipes from a relatively modern and progressive perspective, with the added attraction of always using (with the exception of the irreplaceable Pecorino and Parmesan) local ingredients sourced from the island. Chef Niki Pavanelli, who is originally from Bologna and can often be seen passing from table to table to explain his dishes, complements the à la carte with two extensive menus (Identidad and Il Boccocino). Don’t miss his updated Carbonara 3.0, Il Tortellino, which rekindles memories of his grandmother (la nonna) or, last but not least, the La Scarpetta dessert, through which he invites guests to discover the time-honoured Italian technique of the same name (the expression is “fare la scarpetta”) which consists of completely mopping up your plate with bread as a symbol of appreciation.

Name: Il Buco
Address: II rampa Marina Piccola 5, Sorrento, 80067, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sorrento, the restaurant offers guests the chance to choose from a range of dining areas, each with its own distinct charm but all equally atmospheric. You can dine in the historic dining room, which was converted from a 16th-century cellar once used by the monks as a storeroom, or in the more contemporary areas, which feature a spectacular open-plan wine cellar housing over 1,600 bottles. In the warmer months, the outdoor tables set out along the picturesque entrance staircase add further charm to the experience. The cuisine draws primarily on the traditions of Campania, alternating between seafood and meat dishes, while also incorporating personal interpretations and creative touches that enrich the menu. The dining experience can be tailored either through tasting menus or by choosing freely from an extensive and varied à la carte menu. Among the most impressive dishes were the tacos with ‘minestra maritata’ and tomato ice cream – a successful example of cuisine that blends tradition with modernity.

Name: Il Cantinone e Sport Hotel Alpina
Address: Via A. De Giacomi 39, Madesimo, 23024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A family restaurant run with passion and pride, Il Cantinone welcomes guests on a culinary journey dedicated to the region’s gastronomic treasures, from the mountains to the lake. Buckwheat, trout and eel, venison, polenta, mushrooms, potatoes and truffles are just some of the ingredients that define the authentic spirit of the contemporary dishes created by chef Stefano Masanti.Every now and then, exotic twists appear, inspirations gathered during his travels and brought back to his beloved mountains, capable of adding depth and intrigue to the culinary offering.Working alongside him is Thomas Locatelli, a remarkably talented and highly creative young chef, whose presence brings a touch of freshness and innovation to the kitchen, helping to refine and expand Il Cantinone’s gastronomic identity.

Name: Il Cantuccio
Description: This welcoming, beautifully kept restaurant in the heart of the verdant Brianza region has two dining rooms: one with exposed stonework that gives it a rustic feel, the other more modern and elegant in style. Chef Mauro Elli moves easily between classic Italian favourites, occasionally adding his own individual touch to the dishes. His imaginative reinterpretations demonstrate a fascination with the sea (despite the restaurant’s geographical location), while the menu also offers “daily game specials” throughout the year. One of the most delicious dishes on the menu is the bottoni pasta in a Milanese sauce, served with tender quail and parmesan cream.

Name: Il Cappero
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Today, the cuisine stands out for its exceptionally high standard of quality, underpinned by a clear and distinctive vision. The two tasting menus – available in a more basic version and a more extensive one – showcase a concept centred on the ingredients themselves, which are predominantly local and seasonal, interpreted with technical precision within a contemporary Mediterranean style. At the heart of this philosophy lies the single-protein approach: each dish showcases a single main ingredient, bringing out its full flavour and minimising any superfluous elements. In this context, the care taken in the ageing of the fish stands out in particular; this practice imparts depth and complexity without altering the product’s original character. There is no shortage of elegant nods to European culinary tradition, such as the measured use of French-style sauces or the judicious use of fermentation techniques, which are incorporated with balance, without overpowering. The dessert course is a moment of genuine pleasure: after an initial tasting served at the table, the experience moves to the pastry corner, where the final dessert is prepared on the spot according to the guests’ preferences. To top it all off, the Therasia Resort enjoys a spectacular setting on the Vulcanello headland, from where the terrace offers an unrivalled view of the Aeolian archipelago, often enhanced by sunsets of extraordinary colour.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Address: Le Royal Monceau, 37 avenue Hoche, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Royal Monceau, the corridor leading to your table is embedded with thousands of mother-of-pearl shells, in an elaborate and artistic tribute to the nymphs of Italian Baroque. The dining room, set in what looks like a conservatory painted in spring colours, resembles a genuine winter garden flanked by an alfresco area. In the kitchen, Oliver Piras and Alessandra Del Favero subtly conjure up Italian dishes that are deliciously free of fussy nonsense. Their cooking is meticulous, spot on and flavoursome and aims to highlight the natural tastes and flavours of painstakingly selected star ingredients. The same approach is true of the wine cellar which demonstrates a distinct soft spot for Piedmont and Tuscan wines.

Name: Il Centro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A breath of immortality hovers over this restaurant, where great Piedmontese cuisine finds one of its finest expressions thanks to the Cordero family. Elide at the stoves, her husband Enrico and son Giampiero in the dining room – the latter a profound wine connoisseur and guardian of an extraordinary, ever-growing cellar – carry forward with passion a venue taken over by Giampiero’s grandparents in 1956. Here, tradition takes center stage with hearty, flavor-rich dishes that never tire: from bread agnolotti filled with anchovy and a hint of thyme to the classic braised cheek with caramelized figs. In summer, the offering lightens with some seafood options, while an autumn visit calls for a proper white truffle dish; we suggest the classic egg tajarin. In January, February, and March, the legendary fritto misto del Centro returns, an epic 12-course sequence from savory to sweet, to be reserved well in advance. Just steps from the restaurant are the elegant rooms of Dimora Cordero.

Name: Il Convivio Troiani
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: A restaurant of solid tradition, born in the early 1990s from the vision of three brothers from the Marche region – Angelo, Giuseppe, and Massimo: the first at the stoves, the others in the dining room. Over time, this establishment has become a benchmark in Roman dining thanks to a cuisine of strong authorial character, presented through two elaborate tasting menus – one entirely dedicated to the vegetable world. These menus can be adapted in length and are structured by seasonal rhythms and a constant dialog with Italy’s gastronomic roots. Iconic dishes are available to complement the experience, such as the celebrated “Amatriciana dei Troiani,” on the menu since 1996, or the local lamb. In the cellar, some 3,600 labels form a monumental wine list, featuring vertical selections dating back to the 1990s, true rarities for connoisseurs and collectors. Thanks to Coravin, several of these gems can also be enjoyed by the glass.

Name: Il Cortile
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a pedestrian street of historic Mulhouse, welcome to a 16C building that is a something of a culinary landmark with the locals. Chef Jean-Michel Feger has been rolling out Mediterranean-inspired cuisine here since 2001. Think mouth-watering, technically polished, modern dishes with a distinct Italian twang: saffron-spiked creamy risotto, squid, broad beans and spicy ventricina. In fine weather, soak up la dolce vita and enjoy your meal alfresco on the patio of the small courtyard. Pleasant, unstarched service.

Name: Il Desco
Address: Via Dietro San Sebastiano 7, Verona, 37121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Housed in a fifteenth-century palazzo, the dining room showcases hand-painted exposed ceiling beams paired with exquisite taste alongside Murano glass lamps and chandeliers, complemented by contemporary artwork. Guests sink into the signature leather armchairs to savor an outstanding meal in what may well be one of Verona’s most refined drawing rooms. Opened in 1982 by patriarch Elia, the restaurant is now in the capable hands of his talented son, Matteo Rizzo, who presents a series of tasting menus alongside a focused à la carte selection offering three to five courses. An exceptional wine list is expertly guided by the knowledgeable sommelier.

Name: Il Fagiano
Address: Corso Zanardelli 190, Fasano del Garda, 25083, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set within the elegant surroundings of the Grand Hotel Fasano, the restaurant welcomes guests into a refined dining room where wood, the dominant feature of the décor, helps to create a warm and cosy atmosphere. In the warmer months, however, it is hard to resist the splendid panoramic terrace – the property’s real highlight – from which the view stretches out over the lake, offering a sight of rare beauty. Maurizio Bufi’s culinary offering comprises tasting menus – including one dedicated to plant-based dishes – and an à la carte selection. While there are certainly references to Puglia, his homeland, and to the lake district where he is based, his cuisine stands out above all for its creative and contemporary approach, which draws freely on ingredients and influences from various Italian regions, while respecting the seasonality and quality of the raw ingredients.

Name: Il Falconiere
Address: Località San Martino a Bocena 370, Cortona, 52044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: To get to this exclusive restaurant, you drive through an idyllic landscape of small lanes lined with dry-stone walls and fields belonging to the Baracchi farm estate, of which Il Falconiere and the magnificent hotel of the same name are a part. Many of the ingredients served here, such as wine and olive oil, are produced on the estate and the restaurant’s strong connection with its local landscapes is evident. Specialities such as Chianina beef, local garlic and pici pasta feature in dishes spiced with aromatic herbs and full of the strong flavours of Tuscany.

Name: Il Flauto di Pan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Perched on the promontory of Ravello, Villa Cimbrone is one of the most fascinating and romantic historic residences in Italy. Surrounded by centuries-old gardens that culminate in the celebrated Terrazza dell'Infinito, one of the most iconic panoramas on the Amalfi Coast, it offers a setting of rare beauty. The gastronomic restaurant, housed within the elegant spaces of the villa, allows guests to dine both in the refined interior dining room and on the terrace overlooking the sea. Before dinner, guests may access the Terrazza dell'Infinito, a privilege that renders the experience all the more memorable. The service is attentive and professional, and the cellar represents one of the great strengths of this establishment. The chef offers seafood, meat and vegetarian tasting menus, with an elegant and contemporary cuisine that celebrates the produce of the local area.

Name: Il Fuoco Sacro
Address: Strada di Buddeo, San Pantaleo, 07026, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The very name of the resort where it is situated, Petra Segreta, evokes a secluded and picturesque spot, nestled among the Mediterranean scrub that surrounds the village of San Pantaleo. Il Fuoco Sacro overlooks a magnificent garden and enjoys a spectacular view stretching all the way to the coast. Luigi Bergeretto and Alessandro Menditto are at the helm in the kitchen, offering a contemporary menu that showcases the quality of the ingredients and pays close attention to the local area. Particular emphasis is placed on the aromatic herbs and vegetables grown in the estate’s vegetable garden, which feature prominently in many dishes, while a few beehives provide a small supply of artisan honey. An interesting selection of wines rounds off the experience. Finally, Enrico Bartolini is orchestrating the culinary project, a presence that serves as further assurance of excellence.

Name: Il Gallo Cedrone
Address: Via Cima Tosa 80, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Attention: closed for renovation!Within the Hotel Bertelli, the restaurant’s dining room offers an authentically alpine atmosphere, with a style that inspires both elegance and conviviality. The kitchen presents two tasting menus (plus a vegetarian alternative): the first inspired by the territory, the second featuring classics from other regions with seafood. Dishes may also be selected à la carte according to preference. Equally impressive is the wine cellar, with over 800 labels carefully curated by owner Marco Masè alongside veteran sommelier Giuseppe Greco, and a particular passion for gin and tonic.

Name: Il Lago
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The iconic Four Seasons hotel, Geneva’s oldest luxury hotel (1834), dripping with pilasters and frescoes, is the setting of Il Lago, or Lake Geneva’s classy remake of the dolce vita. The kitchen team offers high-flying Italian cuisine, with the odd Mediterranean accent, rich in aromas, subtlety and delicacy. The quintessence of fine dining.

Name: Il Luogo Aimo e Nadia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A leading figure on the Milanese gastronomic scene for over sixty years, this historic establishment continues to attract lovers of haute cuisine thanks to a menu that celebrates Italian produce and regions with a contemporary twist. The two tasting menus created by Alessandro Negrini and Fabio Pisani elegantly highlight the Lombard roots of the former and the Apulian roots of the latter. As well as the set menus, you can also choose from the à la carte menu, selecting at least two dishes in addition to a dessert. Aimo’s ‘Piatti del Cuore’ are a must-try, including the iconic durum wheat spaghettoni with fresh spring onions, chilli, extra virgin olive oil and Ligurian basil. The extensive wine list, which can be viewed on a tablet, is also well worth a look; it features rare wines and real gems for connoisseurs. The attentive and considerate service discreetly complements the whole experience.

Name: Il Marin
Address: Calata Cattaneo, 15, Edificio Millo, Porto Antico, Genoa, 16121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Old Port, within the same building’s floor that houses Eataly, the dining area thrives on simplicity to accentuate the panorama witnessed through glazed walls, while competent service, primarily female, tends to guests warmly. The cuisine pivots around 'territory', primarily maritime, yet is rejuvenated through modern techniques and ideas; for example, the Martini cocktail spaghetti, shaken in the dining room by Chef Marco Visciola, enriched with algae butter, Martini sauce, caviar, and nebulised Taggiasco gin, as well as the roasted monkfish cooked in bay leaf, almond hummus, kale, and caper Mugnaia. A varied selection exists, also à la carte, within the three tasting formulae presented.

Name: Il Palagio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Il Palagio is the ideal choice for anyone wishing to enjoy an evening of elegance and timeless charm. Housed in the extraordinary Palazzo della Gherardesca, it winds its way through sumptuous rooms leading to the restaurant, featuring fine marble, elegant furnishings and splendid Murano chandeliers. The gastronomic offering features three tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, as well as the option to choose from the à la carte menu. The cuisine focuses on high-quality ingredients, prepared with restraint and a contemporary sensitivity, avoiding unnecessary excess and prioritising balance and flavour. A first-class experience, set against one of Florence’s most picturesque backdrops.

Name: Il Papavero
Description: Papavero is the Italian for poppy, a plant which grows tall and has strong roots, making it an apt symbol for this restaurant housed in a palazzo in the town centre. In a few classic-style rooms, the chef offers a menu that focuses on fish and seafood, although ingredients from the surrounding countryside also feature. Simple, solid recipes made with just a few ingredients, exactly as described on the menu, and a passionate dedication to the Mediterranean result in attractive cuisine which also offers good value for money. In fine weather, meals are served outdoors under the jasmine in a romantic garden. A restaurant that appeals to the heart as well as the palate.

Name: Il Patio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: After more than thirty years of business at its historic premises in Pollone, the Vineis family’s restaurant has moved to the centre of Biella, inside the so-called ‘Palazzone’, in completely refurbished premises that once housed private clubs. The project is currently being developed along two distinct but complementary paths. On the one hand, there is Il Patio, the restaurant’s most contemporary venue, where Simone Vineis – supported by his father Sergio’s expertise and presence – offers a menu that follows the seasons and the inspiration of the moment, with a particular focus on meat, while also venturing into other culinary territories. On the other hand, there’s Il Circolo Bistrot, a more informal and relaxed setting, designed for those seeking the pleasure of good food in a convivial and laid-back atmosphere. Two establishments under one roof, united by a long family history and a well-established culture of hospitality.

Name: Il Pellicano
Address: Località Lo Sbarcatello, Porto Ercole, 58018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Chef Michelino Gioia from Campania, now a Tuscan by adoption, is in charge of fine dining at the famous resort Il Pellicano, whose terrace overlooking the sea, enhanced by the scent of rosemary in the air, makes it one of the most romantic addresses in Italy. Michelino, thanks to a good technique, is highly skilled in creating different textures in the same dish while retaining the precise flavours of the excellent ingredients used, both land and sea (excellent, for example, the cooking of the pezzogna, which remains soft, accompanied by small quenelles of pappa al pomodoro in a creamy version, mussels and lovage). His work is - finally - enhanced by a very extensive wine list and, above all, by the friendly and professional service offered by the numerous staff.

Name: Il Piastrino
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The home of Claudia and Riccardo, Il Piastrino is the realization of a long‑nurtured dream, lovingly refined and enriched year after year amid the rolling hills of Montefeltro. Here, the warmth and simplicity of the countryside blend harmoniously with contemporary details and furnishings. At the heart of it all is chef Agostini’s cuisine which, supported by technical mastery and creativity, brings out the best in seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. His complex and carefully constructed dishes never feel contrived, but instead convey his vision with balance and flavour, occasionally extending their reach into Tuscany. No sea fish here, but freshwater species such as trout and eel, meat dishes are more frequent, and particular interest is shown in aromatic herbs, as well as the outstanding mushrooms of a picturesque territory between hill and mountain.

Name: Il Pievano
Address: Località Spaltenna 13, Gaiole in Chianti, 53013, Italy
Description: In the kitchen, a contemporary cuisine with a distinctive character takes shape, skilfully blending Mediterranean flavours and international influences while remaining firmly rooted in the Tuscan region that is its home. The culinary offering is organised around two tasting menus, ‘Brace Ardente’ and ‘Transverberazione’, which differ in their inspiration and composition but are united by a meticulous focus on ingredients and remarkable precision in execution. In the warmer months, the experience is made even more enjoyable thanks to the tables set up in the romantic tranquillity of the ancient courtyard. When it comes to wine, let yourself be guided by a cellar of exceptional depth, boasting over 800 wines and a particularly well-curated selection by the glass.

Name: Il Refettorio
Address: Via Roma 2, Conca dei Marini, 84010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Within the Monastero Santa Rosa – one of the most iconic and captivating hotels on the Amalfi Coast, whose religious past dates to the seventeenth century, and of which many traces remain to this day – the restaurant occupies a terrace whose view sweeps from the garden and pool to the sea, in the silence of a timeless place. Chef Alfonso Crescenzo interprets Mediterranean cuisine through a philosophy encapsulated in his own motto: "Nothing is more complex than simple cooking." His offering is born from the celebration of the finest Campanian produce, much of it from the family's own organic farm, and unfolds across two tasting menus alongside the à la carte, with a perfect balance between sea, land and kitchen garden. Among the signature dishes, the Mafalda stands out: a homage to the traditional Neapolitan Sunday lunch – Gragnano pasta filled with buffalo ricotta, Agerola moscione cheese and fried aubergine, completed by small meatballs and Neapolitan ragù. The finale is devoted to the celebrated sfogliatella Santa Rosa, born in this very monastery, here reinterpreted in a contemporary version that preserves its echoes of ricotta, citrus and sour cherry preserve.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: 40F, Bvlgari Hotel Tokyo, 2-2-1 Yaesu, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, 104-0028, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant under the supervision of Niko Romito, whose unique philosophy is blazing a trail through the Italian culinary world. From the concept of ‘authentic yet contemporary’, Il Ristorante - Niko Romito brings together fare from every region of Italy. Vegetable soup is prepared without water; instead, moisture is extracted from the ingredients, yielding a pure expression of flavour. Spaghetti pomodoro features concentrated essence of tomato. The pursuit of the flavours and essence of Italy.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: 47F, Bvlgari Hotel, Lane 108, North Shanxi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Stunning vistas of the Pudong skyline, crystal chandeliers and semi-circular leather booths impart style and a sense of grandeur. The menu here, as at the Dubai and Beijing outlets, comprises creations supervised by celebrity chef Niko Romito and underpinned by well-honed skills to reflect seasonality. Handmade pasta is the must-try – the lobster linguine bursts with seafood umami. Be sure to save room for the creamy gelato di ricotta di bufala.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: 1F, Bvlgari Hotel, Building 2, Courtyard 8, Xinyuan South Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This dining concept by Milanese chef Niko Romito is the epitome of Italian luxe. Lit by Murano glass chandeliers and clad in marble, warm wood and leather, the high-ceilinged space overlooks a manicured garden. Classic recipes are given a subtle, modern twist that adds sophistication and depth. Start your meal with vitello tonnato – the thinly sliced veal in a tangy tuna sauce is a classic antipasto, reworked to cater to the modern palate.

Name: Il Ristorante Alain Ducasse Napoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Located within the Hotel ROMEO Napoli, the Alain Ducasse Napoli Restaurant is a place where the fusion of local specialities inspires an elegant, refined and daring cuisine, celebrating the culture and gastronomic richness of Campania. In the heart of the city, the chef, ever passionate about the Mediterranean, draws inspiration from the region’s wonderful ingredients: Paestum artichokes, purple prawns from the island of Ischia, Sorrento lemons and fresh fish from the Tyrrhenian Sea. Working alongside executive chef Alessandro Lucassino, Ducasse pays tribute to these ingredients with a personal and refined vision, where respect for Campania’s traditions meets contemporary haute cuisine. Each ingredient is carefully brought to the fore: brief cooking times preserve the intensity of the flavours, while the preparation methods focus on the essence of the ingredient. French influences blend with an authentic Italian approach, while being guided by the philosophy of naturalness. French culinary techniques refine each detail, paying tribute to the richness of the Campania region with dishes that evoke the sea and the land, the fire of Vesuvius and the wind that dries the ‘piennoli’.

Name: Il Ristorante di Guido da Costigliole
Address: Località San Maurizio 39, Santo Stefano Belbo, 12058, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched in a panoramic setting amid extraordinary rolling hills, this restaurant is housed in a seventeenth-century former monastery transformed into the refined Relais San Maurizio, one of the region’s most exclusive venues. Andrea Alciati and Monica Magnini preserve and reimagine the legacy of Guido and Lidia Alciati, legendary figures in Piedmontese gastronomy. In the kitchen, Cuneo-born chef Fabio Sgrò carries on the family tradition with respect and passion, interpreting it through a modern lens: his revisited menu also features freshwater fish and a selection of off-menu specials that enrich the offering. Among the vegan options, the grilled endive with almond cream and vegetable jus stands out, an intense yet surprisingly harmonious dish. Equally unmissable is the glazed eel with kale, remarkable for its balance and depth of flavor. The wine cellar deserves special mention: an extraordinary selection featuring verticals and rare bottles that adds further allure to the experience.

Name: Il Saraceno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The chef’s Amalfi origins re-emerge in great style in this restaurant at the gates of Bergamo, with a chiefly seafood cuisine of great quality. From raw seafood to spaghetti with sea urchins and breadcrumbs, from seabream to the fish of the day, it is a feast for the palate, culminating in the desserts. The quality of the leavened products is noteworthy, from bread to focaccia with oregano and cherry tomatoes. The wine list is good too, starting with the selection of Champagnes.

Name: Il Sereno Al Lago
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Leaving the road that runs through the village, you descend almost to the lakeshore to find the restaurant within the luxurious Il Sereno hotel, an elegant new structure enhanced by the architectural creativity of Patricia Urquiola. In the summertime, the restaurant is hosted on the terrace with arched openings, offering views of the blue expanse and the villages on the opposite shore. The mastery of the brilliant Neapolitan chef Raffaele Lenzi spans all kinds of cuisine with equal success and balance: some regional references, vegan dishes, Asian influences, Lombard and lake-inspired creations, and a lot of creativity. The interesting wine list includes a rich selection of fine Italian reds, with verticals featuring older vintages.

Name: Il Tiglio
Address: Via Isola San Biagio 34, Montemonaco, 63088, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It is certainly worth the trip to the steep slopes at the foot of the Sibillini Mountains, where Enrico Mazzaroni has created a culinary concept deeply rooted in the local area. The cuisine is, in fact, based on top-quality ingredients – mushrooms, trout, venison, potatoes and many other local produce – often sourced directly from the family’s farm holiday accommodation. This solid foundation is complemented by a distinct creative flair that results in original, contemporary dishes, underpinned by precise technique and a balanced interplay of flavours, as demonstrated by the combination of trout, veal diaphragm and mushrooms. Over the years, the presentations have also taken on a greater sense of theatrical elegance, without losing sight of the substance. The service helps to make the experience particularly enjoyable, thanks to a successful balance between long-standing professionalism and the enthusiasm of the younger generation. The wine cellar is also very well stocked; alongside a wide selection of local and regional wines, it offers an interesting range of artisan wines from various parts of Italy.

Name: Il Tino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Within the Nautilus shipyard, stairs lead to the first floor attic dining room with windows overlooking the marina. Elegant and refined, also in service, chef Daniele Usai creates highly original seafood cuisine, distinguished above all by a skilful use of aromatic herbs, of which the chef is a true master and connoisseur, also of uncommon varieties. The offering is structured around two tasting menus: one featuring his most classic dishes accompanied by their year of creation, the other with his latest creations. Dishes may, however, also be chosen freely from the carte, starting from two courses and a dessert.

Name: Il Visibilio
Address: SP 9 di Pievasciata 32, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: At the end of a dirt road leading from the contemporary art village of Pievasciata to the cultivated hills, you will find the impressive gate of The Club House hotel. Il Visibilio is a small gourmet restaurant that offers a delightful combination of Tuscan cuisine and the creativity of chef Iannotti from the two-Michelin-starred Krèsios restaurant in Telese Terme. Iannotti brings to Siena a formula similar to that offered at his restaurant. A single blind tasting menu, a long gastronomic journey consisting of surprise dishes that alternate between ingredients from land and sea, with extensive use of vegetables. Numerous technical flourishes ensure a top-quality fine-dining experience, starting with the introductory finger food. The inspector recommends: the pigeon with its delicious rhubarb and absinthe sauces.

Name: Im Schiffchen
Description: If we're talking about Michelin-starred cuisine in a beautiful Baroque brick building on Kaiserswerther Markt, we can only be talking about Jean-Claude Bourgueil's Im Schiffchen. At the helm since 1977, he is without a doubt the doyen of Düsseldorf's fine dining scene. Together with his tried-and-trusted kitchen team, Bourgueil delivers creative French cuisine. Whether it be lobster, game or Wagyu beef, the produce is of the finest quality. To complete the picture, there's the impressive selection of wines, the attentive and well-trained wait staff and the gorgeous decor – this ground-floor restaurant has a tasteful maritime look.

Name: Ima
Address: 20 boulevard de la Tour-d'Auvergne, Rennes, 35000, France
Description: (Temporarily closed, reopening planned for mid-September) “Cooking has always been a means of travel for me”, explains chef Julien Lemarié, who has plied his trade in London, Tokyo and Singapore. At his restaurant, Ima, which means “now” in Japanese, this talented culinary technician conjures up instinctive cuisine showcased on tasting menus that combine subtlety with regional and Asian influences. Lemarié enhances his dishes with broths, infusions, spices, aromatic plants and algae. And for those keen to enjoy the full Japanese experience, make sure you take a seat at the bar. It's now your turn to travel!

Name: Imperfecto: The Chef's Table
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This buzzy spot is decked out with brass accents, terracotta, and a tight counter positioned directly under Chef Enrique Limardo’s perch. The counter functions as a restaurant within a restaurant with room for just a handful of diners to enjoy an elaborate tasting menu that celebrates Latin flavors, ace ingredients, and exacting technique. There is an attention to detail, and meals take on an intimate form. Dishes, perhaps a crisp tomato water with chayote squash and clams, or a crudo of prawn tails in a bottarga ketchup and Hokkaido sea urchin with fried plantain, hum with flavor. Desserts are equally skillful, as in pickled peach with matcha sponge cake.

Name: Imperial Treasure
Description: A stone’s throw from the emblematic Champs Elysées, this establishment is just the ticket to try China’s imperial cuisine: sharing, lavish ingredients and time-honoured, even ancestral, recipes. Beneath the watchful eye of a head chef assisted by a kitchen brigade, as talented as they are numerous, each dish becomes a tribute to tradition: Peking duck exquisitely carved by your tableside, dim sum to die for, or chicken in Chinese yellow wine steeped in suave, subtle flavours. In a setting with a sense of occasion, each diner is pampered by a zealous front-of-house team, who also plays the role of guide, pointing out the highlights of this divinely refined Asian universe. The perfect place to sample dishes of rare authenticity.

Name: Imperial Treasure Fine Chinese Cuisine (Tsim Sha Tsui)
Address: 10F, One Peking, 1 Peking Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: This branch of the Singapore-based brand is housed at an iconic skyscraper overlooking the harbour. The stylish dining room is embellished with subtle Chinese motifs, such as ceramic Koi carps and calligraphy. Live seafood is a must – try steamed lobster in chicken fat and Huadiao wine on a bed of silky egg white custard. The winey aromas are mesmerising. Hand-crafted dim sum is another unmissable highlight at lunch.

Name: Imperial Treasure Fine Teochew Cuisine
Address: L307, 3F, Taikoo Hui, 383 Tianhe Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The Singapore-based chain opened its first outpost here in 2019. The head chef from Hong Kong ensures that Chaozhou traditions are respected in the kitchen, while adding a refined touch to his repertoire. The fried tofu skin roll in sweet and sour sauce is filled with ground pork, water chestnuts, shiitake and dried shrimps, delivering a variety of textures. The pork tripe soup with salted mustard greens and peppercorns warms the heart and soul.

Name: Imperial Treasure Fine Teochew Cuisine (Orchard)
Description: Since 2016, this restaurant has been serving traditional Teochew fare with an emphasis on fresh seafood. Only 15 oversized swimmer crabs are steamed and served chilled each day, so order ahead to avoid disappointment. Teochew-style, chilled, steamed fish also impresses with irresistible briny-sweetness, tender flesh and buttery belly. Dip in the delicious Puning bean sauce for extra umami. Other classics, like the oyster omelette, are also worth trying.

Name: Impromptu by Paul Lee
Address: B1, Regent Hotel, 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan Region
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Paul Lee leads a talented young kitchen team in presenting a tasting menu that elevates Taiwanese street food to the level of haute cuisine. Asian and European flavours mingle harmoniously in refined dishes made with quality local produce and imported ingredients are perfected by modern techniques. Non-alcoholic beverage pairings by the mixology virtuoso enhance the experience. On top of the tasting menu, add-ons are available.

Name: Impronta d'Acqua
Address: Via Aurelia 2121, Cavi di Lavagna, 16030, Italy
Description: Between the sea and the railway, an open-space restaurant with a minimalist, contemporary design welcomes guests with its open kitchen, where chef and owner Ivan Maniago and his team transform ingredients from Liguria into sensory experiences. The philosophy is clear: 90% of the products come from small local producers. Three tasting menus offer an original interpretation of Liguria: Altitudine, a jouney from the coast towards inland Liguria; Profondità, an immersion in the wonders of the sea; and Vege-table, dedicated to green freshness.

Name: Imàgo
Address: Piazza Trinità dei Monti 6, Rome, 00187, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: One of the capital’s most iconic gastronomic rooftop venues, this restaurant enjoys a setting of rare distinction: perched atop the celebrated Spanish Steps at Trinità dei Monti, within the Hotel Hassler, it is reached by lift and counts among Rome's most renowned dining rooms, recently renovated to include an open kitchen, new flooring, and carefully considered lighting. Here one dines surrounded by large windows looking out over the city’s most emblematic monuments, from the twin bell towers of Trinità dei Monti to views stretching along the horizon, a constant invitation to rediscover the urban icons. In the kitchen, the brigade led by Andrea Antonini offers two tasting menus that alternate between great classics and more recent creations: a sequence of small, refined, and visually striking dishes that reinterpret local traditions and ingredients, guiding diners towards unexpected pairings and contemporary interpretations full of playfulness and creativity.

Name: In Diferente
Address: Rua do Doutor Sousa Rosa 23, Porto, 4150-719, Portugal
Description: This welcoming restaurant isn’t in the city centre or on the usual tourist routes, yet... it’s truly worth the visit! Angélica Salvador, the Brazilian-born chef at the helm, offers her take on traditional Portuguese and international cooking through a small menu and two contemporary-leaning tasting menus, Homenagem and In Diferente (7 and 9 moments, respectively), both with their own pairing option and the possibility of changing a dish if the diner wishes. Her concept is different and personalised, with signature details, making the most of both the wonderful fish from the Matosinhos or Aveiro fish markets and the fantastic local meats. Standout dishes? We especially enjoyed her Pescada Selvagem, wild hake, and the dessert called Maracujá, passion fruit, made with yuzu, carrot, ginger and coconut milk. The team are extremely attentive and professional!

Name: In Viaggio - Claudio Melis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The name of this restaurant gives a good indication of the experience you can expect here: a culinary voyage through the chef’s varied selection of recipes and ingredients, some from the Alps, others from countries across the globe. Dishes are served on tasting menus of five, seven or nine courses in a quiet dining room with just a few tables, where the chef himself explains his dishes to guests.

Name: Inati
Address: 48 Hereford Street, Christchurch Central City, Christchurch, 8013, New Zealand
Description: Inati means "to share" in Māori. British chef Levy and his wife Lisa opened this beautifully designed contemporary space in 2017, armed with the concept of reimagining European classics for sharing, to be made with the finest Canterbury and New Zealand produce. Signatures include their "Boeuf-nut" (a doughnut filled with braised beef cheek), and roast 14-day-aged duck coated in dukkah spice mix – a hit with its crispy skin, tender meat and exotic kick.

Name: Inatô
Address: The Alley at Karrivin, Karrivin Plaza, 2316 Chino Roces Avenue Extension, Makati - Metro Manila, 1231, The Philippines
Description: Located in The Alley, a buzzing part of Karrivin, this discreet gem blends intimacy with finesse. Ring the bell to enter a chic space in which a sculptural marble counter seats eight facing the open kitchen. Light floors, wooden slats and a textured feature wall add modern charm. Chef JP Cruz reimagines Filipino cuisine with flair. Standouts include yellowtail amberjack and choco tarte – delivered with seamless, warm interaction in a calm, elegant setting.

Name: Indaco
Address: Piazza Santa Restituta 1, Lacco Ameno, 80076, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Don’t miss the appointment with sunset: as the sun sets behind you, the sea before you ignites with marvellous hues, thus revealing the meaning behind the restaurant’s name. We find ourselves in an exclusive area of the Hotel Regina Isabella, a small marina from which the view embraces Lacco Ameno, Casamicciola, the island of Procida, Vesuvius, Bacoli... a unique and unforgettable panorama, with the sea enclosed between lands and islands as if in an enchanted bay. In the kitchen, Ischia-born Pasquale Palamaro evokes his island memories through refined and creative dishes. The offering takes shape in two seafood tasting menus, whose dishes can also be ordered individually à la carte, complemented today by a new entirely plant-based proposal, conceived with the same care and depth of flavour. Of exceptional note is the wine accompaniment, which combines an extensive selection – over one thousand labels – with the passionate and knowledgeable advice of the sommelier.

Name: Indienne
Address: 217 W. Huron St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
Description: In a city where kitchens break molds and defy expectations, Chef Sujan Sarkar makes a splash of his own on this quiet strip of River North. Vegan, vegetarian, and non-vegetarian tasting menus deliver an original, modern vision of Indian cuisine. His food may look like pieces of art but taste like familiar favorites pulled from across his vibrant homeland. At times showcasing a hint of French sensibility, pani puris, chats and curries arrive deftly spiced and elegantly presented. The kitchen is quick, and the overall effect is impressive refinement. All the while, the expansive room balances smooth warehouse floors and exposed ceilings with thick wooden beams, white tablecloths and rose-pink booths.

Name: Ineffable
Description: In a small Provençal village with bags of character, Ineffable promises diners a feast for the senses. The restaurant is run by a couple with a passion for what they do: Nicolas Thomas and Marie Salomez (previously of La Promenade, La Flibuste, Château de Courban). This space with a decor of exposed stone walls and contemporary furnishings, and animated by a soundscape of soothing birdsong has just five tables. The chef riffs on poetic culinary leitmotifs, marrying olives and olive wood, plants and seafood (even meat on the larger set menu). A music lover, he has a sense for timing and harmony, as demonstrated by his composition of vegetables topped with a smoked cream.

Name: Inkiostro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Calabrian chef Salvatore Morello brings a breath of fresh air to the city synonymous with gastronomy. Drawing on an international background, he presents a cuisine that weaves together recipes and ingredients from diverse culinary worlds, united by finesse, personality, and a striking cohesion. Exceptional raw materials, occasionally accented by exotic notes, find precise balance in every course. Special mention goes to the bread program: the loaf, crafted from sourdough and minimally refined flours and baked in a cast-iron pot, captivates with its pronounced crust and unexpected lightness. Equal care is devoted to the focaccias and grissini, all of outstanding quality. The list offers a thoughtfully curated selection of wines, craft beers, sake, and spirits, ideal companions to the dining experience.

Name: Innesto
Description: Innesto is the epitome of modern elegance, and the spruce interior sports a stylish black and white colour scheme, while marble details add a luxurious note. In fine weather, make a beeline for the patio. The front-of-house team is constantly on the ball to make sure you lack for nothing. You will see Koen Verjans in the glazed open kitchen, rolling out his obvious passion for outstanding ingredients as he deploys his creativity and technical background. He is particularly keen on mixing textures of vegetables to underscore their intensity, while sauces add an extra dimension to each dish. He may add a kick to Dombes duck with a gutsy compote of speck and onion, a beurre noisette hollandaise sauce and a big-boned spicy gravy. A medley of potato dishes then chips in with a playful final note. Koen Verjans celebrates the ingredient like no one else, as you will discover in the menu that allows you to choose between five or six courses.

Name: InterStellar BBQ
Address: 12233 Ranch Rd. 620 N., Ste. 105, Austin, TX, 78750, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The mark of a good place is when a line starts forming before they've even opened, and at InterStellar BBQ, it's long before they've swung open the door. Everyone is here for a taste of pitmaster John Bates's barbecue, done low and slow over post oak. Brisket with a simple salt, pepper and garlic rub is outstanding but it doesn't end there. Peach tea-glazed pork belly is meltingly tender; the beer-brined tipsy turkey is moist and delicious; and there are three sausages on offer, including kielbasa. You can't go wrong with any of the enticing side dishes like the Frito pie, though the smoked scalloped potatoes with a golden-brown crust and the poblano creamed corn are standouts. Craving something sweet? Banana pudding and Mexican hot chocolate rice pudding are two favorites.

Name: Interalpen - Chef's Table
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Are you looking for a dining experience with a difference? In the restaurant of the Interalpen-Hotel Tyrol, in a fabulous location on the Seefeld high plateau, the eponymous Chef's Table is just the ticket. Diners are seated in the kitchen, at two high tables. Here, in the thick of the action, you can watch Mathias Hendl and his team at work – the chefs themselves also present their dishes. Made using top-notch ingredients, the creative courses of the seasonal set menu showcase wonderfully harmonious combinations and bold flavours. Exemplifying the outstanding quality is the binchotan charcoal-grilled langoustine, served with fermented carrot, crispy puffed grains, Arctic char caviar and beurre blanc foam. The desserts by pastry chef Manfred Löschl also deserve a mention, for example "cheesecake, rhubarb, hemp, verbena". Wine pairings and alcohol-free alternatives are available. This special "Chef's Table" experience is available by reservation and in the evening only (Mon-Fri).

Name: Interlude
Address: Leonardslee Gardens, Brighton Road, Lower Beeding, RH13 6PP, United Kingdom
Description: The 240-acre Leonardslee Lakes and Gardens were first planted in 1801 and are famous today for their azaleas, rhododendrons and even a wallaby colony. Within the grounds sits an Italianate mansion housing elegant bedrooms and this intimate restaurant. The 'Estate Experience' tasting menu uses seasonal ingredients from their own land, with Chef Jean Delport's South African heritage shining through – such as in the carrot biltong forming part of the signature 'Rabbit Eats Carrot' dish. The wine list continues the South African trend, with choices from their own Benguela Cove estate.

Name: Intuition
Description: Make your way upstairs from the Capucines Brasserie, overlooking the castle of Saint Lô, to this understated, plush establishment. Back in his hometown, Mickaël Marion unveils his keen grasp of inventive cuisine. A steadfast champion of local produce, he frequently forages wild plants and herbs and grows his own veg. His deft score delicately showcases the region’s ingredients: scallops roasted in butter, monkfish served with garden leeks and curly kale. Start the meal with brioche smoked in apple wood and butter laced in the scent of woodruff. Sensitive, distinctive cooking throbbing with flavour.

Name: Ippei Hanten
Description: Chinese cuisine cultivated in Japan interweaves with Cantonese cuisine experienced in Hong Kong. The prix fixe menu puts the accent on fresh, hot and fragrant; each course is limited in quantity, permitting a wide variety of items to be served. Congee expresses the daily rhythms of Hong Kong; dim sum includes shrimp wrapped in rice flour and tofu skin. Longtooth grouper and boar are served in hot pots. Striving for harmony among the five flavours, a wide range of sauces, seasonings and fermented foods are skilfully intermingled in this culinary bridge between China and Japan.

Name: Iris Ristorante
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Within an extraordinary palazzo in the historic center, the experience begins in the fifteenth-century cellars, where an amuse-bouche is served in an evocative atmosphere before guests ascend to the sixteenth-century dining room. Amid frescoes, exposed stone, and brick, with the open kitchen visible at the far end, this ranks among the most elegant restaurants in the region. At the stove, Giacomo Sacchetto offers several tasting menus, with dishes that may be freely selected from one list or another. Both seafood and land-based offerings, elaborate and creative, leave the mark of a thrilling gastronomic experience.

Name: Irma la Douce
Description: This restaurant's name was not simply plucked out of thin air; it refers to the US film Irma la Douce, which is based on the musical of the same name. A classically elegant decor bathed in a warm golden light creates a truly enchanting atmosphere that evokes the spirit of a bygone era. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid back, and top-notch service comes courtesy of friendly waitstaff. The cuisine draws on classic French influences, incorporating creative modern ideas. Flavourful dishes such as the melt-in-the-mouth bœuf bourguignon are prepared using the finest ingredients. The popular ‘Carbonara’ is also on the menu - reflecting the chef's origins. For dessert, the ‘Crème Brûlée’ is a favourite. The wine list is dominated by French labels, and you can count on astute recommendations. Tue. - Fri. there is a simple lunch menu.

Name: Iroha
Description: Dinner at Iroha should be a once-in-a-lifetime experience, the chef decrees, so he lavishes his guests with the flavours of what’s in season. The extensive menu and the chef’s endless ingenuity testify to this commitment. An arranged sashimi dish is prepared using the techniques of skin searing, skin boiling, and kombu pickling. The popular beef cutlets are a hearty meat dish, ensuring that everyone leaves feeling satisfied. True to the restaurant’s name, which means ‘coloured leaves’, dishes are decorated with leaves of the season.

Name: Irwin
Description: Having trained at L'Oustau de Baumanière and L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon, Irwin Durand further fine-tuned his skills working for Alan Geaam and Guy Savoy. He now showcases his expertise at the helm of his own elegant, contemporary-style restaurant that fosters an intimate atmosphere with just seven tables, plus a communal table facing the open kitchen. In his seasonal mystery menu, the finest seasonal produce is spotlighted with flair and technical skill: sea bass ballotine à la grenobloise; veal sweetbreads in a mustard sauce, peas and a reduced veal jus; and a vanilla and miso cream dessert.

Name: Isidore
Address: 221 Newell Ave., San Antonio, TX, 78215, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Located in San Antonio's historic Pearl District, Isidore is a stylish spot with a midcentury modern feel complete with an open kitchen and live-fire hearth. Named for the patron saint of farmers and laborers, there is a clear focus on Texas ingredients and local traditions, even incorporating Native American elements into the bread service. The menu is large, with items intended for sharing and a section dedicated to steak. Narrowing down your snack selection isn't easy, but the popcorn chicken, crispy fried with popcorn aioli and velouté, is a good bet. Cherokee tomato in a house-made kombucha lets local ingredients shine, while the dry-aged Berkshire pork chop with a 23-spice sauce is another highlight. Texas wines are also proudly shared on the list and in an optional pairing.

Name: Islares
Description: This minimalist restaurant with a natural feel to its decor is located opposite the city’s Guggenheim Museum where it exudes plenty of culinary passion in its quest to showcase the traditional cuisine of Northern Spain. Here, under the baton of chef Julen Bergantiños, choose between two unusual menus that change completely with every season (for example, wild mushrooms take centre stage in the autumn, followed by game in the winter), based around seasonal ingredients sourced from small-scale producers with, wherever possible, a constant and skilful use of native condiments and native species. The 9-course option is entitled “A-8” and takes its name from the dual carriageway that connects Galicia, Asturias, Cantabria and the Basque Country, while the other, the 13-course “N-634”, recognises the beautiful road that runs from Santiago de Compostela to Donostia/San Sebastián. The sauces served here are truly delicious!

Name: Italo Bassi Confusion Restaurant
Address: Via Aga Khan 1, Promenade du Port, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Now established as a reference point in Porto Cervo, this restaurant occupies an elevated position overlooking the marina. Mirrors, golden accents, and glass details complement the open kitchen, where Italo Bassi leads his team. Technique and refined presentation stand out, whether in fish dishes (such as the textbook-perfect sole with mint-marinated zucchini and an exquisite beurre blanc foam recalling the classic à la meunière) or in meat preparations. Guests enjoy absolute freedom of choice: two tasting menus are available – one featuring the restaurant’s classics, the other with new creations, offered in various lengths – or they may order à la carte, which also includes luxury ingredients served in pure form, such as oysters, caviar, and raw seafood. On the lower floor, the Bubble Bar & Bistrot offers aperitifs and more informal dishes.

Name: Ithurria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Ithurria on Ainhoa’s Place du Fronton facing the village pelota wall must be the quintessence of Basque! The attractive, traditional family-run establishment has retained its red and white façade and terracotta tiled floors and wooden rafters, paired with modern furnishings. Chef Martin Isabal and his pastry-chef brother Louis sign a modern score, rich in character and founded on their Basque roots. The terroir takes centre stage in delicious recipes underscored by an original, even cheeky dimension. Start with a wild-garlic-laced marshmallow, before moving on to local artichoke, Sturia caviar, yuzu-laced roasted artichoke and Banka trout roe, followed by barbecued Pascal Massonde lamb, green peas and broad beans in anchovy garum and wild garlic-spiked lamb sausage. Slick, seamless service.

Name: Itzuli
Address: Gudamendi Bidea 21, Donostia / San Sebastián, 20008, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Inside the Luze San Sebastián boutique hotel, at the top of Mount Igueldo, this restaurant hides its proposal under a Basque term that could be translated as ‘to return’ or ‘to come back’. Chef Iñigo Lavado, after two decades of success in Irun, has set up the project with his family (his wife, Arantxa Martínez, is in charge of the dining room and one of his sons, Julen, is a professional sommelier), trying to convey to diners, in his own words, a culinary style... ‘of time, stories and a lot of emotion’. In his elegant Belle Époque style dining rooms, with large windows to enjoy the sea views, he offers a proposal that combines his two menus (Luis Irizar, dedicated to his mentor, and the one he calls Cocina de Emociones (Emotional Cuisine), more contemporary and personal) with a menu that includes dishes selected from both options. A highlight? We were surprised by their Ostra al natural (natural oyster), with pickled vegetable cream and suckling pig jus.

Name: Iwaki
Description: To keep each visit feeling fresh, there are no standard dishes. Western vegetables are also woven into the cooking as part of that approach. Tsukuri is given an extra twist through techniques such as curing with kelp and soy marination, while fish and meat dishes may draw inspiration from Western cooking. Desserts end the meal on a refreshing note with shaved ice featuring fruits and vegetables. Yet for all the playful creativity, the cuisine remains firmly rooted in Japanese sensibilities. The chef’s desire to delight comes through in every dish.

Name: Ixi'im
Address: Chablé Yucatán, Tablaje #642, San Antonio Chablé, Chocholá, 97816, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
Description: Amid the greenery-laden beauty of the Chablé Yucatán resort and housed inside a 19th-century hacienda that once produced agave fiber, humble origins have been transformed into an oasis of luxury. Executive Chef Luis Ronzón brings a global perspective to traditional Mayan flavors and techniques, in particular “al pib,” an ancient method of cooking inside an earthen roasting pit, which lends a subtle smoky aroma to the likes of crisped pork cheek and earthy sweet potato glazed with citrus and chile. Ingredients are sourced locally, including from the resort’s own ka'anche, or Mayan garden. Charmingly hospitable service begins from the second one steps foot on the property, and any remaining stress can be eased by their vast tequila collection, in excess of 3,400 bottles.

Name: JAN
Description: South African chef Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen, whose former careers involved working as a chef on private yachts in Monaco and as a photojournalist for a top magazine, has already lived several lives… In his cosy (20-seater), romantic eatery near the port, he signs creative, personal cuisine in the shape of a single set menu, in which he plays on sweet and sour combinations, and dabbles in smoky, spicy and acidic flavours, giving us an insight into South African cuisine. When it is time for cheese, you will discover a cheese bar opposite the restaurant with a buffet of some twenty different cheeses, a range of beverages, preserves and dried fruit.

Name: JER
Description: Good food has no need of fancy fussy frills, as Wim Schildermans so masterfully illustrates. In a tastefully restored manor house that has lost none of its period charm, this creative maestro rolls out his “Just Eat Right” concept. First of all, he sources top-drawer, preferably local ingredients, and then deploys his consummate skill and talent. Chef Schildermans cooks boldly and has no qualms about surprising diners, illustrated by fillet of venison, served rare and underscored by a big-boned gravy enhanced with delicate and subtly vibrant Timut pepper. This is paired with marinated red beetroot and a salad which combines earthy, bitter notes with sweet, fruity accents courtesy of chicory, redcurrants, apples, radishes and beetroot. Attention to detail is paramount and each bite gives rise to a whole new range of sensations, capturing and titillating the tastebuds from the appetisers to the dessert. The wines are expertly curated and accompanied by the highly knowledgeable sommelier’s enthusiastic recommendations and explanations. Simply good food!

Name: JO
Description: The prix fixe menu is joyously imaginative and well balanced. An impressive range of beef cuts are served, each with its own method of preparation for most delicious effect. Seared rump locks in the flavour, slow-grilled tail is fragrant. Chateaubriand is reimagined as a cutlet sandwich; sirloin, served shabu-shabu style, is shorn of unnecessary fat; fillet is grilled over charcoal to a rosy red.

Name: JOHN Chef's Hall
Address: A22 Hotel, Ausekļa iela 22, Riga, 1010, Latvia
Description: Situated within the A22 Hotel, this restaurant bears the name of John F. Kennedy, who stayed here back when he was 22. It’s an intimate spot, made all the more special by the addition of a striking red lounge where you both start and end your evening. The modern tasting menu reflects both the country and the seasons and is also playful in places, but never at the expense of flavour. The chefs present and explain the dishes themselves: maybe tomato with ricotta and redcurrants or potato dumpling with quail and gooseberry. Make the most of the bespoke wine pairings by booking a room for the night.

Name: JOLA
Description: Jola takes its name from the charming duo behind this venture: Jonathan Wittenbrink, who delivers outstanding vegan cuisine, and Larissa Andres, who manages the service in the compact dining space with charm and aplomb. Seasonal and regional ingredients go into the creative surprise set menu, which features memorable dishes such as raviolo stuffed with aubergine ragout, served with courgette, lightly toasted pine nuts and a wonderfully intense tomato essence. Choose between wine and alcohol-free pairings. The setting is stylish and modern yet pleasingly laid back – the open kitchen certainly adds to that. A nice touch: The menu is printed on plantable seed paper – take it home and see what blooms!

Name: JU - Maison de Cuisine
Description: Chef Julien Allano (La Mirande, Le Clair de la Plume) chose to go it alone and set up shop in this beautiful traditional building in the heart of the village. In an interior with exposed stonework, the chef can be seen at work behind a wooden counter. Meanwhile, guests are seated on handcrafted furnishings made of untreated walnut wood – a decor that oozes style. The carte blanche menu, which is divided into several sections, reflects the season from day to day. Heirloom varieties of wheat, peanuts from Malataverne, green beans from a neighbouring farm and pigeon from Sarrians are just some of the carefully sourced local ingredients used to create harmonious, delicate cuisine, rife with the flavours of the South of France, about which the chef is genuinely passionate. The "Cheese Experience" is held in a huge, superb vaulted cellar dating back to the 13C.

Name: JUEUN
Address: 8F Gyeonghuidang, 36 Gyeonghuigung-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul, 03175, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: JUEUN offers a delicate expression of Korea’s four seasons, favouring a classic, understated approach over trends or ornamentation. A variety of fermented sauces form the backbone of the menu, enhancing ingredients with natural depth and harmony, while the seasonally changing courses provide a strong incentive for return visits. The meal follows a thoughtful progression and concludes with a traditional Korean table that highlights a wide spectrum of flavours. Ceramics by local artists and subtle media art create a space where tradition and modernity coexist with quiet elegance. The curated pairings of traditional Korean spirits and wine further elevate the experience.

Name: Jacobi
Description: This restaurant housed in the Hotel Schwarzwälder Hof in Freiburg's old town boasts a relaxed atmosphere and food that is by no means run-of-the-mill. The cooking revolves around high-quality produce sourced from the region. Their wonderful sourdough bread is baked in-house, and fermented components are seamlessly woven into the dishes. The seven-course set menu – which can be extended by a further two courses – features intriguing, innovative combinations such as "emmer, carrot, sunflower" or "venison, cherry, poppy seed". To accompany the meal, there are expertly chosen wine pairings or an excellent selection of house-made alcohol-free drinks. On Wed-Fri evenings, there is also a shorter set menu, with individual dishes from it available à la carte. The chefs themselves serve their creations, talking diners through each course and providing information about the local producers of the carefully selected ingredients.

Name: Jacques Faussat
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Jacques Faussat, born in Gers and proud of it, clearly aspires to the simplicity of his childhood roots. A simplicity also passed down by Michel Guérard and above all, Alain Dutournier. Jacques’ meeting with the latter, also born in Gers, proved to be decisive in his career, starting with ten years spent in the kitchen of the Trou Gascon. He sign flavoursome cuisine made with intelligently crafted produce in a bid to nurture the flavours and aromas. Eater-friendly prices.

Name: Jade River
Address: 3F, White Swan Hotel, 1 Shamian South Street, Liwan, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Diners here unwind with a cup of tea freshly brewed by tea masters. The traditional garden, water features, exquisite woodwork and artisan Manchurian windows give it a serene feel. The food is, of course, no less impressive. Steamed sunflower seed-fed chicken is delivered straight from the farm daily. Baked pigeon with lemongrass and salt is another proud creation of the team. Also try various poultry and meats in white marinade.

Name: Jae
Description: Do not be deterred by the rather plain exterior, as this restaurant is impressive in several respects: Jörg Wissmann (previously at establishments such as Vendôme, Nagaya and Agata's) creates modern fusion cuisine with Asian influences that reflect his half-Korean heritage, while also incorporating classic French elements. With a distinctive signature style, he skilfully combines different flavours, as seen for example in the delicately cured, boldly seasoned hamachi of outstanding quality, served with finely sliced marinated radish and lime koji (a fermented rice condiment), plus chopped pistachios, gim (Korean seaweed) and fresh flowers that lend the dish a unique character. His set menu comes in both a conventional and a vegetarian version. To accompany your meal, you can opt for wine or alcohol-free pairings. A winning blend of Far Eastern and Scandinavian styles makes for a bright, minimalist interior – the seats at the counter offer a fascinating insight into the work going on in the open kitchen. Scan the QR code with your phone to access the menu and wine list. Practical for motorists: The Creativ Center car park is just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Jag
Address: Singapore Tyler Print Institute, #02-02, 41 Robertson Quay, 238236, Singapore
Description: Jag has been housed in this pristine white-walled space with sage green furnishings, brushed brass trims and mid-century rattan chairs. The cooking is vegetable-forward: French produce at peak ripeness – and supplemented by meats and seafood – is key to the ethos. Dishes are light in flavours but strong in creative flair. The cheese trolley impresses with its sheer variety. Round off your meal with a digestif.

Name: Jamavar
Address: Al Corniche Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Part of a small international group, this Indian restaurant is named after the intricate 16th-century shawls of Kashmir and sits inside the Sheraton Grand Hotel. It’s a smart spot, with a mix of modern and traditional elements in its décor. The extensive menu covers all regions of India, from Old Delhi butter chicken to Kerala-style beef, and includes refined small plates and several dishes from the tandoor such as succulent lamb chops. Fine ingredients are used and bold flavours are delivered, with the spicing impressively well-judged.

Name: Jamavar
Address: 8 Mount Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 3NF, United Kingdom
Description: This smartly dressed restaurant is a firm favourite with those who love Indian food.
