The regional-style bistro on the ground floor serves up delicious lunch options during the week. The fine dining restaurant occupies a lovely space on the first floor with exposed timberwork. Bernard Leray, who hails from Rennes in Brittany, has taken to Alsace like a duck to water. After honing his skills at Bernard Loiseau, Leray puts a delicate new spin on local produce, each dish demonstrates his painstaking work and consummate technique – medallion of pike-perch, medley of salsify and endives, creamy broth with black truffle.

Name: La Once Mil
Address: Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec, Miguel Hildalgo, 11000, Mexico
Description: In a city teeming with every kind of taco imaginable, it’s a Herculean task to rise above the throng, but there’s no denying that this bustling operation manages the feat with style. Once seated, diners will find their tables decked out with an impressive array of excellent house-made salsas, ranging from gentle (a vibrant salsa cruda) to incendiary (a beguiling “martajada” with arbol and morita chiles) but the fireworks are just beginning. Top-quality meats are a feature, as in a marvelously succulent, flavorful Prime arrachera — you’ll be hard-pressed to find better in any steakhouse. Just as impressive are the handmade tortillas, with multiple varieties cooked to order with remarkable efficiency. Combined, a single bite is all that’s needed to make you a believer.

Name: La Paix
Description: Taking pride in domestic ingredients, the restaurant presents a distinctly Japanese approach to French cuisine. Dishes are light, with restrained use of fats and oils in line with modern tastes. Seasonal menus highlight fruits such as peaches and strawberries from local farmers, making the most of their natural character. Courses featuring sweetfish, chestnuts and mushrooms are also tempting. ‘La Paix’ means peace, expressing a wish for a harmonious table where producers and chef come together in mutual understanding through food.

Name: La Palme d'Or
Address: Hôtel Martinez, 73 boulevard de la Croisette, Cannes, 06400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the iconic Hôtel Martinez, glitzy haunt of celebrities during the Cannes Film Festival, pays a vibrant tribute to cinema, one of chef Jean Imbert's passions. Lined in wood panelling that wouldn't be out of place on a yacht from Hollywood’s golden era, the decor overflows with authentic movie props and posters. The menu is written like a screenplay, illustrated with storyboards. Under the impetus of director Imbert, chef Christophe Nannoni, a longstanding crew member here for over a decade, works closely with head pastry chef, Loïc Voron. The sea and Provence top the bill: squid and tuna belly braised in embers, piquillos and wine sauce; lamb cooked two ways, green asparagus, confit shoulder and a succulent gravy; vanilla-laced palmier made to order. Lights, camera, action!

Name: La Palmeraie - Château de Valmer
Address: 81 boulevard de Gigaro, La Croix-Valmer, 83420, France
Description: Nestling between vineyards, orchards and the sea, this early-20C hotel-restaurant lounges in a lush garden. No-nonsense, big-boned food is sampled in the shade of a pergola in summertime. The chef conjures up a menu whose six courses, bearing short and sweet titles and flanked by a vegetarian version, all star first-rate ingredients sourced from Provence, the coast and the estate’s own market garden. Heroically wondrous, lip-smacking flavours, illustrated by Tamaris oysters with artichoke or lamb with wild broccoli.

Name: La Palta
Address: Località Bilegno 67, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Still on the plain, yet already at the foot of the hills that can be glimpsed on the horizon, what from the outside presents itself as a typical country house surprises within with an elegant dining room that opens into a sort of veranda overlooking the garden and the greenery of the lower Piacenza countryside. The atmosphere is relaxed and most agreeable, ideally suited to a refined yet never formal lunch or dinner. The menu features references to local ingredients and recipes, alongside the excellent focaccia with ciccioli served among the bread course, a true speciality of the house. The cooking follows a measured and considered creative line, more intent on satisfying the palate than on surprising at any cost: three tasting menus are on offer – Sei nella mia terra, Sei nelle mie mani, and one dedicated entirely to pasta (to order) – with the option, alternatively, of choosing freely from the carte.

Name: La Parolina
Description: Just a few kilometres from Acquapendente, a historic stop on the Via Francigena, the restaurant enjoys a peaceful and scenic location, overlooking the Tuscia countryside. Here, Iside De Cesare and Romano Gordini offer cuisine deeply rooted in the region, based on local produce and authentic flavours, enhanced by a subtle technical finesse. Examples include dishes such as chilled chickpea hummus with local extra virgin olive oil, or the lentil ‘caviar’ that kicks off the dining experience. Among the most typical dishes, the tender and succulent pigeon – when available – stands out, served with bruschetta topped with chicken liver ragù and a canederlo in broth. Rounding off the experience are a well-stocked wine cellar, featuring a range of mature vintages, and the pleasant terraces, which are ideal for enjoying the tranquillity of the surrounding countryside.

Name: La Passagère - Hôtel Belles Rives
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The first thing to strike guests in this hotel, where Zelda and F. Scott Fitzgerald's tumultuous romance played out in the 1920s, is its jaw-dropping location. It's not easy for a chef to make his mark in such a setting, but Aurélien Véquaud does just that. In a fine dining menu that, naturally, embraces the Mediterranean (think superb little tunny, semi-confit tomatoes and rocket vinaigrette), the chef's origins – the Vendée in western France – still shine through on each plate. Unpasteurised cream jazzes up the crab in the signature dish (a soft esquinado cannelloni, verbena foam and fennel), and marinière of shellfish with Oscietra caviar accompanies the sea bass. The terrace commands a breathtaking view of the sea and the mountains of the Estérel.

Name: La Petite Maison de Cucuron
Description: This "petite maison" imbued with a genteel Provençal charm and recognisable by its yellow façade is the stomping ground of chef Éric Sapet. He elevates market ingredients like no other: mushrooms, including truffles, to which he dedicates a set menu in season, vegetables from local market gardeners, Provençal cheeses, game and also shellfish. A devoted gourmet and wine-lover, Sapet already has a solid career to his name and delivers classic Provençal cuisine rife with flavours. Be aware that the restaurant often gets fully booked.

Name: La Pineta
Address: Via dei Cavalleggeri Nord 27, Marina di Bibbona, 57020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name gives you a hint of what’s in store, but not everything – and certainly not the biggest surprise: after crossing a pine forest and leaving your car in the car park, you reach the restaurant and its stunning view – we’re practically on the beach! Opened in 1969 by the same family who still run it today – now in the next generation – the sea almost seems to spill into the dining room, where time seems to have stood still. The atmosphere is simple and retro, evoking memories of family holidays, happy times and days at the beach. The cuisine is in keeping with this setting: naturally seafood-based, the dishes are prepared according to traditional recipes, with the quality of the catch taking centre stage.

Name: La Pomme d'Api
Description: In the heart of Le Clos Saint Yves, this handsome 17C stone-built house (which was a major religious cabinet-making workshop until the late 19C) is the lair of Jérémie Le Calvez and his wife, Jessica, who warmly greet you with a smile. The chef’s delicate and inventive cuisine highlights the best and freshest ingredients of Brittany and reverently respects the seasons. The beautiful dining room with its exposed stonework and view of the small garden provides the perfect foil to sample this high-flying culinary show. Charming guestrooms are available, should you wish to extend your stay and explore the region. What’s not to like?

Name: La Pomme d'Or
Address: 1 rue de la Panneterie, Sancerre, 18300, France
Description: In the heart of a famous wine-growing village, a young couple from Brittany has opted to shine the spotlight on seafood to such an extent that you can almost smell the sea air. Their single set menu, whose dishes are intriguingly and poetically named, offers a choice of flawlessly fresh fish and shellfish, all of which are consummately cooked. The chef, who clearly knows his stuff, has his sights clearly focused on a single goal: taste. The wine list unsurprisingly gives the floor to Sancerre wines, and you'll hear no complaints from us. Cheerful, smiling service in an uncluttered, elegant interior.

Name: La Prensa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: What in the 1970s started life as a wine merchant’s gradually became a leading restaurant on the city’s food scene. Here, the duo of chef Marisa Barberán and her husband David Pérez (sommelier and front-of-house manager) have created a space in which the philosophy is based around one clear concept: a love for a job well done.In the minimalist-style dining room embellished with designer detail, savour contemporary and creative cuisine centred around two set menus, each offering different dishes: The Tasting Menu (tapas, 6 courses, and 2 desserts) and the Gastronomic Menu (tapas, 8 courses, and 3 desserts). The essence of La Prensa’s cuisine is based around an honest approach, the use of the best seasonal ingredients from the region, and a mastery of modern techniques which enables the chef to play with flavours, colours and textures and to create dishes that are highly expressive and innovative.

Name: La Preséf
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set within the La Fiorida complex – a low‑impact, farm‑stay operation – the restaurant La Preséf serves a modern cuisine that is deeply rooted in the local terroir. Most ingredients come from the property’s own garden and the adjoining farm (zero‑kilometer, farm‑to‑table sourcing). The venue features a traditional feeding trough (called a “preséf” in the local dialect) and an on‑site creamery. It stands out for its visual and sensory experimentation, a hallmark of a cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Guests who love alpine products can choose between two tasting menus, selected online at the time of booking: the first is a shorter, more traditional route; the second is slightly more creative while still staying firmly anchored to local tradition. The wine list also offers an excellent selection of indigenous labels.

Name: La Primula
Address: Via San Rocco 47, San Quirino, 33080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Set in the enchanted heart of Magredi, between Pordenone and Aviano, this elegant restaurant is steeped in over 150 years of history under the ownership of the Canton family, now re-energised by the return of their son Marco, a passionate sommelier. Time and tradition go hand in hand here, making this restaurant a timeless classic in the province and an example of reliable, refined gourmet dining. The dining room, with its majestic fireplace, wraps guests in a warm welcome, while in the kitchen, Andrea composes dishes from land and sea, adding modern touches and creating comforting flavours. The wine cellar is a treasure in its own right: a rich selection and bespoke service, even by the glass, with some of the most reasonable mark-ups in Italy. The same building is home to Osteria alle Nazioni, which serves more informal lunches, where the food celebrates Friulian tradition simply and deliciously.

Name: La Promenade - Maison Dallais
Address: 11 rue du Savoureulx, Le Petit-Pressigny, 37350, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Touraine countryside, Fabrice Dallais and his son Clément are writing a new chapter in the story of this family business. A tasteful low-key setting provides the backdrop for hearty helpings of spot-on food that is deeply rooted in the region: Racan pigeon, Géline de Touraine (heirloom poultry), pike, game and fresh vegetables from local market gardeners. Outstanding wine list and insightful tips from the sommelier. Even better, book yourself into one of the two prettily appointed guestrooms and stay overnight.

Name: La Provence
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: André van Alten is a fine example of a chef who continually reinvents himself while remaining grounded in his core principles. His impressive classical training is evident in the perfectly judged cuisson of foie gras and Black Angus fillet Rossini-style, accompanied by an intense Madeira sauce with real depth. We also applaud his eagerness to share his experience with younger generations. His calm, assured manner as he leads his team in the open kitchen is remarkable. Van Alten lets the ingredients speak for themselves, yet continues to innovate. For instance, he showcases the versatility of langoustine by presenting it in four different ways, including a deeply flavoured bisque sauce and a crisp Vietnamese spring roll. His creativity also comes through in the way he prepares the garnishes and incorporates international nuances. The interplay of hot and cold, varied textures and subtle vibrancy creates excitement on the plate. He has a penchant for fish, although saddle of lamb cooked in a coarse sea salt crust is a house classic. The excellent wine recommendations and attentive service from the charming hostess complement the food beautifully. At intimate La Provence, with its tranquil, leafy terrace, they certainly know how to spoil their guests – and have done for over 50 years!

Name: La Renaissance
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: For nearly 30 years, Arnaud and Cécilia Viel have been running their modern establishment with a strong personality in perfect harmony with the chef's cuisine. Here in Argentan, homage is paid to Normandy through exceptional hand-picked ingredients: local butter and unpasteurised farmhouse cream, scallops from Port-en-Bessin, lobster from Carteret, foie gras from the Pays d'Auge, sand carrots from Créances, sometimes combined with premium items such as caviar or black winter truffles. The food impresses with flawless execution and harmonious flavours. The excellent wine list is curated by Cécilia, who presides front of house with elegance and professionalism.

Name: La Revelía
Description: Many will think that its location in the heart of the countryside, approximately 4 miles north of Amorebieta-Etxano, only provides disconnection, relaxation and natural beauty; however... it is the basis of its entire culinary philosophy! In the Agroturismo Azkarraga, an old farmhouse renovated with a Nordic aesthetic and which today also has five cosy rooms, this restaurant dazzles with its interior design, minimalist in concept and with large windows that frame the environment so that the wonderful surrounding landscape enters the room. The chef Fernando González champions a modern cuisine, with a Basque and traditional base, which is not exempt from creative touches, with the option of ordering à la carte or letting yourself be carried away by his tasting menu (La Revelía). Some of the dishes on offer have won us over, such as the combination of tear pea and citrus sabayon or the excellent texture of the hake with its pil-pil, and it is not unusual to see foxes, roe deer and squirrels out of the windows!

Name: La Ribaudière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is housed in a contemporary building exuding rustic charm on the banks of the Charente River and opposite the château that houses the Grand Marnier distillery. Both indoors and out on the terrace, modern decor provides the backdrop for the signature cuisine of father-and-son team Thierry and Julien Verrat. Proceedings open with sourdough bread and summer truffle butter, followed by refined bites with Japanese influences: beechwood-smoked oysters, eel chawanmushi, and chicken liver mousse with XO cognac. The mains continue in this delicate vein: foie gras with seaweed and sturgeon dashi, John Dory with Bigorre bacon and vegetable civet (stew). Straightforward, vibrant cuisine in which technique is at the service of flavour.

Name: La Robe
Description: In his contemporary and elegant restaurant laid out around a lovely patio, Xavier Giraudet creates top-drawer modern cuisine with a focus on vegetables. The various set menus feature local and seasonal produce (sometimes even from the family vegetable garden), expertly cooked and full of flavour. In season, don't miss their exemplary rendition of hare à la royale à la Antonin Carême, a classic dish! A bravura performance.

Name: La Roseraie Modave
Description: A meal at La Roseraie is synonymous with a treat for all five senses. The experience starts with the drive through the lovely Ardennes countryside to this handsome 19C edifice, followed by the vision of the landscaped garden, home to welcoming guestrooms and pretty cottages, the champagne bar and the elegant restaurant, depicted by an exquisite blend of luxury details and home-from-home hospitality. Marie Trignon has respectfully and masterfully taken over the reins from her father.You can expect a classical culinary repertory, flanked by a flair for sourcing the best ingredients, without forgetting a passion for spices and a creative streak rich in delicacy. Chef Trignon enhances a fillet of red mullet with a curcuma-flavoured tabouleh, a tomato salad rich in refreshing hints of coriander and dill and sweet-sour broccoli stalks. She has a knack for crafting felicitous seasonings that underscore without overpowering delicate ingredients such as scallops. What’s not to like?

Name: La Rotonde des Trésoms
Address: Les Trésoms, 15 boulevard de la Corniche, Annecy, 74000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The huge conservatory of this Rotonde commands a splendid panoramic view over Annecy Lake, sweeping diners off their feet, even before their first bite! Originally from Arcachon, Eric Prowalski adds flavours from southwest France to recipes which highlight sustainably grown local produce. This skilled craftsman deftly unfolds a repertory in which creativity never hampers the flavour, developing a delicious "dialogue" between his adopted land and his homeland. The understated interior showcases a subtle blend of warm materials such as leather and oak.

Name: La Rucola 2.0
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the famous castle in Sirmione’s historic centre, this restaurant is immediately striking for its elegant and creative feel. The choice here focuses on four tasting menus, from which guests can choose individual courses à la carte style if they prefer. Francesco Turturro’s cuisine is creative in feel, including various fish and seafood dishes alongside a few meat options and a menu dedicated exclusively to vegetables.

Name: La Réserve Rimbaud
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: “Montpellier the Gifted”, as the city likes to bill itself, provides the backdrop to this well-hidden restaurant on the banks of the Lez. Slightly off the beaten track, it boasts a divine riverside terrace shaded by plane trees – a refreshing haven in hot summers. This modern and sophisticated Reserve is located in an old country house, an Ali Baba’s cavern of gourmet delights, unearthed from the little-known repertory of Languedoc-Roussillon. Former second of Alain Dutournier at the Carré des Feuillants, Charles Fontès signs intelligent compositions that revolves around the ingredient. Subtle plays of textures and flavours with an overriding goal of authentic simplicity. Seabream, squid and red mullet, Camargues eels and Lucques olives feature among the appetisers – Occitania on the table!

Name: La Rôtisserie
Description: Located on the first floor of the Hotel Storchen, La Rôtisserie is every bit as tastefully decorated as the establishment that houses it – which was first mentioned in the 14C. It has a beautiful dining room with high ceilings, large arched windows and elegant, high-quality furnishings – this is a traditional yet contemporary affair. In the kitchen, the chefs work with precision and great skill to produce their own modern, international take on classic cuisine. In fine weather, be sure to head out onto the fantastic terrace – from this wonderful old-town location you can take in views of the Limmat River and the historical buildings laid out on the other side of the water. Fancy a special experience? Then book the Chef's Table in the centre of the kitchen! Brunch is served on Sundays.

Name: La Sala dei Grappoli
Address: Castello di Poggio alle Mura, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The emotion begins along the approach, between vineyards, cypress trees and olive groves that compose the landscape of the most classic Tuscan countryside, culminating in the dramatic arrival before the imposing Castello Banfi, of medieval origin. The restaurant fits naturally into this setting of great evocativeness, recognisable also through the wine-themed frescoes that decorate the interior rooms. When the weather allows it, however, the terrace is the privileged space: here the panorama, attentive service and the quality of the cuisine combine to create a memorable experience. In the kitchen, chef Domenico Francone, originally from Puglia, with a measured hand introduces touches of his homeland, from taralli to small, flavourful panzerotti. The offering is articulated across three tasting menus that speak of philosophy, territory and a particular attentiveness to the plant world. A well-calibrated selection of desserts brings the meal to a fine close, between indulgence and lightness: among them, the milk foam with toffee caramel and peanuts stands out for its balance and pleasantness.

Name: La Salita
Address: Pere III El Gran 11, Valencia, 46005, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A superb example of how perseverance, effort and solid values in the face of fresh challenges helps you to grow professionally. This restaurant, occupying an impressive mansion in the city’s Ruzafa district that has been decorated with plenty of charm and personality, stands out for its different dining options. In addition to the main dining room upstairs, it also boasts a pretty garden, two attractive tables in front of the kitchen and a particularly pleasant terrace where guests can enjoy aperitifs, a meal or a relaxing post-dinner drink. Chef Begoña Rodrigo showcases her talents on several tasting menus which demonstrate her interest in working with vinegars, pickles, citrus fruit and highly original vegetarian charcuterie to create light and fresh dishes that still have plenty of personality: Gaia (meat), Ondina (fish and seafood), Cloris (vegetarian) and La Salita (which brings it all together at its very best). We particularly enjoyed the courses devoted to Dénia red prawns and eel!

Name: La Société
Description: Everything is just right in this compact fine dining restaurant in the student area known as Kwartier Latäng, from the service to the ambience and the food. Chef Leon Hofmockel's fresh and original ideas shine through in his innovative dishes. His creative French cuisine is presented in the form of a five- to seven-course set menu – a vegetarian version is also available upon request. With great skill, he combines exquisite craftsmanship with finesse and bold flavours. This is evident in the XO-sauce-braised carrot with a salty, nutty sunflower seed pesto, a full-bodied vadouvan hollandaise with crispy croutons and an aromatic curry sauce – an exceptional vegetarian course! Complementing this is incredibly friendly and attentive service with a personal touch – the chef even makes an appearance from time to time. One thing to mention is how wonderfully relaxed and stylish the bistro feels. French classics and a three-course set menu are available at lunchtime Sat-Mon.

Name: La Source
Address: 8 allée de La Charpinière, Saint-Galmier, 42330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally from Cuzieu, a mere 2km away, Antoine Bergeron is very much a local boy. Ambitious and passionate about his work, he takes you on a surprise fine dining journey that subtly, creatively and joyfully showcases ingredients from hand-picked suppliers. Comfortably seated in the bright, contemporary dining room, you will enjoy a culinary tour of the region and the local markets. For example, Drôme zander with sorrel, tarragon and vanilla-laced fish stock; fillet of Aubrac beef, red cabbage in walnut oil and anise hyssop sabayon. Food that nurtures the soul, with special mention for the sauces and stellar craftsmanship.

Name: La Speranzina Restaurant & Relais
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Sirmione, La Speranzina is a romantic retreat suffused with the scent of the Mediterranean. The bright interiors, decorated in pale lours, convey a timeless elegance, while, in summer, the terrace offers rare emotional experiences: the sparkling lake, the castle reflected in the water, tables suspended between water and sky. In the kitchen, Delfo Schiaffino creates flavours with an expertise that produces technical yet harmonious dishes, in which blue lobster meets caviar and wagyu beef merges with hints of French haute cuisine, in a dance of textures and aromas that seduces the senses. Every morsel is a story, every glass a journey: the wine cellar celebrates Champagne and great labels like Gaja, while three panoramic suites invite you to prolong the dream.

Name: La Stüa de Michil - Simone Cantafio
Address: Strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: To get to this restaurant you head up towards the church in the prettiest part of Corvara, where you’ll find the La Perla hotel, one of the best in the valley, on your left. Once inside the hotel, you’ll be accompanied to La Stüa (stube in Ladin), where the profusion of wood lends an intimate and romantic feel to the decor. Although the setting is typical of the region, Simone Cantafio’s cuisine will take you on an extraordinary culinary journey. Originally from Calabria, this chef worked for many years in Japan, just one of his many formative experiences. As a result, his dishes feature different influences, often with a focus on vegetables. The name of the restaurant is a reference to owner and manager Michele Costa, an indefatigable and extraordinary figure in the world of Ladin tourism.

Name: La Table - Christophe Hay
Address: 200 allée des Quatre-Vents, au golf de Limère, Ardon, 45160, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Opposite Limère golf course, Christophe Hay's second establishment bears his distinctive hallmark, illustrated by a contemporary interior inspired by nature and the forest, the chef's main sources of inspiration, together with veg from his garden. In a huge open kitchen, the team rolls out a vibrant score that is perfectly in tune with the house ethos and underpinned by flawless technique. The delicate, seasonal repertory is eco-conscious and favours short supply chains and game in season. The first-class wine cellar boasts over 600 labels. Particularly responsive service.

Name: La Table - Domaine du Liziec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Set among flower gardens and century-old trees, this fully restored 16C Breton estate has been enhanced by an elegant contemporary extension. In this refined setting, chef Olivier Samson (formerly of La Gourmandière - La Table d'Olivier) showcases his talent. His refined contemporary cuisine is deeply rooted in the local terroir and presented in the form of tasting menus. Celtic produce is handled with precision: Breton abalone with spinach and a pork jus; sole from small-boat fishing with asparagus and kumquat; roast pigeon with cocoa and pigeon leg bonbon. In dish after dish, buckwheat, sea fennel and buttermilk underscore the Breton identity of this gourmet experience.

Name: La Table Breizh Café
Description: This Franco-Japanese gourmet establishment is on the first floor of a crêperie: welcome to the world of Bertrand Larcher. A champion of buckwheat and Brittany’s culture, Larcher first opened a string of pancake houses in Japan, before doing the same in France with the same success. Now in a dining room overlooking the bay of Mont Saint Michel, chef Raphaël-Fumio Kudaka blends Breton produce with Japanese techniques and seasonings. Sautéed monkfish, langoustine, agedashi of koya-tofu and daikon and a thick shellfish broth; buckwheat soba noodles, gutsy stock of dried Brittany bonito and kombu, fried oyster in a buckwheat crust; pancake filled with cream of sake kasu, marinated orange, orange sorbet and citrus fruit coulis. Top-notch ingredients, surgical precision, savvy seasonings and lashings of delicacy depict this happy marriage between east and west.

Name: La Table Mirasol
Description: In this 1912 villa, a genuine Belle Époque period gem, the fine dining restaurant is run by chef Philippe Lagraula. He deftly blends produce from his native Landes with influences from further afield, particularly Peru, his wife's home country. The tasting menu is consummate, striking, creative and well-paced, marrying minimalism and character: squid stuffed with the first ceps of the season, squab in Armagnac with Peruvian chocolate and Aquitaine caviar. The Armagnac selection more than lived up to our expectations…

Name: La Table d'Adrien
Description: This sleek chalet overlooking Verbier serves big-boned, inventive Italian cuisine in a snug, stylishly appointed hotel. The carefully structured lineup stars a top-drawer cast of exceptional ingredients. In addition to artful plating, each dish reveals surgical craftsmanship, lashings of creativity, superlative quality and spot-on marriages of flavours. The eight-course tasting menu can be whittled down to six, even four courses depending on your appetite. We highly recommend the wine pairings, particularly if you opt for the tasting menu. Slick, seamless service.

Name: La Table d'Antonio Salvatore au Rampoldi
Address: 3 avenue des Spélugues, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
Description: Born in Basilicata in southern Italy, chef Antonio Salvatore’s profession has taken him all over the place from Spain and England to Russia – where he met the new owner of Rampoldi. In the former cigar lounge, he has master-minded a tailor-made setting (only five tables), where he meticulously rolls out top-notch contemporary Italian cuisine. Unsurprisingly, the sourcing is first-class and the chef draws on small-scale producers from around Menton and San Remo, together with some ingredients imported from the south of Italy. A few examples: bottoni di vitello tonnato; cabri dodici ore; texture di cioccolato… Meanwhile, the brasserie features a handful of updated classics.

Name: La Table d'Armante
Address: L'Armancette, 4088 route de Saint-Nicolas, Saint-Gervais-les-Bains, 74170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of a genuine Alpine village dominated by the Miage peaks, a former bakery has morphed into an understated luxe chalet that is home to a swish, sleek mountain restaurant decked out in wood, stone and velvet with an open kitchen. A plush, muted vibe, cosy bar, glazed cellars, a tearoom and dining for forty. The chef celebrates local produce – fish from Lake Geneva, Douvaine duck, in a single set menu of seasonal inspiration. Spot-on, indulgent and consummately crafted cuisine. Just the ticket for high-flying gastronomy overlooking the “roof of Europe”. Alfresco dining with a view in summertime.

Name: La Table d'Asten
Description: The first floor of this house overlooking the port sets the scene for many a fine meal. After a remarkable career (Coquillage at Cancale, La Pyramide – Patrick Henriroux at Vienne and the K2 at Courchevel), chef Samuel Selosse now gives free rein to his creativity. Firmly rooted in the zeitgeist and always exquisitely presented, his cooking showcases first-rate ingredients, be they fish or vegetables, giving rise to delicacies such as cauliflower in citrus fruits and fire roasted cuttlefish, brill from small boats, asparagus and seaweed-flavoured hollandaise sauce or a pine-flavoured creamy millefeuille. His sommelière wife runs the dining room with the same drive and sense of purpose.

Name: La Table d'Aurélien Largeau
Description: Aurélien Largeau is now bringing his culinary creations to life on premises that used to accommodate Sillon, having brightened up the intimate setting of this restaurant a stone's throw from the ocean. The chef from La Rochelle lets Atlantic fish and seafood take centre stage, leaving meat the supporting role. A veritable maritime voyage, his multi-course set menu gives pride of place to Breton shellfish, wild seaweed and even traditional recipes – while also referencing the Basque Country. Exceptional ingredients (but also humble sardines) are adorned with intense jus (the red mullet is a case in point), and textures are juxtaposed (as with the lobster). Even the desserts acknowledge the sea, cleverly combining sweet and briny notes (pear and sea fennel jus). A precise, lively cuisine that moves to the rhythm of the tides. Alongside him, Mathilde Fesneau brilliantly orchestrates proceedings front of house.

Name: La Table d'Hôtes - La Rôtisserie du Chambertin
Description: Thomas Collomb is at the head of an outstanding table d’hôtes in Gevrey-Chambertin, in which nothing is left to chance! Flawless ingredients, most of which from organic, meticulously selected suppliers, recognisable, artfully presented dishes which unfold during a tasting menu rich in surprises and a stylish smart rustic interior. But there is more to come! The wine list is out of this world (well, this is the region!) and the service is professional and attentive, without being oppressive. The pinnacle of fine dining.

Name: La Table d'Hôtes - Le Quatrième Mur
Address: 2 place de la Comédie, Bordeaux, 33000, France
Description: At the Grand Théâtre de Bordeaux, a magnificent example of neo-Classical architecture, even dining is theatrical. Chef Etchebest's 12 guests share the same large table in a vaulted cellar, where they are privy to the behind-the-scenes workings of a restaurant, amid introductions to the dishes and the to and fro of the waitstaff. Everything here is a surprise: from the menu to the wine and food pairings, down to the cutlery that you choose yourself. The same spirit is to be found in the chef's dishes, which are unabashedly original and resolved to strike that harmony of flavours. The technique is impeccable (the foie gras des Landes fried and smoked in duck jus with orange!), plus you can enjoy the food while getting to know your neighbours at the table. Even when Philippe Etchebest is absent, he is still there – via video conference with the guests before the meal starts! An experience, truly.

Name: La Table d'Olivier
Description: At Olivier’s Table, Pierre is in the kitchen, while his partner, Fanny, a talented pastry chef, oversees the front-of-house. Normandy-born Pierre has enthusiastically embraced Corrèze, his land of adoption, in this town centre stone house, whose modern furnishings and designer lighting are the epitome of elegant. The repertory, in tune with the zeitgeist and at bargain prices, ticks all the boxes: enticing, polished and colourful. Examples include poached oysters, marinated seabass with citrus fruit and a lemon-vodka sorbet; veal scallop and sweetbread, ravioles of chanterelle mushrooms and black garlic followed by a chocolate, pecan nut, clementine and citrus fruit sorbet extravaganza to finish. It is well worth taking the time to do justice to such a spread!

Name: La Table d'Uzès
Description: On a square in the historic centre, chef Christophe Ducros is thriving in a stylish snug historic house. Ducros crafts balanced, big-boned dishes of pure-bred Mediterranean inspiration and heritage. A few examples: houmous of Montaren chickpeas with basil-laced ice cream; the chef’s signature - Costières pigeon roasted whole; smoked anglerfish paired with veg direct from Uzès market; pistachio-spiked red fruit minestrone with cream cheese ice cream. The score’s manifest coherence is palpable. Savour this fine dining experience on the rooftop terrace overlooking the cathedral.

Name: La Table de Chaintré
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This quintessential country restaurant, tucked away in a picturesque village in the heart of the Pouilly-Fuissé vineyards, is the brainchild of a friendly, industrious couple. He scours the local markets for fine produce, which he unveils in cleverly crafted dishes. For example, langoustines from Brittany with celtuce and the first tomatoes, frogs’ legs poached and deep-fried in Japanese breadcrumbs, or Bresse chicken with pattypan squash, rainbow chard and heirloom carrots… The food is naturally enough paired with a fine selection of Burgundy and Beaujolais. The set menu changes weekly – all the more reason to return regularly!

Name: La Table de Courcelles - Château de Courcelles
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: With the arrival of Italian chef Massimiliano Sena (originally from Sorrento), armed with his impressive CV, this noble and elegant Grand Siècle-style residence has entered a modern culinary era that bodes well. Local and seasonal ingredients take pride of place, and the chef's Italian roots make themselves felt in a delicate and subtle manner. There's no showboating or recourse to culinary techniques just for the sake of it; the confident expertise and harmoniously preserved marriages of flavours allow diners to fully appreciate the slow-cooked egg with its airy chanterelle mousse, or the cod with courgette, raspberry and black garlic. Terrific wine list with over 700 wines. There is a pleasant view of the formal garden and canal from the glass-roofed dining area.

Name: La Table de Cédric Béchade - L'Auberge Basque
Address: 745 vieille route de Saint-Pée - quartier Helbarron, Saint-Pée-sur-Nivelle, 64310, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Close to Saint-Jean-de-Luz and the coast, this old Basque farmhouse has an elegant contemporary wing overlooking the Rhune (Larrun) mountain and the countryside. It is here in the very heart of the Basque Country that Cédric Béchade welcomes you in the style of a true 21st-century innkeeper. This creative chef (who trained at the Hôtel du Palais in Biarritz, then worked in the kitchens of the Plaza Athénée alongside Jean-François Piège) uses top-notch ingredients sourced from the terroir and prepared with all due care – think squid, bluefin tuna, Ibaiama pork, yuzu from Ahyerre. The terrace is very popular on sunny days, as are the guestrooms to extend your stay. N.B. A bistronomy menu is available for lunch at Café Basque.

Name: La Table de L'Incomparable
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This knockout location overlooking Bourget Lake provides the perfect foil to spot-on, polished cuisine rich in gutsy flavours with a penchant for local country produce: cottage garden veg, trout, fera, farm-reared veal… Dishes that pack a punch and which showcase a savvy mix of contrasting textures. The view from the terrace over the lake and Mont du Chat is out of this world.

Name: La Table de La Butte
Address: 12 rue de la Mer, Plouider, 29260, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Nicolas and Solenne Conraux are the third generation at the head of this establishment, a pioneer in the field of sustainable development and cookery. Local produce reigns supreme in this gourmet map of Finistère: oysters, lobster, abalone, but also seaweed, vegetables and even the 100% Brittany cheeses. Just as Brittany takes the limelight in the plate, it is also celebrated in the décor and the tableware which is the work of local craftspeople. What’s more, the service team is always happy to explain the ingredients and different fermentation and maceration techniques used by the kitchen staff. The bread (baked in the chef’s own bakery) is fiendishly delicious, as are the various Made in Brittany butters (seaweed, fleur de sel, etc). The wine list errs towards small, organic wineries.

Name: La Table de Nans
Address: 126 corniche du Liouquet, La Ciotat, 13600, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Nans Gaillard had a childhood dream of opening his own restaurant in La Ciotat where he was born. After growing up in Brittany and learning the ropes with the likes of Joël Robuchon, he found this inn dating from the interwar period, perched on the cliffs facing the sea with a knockout terrace framed by tall pine trees. In this magical setting, entirely refurbished with natural materials and a muted colour scheme, he pays tribute to regional produce as he subtly tweaks pedigree Gallic traditions: carpaccio of seabream, Baux olive oil; roast lamb cutlets, savory-laced jus and crispy panisse (chickpea fritters).

Name: La Table de Philippe Girardon
Address: Domaine de Clairefontaine, 105 chemin des Fontanettes, Chonas-l'Amballan, 38121, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The fourth generation is at the helm of this family business, established in a splendid 18C edifice surrounded by grounds, which was once the holiday home of the bishops of Lyon. The inventive food is the consummate work of a chef who has had a Michelin star since 1993 and who became a MOF in 1997. Top quality regional produce, surgically precise craftsmanship in a classical vein and the occasional more modern technique depict the culinary ethos. This welcoming scene provides the backdrop to dishes such as a soup of frog’s legs with mushrooms and wild garlic, Grenoble-style arctic char, slowly baked in its juices, risotto of soft wheat and beurre noisette.

Name: La Table de Pierre
Address: Domaine du Mas de Pierre, 2320 route des Serres, Saint-Paul-de-Vence, 06570, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Le Mas de Pierre, a luxury hotel surrounded by unspoilt countryside, stands in landscaped grounds with olive trees and a vegetable garden. Happily seated in the lush green conservatory, with a sliding roof and walls, diners can unwind in the cocooned tranquillity, as they sample a contemporary, colourful score with a healthy dimension and sprinkled with flowers and aromatic plants from the garden. A friendly, bistro vibe and traditional Provençal and Italian cuisine depict the Dolce Provenza bistro.

Name: La Table de Pierre Reboul
Address: Hôtel Renaissance, 320 avenue Wolfgang-Amadeus-Mozart, Aix-en-Provence, 13100, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Olives, which are central to Pierre Reboul’s work, inspired both the low-key, natural interior of his restaurant and his cuisine steeped in creativity. In the stylish, intimate setting of the Renaissance Hotel, exclusive materials and olive-green shades set the scene. A terrace framed by two olive trees and a counter overlooking the open-plan kitchen add the final touches to the portrait. The Chef celebrates regional produce in dishes that look as good as they taste: trompe-l’oeil olives explode in the mouth, a delicate, inventive trilogy on a Mediterranean shrimp theme or a subtle, crunchy courgette flower stuffed with langoustine. Polished and inventive.

Name: La Table de Tourrel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This handsome 17C mansion was where Charles Gounod played the first bars of his opera, Mireille, to Frédéric Mistral, author of the poem that inspired the libretto. In a flavoursome echo of this prestigious past, the venue’s modern-day chef orchestrates a gourmet score, inspired in this case by the regional pantry: fish from Grau-du-Roi, trout from Isle-sur-la-Sorgue, Mont Ventoux pork and lamb from la Crau… The menu, packed in Provençal melodies, is served at a communal table d’hôtes against a backdrop of bare stone walls that set a friendly, cosy tone. The rooftop terrace, which commands views over the village’s skyline, unveils a more casual culinary lineup.

Name: La Table de Xavier Mathieu
Address: Le Phébus, 508 route de Murs, Joucas, 84220, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Raised in Marseille, Xavier Mathieu is a true-blue Provençal lad. Having trained under Roger Vergé and then Joël Robuchon, this chef, who sports a distinctive shock of white hair, breathes new life into Provençal culinary traditions. He puts a spin on family or local recipes – soupe au pistou, black olive tian, leg of lamb from the Alpilles cooked in warm garrigue sand –, adding a dash of finesse, modernity and indulgence. Vegetables, olives and herbs from the kitchen garden feature throughout. His creations are sampled in the exclusive setting of a luxurious bastide whose foundations date back to the Order of Malta. Near the pool, Le Café de la Fontaine, Le Phébus's second restaurant, offers a simpler, more relaxed take on the cuisine of the South of France.

Name: La Table de l'Orangerie - Château de Fonscolombe
Address: Route de Saint-Canadet, Le Puy-Sainte-Réparade, 13610, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This 18C château is set in listed grounds with many species of trees, including an Atlas cedar planted by the late Queen Mother. The restaurant has taken up abode in plush sitting rooms on the first floor, while in summer, meals are served on the monumental terrace. The son of farmers from the Loire region, Marc Fontanne (formerly Le Prieuré at Villeneuve-lès-Avignon) started learning the ropes from his brother, a butcher and charcutier, at a young age. He serves three tasting menus, one of which is entirely vegetarian. Tempura and roasted dwarf broccoli with a red onion and basil jus; flame-licked tomato, Lucca olives, iced tomato; raviole of marjoram-laced artichokes, hazelnuts, parmesan and vanilla emulsion. Fresh local ingredients with playful, graphic plating and a subtle interplay of bitter, sweet and aniseed flavours (like fennel).

Name: La Table de l'Ours
Address: Les Barmes de l'Ours, 100 montée de Bellevarde, Val-d'Isère, 73150, France
Description: This fine dining establishment is part of a luxurious hotel, which feels like a plush chalet. On the edge of the famous ski run, Face de Bellevarde, the restaurant is chic and elegant with a wealth of wood, exposed stone and mirrors. Passionate about his craft, conscientious chef Antoine Gras shows the utmost respect for the ingredients. These he showcases in flavoursome dishes that don't mess around. The combinations are spot on: just-seared langoustine, julienne vegetables, chilled vinaigrette with grated carrots; whitefish from Lake Geneva, sorrel, silky gourd purée with juniper berries. The enthusiasm of the youthful front-of-house team is contagious, and that also goes for the sommelier, an ambassador of Savoie wines. Le Coin Savoyard and La Rôtisserie are the hotel's more laid-back eateries.

Name: La Table de la Bergerie
Address: 3 route de la Pierre, Bellevigne-en-Layon, 49380, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant near Angers, in the heart of the Coteaux-du-Layon vineyards, is well worth your attention. It is the haunt of talented David Guitton, who hails from Loire Atlantique and who has trained under top chefs all over the world from the United States and Britain to Monaco. There is no à la carte menu here, but a voluntarily concise offering that reverently respects the seasons. David sources his ingredients from small, local producers, rustling up dishes that err towards minimalist so that the flavour can take centre stage. Regional wines, including the estate’s organic production, take pride of place on the wine list.

Name: La Table de la Ferme
Address: Domaine de Murtoli, Vallée de l'Ortolo, Sartène, 20100, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: On a huge estate (over 6,000 acres) home to sheepfolds that marry traditional Corsican architecture with modern comforts, Murtoli is clearly in a class of its own. The seasonal score ranges from an à la carte lineup to a tasting menu and piattini (tapas-like snacks) served in a casual vibe. The convincing modern tasting menu, featuring several courses, pays a heartfelt tribute to local produce sourced from the estate’s olive grove, garden, farm and the sea, with a subtle sprinkling of herbs from the sweet-scented scrubland. Alfresco dining shaded by olive trees, outstanding Corsican vintages and on-the-ball service. What’s not to like?

Name: La Table des Pères - Domaine du Château des Pères
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This sprawling estate never fails to make an impression: a Classical 18C castle, a 19C water tower, works of art, a hotel made up of futuristic pods fixed to a central metal mast and, finally, the circular restaurant with a living roof reminiscent of a flying saucer that has landed in the middle of the vegetable garden. Chef Jérôme Jouadé draws on his true affinity with nature and plants to practise his art here. He also makes use of a greenhouse, a snail pen and an orchard, and does his own wild picking. Sturgeon, crème crue and parsley ice cream; ravioli filled with cervelle de canut (herbed cheese spread) and garden vegetables; rabbit ballotine and sausage paired with lobster: his inspired recipes hit the mark every time. The wine list, mostly organic or biodynamic, is terrific.

Name: La Table du 11
Address: 8 rue de la Chancellerie, Versailles, 78000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Awarded a MICHELIN star in 2016, chef Jean-Baptiste Lavergne-Morazzani continues to delight diners in his modern and refined restaurant, nestled in the Cour des Senteurs, a stone's throw from the Palace of Versailles. The set menu, which is regularly updated, whisks you away on a meticulously devised and indulgent culinary journey – dishes include marinated langoustine on a bed of warm rice with a hint of vinegar and agastache leaves, accompanied by a delicious langoustine emulsion. At its core is seasonality and top-notch produce, which is generally organic, sourced from sustainable fishing and farming, but also from the family vegetable garden. The wine list is extensive and varied. A restaurant that has earned its reputation.

Name: La Table du Cap Estel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched atop the rocky cliffside on an enchanting peninsula between Nice and Monaco, this hotel is one of the most secluded and exclusive spots on the Côte d'Azur. Access is via a discreet gate, then a winding path that seems to draw you away from the world. Dining here on the terrace, lulled by the swaying palms of a Mediterranean garden, feels like a rare privilege. Chef Kévin Garcia – formerly executive chef at Frédéric Anton's Jules Verne – enhances the blissful experience with his culinary homage to seafood, garden herbs and top-notch local vegetables. With their clear, unadulterated flavours, eschewing ostentation in favour of showcasing remarkable precision and genuine technical flair: raw bonito, sea-sourced condiments, roasted-rice cream and Oscietra caviar; gamberoni, tomato and basil consommé, and tarragon-infused prawn-head jus; grilled amberjack, spiny artichoke and barigoule.

Name: La Table du Gourmet
Description: In Riquewihr, Jean-Luc Brendel has built up an entire ecosystem: in addition to his fine dining restaurant, he has a modern winstub and also offers luxurious guestrooms for overnight stays. At La Table du Gourmet, in the heart of the medieval city, the chef cooks beautiful seasonal ingredients with great care and a dash of creativity, making each dish his own. His different menus showcase produce from Alsace and from his garden (tended according to the principles of permaculture) such as the delicious Petrowski turnip, served with humanely-reared veal, cooked over the embers. Two wine lists, the first dedicated to the fines wines of Alsace, and all this to be enjoyed in surroundings that combine olde worlde charm (the building dates back to the 16C) with contemporary decorative touches.

Name: La Table du Grapiot
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of a wine-growing Jura village, opposite the town hall, the modern architecture of this restaurant is depicted by wood, glass, steel and zinc. It is run by a youthful team of associates, most of whom have been mates since high school, including chef Vivien Sonzogni and his wife, Noémie. He draws on his experience (Le Château at Germigney, Le Parc at Besançon, Caprice in Hong Kong and Scotland’s Gleneagles) to craft a contemporary score that invariably showcases local produce (snails roasted in garlic butter with foamy curd cheese; Bresse poultry, vin jaune and tarragon sauce, etc.) and the odd creative twist. Fine wine cellar including many Jura vintages.

Name: La Table-Lasne by Alain Bianchin
Address: Rue du Try Bara 33, Ohain, 1380, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Alain Bianchin is a genuine craftsman who sensitively blends his classical background with a modern outlook and a scattering of Asian-inspired influences. His versatility and delicacy are founded on textbook perfect technique and the kitchen is his playground. He may highlight the subtle harmony of tuna and foie gras with blood oranges and a jus of smoked oil and soy sauce, but he is also capable of executing melt-in-the-mouth, aromatic lamb flanked by Mediterranean sides and a gravy laced in Roscoff onions. The menu aims above all to allow premium ingredients to shout their name. The wine list, in the same vein, is well stocked in Burgundies. The view over the rolling hills of Lasne concludes the portrait of this contemporary eatery, which mixes designer with authentic natural materials.

Name: La Tana Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: To reach Tana Gourmet one must ascend to the Asiago plateau, where Alessandro Dal Degan has built one of the most personal and innovative gastronomic experiences in the Italian landscape. His cuisine reflects a vision deeply bound to the concepts of travel, exploration and research: key words defining a culinary journey in continuous evolution. The distinctive character of the offering lies in its capacity to surprise through unusual pairings, refined techniques and a constant creative tension. Particularly significant is the decision to forgo added salt and sugar: a choice that does not limit gustatory intensity but, on the contrary, enhances the identity and depth of the flavours. In the dining room, alongside Dal Degan, Enrico Maglio pursues an equally original exploration of the world of beverages, constructing pairings conceived as an integral part of the gastronomic narrative rather than mere accompaniment. The result is an immersive, coherent and strongly individual experience that confirms Tana Gourmet as one of the most original and stimulating tables in Italy.

Name: La Tasquería
Description: Chef Javi Estévez, who revolutionised Madrid’s culinary scene by elevating humble offal to the realms of haute-cuisine, made the right decision when he moved to this establishment, larger and more welcoming than the one where he took his first steps to success (that establishment still maintains his essence, in a bistro atmosphere, under the name La Barra de la Tasquería).This space on Calle Modesto Lafuente, which has taken a new direction under his hand, remains faithful to an idea that is part of its DNA: ‘we are specialists in cooking offal, but we do other things as well.’ The dining experience here is centred around three tasting menus (Tasquería, Tasquería Extendido and The Menu), the aim of which is to recapture the city’s ‘offal culture’ while reinterpreting it with contemporary concepts and techniques. This concept sees the kitchen working with offal such as sweetbreads, brain, trotters, tripe, combs, and the famous fried and confit head of suckling pig, one of its most popular dishes, and one that we all share on our social media feeds! They also serve fish!

Name: La Terrasse - Cheval Blanc St-Tropez
Address: Plage de la Bouillabaisse, Saint-Tropez, 83990, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: La Terrasse steps in at lunchtime as the restaurant of Le Cheval Blanc hotel. In the shade of umbrella pines, looking out over the Bay of SaintTropez, Arnaud Donckele and his team conjure up Mediterranean cuisine drawing on distinct Provençal influences. The premium-quality ingredients are prepared with a great sense of finesse and rigour: porcini tarte fine; lobster tail grilled in its shell, lobster roe sabayon; rabbit pie, sweetbreads and foie gras. Outstanding and wide-ranging selection of wines. The quintessence of French art de vivre…

Name: La Terrazza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Hotel Eden, the restaurant offers one of the most captivating views of the capital: through the large windows, the view stretches from the Quirinale to the dome of St Peter’s, with Rome taking centre stage in the panorama. In the kitchen, a menu with great character is taking shape, deeply rooted in Mediterranean cuisine and enhanced by a measured yet distinctive use of spices, aromatic herbs and seasonal ingredients. Examples include chlorophyll-stuffed buttons, served with a rich mussel cream sauce, or chicken with peppers, a sophisticated reinterpretation of a traditional Roman classic. The experience is rounded off by a wine list with an international flavour, curated with a focus on depth and careful selection rather than simply the breadth of the selection.

Name: La Torre
Address: Strada Spicciano 7, Tavarnelle Val di Pesa, 50028, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magic of Castello del Nero, a splendid 12th-century residence nestled in the Chianti hills, offers an experience that captures the very essence of Tuscany from the moment you arrive. Panoramic views, history and charm come together in the estate’s elegant surroundings, while extra virgin olive oil, wines and local produce are showcased to the full, thanks in part to a particularly well-stocked wine cellar. At the heart of the dining experience lies a style of cooking that is technically skilful, creative and, at the same time, deeply flavourful, presented with an aesthetic that is in keeping with the setting. The restaurant offers three tasting menus: ‘Evoluzione Vegetali’, ‘La Terra’ and ‘Il Mare’, complemented by an exceptional selection of pastries, as evidenced by imaginative desserts and a refined assortment of petits fours served at the end of the meal.

Name: La Tortuga
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: In Gragnano, La Tortuga has been synonymous with quality and reliability for decades. The dining room, intimate and romantic in atmosphere, is made all the more agreeable by the welcoming manner of Signora Orietta, professional yet pleasingly informal, and a discerning judge of wine: the list bears eloquent testimony to this, with some interesting labels also in vintages. The kitchen delivers a reassuring and accomplished repertoire, built upon excellent produce, from lake fish – as in the very successful spaghettini with lake ragù – to the finest of sea fish. Among the dishes that drew particular admiration from our Inspectors, the fillet of sea bass stands out, cooked with precision and set alongside a raw prawn marinated in liquorice, resting upon a delicate fennel broth and potato cream: a great classic, interpreted with restraint and elegance.

Name: La Tour des Vents
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the highest point of the Bergerac vineyards, next to an old windmill, this opulent establishment commands an unforgettable view. The cuisine in the zeitgeist shines the spotlight on first-class produce (Aquitaine beef, foie gras, Périgord poultry), combining razor-sharp technique, confident, spot-on cooking and big-boned flavours.

Name: La Trattoria Enrico Bartolini
Address: Località Badiola, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Beyond the gate, a long and dramatic avenue lined alternately with cypresses and maritime pines leads to L’Andana, one of the most evocative hotels in the area. On reaching the restaurant, do not be misled by the name: what awaits is not the atmosphere of a trattoria, but refined dining rooms and the cuisine of Enrico Bartolini, here working in partnership with Gabriele Verri. The latter’s Ligurian roots find an echo in certain dishes, others embrace Tuscany, and creativity inspires the rest.

Name: La Trompette
Address: 3-7 Devonshire Road, Chiswick, London, W4 2EU, United Kingdom
Description: The jewel in Chiswick’s culinary crown remains as popular as ever, thanks to its local feel, relaxed atmosphere and, most importantly, its skilled and generous cooking. Largely British ingredients are combined with influences from France and occasionally the wider Mediterranean. So you can expect carefully prepared dishes like corn-fed chicken with potato galettes, celeriac purée and wild garlic salsa verde, where the flavours are as assured as they are satisfying. Bright and delightful on a summer’s day and cosy and warm in winter, this is a restaurant for all seasons and all occasions.

Name: La Trota
Address: Via Santa Susanna 33, località Piedicolle, Rivodutri, 02010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Before entering this restaurant, stop for a moment to admire the crystal-clear waters of the Santa Susanna canal which runs opposite the building. La Trota has revolutionised and raised the standard of cooking freshwater fish, elevating it to the level of other produce traditionally considered to be more refined. At this restaurant, the Serva brothers, ably assisted by their respective children, showcase ingredients such as trout, tench, freshwater crayfish, pike and catfish, which are sourced from the clean waters nearby and which feature on the menu alongside a few meat dishes. They also make good use of wild herbs – guests are given an extract of these to take home, which they can use to make a warm herbal tea or a cool drink. There’s also an excellent choice of wine to accompany your meal, plus a surprising selection of cognacs and liqueurs. In fine weather, guests have the option of dining on the small wooden bridge spanning the canal. The restaurant celebrates its 60th anniversary in 2023.

Name: La Tête en l'air
Address: 43 rue de la Fontaine, Vannes, 56000, France
Description: An enthusiastic and friendly young couple, Clément Raby from Paris and Estelle Mercier from the Gard region, have succeeded in turning heads with what they call their “cuisine libre” (“free cooking”). Served in a relaxed setting, this creative, original cuisine is spot on, with recipes that really work and just the right combination of flavours. On their “blind” menus, dishes aren’t announced until after you’ve tasted them so that guests can really give their senses and tastebuds a workout!

Name: La Vallée Verte
Description: Surrounded by glorious woodland and meadows, this magnificent estate traces its origins to a knight's manor, its 1901 castle completing a picture-perfect scene. At the helm in the kitchen is Alexander Mayer, who, along with his team, presents modern French cuisine incorporating regional produce and international accents. They serve a single set menu comprising four to six courses. One highlight comes right at the start, in the form of the amuse-bouche of exceptionally delicious calf's head accompanied by various quenelles, ranging from fresh and delicately tangy to salty, buttery and nutty. The classical basis of the dishes is reflected in the sauces in particular – the rich beurre rouge accompanying the gently cooked cod is a case in point. Service and expert wine recommendations are provided by an attentive and highly capable team. The restaurant occupies the elaborately designed ground-floor rooms of the castle, which include a stylish, airy, high-ceilinged hall, with murals lending the space an artistic edge. Lovely rooms and suites at Hotel Hohenhaus for overnight stays.

Name: La Verrière
Address: Hôtel Marinca, lieu-dit Vitricella, Olmeto, 20113, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Romain Masset signs high-flying cuisine that shines the spotlight on Corsican produce, without forgoing the odd creative flash or the obligatory mushroom foray, of which he has been a champion since his stint with Jacques and Régis Marcon. The enticingly named set menus take diners on a veritable tasting tour of delicate, savvily crafted, cherry-picked ingredients ranging from olive oil and three-cornered garlic to spider crab, common dentex and suckling lamb. The truly idyllic setting boasts a jaw-dropping view of the Gulf of Valinco and Propriano from the terrace.

Name: La VidA
Description: La VidA is part of the Susana Balbo Winemaker's House & Spa Suites, a small luxury hotel in Chacras de Coria, a small town 13 km (8 miles) from Mendoza, where everything revolves around wine. After the approach along a tree-lined track, the first thing to strike you here is the highly attentive service; you are met at the door and accompanied to the bar, where the experience begins with a welcome cocktail. In the restaurant’s contemporary-style dining room, with its glass-fronted kitchen and exposed beams which add a certain character, you find a single tasting menu designed by chef Flavia Amad Di Leo, who is also in charge of the Osadía de Crear restaurant). Through 7 courses (Terroir, Harvest, Fermentation, Extraction, Ageing, etc.), it seeks to deepen the connection between winemaking and cuisine under the Winemaker Driven concept. Presentation is paramount, with dishes paired with the most exclusive labels from Susana Balbo Wines.

Name: La Vie by Thomas Bühner
Address: 1F, Noke Mall, 200 Lequn 3rd Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: In a palette of muted greens and greys, the lofty space is a masterclass in understated elegance. La Vie is managed by German chef Bühner and a Hong Kong chef presides in the kitchen. The prix-fixe reimagines European classics using locally sourced ingredients – dishes are elaborate and visually striking. Game, such as New Zealand venison, is prepared with aplomb and finesse. Desserts such as the chocolate tart end the meal on a high note.

Name: La Vieille Auberge
Description: This pretty village with a medieval church and 18C obelisk was founded in the 13C by the Counts of Champagne; in the 19C it was restored by architect Viollet-le-Duc. It is the ideal place for experienced and talented chef Nicolas Tissier (who has previously worked with Jean-François Piège and Christian Le Squer) to take over the family business. He gives free rein to his inspiration with surprise set menus packed with premium ingredients: langoustine, monkfish, sweetbreads, chanterelles, which he makes the most of in his balanced and harmonious dishes. The cheese platter, with its 50 or so types, deserves a special mention.

Name: La Vieille Tour
Address: 75 rue de la Tour, Plérin, 22190, France
Description: The contemporary interior, which makes ample use of the light and materials , is admirably paired with the delicate, seafood menu of this country house opposite the estuary. An idyllic setting to sample deftly crafted, first-rate ingredients. Chef Nicolas Adam is not content with awakening your tastebuds, he is also the proud creator of a bakery and of the Rock’n Toques festival that takes place once a year, combining music and quality street food. The glazed wine cellar boasts some 350 references.

Name: La Villa Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: A really lovely restaurant located slightly above the town… and it's not just the interior that is elegant and stylish – the food certainly holds its own. The classic/French-based dishes are subtly polished by the chef, as he brings in regional influences; this approach works particularly well with the saddle of fallow deer, for example. The best way to experience the handiwork of the kitchen is to opt for the set menu, "Le Pin". A vegetarian set menu is also available. At midday they only offer a simple lunch menu with two or three courses. Convenient: parking in front of the establishment.

Name: La Villa de Camille et Julien
Description: Camille Tardif and Julien Lucas’ knock-out villa is a genuine ode to top-drawer Gallic ingredients. Only the best produce, like Brittany lobster and Provence asparagus, gets onto the table. Chef Lucas learnt the ropes in top French restaurants, notably with Joël Robuchon, as you will quickly taste in his high-flying repertory. His steadfast commitment to sustainable development and his love of Luxemburg produce demonstrate how in tune with his era he is. His delicate craftsmanship and flawless technique can be appreciated in dishes like hare à la royale crafted to textbook perfection: strong gamey meat in a rich sauce with a hint of chocolate and a subtle salad. Julien Lucas exalts the intense flavours of pedigree Gallic cuisine with a scattering of contemporary details, such as fruity citrus notes for added freshness and depth. For example, he may cook green asparagus in a stock of tonka beans for extra acidity, then adding slices of fermented asparagus and a foamy mousse of hop beer. The elegant, yet quirky interior, strewn with globetrotting souvenirs and flanked by a lovely cliffside terrace, is the epitome of stylish. The seasoned couple clearly knows how to pamper discerning foodies.

Name: La Villa in the Sky
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Enter the IT Tower and take the lift up to the 23rd floor, before walking up two more flights of stairs. The unique view from this glazed Villa in the Sky commands a jaw-dropping vista over Brussels! The small open kitchen enables you to admire the precision of chef Alexandre Dionisio and his well-oiled team. The food is characterised by first-class produce underpinned by playful notes and subtle side dishes. Alexandre’s high-flying culinary skill is truly in the category of consummate. He may pair a juicy breast of quail and its crispy skin with shellfish for a briny note, a gutsy poultry stock and a cavalcade of different preparations of chanterelle mushrooms for further texture and subtlety. The chef combines delicacy with creativity, juggling with exotic and pedigree Gallic influences. Nice to know: if you don’t have time for the full-blown menu at lunchtime, you can order à la carte dishes (lunchtimes only).

Name: La Zanzara
Address: Via per Volano 52, località Porticino, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In the heart of the Po Delta, a farmhouse nestled in the tranquillity of a small islet offers an experience that goes far beyond a simple culinary stop. Surrounded by enchanting lagoon landscapes, the restaurant is set in a natural setting of rare beauty, where the silence is paced by the calls of the birds that inhabit these watery lands. On the table, the cuisine pays tribute to local produce with a menu centred on fresh fish and seafood, prepared with respect and simplicity. From crispy fried dishes to fish dishes prepared according to local tradition, each course showcases the freshness of the ingredients and the connection with the surrounding environment. An authentic spot that captures the true spirit of the Delta through distinctive flavours and a timeless atmosphere.

Name: Labombe by Trivet
Address: COMO Metropolitan London, 19 Old Park Lane, Mayfair, London, W1K 1LB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the corner of the COMO Metropolitan hotel, with its own separate entrance, this wine bar and restaurant from the Trivet team is a breath of fresh air for the Mayfair dining scene, filled with chatter and the buzz of the open kitchen. It’s difficult to pigeonhole the fun and eclectic cuisine, ranging from snacks like hot tongue bun to classics like pâté en croûte and several dishes cooked over fire. Above all, it's cooking devoid of fuss and packed with flavour. The impressive global wine selection is bolstered by interactive and knowledgeable service.

Name: Labyrinth
Address: Esplanade Mall, #02-23, Marina Bay Promenade, 8 Raffles Avenue, 039802, Singapore
Description: Chef LG Han delves deep into Singapore's food culture, using his childhood memories as a starting point to reimagine the city's culinary heritage through novel techniques and from new perspectives. To echo his ethos, the dimly lit room is dotted with local art, vintage photos and kitchenware. His original tasting menu never fails to surprise, amuse and satisfy. The professional front-of-house team make the experience fun and interactive.

Name: Lady Helen
Address: The Manor House, Mount Juliet Estate, Thomastown, R95 E096, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This luxuruous, high-ceilinged restaurant sits within one of Ireland's best-preserved examples of Georgian architecture – a country house hotel, surrounded by 500 acres of grounds, that still boasts its original stuccowork and hand-carved marble fireplaces. Chef John Kelly's skilful dishes are as boldly flavoured as they are visually impressive, using top-quality ingredients from the Estate and beyond. The meal finishes with a 'Cacá Milis', a wonderfully light and sweet sponge cake inspired by Kelly's memories of a Sunday with his grandmother.

Name: Laesâ
Description: Murrhardther Hof, a culinary institution since 1920, has launched an inspired new concept. What sets it apart is that all diners are seated at a long solid-beechwood table – perfect for mingling, but with enough space for this not to be obligatory. From your seat, you can even catch a glimpse of the open kitchen, where Moritz Bilsing and Emilio Löffler run the show. Dishes are clearly and thoughtfully composed – pared down to the essentials, almost to the point of minimalism. A fine example, with harmonious flavours and delicate contrasts, is the rolled turbot fillet: moist and tender, served with a dollop of wonderfully salty fine-beaded caviar, as well as aromatic barley, sweet apricots and a mild, buttery curry sauce. The single set menu comes in four to six courses, which are punctuated by refined little extras. The experience is complemented by the expert and friendly service, with sommelier Nikolas Reidt providing excellent wine recommendations. As an alternative to wine, there are interesting house-made alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu.

Name: Lai Heen
Address: 51F, The Ritz-Carlton, Galaxy, Estrada da Baía de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re looking to impress, you can’t fail with this Cantonese restaurant atop a skyscraping hotel. The stunningly ornate room is supremely comfortable, as are the private rooms that can be joined into one big one.
