FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The dimly lit space in a century-old building on the Bund feels mysterious and theatrical. The vibe is matched by a season-driven menu divided into acts, like a play. Neo-Chinese creations are finessed by European techniques, and presented in whimsical and ceremonious ways. For a fine dining take on the classic beef in oyster sauce, beef from Shandong is marinated then deep-fried and grilled. Creative wine pairing options add to the fun.

Name: Lingnan House
Address: 5F, Rosewood Hotel, 6 Zhujiang East Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Latticed windows, ceiling fans and chandeliers set the retro Lingnan scene. Chef Feng delves into Lingnan traditions and seasonal local produce, tweaked to the local palate and spruced up with his unique creative flair. His Shunde minced fish soup perfumed with makrut lime leaves tends to sell out fast. An array of dim sum made à la minute are available at lunch, but the popular abalone puff pastry is only on the menu at dinnertime.

Name: Lita
Address: 7-9 Paddington Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 5QH, United Kingdom
Description: Cooking with fire is all the rage these days and Lita is an expert practitioner, although it also offers so much more. While there’s a strong Mediterranean and southern European element to the menu, prime British ingredients – such as Scottish lobster and Cornish turbot – along with big, bold flavours and well-made sauces really make the dishes sing. Many of the plates are designed for sharing, like dry-aged Devon duck with beetroot and kumquat. This is roll-up-your-sleeves sort of food – the type that leaves you licking your lips and planning your return.

Name: Little Pearl
Address: 921 Pennsylvania Ave. SE, Washington, DC, 20003, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Just down the street from Rose’s Luxury and Pineapple and Pearls, this intimate boîte is yet another feather in the same restaurant group’s proverbial cap. Possessing all the charm of a carriage house, the dining room is closer to a sun room encased in glass with expansive views of the green surroundings. This is cooking that is prepared with panache while leaning on the seasons (think butter-poached oysters with fried potatoes and seaweed remoulade or strawberry shortcake with basil). The menu is a revolving door of ideas, except for the signature angel egg amuse-bouche. An eclectic wine list makes for a thoughtful pairing. In total, dinner here goes for less than other tasting menus in town, but with no less boldness, care and creativity.

Name: Liu Yuan Pavilion
Address: 3F, The Broadway, 54-62 Lockhart Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: At this spot serving authentic Shanghainese cooking to a Shanghainese-speaking clientele, it's tempting to think you're in Shanghai. The menu covers all bases, from home-style favourites (sautéed river shrimps; eight treasures in chilli sauce) to painstaking recipes such as stir fried shredded mandarin fish. The dim sum, e.g. xiao long bao, and pan-fried pork buns are also well made. In season, dishes made with hairy crab meat and roe are unmissable.

Name: Llavor
Address: Plaza Islas Baleares 1, Oropesa del Mar, 12594, Spain
Description: Llavor takes its name from a Valencian term that could be translated as “seed”. This restaurant, located in the upper section of the Oropesa residential district is without doubt a real find for foodies. This modern eatery, boasting a large terrace and stunning views of the Mediterranean and neighbouring towns and villages, is run by Jorge Lengua and Adrián Peralta, two young chefs from the region. The dining experience, which takes the form of two tasting menus (Flores de Colores and Nubes de Mariposas), usually begins with superb appetisers on the terrace and is defined by its creativity. Dishes here are always elegantly presented, with the aim of showcasing the flavours of the region and painstaking research into the vegetables, fish and seafood and meat sourced from the sea and mountains in Castellón province. A signature dish here is the grilled squid with pork jowl and Caseta d'Espadà cheese. The restaurant’s decorative features are also in keeping with the theme of its different menus!

Name: Lluerna
Address: Avenida Pallaresa 104, Santa Coloma de Gramenet, 08921, Spain
Description: The best aspect of this kind of family-run restaurant is the unhurried and stress-free approach which is very much in keeping with the principles of the Slow Food movement. The focus of the married couple that run and own Lluerna, Víctor Quintillà (in the kitchen) and Mar Gómez (front of house), is on sustainable cuisine that champions locally sourced ingredients (chicken from the Penedés area, Duroc pigs, Xisqueta lambs, pigeon from the Tatjé family etc). These are showcased via a modern take on Catalan recipes that uses skilled techniques to enhance their delicate textures and maximise each and every flavour. In the kitchen, visible from both the dining room and the chef’s table, the team creates cuisine that is exclusively focused on several set menus served to the whole table: Degustació (lunchtime midweek only), Vegetal, Presentació and Lluerna. The provenance of ingredients (organic where possible) for each dish is usually explained to guests when served.

Name: LoRo
Description: Imaginative, light, and genuinely healthy: that's the cuisine at LoRo. Sea flavors dominate, especially in the appetizers and first courses, creatively and enticingly titled on the menu. Chef Pierantonio Rocchetti often starts with classic Italian traditions, reinterpreting them with flair and originality. Portions are generous, and the flavors are intense, culminating in desserts that provide moments of delightful indulgence.

Name: Loaf On
Address: 49 See Cheung Street, Sai Kung, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Live fish tanks at the entrance may not set this restaurant apart from its promenade rivals, but its food certainly does. Wonderfully fresh seafood is prepared using traditional home recipes that allow the high-quality ingredients to shout their name. Steamed zebra mantis shrimp on egg white custard boasts bouncy, umami-laden meat. The mantis shrimp in chilli and garlic and steamed fish in sea salt are equally good. When booking, ask about the seafood that needs pre-ordering.

Name: Loca Niru
Address: House of Tan Yeok Nee, #02-01, 101 Penang Road, 238466, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: In this restaurant in a restored heritage building, original vintage architectural features meet subtle wabi-sabi touches to great effect. The single tasting menu, which reflects the chef's Japanese background, demonstrates precision and meticulous layering of flavours. His balanced abalone chawanmushi is testament to a deft control of heat. Served tableside, the pan-fried isaki fish in Nyonya beurre blanc is prepared with aplomb.

Name: Local
Address: Salizzada dei Greci, sestiere Castello 3303, Venice, 30122, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Modern and minimalist, with an open kitchen, Local is one of the best and most exciting restaurants in Venice, the result of the synergy between the extremely friendly owner, who works front of house, and talented chef, Salvatore Sodano. With a 7 or 9-course tasting menu, it is an experience not to be missed! Extraordinary wine cellar with almost a thousand labels, most of them Italian.

Name: Localis
Description: Together with his tight-knit team, Chef/owner Christopher Barnum-Dann brings unusual warmth to this intimate setting. His enthusiasm is instantly palpable as he happily explains his inspiration behind particular dishes and even solicits feedback. This is especially true for diners who sit at the spacious counter.The freewheeling tasting menu is thoroughly Californian in its commitment to carefully sourced ingredients, while also drawing upon global cuisines, reimagining flavors from the chef's travels with impressive imagination. Whimsy is a common thread throughout, as in a puffed pillow of crisp potato filled with "Fancy French Onion Dip" and caviar, or "The Dish That Made Us," a single woodfire-roasted octopus tentacle with black peppercorn sauce and pickled cherries.

Name: Locanda Barbarossa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An address at the pinnacle of Ticino’s fine dining, situated within the Castello del Sole hotel (in a tranquil and secluded location): gourmets and refined food lovers – this is your restaurant! With seasonal ingredients – many sourced from the estate itself – the cuisine of Mattias Roock and Leopold Ott offers a successful blend of local inspirations and Mediterranean touches, while fundamentally remaining rooted in the classics, whether you opt for à la carte or one of the two tempting tasting menus. The inspectors’ notes also emphasize the peacefulness of the setting (it is particularly enjoyable to sit out on the lovely terrace, when the weather allows) and the extensive wine selection curated by sommelier Sergio Bassi. Excellent service.

Name: Locanda Don Serafino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Along the road that encircles Ibla (one of the most evocative and picturesque historic centres in Sicily), the restaurant welcomes guests into a spectacular dining room that appears carved from the rock. The space, however, eschews all rusticity in favour of a refined elegance, accompanied by service of a high order: an ideal setting for a romantic and gastronomic evening. Vincenzo Candiano confirms himself as a chef of great talent, engaged in a continual exploration that places dishes now considered classics, which are indispensable fixtures on the menu, alongside more innovative creations, often inspired by the island. The welcome is very pleasant, with a small garden of aromatic herbs – wild fennel, mint, rosemary and other essences – whose fragrances provide a fitting prelude to the gastronomic experience. The cellar is also impressive, now numbering some 2,880 labels.

Name: Locanda Mammì
Description: In an evocative rural setting, among stone farmhouses, absolute tranquillity and a summer terrace that opens onto the surrounding hills, chef Stefania Di Pasquo presents an authentic cuisine, firmly rooted in the produce of her land and enhanced by a personal and unaffected touch. The variation of lamb is impeccable: a freshly cooked cutlet, a slow-braised preparation with onions, and alongside it a richly flavoured liver stew, together composing a coherent narrative of technique and memory. Equally remarkable is the dessert inspired by the traditional peasant breakfast, in which caramelised bread meets a surprising caciocavallo ice cream – a fitting homage to Agnone, not without reason known as the ‘city of cheese’ – finished with a delicate wine sauce. In the dining room, the chef’s husband, Tomas Torsiello, receives guests with grace and quiet assurance in a warm and romantic setting enriched by a fireplace and copper details. His is also the stewardship of the wine list, which reveals a marked predilection for Champagnes. The property also offers pleasant guest rooms, ideal for those wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Locanda Margon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: With spectacular views over Trento and the Adige Valley, the restaurant invites you to discover the cuisine of Edoardo Fumagalli, a chef who skilfully combines technique, creativity and a contemporary sensitivity. The experience is structured around three tasting itineraries, the most notable of which is ‘Passione Bollicine’, designed to showcase Ferrari’s iconic Trentodoc wines through carefully selected pairings. The region’s produce plays a central role, particularly on the menu dedicated to Trentino, but it also features in dishes that draw inspiration from ingredients and culinary traditions from other Italian regions. For those who prefer greater freedom of choice, there is also a small menu featuring some of the most representative dishes from the tasting menus. Next to the restaurant, the Bistrot offers a more informal alternative, serving authentic Italian cuisine and providing the pleasant option of dining al fresco.

Name: Locanda Orico
Description: A focus on sustainability is much more than a simple slogan at this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the old town. Since 1998 here, the owner-chef works with excellent local suppliers in order to provide the best possible experience for his guests, talking them through each dish and the provenance of its top-quality ingredients. There’s nothing mysterious about the process, which results in healthy Mediterranean cuisine with a combination of French and regional influences, and where the menu changes at the beginning of each season and the tasting menu every month. Dishes here are carefully presented, with meticulous attention to detail and a perfect combination of colours. An interesting selection of renowned wines adds to its appeal, including an excellent choice of local and international labels. A simpler business menu is available at lunchtime, when dishes are announced at your table. A stronghold of fine Ticino cuisine! The restaurant has recently installed a recharging point for electric cars.

Name: Locanda San Lorenzo
Address: Via IV Novembre 79, Puos d'Alpago, 32016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: For over a century, the history of this establishment has been intertwined with that of the Dal Farra family. It all began in 1900 with an inn set up to welcome and feed the workers from the nearby mill; in the 1950s, the business passed to the second generation, eventually coming to Renzo Dal Farra, now the chef-owner, who earned a Michelin star in 1997. In a modern and welcoming setting, the restaurant showcases the produce of the region through two tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, as well as an à la carte menu. Trout, game, mushrooms, pulses, cereals, cheeses and Alpago lamb are among the ingredients that best reflect the identity of these mountains. Rounding off the experience is a remarkably extensive wine cellar, which boasts a particularly rich selection of Piedmontese wines, while also extending well beyond the region’s borders.

Name: Locanda de Banchieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Chef Giacomo Devoto from Sarzana has transformed an old 17th-century farmhouse, surrounded by greenery, into a charming inn complete with rooms and a working farm, where tranquillity and hospitality reign. On the bright panoramic veranda, where the gaze reaches as far as the coast and the sea, guests can savour his creations devoted to the most authentic flavours of Lunigiana. The recipes, imaginative yet firmly rooted in the seasons, rest on the fragrance of the ingredients: vegetables – like the extra virgin olive oil – come largely from his extensive kitchen garden, while proteins are selected both from the inland area and from the sea very close by. It is precisely the variety of his garden that also allows him to offer Flora, an entirely green menu that brings together a full range of seasonal vegetables, interpreted with a delicate hand and a deep knowledge of the ingredients. The wine selection carefully accompanies this cuisine rooted in the territory: interesting labels ranging across Italy and France, choosing small producers and established names with the same attention that characterises every detail of the house.

Name: Locanda del Pilone
Address: Frazione Madonna di Como 34, Alba, 12051, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a few kilometres from the town, yet already surrounded by the charm of the surrounding hills, the restaurant enjoys a privileged location from which the view takes in some of the most picturesque vineyard landscapes in the area. Neat rows of vines frame the landscape in each direction, offering particularly spectacular views during the autumn. In its elegant, classically styled dining rooms, the kitchen thoughtfully interprets the time of year and traditions, bringing them to life through a solid and measured approach. A variety of tasting menus, which are flexible and can be tailored to your preferences, including à la carte options, allow you to create a tailored culinary experience. The wine list is also worth noting, with a particularly interesting selection of Champagne. Finally, in the warmer months, the bistro on the stunning terrace allows you to enjoy the experience in an even more relaxed setting with panoramic views.

Name: Loch Bay
Address: 1-2 Macleods Terrace, Stein, Waternish, Isle of Skye, IV55 8GA, United Kingdom
Description: This pretty crofter’s cottage sits in an idyllic spot on the Waternish Peninsula and offers commanding views across the countryside to the mountains. It’s a pleasingly simple place with a wood-burning stove, Harris Tweed-covered chairs and a snug, intimate feel. The skilfully prepared, intensely flavoured dishes have French undertones but a Scottish heart, with Skye's cold, pure waters providing plenty of seafood. The signature langoustine 'pot au feu' is a prime example, using shellfish landed on the jetty opposite the restaurant.

Name: Loco
Address: Rua dos Navegantes 53 B, Lisbon, 1200-731, Portugal
Description: At this restaurant, just a stone’s throw from the 18th-century Baroque Basílica da Estrela, they say they work with micro-seasons to maximise flavour and fulfil their zero-waste policy. Loco brims with surprises from the moment you step through the door, starting with its eye-catching, fully open kitchen and amplified by extensive design details that reflect the house’s creativity and character. Chef Alexandre Silva concentrates his entire culinary philosophy into a single surprise tasting menu of 16 “moments” or steps, inspired by Portuguese tradition yet in constant evolution and viewed through a contemporary lens. A recommendation? Don’t miss the drinks list, which offers not only superb organic wines from small producers but also a variety of craft beers, herbal liqueurs and house-fermented natural juices, most of them made on site.

Name: Locust
Description: Reservations here are scarce — and for good reason. Laidback, quirky and full of charm, Chef Trevor Moran's compact, Japanese-influenced hotspot is a beehive of energy. There’s a simple elegance and a clear attention to detail in every dish, all designed for sharing. Beef tartare hand rolls, a house classic, always delight. From there, explore seafood like Maine diver scallops with shaved green apple. A Japanese omelet with Jonah crab is simple but spot on. Don't skip dessert. The ever-changing iterations of their kakigori may present a sculpted block of the finest, powdery shaved ice dressed, decorated and flavored with everything from passion fruit cream to caramelized honeycomb to raspberry.

Name: Logan Brown
Address: 192 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: Housed in the former National Bank of New Zealand, circa 1920s, Logan Brown welcomes diners into an imposing room complete with a dome ceiling, Corinthian columns and ornate arches. The architectural grandeur is matched by contemporary dishes that boast meticulous detail and nuanced flavours. The signature ravioli filled with pāua abalone in lime beurre blanc and topped with fried kūmara sweet potato shreds reveals distinct layers of flavours.

Name: Logis de la Cadène
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of the town, this logis dating back to 1848 is one of Saint Émilion’s oldest restaurants. Picture plush, cosy dining rooms done up in the same elegant vein as the guestrooms available for overnight stays. The chef Thibaut Gamba crafts delicate, subtle dishes that showcase local produce as much as possible. Some of the fruit and vegetables come from the estate’s farm, as does the honey. Splendid wine cellar, with a knockout selection of Bordeaux reds, ideal when sampled with the establishment’s superlative range of cheeses.

Name: Lohninger
Address: Schweizer Straße 1, Frankfurt on the Main, 60594, Germany
Description: Set on the banks of the River Main in Frankfurt, this restaurant tastefully blends the classic flair of the old building in which it is housed – beautiful high stucco ceilings, herringbone floorboards – with modern minimalist design. The cuisine draws on the Lohninger family's Austrian roots as well as Asian and Mediterranean influences, and the menu has been divided into two sections accordingly: "Die Heimat" (homeland) and "Die Welt" (the world). The dishes stand out for their finesse, intense flavours and the quality of the ingredients; chef-patron Mario Lohninger and his kitchen team are careful to avoid gimmickry and place the emphasis on flavour. This holds for both classics and signature dishes such as Carinthian Schlutzkrapfen (high-Alpine cheese ravioli), Imperial and Royal ox cheek goulash, or Spencer Gulf kingfish sashimi with foie gras, pickled vegetables and a buttermilk and horseradish dressing. The front-of-house team is friendly, attentive and pleasingly relaxed and down-to-earth – anything but stuffy.

Name: Loiseau des Ducs
Description: Housed in the 16C Hôtel de Talmay, a listed historical monument close to the Palais des Ducs, this restaurant is part of the Loiseau Group. Chef Iulian Fistos, former right-hand man to Patrick Bertron in Saulieu, channels his talent into upholding the gastronomical spirit of Burgundy and Bernard Loiseau's classics, with a distinctly contemporary approach: Dijon snails in parsley sauce, garlic purée, celery tempura and watercress soup; Charolais beef fillet, carrot ravioli and beef bone marrow, hay jus. There is a fine selection of wines by the glass and a good-value lunch menu.

Name: Long Trieu
Address: 4F, The Reverie Saigon, Times Square Building, 22-36 Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in one of the city’s luxury hotels, Long Trieu’s lavish dining room boasts jade stonework, traditional gold-leaf painted Chinese scenes and ornate seating. The menu offers a wide selection of à la carte and set dishes that pay tribute to Cantonese culinary heritage, while cleverly incorporating local Vietnamese ingredients into traditional Cantonese techniques. Highlights include the fried prawns with XO sauce and the hot and sour wonton soup.

Name: Longjing Manor
Address: 399 Longjing Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, this restaurant in a Chinese garden with stone bridges and ponds only offers eight private rooms. The chef crafts nostalgic, poetically named Jiangnan dishes and shines the spotlight on local Zhejiang favourites. As a starter, diners are served freshly made sweet or savoury soymilk, flanked by a lineup of sides. The signature double-boiled duck soup with cordyceps chanhua is tasty and nourishing.

Name: Lore Ttipia - Auberge Ostape
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A sprawling country estate on the heights of Bidarray and Itxassou is home to a 17C farmstead and outhouses. A panoramic terrace commands a jaw-dropping view over grandiose rolling countryside. Chef John Argaud, who trained with the best in the Basque Country (the Ibarboure brothers in Ithurria), as well as at Le Meurice Alain Ducasse in Paris, shines the spotlight on outstanding local produce. The food is crisp, legible and dotted with creativity; some ingredients are cooked over embers or finished on a hot stone for an added distinctive edge. An example: morels stuffed with sweetbread and duck hearts. From Monday to Wednesday, the repertory is more bistronomic and simpler, but just as appetising as that available later in the week.

Name: Lorelei
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether or not the weather encourages you to spend time outdoors, it’s worth treating yourself to an aperitif on the terrace overlooking the Gulf, from where you can admire sunsets of rare beauty. As evening falls, the spotlight turns to Ciro Sicignano, a chef originally from Gragnano and a masterful interpreter of the Campania culinary tradition. His cuisine reinterprets local produce and recipes with technical skill, personality and imagination, finding expression in dishes such as Gragnano spaghetti with clams, baby squid with citrus and caponata coulis, or sole with courgettes, flowers and shoots, accompanied by a delicate cream made from Sorrento lemons. This concept, which is closely linked to the world of plants, is further enhanced by the two vegetable gardens at the chef’s disposal, a carefully curated selection of oils, and the elegant setting of Lorelei Londres, overlooking the sea at Sorrento.

Name: Lorenz Adlon Esszimmer
Description: As you enter the exclusive Hotel Adlon Kempinski, the lobby sets the tone for the refined feel of the restaurant on the first floor. With a touch of good fortune, you will get a table with a view of the Brandenburg Gate. The elegant, classically opulent interior meets its match in the sophisticated cuisine of Jonas Zörner, who clinched his first MICHELIN star at GOLVET. His modern, creative style of cooking contrasts beautifully with the Adlon's historic heritage, yet still preserves a classic French foundation. Excellent ingredient quality, beautifully highlighted flavours and depth of taste go hand in hand. The front-of-house team led by maître d' Oliver Kraft and head sommelier Hans-Martin Konrad – two consummate professionals – is simply outstanding. Charming, eloquent and attentive, they guide guests through the evening with the utmost professionalism. In addition to a five- or six-course set menu, Signatures are also available – à la carte or as a set menu. The superb international wine list features over 1,600 labels.

Name: Lorenzo
Address: Via Carducci 61, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
Description: A historic restaurant in Forte, Da Lorenzo has welcomed many famous personalities who have enlivened the Versilia seasons. In the well-kept succession of three rooms, you can feel the love for classic and timeless dining. The menu reflects this, featuring essential dishes that attract a global clientele season after season. The tradition of preparing mayonnaise tableside is a highlight, along with offerings such as the grand raw seafood platter, seafood bavette, Versilia-style spaghetti, and some meat dishes. A vast wine selection, detailed in two elegant bound volumes, showcases depth and exploration, featuring both Italian and international labels, including classics and contemporary discoveries. For the daring, there are even bottles from remote regions of the world.

Name: Los Danzantes Oaxaca
Address: Macedonio Alcalá 403, Interior 4, Colonia Centro, Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: This Oaxaca favorite can count 25 years of history to its name, but that’s not stopping them from forging ahead with their own ideas and sense of refinement. Set in a dazzling, open-air courtyard, the space buzzes as personable servers guide locals and visitors alike. Start with a terrine of vegetables dressed with avocado puree, featuring product from the operation's organic garden north of the city, before moving to the mole sampler, which is a masterclass in sauce work. Salsa borracha is another can’t-miss sauce that shines with tender pork ribs. The tortilla and cafe dessert is a clever play on a traditional local breakfast snack. The restaurant even makes its own mezcal, which is used in their finely made cocktails.

Name: Los Félix
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Heritage corn sourced from across the Americas and seafood fetched from nearby waters are foundational pillars for this youthful restaurant in Coconut Grove. Such sustainability is a point of pride for Chef Sebastian Vargas, who offers a finely poised expression of Mexican cuisine that leans on subtle flavors and top-notch ingredients. Anyone can throw together a fish taco, but few are willing to source grouper from Key West, grill it in a banana leaf, and pair it with a deceptively addicting hazelnut emulsion. Another recent highlight featured a superb griddled corn cake paired with crab, smoked corn sauce, and charred plantains. The intimate setting attracts a handsome crowd with natural fibers, sleek wood, and a high-energy playlist.

Name: Los Guayres
Address: Avenida de los Marrero 2, Mogán, 35138, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Having travelled through the arid landscapes of the Mogán valley, this restaurant appears as an elegant and exotic oasis as if by magic. Los Guayres, a Guanche term that could be translated as ‘The Lords’, is located inside the Cordial Mogán Playa hotel, very close to Puerto de Mogán. Chef Ruyman González spearheads cuisine that celebrates the culinary heritage of the Canary Islands through carefully prepared dishes, contemporary nuances and a deep respect for local ingredients, represented by produce from the islands (gofio, goat, red prickly pear) and the rich Atlantic larder (wreckfish, bluefin tuna, sea bream). They offer three set menus (Degustación, Degustación Clásico and Gran Menú Degustación) each featuring dishes that are big on flavour, such as the scarlet shrimp, vinagre macho and salpicón or their Cherne, pilpil, sancocho and watercress. Looking for a recommendation? If you can, get a table on the terrace – a typical Canary Island-style balcony overlooking the beautiful hotel gardens.

Name: Louise
Address: PMQ, 35 Aberdeen Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Chef Julien Royer, of Odette in Singapore fame, opened this restaurant which sports a 1930s colonial style decor. Start with a drink at the bar downstairs before heading to the dining room for the chef’s delicate creations crafted with quality produce. Served with rice cooked in chicken fat and green salad, the juicy, velvety roasted Hong Kong yellow chicken dish is great for sharing. Ask the sommelier about wine pairings.

Name: Louise
Description: Louise was chef Julien Corderoch's great-grandmother, and it was she who sparked his love of food and, indeed, his culinary vocation. In a warm, contemporary interior, he proposes surprise menus made up of tasty seafood and plant-based dishes, making good use of sustainably caught fish (line and small-boat fishing) and drawing on his knowledge of the maturing process: gilthead sea bream sashimi, wild herb pesto and wild carrot; raw scallops, warm broth of brown shrimp with coriander and ponzu sauce; gently steamed pollack, creamy cauliflower and shiitake roasted in miso butter. The lunchtime menu is a genuine bargain. Reasonably priced wines.

Name: Loumi
Description: Karl-Louis Kömmler, an ambitious chef who also happens to be self-taught, is at work in this small restaurant in Kreuzberg. He has the support of a motivated young team, who clearly enjoy being part of the pared-back modern dining concept here. The food breaks with culinary conventions – based on the classics, it is strongly influenced by Japanese cuisine – and when it comes to the quality of the ingredients, no compromises are made. The menu comprises eight courses, in addition to specials that can be added on as an upgrade. In the veal sweetbread, they have a true signature dish: finely seasoned, crispy on the outside and creamy-tender on the inside, it is served with N25 Kaluga caviar and habanero sauce, which give the dish a pleasing kick with their brininess and wonderful heat – all in perfect harmony. It is powerful, pared down and original. The wine list may be on the short side, but it features a good selection. The front-of-house team is charming and knowledgeable, and the chefs themselves serve and explain the dishes. The minimalist interior is inviting. Some seats are located at the counter, from which there is a view of the open kitchen. There is a small covered terrace in front of this corner building.

Name: Louroc - Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc
Address: Boulevard J.-F.-Kennedy, au Cap d'Antibes, Antibes, 06160, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of this mythical luxury hotel ticks all the boxes. It combines attentive service, tableware produced for the most part by Provençal artisans, a breathtaking view of the Mediterranean, and the talents of chef Sébastien Broda. The pantry abounds with vegetables sourced exclusively from local market gardeners, as well as fish from small-scale fisheries and bespoke meats. This Mediterranean cuisine is exemplified by coherent dishes.

Name: Lu Style (Anding Road)
Address: 5F, Uni Elite, Building 6, Courtyard 5, Anding Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Instead of typical Shandong classics, the chef, who hails from the province, champions a menu starring seafood that is shipped from Weihai port daily. The crisp and tangy Laizhou Bay "penis fish" salad on a bed of ice plant tantalises the taste buds. The donkey soup with Solomon's seal and black garlic, slow cooked for over 10 hours, delivers meaty sweetness and a gelatinous texture from the donkey hide, in a space that exudes traditional elegance.

Name: Lu Style (Huangpu)
Address: Room 207, 2F, Uni Elite, Lane 838, South Huangpi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: With its own herb garden, and the latest catch shipped daily from Weihai and Bohai Sea, this eatery promises food that is as fresh as it gets. Well-versed in the properties of all his produce, the chef fine-tunes his recipes according to the season. The Jiaodong cold appetiser platter includes four kinds of seafood with different seasonings. The braised sea cucumber with scallion and huitlacoche presents deeply aromatic layers of briny-sweet flavours.

Name: Luca
Address: 88 St John Street, Clerkenwell, London, EC1M 4EH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There’s something about Luca that makes it feel like a proper grown-up restaurant, largely because the relaxed clientele just know they’re going to be well looked after. What brings them all here is the expertly rendered Italian food, which is satisfyingly robust yet effortlessly easy to eat. The pasta course will certainly be a highlight – whether that’s cappelletti of salt-baked potato or tortelli of pumpkin with ricotta – but the other dishes, featuring such quality ingredients as Orkney scallops or Hereford beef, won’t ever disappoint. For great value, choose the Express Lunch menu served in the bar.

Name: Luca's by Paulo Airaudo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of artistic and monumental Florence, on the first floor of Hotel La Gemma, a small L-shaped dining room of contemporary and elegant taste is concealed, distinguished by an original green boiserie and enriched by carefully considered details. The kitchen favours an essential and creative approach: each dish in the tasting menu (minimum four courses) is built from a small number of elements, worked with precision to express personal and distinctive ideas. The dessert is emblematic, a goat’s milk flan crowned with a thin caramel crust of strawberry, delicately finished with measured drops of aged balsamic vinegar.

Name: Lucas Carton
Address: 9 place de la Madeleine, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Venturing over the threshold of this iconic historic establishment adorned with its famous carved woodwork by Majorelle is always a treat. The chef strives to replicate the house’s Art nouveau decor in his recipes. He rolls out a creative score with a veggie focus, each dish of which is defined by an aromatic, spicy or acidic theme. Crisp, frank, forthright flavours that hit the spot every time.

Name: Lucide
Description: This place ticks all the boxes! In a central location right by Lake Lucerne, on the first floor of the Culture and Congress Centre, it commands fantastic views of the lake and the city. It boasts a stylish and chic interior. Furthermore, the large, friendly team provides proficient service. And then there's the food: By enlisting Maximilian Huber, previously chef at Munich's mural farmhouse, they have brought in a master at elevating regional cuisine with delicate precision. Proximity to producers and the quality of the ingredients play an important role. The precise technique and balance of flavours are just as impressive – from striking contrasts, as in "carrot, kimchi, sea buckthorn, buckwheat", to delicate and full-bodied combinations, as in "Brüggli salmon trout, mountain meadow hay, fennel, elderflower". In the evening, there is a choice of two three- to six-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. At lunchtime, an inexpensive set menu and a small à la carte selection are available. Another highlight is the "Konzert-Menü", served here at the Lucerne Culture and Congress Centre before performances.

Name: Lucien
Address: 7863 Girard Ave., Ste. 308, La Jolla, CA, 92037, USA
Description: Chef Elijah Arizmendi cut his teeth in New York kitchens before returning home to open this sophisticated tasting menu concept on the third story of La Plaza La Jolla. Whether it's California-raised Iberico pork or locally caught fish, the region's bounty is celebrated on a menu that reflects French and Japanese influences. A meal could begin with canapes like tempura-fried sweet potato topped with caviar; yellowtail in a crispy nori tube; and a rose meringue with beets and green yogurt, before moving into impressive dishes like crisp-skinned ocean tilefish with petite fennel and pomegranate, or poussin with a chicken mousse and truffle stuffing. Desserts are creative, as in the cinnamon caramel-braised pineapple roasted over the live-fire hearth for hours.

Name: Lueurs
Description: Le Petit Serrant, an 18C manor house located at the confluence of the River Maine and River Loire, is the elegant setting for this restaurant, where diners come as much for the cuisine as for the charm of the location. Romain Zarazaga, a chef trained by Laurent Petit, Emmanuel Renaut and the Troisgros, serves a wonderful array of dishes that are perfectly in tune with the times. His masterful jus and sauces are another standout feature of his cooking – for example, line-caught sea bass confit accompanied by a butter-based fish stock with Domaine Mosse vermouth. The charcoal-grilled squab with a condiment of offal and a reduced elderflower syrup sauce – deep, flavourful and with a remarkable texture – is another culinary masterclass.

Name: Luisl Stube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Schlosswirt Forst is a charming 16th-century residence housing a traditional restaurant, some rooms, and most notably, the Luisl Stube: a small gem set among beautiful antique woods and traditional chandeliers of a historic stube. With more candles than tables (only 4), it offers a truly intimate and timelessly romantic atmosphere. The culinary approach is contemporary, thanks to chef Luis Haller, who explores local products while also incorporating some exotic or seafood ingredients. He offers two tasting menus – one vegetarian and the other with animal proteins – that can be mixed as if they were one menu. Talented sommelier Nicola Spimpolo enhances the experience with uniquely intriguing wine pairings, exploring older vintages to evoke memorable enological emotions.

Name: Lukas Kapeller
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This place describes itself as "small, refined, modern", which goes both for the five tasteful guestrooms and the restaurant on the 2nd floor, where a smart modern interior meets with a distinct sense of intimacy. Guests soak up the cosy atmosphere with a personal touch, while in the open kitchen a seven-course set menu is prepared by a team headed up by owners Lukas Kapeller and Michael Schlöglhofer. Dishes such as king oyster mushrooms with celery, tarragon and nut butter or grilled pikeperch with peas, radishes and horseradish steer clear of unnecessary frills and put the focus on regional ingredients. In such a beautiful location on a small hill surrounded by greenery, it is hard to believe you're in the centre of Steyr.

Name: Lukas Restaurant
Description: "France, Japan, Innviertel" sums up the culinary concept here. In the open kitchen, Lukas Kienbauer and his team create a surprise menu whose structure is inspired by the kaiseki tradition. The quality of the ingredients is excellent and the craftsmanship precise. The full menu comprises 12 "moments", with a shorter version also available. Japanese A5 Wagyu can be added on or substituted for another course. There is an excellent selection of wines, to be perused on a tablet, and interesting wine or alcohol-free pairings accompany the set menu. Service is charming and attentive. The tasteful setting is a distinctive combination of old vaulting and modern design. Tip: Combine your culinary experience with a walk along the Inn, which is just a short walk from the Baroque Old Town.

Name: LuluRouget
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Trained by Michel Troisgros, local lad Ludovic Pouzelgues has made his trendy eatery, a stone's throw from the famous Machines de l'Île, a prominent landmark of the city’s dining scene. The produce of La Turballe and Croisic fish auctions is crafted delicately and inventively. Side by side surprise menus, the “Timeless” lineup stars the house’s tried and tested iconic signatures. The result is bang-on confident cuisine steeped in spot-on precision and ever keen to astound!

Name: Lumière
Address: Clarence Parade, Cheltenham, GL50 3PA, United Kingdom
Description: In the centre of this charming spa town you’ll find an unassuming exterior concealing an elegantly stylish restaurant. Helen runs the service and she’s a natural host, so you’ll be warmly welcomed and well looked after. Her experienced husband Jon runs things in the kitchen and his overtly seasonal cooking demonstrates impressive classical technique and attention to detail, exemplified by the expertly cooked venison with a rich red wine sauce. His more playful side comes out in the crowd-pleasing signature 'Tequila Slammer' sorbet.

Name: Lunario
Address: Camino Vecinal Parcela 71 Fracc. 3 Lote 13, San Marcos, El Porvenir, 22750, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Open seasonally and set on the grounds of Lomita winery, Lunario is tucked inside a greenhouse-like building. It's a stunning first impression to walk along the winding path to discover this chic, modern space where an open kitchen draws attention and a few counter seats are available for those who enjoy a front-row seat. Chef Sheyla Alvarado presides over two multicourse tasting menus with a seasonal, contemporary and vegetable-forward focus, and many ingredients are sourced from their own farm. Her cooking is creative and bold, evidenced by dishes like the duo of Baja oysters juxtaposing sweet and spicy and the blue corn sope with a brilliant blend of carrot purée, smoked shrimp, and bright bougainvillea. Flan in chamomile vinegar with honey ice cream is an unexpected triumph.

Name: Lunasia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: One of the most imaginative and original chefs in Versilia, offering a showcase restaurant inside the luxurious Plaza e de Russie hotel. In a modern and bright dining room overlooking the famous Viareggio promenade, Luca Landi's menu features three tasting options: one dedicated to fish, another combining seafood and vegetables, and a third focused on meats, with the possibility to mix and match dishes à la carte. The courses are elegantly crafted, showcasing creativity that is substantial and not just for show, with presentations that truly impress. Supported by excellent ingredients, the chef honors the region, using local seafood and inland products, sourcing as much as possible from trusted small producers, and maintaining a focus on circular cooking to reduce waste. The wine list is a journey through around 800 labels, with a special emphasis on Piedmont, Tuscany, and Burgundy; prices are accessible, and the by-the-glass selection is notably unique.

Name: Lutum
Address: Markt 15, Wijk bij Duurstede, 3961 BC, Netherlands
Description: With a slogan like Volg de natuur ("Follow nature") and a name that refers to the fertile, clay-rich soil of the area, it is immediately clear that terroir is a key focus at Lutum. This vision is carried through into every aspect of the restaurant. The decor has a natural Zen feel, with an abundance of decorative features reminiscent of trees. The menu showcases the freshest ingredients sourced directly from local gardens and food forests. The surprise menu, designed to minimise waste, highlights local produce and adds an international twist with ingredients such as koji and miso. This cuisine is vibrant and exciting. They infuse a variety of pak choi creations, such as a leaf coulis and a stem slushy, with the subtle spiciness of tandoori and the floral complexity of different blooms. The chefs meticulously craft their dishes and regularly amaze diners with their sauces – the depth of flavour of the red wine and cardamom-based sauce they serve with venison is a case in point. The food at Lutum packs a punch!

Name: Lux Lucis
Address: Viale A. Morin 67, Forte dei Marmi, 55042, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Inside the Hotel Principe in Forte dei Marmi, a lift leads up to the elegant rooftop: on clear days, the terrace offers a splendid view of the coastline and is the ideal spot for an aperitif at sunset. From here, you enter the dining room, which opens onto the open-plan kitchen, where the chef, originally from the hills around Modena, brings his menu to life. His cuisine is elegant and contemporary, underpinned by technical precision and creative flair, and is well represented by dishes such as glazed red mullet with citrus fruits, almonds and olives, cacciucco-style clams, mallard duck in a marinara sauce, and a mousse made with caramelised bread, chocolate and Vin Santo. The experience is rounded off by an original wine list, organised by grape variety, presented with expertise and discretion by the head waiter and sommelier, Sokol Ndreko, who has been working alongside the chef since the restaurant first opened: his ability to guide guests in their choices plays a key role in the quality of the hospitality.

Name: Lympstone Manor
Address: Courtlands Lane, Lympstone, EX8 3NZ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Local chef Michael Caines is behind this tastefully restored Grade II listed Georgian house, which sits in peaceful grounds dotted with sculptures. In summer, the pretty veranda makes the perfect place for a drink before you enjoy the sophisticated, well-balanced cooking. Michael's experience and abundant technical skill shine through in classical dishes elevated by his fine judgement and exceptional produce – such as Sladesdown duck with an exemplary jus providing great complexity of flavour. The bedrooms are beautifully furnished and some even come with a firepit and hot tub.

Name: Lysverket
Description: Start your evening with a walk around the octagonal Lille Lungegårdsvannet lake, then head for the KODE 4 art museum where you can dine looking back over the water. Larger than life chef-owner Christopher Haatuft passionately oversees the whole place, both serving dishes and engaging with guests – and while it’s certainly a smart place, the atmosphere remains pleasingly relaxed thanks to his cheery nature. Dishes are informed by Norwegian produce and recipes, with an added modern touch; you’ll find the likes of bluefin tuna crudo with beetroot, tiger’s milk, horseradish and phytoplankton oil.

Name: Légende
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: In a contemporary setting characterized by clean lines, Elliot Beaudoin—once a finalist of TV's Les Chefs! and former associate of the restaurant Tanière³ —serves up a cuisine that is rooted in Québec's terroirs. This establishment sets itself apart with its strictly locavore approach, which sees it using only local ingredients and eschewing exotic ingredients such as chocolate, pepper, citrus fruit, and vanilla. The menu celebrates little-known indigenous ingredients, which are put to clever and creative use. Each dish is thoughtfully composed, demonstrating the chef's keen sensibility in putting the elements together: butter-fried halibut coated in vegetable charcoal, accompanied by a white butter sauce with fermented cherries; venison heart, marinated and then smoked, placed on a delicate tartlet and served with emulsified and candied shiitake mushrooms. The remarkably tender bison hanger steak is elevated by a boreal spice broth and fresh gremolata. Excellent wine list, including nice wine pairings. A legend indeed!

Name: Légume
Address: #207, 2F, Sinsa Square, 652 Gangnam-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06027, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Creating refined and compelling dishes using only vegetables is no easy feat, yet Legume meets the challenge with confidence and creativity. Embracing a fully vegan philosophy, the restaurant draws on a deep understanding of vegetables and diverse cooking techniques to highlight their natural flavours and textures. Thoughtful compositions, layered flavors and precise balance showcase the versatility of plant-based cuisine, offering a sophisticated dining experience that appeals well beyond the vegan community.

Name: Löwen - Apriori
Description: You can sense the dedication of hosts Rita and Domenico Miggiano-Köferli, who, since 2000, have been running this lovely inn that is steeped in history. As well as having tasteful, individually decorated guestrooms and Gaststube (their everyday restaurant), Löwen is home to Apriori, a fine dining restaurant that has held a MICHELIN star since 2018. The setting is modern and elegant, with warm tones and elegant design details shaping a refined interior. The small private dining area, with just five tables, offers a wonderfully intimate atmosphere. Chef-patron Domenico Miggiano puts his heart and soul into his cooking. His culinary style is a modern take on classic cuisine, with Mediterranean accents. In the evening, they serve the "Signature" set menu, comprising four, five or six courses and with an optional cheese course. At lunchtime, in addition to an appealing "business lunch", a wide à la carte selection is also available. The impressive wine list featuring approximately 350 labels provides a brief description of each winery. The charming proprietress is a trained sommelier and her recommendations are excellent.

Name: Līmū
Description: In a town renowned for its splendid villas built by the Palermo aristocracy, this restaurant occupies a small 16C tower on the edge of the historic centre. The name is a tribute to lemon, a fruit that grows in abundance in Bagheria. The restaurant has two elegant, contemporary-style floors, where dinner starts on the small terrace-cum-lounge – the setting for sampling a whole host of delicious appetisers. This is guests’ first encounter with a technical and creative cuisine that sensitively uses the finest local ingredients, while often following paths born from personal and imaginative ideas. The courteous and precise service is overseen by Giandomenico Gambino, a knowledgeable guide for pairings from the rich, well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: L’Abeille
Address: 412 Greenwich St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: L’Abeille reflects the luxurious charms of TriBeCa from its corner perch in this prized zip code. The restaurant is a darling space designed to the hilt with velvet cushioned seats and booths, a striking marble bar and handsome tables set with Christofle cutlery. The young Chef Mitsunobu Nagae is a calm, collected presence in the open kitchen, and years spent working at Joël Robuchon restaurants worldwide are evident. A harmonious union of French cooking with Japanese sensibilities, Nagae’s food is immediately approachable. From Dover sole poached in seaweed butter to white asparagus and langoustine with orange blossom-scented buttermilk foam, each course is a vision of refinement. Charming servers in fitted suits roam the floor, keeping close watch on every seat.

Name: MAE Barcelona
Description: This restaurant, occupying the premises of the now-defunct Freixa Tradició and today featuring a designer interior, brings together the knowledge and dreams of three friends (hence the name MAE, which can be translated as ‘companion’ in the Costa Rican dialect): Mariella Rodríguez (Costa Rica, in charge of management) and chefs Diego Mondragón (Colombia) and Germán Espinosa (Spain).The whole proposal is built on a concept, Sincretismo, which according to the RAE (Royal Spanish Academy, the official institution responsible for overseeing the Spanish language) is the ‘combination of different theories, attitudes or opinions’. It is surprising to see how they bring together products from very different origins, giving us the opportunity to observe how combinations such as Mediterranean red shrimp with Latin American yellow chili unfold. The à la carte is complemented by two good tasting menus (MAE and Gran MAE), where we have found wonderful dishes such as cuttlefish tartare with jalapeño gazpacho and huitlacoche, or leek with smoked vichyssoise and black garlic.

Name: MAIN TOWER Restaurant & Lounge
Address: Neue Mainzer Straße 52, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: A great location in the heart of Frankfurt. Take the lift up to the 53rd floor and bag a table by the window to experience the sort of view you don't often get to enjoy – the panorama over the rooftops of "Mainhatten" is truly spectacular! A contemporary five- or six-course set menu is served, featuring bold, seasonally and internationally inspired dishes prepared with outstanding ingredients. Examples include "Arctic char, Grand Selection caviar, pea" and "ris de veau, lardo, gherkin". The desserts are excellent, as are the "sweets on wheels". You can sip on an aperitif in the lounge before dinner (from 9pm you are also welcome just for drinks). A reservation gets you a free ticket for the lift, which includes access to the observation deck.

Name: MAKIYAKI GINZA ONODERA
Description: A theatre-style open kitchen is centred around a wood-fired oven. Blazing flames flicker as the aroma of burning wood fills the room. All items on the prix fixe menu, from appetiser to dessert, are cooked over this wood fire. Seasonal ingredients from across Japan are prepared through grilling, steaming and smoking. A touch of smokiness and fragrant sauces lend each dish its distinctive character.

Name: MANOIR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The restaurant has had a new chef since 2026. The interior, kitted out like an English manor house, is the reason for the name ‘Manoir’. Eager that guests should relax as if in their own homes, the owner/sommelier serves guests himself. The chef’s aim is to serve light French cuisine. The sweetness and tartness of fruit are overlaid with the umami of fermentation and salt-pickling. Game is delivered by hunters from Hokkaido and other places throughout Japan. Enjoy the wild flavours of game cuisine, with a glass of French wine.

Name: MAPA
Address: Herdade das Valadas, N4, Montemor-o-Novo, 7050-031, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: It offers great comfort and surprises by virtue of its location in the heart of the Alentejo countryside, in the splendid, modern hotel L’AND Vineyards Relais & Châteaux. The dining experience features creative cuisine with traditional foundations, drawing inspiration from the chef's personal experiences and memories. The menu, mostly enjoyed by the hotel’s guests, is presented in an à la carte format and through two tasting menus: Expedição ("Expedition") in 8 moments and Caminhos (“Paths”) served in 12 moments, both inspired by Portuguese travels and the flavours of its former colonies. A standout dish? We loved the Duck, served with rice, snails, and watercress—a unique and delicious combination.

Name: MASHIRO
Description: After Ashiya and Gion, the new frontier for Hiroyuki Koshimo is Karasuma. The shop’s previous name, ‘Roiro’, meant ‘Black as Lacquer’, so Koshimo changed it to ‘Pure White’ to set a different tone. Though his technique is French, Koshimo is not limited by genre, incorporating Japanese elements to broaden the expressive range. Risotto in season, prepared with Yosano rice, is a perennial favourite in this lively and hospitable eatery.

Name: META
Description: Even after META moved to Piazza Riforma in the heart of the city, a visit here is still highly recommended. The entrance is somewhat hidden, with a small staircase leading up to the second floor. The design is chic and elegant, and classic Italian cuisine full of energy, soul and flavour is served at beautiful marble tables. Here and there, Asian accents are also incorporated. There is a set menu as well as à la carte dishes. You will be looked after attentively and professionally. Tip: they offer an impressive selection of champagnes.

Name: MIND
Description: With its stylish urban design, this restaurant would not look out of place in a major city. The chic, modern aesthetic and electronic music are paired with service that is as warm as it is accomplished, creating a pleasingly relaxed atmosphere with an almost homely feel. The "Gourmetmenü" comprises four to eight courses (with an optional cheese course); this tasting menu is also available in a vegetarian version on request. Dishes such as "Huchen, cherry, sage" or "Ibérico pork, brown crab, vin jaune" give diners an idea of the inventive combinations of ingredients they can expect. For all the interesting flavour contrasts, the kitchen delivers food that is beautifully balanced, expressive and full of finesse. To accompany your meal, opt for well-curated wine pairings or an imaginative house-made alcohol-free flight. Between courses, guests are welcome to watch chef Sabrina Fenzl at work at the kitchen island in the front area of the restaurant.

Name: MITA
Address: 804 V St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: Plant-based cuisine is the premise behind this contemporary space set in the Shaw neighborhood. It's tasting menu only, but short and long formats ensure a fit. Chefs Tatiana Mora and Miguel Guerra share their creative spirit at Mita, showcasing Latin American heritage, with influences from Mexico to Chile. Dishes sport originality here. A basket of arepas is a fun dish featuring a variety of textures and flavors with tasty sauces like guasacaca, cashew sour cream with chili oil, and butter made of chontaduro. Order the arracacia soup with a mushroom dashi layered with fava beans and sweet platano, or a creative watermelon crudo with white soy, cilantro and puffed quinoa.

Name: ML
Description: ML is a firm favourite for many a foodie. Mark and Liane Gratama's restaurant and hotel are housed in an imposing listed building in the heart of Haarlem. The modern decor blends vintage elements with chic design. The Chef's Bar, next to the open kitchen, is the place to be if you want to watch enthusiastic chef Mark Gratama and his team at work. Each dish is a creative masterpiece, playfully combining a delightful variety of textures. The unique ingredient combinations demonstrate a willingness to experiment and push culinary boundaries. Refined sauces and broths, often inspired by Asian traditions, provide extra punch. Whether accompanying a succulent sole roulade with an elegant butter sauce flavoured with green herbs or combining a variety of leek preparations with negishio, a Japanese seasoning, the beautifully composed plates consistently reveal a compelling balance of flavours. The vegetarian options are always worth exploring. ML shows that even long-established restaurants can continue to renew themselves.

Name: MO Jasmine
Address: L307, 3F, CP Center, 20 Jinhe East Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, 100020, Chinese Mainland
Description: The dark green façade and warm grey room impart sophisticated taste. The jasmine centrepiece on each table exudes a pleasant scent and befits the restaurant’s name. On the menu, Beijingese melds with Shandong in refined masterpieces that look and taste divine. The signature classic Peking duck can be ordered in individual portions – in addition to pancake, scallion and cucumber, chargrilled duck breast with crispy skin is luxed up with caviar.

Name: MOKO
Description: Alexis Moko polished his skills in Paris and London before decamping to Kyoto. Encountering an old merchant’s house that had once served as a dietary school, he opened a restaurant where he could express his knowledge of French cuisine through Japanese ingredients. Moko makes the most of the freshness of vegetables from nearby Ohara while ageing fish and meat in a curing warehouse to amplify umami. Dishes inspired by classic cuisine are dressed generously in sauces to create a light, refreshing touch.

Name: MONOLITH
Description: MONOLITH links the splendour of classic cuisine to the future. Pastry-wrapped meat symbolises this connection – the diner can choose from several types. Hewing close to time-honoured recipes, beef and lamb are dressed in a Madeira wine and truffle sauce, while pigeon is prepared in a rich salmis. Sauce is assiduously reduced and poured unstintingly, in true orthodox style. Respect for tradition and the classics, eloquently expressed through cooking.

Name: MOS
Description: Picture the scene: as you take in the magnificent view of the IJ, a luxury yacht appears to sail right past yout. Perched at the very tip of the IJdok, MOS boasts a location like no other! Tables on the terrace are coveted, but the interior with its velvet finishings is also a feast for the eyes. Soft pastel tones, colourful flower arrangements, stylish design, and ambient lighting make for a relaxed yet chic setting. Chef Egon van Hoof also knows how to make a visual impression with his elegantly presented dishes. Thanks to his technical skill, he can let his creativity run wild. He is not afraid to push boundaries with unusual combinations, but he never loses sight of the harmony of flavours. For example, he pan-sears skate fillet until it is crispy, locking in the juices, and tops it off with a variety of additions such as earthy mushrooms, Savoy cabbage, tangy sauerkraut and a frothy beurre blanc with a hint of bacon. Egon van Hof's intricate creations tantalise the palate from amuse-bouche to dessert – at a price that won't break the bank.

Name: MOTA
Description: Claus Henriksen's restaurant is set in a listed, early 20th-century red-brick house in the Annebergparken. The area is something of a haven for artisan creatives, with studios belonging to carpenters and glass blowers sitting adjacent to the restaurant; Claus himself even makes the plates that his dishes are served on. Excellent seasonal Danish ingredients are the bedrock of the menus and, while there's an inventive streak to some of the cooking, the chefs also understand the power of simplicity, cleverly allowing the central components – usually vegetables, seafood or game – to really shine.

Name: MUBE
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: ‘Mube’ refers to the fruit of the Japanese staunton vine. The owner-chef adopted the name because it is considered a talisman of longevity and a famous product of his native Shiga. His use of that prefecture’s fermented foods reflects his personality, and he also prepares narezushi, a traditional fermented food of fish, salt and rice, as well as fish sauce and miso. Among his passions lies the interaction between dashi and the umami of fermentation, though he uses the latter’s characteristic flavour with restraint, in deference to modern tastes. A link climbing to the future for the food culture of his forebears.

Name: Ma Cuisine
Description: Candles in wine bottles and tables made from wine barrels are among the details that set the authentic small bistro scene here. Wine connoisseurs will be bowled over by the wine cellar and knowledgeable servers, who know every vintage inside out. Classic French recipes are made with local ingredients to cater to the local palate. Many dishes are meant to share, making this lively spot a great place for get-togethers.

Name: Ma's Kitchen (Jinjiang)
Address: 1 East Kangshi Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: This popular eatery in the bustling Taikoo Li area started out as a stall in Weishan in 1923. Light years from its humble beginnings, this outpost of the chain in Chengdu features a vintage hipster interior and Sichuan classics on the menu. Besides their signature duck blood curd with pork offal and sliced eel, also try the crispy fen zheng rou – pork coated in seasoned rice flour, steamed and then deep-fried. Expect to see a queue from the moment it opens.

Name: Maca de Castro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant that is continually on the up thanks to chef Macarena de Castro (Maca), who has become increasingly committed to sustainability and supports a policy of reafforestation. Located on the first floor of a villa-style building, the restaurant features a dining space with a modern, avant-garde ambience that it shares with the Jardín Bistró (on the ground floor, with a format that is a little easier on the pocket). The single surprise tasting menu is both creative and inspired by the Mediterranean, with a focus on the best seasonal ingredients that Mallorca has to offer, most of which are sourced from nearby auctions, small-scale producers on the island, or from the restaurant’s vegetable garden in Sa Pobla. One of the main signature dishes that is usually on the menu here is the skate with salt and a rock samphire hollandaise sauce. As soon as you walk through the door here, the chef’s love of her local area is clearly evident via a poetically inspired book in which a daily thought for the day is highlighted.

Name: Madame Olympe
Address: Rua Conde de Bernadotte, 26 - loja 101, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Everything people are talking about is Madame Olympe, the restaurant located in the Terrasse Center shopping complex, in the elegant neighbourhood of Leblon. There, the duo of Claude Troisgros and Jéssica Trindade presents a fine-dining concept that celebrates French savoir-faire — most notably in the breads and their exquisitely delicate sauces — while championing Brazilian ingredients and weaving in subtle nods to the world of Japanese gastronomy. In this contemporary space, where original rice-paper lamps evoke floating clouds, everything revolves around an eight-course tasting menu or a shorter four-course option, in which guests choose the dishes they wish to try (don't miss the duck magret with heart of palm, sea purslane, tucupi — a tangy broth extracted from wild manioc — and cauliflower). The celebrated French chef, after more than 45 years living in the land of the Canarinha — as Brazil is affectionately known — confesses to being utterly captivated by its produce, much of it sourced from small local farmers, making the experience all the more singular.

Name: Madcap
Address: 198 Sir Francis Drake Blvd., San Anselmo, CA, 94960, USA
Description: Upscale yet approachable, Chef/owner Ron Siegel's Madcap is one of the Bay Area’s best for contemporary dining. Well-crafted bites on the prix fixe may include a quenelle of tuna tartare with ginger and sesame seeds tucked with a crisp rice cracker that is deliciously simple. Next, a tender, almost-sweet coin of charred octopus rests over a pureed base of fermented pimentos and Tokyo turnip for a clean counterpoint. Supple slices of tart umeboshi, "noodles" of daikon and a creamy ponzu is a creative, pleasure-packed dish, while a tranche of crisp skin-on trout with cauliflower purée and ribbons of kohlrabi is bested with a tableside pour of dashi. The caramel pot de crème with a double hit of almond crumble and ice cream is perfection.

Name: Maeba Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Nestled in the tranquillity of the countryside and off the beaten track, this elegant restaurant is housed in a former 18th-century oil mill, where the charming stone-walled rooms still shelter the historic wine cellar. The contemporary, light and tastefully designed interiors open out onto a garden overlooking rolling hills dotted with olive trees. Chef Salvatore Ciccarelli creates surprise tasting menus comprising 4, 6 or 9 courses, based on the finest local ingredients. The cuisine, contemporary and refined, places particular emphasis on plant-based ingredients without compromising on intensity and character. One of the signature dishes is the warm tubetto with tomato, oyster, spring onion and fennel, a dish that offers a wonderfully balanced flavour and surprising depth of taste.

Name: Maerz - Das Restaurant
Description: Modern tastes meet regional flair with harmonious results – both in the food and the aesthetic of the fine dining restaurant of the hotel Rose, run by brothers Benjamin and Christian Maerz. With its beautiful warm wood panelling and clean lines, the interior is at once cosy, trendy and chic. The cuisine, too, draws on regional culinary tradition as well as contemporary trends, in the form of a set menu dubbed "Heimweh/Fernweh". The chef uses first-rate ingredients sourced from the region, refined with spices from all over the globe, cleverly married in dishes such as "sturgeon in nori, unagi eel, peas & morels, ajoblanco". Christian Maerz will be happy to talk you through the wines or alcohol-free options. Tip: Look out for the "Midweek Special", a three-course set menu including aperitif and drinks pairings on Wed and Thu. There is a pleasant lounge terrace on which to enjoy a pre- or after-dinner drink.

Name: Maeve
Description: Chef Tommy and maître d' Vera have given their charming premises in the centre of Utrecht a stylish makeover. Soft mood lighting contributes to an intimate feel, understated design has a soothing effect and a large mural enlivens the space. Vera runs the dining room with effortless grace; Tommy presents a passionate tribute to his terroir through his dishes. Vegetables, sourced as locally as possible, play a central role (a vegetarian set menu is also available). This is a chef who cooks with great precision, shows a deft touch in applying fresh acidic notes and skilfully plays with temperatures and textures. Creativity, craftsmanship and powerful sauces set his cuisine apart. Take his signature dish of langoustine served on a bed of cashew and chicken skin cream, with samphire, violet flowers, and a dazzling bisque and tandoori sauce. Outstanding! The extensive wine list is equally compelling, and places particular emphasis on Dutch and Belgian labels.

Name: Magoga
Address: Plaza Doctor Vicente García Marcos 5, Cartagena, 30201, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: What we particularly like about Magoga is its young, modest yet professional team with clear ideas and a desire to serve the best cuisine possible. We could easily talk about the duo of chef María Gómez and her husband Adrián de Marcos (sommelier and front of house manager); however, what is most striking here is the sensation of balance and harmony in cuisine which they describe as “an embrace between the sea and the land”. What you will find, both on the à la carte and its tasting menus (Hábitat and Ánima, each with their own wine-pairing option), is contemporary cooking with touches of elegance that always seeks to explore the roots of Cartagena’s recipes while showcasing locally sourced ingredients. These include fish and seafood from the Mediterranean and the Mar Menor lagoon, fruit and vegetables from around Cartagena, and Calasparra rice. One particularly memorable dish that came as a wonderful surprise was the combination of artichoke, smoked eel and foie gras.

Name: Maihöfli by UniQuisine
Description: Chef Robert Steuri heads up the kitchen of this lovely restaurant at a remove from the city centre. In the evening, he and his dedicated team showcase precise craftsmanship and top-notch ingredients in two five- or seven-course set menus, one of which is vegan. A marriage of elegance and bold flavours, the dishes are carefully composed and thoughtfully balanced – intricate without ever feeling overworked. A fine example is the duck with red cabbage, chestnut and orange. At lunchtime, the set menu is shorter, comprising three or four courses. Diners enjoy professional and well-attuned service in an attractive setting: the charming features of the old building, such as high ceilings with decorative mouldings and wood panelling, are seamlessly integrated into its sleek and elegant modern design.

Name: Maison Avoise
Description: After stints in the kitchens of Yannick Alléno, Jean-François Piège and Guy Savoy, chef Alexis Voisenet decided to make his own mark by opening this restaurant in the casemates of the old fort of Issy-les-Moulineaux. A unique historical site whose stone vaults are enhanced with contemporary furnishings. A champion of seasonal produce, the chef's creative, delicate approach results in refined dishes such as the house signature, calf’s sweetbread. In addition to a well-oiled front-of-house team.

Name: Maison Caillet
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Pierre Caillet, "Meilleur Ouvrier de France" in 2011, not only boasts flawless culinary technique, but also reveals a sensitive grasp of the ingredient and infectious enthusiasm. Unusual recipes (like skate wing rolled in a watercress mousse, dotted with kalamansi and coated with a velvety sea urchin sauce), interwoven textures and flavours, premium Normandy produce… and let's not forget the savvy use of herbs and veg from the extensive kitchen garden: it ticks all the boxes. Last but not least, this 19C hostelry also boasts snug, inviting guestrooms with private terraces overlooking the pond.

Name: Maison Chenet - Entre Vigne et Garrigue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Near Avignon, this remote Provençal farmhouse set between cliffs and vineyards does not compromise on authenticity. The scents of the garrigue fill the tastefully renovated interior, which sports a harmonious blend of period details and modern fittings. In the kitchen, Maxime is assisted by his father, Serge Chenet, Meilleur Ouvrier de France. The pair share a love of all things natural and the seasonal ingredients bursting with the flavours of this sun-drenched region. These Bretons, who haven't turned their backs on the staples of butter and cream, work together to concoct a tasty Provençal-inspired market-fresh cuisine. Housed in a 17C cottage, the six guestrooms are conducive to unwinding.

Name: Maison Decoret
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: (Temporarily closed) In a stylish Napoleon III mansion in the heart of Vichy, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Jacques Decoret rolls out his inventive repertory founded on local country produce. He is surrounded by his family (Martine, his wife, in the front of house and his sons in the kitchen: Alexis, savoury chef and Antoine, pastry chef). The score is decidedly surf and turf-centric: cubes of langoustine tails, lentils from the Quatre Vents farm, creamy stock and red butter; roast fillet of lamb, seaweed-spiked Charroux mustard and Cancale oyster seasoning. Finish your meal with the incredible “200 ans de la Pastille” dessert - a tribute to the famous Vichy pastille. A few guest rooms designed in the same contemporary vein as the rest of the property are also available.

Name: Maison Desamy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Previously Alexandre Couillon's sous-chef at La Marine, Simon Bessonnet has set up shop in premises dating from 1860 in the heart of a wine-producing village in the Fiefs Vendéens. But as the contemporary interior he has designed for his restaurant suggests, the chef is very much in touch with the times. Drawing on a regional pantry, he comes up with bold and original combinations and chooses just the right emulsions, jus and condiments to intelligently boost his dishes. As for the desserts, they are models of deliciousness.

Name: Maison Dunand
Address: 55 Soi Sathon 10, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
