Description: Take your seat at one of just 10 tables looking onto a glass-walled kitchen and prepare to settle in for the night, as a meal at this chic seaside resort can last up to six hours. Personalised service from a formal team enhances the intimate atmosphere, and there’s a deep connection with the sea thanks to shell-covered columns, ocean scenes and a great variety of seafood on the multi-course menu. Dishes are centred around luxury ingredients and influences come from the chef’s travels, so you’ll find everything from turbot with laksa sauce to suckling pig with lemongrass and burong mangga.

Name: Ola Martín Berasategui
Description: Located alongside the river, inside of the Tayko hotel. The aesthetics here are almost as impressive as the cuisine, which sees it proudly vaunting its open brickwork and concrete beams to highlight the fact that it was the first building to be constructed using these materials in the city’s historic quarter. The restaurant exudes personality and is keen to immerse guests in a sensory journey via the story of chef Martín Berasategui, enabling them to discover his vision and his particular sense of culinary excellence through the hands of his disciple Raúl Cabrera (known to everyone as Pintxo). The latter faithfully reproduces his mentor’s dishes with great passion, and with a continual emphasis on cuisine that showcases their ingredients and flavours. These are highlighted in exquisite recipes such as the “kokotxas” and slices of cod with a red prawn Vizcaína sauce, and on two tasting menus: Ola and “Lo mejor de la cocina de Martín Berasategui” (The Best of Martín Berasategui’s Cuisine).

Name: Old Stamp House
Address: Church Street, Ambleside, LA22 0BU, United Kingdom
Description: In the heart of the Lake District sits this quirky little restaurant, which occupies the cellars of an old house where William Wordsworth used to work as the Distributor of Stamps for Westmorland. It's now owned by brothers Ryan and Craig Blackburn. The former is in the kitchen, crafting the ‘A Journey Around Cumbria’ tasting menu that showcases his passion for exceptional local produce. The skilfully prepared dishes have been well conceived and carefully balance bold and delicate flavours; each one has a story – sometimes historic, sometimes personal.

Name: Old Tower
Address: 40A, 4F, Building N4, North, TaiKoo Li Sanlitun, 11 Sanlitun Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Sliding doors shield diners from the bustle of the busy shopping hub. Chef Talib Hudda not only helms the kitchen, but also took care of all the design, including brass vegetable inlays in the wooden floor. Inspired by his upbringing and eclectic experiences, he crafts pescatarian tasting menus that push boundaries and follow the seasons. Try the blue lobster with wine-braised shallots and Chinese sauerkraut in dashi beurre blanc and bonito espuma.

Name: Olde Marckt
Description: Olde Marckt, which has been run by the Stoverink family since 1998, has been given a stylish makeover. Albert, the father, ensures seamless service, personally guiding diners through the tempting wine list, which features French, German and Austrian labels (be sure to request a visit to the wine cellar after dessert!). Son Bram has returned to Aalten to take charge of the kitchen, reverently preserving the classics of the house, such as dishes featuring eel, asparagus, and game shot by his father, Albert.But this chef is more versatile than that. His sophisticated cuisine with its subtle cosmopolitan inflections immediately gives away his background, which includes time at De Lindenhof in Giethoorn. For instance, he glazes langoustines of impressive size and quality with tomato, which yields wonderful fruity-sweet nuances. An XO sauce made from scallops and prawns, elevated with goat butter, adds further intensity. This chef avoids gimmickry and brings finesse with individuality to every dish. The menu is extensive - the lunch options are interesting - but the culinary depth is never compromised.

Name: Olio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within The Box, a multifunctional space with vintage cars and contemporary art surrounded by a garden with splendid olive trees, you’ll find the restaurant (bistro service at lunch) and above all excellent seafood cuisine with a small menu dedicated to oysters and caviar. Flavorful and substantial recipes supported by remarkable ingredients, traditional foundations with just the right amount of creativity, nothing excessive. Many memorable dishes, particularly the first courses, including an extraordinary rice with basil pesto, raw and cooked seafood, and cherry tomato extract.

Name: Olive Tree
Address: The Queensberry Hotel, 4-7 Russel Street, Bath, BA1 2QF, United Kingdom
Description: The Queensberry Hotel comprises a series of Bath's archetypal Georgian townhouses and in its basement sits this surprisingly airy, modern restaurant where Chef Chris Cleghorn brings an innovative, personalised approach to his cooking. Colours, textures and flavours are used to full effect in refined, creative combinations which have plenty of depth and, while they may appear simple, that’s all part of their skilful make-up. Desserts are a consistent highlight, such as wonderful Yorkshire strawberries complemented by sweet custard and frozen sheep's yoghurt.

Name: Olivea Farm to Table
Address: Carr. Federal #3, KM 92.5, La Ruta de Vino Valle de Guadalupe, Ensenada, 22766, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Set inside Casa Olivea hotel, this charming restaurant displays a confident simplicity and purity of flavor on a frequently changing seasonal menu. It wears its farm-to-table bona fides on its sleeve thanks to pristine produce that arrives daily from nearby acreage that is organically and sustainably tended. Guests select between multicourse vegetarian or seafood-forward menus, with a handful of à la carte offerings, and will find equal satisfaction in main dishes like their daily catch with a celeriac puree or grilled octopus atop mole blanco. Desserts, like caramelized plums with a purple basil sorbet or a squash-filled eclair with kohlrabi ice cream, are particularly intriguing.

Name: Olmo
Address: Piazza della Chiesa 7, loc. San Pietro all'Olmo, Cornaredo, 20007, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The name pays tribute to the great elm tree that dominates the village’s small pedestrianised square, a symbol of the village and the very heart of the project. This cosy and exclusive restaurant has just three tables and the same number of seats at the counter overlooking the kitchen, offering guests the chance to watch the kitchen team at work up close. The culinary offering takes the form of a tasting menu that interprets the seasonality of the ingredients with creativity and precision, playing with textures, temperatures and balanced flavour contrasts. The result is a contemporary, minimalist and precise style of cooking, which successfully combines technical skill with expressive immediacy. At lunchtime, there is also a more flexible set menu, offering a choice of three dishes, which is particularly good value for money. Among the most compelling dishes, the refined combination of Grana and tomato stands out: Grana cream, tomato confit served with its own jam, and a surprising Parmigiano ice cream, coming together in a harmonious whole, rich in nuances and of great gustatory elegance.

Name: Olo
Description: A pretty yellow townhouse located opposite the pier plays host to this cool, minimalist restaurant, where four rooms decked out with locally designed furniture have a delightfully understated feel. Choose between a four-course menu, a tasting menu or a pre-order seasonal tasting menu, all of which showcase produce from the north of the country, with meats such as moose and elk a feature. The refined yet richly flavoured dishes are beautifully presented and often innovative in design, with the sautéed reindeer with Lappish almond potato the chef’s signature. As well as a wine pairing, they offer non-alcoholic drinks crafted in-house.

Name: Omakase @ Stevens
Description: The chef hails from Osaka and honed his skills in some of Tokyo’s top kitchens. In his 6- or 8-course omakase menu, he revisits his Japanese roots with classic French techniques. Exquisite dishes made with quality seasonal Japanese produce taste light, sophisticated and subtle. With only 16 seats at the pine wood counter overlooking the open kitchen, reservations are recommended. The immaculate service further adds to the experience.

Name: Omakase Table
Address: 3330 Piedmont Rd. NE, #22A, Atlanta, GA, 30305, USA
Description: Here at this serious counter-focused setting, find Chef Leonard Yu and his small team presiding over a multicourse experience that leans traditional while offering a nice balance of variety and seasonality. A smattering of otsumami begin the evening on a strong note with shaved wagyu beef lightly poached in sukiyaki sauce with a quail egg. The chef's signature dish, uni gohan with otoro, is decadent, while corn potage delivers an impressive depth of flavor. Meanwhile, nigiri showcases character without any flash: Kawahagi is topped with flash-frozen liver paste that melts on the tongue, while sharkskin sole with engawa is given a fantastic sear. Finally, Japanese panna cotta finished with fresh strawberries alongside a flavorful musk melon is a light, refreshing finale.

Name: Omakase at Barracks Row
Description: Chef Yi "Ricky" Wang, who trained under Chef Nakazawa before running a series of pop-ups, is now settled in at this counter, located up a set of metal stairs in an industrial-chic space. Take special note of the paintings that line that staircase—they're nods to a longstanding tradition of fishermen brushing their catch with ink and pressing it into rice paper—and you may be presented with a similar piece at your meal. Chef Wang's omakase features a few otsumami, perhaps poached sweet shrimp in a smoked Maine uni sauce, before progressing to nigiri. It's all impressive, from the Boston surf clam finished with kumquat kosho to the hay-smoked Spanish mackerel sourced from the Carolinas that's bold but balanced. Musk melon with strawberries imported from Japan is a satisfying finale.

Name: Omakase by Sergey Pak
Description: A sleek black and grey colour scheme characterises this dimly lit restaurant set within Bergen’s Skostredet Hotel. Just one sitting per night ensures maximum enjoyment of the evening, where Pak shows off his remarkable knife skills via a refined omakase menu that blends high-quality Norwegian ingredients with impeccable Japanese techniques. Appealing dishes could include the likes of reindeer sashimi or wagyu served with caviar and gold leaf, and a choice of three different wine pairings completes the experience.

Name: Omakase by Walt
Description: This restaurant, where all is not what it seems, will come as something of a surprise! What, from the outside, appears to be a simple household appliance shop (you won’t find any sign whatsoever at the entrance) obscures this tiny, discreetly lit restaurant in the purest Japanese style, where the sushi bar and the chef are the undoubted stars of the show. Walter Sidoravicius, originally from Venezuela but with Lithuanian and German roots, has worked and trained around the world, most notably in Tokyo and as an instructor at the Basque Culinary Center. His cuisine is focused on a single Omakase menu that is full of intrigue – guests leave all decision-making to the chef who prepares elaborate dishes in full view that are fully respectful of Japanese tradition (cold and raw options, nigiris served in two parts, dishes served in traditional bowls etc). Guests are asked to arrive at the same time in order to enjoy the culinary experience together.

Name: Omar Dhiab
Description: Almost next-door to Place des Victoires, Omar Dhiab has found himself a minimalist lair with an open kitchen and a swanky white marble counter. His cuisine revolves around flavoursome ingredients, is rich in creative notes and flanked by a meticulous attention to the sauces and seasonings, some of which are of Egyptian origin. Examples include sea urchin au naturel and cumin-flavoured coral lentils, or roast stag with a herbaceous seasoning and smoked mustard. The light, tempting desserts are an ode to the seasons. Front-of-house service by a youthful, enthusiastic team.

Name: Ombellule
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Tabata and Ludovic Mey’s restaurant is steeped in an atmosphere reminiscent of a 1930s Orient Express carriage: dark wainscoting, landscape frescoes and claret-coloured banquettes. Never wont to take the easy route, the couple harness their creativity and technical skills to roll out the red carpet for veggies, as is illustrated by the remarkable starter on the Roscoff onion theme, both crunchy and subtly sweet. Another dish, Arctic char flanked by a lemon-spiked marbled buttermilk sauce with tamari, is packed in umami notes, showcasing the couple’s high-flying culinary prowess.

Name: Omija
Description: In this warm buzzy eatery, chef Romain Bonnet crafts creative surprise menus of Asian inspiration: the ‘omija’ is a Korean fruit, known as the five-flavour berry due to its unique combination of sweet, sour, bitter, salty and pungent flavours. Bonnet is unswerving in his dedication to taste, illustrated by green ‘kombujime’ asparagus flanked by sesame-flavoured ice cream, or squid from la Turballe marinated in Korean pepper. Virtuoso craftsmanship, gutsy stocks and addictive, big-boned sauces. The mainly organic produce is painstakingly sourced (common shrimp from la Cotinière on Oléron Island, line-caught pollock, Vendée squab). An infectiously cosy eatery with unstarched, yet seamless service.

Name: Oniku Karyu
Description: The chef’s love of beef began when he was a boy, when his father would cook thick-cut steaks for him. He is a beef evangelist, proclaiming its appeal to the world. His decision to create a ‘meat kappo’ arose from his training in kaiseki. Wagyu beef is used in every Japanese preparation style, including nigiri sushi, char-grilled and shabu-shabu. The beauty of the traditional building, the kimono-clad service and the colourful dinnerware all add to the ambience. Through beef cuisine, Oniku Karyu is spreading the word about Japanese culture.

Name: Onjium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Pets not allowed
Description: Across the street from the stone wall of Gyeongbokgung Palace, Onjium blends traditional Korean aesthetics with modern architectural calm. Guided by court cuisine specialist Cho Eun-hee and Park Sung-bae, the culinary team reinterprets traditional Korean flavours through modern techniques, seasonal ingredients, and years of research. Each dish is rooted in history yet speaks to today’s palate. Counter seating offers a glimpse into the quiet focus of the kitchen, while carefully curated beverage pairings enhance the experience.

Name: Ono
Description: As the official ‘Tourism Ambassador for Awaji’s Food Culture’, Kota Ono employs Awaji ingredients in each item of his omakase set menu, paying homage to the island of his birth. He proudly sources not only seafood and wagyu but also soy sauce and even salt from his native Awaji, expounding its charms from the bustle of Kitashinchi. Luxury foods of the season adorn a large platter, unstintingly served in hearty portions. The goal is to be a place where flavoursome food is served, without forgetting imagination and playfulness.

Name: Onor
Description: In a small, maritime-themed, luxurious brasserie, (formerly La Marée where he kicked off his career!), Thierry Marx pays tribute to everything he holds dear: the transmission of know-how and a deep respect for nature, individuals, produce and producers, but also a love of culinary innovation. In the company of partner-chef Ricardo Silva, he signs a delicate, spot-on, modern score, dotted with nods to Asia and strewn with Marxian signatures such as soy risotto or, depending on the season, petals of scallops or seabream.

Name: Ontra's Gourmetstube
Description: Peter Grasmeier, owner and head chef of Ontra in the Tech Square technology centre, has set up this modern little restaurant right next door. In the evening, he serves a four- or six-course set menu, available by reservation only. Example dishes include "scallop, sweet potato, jalapeño, coriander" and "Wagyu, whiskey, broccolini, shallot, corn". A vegetarian version is also available. The modern cuisine incorporates international influences and adheres to the seasons, demonstrating a commitment to excellence in terms of ingredient quality and technique. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Operakällaren
Address: Operahuset, Karl XII's Torg, Stockholm, 111 86, Sweden
Description: If you're celebrating, then you've come to the right place. Sweden's most opulent restaurant sits within the historic Royal Opera House, and the sumptuous, high-ceilinged room comes bedecked with glittering chandeliers, huge paintings and original carved and gilded oak panelling dating back to 1895. Conversely, the place is run by a young team and comes with cool music and modern international cooking that might include the likes of mallard with burnt apple and trevisano or langoustine with hazelnut, vanilla, white truffle and brown butter vinaigrette. The accompanying wine list is remarkable.

Name: Opus 388
Address: 77F, Mandarin Oriental, Block A, UpperHills, 5001 Huanggang Road, Futian, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: At a head-spinning height of 388 metres, this elegant restaurant has a lot to offer as well as spectacular views. The chef’s table provides a fascinating insight into the culinary process, while the main dining room sports an airy, tranquil vibe. Italian chef, Alessio Durante, deftly and creatively reworks French classics with the best seasonal ingredients. The tasting menu is the best way to experience his vision, but à la carte options also abound.

Name: Orangerie
Description: To experience a true institution of the Baltic Sea, look no further than this elegant fine dining restaurant in a side wing of the Maritim Seehotel. Chef duo Thomas Lemke and Simone Melis preside over the creation of classic cuisine, to be ordered à la carte or as a four- to seven-course set menu. Options include dishes such as flamed langoustine with butterhead lettuce, tomato, and charcoal notes, or exquisite Müritz lamb with aubergine, parsley and a spicy pomegranate jus. The friendly and professional waitstaff provide excellent wine recommendations. Delightful terrace overlooking the small park and the Baltic Sea promenade.

Name: Oretachi No Nikuya
Address: 194-1 Gongyi Road, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan Region
Description: This paradise for beef lovers is just the ticket for discerning connoisseurs. The young owner-chef knows his cattle inside out and sources prize-winning breeds from all over Japan, including Akage Wagyu from Kumamoto and some rare ones not found elsewhere. Both the set and à la carte menus showcase premium cuts that are perfectly grilled to your order by the highly-skilled team. They also explain every cut in detail, together with where they source their produce.

Name: Oriental Sense & Palate
Address: 57 Sinan Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This multi-storey marvel in a historical mansion exudes understated luxury. Chef Fai creates culinary gems that entice with pretty plating and precise execution. Be sure to order the juicy, deep-fried 20-day-old pigeon with crispy skin. The sautéed dried shrimps with minced pork seduces with contrasting textures and deep, mildly spicy flavours. Seafood dishes including whelk are also popular.

Name: Origen
Description: After a long career working in restaurants in Spain and around the world (Austria, UK, Singapore, Mexico etc), chef Àlex Vidal has returned to his roots to open his own restaurant, which is contemporary in feel and boasts a glass-fronted kitchen on one side of the bright dining room. On the menu, the goal is to showcase honest Valencian cooking, particularly from the Carcaixent area, and to provide a modern vision of traditional dishes and stews which are always prepared with organic and locally sourced ingredients. The supremely delicate broths and sauces warrant special attention thanks to their nuanced flavours and unquestionable technical mastery. Three tasting menus are available: Carcaixent, Origen and Ternils. One dish you won’t want to miss out on is the delicious “amparín” of leek, cuttlefish and peanuts, which pays homage to the area’s gastronomic heritage with its version of Carcaixent’s most emblematic tapa.

Name: Origine
Description: Perfectly at home in this stylish, understated interior, Japanese chef Tomofumi Uchimura, who learned the ropes at Lameloise, rolls out his consummate mastery of Gallic techniques, peppered with discreet Japanese touches. An example: Atlantic cod in a miso crust and umami-flavoured gingerbread with a cauliflower tempura, tarama, bergamot lemon, peanuts and ginger. This fan of Burgundy produce elegantly exalts local ingredients, including organic veg from a Dijon market gardener, Charolais beef, Auxonne saffron, snails from next-door Jura… Nothing is off limits for the chef as long as the quality is up to the mark, particularly when it comes to fresh seafood. A subtle, surgically precise culinary repertory with a particularly enticing veggie menu. Fine wine bin.

Name: Origines
Address: Rue du Clos-de-la-Chaux, Le Broc, 63500, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Is it Adrien Descouls's native region of Auvergne that inspires his ever-so-fresh cuisine? Just outside Issoire, in this modern building perched next to a 14C castle, the chef demonstrates his talents without going over the top: savvy choice of ingredients, ability to showcase the local terroir (and the kitchen garden!) and a youthful energy that sometimes moves mountains. His pared-back contemporary style is underpinned by true technical skill, as seen in dishes such as golden trout steak with an oxidative Chardonnay sabayon and watercress. As you eat, drink in the magnificent view from the dining room.

Name: Origines Restaurant
Description: In this fashionable restaurant, Aveyron-born chef Julien Boscus finetunes bold, crisp cuisine thanks to a solid classical background. His genuine à la carte lineup (something of a rarity these days…) showcases savvily crafted, flavoursome dishes made with top-drawer seasonal produce. Examples include a delicious parmesan and white summer truffle-flavoured soufflé or red mullet from the Vendée coast in olive oil, escorted by Provençal veg, black garlic seasoning and a bouillabaisse-based jus, while special mention goes to his amazing hare à la royale, reworked in a subtle modern vein. The wine list stars an impressive selection of Gallic vineyards, served by a slick, professional team. Friendly and endearing!

Name: Orma Roma
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Orma is today one of the most interesting venues on the city's gastronomic scene, thanks to a contemporary cuisine that transcends geographical boundaries without losing balance or identity. Chef Roy Caceres – Colombian by birth, Italian by adoption, and a genuine citizen of the world – weaves influences from Latin America, Asia and the Mediterranean with natural ease, giving life to a proposal that is personal and refined. Two tasting menus of five or seven courses, with dishes also available à la carte, complemented at lunchtime by a more flexible formula. Among the iconic dishes, "Fregula, ricci e salsa XOrma" stands out: Sardinian fregula – a homage to the chef's wife's origins – meets Mexican mole and Hong Kong XO sauce in an intense and harmonious whole, in which the sweet savouriness of sea urchin, the fermented notes of the sauce and the aromatic complexity of the mole merge in perfect equilibrium. Great attention is also devoted to the vegetable element, fed in part by the restaurant's own kitchen gardens on the outskirts of the city. The experience is completed by a service that is elegant yet informal, impeccable without feeling contrived.

Name: Ormer Mayfair
Address: Flemings Hotel, 7-12 Half Moon Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 7BH, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Not everywhere is about ‘a scene’ – in the basement of the Flemings Mayfair hotel is a restaurant for those who prefer a more discreet, almost secretive environment, away from both hurly and burly, where the style of service is unapologetically formal. The set menus come in two lengths – with pescatarian and vegetarian versions available – and mine such top-drawer ingredients as Cornish mackerel and Orkney scallops. The chef’s Moroccan heritage comes through in dishes like roast Anjou pigeon with preserved lemon and sauce Marocain, and the English saffron dessert with nadorcott.

Name: Oro Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Reaching Oro means beginning the experience before even sitting down to table: the transfer by private motorboat from Piazza San Marco to the legendary Hotel Cipriani, on the island of Giudecca, introduces guests to a context of rare elegance. The restaurant opens onto the lagoon through broad picture windows, while walls lined with mirrored panels, a dramatic gilded dome and geometric marble floors define an interior that is both refined and luminous. The cuisine of Ferrara-born chef Vania Ghedini interprets the great Italian tradition with a contemporary touch, giving life to dishes that are balanced and not overcomplicated. Numerous references celebrate Venice: the recurring use of gold, for instance, evokes not only the name of the restaurant but also the city's extraordinary artistic heritage, from Byzantine mosaics to the gold backgrounds of Venetian painting. Ingredients from the lagoon engage in dialogue with produce from Emilia-Romagna and with measured Moroccan influences, the legacy of the chef's professional journey. Among the most interesting dishes, the seaweed and herb broth risotto stands out, mantecato with butter and cheese and completed by horseradish: it captivates through the intensity of its marine aromas, the elegance of the mantecatura and the perfect equilibrium between the sweetness of the rice, the pungent note of the horseradish and the savouriness of the sea vegetables.

Name: Orobianco
Address: Colina del Sol 49 A, Calp, 03710, Spain
Description: At Orobianco, spectacular views of Calp and its impressive Peñón de Ifach rock are complemented by Italian-inspired cuisine full of culinary nuances under the tutelage of award-winning chef Paolo Casagrande that will undoubtedly leaving a lasting impression! Elegance is an obvious thread here and is clearly in evidence in dishes available on two set menus (Short and Long). The restaurant’s culinary essence is a fusion of Italian cooking and local ingredients that showcase Spain and the Mediterranean through dishes such as cuttlefish tagliatelle, watercress risotto with red prawns, and spaghettoni with a pil-pil sauce. Add to this perfect cooking techniques, clean flavours, astute pairings of ingredients that add a contemporary touch to classic foundations, plus an impressive choice of artisanal Italian bread.

Name: Orsa & Winston
Address: 122 W. 4th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Orsa & Winston pairs Japanese and Italian influences in a prix-fixe menu served from an open kitchen. Chef Josef Centeno's cooking leans exploratory instead of traditional: think peak-season ingredients infused with wide-ranging flavors. Dishes move between familiar and unconventional: crudos accented with fruit and herbs and seafood preparations that nod to both Mediterranean and Japanese sensibilities. The signature satsuki rice porridge, finished with parmesan cream and uni, remains one of the more distinctive expressions of the restaurant's approach.

Name: Ortega
Address: 16 Majoribanks Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington, 6011, New Zealand
Description: Blue walls, glass float pendant lights, and maritime art and memorabilia lend a nautical aesthetic that chimes with the seafood-forward menu. Catch of the day is prepared in myriad styles, ranging from European to Latin American, to accentuate its natural flavours. Highlights include yellowtail kingfish ceviche with avocado and crayfish oil, and market fish with smoked aubergine and confit tomato. Be sure to peruse the drinks list.

Name: Oryori Hirooka
Description: The chef cheerfully welcomes diners, introducing them to the landscape and history of Nara. He takes particular pride in his charcoal-grilled dishes, cooked over a traditional brazier crafted by a Nara potter. Ingredients are seared right before your eyes, with their enticing aromas becoming part of the feast. The rice course features Hinohikari rice cooked in an earthenware pot. The first serving is enjoyed on its own; for the second, diners can add condiments or enjoy it as chazuke (rice served with tea or dashi). For dessert, Yoshino kuzu (arrowroot starch) is used, rounding off the meal with the celebrated flavours of the ancient capital.

Name: Oryori Horikawa
Description: Japanese cuisine reflects a spirit of gratitude for the bounty of nature and of prayer for people’s happiness. The chef values that spirit, pouring it into every dish he makes. The menu, woven from annual festivities, unfolds as a tale of the seasons. Skills honed at a ryotei live in the chef’s painstaking preparation and every detail of arrangements. The origins and customary usages of each cup and plate, related by the proprietress, add grace notes to the meal.

Name: Oryori Mashita
Description: A small shop curtain flutters in a Gion shopping street; walk along cobblestones sprinkled with water to a quiet nook where the noise of the high street is soon forgotten. The menu draws inspiration from a list of poetic seasonal terms. Cooking showcases the peak flavours of each ingredient so as to keep in step with the changing seasons. Precise knife work and pairings of foods with tableware express learning accumulated, like tree rings, over many years. A place to experience the understated poise of Japanese cuisine.

Name: Oryori Tsuji
Description: A cypress counter in a room with adze-hewn ceilings and clay walls – an austere décor by which the proprietor sets the tone. ‘Simple fare’, says the menu, whose offerings avoid shows of splendour in favour of honest presentation. Sense of season flows entirely from the taste and aroma of the food. Sashimi wrapped in kombu, for example, or wanmono prepared with clear soup. Results are all the more impressive for the effort paid where few will notice. Natural flavours to calm the soul.

Name: Oryori Yamada
Description: Both his father and grandfather were chefs, so he naturally aspired to become an itamae, training at a restaurant that follows the tradition of Osaka-style kappo cuisine. At the root of his culinary philosophy is the spirit of avoiding waste, a way of thinking that has also sharpened his imaginative flair. For simmered dishes, instead of relying on bonito dashi, he utilises the broth extracted from the same fish used as the main ingredient. He makes full use of the natural saltiness and flavour of the ingredients, ensuring nothing goes unused. Such subtle ingenuity adds depth to his dishes.

Name: Oseille
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 155, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: Fortunately, there are still restaurants that exist with a strong family lineage – and Oseille is a perfect example. Run by chef Thomas Troisgros (son of Claude Troisgros, grandson of Pierre Troisgros and nephew of Michel Troisgros), it is located in the heart of Ipanema, right above the Toto restaurant (also part of his stable). Here, in a minimalist space that stands out for its profusion of wood and the prominence of a 16-seat “U”-shaped counter with a kitchen in the middle, guests can enjoy a heightened fine-dining experience through a unique, and modern-inspired tasting menu divided into 7 courses showcasing strong French technique and the best local ingredients (we were bowled over by the dish featuring “cavaquinha”, a crustacean similar to lobster). The name of the restaurant takes its inspiration from the legendary “saumon à l'oseille” (salmon with sorrel), created in 1963 by Thomas’ grandfather, the great French chef Pierre Troisgros.

Name: Oseleta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few kilometers from Lake Garda, on gentle vine‑clad slopes, the entrance to Villa Cordevigo, home to L’Oseleta, makes a grand impression as it opens between two rows of cypress trees. Inside are two intimate dining rooms, but the best tables are in the elegant veranda with wide glass windows, where views of the gardens and pool create a charming atmosphere, made even more delightful by impeccable service. In the kitchen, Marco Marras offers two tasting menus (one of which is vegetarian) and an à la carte selection, featuring creative dishes that move effortlessly between references to the Verona and Lake Garda regions and international influences, ensuring a truly enchanting evening in an intimate setting.

Name: Osip
Address: 25 Kingsettle Hill, Hardway, Bruton, BA10 0LN, United Kingdom
Description: Formerly located in the centre of Bruton, Osip is now situated more rurally, in a stunningly renovated former pub that retains the minimalistic elegance of the original. Forward-thinking chef Merlin Labron-Johnson and his enthusiastic team are passionate about their ingredients, with the tasting menus showcasing an array of homegrown produce. Dishes like chilled tomato consommé with fig oil shine in their technical precision and pure, natural flavours. The wine flights highlight organic and biodynamic choices, while there are also non-alcoholic pairings available.

Name: Osmosi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Set in open countryside, surrounded by orderly rows of vineyards, a historic villa houses Fattoria Svetoni, an estate devoted to hospitality, with elegant guest rooms, and to winemaking since 1865. It is here that the restaurant finds its home, arranged partly within the evocative ancient walls of the interior and partly in a strikingly modern glazed veranda that opens onto a pleasant and verdant prospect. The cooking of Mirko Marcelli expresses itself through a creativity that is measured and never excessive: the dishes possess a strong identity without ever imposing themselves, and the pairings are distinguished by balance and coherence, each complementing the other in harmonious fashion. The menu offers three tasting journeys – Materia, Sostanza and Concentrazione (Matter, Substance and Concentration) – from which certain dishes emerge as particularly representative: the excellent ‘constructed’ artichoke, making use of every part of the vegetable, and the sheep meat, presented in an interesting and creative pairing with oysters and endive. On the subject of wine, one may place oneself confidently in the hands of a broad and well-detailed list, and in the passion of Simone, who leads the service alongside the smiling and attentive Elena.

Name: Ossiano
Address: Atlantis The Palm, Crescent Road, The Palm, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is temporarily closed.It's not often sharks and stingrays swim past you as you dine but, then again, there aren’t many restaurants with huge windows looking into an aquarium of 65,000 marine animals. From the moment you descend the marble spiral staircase into this unique restaurant at the Atlantis, you’ll find yourself transfixed and fully immersed. Each course of the ten-course tasting menu tells a story of explorers who have navigated around the Atlantic Ocean; many of the dishes are finished off at the table with an added dash of theatricality.

Name: Osteria Acquarol
Address: Via Johann Georg Plazer 10, San Michele, 39057, Italy
Description: Centrally located and with a plain, almost minimalist interior and a small charming outdoor space on the pedestrianised street for summer dining, Osteria Acquarol serves dishes which are strongly rooted in the region yet prepared with modern techniques and very much influenced by the character of the owner-chef here. Regionally sourced sustainable ingredients often feature in its highly original cuisine, including aromatic and wild herbs grown in the chef’s own garden. In 2023, the restaurant’s kitchen garden was extended so vegetables now play a more dominant role in the two tasting menus served here (seven and nine courses, with dishes that can be chosen à la carte style) – examples include the cold minestra soup entitled “L'orto dietro l'angolo” (“the garden around the corner”) and the unusual green tagliatelle with its carefully balanced bitter flavours. Originally from Cremona, chef Alessandro Bellingeri showcases the region in interesting and original ways.

Name: Osteria Altran
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A small gourmet restaurant surrounded by the verdant landscapes of the Friuli countryside. In what was once a simple farm, owner Guido Lanzellotti has brought this seemingly rustic yet delightfully romantic restaurant to life, creating modern dishes that focuses on top-quality ingredients and careful preparation. Alessio Devidè’s cuisine includes a few local specialities alongside classic Italian dishes which he has reinterpreted with his own personal twist. There’s a huge wine cellar, and if you’re a wine-enthusiast, it’s well worth having a word with the restaurant owner – he has extensive knowledge of the world of wine which he is delighted to share with guests, at the same time as recommending the best labels to accompany your meal.

Name: Osteria Enoteca Cuntitt
Address: Via alla Chiesa 8, Castel San Pietro, 6874, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just above Mendrisio, this charming little village, complete with a historic center and church, offers both visitors and locals a beautiful Lombard-style farmhouse, where the refined restaurant serves modern Italian cuisine with regional influences, as well as a variety of caviar selections and excellent vegetables (the pigeon with carrots is a must-have). The wine list benefits from its own cellar, featuring regional labels and Champagne.

Name: Osteria Giulia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: It seems nearly impossible to have a bad time at Chef Rob Rossi’s Italian stunner. Flickering candlelight bounces off cream-colored walls and blond-oak tables running down the length of this restaurant that feels, at all times, totally under control thanks to a suave staff. And whereas many Italian menus can look the same, Rossi narrows in on the seafood-rich traditions of Liguria. A superbly light vitello tonnato and a piping hot Ligurian flatbread stuffed with stracchino offer promising starts. There must be pasta, like wild snow crab tagliolini with smoked bottarga, and there must be tiramisu. A deep Italian wine list and an especially talented cocktail program round out an experience that is as accomplished as it is hospitable.

Name: Osteria Mozza
Address: 6602 Melrose Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90038, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A perennial hit since opening (expect a wait), this decade-old darling continues to please with creative cocktails and Italian cuisine. The décor veers from typical osteria-style, thanks to handsome dark-wood paneling and a white marble counter but nab a seat at the Mozza bar for a prime view of the antipasti preparation.Bread is something of an obsession here, as is the mozzarella menu. Chef Nancy Silverton's team strives to show you around the corners of Italian cooking, The crispy chicken leg is pure and simple comfort food, and pastas are unsurprisingly phenomenal—try the orecchiette with sausage and Swiss chard. Rosemary olive oil cake dusted with powdered sugar, topped with caramelized sugar rosemary brittle and sided by olive oil gelato is the perfect ending.

Name: Osteria del Viandante
Description: Situated on the first floor of the 13C military fort in the centre of Rubiera, this elegant restaurant boasts five dining rooms, each one more delightful than the last and all frescoed, with the exception of the old limonaia which is decorated with wallpaper depicting its former function. This stylish and romantic setting provides the backdrop for young and enthusiastic chef Jacopo Malpeli who, having been born and raised between Parma and Reggio, creates cuisine that reflects the grandeur and opulence of local culinary traditions. Among his many interesting dishes, a particular favourite is the savarin di riso, which pays tribute to the legendary Mirella and Peppino Cantarelli and their former two-Michelin-starred restaurant in Samboseto. The extraordinary wine list includes several French wines alongside Italian labels and champagnes.

Name: Osteria dell'Enoteca
Description: In a quiet residential area, charm and refinement are the hallmarks of this modern osteria, skillfully and warmly managed by a young couple who offer delicious dishes with modern and creative flair. The large fireplace is the guardian spirit of the restaurant, but in summer, service also moves out to the flower-filled garden, which, like the dining room, features works of art. There is an interesting selection of Ticino wines! The surprise menu “Lascio a voi” (“I leave it up to you”) is available – any food intolerances, as well as vegetarian or vegan preferences, should be communicated in advance.

Name: Osteria della Brughiera
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched in the foothills embracing Bergamo, a garden leads to an elegant country house where parquet floors, exposed beams, and a striking fireplace set the stage for refined hospitality – ideal for an intimate dinner. A fresh wind blows through the kitchen: Bergamo native Paolo Cortinovis, whose impressive credentials include international experience and a previous tenure here, now works alongside Beatrice Arrigoni, who carries on her family’s culinary legacy under her father Stefano’s guidance. Available as both a tasting menu and à la carte, the offerings are broad and dynamic. The cuisine draws from Italy’s varied regional traditions before venturing into more contemporary territory, alternating effortlessly between fish and meat. Heritage staples – such as house-cured salumi – share the stage with more refined ingredients, from lobster to caviar, reflecting a well-calibrated balance of roots and ambition.

Name: Osteria di Passignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the Antinori universe, in one of the most beguiling villages of the Chianti Classico, stands the Osteria di Passignano: a restaurant of great elegance housed within walls steeped in history, alongside the ancient Badia di Passignano, still inhabited by monks and guardian of the barrel cellar of the wine that bears its name, produced from the vineyards that surround the monastery. The setting is of the very highest order, where history, craftsmanship and extraordinary landscapes are woven together. In the kitchen, chef Matteo Lorenzini maintains a close bond with the territory and its produce, articulating the offering between a solid local tradition and a more contemporary reading, frequently open to seafood – as in the accomplished crab salad with caviar and zest from the estate’s own citrus trees. Considerable attention is paid to seasonality, with vegetables and herbs drawn from the Orto della Badia, while the sumptuous wine list, with over a thousand labels from around the world, pays natural and fitting homage to the great Tuscan reds, beginning with those bearing the host’s own signature.

Name: Ostseelounge
Description: Housed in Strandhotel Dünenmeer, Ostseelounge has much to offer. In the clean-lined, chic restaurant, floor-to-ceiling windows afford wonderful views of the dunes and the sea – romantic sunsets included! Chef Christopher Huhnstock-Kerber presents a modern, seasonal set menu, showcasing predominantly regional ingredients with his own creative touch. Clearly structured and with refined contrasts, harmonious dishes such as "Alpine pasture-raised lamb, onion, apple" or "fermented whey, fennel pollen, dill" stand out. A three-, five- or seven-course menu is available, also in a vegetarian version. "Midweek Gourmet Special": On Wed and Thu, the various set menu options come at a reduced price. Service is warm and professional under the leadership of the team's sommelier, Bettina Huhnstock-Kerber. Tip: The chef's table right by the open kitchen is well worth considering. There is also a lovely terrace. For an à la carte alternative, the hotel has another restaurant: Kaminlounge.

Name: Oteque
Address: Rua Conde de Irajá 581, Rio de Janeiro, 22271-020, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: Stepping through the gate of its discreet façade means leaving the bustle of everyday life behind and entering a space with a soaring ceiling height, where the past lives alongside the most modern vanguard. The main room carries a faintly industrial air, retaining its weathered red-brick walls, and is dominated by six large round tables and one special elongated table for five set before the open kitchen. The celebrated chef Alberto Landgraf is defined by simplicity and naturalness—hallmarks visible in his efforts to champion Brazilian roots and the transparency of flavours. His proposition centres on a single tasting menu that changes with the seasons, with some dishes replaced daily and based on the best and freshest ingredients. Good examples include Langoustines, pirão (a creamy cassava flour purée made with stock) and aromatic pepper, and the excellent bread made in-house and served straight from the oven.

Name: Otto Geleng
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within the enchanting Hotel Timeo, a handful of tables on a bougainvillea-adorned terrace overlooking Taormina, the Bay of Naxos and Etna: against this backdrop of extraordinary beauty, chef Roberto Toro presents a cuisine that unites the flavours of Sicily with international techniques and inspirations, without losing its connection to the local area. The offering unfolds across several tasting menus dedicated to fish, meat and vegetables – alongside the option of composing a three-course à la carte menu. Among the dishes that most impressed our Inspector, the Prawn in Two Textures stands out: the Sicilian crustacean is served raw with tomato sauce, almond cream and caviar, whose refined savouriness enhances the natural sweetness of the flesh, while a frozen grapefruit delivers a pleasantly citrus freshness to the finish. The experience is completed by impeccable service, capable of uniting professionalism, spontaneity and genuine hospitality. The wine list, with over 400 labels, celebrates Sicily without forgoing a rich Italian and French selection, and includes interesting productions from small local winemakers.

Name: Outlaw's Fish Kitchen
Address: 1 Middle Street, Port Isaac, PL29 3RH, United Kingdom
Description: Wonky walls, low ceilings and a host of delicious seafood can be found at this intimate 15th-century fisherman’s cottage, which stands right on the Port Isaac harbourside. Top-quality fish and shellfish are the driving force behind the confidently pared-back cooking, which allows the naturally delicious produce to speak for itself, with occasional bolder elements such as gochujang butter showcasing the chefs' fine judgement of flavours. An à la carte is available at lunch, but for dinner everyone enjoys the set sharing menu with a choice of main course from the blackboard.

Name: Oxomoco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set in a spacious, airy corner of Greenpoint, Oxomoco channels Mexican flavors through a contemporary Brooklyn lens. Tostadas and tacos remain central to the menu, but the kitchen reaches well beyond them with seafood, vegetables, and larger plates meant for sharing. Beef cheek suadero comes with roasted jalapeno and bright guacachile, while cochinita pibil is accompanied by black beans, pickled vegetables, and a fruity habanero-pineapple salsa. The wood-fired cooking that has long defined the restaurant remains part of its appeal. Tequila and mezcal anchor the lively cocktail list, and the relaxed dining room and front patio keep things convivial.

Name: Oxte
Description: This tastefully fashionable dinky restaurant tucked away in the Étoile neighbourhood, serves spot-on, contemporary, Mexican-influenced cuisine. Gallic ingredients are tweaked with condiments, herbs and spices by a talented and passionate Mexican chef, Enrique Casarrubias who works side by side his wife and chef, Montserrat Estrada, when he isn’t lending a hand in the dining room. His ever-changing score evolves with the seasons, extending an invitation to travel, often to Mexico. Examples: squid, house-made black pudding and recado negro or pigeon, Oxte mole (sauce), leeks and pickled raisins – the chef signs a savvy, perfectly pitched and masterfully executed score packed in gutsy, vibrant seasonings and condiments. Colourful, punchy and well-seasoned, without forgetting a special mention for the house’s emblematic dessert: avocado, mezcal and lime!

Name: Oyster Oyster
Description: It is highly rare for a tasting menu to leave one feeling—well—energized, but so goes the imaginative cooking at this vegetable-focused gem where local farms are the very essence of this passionate operation. The imaginative compositions from Chef Rob Rubba and his team offer delicious insights into what is possible with vegetables. There is true creativity here, as in Badger Flame beets topped with lightly pickled kohlrabi and a dusting of pastrami spice, or roasted squash finished with a brown butter yogurt sauce. Even the rustic-style bread served with a vegan marigold spread in lieu of butter is special.

Name: P greco
Description: In Italy, the chef experienced the fierce pride the Italians have in their home regions. Deeply impressed by the unique cuisines of people who produce and consume locally all their lives, he set his sights on combining Japanese sensibilities with Italian cooking. One example is anago carpaccio: deboned conger eel accompanied by tomato and bagna càuda. The focus on seafood derives from his love of the bounty of the sea, learned at his grandmother’s house in Okinoshima.

Name: PAVO
Description: The experience begins with the impressive drive up to the Falkenstein! Nestled between the peaks of the Allgäu Alps, the Boutique Hotel Blaue Burg is only accessible via a private road – and the view is breathtaking! The small restaurant is where Simon Schlachter wins diners over with a modern and creative dining concept revolving around sharing. All the elaborate courses that make up his set menu consist of several small dishes – perfect for sharing. Numerous components merge to create flavoursome plates – subtle Asian influences are evident throughout, but regional and classic accents also make their presence felt. Completing the picture, there is the upscale decor and professional service courtesy of the charming maître d', who happens to be the chef's partner. Alternatively, try out Restaurant 1250, which serves regional cuisine (also at lunchtime).

Name: PM & Vänner Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Set within a hotel of the same name, PM & Vänner ticks all the designer boxes: beautiful tables, stylish armchairs, chic lighting – and the fresh flowers and candelabras add a romantic touch. With no windows, you’re ensconced in your own little world, where the team passionately relay the story of the ‘Tabberas’ menu – a walk in the forest between mountains, meadows and lakes – where ambitious dishes showcase produce from their garden and bakery, as well as from local farmers, foragers and hunters. The extraordinary wine list offers a huge array of over 5,000 vintages and a remarkable collection of champagnes.

Name: POTONG
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Pichaya 'Pam' Soontornyanakij's confident Thai-Chinese cooking is the draw at this historic multi-storey restaurant. Her heritage and memories inform the menu. The tasting menu shows assured technique and creativity: a layered Phat Thai with tiger prawn, signature 14-day aged duck, beautifully executed Rat Na – all reworking familiar flavours in unexpected ways. The non-alcoholic pairing and wine pairings deserve consideration. The upstairs bar is worth a post-meal visit too.

Name: PRESQU'ÎLE
Address: 2F, Yodoyabashi odona, 4-1-1 Imabashi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0042, Japan
Description: PRESQU'ÎLE takes its name from a district of Lyons, reflecting the chef’s respect for the place where he trained and his resolve to carry its traditions forward for the next generation. Classical technique underpins French cooking in which sauces play a central role. A speciality is duck and foie gras tourte served with sauce poured tableside. Fruit displayed on the table may also appear as crêpes suzette.

Name: PRIMO PASSO
Description: The name ‘Primo Passo’ means ‘first step’. The chef was in charge of pasta at the celebrated Quattro Passi restaurant in Naples before taking his first step towards independence in Shintomicho. His aim is to create ‘Italian cuisine with a Japanese twist’. He uses plenty of dashi and Japanese ingredients. Also incorporating Japanese elements are the coffered ceiling, mud walls and vertically written menu. He serves several small dishes featuring his speciality pasta to showcase a variety of flavours.

Name: PRU
Address: 60/1 Mu 6, Srisoonthorn Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: PRU continues to champion mindfulness with a seasonal menu made using ingredients from the restaurant's farm and trusted Thai suppliers. Committed to fermenting, preserving and responsible practices, chef Jimmy's team crafts modern Thai cuisine with a strong sense of place. The experience unfolds across the restaurant, beginning with drinks in the lounge before moving into the main dining room, with a brief visit to the kitchen adding another layer to the evening. The signature "King of the Fruits" pairs durian with caviar and sea grapes.

Name: PRUNIER
Address: 2F, Tokyo Kaikan, 3-2-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-0005, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: PRUNIER is the main dining room of Tokyo Kaikan, a meeting-place cherished for generations. The décor conjures images of fish and flowing water, harking back to the restaurant’s earliest days when it specialised in seafood. Here you can enjoy modern French cuisine that reflects the shifting seasons, presented in an elegant setting. Sole bonne femme, handed down from generations of head chefs, keeps a tradition alive and well. Gracious service adds an extra touch to the meal.

Name: PURS Nordic Japanese
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Peter Fridén presents his "New Nordic Japanese Cuisine" in the 17C Alte Kanzlei, tastefully designed by Axel Vervoordt. Located in a small side street, the beautiful building houses this elegant, upmarket restaurant as well as a boutique hotel. In the kitchen, visible through a glass sliding door, Fridén brings together three culinary traditions: he was born in South Korea, grew up in Sweden and trained in French cuisine. His six-course set menu, also available in a shortened version, reflects his personality through an intriguing mix of Asian-Japanese, Scandinavian and French elements. The "ikejime golden trout, whey, kohlrabi, yuzu", for example, impresses with the clarity of the individual flavours and the way they come together. Creative cooking is matched by exceptionally refined presentation. Individual courses and additional dishes can also be ordered à la carte, and the latter can be swapped into the set menu or added as extras. Carefully selected wine pairings by the glass draw on a list of over 1 000 labels; sake and kombucha are also served.

Name: Pablo
Description: This family-run restaurant, in business for over five decades, has a true passion for food and has moved with the times without losing its traditional values. Located just a few metres from León’s cathedral, known as the Pulchra Leonina, this restaurant is full of contrasts, ranging from the masonry on the façade, which is in keeping with its historic surroundings, to its surprising contemporary-style interior design, which features an unusual wood-panelled ceiling. Alongside his wife Yolanda Rojo (the daughter of the founder), chef Juanjo Losada creates what could be described as cutting-edge Leonese cuisine, as part of which his visually creative dishes are built around the best local and seasonal ingredients. The only option here is a single tasting menu (with a wine-pairing option) that flies the flag for the region’s small-scale local producers and changes throughout the year. We were particularly impressed by the striking “bollo minero”, with creamy bacon in the middle and caviar on the outside.

Name: Pabú
Description: A restaurant that is definitely in vogue and one which continues to gain new fans – even the royal family celebrated a birthday here! Located close to the legendary Santiago Bernabéu football stadium, Pabú reflects the gourmet vision of Coco Montes, a Cordon Bleu chef who has worked in prestigious restaurants such as Arpège in Paris, under the baton of famous chef Alain Passard. His cooking is based around the purity of ingredients, hence his championing of micro-seasonal cuisine that changes daily in line with provisions from his suppliers and is highly focused on vegetables, with little protein, delicate textures and plenty of personality. It also highlights an extensive knowledge of classic French techniques and is centred around two surprise tasting menus dedicated to his parents: Bubú and Pate (the latter, with eight courses, can also be taken in half portions). The bread here is made with natural sourdough, while the selection of international cheeses is particularly impressive.

Name: Paca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Please note: relocated to Via delle Ginestre 45, Carmignano. This elegant restaurant reinterprets contemporary Italian cuisine through a meticulous selection of ingredients, sourced largely from small local producers and, where possible, from zero-kilometre supply chains. One of the standout specialities is Colonnata lard, often served alongside a fine selection of artisan breads, ranging from those made with rice flour to those made with chestnuts. A cuisine that focuses on the essence of flavour, complemented by impeccable service that helps to make the experience particularly enjoyable and memorable.

Name: Pajta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Pajta means ‘barn’, which is where it all began for Flóra and Ferenc – in the small barn beside this glass-fronted restaurant. The whole complex has a natural feel, from the beautiful meadow to the two-storey, nature-inspired forest lodges 1km down the road (they arrange transportation). Menus change with the seasons and perfectly reflect the area, championing produce from Őrség in historical Hungarian dishes. Fermenting and pickling are a feature, adding a welcome punch to the flavour-packed creations. Neighbouring Austria and Slovenia join Hungary for a tri-country wine pairing experience.

Name: Palace Garden
Address: Shop 306, 3F, Grand Lisboa Palace, Grand Lisboa Palace Resort, Rua do Tiro, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The room is the epitome of lavish maximalism and one wall is covered in a 35-metre-long Suzhou silk embroidery with a chrysanthemum theme. On the menu, ingredients from around the world are used to craft refined Cantonese dishes, including ancient, labour-intensive recipes. Steamed crab claw on egg custard with lobster bisque uses 2-kg of crustaceans from the Philippines. In the colder months, their snake soup warms the heart and soul.

Name: Palate
Address: 3F, 154 Dalmaji-gil 65 beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan, 48576, South Korea
Description: Palate offers contemporary French cuisine that is free-spirited and adventurous in style. Its sensuous fare is based on the culinary diversity experienced by Chef Kim Jae-hoon. Ever since he boldly opened this diner in Busan, his hometown, the chef has been taking up diverse epicurean challenges while injecting freshness into the restaurant’s concept. This progressive aspect of Palate is well reflected in the cuisine it serves today. When it comes to dining, Busan has much respect for the old and traditional. This urban dining landscape makes one wonder how the chef’s ever-evolving culinary experiments will translate into gastronomic revolutions.

Name: Palatial
Address: Av. da Independência 8, Arcos, Braga, 4705-162, Portugal
Description: This is an unusual project, as it reflects a family business’s investment in diversification, encompassing the world of swimming pools, haute cuisine, and premium accommodation (they also offer 7 suites). The spacious and eye-catching premises, at the southern exit of the town, surprise visitors with a sort of wine tasting bar where they celebrate the region’s finest wines. In its elegant dining room, run by a professional team, they offer an à la carte service and two tasting menus (Tradition and Innovation) that change with the seasons and draw from the finest national seasonal produce. Within its concept, which is based on Portuguese gastronomic tradition but revisited from a creative perspective, with certain licences taken to improve the recipes, we were captivated by the original combination of Sole and "Portuguese stew" as well as the Cheese, quince and hazelnut dessert, which play with temperatures and textures.

Name: Palodú
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive restaurant, just a few steps from the legendary Atarazanas market, is one of those restaurants you’ll love visiting thanks to its constant desire to improve. The couple in charge of the kitchen (Cristina Cánovas and Diego Aguilar), both of whom have trained in leading restaurants, have used the initials of their first names to come up with the concept of “Dual Cuisine” (this sense of duality can also be seen in Palodú’s dining rooms – one, with an open kitchen, decorated in black tones, the other dominated by the colour white). Their cooking is focused on two tasting menus called Alcazul and Palodú, both based around seasonal dishes and accompanied by a wine-pairing option. The intensely flavoured “sequence” of “red mullet - gazpachuelo – potato” served together is particularly recommended. Take a seat at the counter if you enjoy watching food being prepared in front of you.

Name: Palégrié Chez l'Henri
Address: 66 rue de la Tour, Autrans-Méaudre en Vercors, 38112, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As enthusiastic as ever, Guillaume Monjuré (who first came to our attention in Lyon and Corrençon-en-Vercors) plays host to guests in this family-owned barn, which has been renovated into a table d'hôte-style restaurant. Fanning the flames of his passion for cooking over an open fire, he has set up a wood-burning oven in full view of diners; he cooks absolutely everything in it, from bread first thing in the morning, to vegetables and fish during the meal. This is natural, primitive cuisine that is no less personal and creative for all that. He is able to elevate vegetables, herbs and fish from the local fish farm, in dishes such as his ikejime char, matured for a fortnight and accompanied by courgettes and herbs from the chef's garden. This free-spirited chef also makes forays into Mediterranean territory, with dishes such as blue crab served with lettuce, horseradish and lovage. The set menus are apt to change daily. Chrystel, who knows her wines like the back of her hand, will be happy to talk you through a fine selection that features plenty of organic and natural options. An authentic and appealing approach to life and to cooking.

Name: Pang's Kitchen
Address: 25 Yik Yam Street, Happy Valley, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: A household name in the neighbourhood since 2001, this restaurant wins many hearts with its traditional, often painstakingly made Cantonese cooking. This family business, now into the second generation, still impresses with its consistently well-made dishes. The signature baked fish tripe omelette in an earthenware casserole features Cantonese pork sausage that adds richness and wine aromas. Try the snake soup, and stir-fried sticky rice, too.

Name: Pangea
Address: Av. del Roble 660, Valle del Campestre, San Pedro Garza García, 66273, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: After 25 years of operation, Chef Guillermo González Beristáin’s flagship remains a standard bearer for Monterrey’s fine dining scene, offering skillful cooking that combines Mexican cuisine with accents from Asia and France. The stylish space offers diners a choice between an ample à la carte offering and a tasting menu that best highlights the kitchen’s talents. Flavorful dishes, characterized by a sense of balance and astute seasoning, range from a sweet tamal of winter squash paired with crème fraîche and caviar, to a dish of crisp-skinned quail with foie gras mousseline, pistachios, and cherries. Desserts end the meal on an elegant note, like a Pavlova filled with raspberry compote and a sorbet of lychee and white tea.

Name: Pangium
Address: Gallop Entrance, Singapore Botanic Gardens, 11 Gallop Road, 259015, Singapore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: The view of the lush green in the garden is one good reason to visit. But owner-chef Malcolm Lee's exquisite tasting menu that explores the untapped possibilities of Straits cuisine is what makes the experience of dining here unforgettable. Named after the plant that produces buah keluak seeds, a key ingredient in Peranakan cuisine, Pangium pays homage to family recipes passed down for generations with carefully crafted dishes that taste exceptional.

Name: Panorama - Cayenne
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This establishment has been run by the Fuchs family for 40 years, and these days, it is Rolf and Manuela Fuchs who are in charge. The modern, elegant restaurant atop Hartlisberg boasts not only a chic atmosphere but also a truly magnificent view of Thun and the mountains – the terrace is wonderful! The chef-patron's cuisine is no less of a draw. It is modern and clearly structured, yet classical in its foundations, making for bold and expressive dishes that are pared back to the essentials and packed with vibrant flavours. The four- or five-course set menu can be extended by up to two "surprise" courses on request. When it comes to the selection of ingredients, the approach is very much regional and local. The wine selection is also a plus, with recommendations provided by the friendly and knowledgeable waitstaff.

Name: Pantagruel
Description: Just a hop from the Palais Royal gardens, behind an engaging pale blue façade, Pantagruel is depicted by an eclectic interior of terracotta red, electric blue and Directoire chairs. Jason Gouzy, who hails from Rennes and trained at Ferrandi, l’Assiette Champenoise, Le Bristol and Le Baudelaire, crafts fun-loving, modern fare. A ‘gargantuan egg’ with a play on textures of rice and leeks, a croq’homard (lobster toastie), mousseline and bisque of Breton lobster illustrate the bang-on, crisp approach of this virtuoso chef. Slick, youthful, front-of-house team and a colourful mood set the scene in this venue that pays tribute to Rabelais, a famous French foodie!

Name: Paolo Griffa al Caffè Nazionale
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: A historic city restaurant, overlooking Aosta's main square, has been brought back to life by the passion of young chef Paolo Griffa. It offers colourful, balanced and contemporary cuisine, available in 3, 5 or 7-course tasting menus. Always attentive to the harmony of flavours and chromatic beauty of dishes, the chef demonstrates a growing skill in handling vegetables, as evidenced by the vegetarian dishes always on the menu. The service is of an excellent standard and the wine offerings of great depth. Of course, as the name suggests, some spaces are dedicated to excellent coffee, equipped with an excellent pastry corner, making this place recommended for any time of the day, from breakfasts to aperitifs!

Name: Paolo e Barbara
Description: A historic address in the heart of the city, this restaurant retains a charm of a bygone era and offers a seafood cuisine firmly rooted in its territory, placing the highest value on the quality of local produce. There is also modest but noteworthy self-production, including extra-virgin olive oil from the Val Nervia, which – among other offerings – accompanies the excellent snails served with an aromatic cream of twelve wild herbs. Among the first courses, the cappelletti filled with Sanremo prawns, delicately dressed with vegetable broth and saffron, stands out as a dish of great refinement and balance. In the dining room, Barbara guides guests through a selection of wines with considerable expertise, with a particular focus on Ligurian labels, whilst Paolo in the kitchen delivers a solid and coherent experience. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Paris Butter
Address: 166 Jervois Road, Herne Bay, Auckland, 1011, New Zealand
Description: Tucked away in an affluent neighbourhood, Paris Butter has an understated façade, in stark contrast with its elegant interior furnished in modern French style. Chefs Honeyman and Wijlens champion a season-driven tasting menu that embraces Kiwi produce harvested at its peak, underpinned by European techniques and Asian seasonings such as miso. Wine pairing options are available with all-New Zealand labels, or with picks from around the globe.

Name: Parsley Salon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The Park Lane Copenhagen hotel sits in the chic neighbourhood of Hellerup, and within its basement, you’ll find Allan Schultz’s intimate Parsley Salon, where beautifully crafted Danish oak furnishings sit beside shelves packed with cookery books. Allan’s finely balanced, classically inspired dishes showcase locally grown vegetables and seafood from Nordic waters alongside foraged berries and coastal plants, so you might find poached langoustine with seaweed and a sherry beurre blanc or North Sea cod with blue mussels, potato and parsley emulsion. Interesting wine and juice pairings accompany.

Name: Pascucci al Porticciolo
Address: Viale Traiano 85, angolo via Fiumara 2, Fiumicino, 00054, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Just steps from the harbour of Fiumicino, Pascucci al Porticciolo surprises with the unassuming elegance of a bright dining room, pale in tone and classical in atmosphere, attuned to the authentic character of the locality. The welcome extended by Vanessa Melis and her front-of-house brigade is impeccable: professional, spontaneous and capable of putting each guest at their ease. In the kitchen, Gianfranco Pascucci delivers one of the most convincing interpretations of so-called "produce-led cuisine", in which a technique of absolute precision is placed at the service of exceptional raw materials. Amberjack, king prawns, turbot and the rest of the catch impress through their freshness and quality, while the preparations eschew all virtuosity for its own sake, favouring balance, harmony and respect for the ingredient. Among the most memorable dishes, the white grouper tataki with curried herbs, barbecued escarole and green tomato cream stands out. This is a creation that evokes Asian suggestions without losing its Mediterranean identity.

Name: Pashà
Address: Contrada Torre Catena 874, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set within the evocative surroundings of a fourteenth-century masseria, nestled within a park of centuries-old trees, this venue presents one of the most interesting gastronomic experiences in the Puglian countryside near Polignano. At the time of our visit, the menu takes the form of a single tasting menu available in five or seven courses, through which Michele Spadaro interprets the flavours of regional tradition with creative verve. We are told that a more accessible option for the interior dining room is also forthcoming, designed for guests spending longer in this setting of great allure. The cellar is exceptional, counting over a thousand labels and featuring a striking communal table set among the bottles. A carefully managed service and an environment of great visual impact, enveloped in the green of the Puglian countryside, complete the experience.

Name: Pasta|Bar
Address: 16101 Ventura Blvd., Ste. 250, Encino, CA, 91436, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: A stylishly modern space hidden inside an unassuming strip mall, this hip concept's tasting menu is one for the books. Drinks and a snack kick things off in a well-appointed front bar and the staff is wonderfully engaging as they serve a host of delectable, hyper-local items. The eclectic cuisine travels beyond the borders of Italian tradition, offering up such creations as a single agnolotti tucked with braised oxtail, crispy onions and a Comté cheese espuma, or sunchoke gnocchi with Ibérico pluma and crispy sourdough breadcrumbs. A delicate, twirl of tagliatelle made from porcini powder is given an earthy boost with roasted mushrooms in a Madeira sauce. Desserts, like a bone marrow custard filled with blackberry granita and crisp meringue, are equally intriguing.

Name: Pastis Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Wend your way along narrow Rue Terral to this snug, attractively appointed restaurant and you will quickly find out why it is one of Montpellier’s most popular eateries! It is impossible to resist Daniel Lutrand’s cuisine, which is both inspired and inspiring, refined and refreshing, in a bid to showcase the region’s top producers. An example: confit celery in house-made Thai curry with green spinach and a curry-coconut cream or Ségala veal cutlet flanked by miso-laced confit leeks, seed cromesquis and veal gravy. Two sensibly priced lunchtime menus and a “surprise” menu in the evening, whose composition depends on the chef’s inspiration. Cheerful, enthusiastic service by manager and business partner Jean-Philippe Vivant. The stunning wine list with over 600 references is flanked by a savvily curated range of alcohol-free wines and cocktails.

Name: Patio
Description: Located in Vouliagmeni (a picturesque coastal area on the shores of the Saronic Gulf, half an hour from Athens), this restaurant occupies the charming inner courtyard of the luxurious Margi hotel. Here, in this verdant setting far from the hustle and bustle of the city, it is much easier to highlight the philosophy and the “farm to plate” concept that has been adopted by the Chef Panagiotis Giakalis. His proposal is divided into two tasting menus that showcase modern Greek cuisine of a high technical standard, with a special focus on the flavours of Greece and the Mediterranean in general, using ingredients (eggs, vegetables, fruit, olive oil, etc) sourced from his own farm whenever possible. The iconic “The Fish and the Farm” warrants a special mention as it has been on the menu since it first opened and is presented personally by the chef. At the end of the meal, guests are given a basil seed pencil which highlights the importance of sustainability and which can be planted at home.

Name: Paul Ainsworth at No.6
Address: 6 Middle Street, Padstow, PL28 8AP, United Kingdom
Description: Guests are put centre stage and are treated to a real experience at this restaurant set in a delightful Georgian townhouse. Paul Ainsworth has developed his own style over the years and the menus are a wonderful showcase for his considerable talents. The finest Cornish produce and well-honed classical techniques underpin the cooking, which is studded with playful creative touches – such as the brilliantly conceived "Yesterday's Scone" crossover course before dessert. Friendly, well-versed service helps to make your visit a memorable one.

Name: Paula
Address: Markt 88, Sankt Wolfgang im Salzkammergut, 5360, Austria
Description: Housed in Weisser Bär Hotel & Wirtshaus, right on Marktplatz, this trendy yet cosy little establishment is run by an enthusiastic restaurateur duo.
