Sebastian Leutgeb is a young chef who masterfully blends Austrian and French influences in his creative cuisine. Your friendly hostess and sommelier Miriam Grädler provides impeccable service. A six- to eight-course set menu is served, with dishes along the lines of "char, young turnips, saffron" and "Miéral pigeon in two servings". The name of the restaurant is a tribute to the chef's grandmother, Paula. Tip: In the summer season, on Wednesdays and Saturdays, local musicians put on a small concert in the village, which is well worth experiencing – you can also see and hear everything from the comfort of the restaurant.

Name: Pavus
Address: Grad Tabor Laško, Cesta na Svetino 23, Lasko, 3270, Slovenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The ascent to Grad Tabor castle in Laško, founded in the thirteenth century and, after centuries of history and varied use, transformed today into a gastronomic restaurant of romantic fascination, is well worth making. In this suggestive setting, self-taught chef Marko Pavčnik expresses a cuisine that is personal and unmistakable, little influenced by passing trends, and capable of celebrating the territory with creativity and contemporary sensitivity. Great attention is paid to quality: local ingredients, foraging, and whole-animal cookery. The dishes, with their clear and well-defined flavours, tell the story of Slovenia with elegance, as in the smoked trout with elderflower sauce. To appreciate the proposal fully, a tasting menu is recommended. The experience is completed by a rich wine list centred on Slovenian labels, among which the whites of Styria, a region renowned for wines of great character, stand out. In summer, the panoramic courtyard offers a truly singular atmosphere.

Name: Pavyllon London
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, Hamilton Place, Mayfair, London, W1J 7DR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Yannick Alléno's place among the pantheon of great French chefs is assured, and the Four Seasons in Mayfair was the chosen venue for his first foray into the UK’s dining scene. It’s a smart, spacious dining room, with lots of natural light and a focus on comfort – the large open kitchen, which is led by Chef Benjamin Ferra Y Castell, is skirted by a luxurious counter for those wanting a close-up view. The food is underscored by classic French recipes, but influences can range from Italy to North Africa to Japan. Ingredients are naturally from the luxury side of the ledger and set menus are the best way to go.

Name: Pavyllon Monte-Carlo, un restaurant de Yannick Alléno
Address: Square Beaumarchais, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
Description: Yannick Alleno’s gourmet counter food, after finding favour with Parisian city slickers, has set up shop in the Hermitage Hotel in Monte Carlo with the same sure-fire recipes. Namely, gourmet fare that boldly asserts a distinctive unorthodox culinary identity. The open kitchen faces the terrace and the impressive tasting counter in metallic wood, in an elegant blue colour scheme that echoes the nearby sea. In terms of food, the accent is on the seasons and wellbeing, anchored in plants, seafood and low-sugar desserts. In fine weather, meals are served on the Mediterranean garden patio commanding a view of the deep blue sea as a bonus.

Name: Pavyllon Paris
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Under the aegis of Yannick Alléno, the third Pavillon Ledoyen venture is a chic restaurant with, notably, a counter to seat 32. The cuisine is built on fine classic foundations, bolstered by international flavours and details. Pitch perfect, the food is refined and delicate – to be savoured in the smart yet relaxed ambience: an excellent time is sure to be had. Gorgeous terrace surrounded by greenery.

Name: Paznaunerstube
Description: Executive Chef Martin Sieberer has been overseeing the kitchens of this restaurant in the luxurious Trofana Royal holiday hotel since 1996, and it's fair to say he/it's become something of an institution. His two sons, Thomas and Michael, now support him as chefs, and together they use carefully selected ingredients to turn out contemporary dishes based on classic recipes. "Sea bass from Concarneau, potatoes, onions, pepper" or "French pigeon from head to toe, peppers, sweet potatoes" are excellent examples. You can choose between a surprise menu – comprising four, six or eight courses – and a six-, eight- or ten-course set menu, dubbed the "Royalmenü". The stylish and distinguished atmosphere smacks of Alpine sophistication. The service is unparalleled, with a well-coordinated and professional team cordially and attentively catering to diners' every desire. Wine lovers are in for a treat, as the cellar houses a remarkable selection of carefully selected high-calibre wines.

Name: Pea Porridge
Address: 28-29 Cannon Street, Bury St Edmunds, IP33 1JR, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away on a residential square, this neighbourhood restaurant is warmly and personally run by a husband and wife team, and the unusual name is a nod to the old town green which once stood out front. The daily changing menu of North African, Middle Eastern and Mediterranean dishes involves a range of ingredients cooked over charcoal. The sourdough flatbread fresh from the oven kicks things off perfectly and the unfussy dishes deliver bold, well-defined flavours which are skilfully executed. The esoteric wine list champions organic and natural wines, while the lunch menu provides great value.

Name: Pearl Dragon
Address: Shop 2111, 2F, Star Tower, Studio City, Estrada do Istmo, Cotai, Macau, Macau SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: No expense was spared in fitting out this upscale restaurant, whose recurring dragon motif and stunning floral chandelier in the foyer are the epitome of lavish. The menu is equally elegant and rich in flavour: the squab two ways is a must – the crispy skin deep-fried bird showcases the precision of Cantonese cooking while the version steeped in Chaozhou spiced marinade oozes savoury depth. The tea counter boasts over 50 premium teas.

Name: Pearl by Paul Proffitt
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Head for the Flesborg Fjord, and at the water’s edge you’ll find this early-20th-century villa boasting a cosy bar, parquet floors and light wood furnishings. After almost a decade working at Henne Kirkeby Kro, British-born Paul Proffitt set upon his own in this most idyllic spot on the opposite side of south Jutland; book a space in the glass-cubed ‘Doris’ to watch him up close. Modern cuisine marries local produce and a little playful childhood nostalgia, in dishes such as dripping served with a buttery brioche, aged dairy cow tartare or a surf 'n' turf of sirloin with oyster cream.

Name: Pedro Lemos
Description: Eating at this restaurant, facing the mouth of the Douro, is always a gratifying experience; not for nothing does it occupy a warehouse linked to the city’s naval history, and chef-owner Pedro Lemos introduces himself by saying: “If I feel I don’t fit into this world, it’s because I was born to create my own.” In this space, striking for both its minimalist atmosphere and the presence of large curtains that organise the interior (there’s a bar area where the first aperitifs are served and a beautiful main dining room), the chef champions a contemporary cuisine with strong classical roots, always elegant, using high-quality regional produce (eel, bivalves, red mullet...). Care to take a recommendation? It’s well worth visiting the wine cellar (you can choose wines that aren’t on the list) and hopping on the charming line 1 tram, which will take you along the riverbanks on a lovely route.

Name: Peix & Brases
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: (Temporarily closed for refurbishment) Located almost in front of the port, with the sound of seagulls as a backdrop, Peix & Brases has two distinct ambiences: the gastro-bar on the ground floor serving more informal fusion-style dishes that it calls Mediterrasian, and its gastronomic dining room on the first floor, with access to an attractive rooftop terrace. Here you’ll find a small, seafood-inspired à la carte focused on high-quality ingredients (notably featuring a section dedicated to rice dishes, one of the restaurant’s hallmarks) and two tasting menus: Origen and Recorrido Gastronómico. Don't miss the Dénia red prawns, boiled in seawater, the local way!

Name: Pelagos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Looking to escape the hustle and bustle of Athens? Head to the Four Seasons Astir Palace (three MICHELIN Keys), a luxury hotel south of the Greek capital, and make a reservation at Pelagos. This restaurant delights its guests both with its spacious terrace overlooking the Aegean Sea and with its refined Mediterranean-inspired offerings, featuring touches of Italian and French cuisine. In the kitchen, talented chef Luca Piscazzi uses modern techniques to showcase local ingredients. The end result is reflected in an à la carte and a tasting menu that combine magnificent dishes inspired by the country’s islands and by the chef’s own creations throughout his career. Fun fact: Sometimes, the menu becomes interactive and is guided by a unique deck of cards, each one dedicated to a seasonal ingredient waiting to be discovered (red prawns from Koilada, Aegean dentex fish, courgette, etc.). Shuffle the deck and let fate decide!

Name: Pelegrini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of the old town, the restaurant occupies Villa Pelegrini-Tambača, a Renaissance palazzo situated next to the Cathedral of St. James. Chef Rudolf Štefan, deeply knowledgeable about the region, distinguishes himself through constant pursuit of local products: he collaborates with top winemakers for exclusive wine production, makes his own olive oil, and prioritizes land and sea ingredients from Šibenik and its surroundings. Two tasting menus of four and six courses offer a modern reinterpretation of traditional Dalmatian cuisine with creative touches and refined presentations. Among the house signatures is lobster served on mushroom carpaccio with ricotta, sea grapes, and pickled cornichons: a surprising balance of sweetness and acidity. The wine list, with over 500 labels, is of considerable depth and breadth. In warmer months, dining is available along the external staircase with splendid views of the cathedral.

Name: Pentonbridge Inn
Description: There's an inviting, contemporary feel to this 18th-century Cumbrian inn that's situated so far north, it nearly crosses the Scottish border. If you time your visit right, you'll get a glimpse of a truly spectacular sunset. The adept kitchen team match the wonderful surroundings with ease, eschewing unnecessary flourishes and instead delivering beautiful balance and depth of flavour with just a few ingredients – as evidenced by superb vadouvan-spiced scallops. Extend your visit with a stay in one of the smart bedrooms.

Name: Per Me Giulio Terrinoni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a few metres from Via Giulia in the heart of the historic city, this restaurant is home to chef Giulio Terrinoni who, over the years, has built a reputation for his superb fish and seafood cuisine which he serves in classic, unfussy style with a focus on top-quality ingredients (meat and vegetarian options also feature on the menu). If you’d like to watch the chef at work and experience a more creative surprise menu, book one of the two seats at the counter facing the open-view kitchen.

Name: Perceel
Address: Dorpsstraat 3, Capelle aan den IJssel, 2902 BC, Netherlands
Description: Flowers are a thing at Perceel. They add a vibrant touch to the modern interior design, which draws on the building's old-world character. Outside, there is a terrace right by the Ijssel River, as well as a herb and flower garden. Flowers are not only part of the decor; Jos Grootscholten also likes to add them as a final flourish to his dishes. He shows you what it means to be in perfect harmony with nature. Herbs from his garden and zesty notes are at the heart of his cooking. The beef tartare with kimchi and sweet-and-sour cornichons is a signature dish. Another standout: crispy veal sweetbreads with cauliflower and hazelnut, served with an exquisite lavender-infused veal jus and a potato espuma. At Perceel, the food is exciting and meticulously prepared. The chef's taste for experimentation extends to the drinks as well – he creates intriguing kombucha-based pairings to complement his dishes. Sharon, your ever-obliging hostess will be happy to walk you through the tempting à la carte menu.

Name: Pertinence
Description: Ryunosuke Naito and Kwen Liew met at Restaurant Antoine in 2011. Ryunosuke is Japanese and has worked in some of the top houses of Paris (Taillevent, Meurice) and Kwen is Malaysian. Together they have created this elegant minimalist setting, depicted by light wood and Knoll chairs, whose understated, cosy vibe is perfectly in keeping with their characters and ethos. In the kitchen, they craft market-fresh dishes overflowing in powerful flavours, brushing the cobwebs off French culinary tradition along the way. Spot-on cooking as the name suggests…

Name: Petit Amour
Description: Eike Iken and Monique Lingg are your dedicated hosts. The chef-patron skilfully weaves together modern, classic French and Nordic influences (his cod, mussels, curry and cauliflower, for instance, is delicious). Knowledgeable staff provide cordial service, and the chefs come to the table to present the dishes that form the four- to six-course set menu. To accompany the food, there are carefully selected wine pairings, plus a premium option; the high-calibre house-made alcohol-free accompaniment is also recommended. The small restaurant with its 12 tables has a pleasant, almost intimate atmosphere that makes you feel right at home. Tip: Be sure to book a table!

Name: Petrus
Address: 56F, Island Shangri-La Hotel, Pacific Place, Supreme Court Road, Admiralty, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Heavy drapes at the windows, thick carpets and elegantly laid tables give this restaurant the look of a grand Parisian salon – but here you also get fabulous harbour views. The French cooking, however, shows a certain modernity; the menu is ingredient-led with the luxury ingredients coming from as far as France or sometimes no further than Hong Kong Island. The wine cellar is notable too and includes 45 vintages of Château Pétrus dating back to 1928.

Name: Pfefferschiff
Description: Just outside Salzburg, Iris and Jürgen Vigné's establishment offers an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. In a lovely 17C parish house, dine in one of the charming, cosy rooms, outside on the attractive terrace or in a lounge. The cuisine is characterised by a bold and inventive spirit, infused with a personal touch that shines through in dishes like the foie gras terrine with cauliflower and passion fruit; a symphony of textures and flavours that showcases the chef's mastery of contrasting elements. When it comes to the quality of his ingredients, Jürgen Vigné sets great store by working closely with nature and is mindful of the produce he buys in. There are two set menus, one vegetarian and each comprising five, seven or eight courses. Alternatively, you can opt for a five-course set menu that varies according to what the market has to offer. Iris Vigné is a natural-born hostess who ensures that her guests feel at home. The well-curated wine list focuses on Austrian labels. They also cultivate a vineyard in the Kamptal.

Name: Philipp
Description: For more than 20 years, Heike and Michael Philipp have been dedicated to keeping their guests happy. The very popular "Classique" set menu showcases a modern take on classic cuisine in four or six courses. The cooking is remarkably precise and bold, seamlessly incorporating Mediterranean and Asian accents. A standout example is the house-made agnolotti with lightly smoked mushrooms, miso and Périgord truffle. The carte blanche surprise menu is available as an alternative on Sat and Sun lunchtime and Sun evening. When it comes to wine, you can rely entirely on the recommendations of your extremely charming and accomplished hostess and sommelier, Heike Philipp. The setting is also worth a mention: Housed in a picture-perfect 400-year-old Renaissance palace in the middle of a pretty winegrowing village, this stylish and cosy restaurant exudes historical flair. In addition, two suites and one double room are available for overnight stays.

Name: Philipp Soldan
Description: The three lovingly restored historical houses in the middle of the charming old town are really something to behold. Here, the tasteful Hotel Sonne has various dining options, including this restaurant. The fine dining restaurant in the basement of the centuries-old Stadtweinhaus is chic, modern and pleasingly laid-back. (If you are not coming from the hotel, you get to the restaurant via Untermarkt.) In the open kitchen, Erik Arnecke oversees the preparation of a five-course set menu. Dishes such as Ederbergland venison saddle with butternut squash cannelloni, tamarind, pickled beech mushrooms, and a purple cinnamon leaf jus highlight his refined technique and well-judged flavour combinations. This is complemented by a superbly curated international wine list. Tip: Come on a Sunday for the three- or four-course lunch set menu. In case you were wondering, Philipp Soldan is the sculptor, whose carved wooden figures adorn the town hall.

Name: Philippe Fauchet
Description: Philippe Fauchet enjoys straying from his comfort zone and since 1996, he has been finetuning his distinctive signature in this snug yet buzzy eatery deep in the Liege countryside. An artisan at heart, he crafts everything from scratch, including the succulent bread. While impossible to sum up in a single word, let’s say his style is quirky and scattered with international accents, but always with a firm focus on local ingredients and veggies, thanks to partnerships with regional farmers. His dad’s market garden also frequently supplies the kitchen in veg and herbs. All of which is combined in intriguing, jazzy, amusing recipes, illustrated by different preparations of Lothar Vilz veal, including medium rare loin with a powerful gravy and a scattering of tangy fresh herbs, but also a dish inspired by vitello tonnato, sliced wafer thin and served with subtly acidic shimeji mushrooms. The chef plays with contrasts and textures in a bid to constantly titillate and tease our tastebuds. The (mainly Gallic) wine list and food-wine pairings are fully in line with this amazing experience. You can expect boldly unorthodox, crisp, distinctive cuisine.

Name: Philippe Meyers
Address: rue Doyen Van Belle 6, Braine-l'Alleud, 1420, Belgium
Description: Philippe and Valerie Meyers are sincere, warm-hearted folks, adjectives that also depict the interior design of their dinky eatery which showcases a magnificent collection of Michelin Guides. Valérie plays the role of hostess with great spontaneity and adores waxing lyrical about the chef’s passion for Walloon produce and his ability to tell a tale with just a few ingredients. Take for example his signature dish of speck, cooked for 17 hours, which he pairs with lemon-flavoured Eau de Villée, seared, still translucent langoustine tails and a gutsy sauce of hoisin and confit lemons. Alternatively, how about a lovingly reduced (and highly addictive) gravy rich in suave green pepper notes to enhance a dish of crispy sweetbread? Authentic generosity is the baseline of the attractively priced menu that will enable you to make your choice from a wide range of thoroughly tempting dishes. Philippe Meyers is seventh heaven for foodies!

Name: Piano35
Description: On the ground level of what has become one of the symbols of the Turin skyline, the Intesa Sanpaolo skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, there is the entrance to the restaurant. From here, a lift takes you quickly up to a height of 150 metres, but before taking your seat, it’s worth stopping off at the panoramic terrace, which offers a splendid view of the city. In the bright dining room surrounded by the conservatory, the menu is organised into three tasting menus: one dedicated to Piedmont, one inspired by the cuisine and flavours of Italy, which also features seafood dishes such as turbot with a sauce of saffron, rosemary and candied lemon, and a third menu that is vegetarian. At lunchtime, however, the menu takes on a more informal feel, thanks to a bistro-style offering that is simpler and more straightforward.

Name: Piao-Xiang
Description: With ‘Old Sichuan’ as its guiding principle, the restaurant reinterprets and refines the flavours of Sichuan’s past. Each course draws inspiration from Chinese history and its notable figures. Dish names are written in two kanji characters, inviting guests to imagine their flavours. ‘Furong’ takes its cue from the hibiscus, the official flower of Chengdu, while ‘Guifei’ incorporates the wine favoured by the famed Tang-era beauty Yang Guifei. The chef’s passion is thoughtfully conveyed through the manager’s explanations.

Name: Picchi
Address: Rua Oscar Freire 533, São Paulo, 01426-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If you have a craving for a good bowl of pasta, book a table at Picchi, an Italian restaurant located on the ground floor of the Regent Park hotel in the Jardins district with its upscale boutiques and art galleries. Here, chef Pier Paolo Picchi looks back to his childhood memories to create highly interesting cuisine that is showcased in enticing dishes based around classic Italian recipes and, in some cases, a more innovative approach that makes full use of the best seasonal Brazilian ingredients. The à la carte, which includes the traditional gnocchi, spaghetti, tortelli, pappardelle etc, is complemented by three set menus: one specially created for aficionados of Italian pasta called Tutto Pasta; a second called Tradizione; and a third (Picchi) which has more of a gastronomic feel. During the evening, the space takes on a more romantic atmosphere and offers a broad selection of Italian and French wines!

Name: Pico Velasco
Description: Located in the heart of the Parque Natural de las Marismas de Santoña, Victoria y Joyel, between the green mountains and the Cantabrian Sea, the Pico Velasco boutique hotel is a superb example of 17th-century Cantabrian civil architecture. In the tastefully renovated interior, Inés Aguirreburualde and award-winning chef Nacho Solana showcase a traditionally based modern cuisine that always aims to highlight the full value of local and seasonal ingredients. Choose between two tasting menus: Albiar (which translates as “sunrise”), and Sincio (a Cantabrian expression that is used to denote a desire or craving). What sort of dishes will you find? Some lovely starters (Anchovy Platter) and small plates such as Alubias marinas or the so-called Lonja del Cantábrico, featuring fish, vegetables and seaweed.

Name: Pied à Terre
Address: 34 Charlotte Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 2NH, United Kingdom
Description: Over the decades, few parts of London have seen more restaurants come and go than Charlotte Street, but one constant over that period has been David Moore’s Pied à Terre. Reinventions have kept things fresh over time, be that a new colour scheme or the embracing of plant-based cooking with a serious vegan offering. The classically based dishes are seasonal and colourful, showing off top-notch ingredients in harmonious combinations, such as Welsh lamb with basil, anchovy, girolles and a top-drawer red wine reduction with red currants.

Name: Pierre
Address: 20F, InterContinental Osaka, 3-60 Ofukacho, Kita-ku, Osaka, 530-0011, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Freshness is number one with the chef of Pierre, so he focuses on ingredients grown and raised in Japan. The menu only lists the ingredients, encouraging guests to give their imaginations free rein. Japanese seasonings such as mustard and chilli peppers mixed with yuzu zest lend a distinctive accent. French cooking techniques are married with Japanese ingredients, which are then prepared with a light touch. Spellbinding views from the spacious dining room high in a tall building add to the ambience.

Name: Pieters Restaurant
Description: Dining at Pieter and Paula's cheerful restaurant feels a bit like coming home. The welcoming interior is the perfect setting for culinary indulgence, and the hospitality truly comes from the heart. Chef Pieter brings a wealth of experience and a keen intuition to his cooking. No frills – just pure classical finesse, expertly executed and spiced up with a dash of playful originality. For instance, he drizzles a succulent fillet of sea bass with a light white wine sauce with a little oyster liquor added to give it a gentle tang. An intense fish broth and spiced focaccia make this hearty dish complete. This cuisine is down to earth and features harmonious combinations and top-quality ingredients – you might even be tempted to lick your plate clean! The range of French and Italian wines certainly has the perfect pairing in store. Foodies find their place at Pieters Restaurant.

Name: Pilgrim
Description: After two years at Duende in Nîmes, Masaki Nagao is back on a pilgrimage to the capital as he breathes new life into this establishment. In the wake of Vantre and Le Clarence, the Japanese chef signs a crisp, modern, subtly inventive Gallic repertory guided by the seasons. He avows a weakness for briny shellfish, that he adds raw, cooked and in broth to structure his culinary score. You may sample a veggie composition on a carrot, radish and turnip theme, laced with a shellfish consommé, or sashimi of first-class scallops flanked by pear, smoked ricotta and Castelfranco. More concise menu at lunchtime.

Name: Piment
Description: Beyond the lovely interior decor in warm tones and the friendly, competent service, it is first and foremost Wahabi Nouri's cuisine that sets this restaurant apart. You can really feel his passion for food! His cooking owes its personal touch to his respect for his heritage: Nouri comes from Casablanca and incorporates subtle North African nuances. Spices are a constant presence in the set menus and merge harmoniously with French influences. The result is a sophisticated and finely balanced interplay of flavours. One particularly exciting feature is the chef's surprise main course, which changes every day. A vegetarian version of the set menu is also available. Tip: The cosy atmosphere makes this an excellent spot for a date.

Name: Pin Ning Fu
Address: 39F, The Ritz-Carlton, 18 Zhongshan Road, Xuanwu, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The views of Xuanwu Lake and Mt Zijin are beautiful to behold, but the light-filled open kitchen, where the experienced chef prepares updated Huaiyang and Nanjing classics as well as seasonal dishes, also catches the eye. The crystal pork aspic boasts meaty flavour and a bouncy texture, with vinegar pearls providing mini explosions of tartness. The thinly shredded tofu in umami-laden Wensi tofu soup with crabmeat is testament to impressive knife skills.

Name: Pine
Address: Vallum Farm, Military Road, East Wallhouses, NE18 0LL, United Kingdom
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at Cal and Siân Byerley's rustic restaurant, where they're all about showcasing Northumbrian ingredients. Cal knows the local area intimately, plucking fresh ingredients from the kitchen garden and leading his team on foraging missions. He and the chefs use this produce with skill and originality, in dishes such as the brilliant fondant cake made using the rare dryad saddle mushroom. The wine flight – including several English wines – is worth going for, and they also make their own juices, tonics and teas.

Name: Pineapple and Pearls
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Pineapple and Pearls continues to provide a theatrical experience, where oversized Champagne bottles, balloons, pop music and playful tableside presentations create an atmosphere closer to an extravagant dinner party than a traditional tasting menu restaurant. The cooking draws inspiration from nostalgia and luxury ingredients, often presented with a sense of humor and deliberate excess. Courses may range from theatrical bites, like the beggar’s purse with caviar and crème fraîche, to more whimsical reinterpretations such as walnut lobster inspired by honey walnut shrimp. Throughout the meal, the service team enthusiastically narrates the restaurant’s many references and stories, while cocktails and wine pairings remain central to the overall concept.

Name: Pingjiangsong
Address: 54 Daru Lane, Gusu, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Tucked away in the Pingjiang historic quarter, this restaurant was remodelled from an ancient mansion encompassing the quintessence of classical Suzhou garden and architecture. Similarly, the season-driven menu is based heavily on Suzhou culinary traditions, enlivened by modern twists. Mantis shrimps with soft roe are dressed in fermented rice lees marinade and topped with caviar. The duck soup with ham and fox nuts presents rich flavours and deep umami.

Name: Pipe and Glass
Address: West End, South Dalton, HU17 7PN, United Kingdom
Description: Look for the church spire to help you navigate through the maze of country lanes that lead to this charming 15th-century pub, which was originally the gatehouse of Dalton Park. The dishes are generous in both size and flavour, refining and elevating pub classics and comforting favourites – such as the terrific rabbit, pancetta and duck liver boudin blanc or the house take on a fish pie – thanks to top-notch ingredients and the kitchen's keen sense of balance. The charming team ensure everyone is looked after with a smile, and smart bedrooms add a luxurious edge.

Name: Pipero Roma
Address: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II 250, Rome, 00186, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated opposite the church of Santa Maria in Vallicella (known to locals as Chiesa Nuova or new church), this restaurant is named after its owner Alessandro Pipero. Ciro Scamardella, a young chef from Campania who is not yet in his forties, is at the helm in the kitchen, where he prepares modern and creative meat and fish dishes with a focus on the seasons (the beef with spinach, bay leaf and black garlic sauce is particularly good), including a few specialities from his native region. His recipes feature ingredients such as rapini, escarole and lemons and his beautifully presented cuisine demonstrates a continuous search for balance and colour. Front of house, friendly Achille Sardiello leads a team that is fully focused on the needs of guests.

Name: Plaisance by Mauro Colagreco
Address: 1F, 1 Duddell Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Mother of pearl trimmings, shades of turquoise and a sculpted whirlpool of metallic fish set the ocean scene. The seafood-led menu delivers spellbinding dishes that showcase the best ingredients from around the world alongside local vegetables, all finessed with solid French technique and a healthy dose of creativity. House-made sauces are one of the highlights, as is the extensive wine list. The open kitchen puts on an entertaining show.

Name: Plates London
Address: 320 Old Street, Shoreditch, London, EC1V 9DR, United Kingdom
Description: There’s an appropriately earthy, natural vibe to this elegant restaurant dedicated to promoting plant-based cuisine. The slate floor, warm hues and rustic plastering help it feel stripped-back yet stylish, with some counter seating providing another on-trend touch. Chef Kirk Haworth – who owns Plates with his sister Keeley – brings his strong classical technique to bear on inventive and inviting vegan dishes that give vegetables the respect they deserve. The signature maitake mushroom with black bean mole is superb, while desserts like 'Flavours of Banoffee Pie' are equally likely to satisfy.

Name: Plumed Horse
Address: 14555 Big Basin Way, Saratoga, CA, 95070, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This location has housed a Plumed Horse since 1952, though the current iteration, approaching its second decade, is undoubtedly its most impressive. An elegant, comfortable space serves as the culinary stage for Chef Peter Armellino, who delivers his own take on Californian cuisine. Served either as a longer set tasting menu or a multicourse prix fixe with a variety of options, offerings change with the seasons, though the luxurious black pepper and parmesan soufflé with uni and Dungeness crab sauce is considered an essential. House-made pastas, as in pappardelle with beef cheek ragu and stracciatella, are appealing, though the kitchen navigates meat, seafood and vegetables with equal aplomb. A world-class collection of wines (visible in their glass cellar) is a worthy accompaniment.

Name: Poemas by Hermanos Padrón
Address: León y Castillo 227, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, 35005, Spain
Location: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
Description: A dazzling dining experience both in terms of the elegant setting and the gastronomic cuisine on offer in the exclusive and historic Santa Catalina hotel, a Royal Hideaway Hotel, in the heart of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. At the helm you’ll find chef Adrián García, from nearby Arucas, who has been superbly trained by the Padrón brothers (Juan Carlos and Jonathan) and who recreates the flavoursome cuisine of these award-winning chefs along with all of their renowned creativity. This dining space, which has its own separate entrance next to the hotel piano-bar (where a pianist provides the musical backdrop), boasts a refined and classical interior design with a profusion of wood that comes as a pleasant surprise. The Poemas tasting menu (on which we particularly enjoyed the impressively presented prawns with a prawn head toffee and shiitake mushrooms) is complemented by the more concise Clásicos menu, however both menus feature some of the Padrón brothers’ signature dishes.

Name: Poetry‧Wine (Dongsanhuan Middle Road)
Address: 61 Dongsanhuan Middle Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, 10020, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A high ceiling and red brick walls set the scene in the industrial-style dining room, whose rough raw vibe is attenuated by modern sculptures and paintings. Their signature juicy and tender fish head is nicely braised in an aromatic brown sauce. 40-day-old roast duck is chargrilled to perfection and exquisitely plated. Save room for creamed yam and osmanthus sweet soup. Sensible prices and a well-curated wine list add to the appeal.

Name: Poggio Rosso
Address: Località San Felice, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Set in the heart of the Chianti hills, Borgo San Felice Resort offers an experience that captures all the charm of the most authentic Tuscany, amid vineyards, olive groves and an atmosphere of great elegance. In this refined and relaxing setting, Stelios Sakalis presents a culinary experience that stems from the fusion of Tuscan culinary heritage and the wealth of experience the chef has gained in leading European kitchens. The dishes combine technique, balance and a contemporary sensitivity, enriched by references to his Mediterranean roots. The experience is rounded off by attentive and well-organised service, which guides guests with professionalism and discretion in a setting of great charm.

Name: Point
Description: Originality is demonstrated here through ingredients from each season and classic techniques. Omakase set menus feature refined, beautiful arrangements, with light flavours to suit a modern sensibility. The name declares that the house is a gathering point, bringing together everyone and everything else involved in food and restaurants. The site chosen for its relaunch was where Point first started. Anticipation is building for this fresh turning point.

Name: Pollen
Description: As you explore the winding lanes of Avignon, you may come upon this attractive restaurant with a large open-plan kitchen. The chefs deliver the food to the table themselves, while you drink up the savvy tips of an enthusiastic sommelier, who is something of a connoisseur of biodynamic wines. Mathieu Desmarest crafts a surprise menu depicted by legible, pared-down, balanced dishes, courtesy of seasonal produce sourced from local suppliers, enabling him to make the most of this cornucopia of impeccable ingredients (octopus, bluefin tuna, pigeon). The subtle and creative recipes and marriages of bold flavours effortlessly win the hearts of diners.

Name: Pont-Neuf
Description: Chic and cosy, the Pont Neuf, dripping in Flemish good taste, sports a dockside terrace that is just the ticket to soak up the infectious buzzy vibe of this trendy neighbourhood (weather permitting). Dominique Leroy pampers her guests as she shares her love of Italian wines and there is always a bottle of red Barbera d’Alba open for a glass among friends. Chef Tommy Bocklandt’s culinary score demonstrates a distinct preference for North Sea produce. His cooking focuses on preserving the purity of the main ingredients, leaving the sauces and side dishes to add nuance in a repertory that is traditional, but distinctive. Examples include immaculately poached brill, paired with a coulis of green peas, a medley of crunchy dry veggies, slices of grapefruit for a fresh tangy edge and a delicate lemon-laced stoemp of mashed veggies. Fish, whether cooked in stock, braised or fried until golden in butter, is taken to a whole new level thanks to this high-flying chef. The only challenge is to make your choice from the extensive à la carte menu or the suggestions of the day!

Name: Porcino
Description: Inside the modern Badia Hill hotel, patron Marco Verginer offers two tasting menus: one focused on seasonality, the other inspired by his creativity, featuring ingredients such as Wagyu beef produced in Alto Adige. The pairings are flavorful and lively, with extensive use of vegetables, often from the home garden. The result is an excellent dining experience served in a contemporary setting surrounded by glass walls that offer splendid views of the surrounding landscape. The menu presents a succession of mountain territory references combined with Mediterranean and international touches in highly elaborate dishes.

Name: Porte Neuf
Description: Among Detmold's restaurants, this spot on the outskirts of the Old Town is a fantastic find. Chef-patron Daniel C Fischer presents ambitious dishes that meld French and Far Eastern elements with a modern twist. The set menu comes in a four- or six-course format, and can be extended to nine courses with advance notice. The wonderful food is complemented by dedicated, friendly service and expert wine recommendations. The chefs bring their dishes to your table personally. The intimate restaurant's chic, modern design creates a warm and inviting atmosphere. There is also a lovely terrace for an aperitif, digestif or coffee.

Name: Portland
Address: 113 Great Portland Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1W 6QQ, United Kingdom
Description: The cooking at Portland respects the principles of sourcing and seasonality; in fact, the menu is often reprinted after lunch as ingredients are used up and replaced by different ones. The kitchen believes in doing as little as possible to the raw ingredients to allow their natural flavours to come through, and dishes are never over-crowded, with every component there to enhance another – like the rich rolled lamb loin lifted by a little anchovy and fresh tarragon. The pared-down look of the room matches the understated food.

Name: Pottkind
Description: Enrico Sablotny and Lukas Winkelmann, the duo who run this little restaurant, are from the Ruhr Valley – hence the name! In the kitchen, first-rate ingredients are transformed into distinctly original, creative compositions. Skilfully combined flavours and harmoniously balanced contrasts are particularly evident in dishes such as "Crevette rose, young almonds, fig leaf & fermented asparagus" and "Miéral pigeon, radicchio, elderberries & liver bread". The carte blanche set menu never fails to surprise. Excellent service comes courtesy of very attentive, competent and charming waitstaff, contributing to the pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere. The seats at the counter overlooking the open kitchen are especially popular. In summer, soak up the lively atmosphere of Cologne's Südstadt neighbourhood on the terrace.

Name: Pourquoi Pas
Address: Hôtel Castelbrac, 17 avenue George-V, Dinard, 35800, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of Hotel Castelbrac is named after the boat of Commander Charcot, a famous polar explorer. The chef’s score bears witness to his fondness for seafood presented like a carte blanche theme menu. Cosy dining room and panoramic terrace overlooking the sea with Saint Malo on the horizon.

Name: Prairial
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Gaëtan Gentil's new restaurant in the Confluence neighbourhood is housed in a building that is eco-responsible from floor to ceiling, and that includes the French oak tables. From the open kitchen in the middle of the space, he creates his seasonal cuisine that highlights the produce of the Rhône Valley terroir, using herbs and wild plants to great effect. This creative, instinctive yet carefully thought-out cooking is based on the elevation of ingredients, which are subject to numerous variations and enhanced by sauces packed with flavour. All his chosen suppliers share the same commitment to the environment: permaculture market gardeners, more sustainable livestock farming, wild or more appropriately reared freshwater fish. The 950 organic and natural wines on the wine list follow suit, slotting into a meal that is delicious but does not come at the expense of the planet.

Name: Pramerl & the Wolf
Description: This former pub in Vienna's ninth district is now a great casual fine dining restaurant. In a pleasingly laid-back and intimate setting, diners receive attentive service from Wolfgang "the Wolf" Zankl-Sertl and his team. The cuisine, inspired by modern trends, is bold and replete with well-balanced contrasts and appealing textures. A shining example is the carbonara made with calamari, smoked eel and Parmesan – entirely pasta-free! The surprise menu, prepared with exceptional ingredients, can be paired with either wine or alcohol-free options. On Wed and Thu, dinner service begins at 7pm; on Fri and Sat, there are two seatings: "Early Bird" 6-8pm and "Prime Time" from 8.30pm. Tip: Take the U4 underground line to get here.

Name: President
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: From the kitchen emerges a personal reinterpretation of Campanian traditions, which in certain details – such as the *siligineus* bread, inspired by recipes of ancient Rome – draws roots from distant eras. The dishes, always carefully considered in both flavour and presentation, are arranged across several tasting menus, with the option of freely composing one’s own journey, also from the à la carte selection. We followed the thread of the sea, appreciating preparations such as the “Rosso Pompeiano”, in which red mullet and beetroot engage in an elegant dialogue, and the salt cod acqua pazza, interpreted in a more contemporary key; but the land-based offering is equally distinguished by its solidity and quality. In the dining room, direction is entrusted to the expertise and courtesy of the chef’s wife, ready to suggest well-judged wine pairings, with the option of tasting notable labels by the glass as well. Alongside her, the new generation of a family that has made hospitality and fine cooking a true vocation is beginning to make its mark.

Name: Press
Address: 587 St. Helena St., Saint Helena, CA, 94574, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set just off Highway 29, Press offers a composed expression of contemporary Californian dining in a grand Wine Country setting. The soaring dining room, anchored by a fireplace and warm wood tones, feels elegant without any stiffness, making it well suited to long, unhurried meals. The cooking favors clarity and precision, allowing pristine ingredients to lead. Dishes like charcoal-grilled lobster, ricotta gnudi finished with a tableside pour of consommé and American wagyu rib cap show a kitchen confident in balance and restraint, not excess. Desserts, including a milk-chocolate mousse, reflect the same disciplined hand. An extraordinary, Napa-centric wine program remains a defining pillar of the experience.

Name: Prezioso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Leaving Merano behind, a panoramic road that winds through apple orchards, chestnut groves and vineyards leads within a few kilometres to Castel Fragsburg, a historic seventeenth-century residence immersed in greenery. Here, amid the charm of South Tyrolean aristocratic architecture and an understated alpine elegance, the Prezioso restaurant finds its home. In the warmer months, the terrace suspended above the valley offers a spectacular view that contributes greatly to the evocative quality of the experience. The beauty of the setting is matched by a solid cuisine firmly rooted in the local area, built around its produce and clean, precise flavours. Freshwater fish such as Arctic char and trout appear frequently in the tasting menus, alongside preparations that celebrate the quality of the meats. Among the most convincing dishes, the veal served in two acts: first accompanied by roasted onion, tarte tatin and meat jus, then with an intense sweetbread served with onion cream and wild herbs, a mouthful of real character and gustatory depth.

Name: Primo Restaurant
Description: Primo Restaurant is the place where contemporary, refined cuisine – deeply rooted in the Apulian region – takes shape, skilfully blending aesthetic appeal with intense flavours. The menu features a number of tasting menus of varying lengths, while those who prefer to choose freely can opt for the ‘signature’ dishes – those that have proved most popular since the restaurant opened. Among these, the extraordinary Gallipoli-style scapece ravioli with anchovies, beurre blanc and saffron is particularly worth mentioning – an ideal blend of tradition and contemporary flair. Each menu showcases creative, technically skilful and balanced cuisine, making this restaurant one of the region’s most interesting gastronomic destinations.

Name: Principe Cerami
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Massimo Mantarro presents a cuisine that interprets Sicily with contemporary sensitivity, without losing its connection to the local area. Clean flavours, vivid colours, and refined pairings accompany the guest on an ideal journey through the island, from the sea to the hills of the interior and through to the suggestions of Etna. Seasonality guides each offering: vegetables, fruit and aromatic herbs take on a central role in creative and harmonious dishes where technique, elegance and exploration bring out the very best of Sicily's exceptional raw materials.

Name: Procaccini
Address: Via Giulio Cesare Procaccini 33, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: Talented chef Emin Haziri, originally from Kosovo but raised in Italy and with significant professional experience behind him, now signs a line of contemporary and personalised cuisine. Alongside the more creative and imaginative offerings we find another with raw seafood, from oysters to caviar, from Sicilian shrimp to scampi. In the elegant and refined dining room with harmonious colours and fine furnishings, the open kitchen and marble counter with velvet stools stand out. The restaurant also has the soul of a cocktail bar where you are led once you enter for a welcome drink, before sitting down accompanied by live piano and vocal background music. And, as if that were not enough, kudos to the good Eduardo, sommelier and maître who will guide you through the wine selection, which is not very wide, but well conceived. We had pleasure in pairing a Mazzara red shrimp with a 2023 Etna Graci, fresh and mineral.

Name: Prodigi
Description: The first thing to attract your attention at Prodigi is its name, created from the first syllable of three neighbouring streets (Provença, Diagonal and Girona).In this contemporary-style restaurant, the à la carte remains faithful to seasonal ingredients despite its concise nature and extols the virtues of traditional Catalan cuisine which it has successfully brought up to date. It is complemented by two set menus (one a three-course meal only available at lunchtime during the week, and a second more extensive tasting menu-style option). Chef Jordi Tarré, who is renowned for his highly elegant dishes with a traditional base and nuanced international influences, is constantly looking to surprise his diners, which is why he changes up the dishes depending on the season. On our last visit, we really liked his squid and sobrassada rice with squid and lime slices, wasabi emulsion and marine sprouts!

Name: Project
Description: Cameron and Anna Irving are the husband-and-wife team behind this cosy restaurant and, along with the help of their friendly team, will make you feel particularly well looked after during your time here. The room itself has a simple appeal, keeping the focus firmly on cooking that comes with a seafood and game bias, as well as Japanese overtones. Choose between a long and short tasting menu, where well-balanced dishes could include the likes of sashimi of langoustine with strawberry vinegar and pickled roe, followed by wild Swedish duck with blueberry miso, perilla emulsion and roast chicken jus.

Name: Protégé
Address: 250 California Ave., Palo Alto, CA, 94306, USA
Description: Chef Anthony Secviar and Master Sommelier Dennis Kelly are both alums of The French Laundry, but although the service is adroit (and the wine list excellent), this sleek modern space is far from stuffy. Likewise, expect thoughtful, well-balanced cuisine that shows refinement without being precious. The dining room's multicourse tasting menu includes the likes of Pacific sablefish with sweet onion dashi, 9-layer morel mushroom lasagna with Madeira sauce, and Flannery Beef with green garlic gnocchi. An à la carte menu is on offer in the lounge—think brick chicken with piperade, capers, and chorizo—plus a dessert trolly that features excellent tarts and cookies.

Name: Provenance
Description: Chef Nicholas Bazik and his team know exactly what they’re doing in this historic row house. In full view of the counter, they deliver a high-wire, high-stakes performance defined by precision, harmony and, of course, taste. Korean and French influences come and go with this elaborate tasting menu where special soys, vibrant oils and glossy sauces give wonderful dimension to pristine seafood and dry-aged proteins. Think marinated vegetables with a celery vinegar and anchoïade or noodles with chili crunch, caviar and uni. The ideas are original, the flavors bold. Such creativity hews closely to the seasons, and even a salad can arrive as a revelation. All the while, service is seamless and warmly choreographed.

Name: Pré de chez vous
Description: Julien Malaisse pays frequent visits to the best Walloon producers, whose first-class ingredients he has been championing for eons. Meat from Sébastien Van Lommel and veg from market gardener, Régis, unveil all their nuances in the chef’s unorthodox cuisine. Malaisse takes the time to lovingly craft powerful sauces, lends a hand in the dining room and has a knack for concocting a wide range of varied yet coherent flavours by way of inventive side dishes. His apparently laid-back style demonstrates a weakness for floral notes and an ability to capture an ingredient’s vibrant essence. A few examples: he may baste breasts of medium rare pigeon and confit legs with a gutsy gravy jazzed up with blackcurrant liqueur, which is in turn underscored by distinctive contrasting textures of blackberries and mushrooms. The veteran sommelier can be relied upon to suggest pairings that may surprise but which will subtly balance your meal thanks to his savvy insights. It feels as if you’re eating in the chef’s home thanks to the log-burning fire and open-plan kitchen - we only wish that this friendly eatery were in our own backyard! We highly recommend staying overnight in one of the lovely guestrooms.

Name: Prévelle
Description: "Prévelle" is a lyrical name that perfectly reflects Romain Meder's cuisine. Alain Ducasse's former protégé pays homage to his rural upbringing with a plant-centric menu that is rooted in local Île-de-France produce and complemented by poultry, fish and shellfish. His modern and resolutely seasonal dishes demonstrate impressive technical skill: bold seasoning, vegetables roasted with the same care as meats, in pursuit of the deep, rich juices and flavours born of the Maillard reaction, a culinary process favoured by his mentor. Beyond the open kitchen and its adjoining table, a staircase leads upstairs to a hushed, understated and dining space that, with its clean lines, exudes a peaceful atmosphere.

Name: Publiek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Publiek is a one-of-a-kind star establishment and its friendly vibe is pivotal to its loft-inspired, cosy bistro interior and its home-from-home ambience. The mix of designer and vintage details courtesy of artist friends lend it a quirky personalised feel. The bar even features its old beer pump! The team’s enthusiasm is contagious, and the talented chef frequently serves the main course himself. Don’t expect posh, luxury ingredients, because Olly Ceulenaere is a staunch champion of little-known veggies and produce. His intelligent recipes hit the spot every time and he is a past master in the art of unexpected yet felicitous combinations, such as fillet of rockfish which is coated with a lacquer made out of shrimp heads and then flanked by a jus of yellow beetroot in shrimp stock and a spicy lovage oil. Ceulenaere juggles with techniques and flavours to exalt familiar ingredients, whose every facet he explores in a fascinating creative quest. The menu changes frequently, in keeping with the chef’s mood and inspiration (different lunch and dinner menu). The expert sommelier suggests excellent wine-food pairings, featuring traditional and unusual natural wines. Every meal at Publiek is a culinary adventure.

Name: Published on Main
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Timing is everything, but Chef Gus Stieffenhofer-Brandson and his team have a preternatural ability for sensing when produce is at its peak. Whether showcasing it on the plate or pickling and preserving it (those jars even double as decor), they're sourcing and foraging from local farms and forests.The contemporary fare bears the chef's distinct imprimatur. This is food that is at once familiar and surprising. Pappardelle comes stuffed with fresh cheese atop green summer legume sauce. Fraser Valley duck breast is artfully plated with cabbage, beets and a tableside pour of lingonberry sauce for a study of red.

Name: Pulejo
Description: In the refined Prati quarter, the elegance of the surroundings finds a natural extension in the interiors of the restaurant that – with an only apparent ‘j’ – bears the surname of its chef-patron. Dinner is taken in a romantically subdued light, in a dining room that continues to evolve with both consistency and taste, supported by service of the highest professionalism: discreet, watchful, and perfectly timed to anticipate each moment of need. The cooking plays upon balance and variety, weaving references to the flavours of Lazio together with influences gathered during the chef’s earlier career. The result is a series of creative and accomplished recipes, among them razor clams paired with nervetti and finished with a broth drawn from the crustacean’s trimmings, enriched with a vegetable gremolata, oil of celery and bone marrow – a clear homage to his starred past in Milan. Dish after dish is marked by careful attention to detail, underpinned by excellent produce and cooking of the utmost precision.

Name: Pur' - Jean-François Rouquette
Address: Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme, 5 rue de la Paix, Paris, 75002, France
Description: Chef Jean-François Rouquette has set up shop in this stylish dining room, signed by a Franco-Mexican designer, as he continues to roll out his virtuoso talent, illustrated by succulent fillets of John Dory and courgette flower flanked by olive-spiked gnocchi and a delicately acidic jus of provençal tomatoes. The delicacy with which he marries excellent produce in his creative and inspired cuisine definitely errs towards ‘pure’ and utter bliss!

Name: Pureté
Address: 79 rue de la Monnaie, Lille, 59000, France
Description: In the heart of historic Lille, Gérald Guille plies his trade in an attractive long narrow dining room with an open kitchen. "Pure" materials (earthenware, concrete, wood, leather) create a focused, tranquil atmosphere, mirroring the style of the chef, who delivers, in his own words, "creative, uninhibited food" that is rich in personality and flavour. He slaloms between invention and classicism over the course of subtly balanced tasting menus: trout, beetroot, bloody orange and sage; scallops, leeks, mimolette and limequat; fingered citron, honey and saffron…

Name: Pétrus by Gordon Ramsay
Address: 1 Kinnerton Street, Belgravia, London, SW1X 8EA, United Kingdom
Description: Named after the famous Pomerol estate in Bordeaux, wine plays an understandably pivotal role at this impeccably run restaurant that caters to both well-to-do locals and those looking for a special night out. At the heart of the elegant room is its striking glass-walled wine store, which features over 700 bins, including Château Pétrus going back to 1959. The cooking itself offers sumptuous luxury ingredients from lobster to turbot, presented in precise, refined dishes with a classic French heart and little regard for unnecessary frills.

Name: Qafiz
Address: Località Calabretto, Santa Cristina d'Aspromonte, 89056, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A captivating journey through the wild countryside and olive groves of Aspromonte serves as a prelude to an almost mystical experience at Qafiz, where Chef Nino Rossi tells the story of Calabria and its roots through an instinctive, profound, and remarkably accomplished cuisine. Guests are seated around a small kitchen in omakase style, embarking on an immersive gastronomic journey supported by an impeccable wine selection and service that keeps the energy of the moment alive. For those wishing to fully immerse themselves in the spirit of the place, Casa Qafiz offers the possibility of an intimate, refined stay, while at AsproCocktail Bar one can savor a signature spirit beside the crackling fireplace. A perfect conclusion to an experience that unites authenticity, terroir, and a contemporary vision of Calabria’s gastronomic heritage.

Name: Qing You Yu
Address: 2F, 535 Huaifu Road, Fengze, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The incredible range of quality live seafood on offer, prepared meticulously with exquisite technique, is the main draw here. There is no menu – diners choose from the three-tier fish tanks at the entrance themselves, then specify how they would like their pick to be cooked. Enjoy the soft roe and firm, flavourful meat of the chilled swimmer crab, or try the silky and aromatic swamp eel braised with tea seed oil and basil.

Name: Quadras
Description: Fleeing the limelight, Ricarda Grommes devotes herself body and soul to her stylish, trendy eatery, where you can feel and taste her quest for perfection, including in the elegant, spot-on table service. Ricarda’s inventive streak shines through in knockout appetisers and it is obvious that she attaches great importance to plating, while demonstrating a consummate grasp of modern techniques. Each dish is intelligently crafted and underscored by sides. The chef effortlessly navigates between French tradition and Asian precision and you will taste regional produce and exotic ingredients. An example: rare rib steak with succulent calf’s sweetbread and a fillet of veal in a crispy flaky pastry crust, paired with various textures of chickpeas, a calamondin dressing and a gutsy gravy jazzed up with a fruity dash of vin jaune. Ricarda Grommes’ cuisine is the summum of feminine elegance!

Name: Quadri
Address: Piazza San Marco 121 (primo piano), Venice, 30124, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Il Quadri showcases traditional Venetian dishes interpreted with a contemporary twist by chef Sergio Preziosa, who focuses on ingredients from the lagoon, such as fish from its shallow waters, vegetables from SantʼErasmo island, shellfish and game in season. Ask the staff for wine recommendations and you’ll discover some unusual labels on the extensive and varied wine list, such as the Adega do Vulcão Ameixambar, a white wine from the Azores with mineral notes and great flavour – the perfect accompaniment to the rich, tasty cuisine served here.

Name: Quai des Saveurs
Address: 69 rue de la Gare, Hagondange, 57300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Frédéric Sandrini has hung up his hat in this pink sandstone and white fronted edifice opposite Hagondange railway station, depicted by a pleasantly low-key, contemporary interior. Your tastebuds will be delighted by the modern, imaginative, ever-changing craftsmanship of this chef who works with painstakingly selected supplier-partners: abalone, hand-harvested by divers in the Bay of St Brieuc, fish from Saint-Quay-Portrieux or Boulogne-sur-Mer and a trolley that stars the work of master cheesemakers. Surprise menus and daily suggestions.

Name: Quatre Molins
Address: Comte de Rius 8, Cornudella de Montsant, 43360, Spain
Description: Given his unique nickname, it would be a surprise not to have heard of Rafel Muria, the so-called ‘honey chef’, for whom this natural product is much more than a fad, given that his family have been involved in beekeeping since 1810 through their company artMuria.In this simple restaurant, this chef who trained in renowned restaurants in Spain, France and Italy focuses on high-level creative cuisine which he showcases via elaborate dishes involving the discreet use of honey to add balance and stability. The concept, which is attuned to conscious gastronomy and seeks to highlight the wines from estates from the Montsant and Priorat areas, is focused on a single menu (El Rusc), which guests can fully customise to their preferences, making each dining experience personal and unique. They always give the option of adding three stand-alone dishes: his famous tuna royale with pear compote, crayfish ravioli with a foie gras sauce and black truffle, and, for dessert, the ‘Coulant’ with vanilla ice-cream (a Michel Bras recipe dating back to 1981).

Name: Quellenhof Gourmetstube 1897
Address: Via Passiria 47, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A young chef and a brilliant maître-d’ work together at this restaurant, where the cuisine is full of character and has its roots firmly anchored in the region. The menu allows guests to choose from four to six courses, all prepared using local ingredients such as lamb raised on a nearby farm served with parsnips and a refined jus, or reinterpreted dumplings served with morel mushrooms and spring peas. Matteo oversees the wine list, guiding guests on a unique journey through Italian and international labels collected over the past twenty years, all offering excellent value for money. Three impressive wine cellars can be visited by guests, while fine wines and historic vintages (especially from Tuscany and Bordeaux) are evident on the wine list. Excellent bread and dessert options complete the picture.

Name: Quetzal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: This boisterous hotspot offers up no shortage of personality. Almost everything on this distinctive menu passes through a battery of roaring wood-burning grills and hearths, lending a primal smokiness that pervades the food and room alike. At the end of the line is a single cook at an earthenware comal, preparing tortillas from heirloom corn nixtmalized and ground in-house. Menu standouts include the empanada oaxaquena, a turnover made with corn tortillas, stuffed with braised lamb barbacoa and served with salsa molcajete, and the lamb chops set over a black garlic mole negro with fried hoja santa leaves. Those hard-pressed to make decisions can opt for a tasting menu. In tandem, the bar provides a wealth of imaginative agave-based cocktails.

Name: Qui Plume la Lune
Description: Qui plume la Lune boasts two very different interiors: one with bare stone walls and natural materials and the other a riot of colour and dried flower compositions. The chef executes a creative score that showcases the season’s finest ingredients: fillet of croaker, risotto of tapioca pearls; tender beef fillet with mash and roast celery; poached pear and muscovado sorbet. The dishes are artfully plated and indulgently served, the cooking is spot on and the flavours and seasonings exquisitely balanced: just the ticket for a good meal in a warm, elegant setting.

Name: Quilon
Address: Taj 51 Hotel, 41 Buckingham Gate, Westminster, London, SW1E 6AF, United Kingdom
Description: Head Chef Sriram Aylur and his team offer a comprehensive tour through the classic flavours of southwest India and the Malabar Coast. Just try the lemon rice or paratha with your fish curry or kori gassi and you immediately know you’re in safe hands – and do start with the delicious pepper shrimps. There’s a separate vegetarian menu along with the tasting and à la carte options, so everyone will be happy. The spacious and comfortable room, run by a smart and knowledgeable team, also feels authentic to the south with its use of sandstone and rattan.

Name: Quimbaya
Description: If you’re keen to take your tastebuds on a culinary journey, Quimbaya provides the perfect opportunity, thanks to chef Edwin Rodríguez’s ability to recreate the flavours of his native Colombia, the birthplace of the movement known as Magic Realism.This restaurant, which takes its name from an indigenous native tribe famous for its gold craftsmanship, features a small bar displaying a superb array of Colombian spirits, and a minimalist dining room with an open-view kitchen where guests can interact with the chefs at work. The cuisine here is based around three tasting menus: Clásicos Q (offering their most iconic dishes, with the option to choose according to your tastes), the so-called Experiencia QUIMBAYA (a trip to the living memory of Colombia) and, finally, the Gran Menú QUIMBAYA, its maximum expression of Colombianness to thrill our souls, with the inclusion of delicious bites and some other key dishes.

Name: Quinsou
Description: Just opposite Ferrandi, the legendary culinary school, Quinsou ("chaffinch" in Occitan) is ideally positioned to influence the great chefs of tomorrow. In a trendy, vintage interior (cement tiles and zinc bar counter), the warm owner-chef, Antonin Bonnet, signs a spot-on, authentic take on artisanal cuisine. The excellent value for pleasure lunchtime formula is a hit every time with a choice of two menus devised around premium market-fresh ingredients. The duck and foie gras pâté en croûte, which keeps pace with the seasons, is a masterpiece of culinary balance from the delectable pastry crust to the melt-in-the-mouth stuffing. A dinky establishment where pleasure goes hand in hand with simplicity.

Name: Quintessenza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: What a fascinating historical context: the Swabian castle is right in front of the restaurant, the dining rooms, on two levels, are also within period walls, and finally there is the possibility, when the weather permits, to eat on a panoramic terrace from which you can also see the famous bell tower of Trani cathedral (as well as a table set up in a small room used as a wine cellar for dining among the bottles). No less than four brothers, between the dining room and the kitchen, share the restaurant's tasks; at the cooker, Stefano Di Gennaro, who creates a cuisine rich in substance and flavour, avoids unnecessary complications and virtuosity and aims firmly at satisfying the palate, in dishes that mostly reinterpret the classic Italian tradition using various Apulian products.

Name: Quirat
Address: Avenida de Rius I Taulet 1, Barcelona, 08004, Spain
Description: The gourmet restaurant at the Intercontinental Barcelona is another example of a hotel keen to diversify its services for guests by transforming itself into a foodie destination in its own right. Quirat, which has its own independent entrance (as well as access via the lobby), represents, in its own words, “the purity and wealth of the elements that form the land”. Chef Víctor Torres, who is renowned for his cuisine at the Michelin-starred Les Magnòlies in Arbúcies, creates contemporary Catalan cuisine that always showcases locally sourced ingredients while at the same time fully respecting seasonality. Dishes here are full of depth and flavour, with simplicity only evident in his sauces and reductions. Highlights on the menu include Maresme peas with onion soup and sea urchin; artichoke, romesco sauce and Mas Farró cheese; and “cap i pota” stew with sea cucumber – dishes that Víctor Torres views as tiny jewels, hence the naming of his menus 18K and 24K. The hotel even has its own kitchen garden.

Name: RAR Fine Dining
Description: Following stints at renowned establishments (including Bobby Bräuer's ‘EssZimmer’ at BMW Welt in Munich), Maximilian Reuter has found the ideal setting to pursue his ambitions as chef at the fine dining restaurant of die HOCHKÖNIGIN hotel. His culinary vision comes to life in his two set menus: "Asian Alpin" and the entirely vegan "Asian Green" – both available in five or seven courses. Combining Alpine tradition with Asian flavours, the dishes are made using a wide range of regional ingredients, including herbs from their kitchen garden and organic beef from its own farm. The kitchen team present each course themselves, which brings a personal touch and makes your dining experience even more special. Another draw is the intimate atmosphere – the cosy little space with its vaulted ceiling and upscale furnishings accommodates only a few diners, who enjoy dedicated and attentive service. The alcohol-free drink pairings created by the bartender are also excellent. The petits fours are a unique touch – there are a few surprises in store!

Name: RAU nature-based cuisine
Description: Klemens Gold is a chef who is forging his own path. In his idyllically secluded little restaurant, he draws his inspiration entirely from his natural surroundings, which makes for a unique and exciting set menu. For his seasonal concept he uses the best the market has to offer, forages some items himself in the forest, grows vegetables and herbs in his garden, ferments and pickles. One example featuring a captivating interplay of flavours is the combination of oysters, sauerkraut juice, horseradish cream and parsley oil. The minimalist ethos of his "nature-based cuisine" is reflected in the upscale interior design with its clean lines, natural materials, earthy tones and floor-to-ceiling windows that look out onto the greenery. Service is cordial and adept – maître d' and certified sommelier Paul Piaty provides exceptionally well-matched wine pairings.

Name: RIJKS®
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Joris Bijdendijk has put the Rijksmuseum's gem of a restaurant on the map with his highly personal culinary approach, working predominantly with homegrown vegetables spiced up with the exotic influences that characterise Dutch cuisine. He has forged a distinctive culinary identity in which vegetables play a leading role, drawing diners effortlessly into his world. The elegant interior, with its abundance of natural materials and welcoming ambience, has been designed with an immersive experience firmly in mind. RIJKS® is a reflection of the bustling city of Amsterdam. The sophistication of the well-considered dishes is immediately striking. Each mind-blowing idea seems to outdo the last. What appears simple at first glance reveals extraordinary layers of flavour. From a millefeuille of earthy beetroot paired with a beurre blanc enlivened by Tomasu soy sauce and fresh parsley oil, to gently braised goat seasoned with a refined fish sauce, this cuisine fascinates and intrigues in equal measure. At RIJKS®, you will discover Dutch gastronomy 2.0.

Name: Racines
Address: GF, 22 Upper Station Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Chef Romain from southern France revisits his culinary roots at Racines (literally "roots" in French). Classic heirloom recipes get a modern makeover and are crafted with seasonal produce from his home country and Hong Kong. From house-made sourdough with smoked butter to petits fours in a vintage biscuit tin, his tasting menu brims with personal touches. Crispy Brittany pigeon, a staple on the menu, is nicely balanced by the fruity tartness of berries.

Name: Racines
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: When a talented chef from Rennes, Virginie Giboire, embraces her roots (or ‘Racines’), the result is elegant cuisine in the zeitgeist. Giboire delivers savvy, distinctive cuisine that always hits the spot, courtesy of a concise menu. Interesting interplays of textures, subtle marriages of flavours and a steadfast commitment to premium ingredients, often from small-scale Breton producers. The interior is bright and modern and the chef’s partner, Fabien Hacques, can be relied on for insightful wine tips thanks to a fine selection featuring small winegrowers and prestigious houses.

Name: Racines - Bruno Cirino
Description: (Temporarily closed) Bruno Cirino and his faithful right-hand man, José Vidal, regale diners with a bargain-priced single set menu composed entirely of local organic or sustainably grown fruit and vegetables in their small eatery. They propose "kitchen garden cuisine" using ingredients that are picked only when perfectly ripe. Their talented craftsmanship shines the spotlight on characteristic Mediterranean produce, like garlic, olive oil and basil. Dig into a soup of red spring onions and basil; purple artichoke with a cheesy emulsion and grilled spiny artichoke; compressed root vegetables à la “César Baldaccini”; baked miniature apple and burnt barley ice cream… Fine selection of reasonably priced vintages. Smiling service. Booking recommended.

Name: Radio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: From the upper reaches of town, this attractive hotel dating from the 1930s broadcasts a non-stop resounding tribute to the electro-magnetic waves and the triode vacuum tube that made the invention of the talkies and the wireless possible. Its Art Deco decor has lost none of its splendour – mosaic flooring, decorative wrought iron and a marriage of glass and mirrors. In the kitchen, chef Wilfrid Chaplain mixes influences from his native Normandy and his adopted Auvergne, drawing out their gentle, little-explored harmonies. Technically proficient, he creates ambitious, subtle and delicate cuisine that delights the taste buds: Normandy scallops, lime crab, gentian and seaweed; Auvergne guinea fowl, salsify and burnt chestnuts, full-bodied jus. As for the platter of Auvergne cheeses, it creates a buzz all of its own.

Name: Radis
Description: Radis is one of those places in which a young chef (Juanjo Mesa) with the restaurant business in his blood, experience working in leading restaurants behind him, and an undeniable desire to please has set up a business with a view to revolutionising the city’s dining scene. In 2023, Mesa won the title of “Best Olive Oil Chef” at the “Jaén, Paraíso Interior” contest organised as part of the San Sebastián Gastronomika festival, and in this small, centrally located eatery with a contemporary bistro feel and open kitchen he puts all his efforts into two surprise tasting menus (Bercho and Charca, with 9 and 15 courses respectively) inspired by tradition and his childhood memories from the small town of Pegalajar, in the municipality of Sierra Mágina. He has brought this cuisine fully up to date thanks to strong technique, a delicate touch and superbly crafted French-style sauces and jus.
