The essence of his cooking is summed up by one particular dish: broad beans, cod and radish, a delicious homage to his mother and to his roots.

Name: Radius by Stefan Beer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In his kitchen in the restaurant of the time-honoured Victoria Jungfrau Grand Hotel, Stefan Beer uses only ingredients sourced within a 50km radius (the clue is in the name!). There are two set menus – conventional and vegan – plus a "Sommelier Menu" with wines from the surrounding area. Diners are talked through the pleasingly uncomplicated dishes – sometimes by the chef himself. Produce that they harvest themselves is used alongside local shrimps and caviar from the region. The high standards of quality are also reflected in the tasteful, upscale interior decor. Friendly service from the knowledgeable team adds the finishing touch.

Name: Rakushin
Description: The name means ‘spirit of fun’ and also refers to the chef’s given name, Shintaro. All occupations have their joys and sorrows, but the chef maintains a spirit of fun. At the same time, he never forgets reverence for tradition. Lacquered wooden trays and dishes garnished with flowers convey each season. Self-expressive yet respectful of traditional boundaries, his goal is the evolution of Japanese cuisine. Cuisine is a mirror of the soul; joy itself.

Name: Rania
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This fine dining concept seems fit for a queen, and good thing too, since Rania translates to "queen" in Hindi and Sanskrit. The team delivers something entirely enticing here with an inventive menu. There are plenty of contemporary touches along with a few surprises with dishes like chana masala panisse dressed with green garlic chutney, or hay-aged pork vindaloo featuring tender flavorful loin and a block of crispy skin belly accompanied by a rich bowlful of dal Kolhapuri, fluffy Kashmiri pulao and butter-brushed hot naan. Cocktails are designed to complement the rich, bold flavors.

Name: Raro im Mühlenhof
Description: The farm-to-table ethos is consistently put into practice in this culinary gem nestled in verdant surroundings. Almost everything on your plate comes from the restaurant's own produce: around Heidelberg, some 750 varieties of vegetables, herbs and fruit are cultivated across approximately 7 000m2. Each day's set menu is determined by what the gardeners have freshly harvested in the fields and brought to the kitchen that morning. Staff take pleasure in explaining the underlying philosophy to diners and service is charming. The seasonal seven-course set menu also comes in a vegetarian version, both with the option of wine or alcohol-free pairings. Pre-dinner drinks are served in the scenic garden in summer and in the mezzanine over the kitchen in winter. Astute wine recommendations from an interesting selection of primarily German wines. The inviting premises – once a paper factory and later a candle factory – have been turned into an attractive location with airy architecture, clean-lined, modern design and a half-open kitchen.

Name: Ratatouille Food & Wine
Description: With Jozua Jaring, not everything is as it seems. He pays great attention to detail in the meticulous presentation of his dishes and likes to surprise diners with contrasting colours and forms. This is a restaurant with a real "wow" factor – chef Jaring puts his own exciting spin on classic flavours, taking your taste buds on a culinary adventure: conjuring up vegetable ice cream concoctions, dabbling with Asian citrus notes or rounding off a dish with a classic, deeply flavoursome vegetable jus. Such inspirations take this chef's top-quality ingredients to the next level. Think sweet and smoky barbecued langoustine accompanied by al dente ravioli stuffed with langoustine meat, along with various textures of carrot and a full-bodied bisque. This chef has mastered the art of working with fish and seafood, and his creativity does not lose any momentum when it comes to devising vegetarian dishes. This characterful building has an equally tasteful decor: a little rustic, a tad eclectic, but very much on trend – with an imposing open Molteni kitchen serving as the hub of the action. And then there is the cosy waterside terrace (specify when booking).

Name: Ratsstuben
Description: In the middle of the Old Town, a stone's throw from Marktplatz and the striking Kirche St Sixtus, is the small Ratshotel. Not only does it have attractive, comfortable guestrooms, but it also boasts an appealing restaurant. Chef-patron Daniel Georgiev prepares a classic set menu, drawing on modern and seasonal influences. His dishes showcase select local ingredients such as Müritz venison and Wipperfürth salmon trout, but also international specialities like Balfego tuna or truffles. You are free to decide the number of courses according to your own taste. The excellent wine list features over 300 labels including an impressive champagne selection. Friendly, attentive and professional service come courtesy of charming hostess Petra Georgieva and team. In the chic and elegant interior, the walk-in wine climate cabinet is sure to draw the eye. For a more down-to-earth alternative, head to Gute Stube for steaks etc.

Name: RavioXO
Address: Plaza de Manuel Gómez Moreno 5, Madrid, 28020, Spain
Description: Chef Dabiz Muñoz reminds us that RavioXO is ‘the luxury of eating time’, a perfect metaphor to express all the work that goes into making each filling and each sauce for their pasta. They redefine the concept of ‘dough’ in a haute cuisine proposal!The spacious restaurant, with beautiful interior design by the Lázaro Rosa-Violán studio, is run by chefs Raúl Bernalte and Valerio Gargiulo. They reflect, through both the à la carte and its tasting menu (Festival 360º), a fusion that covers almost all of Asia, incorporating sauces, wok techniques and exotic raw ingredients (yozukosho, Korean tempura, Singapore spider crab, umeboshi, Gochujang pasta, etc.) that are combined with Spanish cuisine. Within its offer, designed for sharing, the dumplings, the eggs with blood sausage, the legendary Cocido Hong Kong Madriz all stand out... without forgetting lighter bites, still full of flavour, such as the Guinea fowl steamed bun or the Tortilla bèi tan zuo sī.

Name: Raíces-Carlos Maldonado
Address: Ronda de Cañillo 3, Talavera de la Reina, 45600, Spain
Description: Chef Carlos Maldonado knows no limits and it is this which characterises his cooking, which is firmly steeped in the flavours and ingredients of La Mancha but which is also open to influences from around the world, as witnessed by the twinning between his beloved Talavera de la Reina and Puebla (Mexico). The restaurant, which could almost pass unnoticed because of its discreet façade, boasts a classic-contemporary decor in varying tones of white, plus an adjoining dining room with curtains hanging from the ceiling that add a more intimate feel to the tables. His tasting menus (Básico and Hechos de Barro) feature daring, highly technical dishes starting with a selection of snacks (calamari rolls, smoked partridge breast and caviar tartlet, partridge “bonbon”, vegetables and Toledana sauce, trout with an ajo verde salsa, etc) that is worth ordering for the visual effect alone as it is served on an exquisite piece of local ceramic. The tableware here has been designed by the restaurant itself, with more modern creations that incorporate the fingerprints of the chef’s son!

Name: Raúl Resino
Description: Raúl Resino, who is known as the fisherman-chef, signals his philosophy in a single sentence: “We cook as we think, we don’t think how we’re going to cook”. His creative cooking showcases a constant desire to move forward, hence his nod to Japanese cuisine and, above all, a strong focus on fish, seafood, rice and ingredients from nearby market gardens. He is also a great advocate of locally sourced ingredients and often heads out to catch his own fish. His cuisine (a single tasting menu called Raúl Resino) is centred around the biodiversity of Castellón’s Mediterranean shoreline and recipes that local fishermen traditionally prepare on their boats. A good example is the “canana” rice, prepared with a local mollusc similar to a squid. His particular dream is for more humble and lesser-known fish (such as wrasse, scald fish, trumpet fish, and beard fish) that don’t always make it to auction to become better known to a wider audience.

Name: Re Santi e Leoni
Description: Steps from the cathedral, within a refined historic palazzo, a luminous passageway leads guests towards the open kitchen, through contemporary interiors of essential design. At the table, the quality of the raw material is the starting point of a gastronomic offering that is precise and dynamic, enhanced by excellent artisan breads and desserts of notable elegance. Three tasting menus are available, complemented by an à la carte that follows the rhythm of the seasons and interprets the cuisine with balance, technique and clarity of flavour. The chef presents personal and measured dishes, capable of uniting rigour and creativity with a contemporary touch. Completing the experience, a broad and well-constructed cellar with a selection that pays homage to the most interesting expressions of the Italian wine landscape.

Name: ReComiendo
Description: Fun, flavour, strong technique, professionalism and time-honoured memories are to the fore here, coupled with the philosophy of chef Periko Ortega, who does his utmost to add “power” to every dish. This restaurant, which is located in a residential district somewhat away from the city’s main tourist haunts, is modern in style and designed to create a culinary journey (as an example, snacks and appetisers are served at the highly original bar before heading into the contemporary dining room). Once seated, you’ll start to discover ReComiendo’s creative cuisine built around memories and a desire to deceive and surprise, as is the case with the appetisers dedicated to the four meals of the day (breakfast, lunch, afternoon snack and dinner). Here, everything revolves around two tasting menus that are constantly changing: ReCuerdos (18 courses) and NoStalgia (24 courses), both of with offer a wine-pairing option. We were particularly impressed by the “mazamorra”, a typical dish from Córdoba, as well as the delicious “artisanal bread from the La Tradición 1913 oven”, which is accompanied by over 20 different olive oils!

Name: Real Balneario
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Looking to have lunch or dinner overlooking the Bay of Biscay? You will struggle to find a better place, as this restaurant has its foundations on the very sand of the beach and has lots of tables with views, some overlooking the Philippe Cousteau Anchor Museum.Isaac Loya has been able to put his father and grandfather’s wise advice into practice, so he has made fish and seafood from the Bay of Biscay the cornerstone of his cuisine. There are two lines of work: one that pays homage to the classic, simple and respectful elaborations with the product, and another that seeks a more complex culinary venture, giving some dishes an original touch without distorting their essence. The à la carte, featuring signature fish dishes such as sea bream, bonito and sea bass, is complemented by three set menus: La Peñona, the Isaac Loya (more gastronomic) and one called 35th Anniversary, this one with the house’s iconic dishes. A great classic? Discover the ‘Félix Loya’ sea bass in champagne, a dish created by the chef's grandfather half a century ago.

Name: Rebelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Behind the unassuming façade of Rebelle, you will discover a warm, minimalist interior decked in salmon and terracotta colours. Fuss-free and casual, Rebelle aims to serve excellent nosh in an easy-going vibe. The man behind the creative score, Martijn Defauw, rustles up fascinating food and knock-out seasonings, often with an oriental twist, that come up trumps every time. He has a knack for sourcing the best produce, such as flawlessly fresh North Sea fish or locally grown tender young hop shoots. His close ties with his producers are a source of inspiration, as are his travels. For example, he may spread flavoursome tapioca pearls, slices of green apple and radishes over a fleshy raw oyster, all of which is paired with a seaweed roll and then even further enhanced courtesy of a warm beurre blanc of plankton that underscores and balances the other ingredients. Heavenly! The big-boned flavours of each dish are further enhanced by a superlative wine cellar and the sommeliers suggest natural or classical tipples to pair with chef Defauw’s culinary masterpieces. To quote them: “Warm, Pure, Unique” - a meal at Rebelle is felicitous from start to finish.

Name: Rebers Pflug
Description: As soon as you enter the restaurant, you will pass the open kitchen, which is sure to whet your appetite! The menu is really wide-ranging, from regional classics such as Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth) or Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions) to the set menu ("Genießer-Menü") comprising three to six courses – these might include the likes of "sea bass and Bouchot mussel bouillabaisse, aubergine, fennel, black garlic". There is also a vegetarian set menu. And then there are the prized steaks… Needless to say, chef-patron Hans-Harald Reber gets his excellent meat from his trusted butcher, who just happens to be his cousin! He cooks alongside Edmund Schmidt. You can soak up the friendly and pleasantly informal atmosphere, safe in the knowledge you will be looked after attentively by the proficient front-of-house team. Plus you have the option of booking one of the comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Red Brick
Address: Farmers Circle, Žirgyno gatvė 1, Radiškis, 20364, Lithuania
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An hour out of Vilnius is The Farmers Circle, a wonderfully remote 1,730-acre working farm, and at its centre is this beautifully restored barn. Naturally, produce grown and reared on their farm features on the set menu. You start with beautifully rendered snacks, like beef tartare with egg yolk, followed by dishes that celebrate Lithuanian’s own culinary traditions, such as an updated version of balandeliai. The chef applies his own delicate touches but always with the purpose of highlighting the quality of the main ingredient. ‘Sleepy Horse’, the converted stable block, also houses 15 bedrooms.

Name: Refectorio
Address: Carretera N 122, Sardón de Duero, 47340, Spain
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Alongside its unquestionably high levels of gastronomy, Refectorio enjoys a spectacular setting in a 12th-century monastery surrounded by nature, wine cellars and vineyards, and is renowned for its spectacular and pinpoint service, which includes an aperitif in “La Cueva” (home to the bodega’s private collection).Reus-born chef Marc Segarra offers guests a choice of menus (Origen and Legado) and a highly creative culinary experience with wine-pairing options that provide a perfect opportunity to taste some superb vintages. Seasonal produce from the farm here and ingredients sourced from small-scale local producers also add to the appeal. Some top dishes or interesting facts? Two caught our attention: MEMORIA 2021, based on pickled partridge, and ARRAIGO 2026, with an excellent cut of suckling lamb, a liquid salad and a Castilian anchoa (lamb meat, cured and covered with oil).

Name: Reflet d'Obione
Description: Trained in star Swiss, French (and even Australian) establishments, chef Laurent Cherchi is a stalwart champion of the environment. He offers two menus, one of which is lacto-ovo-vegetarian, while the other is all-out vegan (without animal ingredients) – which is nothing if not rare in the universe of French star-rated establishments. All his produce is rigorously sourced locally, from the Cévennes to the Mediterranean (beef from Aubrac, saltbush lamb from Camargue, tomme cheese from Larzac) and the front-of-house team is more than well-versed in the ins and outs of each ingredient’s provenance. Each dish has been endlessly pondered, puzzled over and tweaked, to allow the chef’s impeccable technique (fermentation, extraction) and knife-edged accuracy to showcase the stars of the show: the veggies. Three dining rooms, which sport a stripped back vibe, and the tableware are all made to measure by local artisans.

Name: Regina Montium
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A great place to experience nature untamed – in a sensational location at an altitude of 1 550m! Under the direction of Benedikt Voss, thoughtful and imaginative cuisine is prepared with precise craftsmanship and great attention to detail. Only premium, mostly organic produce from Switzerland is used, as well as over 400 different herbs from the restaurant's kitchen garden. Available in either a nine- or five-course format, the "Terroir" set menu reflects the region in all its facets. Tip: Try the alcohol-free drink pairings, which include house-made lemonades. The wine list features exclusively biodynamic wines from Switzerland. Service is friendly and attentive. The terrace is the perfect spot to enjoy a drink before dinner. To soak up the sensational setting and nature-centred philosophy a little longer, book one of the simple but well-kept guestrooms at the Kräuter Hotel Edelweiss, in which the restaurant is located. To get here from Vitznau, take the Rigi-Bahn railway to Staffelhöhe, the station just outside the building.

Name: Regueiro
Description: When you hear ‘Never stop believing’, you might begin to think of football; but here it is the motivational motto that chef Diego Fernández lives by! In this surprising restaurant, located in a somewhat disruptive chalet-style with a large garden surrounded by farmland, you will find contemporary urban interior design and a menu that exudes personality, as it moves away from Asturian flavours to reveal a fusion cuisine built around Indian, Mexican and Southeast Asian flavours. The dishes, which are balanced, elegant and based on domestic produce, are presented in three tasting menus (Corto, Diego and Hedonista) that reveal the chef's mastery of both the tandoori oven and the preparation of different curries and homemade moles. A standout dish? His lobster marinated in fenugreek oil, red prawn curry and green mango, pickled vegetables, and agripicante (spicy and sour) balchão with tandoor naan bread.

Name: Relais Blu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking Capri, in a simply spectacular setting, the restaurant offers one of the most breathtaking views of the Sorrento Peninsula: from the windows and the terrace, your gaze is drawn to the island’s unmistakable silhouette, suspended between sea and sky. In the kitchen, Fumiko Sakai interprets the local area with his own personal touch and a wealth of experience, gained through years of working along the Amalfi Coast. His menu is firmly rooted in the culinary traditions of Campania, making the most of ingredients sourced from the restaurant’s own vegetable garden, while occasionally incorporating subtle Eastern influences that enrich certain dining experiences. The offering is presented as four tasting menus, with the option to order à la carte as well. The star of the show is, of course, the sea, with plenty of focus on fresh fish, while also showcasing excellent local meats such as Caserta black piglet and Laticauda lamb, alongside more cosmopolitan creations that blend Mediterranean influences and Japanese touches in an original and finely balanced harmony.

Name: Relais Louis XIII
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: This edifice, steeped in history, stands on the cellars of the former Grands-Augustins convent and it was here on 14 May 1610, an hour after his father King Henry IV had been assassinated, that Louis XIII learned that he was the next king of France… The memory of this rich heritage lingers on in the ornate dining room which sports half-timbers, bare stone, wainscoting, stained-glass and wall hangings, although the profusion of heirlooms is set off by a few cutting-edge details (glazed cellar, modern sculptures). The setting with a sense of occasion is the perfect foil to the food of chef Manuel Martinez, an ardent champion of Gallic culinary classicism. After training at Ledoyen, the Crillon and the Tour d’Argent, the Meilleur Ouvrier de France (Best Craftsman of France) decided to settle in this prestigious establishment to pursue high-flying French culinary traditions. Enduringly popular with regulars, in particular for the excellent eater-friendly lunchtime prices!

Name: Relais de la Poste
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: In their establishment overlooking the pine forest, the Coussau family champion classic French cuisine and pay homage to the Landes terroir: foie gras, poultry, Chalosse beef, and fish from Capbreton. Regulars will be delighted that mainstays – scrambled eggs with black truffle, warm duck foie gras with grapes, and sole with porcini, or the traditional hot Grand Marnier soufflé – are still on the menu. In autumn, there is roast wood pigeon or hare à la royale: tradition is taken seriously here.

Name: Ren He Guan (Xuhui)
Address: 407 Zhaojiabang Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Dim yellow lights, 1930s memorabilia, golden oldies performed by singers dressed in qipao… but, surprisingly, the ambiance doesn't steal the show. It's the first-rate Shanghainese fare at bargain prices that keeps the place packed. One highlight of the fish-focused menu is crab, as the owner picks the best from his own farm; the crabmeat and roe on rice is a must. Fried shredded eel with water bamboo affords a nice contrast of textures.

Name: Ren Mishina
Description: True to his creed, ‘Life resides in cooking that is free of affectation’, the chef strives to serve food that is honest and down-to-earth. Paying close attention to the strength of his cooking flame, he sources the flavours of each season—bamboo shoots, pike conger, matsutake mushrooms, and puffer fish—and slow-cooks them over charcoal. Indian-ink paintings behind the counter depict lotuses in each season. In the language of flowers, the lotus represents a pure and chaste spirit. The chef’s honesty and respect for foodstuffs are reflected in his carefully pared-down creations.

Name: Resonance
Address: 108, 4 Soi Sukhumvit 65, Phra Khanong Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Tokyo-born chef Shunsuke Shimomura takes diners on a journey through his past, weaving dishes from his experience working around the world with his Japanese roots. The seasonal set menu is full of delights, from delicious clam soup to grilled seasonal vegetables, Japanese curry to homemade ice-cream. The restaurant fills the ground floor of a contemporary two-storey house, with a minimalist décor that puts the focus firmly on the cooking. A large team provides polished and attentive service; the wine list is strong on Burgundy but consider the imaginatively compiled drinks pairing which could also include beer and sake.

Name: Ressources
Description: In his new restaurant, chef Tanguy Laviale (previously at Garopapilles) is calmly going about extricating himself from the traditional codes of gastronomy – with the help of his associate, Maxime Courvoisier, a sommelier who thinks outside of the box. Imagine: a short menu, comprising just eight dishes to be mixed and matched as you please (four or five of these small plates amount to a meal). The talented chef's technical approach always hits the mark, from the judicious combinations to the quality produce enhanced without any showboating, not to mention the impeccable garnishes and seasonings. Examples include breaded red mullet, kale and sour cream; line-caught hake with an oyster and mint ravigote sauce. Wine, too, takes centre stage here: over 700 ready-to-drink labels (plus plenty more in the cellar), ranging from big names to small-scale producers – something for every budget! Sommeliers first and foremost, the head servers make a point of promoting young winemakers.

Name: Restaurant 12
Address: 12 Jianye Road, Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched on a hillside in Yangmingshan, the cosy bungalow features full-length windows and an open kitchen. The Spanish chef rolls out a contemporary, season-driven menu that melds French and Spanish cuisine and stars mostly local produce. His exquisite plating and knack for layering flavours using tangy components like fragrant lemon and roselle calyces are especially impressive. The extensive wine cellar unveils a well curated cast of vintage tipples.

Name: Restaurant 1857
Description: Restaurant 1857 prides itself on being chic but by no means stuffy. A narrow street leads to this former coach house – the old horse trough is still in the open kitchen! – that exudes an elegant combination of authentic charm and contemporary sophistication. Joke, your charming hostess, is also the talented pastry chef behind the restaurant's fabulous desserts. Joey van Heesbeen's creative dishes are technically impressive, visually striking and at times complex. He likes to experiment with bold flavours and the umami-rich nuances of Asian cuisine. In his unique take on beef Wellington, he incorporates miso mustard and a powder made from dried vegetable scraps. He pairs briefly seared langoustine, with a creamy shellfish-based XO sauce. Langoustine mayonnaise, yuzu gel and salty caviar add an extra kick to this intense creation. Round off your meal with a coffee or tea and sample one of the expertly crafted treats from the dessert trolley – another testament to the chefs' skill. As well as the set menu (vegetarian version available), there is a tempting à la carte selection.

Name: Restaurant 1950
Description: This fantastic restaurant is actually housed in what was once a piggery. The attractive modern dining area features high ceilings (the hanging herb boxes are an original detail) and an open kitchen. Here, the chefs prepare a vegetarian set menu featuring dishes such as "potato & herbs" or "fennel & tomato", each centred on two carefully selected ingredients. A meat component can be added on request. Diners are given information about the ingredients, all of which (except for the salt) are sourced within a 25km radius. Far from run-of-the-mill, this is cuisine driven by original ideas and a consistent commitment to ecological and organic principles. Nothing goes to waste; each ingredient is celebrated in its entirety. To pair with your food, you can choose between wines from Baden and Württemberg or interesting house-made alcohol-free juices. The very friendly staff keep things informal. Simon Tress also helps with the service – he calls the restaurant his "living room", which is fitting given the pleasantly personal atmosphere and the fact that there is space for no more than 12 diners. On Wednesday evenings, the "Chef's Table" brings all guests together around one communal table. There are attractive guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Restaurant 20 Victoria
Address: 20 Victoria St., Unit 100, Toronto, M5C 2N8, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Located on a quiet stretch of downtown Toronto, this tiny-but-mighty restaurant enters a new era under Chef Rafa Covarrubias. Ideal for intimate dates and built around a carefully run open kitchen, the dimly-lit restaurant offers a refined, contemporary tasting menu flecked with Mexican influences. A custardy tamale with salsa roja and snow crab has few equals, but the scallop with mole verde is excellent as well. The main event is a dry-aged roasted duck, first presented with a bit of tableside flair and later served with a glossy jus and chimole negro. Service is warm and personable, and thoughtful, esoteric wines are served with genuine passion in a room buzzing with excitement. Reservations are scarce so plan accordingly.

Name: Restaurant 360
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of Dubrovnik's harbour, the slightly elevated restaurant affords splendid views of the sea and marina. The exclusive terrace, which stretches along the medieval walls and St. John's fortress, provides a lovely setting for a summer dinner. For a more romantic and intimate dining experience, choose one of the glass-fronted booths, known as “tents”, opposite the kitchen. Chef Marijo Curić, returning to his home town after significant experiences around Europe, holds true to expectations with technical and well-presented cuisine in which Mediterranean elements are enriched with Asian touches with a refined combination of French cooking techniques. Vacuum cooking, robata grilling, and well-mastered fermentations enrich each dish with a unique flavour. Two tasting menus are offered: one with the chef's iconic dishes and the other with the restaurant's classics. Try the snapper with beurre blanc, shellfish sauce and mussel and red shrimp cappuccino. The restaurant also boasts a superb wine cellar, with as many as 450 labels. The selection honours Croatia but is also open to the rest of the world, offering an excellent choice of international labels. The wine list is accompanied by customised wine pairings that may also include creative cocktails.

Name: Restaurant Affect
Description: Lars Aukema does not need luxury ingredients to create exciting dishes. Having spent many years working under Jonnie Boer's wing, he demonstrates sensibility when it comes to regional and international influences. His signature dish of avocado carpaccio with lettuce, macadamia nuts and jalapeño, all brought together by a Madras curry emulsion with remarkable depth, shows that less really is more here. This is subtlety that leaves a lasting impression, with ingredients allowed to speak for themselves. The chef has a refined technique and is not afraid of striking combinations.Diners can choose between two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, and a tempting à la carte selection. You can rely on sommelier Robin for well-matched wine pairings, and charming hostess Lisa also deserves a special mention. Restaurant Affect is an exceptionally welcoming place for lovers of ingredient-led cooking.

Name: Restaurant Alexander Huber
Description: This long-established inn has been run by the same family since 1612 and is now in the capable hands of Alexander Huber. Following a change in concept, the property now comprises two venues: the traditionally Bavarian Wirtshaus Huberwirt and Restaurant Alexander Huber. The latter serves as the fine dining counterpart and a presents a five- or seven-course tasting menu comprising dishes such as turbot with mussel chowder, artichoke, preserved lemon and cured egg yolk, or Pleiskirchen duck – breast and dumpling with shoyu, ginger, salsify and pointed cabbage. A vegetarian set menu is also available if pre-ordered. The cosy dining room has just seven tables – a setup that lends the evening a certain sense of exclusivity. Service is warm, attentive and refreshingly down-to-earth – with excellent wine recommendations by the glass. The restaurant's own cookery school is right next door.

Name: Restaurant Atelier
Description: At Atelier, you never know what to expect. Creative chef Hans Kinkartz knows how to link familiarity with novelty, and every dish has a surprise in store. His wealth of experience, combined with the youthful dynamism of the kitchen brigade, creates a distinctive culinary identity. Langoustines grilled to a translucent finish are elevated by various interpretations of Massaman curry, each expressing spice in a different way, while thin slices of aged entrecôte and silky-soft pepper bring savoury depth and subtle sweetness. Chef Kinkartz is known for his love of Asian flavours, which lend his dishes that extra dimension. Classical cooking techniques, vibrant acidity and creative freedom all have a part to play. Each and every dinner in this historical half-timbered house, with its elegant symbiosis of contemporary design and industrial austerity, comes with its own unexpected delights. Hostess Ellen, whose passion for wine is infectious, offers exceptional pairings. Atelier is synonymous with bespoke culinary craftsmanship.

Name: Restaurant Brogsitter - Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter was renowned for its wine back in the 13C, when it was the Hof- und Weingut des Kölner Domstifts (estate and vineyard of the Cologne Cathedral Chapter). In that regard, nothing has changed to this day, insofar as this characterful property is run by the Brogsitter family, who have a long tradition of winemaking. With numerous stints at top establishments to his name, chef Sebastian Baumann lives up to the standards of this traditional restaurant by demonstrating clear ambition. His distinctive style comes through in extremely flavourful dishes that are full of clever contrasts, such as "morels, pork belly, prawns, shellfish foam" and "Miéral pigeon, purple curry, radicchio, salted plum". These come as a four- or five-course set menu, but you can also choose à la carte. Take your pick from the extensive wine list, which has a good selection of wines by the glass, including from the restaurant's own vineyard. Waitstaff are confident, cordial and knowledgeable. The chic, elegant room boasts striking features such as the high, gabled ceiling with exposed beams and the Murano chandelier. In summer, there is a lovely terrace. "Gourmet Lunch" is served Thu-Sun.

Name: Restaurant Calva
Description: Tom Beckers leaves nothing to chance when it comes to pleasing his diners. He rolls out the red carpet to welcome you into his cosily decorated restaurant. The striking open kitchen grabs your attention from the get-go. As soon as the shellfish bisque arrives with the amuse-bouches, you can sense the personality behind the cooking. Thoughtfully crafted dishes showcase classic expertise and precise technique across a fabulous set menu.This chef knows the art of less is more. The way he brilliantly presents spiced North Sea crab alongside a caramel-accented crisp, a poultry mousse, a chilled, deeply flavoured shellfish velouté and a drizzle of lime oil, demonstrates his understanding of flavours at their most fundamental level. His signature dish featuring foie gras, brioche, hazelnut and apple is not to be missed.You can place your full trust in the wine pairings, which have some delightful surprises in store. Everything at Restaurant Calva radiates passion – making a meal here a joy for any foodie.

Name: Restaurant Château Neercanne
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The character and historical charm of this château with its terraced gardens stir the soul. Classical elegance permeates every corner, from the hardwood flooring to the magnificent chandeliers. The views across the Baroque gardens and the Jeker Valley are simply breathtaking! An aperitif or coffee in the historical Marl Caves is an experience in itself. The remarkably attentive front-of-house team further enhances the magical atmosphere, arriving with an aperitif trolley and even a dedicated butter trolley. With a feel for the zeitgeist, Robert Levels breathes new life into French classics. Vegetables are harvested from his own garden (an appealing vegetarian set menu is available), and the sauces are always outstanding. His impeccably prepared foie gras terrine is paired with a compote that lends freshness and sweetness, along with an intense veal-jus vinaigrette. A flawlessly risen vanilla soufflé with fig leaf ice cream and expressive garnishes of fig, blueberry and goat's cheese makes for a finale that will leave any connoisseur in awe. Chef Levels tempers the intense flavours of classical cuisine with exciting exotic touches, focusing on vegetables and palatability. A castle fairy tale par excellence!

Name: Restaurant De Burgemeester
Description: Anne and Sander Spruijt have set up shop in the former town hall of picturesque Linschoten. The characterful building has retained its original charm and been enhanced with elegant additions. One look at the large glass-walled wine room makes it clear you have come to the right place to sample some first-rate labels. From the warm welcome to the post-dinner coffee and dessert, you can look forward to genuine hospitality at De Burgemeester. Sander Spruijt is a technically proficient chef who loves to showcase his culinary skills – from marinating and smoking beetroots to dry-ageing beef in butter and herbs, he is a master of his craft, expertly combining textures and bold flavours. Succulent short ribs glazed with their own jus are topped with shredded beef and given a Mediterranean twist in the form of a red onion stuffed with red pepper cream, accompanied by aubergine purée and a potato boulangère. His meticulous attention to detail ensures everything is spot on. A firm favourite!

Name: Restaurant De Kas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: De Kas has grown steadily since it was established in 2001 and has now reached maturity. "From plant to plate" has always been the motto here, a vision of mindfulness that seemed a tall order at the outset. Persistence has paid off, and De Kas has become a benchmark in its field. They grow about 300 varieties of vegetables, herbs and fruit both on site and in their larger field in the Beemster Polder. What is harvested in the morning from the imposing greenhouse will take pride of place on the plate a little later, in light, modern creations. Tip: Make a beeline for the fabulous garden terrace. Wim de Beer and Jos Timmer are masters in the art of delicately balancing sweet and sour flavours. Subtle sauces highlight the creative vegetable dishes (sometimes with meat or fish). Celeriac, for instance, is gently cooked and paired with aromatic black truffle to accentuate its earthy character, alongside goat's cheese cream and a rich buttermilk sauce finished with herb oil. The wealth of natural produce that these chefs have at their disposal is a constant source of inspiration for their seemingly boundless creativity, and that is what foodies really revel in.

Name: Restaurant De Lauzun
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Pézenas is not only the city of Molière, it is also the HQ of Matthieu de Lauzun. Established in a winery in the priory of Saint-Jean de Bébian, this venue provides a stage for the chef to demonstrate his manifold talents. A chic neoteric interior, done up in stone, wood and copper, sets the scene for the chef’s delicate, tasty Mediterranean score, liberally scattered with childhood and wayfaring souvenirs. The well-curated lineup of Languedoc wines further adds to the pleasurable dining experience.

Name: Restaurant GERBER WYSS
Description: In the heart of Yverdon-les-Bains, the GERBER WYSS establishment is a fine dining eatery, a bakery-chocolaterie and a tearoom. The former’s distinctive style is founded on cryoconcentration, fermentation, fresh herbs and vegetables, in a bid to enhance Swiss produce. This virtuoso, veggie-centric technique is packed in emotion, precision and visual appeal. The eight-course Signature Menu immerses you in this universe with dishes such as poultry oyster meat, fermented shiitake water and Suchy hazelnuts. The terrace is perfect for an aperitif before dinner or snacks. A warm interior and stylish, slick service.

Name: Restaurant Girardin
Description: The Maison des Têtes, a listed Renaissance edifice lavishly decorated with grimacing faces, is as superb as Colmar itself. The restaurant's decor is minimalist, in keeping with Éric Girardin's tasting menu, which showcases the terroir of Alsace. Each dish is the epitome of beauty, flavour and delicately refined aromas. You will be won over by the trout "in three acts" and its hollandaise sauce with herbs, or the pigeon with cabbage, orange and cashew nuts. There is also a brasserie, plus guestrooms that sport a spirit of timeless elegance.

Name: Restaurant Gordon Ramsay High
Address: 60th Floor, 22 Bishopsgate, City of London, London, EC2N 4BQ, United Kingdom
Description: When your restaurant is on the 60th floor, thus becoming the tallest in Europe, it makes complete sense that the 12-seater counter faces the window and the stunning view over the city, rather than the chefs in their open kitchen. Gordon Ramsay’s exclusive little sky dining restaurant offers a surprise tasting menu, built around ingredients from the top drawer. Highlight dishes could include 14-day aged duck with celeriac and Alsace bacon, and lobster with pumpkin and pine. Everyone is served together so be punctual – and allow a little extra time for security checks on the ground floor.

Name: Restaurant Guy Savoy
Address: Caesars Palace, 3570 Las Vegas Blvd. S., Las Vegas, NV, 89109, USA
Description: Ensconced in a quiet corner on the second floor of the Augustus tower of Caesars Palace, here guests will find a private world of elegance and luxury. Prices are lofty, but it’s best to put that out of mind; instead enjoy the graciously poised service and turn your eyes to lovely views of the city lights, or the stately procession of carts loaded with Champagne, breads, cheeses and sweets. The cuisine offers a vintage French sensibility and can be had either à la carte or as a tasting. In both cases, the signature dishes are the highlight, like the indulgent black truffle and artichoke soup, accompanied by toasted mushroom brioche. A truly epic wine list, the size of a medieval manuscript and arriving on its own side table, boasts both legendary bottlings and surprising finds.

Name: Restaurant H
Description: The "H" is for Hubert Duchenne, a chef hailing from Normandy, whose CV includes stints working for Akrame Benallal and Jean-François Piège. Behind the discreet, elegant façade, the intimate space done out in a chic yet cosy style accommodates fewer than 20 diners. The dishes are deftly done and always on point, whether razor clams with parsley (their signature dish), pollack with amaranth seeds – puffed and as a risotto or barbecued Jersey beef with creamy carrot and activated charcoal: almost every plate enchants the palate thanks to a remarkable balance of roasted and tangy notes. The chef's inventive and skilfully executed dishes, based on premium seasonal produce, form a single set menu – you're in for a treat!

Name: Restaurant Hervé Busset
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Hervé Busset, who describes himself as a "forager-chef", gathers ingredients from the surrounding fields and forests, supplementing them with purchases from the market opposite his restaurant. His creative cuisine is inspired by nature: comfrey, marigold, wood sorrel, meadowsweet and nasturtium flowers grace the dishes comprising his surprise set menu with harmony and finesse. Completely refurbished, the plush and inviting setting ensures privacy for guests. The bubbly, humorous sommelier has excellent wine recommendations.

Name: Restaurant Hiramatsu Kodaiji
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets not allowed
Description: From the glass walls of the airy dining room, Kyoto stretches out below, punctuated by Yasaka Pagoda. Paintings by Joan Miró hang on the walls, bringing modern art into dialogue with the borrowed scenery beyond. The cooking is contemporary in style yet grounded in classic techniques and sauces. Like Miró's paintings, known for their vivid colours, the delicately presented dishes evoke an artist's palette.

Name: Restaurant Hywel Jones by Lucknam Park
Address: Lucknam Park, Colerne, SN14 8AZ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Drive down a long, narrow lane and you will find yourself at the sumptuous Lucknam Park hotel, a Palladian mansion surrounded by formally laid gardens that is the epitome of British country house splendour. The dining room is as good-looking as the rest of the hotel, with the added bonus of commanding countryside views. Hywel Jones has held a MICHELIN Star here for over 20 years and his experience shines through in tried-and-tested dishes filled with top-drawer ingredients and expertly crafted sauces – such as Brecon lamb with a rich, glossy lamb and red wine jus.

Name: Restaurant Julien Binz
Description: On the Wine Road south of Colmar, the picture postcard wine-growing village of Ammerschwihr nestles in Kaysersberg Valley, dubbed the valley of stars - Michelin stars of course! It is home to a veteran chef and former member of the Auberge de l’Ill team, Julien Binz, for whom the world of cooking has no secrets. Against a plush, stylish background, he rustles up seasonal dishes founded on lashings of culinary technique with an Alsace accent: duck foie gras crafted two ways; a “striped” trout with choucroute and a creamy Kaefferkopf riesling sauce; tortellini of Munster cheese and a buttery stock… Perfect to brush up your gourmet classics!

Name: Restaurant Karner
Description: This quintessential Chiemgau country inn, which is over 600 years old, blends tradition and modernity to delightful effect. Warm, aged wood and premium contemporary design elements are juxtaposed to make for a tasteful and comfortable setting. Headed up by Hannes Fussel, who has worked in some of Austria's finest kitchens, the team serves up dishes packed with flavour and personality that are very much inspired by the Chiemsee region. The set menu (aptly named "A Stroll through Chiemgau") features, for example, tenderly glazed sturgeon on a ragout of artichokes, accompanied by sauerkraut beurre blanc with Alpine caviar. The nibbles served beforehand are also fantastic – think crispy pastries filled with Chiemsee smoked eel mousse. Diners can opt to have a four- or six-course format of the menu, with wine pairings available on request. Alternatively, there is the second restaurant, Westerndorfer Stube. Landgasthof Karner has pretty guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Restaurant Kasteel Heemstede
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Admire the grandeur of this fully restored 17C château as you make your way up the drive, cross the bridge and immerse yourself in its beautiful blend of historical features and contemporary luxury. Kasteel Heemstede is an exceptional and enchanting place. A seat on the waterside terrace becomes truly magical at sunset. Ollie Schuiling, meanwhile, showcases his talent through dishes of impressive intensity. His sublime sauces and eye for top-quality ingredients demonstrate his classical craftsmanship, while his inventiveness adds depth and an element of surprise. His visually appealing dishes are intricately crafted and meticulously executed. He likes to balance powerful flavours with subtle sweetness. For example, succulent pink-roasted lamb fillet is balanced by a herb coulis and lamb jus enriched with apple syrup; a subtle mandarin oil and gel give the delicate flavour of North Sea crab an extra lift. His cooking achieves depth on many levels. Be sure to explore the extensive wine list to add another dimension to the experience. One thing is certain: this truly is a fairytale castle!

Name: Restaurant Ki
Address: 111 San Pedro St., Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
Description: You'll need to read the instructions sent ahead of time to find the entrance to Chef Ki Kim's restaurant, but any navigation woes are quickly put to rest once you're inside this ten-seat spot. The contemporary Korean tasting menu pulls in global influences, and meals begin with a few bites such as shirako gimbap, a shell filled with truffle rice and diced kimchi, or crispy, tender octopus in a creamy sauce with octopus head and gochujang. Charred sugar snap peas with steelhead trout roe and tuna or creamy pasta made with perilla seed and topped with fresh winter truffle display a creative flair. Main dishes include the likes of barbecue roasted squab with foie gras sauce, and 45-day dry-aged dairy cow with golden beet jus and Korean bone broth. A mushroom ice cream sandwich seals the deal.

Name: Restaurant Kunz
Description: The Kunz family have run this establishment in the village of Bliesen for many years, working together like a well-oiled machine. The proprietor and his chef Patrick Jenal propose two set menus ("Signature" and "Traditional") – both for a minimum two diners – and an à la carte selection as a pleasing alternative. Alongside classic French dishes such as Breton sea bass with artichokes, fennel, sauce Béarnaise and jus, you will also find the well-known Kunz classics, including cordon bleu of milk-fed veal loin filled with honey-cured ham and Taleggio cheese. The quality of the ingredients is outstanding. Through the glass front of the elegant modern conservatory, you get a splendid view of the impressive parish church (St Remigius or "Bliestaldom"). Very friendly service. Alexander Kunz is also known for his event catering and the Alexander Kunz Theatre dinner show in Saarbrücken.

Name: Restaurant LA
Description: If you're not careful, you might end up walking right past the narrow façade of this mid-terrace restaurant. This charming, lively little establishment is right at home here in Basel's St Johanns-Vorstadt district. Both the slick interior and chef-patron Matthieu Judenne's seasonally inspired cuisine are modern, but for all their creativity they remain pleasingly accessible and ingredient-driven. The focus is undisputedly on flavour – soul food rather than frills is the order of the day here. This ethos is evident in dishes such as "poached egg, pea tartare, tarragon foam" and "octopus, Kalamata olives, chorizo, haricot beans, fish reduction". There is a four- or six-course surprise menu. In addition to the wine pairings, the alcohol-free alternative can also be recommended. From some tables, you can steal glimpses into the kitchen. In summer, tables are set up on the pavement outside, overlooking the tram line.

Name: Restaurant Mohn
Description: Laura Überschär and Joris Hogervorst have been running this charming country house since September 2024. Having worked at respected establishments in Germany and his native Netherlands, the chef showcases his talent through clever combinations of seasonal ingredients. Regional produce goes into delicious vegetable-forward dishes with a unique twist. The four- or five-course set menu comes either with fish and meat or in a vegetarian version. The wine list includes a selection of organic wines. To go with the set menu, there are wine pairings or an alcohol-free alternative. The front-of-house team is exceptionally friendly and professional; the chef, too, often puts in an appearance – they are happy to talk you through the dishes and provide information on the provenance of ingredients. Wood and a palette of muted tones make for a relaxed, cosy atmosphere.

Name: Restaurant Naides
Address: 708 Bush St., San Francisco, CA, 94108, USA
Description: Named after Chef Patrick Gabon's mother, there's no mistaking this jewel box operation as anything other than a labor of love. Drawing upon the fine dining experience of both Chef Gabon and partner Celine Wuu (who deftly manages the floor), Naides serves an original interpretation of Filipino cuisine in the form of a stylishly modern tasting menu. Pulling together Californian ingredients (including foraged herbs and flowers), traditional flavors and bold creativity, the dishes are as pleasing to look at as they are to eat. To illustrate: fluffy brioche “pandesal” is paired with lip-smacking braised chicken gizzards in a clever take on tangy, savory sisig, while impeccably cooked dry aged duck breast “adobo” is paired with soy jus and horseradish. The results are easy to fall for.

Name: Restaurant Pierre Grein
Description: Venture into the business park and make your way to this stylish contemporary establishment – you won't regret it! In a comfortable and light-filled glazed conservatory space, chef Pierre Grein delivers a single multi-course menu that is constantly evolving in step with the food markets. His refined modern cuisine, which draws inspiration from Provence and the Mediterranean, is both generous and technically accomplished. The sauces and jus deserve a special mention, as does the slick, friendly service.

Name: Restaurant Showw
Description: It was at the MICHELIN-starred Bougainville that Chef Dorus Floris and sommelier Lendl Mijnhijmer first crossed paths and the seeds of this partnership were sown. The synergy between them is palpable – in the impeccable service, the lounge-like ambiance of this elegant open-plan restaurant, and especially in the way everything complements the food on your plate. Chef Floris effortlessly experiments with seasonings from around the globe and refreshing nuances. His intricate sauces showcase his exceptional technique. He artfully combines perfectly seared langoustines with Jerusalem artichoke, an intense bisque enriched with espresso and curry oil for just the right amount of heat. A symphony of flavours! Sommelier Lendl Mijnhijmer knows his stuff. He serves the wines without revealing the label, encouraging diners to discover the nuances before he provides his expert commentary. The extensive à la carte menu is testament to the pair's commitment to delighting diners. Showw is the result of two passionate creative minds coming together.

Name: Restaurant Smink
Description: Built in 1625, the national monument Huize Lindenoord has kept its historical character intact. Inside, the gorgeous ornate ceilings adorned with chandeliers and graceful curves harmonise beautifully with the modern upscale decor of this restaurant. The surrounding parkland and garden lend this sumptuous setting an added air of distinction. Jan Smink, a proud farmer's son and true Frisian at heart, proves himself to be a charismatic chef who dares to push boundaries. His culinary style is thoughtful, bold and exciting. Backed by great technical prowess, he artfully dances with textures, temperatures and flavours. Think velvety potato mousseline with chives, topped with a few earthy sautéed morels. This is accompanied by mushrooms in a vibrant marinade and al dente white asparagus crowned with melted pancetta and briny caviar. A beurre blanc enriched with pancetta oil melds all these exuberant nuances into a dish that is full of depth. This is Jan Smink through and through: creative and unconventional, but never complicated for the sake of it. He infuses every dish with personality and consistently captivates with his surprise menu.

Name: Restaurant St. Barts
Address: 63 Bartholomew Close, City of London, London, EC1A 7BF, United Kingdom
Description: The Nordic-style interior design, warm colour palette and picture windows overlooking the church cloisters create a handsome and comfortable environment for this relaxed restaurant, especially when you add in the gorgeous handmade crockery and confident, affable service. The well-balanced set menus provide an immeasurably satisfying experience, focusing on prime ingredients in contemporary dishes that may be quite delicate in their appearance, but deliver plenty of wonderful flavours. Orkney scallop with Mangalitsa pork and wild garlic is a prime example.

Name: Restaurant Twenty-Two
Address: 22 Chesterton Road, Cambridge, CB4 3AX, United Kingdom
Description: This Victorian townhouse has hosted a restaurant for many years and has long been a feature of Cambridge’s dining scene. Its current guardians are Sam and Alex, who have really made it their own. Sam’s food is poised, detailed and very precise, with his technical skill shining through in beautifully presented dishes such as roasted quail with a buttery vin jaune sauce. The house has a bright, understated style and the enthusiastic service team – who explain the make-up of the dishes in full – keep the atmosphere welcoming and relaxed.

Name: Restaurant Villa Merton
Address: Am Leonhardsbrunn 12, Frankfurt on the Main, 60487, Germany
Description: For years, owner André Großfeld and the proficient team led by head chef Philippe Giar have been putting their heart and soul into running the elegant Villa Merton, establishing a real destination for connoisseurs. Their cooking style could be summed up as creative, passionate and regionally influenced. The quality of the ingredients is second to none. With its ceiling mouldings, hardwood floors and stylish details, this listed villa in the elegant diplomatic quarter makes for a prestigious setting. To the rear of the building there is a gorgeous terrace. The friendly, professional staff are always on hand, yet discreet. Tip: The Monday evening "Gourmet Special". The Chef's Table can be booked Tuesday to Saturday. In addition to the fine dining restaurant, which is open in the evening, at lunchtime there is a bistro menu.

Name: Restaurant Wolfslaar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Wolfslaar is the very definition of an established favourite. The restaurant first opened in 2000 and was awarded its first MICHELIN Star just five years later. The sense of prestige is palpable from the moment you drive onto the magnificent estate. As you approach the former coach house, you will be struck by the natural beauty of your surroundings, which you can enjoy to the full on the terrace. The interior is stylish and elegant, with walnut wood and marble creating a warm and luxurious atmosphere. In this enchanting setting, Maarten Camps takes you on an exciting adventure, in which each ingredient is thoughtfully prepared in a multitude of ways. His cuisine displays classical depth, often with Dutch influences and occasional Asian touches that lend additional character. Sole fillets cooked to a succulent finish in smoked butter are accompanied by pickled cabbage reminiscent of sauerkraut, a pork belly jus and a fish fumet emulsion. One thing is certain: the chef's sauces elevate every dish. The sommelier plays his part with an extensive wine list and perfect pairings, making your experience here all the more memorable.

Name: Restaurant Yuu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: At the start of service, the lights dim and servers pull back curtains to reveal the full kitchen team dressed in stark whites and standing at attention. This is just the beginning of a carefully choreographed performance by Chef Yuu Shimano, whose classic French training and Japanese heritage translates to beauty and boldness on the plate. The lengthy menu celebrates top-grade shellfish and proteins that waver between light and indulgent. Think smoked surf clam with celeriac or abalone risotto with nori powder. The signature duck and foie pastry is a treasure from another era, while a pre-dessert “mojito” is a sweet flash of modern-day brilliance. The warehouse-chic space is impressive in scale and carefully tended to by a quiet but attentive team.

Name: Restaurant auf Schloss Filseck
Description: With its beautiful grounds, Schloss Filseck is not only a place for art, culture, socialising and relaxation, but also a destination for food lovers! The restaurant blends a classical atmosphere with modern touches, and the wooden ceiling and rough-hewn stone walls lend it old-world rustic charm. Alternatively, you can dine on the wonderful terrace in the courtyard. Daniele Corona's cuisine draws on Italian and Mediterranean influences, with intricate, multifaceted dishes. Inspired by the historic Via Francigena, the legendary pilgrimage route to Rome, he gives Italian cooking traditions a creative, contemporary twist. In the evening, you can embark on this culinary journey with the six-course "Piccola" or eight-course "Grande" set menu, both available in vegetarian versions. There is a well-curated wine list, and expert advice to help you choose. At lunchtime, the concept is quite different: "mezzogiorno" is a simpler, reasonably priced set menu. A handy extra: A free shuttle service operates within a radius of around 20km of Schloss Filseck (booking required two days in advance).

Name: Restaurant de l'Hôtel de Ville
Description: In the centre of the village, near the bell tower, this quintessential rural establishment celebrates tradition quietly and simply. Beneath the vaulted ceiling of the dining room (refreshingly cool in summertime), you will taste a seasonal Gallic lineup with a choice of menus and courses. Grégory Halgand conjures up creative dishes such as asparagus, grapefruit and pistachio or Brittany lobster, red beetroot, blackberries and fish bisque. The desserts are the work of Audrey Feutren-Halgand, who also respects the seasons, with delicacies such as a medley of apricots (stewed, jellied and grilled), flanked by a frothy coconut mousse. Audrey is also responsible for the house-made bread. Artwork (paintings and sculptures) graces the interior, and there is a pleasant outdoor patio for a final alfresco flourish. The ‘café’ section offers a brasserie-style menu and a more casual vibe and there is a cosy lounge with a fine selection of cigars.

Name: Restaurant de la Loire
Address: 30 rue de la Berge, Pouilly-sous-Charlieu, 42720, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set on the banks of the Loire, this inn, refurbished in a tasteful modern vein, is the bolthole of Marie and Fabien Raux (born in northern France, the chef’s eclectic career has taken him to fine establishments from Morocco to Alsace). The chef crafts dishes in the zeitgeist, curated into a single set menu and starring seasonal produce. The vegetables come straight from the nearly 5 acres of garden and orchard that supply 90% of the restaurant’s needs, even in winter! The remainder is sourced from a handful of local producers: Loire zander, lamb, rabbit… Everything tastes of something in this gutsy lineup of flavours served in a warm jovial vibe. In summer, alfresco dining on the lovely terrace shaded by linden trees in the garden is heavenly.

Name: Restaurant Überfahrt
Description: Cornelia Fischer, who heads up the kitchen at the fine dining restaurant of the splendid Althoff Seehotel Überfahrt, is by no means a rookie when it comes to running a kitchen. Most recently head chef at Zur Schwane in Volkach, she is now showcasing her contemporary take on classic cuisine here at Überfahrt. Excellent ingredients go into the two four-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. The fresh, tenderly cooked Breton langoustine with delicious braised fennel and a classic shellfish and orange sauce is one outstanding example. Additional dishes can be swapped in or out to tailor your meal, or you can dine à la carte. The food is complemented by a wonderfully curated international wine list. The sleek and stylish interior design is also appealing, and service is provided by an excellent and pleasingly laid-back team. Tip: Book the Chef's Table and enjoy a four-course set menu served in the kitchen every first Thursday evening of the month.

Name: Retama
Description: Retama (“broom” in English), takes its name from this bush with yellow blossom that is a very common sight on Spain’s Central Meseta and in the area around La Caminera, an exclusive and tranquil country hotel with a 9-hole golf course and even its own aerodrome. Its restrained yet charming backdrop of bare tables and Nordic-inspired decor is the perfect setting in which to discover the cooking of chef Miguel Ángel Expósito – a champion of local ingredients and produce and the culinary heritage of traditional La Mancha recipes. His cuisine revolves around three tasting menus (Tradición, Finca La Caminera and Retama) that showcase the restaurant’s solid ties with this region (wild rabbit à la royale, “sequence of partridge from our estate”, shank of wild boar, beetroot escabeche etc), reinterpreting dishes from a modern perspective that incorporates the latest culinary techniques. The views of the countryside from your table are an absolute delight!

Name: Retroscena
Address: Largo del Teatro 3, Porto San Giorgio, 63822, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Porto San Giorgio’s picturesque old town, among the exposed brick houses, is a dining room of refined minimalist elegance, with just a few tables and an intimate atmosphere. When guests are not captivated by the dishes, they will find themselves fascinated by the open kitchen, where the crew works with precision, creating courses that express the restaurant’s contemporary signature style, characterised by a deft use of acidity as a distinctive note. Although the team is young, the technical level is high and the cuisine, while retaining a few echoes of its Modenese training, develops above all through an inventiveness capable of stirring deep emotions. For a broad and creative overview, the ten-course Labor Limae tasting menu is the ideal choice, designed to capture nuances and ideas in constant evolution. The wine offering is excellent too: a cellar in continual expansion, with carefully curated selections and well-conceived by-the-glass options. Completing the picture is a convincing selection of cocktails, spirits and liqueurs, further enriching the overall experience.

Name: Reuter
Description: Founded in 1894, this is a family business with a long tradition – and genuine dedication to match. In the beautifully refined and elegant restaurant of the hotel of the same name, Iris Bettinger has made a name for herself with her "interregiomediterraneurasian" menu – a blend of regional, Mediterranean and Asian influences. After stints at Hotel Colombi in Freiburg and Käfer-Schänke and Mandarin Oriental in Munich, she took over the kitchen here in 2007 – which makes her the fourth generation at the helm. Her cooking marries classical French foundations with regional character and international ideas. Dishes such as "crispy Münsterland Töttchen (veal ragout) praline, warm-marinated veal tongue, turnip greens salad & mustard fruits" are based on fresh, top-notch seasonal ingredients, often sourced from nearby producers. Service is pleasingly professional throughout, and the passionate sommelier is on hand to guide you through a well-stocked list of around 250 wines.

Name: Revithia
Address: Temenni Mahallesi, Eski Kayakapı Mahallesi, Davut Ağa Sokak No:1, Ürgüp, 50400, Türkiye
Description: Before you've even taken a bite, Revithia captures your heart. The restaurant is set in Kayakapi – the name of both the hotel and the UNESCO-listed historic neighbourhood. Inside, the traditional decor exudes charm; outside, the terrace affords breathtaking views over the valley and the city. And the celebration of the region continues on the menu. Duran Özdemir and his team use the finest local ingredients in a homage to age-old, nearly forgotten recipes, which they spruce up here and there with playful textures.The way in which different textures of aubergine – including an airy dip and a cream with tahini – come together so harmoniously in combination with a fruity, sweet and sour vinegar is captivating. And then there's the meltingly tender veal tail with a refined demi-glace, chickpea-and-sweetcorn purée and plum compote finished with mint leaves. This is ingredient-led cooking, in which every element bursts with flavour – intense yet silky smooth. The menu changes three to four times a year, bringing a sense of renewal every season.

Name: Rezdôra
Address: 27 E. 20th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Rezdôra presents itself as a focused exploration of the cuisine of Emilia-Romagna, bringing the region’s pasta traditions to a well-designed space in the Flatiron District. The menu centers on handmade pastas and classic preparations, with an emphasis on regional forms and familiar flavor profiles. Starters like gnocco fritto arrive as puffy, fried pillows served with high-quality prosciutto di Parma, mortadella and guanciale. Pastas include anolini di Parma with a pork filling and gramigna tossed with a slow-braised sausage ragù in bianco, finished with Parmigiano-Reggiano. Dessert continues the regional theme with a torta d'oliva. This is cooking that favors tradition and simplicity, offering a straightforward interpretation of Emilia-Romagna’s culinary canon.

Name: Rezzano Cucina e Vino
Address: Via Asilo Maria Teresa 34, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
Description: The historic family restaurant on the Ligurian Levant sees young Matteo in the kitchen, marking the fifth generation of Rezzano involved in this field. This year they've also recruited Jorg Giubbani, who boasts stellar experiences in the area, further elevating the quality of the offering with three tasting menus primarily dedicated to seafood and gardens (three in total) to deliver dishes consistently delicate but flavourful, balanced in pairings, never contrived and visually striking. We were particularly conquered by the caponata of mackerel and desserts, all served in the lovely veranda overlooking the setting sun and central square or at tables just beyond the welcoming, wooden-toned entrance.

Name: Ricardo Temiño
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Ricardo Temiño's latest venture sits adjacent to La Fábrica, but they share the same entrance. It is a space with its own character where he aims to take Burgos' rich gastronomic culture one step further. The experience begins with the first appetisers after the chef's welcome, where the fully stocked wine cellar is located, then he will take you through the kitchen to see how the lamb is matured, and finally to the modern dining room, with a semi-open kitchen. Here, the cuisine, which is more conceptual and typical of modern market culture, is brought to life through two tasting menus (Camino Corto and Camino Largo) inspired by the chef's own journey and family life (there are nods to his honeymoon, his grandmother, the La Fábrica restaurant in its infancy, etc.), as well as the great routes that have marked the province's storied history (the wool route, the fish route, the Cid route, the Camino de Santiago, etc.). They’re putting their own spin on some local tapas!

Name: Riccitelli Bistró
Address: Callejón de La Reta 750, Mendoza, M5509, Argentina
Description: At the Riccitelli Bistró, they have gone one step further to bring together fine cuisine, an appreciation of wine, and sustainability. The Matias Riccitelli Wines bodega in Luján de Cuyo has created this restaurant, built out of remodelled containers and “planted” amid old vineyards, to enhance its wine experience. Chef Juan Ventureyra’s cuisine, which can be sampled in an informal dining room or on the lower terrace, explores Mendoza’s culinary roots on two menus (Mendoza and Argentina, both of which include a visit to the winery) with a strong focus on native, locally sourced produce and ingredients mainly from its own gardens. Vegetables play a starring role here, hence the vegetarian influence in its “farm to table” concept (in summer, it grows over 90 varieties of tomato from seed), enhanced by adding protein to its dishes. We particularly enjoyed the snacks here as well as the dish entitled “Espinal” (duck, cauliflower, apricot and mustard).

Name: Riff
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: A German chef who considers himself Valencian at heart is at the helm of this restaurant where he constantly reinvents the food on offer. Globe-trotting chef Bernd Knöller has moved onto an important stage in his career which sees him interacting with his natural surroundings. This has led to him making a name for himself on the local food scene through his occasionally anarchic and always liberated vision of creative Mediterranean cuisine. From his kitchen, open to the dining room and surrounded by a bar that allows us to watch him work, he champions a fixed-price à la carte (three dishes of your choosing) and two set menus, one at lunchtime and another tasting menu (the latter has a vegetarian option). Through his dishes you will discover his passion for charcoal grilling (even vegetables), the extraordinary fish and seafood he acquires at the fish market and, of course, those rice dishes that showcase his love for his adopted land. You can't leave without trying the Arroz brut!

Name: Rijnzicht
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Briefly seared langoustine is served with a punchy sauce infused with tandoori spices, complemented by watermelon and pickled red onion for a refreshing contrast, as well as an intense crunch of slivers of Wagyu fat, Wagyu short rib, lemongrass foam and a langoustine bisque jus with meat oil and ginger. This signature dish is typical of the inventive, highly technical creations that demonstrate Mike Cornelissen's talent. Representing the fourth generation of his family to run the restaurant, he has made it entirely his own. The interior has been transformed into a sleek and stylish space, and the terrace has retained its original charm. It is, above all, his creativity and the meticulous presentation of his dishes that impress. His spectacular plating is endlessly intriguing, and his imagination knows no bounds. Fine local ingredients such as trout from 't Smallert farm and Betuwe cherries are carefully combined with international seasonings, which he often uses to add nuances of umami. This is a unique culinary adventure, rounded off by toasting your own marshmallow over a tabletop charcoal fire. Choosing between the à la carte selection and the "Signatuur" and "Innovatie" set menus is quite a challenge!

Name: Rincón de Diego
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant with a little bit of history and with that ‘savoir-faire’ that only comes with time, this is a great option!The restaurant is split between two floors with a highly contemporary ambience, where guests can savour cuisine by the acclaimed duo of chef Diego Campos, one of the bastions behind the resurgence of local gastronomy, and his son Rubén, who brings a fresh approach to the proposal. The à la carte, closely linked to seafaring tradition from a modern perspective, is completed with three set menus (Gastronómico, Súmmum and Del Cava). It is pleasantly surprising to see how well this updated take on traditional cuisine that prizes the fish and seafood from Cambrils (such as sea bass with pil pil and Maresme peas or cod loin El Barquero, its tripe and sauces of ‘Cap i Pota’) coexists with the delicious rice dishes that are made in these lands (here they offer a wonderful Mediterranean red lobster rice).

Name: Ristorante del Lago
Address: Via Acquapartita 147, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Leaving the main road behind, a series of hairpin bends leads up to Acquapartita, a hamlet at an altitude of almost 800 metres, where one of the most interesting places in the area is to be found. Here, the Bravaccini brothers have built a solid and well-balanced venture, naturally dividing their roles: in the kitchen, Simone proudly champions the restaurant’s connection to the local area, creating a menu that showcases local produce such as game, mushrooms and trout; among the most representative dishes are the ‘Spaghetto cacio e pepe with marinated trout’, which was also praised by the inspectors, and the flavourful ‘Charcoal-grilled quail, stuffed with livers and black truffle’, not to mention a selection of delicious and well-crafted desserts. In the dining room, Andrea welcomes guests with expertise and a friendly, convivial manner, orchestrating precise and attentive service while managing a truly encyclopaedic wine list, divided into two volumes featuring some 1,600 labels: there is a strong focus on Italian wines and an equally extensive selection of French wines, accounting for nearly 40% of the range; in addition to its breadth, the quality of the selection and the excellent service are particularly impressive.

Name: River Café
Address: Thames Wharf, Rainville Road, Hammersmith, London, W6 9HA, United Kingdom
Description: It should go without saying, but be sure to ask for a seat on the terrace at this icon of London's Italian restaurant scene. The on-view kitchen with its wood-fired oven dominates the stylish and buzzing riverside room and the menu bursts with authentic Italian flavours which make one’s mouth water in anticipation. The honest, hearty dishes have a rustic Italian simplicity, relying as they do on the quality of their ingredients, whether that be clams, crab or wild sea bass. Arguably the best Italian wine list in London is the icing on the cake.

Name: Robuchon Monaco
Address: Esplanade du Portier, Monaco, 98000, Principality of Monaco
Description: On an esplanade overlooking Boulevard du Larvotto and the Japanese Garden, this restaurant pays tribute to the great French chef. Behind a swanky black façade, a rattan-furnished terrace leads into a cosy dining area with green-upholstered banquettes and chairs and a marble floor. While the famous Robuchon mashed potato is served with each main course, the master’s influence remains discreet. The à la carte lineup stars pedigree Gallic classics with a scattering of Mediterranean notes: carpaccio of greater amberjack in citrus fruit and pink berries, salt crusted seabass, free-range poultry and morels in vin jaune, Rossini beef and Périgueux sauce.

Name: Rocca
Address: 323 W. Palm Ave., Tampa, FL, 33602, USA
Description: Chef Bryce Bonsack blends his New York know-how with Italian training to great effect in this of-the-moment eatery.
