Ingredients are sourced from the Wye Valley and their own kitchen garden, and are used in dishes with a creative streak. Middle White suckling pig is one of their signatures, prepared with a nose-to-tail ethos that includes a croquette of minced pig's head, an offal faggot and compressed shoulder. There’s also a particularly creative vegetarian menu. Bedrooms follow the theme of bringing nature inside.

Name: The Wilderness
Address: Unit B, 27 Warstone Lane, Birmingham, B18 6JQ, United Kingdom
Description: With its dark and moody colour scheme, informal vibe and rocking soundtrack, this excellently run restaurant brings something a little different to the Birmingham food scene. Chef Alex Claridge is known for the originality of his cooking, which is always underpinned by superb ingredients (often aged in-house) and clever balancing of both flavours and textures. Stand-out dishes could include a take on brioche bread and butter pudding with barbecued brassicas, or a delicate dessert of smoked chocolate and prunes. Accompany your menu with either an interesting wine flight or creative non-alcoholic pairing.

Name: The Zillers Rooftop Gastronomy
Description: This restaurant occupies the former family home of the German architect Ernst Zillers, who came to Athens to design some of its public buildings, fell in love with the city and remained here for the rest of his life. The building, which is situated next to the Greek Orthodox cathedral and has now been converted into a hotel (Zillers Boutique Hotel), boasts a rooftop terrace and multi-purpose Roof Garden with fine view of the cathedral and the Acropolis. The Zillers restaurant is only open in the evening and chef Vasilis Roussos offers two tasting menus: Synecdoche and Synthesis, both with creative dishes of traditional Greek influence and touches of international flavour. One standout dish was the Prawn Valley, a refreshing combination of raw prawns with a delicate tomato sauce, bergamot and kumquat that will definitely leave a lasting memory. The wine list also features a variety of Greek options to pair with your meal.

Name: Theodor's
Description: This restaurant in the Beuel district has an inviting, chic and contemporary feel. At the helm are siblings Jana and Fritz Benson, who go about their work with palpable dedication. In the open kitchen, the chef-patron and his team put together a creative seasonal set menu, available in four to six courses, which can be supplemented with optional additional courses. The craftsmanship on display and the quality of the produce impress in equal measure – a case in point is the Dieppe scallops with a fruity, tangy pineapple vinaigrette, finished with a delicate mace-infused foam. Each dish is also presented in a pleasingly clean, unfussy style. The front-of-house team, headed up by the proprietress herself, provides attentive, expert service, with the chefs also known to lend a hand. Motorists can park at the Tiefgarage Rathausplatz.

Name: Thierry Schwartz - Table Naturelle
Description: The scene is unabashedly rustic: think lots of wood, displays of seasonal vegetables and a log-burning fire. Thierry Schwartz conjures up legible dishes in which plants take the limelight, although not to the exclusion of meat: tomatoes cooked for 7 hours in dried lime, shoulder of lamb with tetragonia in a wood-burning oven… Impressive selection of over 1700 (natural of course) wines.

Name: Ti Trin Ned
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: The up-and-coming former industrial district of Kanalbyen plays host to this contemporary, design-led restaurant on the ground floor of a modern apartment building at the water’s edge; take in the view over the Lillebælt Strait, while the service team look after your every need. Behind the scenes Michael Nørtoft creates refined, technically accomplished fish and vegetable dishes with deceptively simple names – maybe ‘brill, asparagus and ramson’ or ‘blackberries, cep and fennel' – which belie the complexity that goes into their creation. To complement are some interesting wine and juice pairings.

Name: Tien Hsiang Lo
Address: B1, The Landis, 41, Section 2, Minquan East Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, 104, Taiwan Region
Description: The Ten scenes of West Lake – iconic spots in Hangzhou – are the inspiration behind this hotel restaurant's modern decor. The head chef reimagines traditional Hangzhou recipes with new ideas. Try his fairy duck soup or Dongpo pork with a trio of sides. Eating here is a multifaceted experience, with tea sommeliers who are well-versed in tea pairings and, at dinnertime, calligraphers who turn your order into artwork for you to take home.

Name: Tilia
Description: This glass and steel cube in the middle of the garden of the former Grand Hotel in Dobbiaco has been home to the Tilia restaurant since 2010 and is now more intimate than ever, with just five tables and seating for 12 diners (booking is highly recommended). Chef Chris Oberhammer’s menu is enticing, featuring just under 20 dishes with a modern yet regional flavour. Many of the ingredients (such as the flour and some of the meat) are sourced from the “Klaude” farm which is run by one of the chef’s childhood friends with whom he works very closely, while other more exotic fare comes from further afield, adding luxury ingredients such as caviar, truffles (in season) and prawns to the mix. Anita Mancini oversees the front of house with skill and professionalism, as well as taking care of the wine list which includes a selection of international labels.

Name: Timberyard
Address: 10 Lady Lawson Street, Edinburgh, EH3 9DS, United Kingdom
Description: A big red door indicates that you have arrived at this rustic warehouse conversion, in which the chefs practise a culinary ethos that centres around outstanding produce and letting it speak for itself. It takes a lot of skill and no little ability to take just a few prime ingredients and fashion dishes that are so well defined and satisfying, and the kitchen here pulls it off with aplomb, in the likes of turbot with girolles, suyo cucumber and smoked roe. The lovely service team have brilliant attention to detail and play their part in a wonderful all-round experience.

Name: Timilìa
Description: A charming little Italian restaurant run by a chef who hails from Lorraine but has Sicilian roots, and his Milanese partner. By no means fixated on the classic repertoire, the restaurant serves a tasting menu entitled "Scoperta della Pasta", which showcases their house-made pasta. Much care goes into dishes that incorporate top-notch, at times premium ingredients, many imported from Italy. With its pared-back decor, just a handful of tables, dark parquet flooring, white walls and colourful Abstract paintings, the interior is both contemporary and intimate. Excellent selection of local wines.

Name: Tinèlle
Description: The historic Het Predikheren served as a convent and military hospital from the 17C. Today it has morphed into a venue devoted to culture and fine dining. The left wing is home to this vibrant, modern eatery starring Jenny Callens in the unstarched, buzzy dining room, while veteran chef Ken Verschueren joyfully dusts the cobwebs off culinary tradition. Ideal to dig into Franco-Belgian grub, free of fussy, futile frills and at prices that make sense. It would be a crime to miss the lunchtime menu that changes daily. The chef demonstrates his love of fine produce, crafting dishes that bear witness to his consummate flair for contrast. Crab is a staple on the menu, with, for example, North Sea crab cannelloni, set off by a stunning marriage of tangy grapefruit and fresh, crisp fennel. Chef Verschueren deploys the full gamut of his culinary mastery in chilled seabass and crispy cuttlefish dotted with playful touches, like a perfectly judged dollop of soy sauce on fieduà pasta and its accompanying cuttlefish sauce. Tinèlle is synonymous with crisp, legible, fuss-free flavours and authentic sauces. The knockout wine list further confirms the establishment’s dedication to quality.

Name: Tipken's by Nils Henkel
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is located in Severin's Resort & Spa, where guests can enjoy a stay in pleasantly understated luxury. In summer, take an aperitif on the quiet, leafy terrace behind the building, before heading inside to the upscale, stylish modern dining space to savour René Verse's culinary creations, which are crafted with precision and feel delightfully effortless. Nils Henkel, after whom this place is named, has clearly put his own stamp on the menu. His vegetable-centric cuisine, with which he made a name for himself once upon a time, is skilfully integrated here, including in both set menus, "Flora" and "Fauna". Ingredients of the very finest quality are showcased in dishes such as "Fonduta Ravioli – porcini, Comté foam, thyme broth" or "Carabinero – coconut milk, pea, calamansi". Courses can be swapped between set menus or ordered à la carte. The wine list deserves a closer look too, particularly the excellent selection of mature Bordeaux wines. Alcohol-free beverage pairings are also available, developed anew in house for every dish.

Name: Tisane
Description: Located in the chic Augustinerhof building complex in the Old Town, this is a cool, vibrant and trendy "chef's table restaurant". The open kitchen is the centrepiece – not only providing a fascinating display to watch, but also a clever interplay of aromas, background music and communication. Diners sit at a striking counter with a natural stone finish; interaction between chefs and diners is a key part of the concept. You experience first-hand how René Stein and his team prepare a modern, creative set menu comprising pleasantly pared-down dishes made from first-rate ingredients – pre-order the vegetarian alternative. An original touch that heightens the curiosity and anticipation: At each seat, a daily Polaroid photo showcasing the main components of the menu replaces the menu itself! On Tue and Wed, 5-10pm, a bar concept takes over the premises – no set menu and no need to book.

Name: Tivoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Along the road leading to the Falzarego Pass, at the foot of the Tofane mountains, in a typical Alpine house just outside the town centre, Graziano Prest offers a wide range of dishes ranging from traditional mountain fare to more creative creations, featuring both meat and fish, with a particular flair that is also evident in the desserts, as well as a vegetarian menu. An extraordinary selection of wines: the cellar houses more than 1,300 wines from leading producers, historic vintages and superb French wines of the very highest quality. The panoramic terrace offers picture-postcard views of the centre of Cortina – the same view that can be admired from inside, provided you book one of the two sought-after tables by the window well in advance.

Name: Toki
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: Savour Japanese cuisine in this exclusive restaurant bearing the hallmark of famous sommelier Marcos Granda, where the full focus is on enjoying the experience without worrying about the time (“toki” in Japanese). In this intimate and exclusive setting centred around a single sushi bar that is designed to personalise the guest experience to the full (Toki only has six seats!), chef Tadayoshi Teddy Motoa guides us on a magnificent journey through the history and evolution of Japanese cooking. His tasting menu shows us how the preparation of nigiri has changed over time (especially in the preparation of rice). In so doing, he enters into a dialogue with guests through three recipes (one contemporary, one from the 18C, and the third from the 16C) that are the height of delicacy, as well as premium ingredients that will delight the tastebuds. The extensive sake list is an added bonus.

Name: Tom Brown at The Capital
Address: 22-24 Basil Street, Knightsbridge, London, SW3 1AT, United Kingdom
Description: After running his own restaurant Cornerstone in Hackney, Chef Tom Brown returned in 2025 to the genteel surroundings of The Capital Hotel, the place where his reputation was first established. The dining room is intimate, immaculate and perfect for that discreet lunch or celebratory dinner. As is the case with all Brown's endeavours, the focus is largely on seafood and the visually thrilling dishes make great use of superb prime ingredients, whether that be turbot with a beautiful array of courgettes or more inventive dishes like the cuttlefish ‘cacio e pepe’.

Name: Tomy & Co
Description: Two minutes from Rue Saint Dominique, this establishment bears the hallmark of Cambodian-born chef, Tomy Gousset, who is forging ahead in a no-holds barred, gleeful approach. A relative latecomer to food (23 years old), he perfected his skills at the Meurice, Taillevent and Boulud in New York. Today he plays a gourmet-bistro score, firmly in tune with his era, placing his “karma” (his own words) at the service of taste and the ingredient in a genuine spirit of local sourcing. His motto: “Simplicity and sophistication”, or, in our words this time: “A slap up good meal”!

Name: Topolobampo
Address: 445 N. Clark St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
Description: This jewel in Rick Bayless' crown welcomes a rush of diners for original Mexican food with an upscale twist. The menu, boasting a panoply of flavors and textures, spins with the seasons. Though each dish is rooted in tradition, there's no shortage of flair, as in a celebration of the cuisine of Puebla which featured the memela divorciada. This oval of griddled corn masa, blue on one side and yellow on the other, was filled with black beans, topped with seafood longaniza, and set in a duo of luscious salsas. Other highlights revealed tamal colado presented with roasted poblano cream; and slow-roasted salmon dressed with Pueblan green pipian and smoked leeks. The beverage pairing is an education in agave spirits and is highly recommended to accentuate your meal.

Name: Torakuro
Address: B1F, Imperial Hotel Tokyo Main, 1-1-1 Uchisaiwaicho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 100-8558, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘Tradition and innovation always travel together’ is the credo of the Imperial Hotel. ‘Growth and happiness for the future’ is the motto of the Ishikawa Group. Together the partners founded Torakuro, whose cuisine is guided by both convictions. French techniques such as consommé and confit are overlaid with Japanese traditions like dashi soup stock and char-grilling. One of the Imperial Hotel’s founders, Eiichi Shibusawa, once said, ‘Serve the customer courteously and you create a memory for a lifetime’. Here, that spirit is taken to heart.

Name: Torien
Address: 292 Elizabeth St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
Description: Blacked-out windows mark the entrance to this NoHo sibling to Tokyo's Torishiki; diners are then buzzed in at street level, both of which add to the mysterious proceedings. A staff member then pulls back a curtain—et voila—you're here. Inside, Executive Chef Hideo An may be found working his skills like a master pianist—turning, fanning, saucing and brushing. It's a pristine workspace and the menu is a tribute to the yakitori tradition. Naturally, chicken takes center stage, though binchotan charcoal plays as vital a role as the fowl itself, with the aroma becoming one with the space and skewer. Begin with an appetizer like their nikomi, and though chicken is the focus, there are vegetable skewers like broccoli or Brussels sprouts.

Name: Torisaki
Description: Greatly impressed by a master yakitori chef, he sought an apprenticeship with him. Wearing a twisted hachimaki and fanning the charcoal with an uchiwa fan are both traditions inherited from his mentor. Grilling brand-name chicken from Fukushima close to an intense charcoal fire is another legacy of his training. He incorporates locally raised Kyoto chicken to support regional producers while also showcasing his own individuality. The restaurant's name, Torisaki, stands for 'yakitori no saki', meaning the future of yakitori. True to this name, he is determined to stay ahead of the times and lead the way forwards.

Name: Torisho Ishii
Description: The purely Japanese interior, with its orderly row of lacquer trays, is a setting fit for a kappo. The chef’s kaiseki experience manifests everywhere in the restaurant’s offerings. The name-brand chicken he uses is tender and richly flavoursome. Salt is used with restraint; instead, a light dipping sauce brings out the native flavour of the chicken. Breast meat fried with crumbled rice crackers and rice cooked with seasoned chicken mince are ideas that spring from Japanese cuisine. The restaurant’s name means ‘chicken artisan’, and it’s not hard to see why.

Name: Torkel
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With its winning combination of historical and modern features, this restaurant has a really appealing look. The dominant feature of the dining room is a lovingly preserved old wine press (or Torkel in the local dialect), which blends in well with the modern decor that surrounds it. The conservatory is fantastic: the walls can be open up, so you feel like you're sitting on a terrace among the vines with views of the Rhine Valley. Proprietor Ivo Berger and his team propose a contemporary take on classic cuisine. Dishes such as "hand-dived scallop, miso nage, radish, quinoa", as well as grilled meat and fish, showcase top-quality ingredients. presented without unnecessary fuss, they impress with their balance and flavour. An attentive and charming front-of-house team provides excellent wine recommendations – the list of around 850 labels includes both wines from the estate and an outstanding international selection.

Name: Torrisi
Address: 275 Mulberry St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: There is perfection in the details at Torrisi, where waiters are crisply dressed in dinner jackets and tables are draped in pressed linens, but the buzzy warmth is as charming as the good looks. Nestled inside the landmark Puck Building, this highly imaginative restaurant expertly balances the creative and the familiar. Nothing feels copied or contrived, and while some of the dishes may seem familiar, they've all been revamped with panache. The team caters to excited diners who feast on items like tuna with pickled caponata, penne with sauteed baby chanterelles in a luscious butter sauce, and an Italian riff on Dover sole with Francese sauce. Affogato arrives in an oversized martini glass with vanilla ice cream, chocolate fudge, and an espresso granita.

Name: Tosara
Description: The book ‘Tosara no Ryori’ (‘Ten-Plate Cuisine’) became the guiding light of the chef’s life. One line in the book defines ‘cuisine’ as ‘a word that conveys boundless gratitude to the greatness of Nature for the vast bounty the Earth provides’. Deeply moved by the author’s values and perspective on life, the chef expresses the fascination of the natural world and food producers through a prix fixe menu of ten courses. Cuisine formed from his bonds with others is the tale of the chef’s journey.

Name: Tosca
Address: Rue de la Mairie 8, Geneva, 1207, Switzerland
Description: In the heart of Eaux-Vives, Tosca embodies Tuscany’s stylish dolce vita. Ivan Baretti, born in Florence and who trained at L’Arpège in Paris, blends his command of Italian tradition with a contemporary Gallic twist. Baretti’s expertise, skill and flair are harnessed to coaxing out the best of fresh premium produce. Highlights include Piedmont-style ravioli filled with guinea fowl, 36-month-old parmigiano and a rich game sauce. A sleek, fashionable interior, which mingles frescoes and velvet upholstered armchairs, leads onto a lovely alfresco summer terrace, while the front-of-house team is friendly and on-the-ball. Just the ticket for fans of la cucina italiana and a fine selection of Tuscan wines to boot.

Name: Tosca di Angelo
Address: 102F, The Ritz-Carlton, International Commerce Centre, 1 Austin Road West, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Sicilian chef champions dishes that may look deceptively unfussy on the plate, but their obvious refinement makes them especially delicious. His signatures include house-made pasta and blue lobster dishes, while his modern take on rum babà is quite something. The set menu comprises seasonal and signature dishes, making it the best way to sample all specialities. Did I mention its sweeping views from the 102nd floor?

Name: Tour D'argent Tokyo
Address: Lobby floor, Hotel New Otani Tokyo (The Main), 4-1 Kioicho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, 102-8578, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The Tokyo location was born from a meeting between the founder of the Hotel New Otani and the owner of the Paris flagship. The original restaurant, established in 1582, is said to be where the fork was first introduced. The legendary ‘Three Emperors Dinner’ at the 1867 Paris Exposition remains a historic milestone. Among the enduring specialities, the Three Emperors- style goose foie gras remains a constant. This stage for haute cuisine continues to foster connections and inspire harmony.

Name: Tour d'Argent
Address: 15 quai de la Tournelle, Paris, 75005, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in 1582, this legendary restaurant continues to enchant diners with its magical view of the River Seine and Notre-Dame, its huge open kitchen and its steel kinetic-effect ceiling. In the kitchen, chef and Meilleur Ouvrier de France Yannick Franques strikes the perfect balance between traditional and contemporary, not least on account of his fine work with sauces. Presented in the form of an elegant triptych, the menu features a modernised take on the house classics, which are masterfully finished tableside, as well as more personal elements that reflect the chef's years spent in the South of France. The extraordinary wine cellar is home to over 300 000 bottles. Finally, there is the ground-floor Bar des Maillets d'Argent, done out in a traditional 1930s style, and Le Toit de la Tour, a lush roof terrace with a panoramic view, where you can enjoy a drink as you contemplate Paris.

Name: Tout à Fait
Description: Tradition and originality are combined with a sure touch at Tout à Fait. Outside, you have the charm of Maastricht's centre, while inside you can enjoy the ambience of this chic restaurant, in which minimalist design underscores the character of the historical building. This is definitely a place where diners can feel comfortable – all the more so once the first amuse-bouches arrive at your table. Bart Ausems is a passionate chef who has accumulated years of know-how when it comes to the classics – he has retained a MICHELIN Star since 2002! No one can top him when it comes to cooking venison saddle to a perfect medium rare. He elevates it with a rich flourish – slow-braised venison shoulder crowned with foie gras – and ties it all together with a deep, robust jus. His light sauces and penchant for zesty notes denote his awareness of modern influences. Chef Ausems also likes to demonstrate his range of techniques by cooking top-notch produce such as pigeon on the rotisserie. This is an institution where the dedication runs deep – the chef even lights a candle before each service for good measure.

Name: Towa
Description: The name is both a play on the owner’s name and a prayer for everlasting prosperity. The menu combines kaiseki and beef, showcasing Japan’s famous wagyu. Tsukuri and wanmono start the evening, celebrating the season. A procession of wagyu variations follows: beef-tail spring rolls, char-grilled tongue, and a main dish of beef cutlet. Japanese and beef dishes delight in equal measure.

Name: Toya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name is a nod to Tōya, a famous volcanic lake in the Shikotsu-Tōya National Park on Japan's northern island of Hokkaido. Globe-trotting chef-owner, Loïc Villemin considers the region to be something of a culinary paradise, in which wild fish, plants and herbs abound. In addition, extensive animal husbandry and premium market gardening are practised there – plenty to enrich this restaurant overlooking a verdant golf course and with a trendy and soothing nature-inspired decor. The chef was also a disciple of some of the great culinary masters: Jean-Georges Klein, Nicolas Le Bec, Bernard Loiseau and Arnaud Lallement. He loves working with fine ingredients to create a mystery menu that changes on a weekly basis. In his generous compositions, cutting-edge technique and creativity find powerful expression in wonderful flavours. Unmissable!

Name: Toyo Eatery
Address: The Alley at Karrivin, Karrivin Plaza, 2316 Chino Roces Avenue Extension, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: "Toyo", Tagalog for "soy sauce", hints at the restaurant's appreciation of apparently simple items that in fact take time and are complex to craft. Ingredients are sourced exclusively from the Philippines; fermenting and preserving is done on site. The chef balances seasoning – soy, vinegar and fish sauce – to enhance the dishes and highlight the natural flavours. For a traditional experience, try kamayan: a shared meal served on banana leaf, eaten with your hands.

Name: Tozentei
Description: In a residential area near Kitano Tenmangu, this family-run restaurant occupies a converted former home. Japanese touches and a homely warmth give the space an inviting feel. The cooking lets the ingredients speak for themselves, while inventive pairings bring added interest. A signature dish is tilefish steamed with plums and kelp, inspired by the natural affinity between white fish and plums. Such subtle twists in flavour invite another sip of sake.

Name: Trattoria Zappatori
Description: Beyond the porticoes, a secluded courtyard leads to an early twentieth-century building that now houses a historic trattoria, transformed by chef Christian Milone into a restaurant of refined elegance. Its original features have been intelligently preserved and enhanced by contemporary touches, creating a harmonious dialogue between past and present. At carefully laid tables, almost tailored in their precision, the culinary offering unfolds through two distinct routes: on the one hand, the “1975… le mie origini” menu, which revisits Piedmontese roots with balance and understated imagination; on the other, “Materie Prime”, a freer expression of creativity in which individual ingredients become the focus of entire tasting experiences. Particular attention is paid to the provenance of the produce, much of it coming from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden or from carefully selected local suppliers. For a more immersive experience, a chef’s table overlooking the kitchen is also available.

Name: Trattoria al Cacciatore - La Subida
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the heart of Collio, among gentle hills just steps from the Slovenian border, this restaurant stands as a true gastronomic ambassador of the territory, celebrating tradition with consistency and warm hospitality in relaxing surroundings where time seems to slow down. The menu embraces the most authentic cuisine – the zlikrofi, potato-and-chive-filled tortelli served with pan juices and shavings of aged Montasio are emblematic – alongside more contemporary interpretations, such as an elegant, restrained squab presented in two services. The carefully curated cellar tells the story of the land through an almost climate-based organization of labels, enriched by numerous reserves and captivating vertical selections.

Name: Trattoria contemporanea
Description: A young team led by talented chef Davide Marzullo surprises guests with modern techniques and cuisine, offering dishes that showcase both national and international flavours and combinations, including a completely vegetarian - Istinto - menu, including a not-to-be-missed risotto with goat's milk, capers, liquorice and soya. At lunchtime, the menu is lighter, but you can also enjoy à la carte specialities and three tasting menus (with varying numbers of courses). The industrial redevelopment of a former cotton mill provides a fitting backdrop for all this energy.

Name: Trattoria da Amerigo
Description: In the foothills just beyond Bologna, Amerigo celebrates the idea of the traditional Italian trattoria, taking us on a nostalgic journey into the past that is part of our collective memory. It is situated just a few metres from the village’s main square and also has a shop, should you wish to take home a culinary souvenir from the area (wines, sauces and other delicacies). A number of function rooms – including what was once the town’s first TV lounge – each one more charming than the last, featuring period memorabilia and a pleasantly informal atmosphere. Alberto Bettini is in charge of the whole operation, offering an extraordinary selection of the produce and recipes of the area. Savigno is famous for its truffles, so mushrooms, but it also boasts one of the most remarkable selections of cured meats (the long-cured prosciutto is exceptional), obviously a variety of fresh pasta dishes, ranging from tortellini in old hen’s stock to tagliatelle with ragù, as well as tigelle, with the main courses consisting chiefly of meat and a range of delicious desserts.

Name: Traube
Description: A beautiful historical house in the small wine-growing village of Blansingen. The couple who run the place have plenty of experience in high-end gastronomy (Maaemo in Oslo, La Vie in Osnabrück), and it's immediately obvious that professionals are at work here. Headed up by the charming Daniela Hasse, the front-of-house team is pleasantly informal, chatty and highly professional. Canadian-born head chef Brian Wawryk never fails to impress with his meticulous craftsmanship and well-balanced dishes. His modern cuisine is creative and focuses on regional products, including ingredients preserved the year before. Insider tip: in winter, try to bag yourself the small table in the "Kuschelecke" ("cosy corner") by the tiled stove! The leafy terrace beckons in summer. Bear in mind that Traube is also a great place to stay overnight.

Name: Traube
Description: Since chef-patron Arno Sgier took over the reins in 1993, this restaurant in the little town of Trimbach has developed into a real culinary gem. Traube is a lovely place to be, with its chic and modern interior done out with premium furnishings, and its well-trained front-of-house team attending to your every need. Then there is Arno Sgier's technically ambitious cuisine. His classic yet really modern style is evident in, for example, the delicately acidic Lostallo salmon marinated in buttermilk and chive oil, served with textures of cucumber and quinoa crisps. The classics, too, are given a modern twist. Those who like a glass or two of good wine as part of a first-class meal are in for a treat, because the wine list really does have many treasures in store, especially in the bottles section. In the evening, you can choose between the "Traube" set menu and a set menu of starters; there is a three-course set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Trb Hutong
Address: 23 Shatan North Street, Dongcheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Hidden in the courtyard of a historic temple, this cosy, modern, professionally run dining room raises customer expectations. Polished, immaculately crafted dishes starring top-notch local produce hit the spot every time. The premium signature menu is inspired by the chef’s personal history and stars luxury ingredients. The seasonal menu lavishly calls upon ripe, mature produce and Le Grand Dessert finale is definitely worth writing home about.

Name: Tre Olivi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: At the Savoy Hotel & Spa, in the heart of Cilento, a culinary experience is taking shape that combines contemporary elegance with a deep connection to the local area. The offering comprises tasting menus and a menu that showcases local specialities, many of which come from the establishment’s own farm. The ingredients, flavours and traditions of the Cilento region and the Mediterranean diet are reinterpreted with a modern sensitivity, giving rise to well-balanced dishes that are simple in appearance yet rich in character. One of the most interesting new features is a sophisticated room with its own kitchen, designed for private events and bespoke dinners. In the dining room, attentive and professional service enhances the experience with discretion and care, helping to create a warm and relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Trente-Trois
Address: Maison Villeroy, 33 rue Jean-Goujon, Paris, 75008, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This plush, wainscoted Belle Époque dining room is located at N°33 in a discreet hotel, set in what is known as the Golden Triangle near the Champs Élysées. Chef Sébastien Sanjou has a knack for selecting premium produce, with which he composes a voluntarily concise menu, signing subtle, up-to-date, seasonal dishes that hit the spot every time from impeccable cooking and superlative jus and sauces to exquisitely balanced flavours. Decadently discreet.

Name: Trescha
Description: After an extensive period working aboard, which saw him train at Le Cordon Bleu in London and then in other culinary pantheons such as Azurmendi (Spain), Frantzén (Sweden) and the erstwhile 108 (Denmark), young chef Tomás Treschanski has returned to his homeland with a limitless contemporary repertoire built around diversity. Occupying a remodelled house in the Villa Crespo district, this exclusive restaurant features a bar with an impressive collection of whiskies, an attractive glass-fronted terrace, and a contemporary-style dining room with just a single but elegant cedarwood counter for 11 guests who are able to interact with the chefs. Here you will find a tasting menu based on small bites (constantly changing throughout the year), using more than 350 premium products from all over the country and a variety of techniques (ageing, emulsions, mousses, gelatinised textures, searing, etc.) on the same plate. On the first floor is the Test Kitchen, their R&D area!

Name: Tresmacarrons
Address: Avenida del Maresme 21, El Masnou, 08320, Spain
Description: The name of this family-run restaurant is an unmistakeable reference to Michelin’s stars which the French refer to colloquially as “macaroons”.Here, in a modern yet welcoming ambience, discover chef Miquel Aldana’s propensity for high-quality Catalan cuisine that is contemporary in style, adapted to seasonality and firmly connected to the surrounding El Maresme area of Barcelona province. Tresmacarrons’ culinary philosophy is based around the pleasure of a job well done and complete commitment, as demonstrated by its tasting menus (Corto and Tresmacarrons). If you like the tableware here, make sure you tell Núria Orra, the front of house manager, as she was involved in its design and production!

Name: Tri
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: In a small coastal town by the North Sea you'll find this contemporary greenhouse-like building. Made from wood and glass, it is a bright and airy space that is filled with customers enjoying quality cooking. Chef Nicolas Min Jørgensen has created a menu themed around seasonal and local produce, which is used with a nose-to-tail, low waste ethos. Dishes provide pure, natural flavours and are prepared with care and precision.

Name: Trigo
Description: It has always been said that wheat (“trigo” in Spanish) is the gold of Castille, hence its historical importance to the region.The restaurant, located just a few steps from the cathedral, reflects the strong passion that chef Víctor Martín has for his cuisine. Alongside his wife Noemí Martínez, a renowned sommelier who runs the dining room, he focuses on creative and contemporary cooking with strong roots in tradition, and is based on his relationship with small suppliers and their superb local produce and ingredients (vegetables from Tudela de Duero, pigeon from Tierra de Campos, chestnuts from Cacabelos etc). Not forgetting traditional pork products from his native León and the occasional seasonal fish dish. Allow the kitchen to treat you to their flights of fancy, accompanied by a wine from the splendid cellar.

Name: Trinity
Address: 4 The Polygon, Clapham, London, SW4 0JG, United Kingdom
Description: A rightly popular neighbourhood restaurant, this is a place you can’t help but fall in love with. Located close to Clapham Common, it’s an intimate operation where the open kitchen lets you in on the action. Kick off with a G&T made using their house distilled gin, before enjoying fine British produce crafted into deceptively complex dishes packed with bold flavours. The inventive 'sardine bolognaise dumpling', for instance, showcases consummate seasoning and meticulous attention to detail in every element. The smooth service team bring welcome personality to proceedings.

Name: Triptyque
Description: Niven Kunz is famous for his 80/20 concept: at Triptyque, vegetables and fruits make up at least 80% of each dish. A true ambassador for Westland, he frequently crosses the region to visit his suppliers. Along with hostess Virginie van Bronckhorst-Kunz, he aims to help you feel at one with nature. They do this subtly, with a certain natural ease. The elegant luxury of the decor also has a natural undertone, with details like dried flowers adding a touch of sophistication.With a highly personal creative approach, the chef puts the terroir in the spotlight. His dishes are defined by their deep, complex flavours. Through a multi-day process, he transforms carrots into a plant-based steak tartare that looks and tastes astonishingly like the real thing. A pickle gel and crunchy croutons add the final touch to this remarkable dish. He blends vibrancy and innovative techniques with rich sauces that provide a powerful foundation. This is purity redefined, paired with outstanding wines.

Name: Trishna
Address: 15-17 Blandford Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 3DG, United Kingdom
Description: A light refurbishment in early 2025 freshened up the look of this ever-popular Indian restaurant, while the service remains as pitch perfect as ever: professional and attentive, without being stiff or formal. But what continues to make it special is the quality of its cuisine. Dishes inspired by India’s coastal cooking are not to be missed, like the generous and delicious Dorset brown crab or the Hariyali bream from the tandoor, but don’t ignore the more original offerings like beef short rib coconut fry. Look out for the special menus that celebrate India’s festivals and seasons.

Name: Troubadour
Description: Melissa and Sean McGaughey began their romance working together at SingleThread (as baker and sous-chef, respectively), and here they've wedded their talents to make a singularly charming Healdsburg destination. The lovely little space is a popular sandwich shop and bakery by day (they also run nearby Quail and Condor); at night transforming to offer an exciting tasting menu that highlights Californian ingredients with flair and technical precision. Classical underpinnings are enlivened with a modern sensibility, seen in a "bouillabaise" of gently cooked rockfish with saffron-yuzu emulsion and a clam croquette, or seared duck breast with malted potato cream and a morel stuffed with chicken mousseline. Naturally, the bread course is a highlight.

Name: Troyka
Description: Chef duo Alexander Wulf and Marcel Kokot propose a one-of-a-kind culinary experience, serving up modern dishes with a Russian twist – sometimes incorporating quintessential flavours such as dill, sour cream or beetroot, and at other times creating elegant interpretations of Russian classics such as vareniki or zakuski. Shining examples include "red cod, Russian kimchi, kohlrabi, peanut" or "Maibock (seasonal venison), vareniki, mushrooms, pine cones". The set menu is served by a highly adept and knowledgeable yet laid-back young team led by sommelier Ronny Schreiber – a real connoisseur, he surprises diners with interesting, not always conventional wine recommendations. In summer, the minimalist-style indoor dining space is complemented by a gorgeous terrace. Tip: Nab a seat at the counter facing the open kitchen for some fascinating insights into the chefs' work. There is also a screen showing the action at the kitchen pass. Fun fact: The name, the Russian word troyka means "three-horse team" and refers to Wulf, Kokot and Schreiber, who run this operation like a well-oiled machine and with great enthusiasm. As an alternative to the fine dining set menu, you can order more down-to-earth bistro fare.

Name: Truube
FacilitiesAndServices: Bring your own bottle,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This quintessential Appenzell building looks inviting from the outside, and the interior is equally stylish. Come and savour Silvia Manser's cuisine, which is based on carefully selected ingredients, in a pleasingly simple yet upscale setting. In her four- to seven-course menu – available in both vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions – she brings together modern interpretations of classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences and occasionally incorporates Middle Eastern and Asian accents. Her talent for combining boldness with finesse is evident in dishes such as "tuna tataki, mango, onion, coriander", "leek 'carbonara', cured egg yolk, shiitake", or "Appenzell lamb, falafel, chickpeas, courgette". Silvia Manser runs the restaurant with her husband Thomas – the two form a perfectly attuned team. She is at the helm in the kitchen; he oversees the service with warmth and expertise, guiding diners through an excellent wine list devoted to Switzerland, France and Italy, including a fine range of vintages.

Name: Tsujifusa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Shoes must be removed
Description: The owner has devoted himself wholeheartedly to Kyoto cuisine. In pursuit of savoury depth, he pays close attention to the harmony between the flavours of the ingredients and the dashi. Citrus and vinegar bring acidity, lending contrast and rhythm to the progression of the meal. The kumiko latticework in the transom window above the entrance and in the lighting above the counter is a traditional craft from Okawa in Fukuoka Prefecture. This detail reflects the chef’s affection for his hometown, which is renowned for woodworking.

Name: Tsukimi
Address: 288 E. 10th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: At this elegant East Village counter, Tsukimi offers a modern interpretation of kaiseki rooted in seasonality and restraint. Named for the Japanese moon-viewing harvest tradition, the serene room glows with illuminated ceramics, mirrored panels and an open kitchen framed by soft arches. The tasting menu changes frequently, drawing on Japanese ingredients and subtle flavors. A silky chawanmushi with oyster, uni and Kaluga caviar is a highlight, while seasonal combinations like bamboo shoot with firefly squid and charcoal-grilled duck with spring vegetables showcase the kitchen’s refined approach. Beverage pairings are available, though the sake selection deserves special attention.

Name: Tsé Fung
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Frank Xu, the proud heir of a Sichuan cooking dynasty, has set up his HQ in the lavish La Réserve hotel, where he rolls out Chinese cuisine strewn with subtle European accents. Regional delicacies, notably first-class shrimp and beef, enjoy guest-of-honour status on the extensive menu. The savvily curated wine cellar is as impressive as the well-oiled seamless service. The summer terrace provides an outstanding stage for alfresco dining. Popular with tourists and city slickers for its gourmet repertory and glamorous interior which brings to mind the high-society cosmopolitan aura of 1930’s Shanghai.

Name: Tuber Umberto Bombana
Address: Shop 113A, 1F, K11 Musea, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: This dining concept by the eponymous chef is dedicated to the black and white treasure of gastronomy; its name also refers to the genus to which truffles belong. The head chef, who worked under Chef Bombana for over 20 years, demonstrates dexterous handling of seasonal ingredients from around the world, including jumbo carabinero prawns from Spain. The tasting menu offers a choice of dishes from starter to dessert.

Name: Tudor Hall
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: If the prospect of lunch or dinner on the elegant terrace of a hotel appeals to you, with the added bonus of background piano music and the eternal Acropolis as a backdrop, Tudor Hall is definitely a good option, especially for a romantic candlelit dinner – but make sure you book ahead. Here, on the 7th floor of the King George Hotel, next to the central Syntagma Square, chef Nikos Livadias showcases his contemporary version of Greek cuisine, based on a concise à la carte menu plus a tasting menu. The end result is a superb combination of well-balanced dishes that display strong technical ability, such as the breast of guinea fowl beetroot purée, blackberries, amaranth and praline sauce with juniper. The icing on the cake comes courtesy of the meticulous service provided by head sommelier Evangelos Psofidis, who always conveys his passion for wine to guests via his highly astute recommendations.

Name: Tula
Address: Avenida de la Llibertat 36, Xàbia, 03730, Spain
Description: If everyone is talking up a restaurant, it must be doing something right!In this unpretentious eatery in the immediate surroundings of Arenal beach, couple Borja Susilla and Clara Puig offer guests enticing modern dishes with the essence of the Mediterranean with a northern flair (mainly Asturian and Basque) in which their training in leading restaurants (they met while working with chef Quique Dacosta) is clearly evident. Choose between an array of market-inspired specials (fresh fish, in particular) that you won’t find on the menu as well as a seven-course tasting menu and many dishes designed for sharing. The latter can be ordered as half portions so that everyone can create their own menu and taste lots of dishes. Make sure you order the shisho leaf taco with pancetta, smoked eel and misonnaise or their delicious grilled hake kokotxas with Iberian pork consommé, artichoke textures and pine nuts.

Name: Tuome
Address: 536 E. 5th St., New York, NY, 10009, USA
Description: Classically trained Chef Thomas Chen is the one to thank for the fabulous Tuome. It's an Asian-inspired menu, which is no surprise as the chef is a master of weaving together ingredients to delicious and surprising effect. The intimate space is outfitted with a backlit bar, bay windows, and comfortable purple seats. Service is fittingly unfussy yet deeply knowledgeable. Don’t miss the seared octopus served atop pork XO sauce or the lamb chops, served perfectly medium rare and finished with a shishito chimichurri, black pepper jus, and a dollop of onion soubise. Finally, deep-fried buns which arrive as Chinese “beignets” accompanied by vanilla ice cream laced with red bean paste, goat's milk caramel, and yuzu marmalade render dessert wholly unmissable.

Name: Tussock Hill
Address: 210 Huntsbury Avenue, Cashmere, Christchurch, 8022, New Zealand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A boutique vineyard specialising in organic wines, Tussock Hill incorporates an on-site restaurant that affords views of its verdant grounds and Christchurch in the distance. Open for lunch only, it offers a small menu of sharing plates crafted with seasonal local produce, specifically designed to complement their wines. From house-made sourdough to beef carpaccio or wild caught fish, the food deeply resonates with the art of winemaking.

Name: Tutoiement
Description: The name Tutoiement means 'to speak in a friendly, informal way', reflecting Chef Do-hyeon Kim’s desire to connect casually with diners through food. Interestingly, in contrast to this relaxed approach, the precisely cooked and sophisticated French cuisine engages the senses, placing the focus firmly on the food. The chef expresses the subtle flavours, textures, and nuances of each ingredient with care, plating dishes to highlight harmony between the components and their accompanying sauces. His cooking reflects a personal journey, guided by clarity of vision and a desire to create a dining experience that feels both thoughtful and memorable.

Name: Txispa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Can Japanese techniques be merged with grill work, like in a Basque steakhouse? Japanese chef Tetsuro Maeda, who has restored a century-old farmhouse in a small village where you can hear the silence, resoundingly shows us that you can, committing to simplicity based on exceptional products (they work with seasonal vegetables from their own garden, mushrooms and wild plants harvested in the surrounding mountains) that reveal surprising nuances. Kabayaki eel, caviar with tofu (chickpea tofu with hot-smoked caviar on kombu), Txuleta of old and matured beef, sakura flan from their own cherry trees... the menu is a surprise, in constant evolution, designed based on the best in-season raw ingredients. The experience begins in the kitchen, where the first appetisers are served contemplating the grill, and reaches its zenith in the coquettish dining room. Friday and Saturday nights are the time for Yakitxori, a more casual proposal!

Name: Têtedoie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In the wake of his mentor Paul Bocuse, Christian Têtedoie has built a small gourmet empire. Perched on Fourvière hill overlooking the city, the Têtedoie is a gourmet showcase. A champion of Gallic culinary traditions, this fan of contemporary art is committed to finetuning and even modernising this heritage. Bites of snails, foie gras and pistachio; “portfolio” of red mullet, carrots and game sauce; mallard duck, grilled chestnuts and Jack Be Little pumpkins: his dishes sometimes read like an abstract art exhibition. It’s impossible not to mention his signature dish: lobster casserole with a calf's head cromesquis that he has renamed HTV (after Homard Tête de Veau in French). Generous, sensitive cuisine depicted by an intelligent array of textures and flavours.

Name: Tầm Vị
Address: 4B Yen The Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Now with a two-storey expansion and lush courtyard, English-speaking staff and a photo menu, this vintage tea house is more tourist-friendly. It retains its North Vietnamese charm with antique decor, artwork and a rustic elegance, and continues to impart the essence of Vietnamese cuisine. Highlights include chả ốc (ham with periwinkle snails) served with herbs, vegetables, vermicelli and fish sauce, and the subtle crab soup with malabar spinach in a clear broth.

Name: UNALOME by Graeme Cheevers
Address: 36 Kelvingrove Street, Glasgow City, G3 7RZ, United Kingdom
Description: In the lively hub of Finnieston, this elegant spot in a period building represents local chef Graeme Cheevers' desire to create a restaurant for all occasions. His considerable culinary skills are evident in dishes that pay their respects to the finest of Scottish produce from Orkney scallops to North Sea cod – the latter of which might come with peas, asparagus and subtle hints of mint and wasabi, providing a fine example of the precision and sophistication you can expect here. It's well worth going for the full tasting menu and the thoughtfully considered wine pairings.

Name: Uberto Restaurant
Address: 2 Jimmy Clark Rd., Gay, GA, 30218, USA
Description: This distinctive spot about an hour from Atlanta rests amid rolling green hills as part of the World of Quercus resort. Chef Ryan Smith oversees this ambitious dining room that is open on Friday and Saturday evenings only (though hotel guests are invited to additional meals outside of these constraints). The tasting menu celebrates farm-grown ingredients, harnessing fermentation and preservation techniques to make the best of their products. Creative cooking with plenty of on-trend inflections take center stage with plates like miso and Alabama blue crab chawanmushi. Cold-smoked, dry-aged Rohan duck is grilled over binchotan coals and paired with a vibrant carrot puree. To finish, expect the likes of fig ice cream with buckwheat sponge and crumble.

Name: Ubuka
Description: Love of shellfish above all else led the chef of Ubuka to tread the culinary path. He has done his homework, and the results show in a menu filled with crab and prawn suggestions. Some items follow kaiseki style, while others are Western in influence. Terrine of hair crab is an idea borrowed from French cuisine; fried prawns are immersed in sauce américaine. The meal concludes with crab and vegetables on rice cooked in an earthenware pot. Portions are generous to ensure guests can fully appreciate their shellfish. No wonder this restaurant is so busy.

Name: Udtryk
Description: Start with a drink in the courtyard of this handsome yellow building in the city’s Latin Quarter before heading for the elegant, contemporary dining room. Udtryk means 'expression' in Danish and the well-balanced tasting menu blends techniques and flavours from across Asia and Europe in refined, interesting dishes. You might find a claypot of koshihikari rice, Norlin Wagyu, Danish eel and shiitake mushrooms, followed by monaka with hand-dived Norwegian scallops, watercress and gingko nuts for dessert.This restaurant is temporarily closed and set to reopen in December.

Name: Ugly Butterfly by Adam Handling
Address: The Headland, Headland Road, Fistral Beach, Newquay, TR7 1EW, United Kingdom
Description: Following a relocation from Carbis Bay, the second iteration of Ugly Butterfly still comes with spectacular views, this time over Fistral Beach thanks to its new home inside the Headland Hotel. Sip a cocktail on the sun-drenched terrace while you choose between the tasting menu and the à la carte, which allows you to have either three or four courses. Adam Handling’s experience and commitment to quality produce are all on show – such as in the wild bass with courgette and bone sauce, a clean, confident dish that shines in its purity of flavour.

Name: Ugo Chan
Description: A contemporary restaurant with an open-view kitchen, two counters and a Japanese ambience that is far from lacking in personality. Its meticulous, constantly evolving cuisine could be described by quoting the Greek philosopher Heracles: “No man ever steps in the same river twice”. In his restaurant, which shares the nickname given to him by his grandfather when he was a boy (“Hugochan”, or “little Hugo”), chef Hugo Muñoz conjures up Japanese cuisine (on an à la carte and a personalised Omakase menu) in which seasonal ingredients take centre stage, incorporating enjoyable influences from other cultures and with a nod to iconic Madrid dishes (such as the tripe gyozas “a la madrileña” and his version of “Soldaditos de Pavía”) and other legendary chefs (Martín Berasategui, Joël Robuchon etc). One dish that we particularly enjoyed was the highly memorable caviar lentil Japanese curry with smoked breast of wood pigeon and coconut.

Name: Ukitacho Ima
Description: The chef spent years fine-tuning his skills in a Japanese restaurant in Hozenji Yokocho. While treasuring the lessons he learned there, he now blazes his own culinary trail. Mindful of how knife technique can affect the flavour of sashimi, he practises daily and his grounded approach to cooking is reassuring to watch. Bringing together everything he has learned over his career, he expresses it in cuisine of the ‘here and now’. Rather than just copy his mentor, the chef treads his own path in the gastronomic world.

Name: Ullrs Gourmetstube
Address: Alte Arlbergstraße 2, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: "Alpine Soul – Japanese Spirit – Nordic Air" is the philosophy of the fine dining restaurant in the Ullrhaus designer hotel. This cosmopolitan approach is reflected in modern, creative dishes such as "essence of shellfish, king crab, taco, tomatillo" or "Miéral pigeon, beetroot, purple shiso, plum umeboshi", which are a true delight, thanks to remarkably precise craftsmanship and punchy flavours. Components are skilfully balanced, not to forget the first-class quality of the products, which are used extensively. The fantastic large-scale set menu is accompanied by a high-calibre wine selection with a focus on Austria, Italy and France, including some major names. The space, in which diners are seated at four large tables, has a sophisticated feel, with the warmth of Scandinavian-style wood and decorative green tiles on the walls. Service is charming and professional.

Name: Umami
Description: In the heart of Petite France with its picture postcard half-timbered houses, as its name suggests, this restaurant combines flavours from near and far. Umami is the fifth flavour in Japanese cuisine, alongside sweet, sour, bitter and salty. A seasoned globetrotter, chef René Fieger signs a market-fresh score scattered with Asian notes yet solidly rooted in Gallic traditions. The chef works alone in his kitchen, conjuring up heroically wondrous fare. Highlights include wontons of veal and a powerful Thai stock of coconut milk or duck breasts flanked by an amazing, orange-flavoured sauce of Asian origin. A fully vegetarian version of the menu is also available on request when booking.

Name: Umberto a Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In a spectacular setting beneath the Church of Soccorso, with breathtaking sunset views over the sea, Umberto rises to match such natural beauty with elegant, contemporary Campanian cuisine. The tasting menu Sogno di una Notte di Mezza Estate (A Midsummer Night’s Dream) dazzles with the signature Gioco di Mare dish, while the dessert selection is equally memorable. Don’t miss the grouper tortelli or the daily catch, prepared with modern techniques. The visitable wine cellar houses over 1,500 labels, featuring exceptional Champagnes, great French classics, and outstanding German Rieslings. Special praise goes to the young sommelier-owner, whose passionate and precise recommendations enhance the entire experience.

Name: Umu
Address: 14-16 Bruton Place, Mayfair, London, W1J 6LX, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: From its discreet entrance to its elegant décor, Umu has always been a restaurant for that special occasion. The menu is influenced by the delicate cuisine of Kyoto, but other regions of Japan are also represented. You can expect a nod to British produce as well, with dishes like ginjo sake cured Scottish langoustine. The ingredients are of top quality and their natural flavours are always brought to the fore. Some dishes are simple; others are presented with a flourish at the table – but all are prepared with considerable care and respect.

Name: Un Max de Goût
Description: Maxime Zimmer is a chef who is going from strength to strength as he finetunes his sophisticated palette. Foodies have long known his Ardennes establishment, whose contemporary elegance blends seamlessly into the picturesque landscape of the Ourthe that meanders outdoors and where this young master chef is thriving. The ingredient-focused lineup of this artisan relies on produce from local suppliers and his own creative flair, as he transforms familiar ingredients into fascinating dishes.He may start by searing a rib-eye steak to give it a crisp crust, before smoking it over the barbecue and then pairing it with a powerful sauce of crushed pepper corns and celeriac soaked in cognac. Similarly, he highlights the numerous facets of celeriac by way of different preparations: cooked in a salt crust, in a crème, fried, but also like a risotto in a creamy jus. The chef shines the spotlight on the work of his suppliers, courtesy of playful, yet polished recipes. A quick glance at the wine wall (of mainly French vintages) behind a glazed partition may well prove irresistible and the front-of-house team is always close at hand with pairing suggestions.

Name: Un Piano nel Cielo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: An atmospheric panoramic lift leads from the Casa Angelina hotel to the restaurant: in good weather you can dine on a terrace, by candlelight and with a breathtaking view of the Coast. Leopoldo Elefante's cuisine is Mediterranean and largely dedicated to the sea, although there is never a shortage of excellent meat specialities. Not to be missed is his “soufflé alla pastiera”, a signature dish that combines an international dessert with typically Neapolitan flavours. Great care is given to presentation and the lighting uses various colours to accompany the guest through the different courses, changing in tone and intensity throughout the meal. The chef is well supported by the service, precise and friendly, and an important wine list. The wine cellar is around 1500 labels, with an incredible availability of large formats for connoisseurs.

Name: Under
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This breathtakingly stunning building half-submerged in the sea provides a singular and spectacular setting in which to dine. The sense of anticipation grows as you descend the beautifully crafted oak-and-steel staircase to the dining room 5m under the sea, where panoramic windows afford an underwater view. It's no surprise to find plenty of seafood on the seasonal tasting menu, where superb produce, like sweet and juicy langoustine tail, is treated with a light touch and welcome restraint to bring out its natural flavours.

Name: Under Grain
Description: Housed within the stylish Rosselli Hotel, on one of Valletta’s most elegant streets, Under Grain welcomes guests into a setting as sophisticated as its cuisine. The restaurant occupies the building’s historic lower level, where diners pass by the kitchen before entering a dining room crowned by a vaulted stone ceiling. Inspired by the tailor shops that once lined Merchant Street, the concept is woven throughout, from sewing-pattern menus to displays of garments, and even the pincushion used to present the bill. The offering is fully à la carte, with the option for guests to create their own tasting menu, reflecting the chef’s distinctly creative approach. At times, he ventures into bold, unexpected combinations – as in one of his signature dishes pairing mussels with sweet Gorgonzola and passion fruit – while at others he embraces more classic flavours. Even the bread course is memorable, evoking the chef’s childhood snacks. The wine list is thoughtfully curated and rich in gems from around the world, with a particular focus on Italy and France, alongside an excellent by-the-glass selection.

Name: Une
Description: Situated in a hamlet of Foligno criss-crossed by springs and streams (UNE is the word for water in the old language of Umbria), this restaurant occupies a 17C mill. The dining room has retained all the rural and romantic charm of the original building, which was once used for the milling of cereals and later for the production of olive oil. Today, young chef Giulio Gigli brings a touch of modernity to the restaurant. Having gained experience working in Italy and abroad, he creates elaborate and personalised dishes from local produce, most of which is grown and raised within a 20km radius of the restaurant, as well as occasionally more exotic ingredients, showcasing his dishes on two tasting menus. The wine list follows the same philosophy as the cuisine, featuring local labels alongside bottles from elsewhere in Italy and further afield which are sourced from small wineries with a focus on organic, biodynamic and natural wines.

Name: Une Table, au Sud
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Chef Ludovic Turac is at the helm of this stylish seaside-themed restaurant firmly anchored in the South of France. The chef signs unmistakably Marseille menus, strewn with nods to his travels around the Mediterranean and his own Armenian heritage. His inventive recipes are always packed with flavour and are perfectly in tune with the knockout panorama over the Vieux Port and the city’s iconic basilica. Signatures include aïoli, pan-seared Mediterranean squid, lacquered and smoked greater amberjack, bouillabaisse of red mullet or Corsican tigerstripe veal, all of which unveil outstanding surf and turf combinations, big-boned jus and a confident use of Middle Eastern spices. Corsican and Provençal wineries take the limelight in the spot-on, coherent wine list, which is thoughtfully explained to diners.

Name: UniQuisine Atelier
Description: "Dining at a friend's place" sums the vibe up nicely, and the unique location, for starters, is part of that: The relatively small restaurant is in an apartment on the third floor of a residential and restaurant block. The upscale interior has a modern-minimalist aesthetic feel – art on the walls and a stylish fireplace enhance the visual appeal. The pleasingly intimate feel results not least from the central open kitchen, which means you're right there in the thick of things! Diners are in good hands with chef Christoph Oliver Aebersold and restaurant manager Agron Tunprenkaj – two consummate professionals who provide high-calibre, cordial service in their respective domains. The contemporary and creative cooking homes in on top-notch ingredients. Opt for a five- or seven-course set menu, which showcases dishes such as "Beef, Radish, Mustard" or "Salmon, Cauliflower, Vin Jaune". With his harmonious wine recommendations, Agron Tunprenkaj proves himself to be an accomplished sommelier, too. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif on the beautiful balcony terrace with views of the Pilatus and Stanserhorn mountains.

Name: Unic
Address: Les Begònies 18, Sant Josep de sa Talaia, 07817, Spain
Location: Sant Josep de sa Talaia, Spain
Description: This restaurant impresses guests both for its location—in two glass cubes joined beneath a large dome—inside a courtyard of the modern Migjorn Ibiza hotel (near Playa d’en Bossa), and for its excellent design, featuring sand lamps, designer pieces, and even a garden-bath dedicated to Posidonia. Here, French chef David Grussaute offers two tasting menus (Unic and La Xanga, with sections entitled Prelude, From the Sea, Surf & Turf, From the Land, and A Moment of Sweetness) that always champion locally sourced ingredients which enable him to showcase the culinary essence of both the island and the Mediterranean in close collaboration with small-scale producers, breeders and the local fishing community. All his dishes feature marked, intense flavours and perfectly balanced sauces, although if we had to highlight one dish that will remain in the memory, it would be the ‘Pityuses, island of pines’ dessert, which was as refreshing as it was unexpected, and akin to eating a Mediterranean forest!

Name: Uozuya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Shoes must be removed
Description: A procession of dishes that linger in the diner’s memory. Seasonal flavours are used in generous measure, such as Japanese pepper flower, pike conger, matsutake mushrooms and crab. Preparation methods, whether that be grilling, boiling or more, are astutely tailored to each ingredient, showcasing its qualities from every angle. This talent for bringing out the best in food is born of long years of experience. A favourite haunt of the literati, the Uozuya sign calligraphy is by essayist Masako Shirasu.

Name: Upstairs
Address: 36 Nguyen Ba Huan Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Set above a wine bar, this intimate spot has just four tables in its calm interior of curved lines and a palette of soft pinks and beige tones. Chef Hiep Truong's modern Vietnamese tasting menu, rooted in Central traditions, puts an elegant spin on classics such as gỏi bò cà, in which Wagyu tartare meets aubergine purée and egg yolk in a crisp shell. The wine list features boutique wineries, with a selection by the glass recommended by a savvy sommelier.

Name: Upstairs by Tom Shepherd
Address: 25 Bore Street, Lichfield, WS13 6NA, United Kingdom
Description: The beautifully balanced tasting menu at this town centre restaurant features an impressive array of creative and eye-catching dishes, all made using quality ingredients like Orkney scallop, Anjou pigeon and wild Shetland halibut. The eponymous chef and his team are on-view in the open kitchen, while the bright young service team have an infectious enthusiasm, which helps keep the atmosphere buoyant and relaxed. Plans are currently afoot to absorb the ground floor – formerly a jewellery shop run by the chef’s father – into the restaurant to complement the upstairs dining room.

Name: Ursprung
Description: Anna and Andreas Widmann (the eighth generation of the family at the helm) have two restaurants, and this is the fine dining option. In the oldest part of Widmann's Löwen – where the village butcher's shop used to be – this small restaurant combines warm wood and a minimalist, contemporary style to create a tasteful, sophisticated ambience. In the kitchen, traditional Swabian fare meets fine dining. Sourced from local growers and producers, premium ingredients are used in dishes brimming with creativity, flavour and original ideas. There is a regularly changing set menu featuring five or seven courses, according to the seasons, also available in a vegetarian version. Service is attentive, as you enjoy dishes such as "crayfish from Seefeld with asparagus and XO sauce" or "matured Ostalb lamb with green asparagus, quinoa and gremolata". Each course is accompanied by the perfect wine pairing – Anna Widmann is not only a charming hostess but also a sommelier and the force behind the carefully curated wine list. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay, plus a shop selling dishes and delicatessen wares to enjoy later.

Name: Ursus
Address: Maison Bouvier - Les Suites, 39 rue du Val-Claret, au Val-Claret, Tignes, 73320, France
Description: Housed within one of the resort’s top hotels, this restaurant loves nature, hence its name that pays tribute to the last remaining species of brown bear in the Alps. The interior resembles a forest with slim tree trunks separating the tables into little thickets, a ceiling covered with a canvas depicting foliage and magnificent tables carved from walnut wood. Chef Clément Bouvier, former second to Jean-François Piège, signs creative Alpine cuisine with a rustic edge, mixing freshwater fish or game with aromatic herbs and plants picked in the mountains. On a constant quest for the best local ingredients, each dish is fully in tune with the seasons. The cheese trolley is 100% Alpine in origin and is escorted by an impressive wine list.

Name: VELROSIER
Address: 2F, Good Nature Station, 318-6 Inaricho, Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, 600-8022, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: The interior’s keynote black bespeaks modern dining; the cuisine, modern Chinese with further innovations, confirms the impression. The concept of Chinese-French fusion cuisine adds uniqueness, exemplified by the foie gras sandwiched between two thin, crisp wafers redolent with Shaoxing wine. Use of decompression cooking and liquid nitrogen ensure that ingredients retain all their flavour. Advanced methods give rise to new directions in cuisine.

Name: VILLA COMMUNICO
Description: An auberge set amidst the natural beauty of Nara Park. COMMUNICO means ‘sharing’, reflecting the desire to create a retreat where the passion of chefs and producers, along with the bounty of each season, can be shared with guests. Ingredients sourced from like-minded producers are transformed into innovative dishes by skilfully harnessing the elemental heat of glowing wood embers. The appetiser of freshly made burrata cheese and caviar is a perfect example.

Name: VILLINO
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: From the stylish, airy, high-ceilinged restaurant, which is reminiscent of an orangery, to the charming inner courtyard with a fountain, this pretty property set amid the orchards has an almost Mediterranean feel. It's a real family affair here, enthusiastically run by hostess Sonja Fischer, her daughter Alisa and her brother Rainer Hörmann, a trained sommelier. The front-of-house team provides professional, cordial service, and savvy wine recommendations – and the lady of the house is always present too. Toni Neumann's cuisine is clearly influenced by Mediterranean – principally Italian – cuisine, and also draws on inspiration from Asia. There are three set menus to choose from: "Villino Tradizionale", "Cucina della Passione" and "Cucina Naturale" (vegetarian). Their signature dish is the "Asian mixed appetiser". Tip: Stay overnight in the hotel of the same name.

Name: VINHO
Address: #162 Wellstone Bldg, 38 Hakdong-ro 43-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06059, South Korea
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: Beneath an industrial-style ceiling, a dark-toned counter wraps around the open kitchen, allowing guests to observe each dish taking shape up close. Bright, upbeat music and the team’s easygoing service create an atmosphere that feels both relaxed and refined. Drawing on experience from well-known kitchens, co-owner Chef Sung-bin Jeon presents a seasonal menu that blends Korean tradition, modern technique, and personal interpretation. Subtle, expressive flavours and a bold yet minimalist aesthetic define the course experience. A thoughtfully curated wine pairing is recommended for those seeking a deeper journey.

Name: Vaisseau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Adrien Cachot’s signature hallmark is packed in character, illustrated by pimento that is a recurring theme of his score. In an interior entirely garbed in black, the chef unveils his creative skills, crafting dishes that often exhibit unexpected pairings, such as his show-stopping, explosive peppery "Cachot e pepe" mochi, one of his signature dishes! He also has a penchant for unconventional produce, such as offal, which contributes unusual textures, without forgetting surf and turf marriages, depicted by flambadou-smoked oyster, covered in cured beef from León and crowned with an Oscietra caviar-spiked quenelle. Over the course of an unapologetically playful carte blanche menu, a singular personality emerges that has no qualms about disrupting our culinary habits. The website indicates the days and times when bookings are open – don’t miss this opportunity…

Name: Vandelvira
Address: Plaza de San Francisco, Baeza, 23440, Spain
Description: If you’re visiting Baeza’s marvellous historic quarter, a Renaissance jewel that has been declared a World Heritage Site, eating in this restaurant will add an extra-special touch to the experience. Vandelvira occupies part of a 16C monastery with comfortable dining rooms and beautiful covered cloisters where guests can nowadays enjoy a glass of manzanilla sherry. The focus of owner-chef Juan Carlos García is on two tasting menus of creative cuisine, with a preference for humble ingredients from his own vegetable garden or the region, which he transforms into haute-cuisine dishes that showcase finesse, flavour and an extraordinary level of presentation. One dish that particularly appealed to us was the squid and Iberian ham, accompanied by a concentrated Iberian ham dashi broth and a delicious squid tartare.

Name: Variety Jones
Address: 79 Thomas Street, Dublin City, D08 F2RN, Ireland
Description: You’ll find charming chef-owner Keelan Higgs working calmly in the open kitchen of this inviting corner restaurant. Terracotta tones, exposed brickwork and warm lighting add cosiness, while the relaxed atmosphere is helped along by the laid-back service team. The generous surprise tasting menu is filled with highly original yet unfussy dishes which burst with freshness and flavour, including the signature spaghetti Alfredo. Several courses are cooked over fire, a concept Higgs loves as no two dishes will ever be exactly the same. The mostly organic wine list is passionately compiled.

Name: Vea
Address: 30F, The Wellington, 198 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: An imposing counter and an open kitchen dominate the room, commanding the best view of chef Cheng in action. You are definitely in for a stellar experience, thanks to his 8-course tasting menu that rolls out a “Chinese x French” concept. Each course tells a story about Hong Kong’s food culture and his childhood memories, using Chinese and local ingredients finessed by blue-ribbon Gallic technique. Creative cocktail-food pairing suggestions.

Name: Vecchia Malcesine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Situated at the entrance to the old town, the restaurant is fronted by a small but delightful garden of olive trees, from which you enter the dining room, which overlooks the rooftops of Malcesine, the lake and the opposite shore – an enchanting view. In the kitchen, Leandro Luppi creates delicious, flavourful dishes, with a range of options centred on freshwater fish – but that’s not all. Some are particularly creative – his ‘carbonara di lago’ is famous – while the presentation is sure to be remembered for its attention to detail and elegance.

Name: Vecchio Ristoro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
