Name: Bei Men Niu Xie Geng
Address: 580 Chicheng Road, Tiantai, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The simple room may be a bit dated, but the incredible smell of its beef blood curd soup is irresistibly enticing. Its signature soup is the classic comfort food of the landlocked county; chunks of silken blood curd and melty white radish nestle in a savoury broth seasoned with dried chillies. Their beef offal noodle soup is equally famous: the offal is meticulously crafted and the flavourful broth clings nicely to the springy noodles.

Name: Bei Ya Duck Thick Soup
Address: 169 Guangming Street, Xindian District, New Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: The built-in stoves and soup pipelines lend this simple shop its unique character. For over 20 years, it has focused on just two items on the menu – duck thick soup and duck meat rice. At about 75 days old, local mule ducks are braised, deboned and thinly sliced, boasting tender, silky meat. Onion, bamboo shoot and garlic are added to the broth for mild warmth and sweetness. A sprinkle of chilli powder gives an extra dimension of flavour.

Name: Beirut Sur Mer
Address: Lilac 5, Jacques Chirac Street, Saadiyat Cultural District, Soul Beach, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: The name says it all – this is about enjoying Lebanese food by the sea. Managed by MBT and with an experienced team occupying the open kitchen, you can expect all the classics, from mezze to mashawi; and don’t skip the desserts as they’re good too. Portions are generous and prices are reasonable. The large, colourful and contemporary dining room also boasts a beautiful beachfront terrace. An ideal spot for post-cultural refuelling after visiting the nearby Louvre Abu Dhabi.

Name: Bela Reka
Description: Tucked away on the outskirts of the city centre, the exceptional quality of this restaurant’s food makes the journey well worth the trip. Drawing inspiration from pedigree Serbian cuisine, it proudly showcases local and regional ingredients; most of the ewe’s milk cheese, for example, comes direct from the restaurant’s own farm in the Homolje Mountains. Among the house specialties, the shoulder of lamb matured in dry aging cases is highly recommended, as is the house-made Serbian bread. Hearty, generous portions.

Name: Bellavista
Description: It is always a pleasure to return to this eatery at the foot of the ramparts. The menu is the epitome of regional, which is not surprising as the chef uses local produce delivered by the farmers in person. Slow-roasted haunch of tender Pyrenean veal, hazelnut-flavoured Catalan picada sauce and millefeuille of potatoes… without forgetting cheese from the Pyrenees! Cosy rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Belly of the Beast
Address: 5200 FM 2920 Rd., Ste. 180, Spring, TX, 77388, USA
Description: In an unassuming dining room in Spring, Chef Thomas Bille is putting it all on the plate. Unafraid to mix and match the cuisines that inspire him, he cooks largely with Mexico in mind. Think saag paneer with spinach mole verde and a stack of warm, sumptuous tortillas made with half corn and half flour. Other possible starters—all of which are portioned to share— include tuna tostadas with nori or street corn agnolotti. Such twists and turns make for immensely satisfying courses that feel bold and balanced. The smartest twist of all might be the finely spiced cherry mole with Rohan duck breast. It’s unlikely you’ll make it to dessert with much spare room, but do consider the tres leches, cleverly prepared with passionfruit and torched meringue.

Name: Benikurage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
Description: ‘Benikurage’ refers to the immortal jellyfish, a creature whose cells rejuvenate so it never grows old or dies. The chef, a lover of both marine life and sake, chose the name in hopes for long-term success of his shop. Painstakingly selected sakes from throughout Japan enhance the restaurant’s appeal. To keep the sake flowing, sashimi is served with soy sauce; clear soup with the dense flavour of kombu kelp. With the kimono-clad proprietress radiating calm beside the chef, the restaurant exudes the intimacy of a small eatery.

Name: Berbena
Description: A diminutive, unpretentious and informal restaurant with a name that pays homage to the traditional “berbena” festivals. At the centre of everything here is Carles Pérez de Rozas Canut, whose focus is on simple yet well-though-out and highly captivating dishes (all available in half- and some even in quarter-portions) based around seasonal Mediterranean ingredients, but which also feature influences from Asia and South America. Personality in spades, with an open kitchen and enticing recipes that tell us lots about the chef, his travels and his work in other countries. His magnificent desserts add a final flourish at the end of your meal – the crème fraîche ice-cream with olive oil and salt is definitely one you won’t want to pass up on.

Name: Berenjak
Address: 27 Romilly Street, Soho, London, W1D 5AL, United Kingdom
Description: Based on the hole-in-the-wall 'kabab' houses of Tehran, this is a terrifically fun little spot in the heart of Soho. Exposed brick and painted plasterwork suit the buzzy atmosphere, with the best place to sit being at the kitchen counter so you can watch your food being prepared in the tandoor and the mangal barbecue. The cooking is generous and flavoursome, with dishes such as coal-cooked aubergine or lamb shoulder kabab. There are other branches in Mayfair and Borough Market, as well as around the world.

Name: Berenjak
Address: Dar Wasl Mall - Shop 01 - Al Wasl Rd - Al Wasl, Dubai
Description: An outpost of the original in London, this Persian eatery is located in Dubai’s smaller malls in the residential area of Al Wasl. It’s a large space decorated with oriental mosaics, carpets and portraits, all adding to the atmosphere. Expect plenty of appealingly priced Persian classics in its selection of hot and cold mezze and charcoal-grilled kebabs, all of which are complemented by vegetables, herbs and aromatics. A separate room for families and large gatherings is also available.

Name: Berenjak Al Maha Island
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of an ever-growing group, this Persian restaurant is located on the popular Al Maha Island with great views of the city – a seat on the terrace is always a top choice when weather permits. The food is pure Persian; all the favourites are here such as wonderful breads, tasty black chickpea hummus and kebabs cooked over coals. Don’t miss out on other dishes too – some to share – like the Ghormeh Sabzi, a deliciously flavoured stew, and save room for their saffron-flavoured crème caramel. Pro tip: tea reigns over coffee here.

Name: Bergamote
Description: This bistronomic bijou is tucked away in the heart of Lyon’s Gerland district. In a snug, nature-inspired interior, youthful Maxime Pujol showcases his technical skills as he rolls out masterfully plated, seasonal dishes, packed in crisp flavours – all at eater friendly prices. Surprise evening menus; buzzy vibe.

Name: Berggasthof Schlüssel
Description: This mountain hotel and restaurant, which has been around for well over 100 years, has various comfortable rustic-style rooms, in which guests tuck into regional cuisine with a contemporary twist, crafted by chef-patron Jakob Brasch. The menu features a bouillabaisse-inspired fish soup, a wonderful beef broth with Flädle (pancake strips) or a classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) in horseradish sauce. In the evening there is also a more ambitious five-course set menu; a selection of traditional snacks is available throughout the day. Tip: Ask for table 15 by the tiled stove. Given the location in the Pfaffenberg area, at 700m above sea level, the terrace comes into its own in summer, affording views across the region. Well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Bettina
Address: 1014 Coast Village Rd., Santa Barbara, CA, 93108, USA
Description: After making a match at NYC’s Roberta’s, Brendan Smith and Rachel Greenspan took their pizza-powered love affair to the West Coast to a gleaming perch in the Montecito Country Mart. Each night, the pair dishes up a bevy of pie varieties tattooed with the delicate char of their wood-fired oven. Even staples like pepperoni are exceptional, thanks to the slow-fermented dough, house-pulled mozzarella, and tangy, ripe tomatoes from Bianco DiNapoli, and seasonal options like a creamed leek pizza with pork sausage and crispy shallot are equally satisfying. Pastas, like a hand-cut tagliatelle with braised lamb shoulder, show similar care. This oven also does a solid sideline in baked goods, so grab some brown-butter chocolate chip cookies or a crusty sourdough loaf on your way out.

Name: Beynel
Address: Adliye Caddesi No:63, Bitez, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: Take a seat on the terrace of this open-air restaurant, among the mandarin and lemon trees, and prepare yourself for some Anatolian generosity. The mezze- and kebab-style dishes are perfect for sharing with friends or for a romantic dinner for two. Tempting options on the menu include roasted aubergine stuffed with meat seasoned with paprika and a yoghurt dressing, and flatbread with a lamb brochette, lamb pastrami, Golot cheese and an onion salad with sumac and fresh herbs. Discover a world of rich flavours that won't break the bank!

Name: Beğendik Abi
Address: Tatar Cami Sokak No:12, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: There is a rustic charm about this place that is reflected in the food. At the counter, there is an impressive selection of mezze and hot dishes that you can also order straight away. Market-fresh Turkish cuisine is prepared with great passion and respect for tradition. Take, for example, the green beans cooked in a tomato sauce with onion and smoked aubergine, served with well-seasoned yoghurt, or the lamb stew with a light stock made from tomato, garlic and pepper, enhanced with cumin and coriander. At Beğendik Abi you are guaranteed a delicious and affordable dining experience. The queue that often forms at the door doesn't lie.

Name: Beštija
Description: In the inner courtyard of a building in the town centre is this simply styled bistro, frequented by a young and varied clientele, which is also reflected in the background music with a "cool" feel. The culinary offerings are not extensive (as is the wine list, offset, however, by a small selection of cocktails), and are based on market ingredients and local produce. Both meat and fish dishes on the menu are Mediterranean-inspired, designed to enhance taste and a certain indulgence.

Name: Bi Dian Hai Xian ‧ Tou Deng Cang
Address: 18 Binshui Road, Hexi, Tianjin, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This glitzy restaurant with huge fish tanks is the flagship of an F&B group. Fish and shellfish are shipped from around the world, but the spotlight is on produce from around the Jiaodong Peninsula that is crafted in myriad ways. Traditionally, sea cucumber is braised with scallion, but it also tastes great as a cold appetiser or blanched in soup. Hand-wrapped dumplings are another must-try – especially stuffed with marine spoon worms and chives.

Name: Bianca
Address: 4/2 Robert Street, Ellerslie, Auckland, 1051, New Zealand
Description: The uncluttered room sports wooden booths and tables, and a few counter seats overlooking the kitchen, where you can see their famous pasta, renowned for its texture, handmade from scratch. The owner-chef curates a concise menu of deftly crafted dishes that focus on premium New Zealand produce, delivering fresh, honest flavours. Soft, fragrant focaccia sets the tone for a lovely meal. Sit at the counter to see the alchemy unfold.

Name: Bibijae
Address: 45 Namcheonbada-ro 10 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48314, South Korea
Description: Bibimbap is a versatile Korean dish with flavors that can drastically change depending on the ingredients. Bibijae offers bibimbap dishes made with creative combinations of ingredients and flavors. Diners can not only enjoy classic bibimbap but also enjoy creative twists with seasonal ingedients. There’s more - for those who prefer piping hot bibimbap, all dishes can be upgraded to a hot stone bowl. It is exciting to see what new flavor profiles Bibijae adds to the humble bibimbap.

Name: Bibik's Kitchen
Address: 73 Jalan Sri Bahari, George Town, 10050, Malaysia
Description: “Bibik” is an honorific used to address older Peranakan women, and the room is aptly decorated with classic Nyonya motifs. Naturally, the menu showcases the owner’s heirloom Peranakan recipes that are slightly less spicy than their counterparts elsewhere. Dishes come in three sizes – try their jiu hu char (stir-fried yam bean with shredded cuttlefish), and loh bak (deep-fried five-spice pork rolls).

Name: Bibine Buvette
Description: This is the second restaurant of Chloé Ouellet, chef and owner of Au Pâturage – Espaces Gourmands in Sainte-Perpétue. Dishes draw on vegetables from its kitchen garden and Quebec ingredients such as halibut, venison and scallops. The short and punchy menu lists a dozen appealing dishes, including home-made bread with garlic confit butter, pan-fried scallops with corn and peaches, and venison loin with carrots, barley and blue cheese. Precise seasoning, vinegary notes and bistronomy spirit – it's a home run. The large bar and covered terrace add to the convivial atmosphere.

Name: Biblioteka
Address: Zamek Książ, Piastów Śląskich 1, Wałbrzych, 58-306, Poland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: As settings go, few restaurants can top this. Even the drive here is impressive, passing extensive well-kept gardens and grounds before reaching the imposing Zamek Książ castle. In its former gatehouse, up a spiral stone staircase, sits this delightful eatery in the old library. Well-crafted and wallet-friendly dishes ensure you get plenty for your money, with satisfying flavours bursting from the likes of Kwaśnica soup or chicken supreme with polenta cake. The team are charming and the minstrels’ gallery is the perfect spot for private parties.

Name: Biestro H-eat
Description: This hip bistro never fails to appeal. Trendy lighting, a vintage wood-burning stove and a full view of the chefs working in their flame-licked open kitchen. Ellen graciously and seamlessly supervises the front of house. A patriotic lineup of Flemish classics, complete with Asian twists and Mediterranean flair, are blended into enticing set menus. Belgian staples such as eel have no secrets for the consummate chefs, who serve this family favourite in a sabayon of green herbs with heaps of piping hot crunchy fries. Or how about a fillet of halibut with a frothy velvety bearnaise sauce, nobashi shrimps and oyster leaf? Generosity shines through in every detail of this friendly bistro that hits all the right buttons!

Name: Bij Erik
Description: Wood, metal and leather lend this restaurant an intimate feel; a striking glass-fronted wine cabinet adds the perfect final flourish. In fine weather, a table on the terrace is the best choice – the view of the lock and windmill is magnificent. Chef Erik Tas delights diners with bright, harmonious pairings in which sauces and broths are delicately balanced. Take his multi-layered signature dish featuring pork belly, langoustine and foie royal, accompanied by herb oil and a peppery jus. Service is friendly and professional, with the chef himself often welcoming diners warmly. Bij Erik is impeccably run and delivers superb value for money.

Name: Bij Mette
Description: Picturesque Linschoten is worth a visit in its own right, but be sure to seek out this beautifully converted grocery shop with its distinctive spiral staircase, a stone's throw from the leaning clock tower. This is old Dutch charm at its best! Chef-patron Carel Alberts welcomes you personally before going on to showcase his expertise in the French classics, with the occasional Mediterranean flourish. Wonderful local produce, intense sauces, respect for tradition: it all makes for an enjoyable culinary experience. Take, for example, the generous duck breast dish with a jus from the duck itself, laced with just the right amount of chilli, served with accompaniments such as roasted cauliflower and Brussels sprouts. Ask the chef about his wine list; he will be happy to elaborate. The Bib Gourmand set menu is always a good choice!

Name: Bird
Description: In the heart of this charming borough, on a pedestrian square near the town hall, a pocket-sized restaurant run by a young chef with an impressive cv. Market-inspired menu with the likes of fresh pasta with mussels, calamari and langoustines, or poultry quenelles with freekeh... Scandinavian style dining room, terrace overlooking a fountain. Delicious prices.

Name: Birdy's by Achtien
Description: If you love sharing plates, this place is made for you! At both lunch and dinner, chef Christian Vogel presents his "Sharing is Love" concept – an engaging dining experience set in a relaxed, contemporary atmosphere, where great food and lively conversation go hand in hand. The cuisine is plant-forward but can be complemented by top-quality fish or meat. Choose dishes à la carte, such as "Caesar-style lettuce salad" with wild garlic, Sbrinz AOP and beetroot, or celery tarte Tatin with apple, walnut and celery, or opt for the surprise sharing menu for two. As an alternative to the wine pairings, the thoughtfully composed mocktails are well worth trying. A dedicated children's menu makes this a wonderfully family-friendly option. Set against the magnificent backdrop of the Alps, the location enjoys sweeping views over Lake Lucerne. Tip: In the centre of the restaurant, The Nest operates as a food bar in the evenings – an excellent alternative.

Name: Biriyani Osawa
Description: Once served in royal courts, biryani later became a beloved dish among the public. This rice dish, cooked with spices and various ingredients, is the restaurant’s sole offering—made with either mutton or chicken. The basmati rice is richly fragrant, with distinct, separate grains. Oil is used sparingly, to bring the umami of the ingredients and the flavours of the spices to the fore. Meal preparation is carefully timed so the biryani finishes cooking just as all guests are seated, ensuring everyone enjoys it in all its fresh-from-the-pot deliciousness. Passion and spirit imbue every dish.

Name: Birrieria Zaragoza
Description: Now hosting in Uptown since their Archer Heights location is closed, this Mexican institution specializes in a single item—birria—tender, stewed goat. In fact, goat is all that’s on the menu, though you’ll get a few options as to how to enjoy it: on a plate or in a bowl, in a small or large portion, bone-in or bone-out. The bowl option drowns the goat in a generous dose of hearty consommé, while the plate is accompanied by handmade corn tortillas for build-your-own tacos, with a small side of the broth for dipping. You can’t go wrong either way, but if you’re feeling extra decadent, go for the quesadilla, a perfect trinity of pillowy tortillas, gooey cheese, and savory goat meat goodness.

Name: Bis Bistró
Address: Vicente López 1661 Local 12, Buenos Aires, C1018ABA, Argentina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Few places in Buenos Aires are as original as Bis Bistró, located in a charming passageway full of shops that inevitably draws comparisons with the romantic alleyways so typical of Paris. This bistro, which could be described as the younger brother of the renowned Aramburu (located opposite – chef Gonzalo Aramburu is in charge of both), has a classic ambience that comes as a pleasant surprise, having retained its 1950s-style bistro essence and appearance (high ceilings, globe lamps, long banquettes, mirrors etc) alongside a glass-fronted kitchen and a small bar. The reasonably contemporary à la carte (potato omelette, fresh capers and anchovies, rack of Patagonian lamb, pavlova with seasonal fruits etc) aims to re-create delicious recipes with traditional roots and modern tastes, complemented by a two- or three-course weekday lunchtime “executive” menu. The background music here is particularly pleasant.

Name: Bismillah Biryani (Little India)
Description: Biryani is the standout dish in this place specialising in North Indian food. The lamb shank biryani is recommended for its fork-tender texture and meaty flavour. Haleem, mutton nihari and aloo gobi are also good choices.

Name: Bistro
Description: It's no wonder the charming restaurant in this spruce historical building is so popular: the food here is unpretentious and packed with flavour! The combination of a modern yet cosy interior and genuine, personable service overseen by the owner fosters a truly pleasant and welcoming atmosphere. The small terrace overlooking the church and market square is also lovely. At lunchtime there is a small a la carte option or a three-course meal deal and in the evening the ‘St Benedict’ gourmet menu. Tip: They also have a cookery school.

Name: Bistro
Description: Elegance meets a welcoming warmth and a touch of intimacy in this manor house, which is also home to De Gieser Wildeman for those seeking a more refined dining experience. The chalkboard menu lists accessible brasserie classics with a modern twist (always with meat, fish and vegetarian options). Expect dishes such as succulent farmhouse chicken leg with crispy skin, served with a creamy mushroom sauce, mashed potatoes, sautéed mushrooms and freshly cooked chips. No-nonsense generous dishes that always satisfy.

Name: Bistro Aragosta
Description: Intimate Aragosta has the easy-going charm of a classic bistro, with tables set close together, a warm welcome and an appreciation of good wine. Opt for the surprise menu or the dedicated lobster menu, but be sure to ask about the à la carte selection too. If you prefer one of the suggestions to a dish on the set menu, the team will happily make the swap. Chef Wouter and his team are well versed in classic French cooking, though the surprise menu reveals a more modern approach. The veal blanquette is a textbook example of classic comfort food: succulent veal with meatballs and porcini with a crisp puff pastry lid. Bistro Aragosta's honest and generous cooking represents exemplary value for money.

Name: Bistro B
Description: This bistro has reopened after a full-scale makeover that sports more comfort and elegance, new furnishings, modern light fixtures and a glazed wine cellar. The vibe is as warm and welcoming as ever, depicted by an open-plan kitchen offering a splendid view of the team at work. The chef now focuses on smaller but ever indulgent helpings, in a more forthright and less Gallic vein, but always courtesy of high-flying ingredients and attractive plating: steamed cod, caponata and puttanesca seasoning; lamb’s sweetbread sausages and foie gras; biscuit, ganache and chocolate ice cream. The owner’s market garden supplies the majority of the restaurant’s fruit and veg in season.

Name: Bistro Cerisier
Description: The antique interior evokes the charm of a countryside bistro. Captivated by French cuisine, the owner has brought her dreams of France to life. Regional dishes line the menu, with offerings including fish soup, goat's cheese salad and sautéed frog. Stewed dishes such as choucroute and cassoulet are served in generous portions. Diners can savour a taste of France right here in Kyoto.

Name: Bistro De Ertepeller
Description: The view of the Drierivierenpunt and the endless stream of boats always draws plenty of attention in this sleek yet cosy bistro. A glance at the tempting set menu reveals that the chef likes to elevate French cuisine with North African spices. From tender lamb neck served with a robust meat-based jus, to crisp pistachio-filled baklava accompanied by mint and yogurt ice cream – this cuisine is defined by precise technique, bold flavours and meticulous plating. The 250-label wine list, with a particular emphasis on Burgundy and broad international reach, is sure to pique your interest.

Name: Bistro Français
Address: 165/167 King William Road, Adelaide, SA 5061, Australia
Description: From the posters to the pendant lights illuminating the space, Bistro Français has the classic look down pat. This cozy spot brings the spirit of France to this residential area just south of downtown Adelaide. The kitchen delivers a hit list of dishes like onion gratin soup and duck confit, while escargots and beef à la Bourgogne speak to the chef's training. Savor the traditional preparation of smooth and creamy chicken liver terrine served with a warm thyme- and garlic-flavored baguette. It's enough to share, though you may find yourself feeling selfish. A large bone-in pork loin is tender and moist, served with green pepper sauce and duck fat potatoes.

Name: Bistro Loora
Address: Ul. Ivana Pavla II 5, Đakovo, 31400, Croatia
Description: Located on a lively pedestrian street in the center leading to the striking Cathedral of St. Peter, this small, welcoming bistro is recognizable by its pleasant outdoor seating nestled in a shaded courtyard. The contemporary interior offers a relaxed atmosphere for enjoying regional cuisine reinterpreted with creativity and a modern touch. Don’t miss the chef’s signature take on Beef Wellington.

Name: Bistro Lupa
Description: Not far from Nordhavn lies this vegan bistro that comes with simple décor and a lively atmosphere. Environmental awareness is a big theme, with a focus on local and seasonal produce, some of it foraged locally or sourced from their own mushroom farm. The good value tasting menu shows off a great range of techniques, with the well-balanced dishes ranging from roasted cauliflower glazed with sticky hoisin sauce to their signature fried blue oyster mushrooms with tamarind ketchup. The serving team are both charming and knowledgeable, and the homemade sparkling kombucha comes highly recommended.

Name: Bistro Luux
Description: No need to wonder whether Bistro Luux is open: this upscale bistro welcomes diners every day, both at lunchtime and in the evening – and whenever you decide to come, the mood inside is wonderfully relaxed. The terrace on the market square is also inviting. In the open kitchen to the rear, you can see seasoned chef Ron Lemmens at work. He closed his previous restaurant (Flavours) in order to pursue a more accessible cooking style, more akin to French cuisine. From his lavish bouillabaisse with impeccably fresh fish to a vol-au-vent enriched by a rich velouté and crisp vegetables, or even a whole lobster Bellevue, he brings tradition to life with generosity and a commitment to quality. The broad menu will undoubtedly make choosing difficult. You could happily make this a daily habit.

Name: Bistro Margarete
Description: With this lovely bistro, Thorsten Bender offers an alternative to sein, his restaurant right next door. The place has a stylish and lively feel; the terrace in the courtyard makes for an irresistibly romantic setting in summer. The commitment that the owners bring to their work is palpable – both in the delicious regional cuisine, which includes classic and modern dishes, and the inviting and pleasingly laid-back service under the direction of the lady of the house. Good food is accompanied by wines at prices that won't break the bank. At lunch, the reasonably priced set menu draws a crowd. Tip: Adjacent to the bistro is the intimate and stylishly cosy Séparée. Here, a six-course set menu with wine or non-alcoholic pairings is served to up to 10 diners at the communal "Community Table" – can be booked Thu-Sun evenings.

Name: Bistro Nijeholt
Description: This inviting bistro is located on the Lauswolt country estate, a beautiful green oasis where you can also stay in luxurious guestrooms and dine at MICHELIN-starred De Heeren van Harinxma. The atmosphere here is wonderfully relaxed. Expect no unnecessary frills, but generous dishes that combine flavours from further afield with local ingredients and what's available at the market, all served as part of a fantastic set menu with a choice of options. The chefs are equally at home serving up a refreshingly tart ceviche and reworking the traditional Haagse bluf – a generous dessert made with whipped egg whites, redcurrants and vanilla ice cream. A Bib Gourmand through and through!

Name: Bistro Saine
Address: 1F, 51 Albert Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: With his multicultural background, Chef Yutak Son reimagines bistro classics with subtle Mediterranean touches that showcase a seasonal, ingredient-driven lineup. His velvety chicken liver parfait bursts with flavour; his rack of lamb with anchovy sauce and pommes dauphine is juicy and tender. The well-curated wine list spans the Old and New Worlds, with a splendid by-the-glass range. The understated, stylish interior exudes a laid-back vibe.

Name: Bistro Toost
Description: In Amstelveen's Oude Dorp, the old part of town, Toost is a welcoming and vibrant bistro where the dried leaves hanging from the ceiling lend the setting a Mediterranean feel. A seat at the long bar is always a good idea. Diners order à la carte, choosing from a variety of classic dishes served in smaller portions. The appealing simplicity of egg mayonnaise, the succulence of steak tartare with fresh chips, or the generosity of honey-glazed, crisp-fried veal sweetbreads, with the punch of an airy mustard foam and slivers of green apple for acidity – this is straightforward cooking designed to please. Familiar cooking with a focus on ingredients that really make a difference – and at excellent value for money. Don't forget to book!

Name: Bistro Yanagihara
Description: A bistro by a chef who apprenticed in Alsace. For appetisers, he showcases his skills with choucroute of salt-pickled fermented cabbage, confit of foie gras and charcuterie of ham and sausages. His main dishes are prepared with no less care: items such as beef simmered in red wine and pâté grilled in a pastry shell have their flavours drawn out over time. Hearty portions ensure a full stomach.

Name: Bistro by Regina Montium
Description: Whether you hike up or take the mountain railway (ideal from Vitznau), it's well worth stopping off here. The location is idyllic – at 1 550m above sea level, the terrace is wonderful – and the "natural cuisine" is another big attraction! Many of the ingredients are drawn from the immediate surroundings or harvested from the restaurant's own garden. The menu features smaller plates and regular dishes such as "terroir burger", ragout or medium-rare cuts of Rigi organic beef. Vegetarian options include organic potato gnocchi or "Alpine omelette". Friendly and well-informed staff talk you through the individual ingredients. And as an apéritif, why not try an alcohol-free"Chrüterwässer" made with garden herb extracts and cherry juice? Both the Bistro, for lunch, and fine dining restaurant, Regina Montium, for dinner, are housed in Kräuterhotel Edelweiss, where you can stay overnight after your meal.

Name: Bistrobar Berlin
Description: Bold and trendy, this bistro bar shares Berlin's avant-garde spirit. The music is a little louder downstairs, and it is more comfortable upstairs, but the restaurant's creative streak is evident throughout. The enticing menu brings together a variety of dishes, ranging from adventurous and eclectic to more familiar. Sea bass, for example, is pan-fried until succulent with beautifully crisp skin and paired with a subtly spicy oyster mushroom rendang, refreshing grapefruit and a light lime-leaf sauce. The chefs deftly play with texture and pronounced flavours without making their dishes overly complex. Bistrobar Berlin has a youthful energy that keeps diners coming back.

Name: Bistrot 1965
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: There are some places, such as this restaurant occupying the former bar of the Hotel Empòrium, that can pass almost unnoticed compared with their more famous siblings (the award-winning and elegant Empòrium is also located here) due to the fact that they are simpler in style and more affordable to the public. Despite this, Bistrot 1965 is definitely a spot with its own personality. Its cuisine, which is also overseen by brothers Màrius and Joan Jordà (they alternate the cooking between them every week), is centred around a single fixed-price menu, to which you can also add more dishes from a list of specials. The aim of the tasty dishes designed for sharing is to provide an updated take on traditional recipes and to showcase the native ingredients of the Alt Empordà region (eggs from free-range hens, duck ampordanès, Ripollés sheep yogurt, artisan cheeses, etc.).

Name: Bistrot Brioude
Description: Under the same roof as its sister restaurant, Brioude, is the bistro, which has its own separate space – itself split into two bright areas. It serves a smart, traditional market-fresh menu: poultry, pistachio and morel pâté en croûte; fin gras du Mézenc, porcini and carrot purée; feuillantine praline and coffee ice cream. Suffice to say, you're in for a treat – and at an affordable price! On top of that, there's a terrace and a cordial welcome awaits.

Name: Bistrot DuPont
Description: This pleasant traditional French bistro by the River Seine has a friendly front-of-house team serving up good old-fashioned recipes. Tuck into veal kidneys with mustard sauce, coq au vin, or frogs' legs with persillade sauce in a lively atmosphere… Be sure to sample the house speciality: andouillette.

Name: Bistrot Dumas
Description: This buzzy bistro located in the Champel neighbourhood is often fully booked. The interior is done out simply and tastefully – it is the Art Nouveau stained-glass ceiling panels, as well as the columns, that draw the eye. Their classic take on traditional French cuisine is flavoursome and aromatic, plus everything is made in-house. The service is efficient and attentive.

Name: Bistrot Le Héron
Description: At the foot of this gorgeous village, known for its abbey church and Pierre Soulages's stained-glass windows, Moulin de Cambelong is home to this bistronomy restaurant, a friendly and down-to-earth alternative to Émilie and Thomas's MICHELIN-starred restaurant. Tuck into indulgent cuisine: tomato gazpacho, mussels and vierge vinaigrette; pulled pork with sorrel sauce.

Name: Bistrot Louise
Description: In the heart of a village of orchards devoted to walnut growing, this lovely stone building is where Yann Tanneau rolls out a creative and enticing lineup. After learning the ropes in top houses, this tattooed and enthusiastic chef crafts and serves, entirely single-handedly, perfectly executed first-class dishes. You may start with a yummy association of oeuf parfait, creamy celery, smoked haddock and Iberic lomo. For the main course, we recommend juicy, tender poultry breast, underscored by cardamon, combawa and green curry. This elegant, gourmet feast is sampled in a simple, welcoming interior. Booking is essential in this establishment, whose value for pleasure ratio is truly exceptional.

Name: Bistrot Lucien
Address: La Rôtisserie du Chambertin, 6 rue du Chambertin, Gevrey-Chambertin, 21220, France
Description: Bare stone walls, bench seating and a superb wooden counter set the scene in this bistro, which is housed in its parent hotel. Expertly crafted burgundy recipes take pride of place on the nostalgic menu: home-cured ham, poached egg in wine, Bresse poultry, profiteroles... Fantastic wine list!

Name: Bistrot Saveurs
Description: British chef Simon Scott worked his way from London to Provence, before setting up shop here in the Tarn département. The vivid red façade leads diners into a vibrant and cosy pop-inspired decor. This eclectic chef and master craftsman works exclusively with good-quality (local) ingredients, in a bid to serve his guests precise, colourful and tasty dishes that change regularly according to the market stalls. This Bistrot des Saveurs is certainly aptly named!

Name: Bistrot Vivienne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
Description: A bistro run by a sommelier and chef. Keen to impart a sense of everyday life in France, the partners focus on charcuterie and hometown cooking. Populating the menu are delights such as cassoulet, quenelle and beef cheek simmered in wine. Respecting the classics, dishes baked in pie pastry are also included. In keeping with the regional tenor of the bistro, wines of every region are here for the asking; pair them with dishes of the same region for the consummate mariage.

Name: Bistrot d'Antoine
Address: 27 rue de la Préfecture, Nice, 06300, France
Description: The lilting accent of the South of France can be detected in this bistro, where a really convivial atmosphere reigns. Things hot up in the kitchen, with delicious dishes such as old-fashioned pork casserole with creamy polenta, knife-cut beef tartare or grilled veal kidney with wholegrain mustard and baby potatoes in a parsley sauce... Crowded? Well, yes: Antoine has a huge (and well-deserved) success on his hands.

Name: Bistrot de la Maison Tiegezh
Address: 7 place de la Gare, Guer, 56380, France
Description: Garden-fresh tomato salad and courgette cream, local fish of the day, grilled meat and vegetables from local growers, followed by a vanilla millefeuille pastry with salted butter caramel: taste the market-fresh, country cuisine, without killer prices, of a star chef in this bistro, next-door to his star establishment.

Name: Bistrot des Anges
Address: Rue de l'Ouest, Le Cannet, 06110, France
Description: This brasserie, run by the team from Villa Archange, sports a modern decor, a buzzy vibe and set menus inspired by sunny climes! Tuck into white and green asparagus tartlet with feta cream, loin of croaker paired with mint-flavoured green peas and gnocchi. For dessert, all that remains is to try and make your choice from a wickedly tempting sweets trolley filled with treats. You'll be in seventh heaven!

Name: Bistrot des Fables
Description: A fabulous bistro repertoire of tried-and-true classics: think herring fillets, potatoes in oil; œufs mimosa (devilled eggs); scallops roasted in butter; veal blanquette; profiteroles, vanilla ice cream and chocolate gianduja. The menu is devised by David Bottreau in the spirit of Christian Constant, his long-time associate and mentor. Generous, flavoursome cuisine in a typical Parisian bistro atmosphere, where diners tuck in cheek to jowl at small tables laid out next to each other.

Name: Bistrot di Pescheria
Description: This attractive, contemporary-style bistro is the “low-cost” sibling of the Pescheria restaurant situated in a more upmarket location on Salerno’s seafront. Run by the same management, the bistro aims to serve simpler dishes at more modest prices yet with the same focus on freshness and attention to detail evident in its sister-restaurant. As a result, you’ll find options such as oily fish and local white prawns on the menu rather than oysters and caviar. Don’t miss the squid soup with nduja sausage, potato mousse and crispy bread.

Name: Bistrot du Lion d'Or
Description: In the restaurant of this hotel dating from 1750, the team conjures up a cavalcade of delicate, expertly crafted Gallic dishes, made with seasonal produce. Examples: artichoke, smoked whitefish from the nearby lake and buckwheat, or pan-fried calf’s sweetbread, morels and asparagus. The well-curated wine list is definitely worth a gander. The cheerful front-of-house team enjoys explaining the finer points of each dish. The interior sports small bistro tables, there is a peaceful terrace to the rear that is heavenly in fine weather and a casual, affable spirit reigns throughout.

Name: Bistrot du Pollet
Description: In Dieppe’s historic fishermen’s quarter (Le Pollet), this bistro in the zeitgeist pays tribute to the local catch, which naturally dictates the menu: scallops, monkfish, John Dory, squid… Everything is flawlessly fresh, of the finest quality and generously served. A few meat dishes are also available à la carte (like ravioles of poultry with foie gras, sweetbreads or fillet of duckling). Buzzy, casual vibe.

Name: Bistrot la Coulemelle
Description: Bang in the middle of the village, the historic HQ of the Marcon family is today a bistro-leaning outpost devoted to big-boned flavoursome cooking in harmony with the seasons. Gravlax of zander with dill-laced cream; roast saddle and confit leg of rabbit with puréed peppers and a blueberry soufflé with pistachio ice cream to die for… Everything is devilishly delicious and the open kitchen lends the place a homely feel. What more can we say?

Name: Bistró Amunt
Description: With this bistro, located on the upper floor of the award-winning L'Antic Molí and with its own entrance, chef Vicent Guimerà diversifies the business by offering something that reflects the essence of his cuisine but in a more informal way. The proposal, with tradition at its core but with modern touches, revolves around a set menu with a choice of main course (there is also another, with the same offer, which includes two glasses of wine). The cuisine continues to be built from a focus on the seasonal produce of Terres de l'Ebre, Terres del Sénia and Parc Natural dels Ports. Among the dishes you will find stuffed peppers with aurora sauce, cabbage trinxat with pork belly, crispy rice with rabbit, lamb with shitake, shimejis and pumpkin, and more.

Name: Bitan Chiao Tou Goose
Address: 127, Section 1, Beixin Road, Xindian District, New Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: This bright, airy room with an open kitchen by the entrance stands out on a street lined with older residential buildings. Smoked goose is the signature here – meticulously sliced and always tasty. You can order a specific number of portions or specify which cuts you prefer. It opens for four hours daily and the goose tends to run out before 1 pm. Generous table spacing and partitioned semi-private spaces ensure privacy and comfort.

Name: Blasers Restaurant
Description: A popular place to eat! A relaxed atmosphere reigns in this inviting contemporary interior, where diners tuck into pleasingly unpretentious dishes that impress with their flavours and craftsmanship. The menu features not only traditional regional dishes, including classics such as beef tartare, but also Asian specialities in the "Thai Corner" section of the menu, such as gaeng mussaman – a mild Thai curry with peanuts and king prawns. There is also a pleasant terrace with a magnificent view of the mountains of the Bernese Oberland. Next to the restaurant, the small Hotel National has cosy guestrooms. It also has its own confectioner's.

Name: Blisko Bar
Description: Enter this inviting neighbourhood spot and you’ll soon see the walls filled with natural and low-intervention wines – which are a perfect fit for the relaxed, on-trend vibe and cosy surroundings. Settle in at your table amidst the exposed brickwork and ask the charming team for recommendations on which wines to try, then accompany them with the brilliantly priced cooking. Both the light Neapolitan-style pizzas and the seasonal small plates provide bags of flavour in every mouthful. Bring your friends, order lots and have a simply wonderful time.

Name: Blood Bros BBQ
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Few smokehouses celebrate the city’s diverse cultural footprint quite like this one, where Texas barbecue traditions merge with Chinese, Vietnamese and Korean flavors. Where else will you find banh mi with pho-rubbed beef belly, a swipe of garlic aioli, chicken liver pâté? How many pitmasters glaze their ribs in gochujang? Classic offerings of brisket and ribs satisfy, but the restaurant’s heart lives in the daily specials, which change with great frequency. Take a look around: A nearby table (indoors or out) will always have a dish you wish you had ordered. How’s the brisket fried rice? What about that smoked char siu banh mi? Do you have room for the watermelon salad? These are questions for the next visit – and the visits after that.

Name: Blossom
Address: L501, Plaza 66, 1266 West Nanjing Road, Jingan, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: The wood-rich and fabric upholstery of the decor leans towards Scandinavia, yet the kitchen team of mostly Chaoshan natives specialises in no-frills traditional Chaozhou dishes. One of their eight signature items, marinated pork trotter, is loaded with collagen and the marinade delivers layered aromas and sweetness. Another must-try is silver pomfret in soybean sauce that sports perfect doneness, tender flesh and savoury depth.

Name: Blume
Description: This charming restaurant serves regional cuisine prepared with high-quality ingredients – the chef has a particular passion for risotto. Offal dishes, such as tripe or liver, are also available. The Gourmet Galgenspiess flambiert (flambéed hanging skewer) and the Chateaubriand have to be ordered in advance and are served to the whole table. The rustic downstairs space makes for a cosy setting; the upstairs room is a little more elegant. With her friendly, outgoing manner, the proprietress brings a personal touch to the service. The peaceful rural location, about 25km from Zurich, is a draw in itself.

Name: Bobe
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This relaxed, homely bistro sits within an attractive 18th-century townhouse on an ancient cobbled square in the Old Town and is run by local celebrity chef Bo Bech. The team work calmly in the open kitchen crafting honest, bistro-style dishes from local ingredients; lunchtime sees a selection of smørrebrød – maybe duck sausages with pickled beetroots and chives or suckling pig with baked Jerusalem artichokes and a fried egg – while dinner offers well-priced dishes such as lamb heart with cherries and wood sorrel. If you come in the evening, arrive early for a drink in the basement wine bar.

Name: Boda
Address: 13F, Mövenpick Hotel, 8 Customs Street East, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Boda means ‘to see’ in Korean. Perched atop a hotel tower, the dining room commands truly knockout harbour views and the food also looks as good as it tastes. The Korean-born chef champions modern Korean fare that hinges on fresh, seasonal ingredients, as well as recipes inspired by his family heritage. His ricotta gnocchi tteokbokki in soy beurre blanc with parmesan and smoked leeks deftly juggles Korean and Italian flavours.

Name: Bohemian Spirit Restaurant
Address: 321 E. 73rd St., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: It's old-world Bohemia, not hippie-chic, at this Czech beer hall located on the first floor of the National Bohemian Hall building. It exudes a classic European bar vibe with wood paneling, simple wood tables and vintage knick knacks. Naturally, beers and pilsners are the drink of choice, but for grape lovers, there is a nice European-focused wine list sprinkled with Czech wines. Hearty fare is definitely in store here. A large bowl of borscht arrives redolent of dill and is tangy and vibrant with a buttery finish, while grilled kielbasa is smoky and moist, sided by a mustard-forward potato salad. Dumplings litter the menu, even at dessert, where strawberry-filled dumplings topped with crumbled gingerbread are a delicious finale.

Name: Bohém
Description: Delicious and perfectly presented traditional Czech cuisine! With passion and culinary expertise, the kitchen team cooks up regional classics such as braised duck leg, rabbit and trout. A special mention goes to the Carlsbad dumplings – really delicious, fluffy bread dumplings! The moderately priced lunch special is very popular. The decor is chic and modern, and the service is friendly and professional. The restaurant is housed in the venerable Hotel Aplaus, very close to the market square, and boasts gorgeous guestrooms. Fun fact about the town: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, the castle is the birthplace of composer Bedřich Smetana.

Name: Boivin
Description: A traditional trattoria in the picturesque historic centre, with a pleasantly familiar and informal atmosphere. Many dishes on the menu reflect the traditions of Trentino, including freshwater fish. Among the most accomplished offerings: the alpine grey tongue pastrami with borlotti beans and sauerkraut, and the Mòchena spotted kid terrine with fermented giardiniera.

Name: Bokkia Tha Din Daeng
Address: 323 Tha Din Daeng Road, Somdet Chao Phraya, Khlong San, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
Description: Tucked away in a small market stall, this family-run dessert shop is famous for its sweet Bokkia. It's a unique treat: egg noodles, topped with crushed ice and syrup, which is amazingly refreshing and not too sweet. The condimental options are also good quality.

Name: Bolero
Address: GF, Verve Residences Tower 2, High Street South, 26th 27th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, 1634, The Philippines
Description: Led by chef Fernando Alcalá Garaizábal of Kava in Marbella, Bolero charms with its Spanish soul. The largely Spanish menu is laced with Mediterranean notes and the odd global influence – built for sharing, generous portions make for great value. Start with a cocktail from the extensive list. Dishes such as coal-grilled Ibérico presa and ribeye empanadas impress, but the highlight is a decadent, molten-centred cheesecake – an award-winner in Spain.

Name: Boma
Description: Tucked away behind the town hall, this compact restaurant has a somewhat unusual basement-level dining room with exposed stone, metal beams, glass partitions and modern light fittings. The chef cooks up hearty dishes, remarkable for both their generosity and bold flavours: maiale tonnato, Parmesan and capers; magret de canard, mashed potatoes with whole-grain mustard, vegetables and a piquillo pepper coulis. Friendly welcome and service, and the lunchtime set menu is a steal!

Name: Bomb Biscuit Co.
Address: 519 Memorial Dr. SE, Ste. B-02, Atlanta, GA, 30312, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Once a pop-up and a food stall, this popular breakfast and brunch restaurant has moved down the street from their original brick-and-mortar location in Grant Park. The new space may be larger and more contemporary, but that freshly baked vibe remains. The menu shows off simple but successful plates ranging from breakfast sandwiches to brunch plates with fried chicken and other staples. Baked goods, like cinnamon rolls with a thick, tangy cream cheese glaze, are exceptional, but given the name, biscuits, ranging from traditional to jalapeno and cheddar, are an absolute must. Go for broke with a hearty biscuit sandwich stacked high with egg and cheese or hot honey chicken with pickles.

Name: Bombance
Address: 23 rue de la Chalotais, Rennes, 35000, France
Description: The name hints at an abundance of food, drink and fun with friends, a promise that is kept within the stone walls of this bistro with an open kitchen and a few seats at the counter. The lunchtime and evening menus offer dishes ranging from roast pak choi, paprika sabayon and roasted hazelnut to skate wing, citrus butter, cream of celery, smoked Jerusalem artichoke, chestnuts and a langoustine jus – or plates to share washed down with a well-curated list of biodynamic or natural wines. Fresh ingredients, fine craftsmanship and overflowing with vibrant flavours and skill.

Name: Bombay Palace (Wānaka)
Description: The snug room juggles contemporary and traditional Indian motifs, but it’s the terrace commanding unobstructed views of Lake Wanaka that will really blow you away. The menu spans the diverse food culture of South India and Mumbai with traditionally crafted recipes. For larger parties, the tandoori platter is a great way to start the meal. The indulgent, satisfying curry butter chicken with garlic naan is even better with a glass of mango lassi to cut through the richness.

Name: Bombay Street Kitchen
Address: 6215 S. Orange Blossom Trl., Orlando, FL, 32809, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Amit Kumar's fresh and fine outlet sports a welcoming exterior and cheerful interior, done up with orange booths and bright accents. Diners may settle in for a range of enjoyable, well-prepared South Indian small plates which form the nucleus of this tempting menu.The street special dosa is a departure from the norm, here stuffed with potato, cabbage, paneer and red onion, and served with coconut sambal and curry gravy for dipping.Vegetarians will thrill to the sight of meat-free specials, like kathal masaledar, featuring tender chunks of jackfruit in a zesty tomato-and-onion masala; while tandoor options like hara teekha murg tikka (skewers of white meat chicken marinated in a herbal mixture) is grilled to luscious, crisp perfection.

Name: Bombera
Description: Fire provides the central motif for this boisterous community staple, from the venue itself (a former fire station) to the name (Spanish for fire woman), all the way to a crackling wood-fired oven that not only animates the kitchen, but also provides ash used to nixtamalize corn for house-made masa. All of this seems perfectly fitting for Chef Dominica Rice-Cisneros, whose passion has helped to shape Oakland's current Mexican restaurant scene, combining a locavore pedigree and fine dining chops with a respect for the generational knowledge of heritage cooking. The single best illustration might be a dish of beautifully rendered duck leg confit, paired with a delightfully complex, nutty mole verde, just-right black beans and handmade blue corn tortillas.

Name: Bona Fide
Description: Located midway between Helsinki Cathedral and the sea, is this simple little bistro decorated in blue and white tones, where the welcoming service team help to create an upbeat atmosphere. Two regularly changing, keenly priced set menus are the draw, with the natural, uncomplicated dishes inspired by modern Mediterranean flavours. The chefs have a great understanding of their ingredients and treat them with care, and flavours are subtle but put together in well-thought-out combinations, such as asparagus and nori seaweed or rhubarb with Earl Grey and lemongrass.

Name: Bonnie's
Description: Located within earshot of the BQE’s rumble in east Williamsburg in a nondescript corner, Bonnie's is an absolute discovery. Inside, the look is retro Hong Kong diner through and through but Chef Calvin Eng plates Cantonese regional cuisine with modern interpretations. Yeung yu sang choi bao is a wonder, stuffed with shrimp, green mustard and lettuces, then crisped and presented whole. The salt and pepper shrimp is tossed with melted red onions and is ideal for sharing. Don't sleep on the classic Hong Kong street food like cheung fun, with tender, seared rice noodles tossed with shrimp and scallop X.O. sauce and bits of cured pork. The creativity extends through dessert.

Name: Boon & De Koot
Description: A charming vintage bistro with tables set close together for a cosy feel, an irresistible menu filled with accessible yet flavoursome dishes, and a broad European wine selection put together with real expertise. What a delightful place this is! The chef enjoys working with vegetables and embraces the power of simplicity. A briefly deep-fried egg with Jerusalem artichoke cream and a medley of crispy potato skins and wild mushrooms finished with chives is a perfect example. With just a few components, he conjures up rich, playful dishes – all at moderate prices that are sure to win you over.

Name: Boon Keng Road Fish Head Bee Hoon
Description: Come here for fish head noodle soup, and choose between Spanish mackerel, red grouper and regular grouper. The fish is fresh and the broth is flavoursome. The version with poached or fried sliced fish is also worth trying.

Name: Boon Tong Kee (Balestier Road)
Description: You won’t have any trouble finding this enduringly popular restaurant – its colourful neon sign will guide you in from afar. The group may have expanded over the years but this is the original branch, opened in 1983. Their signature boiled chicken, which boosts succulent and tender meat, is still the biggest draw and comes in three different sizes, but those looking for a full zi char feast won’t be disappointed. Avoid peak times if you’re not prepared to queue.

Name: Boonie's
Address: 4337 N. Western Ave., Chicago, IL, 60618, USA
Description: The intoxicating, unmistakable aroma of garlic fills the narrow room every time someone opens the rice cooker. This rice is the foundation of all things that are good at this homey Filipino restaurant that started out as a food stall. To begin, Bundok's fried chicken is sided by a delightful grated green apple with chili. Tocilog, or griddled pork belly set with garlic fried rice, is accompanied by tasty lime and chili sauce. Dessert is a must, especially the halo halo.

Name: Borgo Poscolle
Description: This small family-run trattoria is nestled in the heart of Carnia and is an excellent example of mountain hospitality. Most of the ingredients used in the kitchen are sourced locally and are complemented by vegetables from their own organic garden. The chefs are passionate about tradition, which they present to guests with a delightful personal touch, as in the case of their cjarsons, the area's famous ravioli, the filling of which changes with the seasons.Those with a sweet tooth really must try the chocolate trilogy, one of the restaurant’s most successful and popular desserts.

Name: Bornheimer Ratskeller
Address: Kettelerallee 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60385, Germany
Description: A fantastic concept showcasing regional cuisine at outstanding value for money. The kitchen takes its cue from the changing seasons, and the menu provides information about the restaurant's nose-to-tail approach and the provenance of the ingredients. The dishes change daily according to availability and are only revealed when the restaurant opens at 5pm. Many items are so popular that they appear time and again, such as Odenwälder Handkäse (a traditional Odenwald soft cheese) or a delicious pâté. The inviting tavern-style interior and very friendly service create a charming atmosphere in which to savour good food.

Name: Boro6 Wine Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in the heart of Hastings-on-Hudson, Boro6 Wine Bar is a comfortable neighborhood spot built around a thoughtfully curated wine list and straightforward Mediterranean-inspired cooking. The menu is equally suited to a light lunch or an evening over a bottle. Begin with bright gambas al ajillo, where shrimp are sauteed with garlic and white wine, before moving to simply prepared market fish cooked acqua pazza with clams, olives, tomatoes and artichokes. Sandwiches, salads and small plates round out, and the extensive wine selection, with an emphasis on organic and biodynamic producers, encourages lingering over another glass.

Name: Botschaft
Description: After working up an appetite with a walk around the nearby Søerne Lakes, head for this elegant restaurant with a small wooden terrace, a mosaic-tiled floor and a striking green moulded ceiling. Start with a drink in the intimate hidden cocktail bar, then settle in to enjoy authentic German and Austrian dishes crafted from a mix of classic and family recipes. You might find maultaschen (pork dumplings), gebackener kalbskopf (fried calf's head) or hirschgulasch (venison stew), followed up with kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) for dessert. Wines from the two countries provide the perfect accompaniment.

Name: Bovenmeester
Description: The warm, contemporary interior of this former school (coat hooks still in place) exudes a lively brasserie atmosphere. Chef Raymond crafts à la carte dishes and a tasting menu, presenting classic flavours with modern precision. Think succulent veal cheeks served with crispy pommes dauphine, onion compote and Belgian endive braised in orange. Two rich sauces – one mustard-based, the other a Spanish wine reduction – complete the dish. Confident cooking, in generous portions that leave a lasting impression.

Name: Brandstätter
Description: A real Salzburg institution! The atmosphere in the various dining areas is perfect for a cosy dinner, but in the summer, you might prefer to sit out on the gorgeous terrace. Traditional Austrian fare dominates the menu – be sure to try the wonderful creamy veal goulash with dumplings! For those who prefer something a little more upscale, there are options such as sole and beef fillet. The service comes courtesy of an attentive and well-drilled front-of-house team. Comfortably furnished guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Good to know: You can buy house-made jams to take home. Practical for motorists: There is a large car park right in front of the building.

Name: Brasserie Barbara
Description: Open from noon to 8.30pm, Brasserie Barbara is an appealing daytime alternative to the fine dining restaurant here at the Auerhahn "wellness hotel", which is just across the road from the lake, Schluchsee. The bright, friendly atmosphere is inviting. The completely open kitchen produces cleverly devised dishes that are both bold and pleasingly uncomplicated. Based on top-notch ingredients, they are deeply rooted in regional culinary tradition. Options on the appealing à la carte menu include starters such as "Black Forest croquetas" or beef tartare with french fries, followed by a main course of local trout with a pepper salsa or fried black pudding with apple and mashed potatoes.

Name: Brasserie Bruis
Description: At Bruis, located in the centre of Haarlem, Jozua Jaring of MICHELIN-starred Ratatouille gives the floor to the next generation of culinary talent. Out front, the pavement terrace is all set; inside, the lighting underscores the intimate character of this cosy establishment. The chefs invite you to compose your own set menu from an enticing selection of French-inspired dishes with a contemporary twist. Expect dishes such as pan-seared sea bass with pancetta and a delicately zesty antiboise sauce with fresh herbs. A fitting finale comes in the form of a Paris-Brest featuring silky buttercream, caramel ice cream; a sprinkling of coarse salt rounds off this generous dessert. Get ready to savour indulgent flavours in a relaxed setting.

Name: Brasserie Brunet
Address: 10 rue de la Poste, Annecy, 74000, France
Description: At this restaurant a stone's throw from the train station, you receive a warm welcome in a British-style decor with exposed stonework, wood panelling and moleskin-clad banquettes. "Brunet" pâté en croûte; black pudding with onions, apple and lamb's lettuce salad; calf's liver and spelt risotto – an avalanche of delicious dishes served in a relaxed atmosphere by a smiling team in black attire and leather aprons.

Name: Brasserie Le Gogant
Address: Route de France 8, Le Brassus, 1348, Switzerland
Description: Both the restaurant, and the Hôtel des Horlogers in which it is housed, are the epitome of sleek, cutting-edge cool. In addition to an elegant designer interior, guests can savour panoramic vistas of nature through huge picture windows. The seasonal lineup harmoniously blends classical and traditional flavours (succulent stocks and addictive sauces) and is crafted from primarily regional ingredients. An uncluttered decor provides the perfect foil to bold, modern plating and high-quality recipes. If you are dining in a party, don’t hesitate to order the dishes to share, but before that, it would be a crime to skip the delectable gruyere-flavoured malakoffs (fried cheese balls) – ideal with an aperitif. The entire team, from the slick front-of-house staff to the crack white-jacketed brigade, is polished and professional. The hotel offers top-of-the-line guestrooms in the same vein that enjoy a view over the forest of Risoud.

Name: Brasserie Le Jardin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The little sister of the Château les Crayères, housed in an outbuilding in the park, is a smart, very contemporary and elegant brasserie with its own veranda and terrace just opposite the herb garden. Flavoursome seasonal cooking.

Name: Brasserie Marie
Description: Marie possesses that charm typical of the South of France. The brasserie decor exudes luxury, but the terrace overlooking the boats and bridges is where everyone wants a table. This tranquil oasis in the heart of the city is enhanced by the Mediterranean finesse of the cuisine. The lamb fillet and cheeks with a perfectly balanced hollandaise sauce, the salt-baked sea bass, the generous beef tartare: these are down-to-earth dishes that pack a punch, and they are simply irresistible. This is what Bib Gourmand is all about!

Name: Brasserie N4
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This friendly family brasserie is not far from the busy N4 highway, but as soon as you see the rolling Ardennes countryside, your peace of mind is restored. The interior is steeped in the charm and nostalgia of the inns of yesteryear. Chef Frédéric Bolis finds his inspiration in purebred French classics, to which he is not averse to adding a generous modern spin. Perfectly poached egg in velvety mushroom soup with wild mushrooms and gutsy Ardennes cured ham: the quintessence of fine country fare, as is the case of the meat cooked in a Josper charcoal oven and the punchy sauces. You have here an irresistible mix of comfort food executed with razor-sharp precision.

Name: Brasserie Victória
Address: Avenida Presidente Juscelino Kubitschek 545, São Paulo, 04543-010, Brazil
Description: It is estimated that the Lebanese community and its descendants living in Brazil nowadays is greater than the current-day population of the Lebanon. The first immigrants arrived in the 1880s, consequently, many dishes of Arabian origin became typical Brazilian dishes, such as sfiha and kibe. This brasserie has been serving authentic Arabian cuisine for seven decades, transforming the Victoria into a gastronomic icon in the Greater São Paulo area. Founded by Dona Victória, it has been run by the same family for several generations. The menu offers a wide variety of mouthwatering options such as kaftas, sfihas (open, closed and folded), kibes, labneh and pitta bread. Make sure you save space for the incredible desserts here, such as the nut-filled atayef pancakes topped with a delicious lemon syrup.

Name: Breizh Café Cancale
Description: On the port of Cancale, Breizh Café has one motto: "A new take on crêpes." After all, the concept was originally born in Japan! The owner, Bertrand Larcher, was the first to export Brittany's galettes (buckwheat pancakes) to Tokyo, and several Japanese restaurants later, he has opened one back home. The produce is premium and organic (eggs, cheese, meat) and the crispy flavoursome galettes and wafer-thin, soft pancakes are made entirely traditionally. The filling depends on your fancy, ranging from classical to unusual: artichoke rolls, spider crab, Comté cheese and Saint Malo wakame seaweed. The glazed façade commands a fine view of Cancale harbour. Something of a local landmark, it is often fully booked.

Name: Breizh Café Megève
Description: In the heart of the village, on the pedestrian street next to the church where a large Christmas tree is erected in winter, this converted chalet is home to an authentic Breton eatery. Yvon Madec oysters are served alongside Breton pancakes – buckwheat galettes and wheat flour crêpes – enhanced with Japanese or Savoyard touches, for instance "Breizh Roll" with Reblochon cheese, or raw milk raclette galette. Locally sourced produce, cheese from a refiner in nearby Manigod and a fine selection of ciders and wines… plus wallet-friendly prices.

Name: Breizh Café Rennes
Address: 1 place de la Trinité, Rennes, 35000, France
Description: Why change a formula that works? Bertrand Larcher, the man who introduced the Breton crêpe to Japan, has set up shop in Rennes, a stone's throw from the city's Marché des Lices. The setting is a modern, industrial-style space with an open kitchen. The ingredients for success are still the same: high-quality produce that is predominantly organic (stone-ground wheat grown in Brittany, buckwheat flour milled in Vitré, organic eggs, artisanal Basque charcuterie from Pierre Oteiza). Alongside the classic galettes (buckwheat pancakes), there are more original iterations, some with a Japanese twist, such as the kinako crêpe with Okinawa black sugar and matcha ice cream. There is a short menu of nibbles and oysters.

Name: Briar
Address: Number One Bruton, Hotel, 1 High Street, Bruton, BA10 0AB, United Kingdom
Description: Nestled within a boutique hotel at the heart of this popular Somerset town, Briar occupies a space which was once an ironmonger's shop. It’s now the kind of restaurant that warms your heart, run with a genuine friendliness and enthusiasm that’s mirrored by the bright, fresh cooking that can’t help but put a smile on your face. Order three to four of the sharing plates per person and you’ll be treated to great value dishes that burst with flavour – like the chocolate marquis with cherries and buttermilk ice cream that will ensure your meal ends on a high.

Name: Brick Corner
Address: 151 Forbeswood Heights, Forbestown Road, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Exposed brick, bright colours and warm lighting make this a vibrant and inviting setting. The menu hones in on North Indian cuisine – rich, spiced and hearty fare. Ranging from traditional snacks to a variety of curries, dishes include butter chicken, dal makhani and the standout mutton bhuna masala, which is slow cooked to tender perfection. Don't miss the naan baked in a tandoor for a chewy texture and smoky aroma that complements the flavours beautifully.

Name: Bridge Street Prawn Noodle
Description: Come here for the famous prawn mee: choose between yellow and rice noodles, then pick the soup – the spicy prawn broth is loaded with deep flavours. Finally, consider ordering add-ons such as braised pork spareribs or fish balls.

Name: Briemm
Description: "Briemm" is a contraction of Brice and Emmanuelle, who have partnered up (in business and in life) to found this dinky eatery in a lovely stone-built house, which is depicted by generous cooking and a gracious welcome. The sensibly priced patriotic lineup stars a succulent list of dishes that reveals a genuine eye for detail and a fine bouquet of flavours, e.g. crunchy pig’s trotters, purée of granny smith apples and caramelised walnuts, or flame-licked mackerel flanked by watercress soup and squid ink-laced shortbread. What’s not to like?

Name: Brigade du Tigre
Description: The duo at the helm of Eels, both of whom trained with William Ledeuil and both of whom are passionate about Asia whose continent they’ve roamed, celebrate the joyful diversity of Asian cuisine in this their second establishment, a two-storey bistro-style affair. The result: delicious fragrant small plates, concocted from quality produce, such as this black sesame onigiri, filled with 14 month aged comté cheese and spinach, or the hoisin-glazed beef check with celeriac, grapefruit and medjool dates.

Name: Brigecio
Address: Avenida Constitución 28, Morales de Rey, 49693, Spain
Description: Impressively run by a friendly married couple, this restaurant located in a small village 10km to the northwest of Benavente takes its name from an ancient Asturian hill fort known as “Castro Brigecio”. Behind its façade, you’ll find a single, slightly impersonal contemporary-style dining room, albeit with a welcoming fireplace and excellent service. The extensive à la carte of traditional cuisine (on which you’ll also find the occasional more modern and contemporary recipe) is complemented by a selection of cod dishes (“bacalao a lo Tío” and “bacalao con crestas de gallo” (chicken comb) etc) and an impressive daily menu (except in summer). The famous Zamora-style octopus is a must!

Name: Briket' Bistrot
Description: On the heights of the village of Guéthary, the Ibarboure family hotel operates this pleasant bistro, independent from their fine dining restaurant. The chef meticulously adds an inspired new spin to traditional recipes in an uncluttered setting. Basque ingredients dominate the indulgent dishes of the concise menu: Bayonne ham, bellota chorizo, Banka trout, Ardi-Gasna cheese. A youthful, friendly team and sensible prices. Lovely terrace to the rear. A real treat.

Name: Bris'Art Culinaire
Description: There is space for just eight diners at the large counter laid out face to face with the kitchen, plus a few more tables to the rear. Every day, a single fish-forward set menu is improvised by chef Guillaume Brisard, who has forged an impressive culinary path (Fort de l'Océan in Le Croisic, Le Skipper in Saint-Nazaire). Fine ingredients inspire his dishes, which you can savour as you engage in conversation with the chef.

Name: Briscuits
Description: Few things go together as perfectly as biscuits and barbecue, and that’s the premise behind Christopher McGhee’s truck, located on the Radio Coffee lot. It’s popular but they have ordering down pat with a QR code and a call-ahead option that keeps things moving along. Good thing too, as you won’t want to wait for a bite of their melt-in-your-mouth brisket and flakey biscuit sandwich with a swoop of smoked strawberry jam thrown in for good measure. Or, try the pork belly with spiced apple pear preserves, a fried chicken biscuit, or even a simple egg sandwich biscuit sided by hash browns—it’s all good. To top it all off, beef sausage and wings, as well as sides like pimento cheese grits, round out their barbecue staples.

Name: Brisla Trattoria
Address: Strada Luigi Carlo Farini 41/a, Parma, 43121, Italy
Description: A contemporary trattoria where you can enjoy some of the region’s delicious specialities, all of which are faithfully reproduced with maybe just a hint of modern flavour – this is one of the most interesting restaurants in central Parma! We particularly enjoyed the bomba di riso (stuffed rice pie) with pigeon ragù, as well as the fresh pastas and the roast meat stuffed with roast potatoes.

Name: Bros' Trattoria
Address: SS172, zona G 61, Martina Franca, 74015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Sharing its entrance with the Relais Villa San Martino, the car park leads to a cluster of romantic trulli surrounded by a small vineyard. The kitchen is entrusted to the Pellegrino-Potì duo from the nearby gourmet restaurant, yet here it is tradition that holds sway: dishes rich in flavour, often cooked in the wood-fired oven, with a menu that changes frequently to follow the freshness of the season and the market. A straightforward and satisfying offering that honours ancient techniques and the produce of the territory within a setting of great rural charm.

Name: Brota
Address: Rua Conde de Irajá, 98, Rio de Janeiro, 22271-020, Brazil
Description: Brota occupies a charming mansion in Botafogo and is surrounded by a well-maintained garden. Inside, the elegant ambience features a contrast between striking red mouldings on the doors and large windows, a wood-inspired decor, an impressive bar, and leafy plants that add a touch of freshness to the setting. The kitchen is run by chef Roberta Ciasca from the renowned Miam Miam. The cuisine here is based around innovative vegan and vegetarian dishes designed for sharing. The menu includes classics such as the superb “brotinha” rice balls filled with tomato, pesto and olives or wasabi cream with chutney and the Thai curry served with basmati rice and sesame farofa.

Name: Brots
Description: A gastronomic surprise tucked away in this small village in the Priorat wine region, nestled between mountains and surrounded by vineyards. Here, in this tranquil setting, chef Pieter Truyts, who trained in Michelin-starred restaurants in his native Belgium as well as in France and Spain, discovered the perfect place in which to “cook from the heart”, developing creative and highly interesting cuisine that showcases the very best local and seasonal ingredients, with a gift for combining them to maximise their flavour. There’s a small à la carte featuring traditionally inspired dishes with a modern touch, as well as two tasting menus (Arrels and Brots). We particularly enjoyed the creamy flavour of the cep risotto.

Name: Brut Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Chef Janek Wojtalik and sommelier Maciek Łyko, who worked together at Kontakt in Warsaw, have brought their knack for full-flavoured cooking and passionately curated wine lists to Gdańsk. Their simply styled bistro has a proper neighbourhood feel, which is reflected in the generous pricing and friendly service. The menu blends a Polish heart with international influences, such as pork chop cooked over wood then served with ponzu and an Asian-style slaw. Smaller, natural producers are favoured in the interesting wine selection.

Name: Brutto
Address: 35-37 Greenhill Rents, Clerkenwell, London, EC1M 6BN, United Kingdom
Description: You can’t help but have a great time at this wonderfully relaxed trattoria. With its gingham tablecloths and walls filled with a jumble of pictures, it's rather like stepping into nonna's house for a couple of hours. The place is perennially packed and it's easy to see why, with a terrific atmosphere accompanying the hearty, meat-centric dishes that never skimp on flavour, whether it's the dough ball ‘cuddles’ or the pork and fennel sausages. The signature negroni is as terrifically well-priced as the food.

Name: Bruxaboschi
Address: Via Francesco Mignone 8, San Desiderio, 16133, Italy
Description: Anticipate a little time and patience tackling a winding progressively less urban road to reach, inland, San Desiderio, where Bruxaboschi has been delighting clients since 1862 under the same familial management. It will be worth it. Rightly renowned, the cuisine pays homage to local traditions (nearly exclusively meat), commencing with an excellent Genoese cima, picagge and pansotti among pastas, and fried rabbit. In season, obligingly, is the unmissable fungi engagement.

Name: Bua Thai Cafe
Address: Yas Bay - Yas Island - YS2, Abu Dhabi
Description: Hidden in a massive retail complex in the heart of Yas Island sits this cosy and colourful Thai café. Expect simple Thai lunches and an authentic menu adorned with the likes of steamed hagao, vibrant chicken green curry and, of course, the ever-so-loved mango sticky rice dessert. Take a seat on the terrace during cooler months, but be sure to book ahead, especially at weekends.
