Description: This exclusive, cosy establishment with only nine counter seats specialises in meat, seafood and veggies grilled over bincho and fruit tree charcoal. The chef earned his stripes in luxury hotels and prestigious kitchens in Beijing and Tianjin, before perfecting his craft in Japan and Yunnan. His signature maitake boasts nicely charred edges and a juicy centre, as potato espuma and shaved black truffle elevate the smoky edge and earthy umami.

Name: Emilia
Address: 2 East Street, Ashburton, TQ13 7AA, United Kingdom
Description: The northern Italian region of Emilia-Romagna provides the inspiration behind this classic osteria set within a former bank in the centre of town. The daily changing menu is chalked on the door of the old vault, which now houses the wines, and from the tiny kitchen comes forth flavoursome and generously priced dishes that you feel are doing you good. There’s a daily offal dish and the pasta is made in-house.

Name: Emmer & Rye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Since opening in 2015, Emmer & Rye has become one of Austin’s defining restaurants. The contemporary dining room remains lively, and the kitchen showcases seasonal ingredients sourced from local farmers, ranchers and foragers. The menu changes frequently based on availability, but certain themes remain constant: house-milled heirloom grains, handmade pastas, thoughtful fermentation and an unwavering commitment to Texas products. Dishes such as beef carpaccio with fermented shiitake and beef garum, or tortelloni filled with smoked ricotta, show the kitchen’s ability to combine rustic flavors with refined technique. An extensive beverage program, featuring both Texas producers and classic wine regions, rounds out the experience.

Name: Empire Empire
Address: 16 All Saints Road, Notting Hill, London, W11 1HH, United Kingdom
Description: From the people behind the Gunpowder restaurants comes this neighbourhood spot specialising in cuisines from across Punjab and Northwest India. Expect plenty of biryani and kebabs on a menu that’s so appealing, the hardest decision is choosing what not to order. If you're stuck, the butter chicken is a house speciality and you'd be a fool to overlook the terrific 'King Prawns Kadhai Masala' – a prime demonstration of the kitchen's skill with flavours. There is a loose disco theme and a cool vintage vibe, thanks largely to the fantastic jukebox and a photo booth.

Name: Eng Kee Noodle Shop
Address: GF, 32 High Street, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: This family-run shop is always jam-packed with hungry locals craving Cantonese noodle soup. No matter for dine-in or take-out, expect a reasonable wait. It prides itself on its signature beef brisket – braised one night ahead and steeped in a spiced marinade overnight for silky tenderness and deep flavours. Their oven-grilled char siu is made with pork shoulder and pork neck and has a juicy, springy texture thanks to the fine marbling.

Name: Engine Social Dining
Address: 72 Wharf Street, Sowerby Bridge, HX6 2AF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: While this friendly neighbourhood restaurant is housed in a traditional stone building, its interior is contrastingly modern, with closely-set, dark wood tables looking onto an open-plan kitchen with a wood-burning oven. The menu of well-priced sharing plates may have a Spanish heart – from the boquerones to the croquetas – but also offers the opportunity to go on a global culinary journey. Start in Mexico with the generously topped tacos, fly over to Vietnam for the bánh mì prawn toast, then end up back in Blighty for sticky toffee pudding. Whatever you choose, it will burst with colour and flavour.

Name: Enning Liu Fu Ji (Donghua East Road)
Address: 547 Donghua East Road, Yuexiu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: In the 1940s, the founder opened a shop on Enning Street that made noodles with duck eggs and flour only. Nowadays, his successors honour this heritage and make everything like in the olden days. In the signature shrimp wonton noodle soup, bite-sized wonton packed with springy shrimps come in a clear broth flavoured with dried plaice, dried shrimps and yellow chives. The blanched noodles tossed in lard, another must-try, are simple but addictive.

Name: Enomania
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Damiano Alberti opened this unfussy trattoria back in 2009 and it’s easy to see how it’s built up a loyal band of local followers over the years. Its name means ‘Wine Mania’ and it offers an impressive list of over 1,000 wines, mostly from Burgundy and Alberti’s native Piedmont, which you can sample via a tasting in the wine cellar. The weekly changing menu offers straightforward, satisfying dishes that respect Italian traditions, including the likes of 'risotto ai funghi con brasato di cinghiale' – a rich, flavourful offering comprising creamy mushroom risotto and braised wild boar.

Name: Enoteca
Address: rue de la Casquette 5, Liège, 4000, Belgium
Description: You cannot fail but feel at home at the Enoteca. Foodies have been flocking here for over thirty years, lured by the warm buzzy vibe, friendly service and text-book perfect Italian cucina. Al dente farfalle with confit lemon-spiked tomato sauce, briny grey shrimp and steamed leeks will give you an idea of the heartwarming lineup you can expect. The set menu always offers a choice between fish or meat in line with the establishment’s generous ethos. In addition to forthright, down-to-earth flavours, Enoteca also boasts an intriguing wine cellar that just begs to be tasted!

Name: Enoteca San Nicola
Address: Contrada di San Nicola 11/a, Bobbio, 29022, Italy
Description: In the historic heart of Bobbio, on the first floor of a former 17th-century convent, three intimate, well-appointed rooms welcome you with lively paintings and vintage objects. The menu is lean yet rich, offering four options for each course, blending tradition with playful flavors. The wine list is like a small encyclopedia, featuring a thousand labels from around the world, with vertical selections for connoisseurs. Don't miss the ricotta pearls with sun-dried tomatoes, black olives, and Parmesan.

Name: Enoteca Sociale
Address: 1288 Dundas St. W., Toronto, M6J 1X7, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This Roman-style restaurant is as inviting as they come, radiating comfort and anchored by a marble bar that welcomes solo diners like long- lost friends. From bread to charcuterie, practically everything is made in-house here, down to the fantastic pastas that make up the very heart of this menu. Comforting starters like golden-fried arancini stuffed with mozzarella di bufula or clever riffs like caprese sformato or tagliatelle with lamb, mint and peas reflect the many talents of this capable kitchen, which also offers a tasting menu.

Name: Entre Nous
Description: This restaurant is housed in a 16C building on a cobbled street in the town centre. The decor is chock-a-block with charming details: a large fireplace, stone window frames, exposed beams and colossal wooden branches from which the light fixtures hang. Your discreet hostess (who is also the pastry chef) and the chef, who can be seen fully focused and hard at work in the open kitchen, extend a smiling welcome to their guests. The seasons dictate the menu and the lunchtime lineup is a steal.

Name: Enxebre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The first thing that draws you to this restaurant, where the Galician name translates as something that is pure, authentic and genuine, is that it is run by a young couple, chefs Marcos Rodríguez and Patricia Uceda, the former from Vigo itself, the latter from Toledo. This modern space, laid out on two floors and boasting a semi-open-view kitchen, also has a bar counter where guests can dine while watching the chefs hard at work. The contemporary inspired à la carte showcases plenty of technical prowess through signature tapas such as the seasonal “cocido stew doughnut” and Enxebre’s own version of a cockle empanada, and is complemented by two tasting menus (Xenuíno and Xeitoso). Make sure you try the creamy cheesecake (which you can also order to take away).

Name: Epona
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Epona, Gallic goddess of travellers and abundance, watches over this welcoming restaurant conveniently located between Valence and Montélimar in the Ardèche. Rustic and warm, as the chef himself describes it, his cuisine is rooted in the local terroir. Complete with authentic jus and attractive plating, his dishes are testament to a deft touch – creamy courgette soup with Espelette chilli oil, or veal fillet served with seasonal vegetables. The lovely selection of local wines is mostly organic.

Name: Er Ba Jiu Su Mian Guan
Address: 289 Tianzhu Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Next to Fajing Temple, this tiny vegan joint is always packed with tourists and locals. The location certainly accounts for its popularity… large portion sizes and very affordable prices play their part too. Their signature noodle soup with assorted vegetables has a rich and sweet tomato broth, plus bamboo shoot, peas, fried gluten, wood ear mushroom and cashew nuts. Consider ordering the dumplings filled with dried tofu and potherb mustard to go with it.

Name: Erasmo
Description: Venetian chef Matteo Vianello chalked up experience in the kitchens of Alain Ducasse and Jean-François Piège. Now established nearer the sea, he has dedicated his small contemporary bistro to the island of Sant Erasmo (home of the famous purple artichoke). He has certainly not lost his touch, revisiting the classics in mouth-watering dishes that convincingly draw on Breton and Italian scores – for instance, ravioles of snails, sweet garlic stock, roast buckwheat or tiramisu.

Name: Erbgericht Tautewalde
Description: Inside, the modern dining rooms are done out in a pretty, rural style; outside, there is a lovely courtyard with a view of the kitchen. The seasonal cuisine is regional and international, and they are keen to use local produce. You can choose between the "Landidyll" set menu and "A la carte menu". And those who want to do without meat can look forward to a vegan set menu. Overnight accommodation in the traditional Erbgericht.

Name: Erge Shih Tang
Address: 145 Cinghai Road, Gushan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan Region
Description: The room isn’t particularly spacious, but it does exude a homely feel. Similarly, the menu features Taiwanese home-style cooking, that is lightly seasoned and in smaller portions. The signature grilled Pacific saury in honey sauce is braised until the bones are tender and edible, perfect with a bowl of steamed rice, pork lard rice, or braised pork rice. Or you can opt for steamed taro root cake with shiitake and dried shrimps as starch.

Name: Ernele
Description: At this restaurant, you can see the mindful idea in practice, not least in Felix Groß's cuisine. He cooks with a close eye on the seasons, and almost all ingredients are sourced from the immediate vicinity – within a 100km radius. The ibex ragout with pumpkin espuma and tarragon, for example, is very carefully prepared and really delicious. Be sure to save room for one of the desserts, such as salted caramel ice cream with blueberries and walnuts! Modern lines and a touch of rusticity are combined in the decor. The open kitchen and large shelves stacked with all kinds of products that are available to purchase draw the eye. This is the second restaurant within the hotel Das Schiff, alongside Wälder Stube 1840.

Name: Erst
Address: 9 Murray Street, Ancoats, Manchester, M4 6HS, United Kingdom
Description: With its open kitchen, sharing plates, faux-industrial design and bounty of natural wines, there's something incredibly current about Erst. It's truly a restaurant for our times, but cooking like this would be a joy in any era. The underlying themes across the menu are great value and bright, punchy flavours; make sure you start with one of the freshly charred flatbreads, which might come topped with sweet Vesuvio tomatoes. The cuttlefish risotto is terrific too, offering impressive depth of flavour. The friendly team provide natural, attentive service.

Name: Esmen
Address: 10 F. Rallos Street, Pasil, Cebu, Cebu, The Philippines
Description: For 60 years, this market-side eatery has been loved for one thing: linarang, a sour fish soup made with fresh porcupine fish simmered over wood fire. The broth is tangy, rich and slightly oily, with tender fish and deep flavour. Enjoy it on rice before noon when it's at its freshest.

Name: EssBar fein & pfiffig
Description: This inconspicuous-looking restaurant is a stone's throw from the Hofgarten public park. Chef Daniel Baur and Olga Jorich have plenty of regulars here, and with good reason. The fresh, flavoursome dishes are carefully crafted using quality ingredients and represent excellent value for money. The veal rissoles are well worth trying. Neither will you be disappointed by the wine list! Olga Jorich's friendly and thoughtful approach to running the service plays a key role in creating the inviting atmosphere. Charming sheltered terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Esszimmer
Description: With its sleek, modern interior done out in warm hues, and friendly, professional waitstaff, as well as the regional and seasonal cuisine, this restaurant housed in a fitness centre a little out of town is very inviting. It's all about sharing here; tapas-style dishes are placed in the middle of the table for everyone to dig into – mix and match vegetarian, meat and fish options as you see fit. Perhaps you will be tempted by arancini stuffed with burrata and mushrooms, or samosa with locally hunted venison, sweetcorn and mint lassi. Be sure to try the wonderful spelt flatbread with one of the delicious dips! In keeping with the dining concept, dessert comes in the form of sweet tapas, such as salted caramel crème brûlée.

Name: Esther's Kitchen
Address: 1131 S. Main St., Las Vegas, NV, 89104, USA
Description: Named for Chef James Trees' aunt, this Arts District hotspot boasts a convivial vibe, which is due in no small part to a large and welcoming U-shaped wood bar. There is an open kitchen, as well as a designated area where the sourdough bread, pizza and brass die-extruded pasta are produced. The look is rustic with wood plank flooring, dark walls hung with vintage silver trays and bold wallpaper accents. The menu is strongly Italian-influenced, and product focused. Farmers and suppliers are highlighted on the menu which features seasonally inspired fare in items such as salads, wood-grilled Calabrian pork sausage and red wine-braised beef cheek with polenta.

Name: Estime
Description: Tucked away in a narrow pedestrian street in the city centre, this pleasant, modern bistro sports a vibrant interior of white beams, whitewashed walls, mirrors, a stone and brick fireplace and period parquet floors. The chef deftly crafts a score in the zeitgeist depicted by razor-sharp precision and lashings of generosity. An example: red mullet with shrimps and grapefruit, or pressed beef. The set lunchtime menu is excellent value for money. A dining experience worthy of esteem.

Name: Estrellita
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It's a tiny space, but Owners Hope Webb and Walter Cortado have fashioned a likable space with a modern bent at Estrellita. Equally small but mighty is the kitchen, which turns out Filipino classics and meat-forward dishes. There are always specials to keep an eye out for, and patience is key, as the kitchen team is often handling to-go and catering orders simultaneously. It's walk-in only, so pull up a chair to enjoy roasted pork belly lechon cooked Cebu-style, with crispy skin and rolled with lemongrass, green onion and garlic. Vegetable and beef versions of lumpia are available; the beef delivers three crispy lumpia filled with Angus beef sautéed with green beans, bean sprouts, celery and onions for dish that is both unexpected and tender.

Name: Estrò
Description: A lively bistro with a youthful feel, set in the heart of the town centre and featuring a pleasant outdoor terrace overlooking the square. In the kitchen, chef-owner Della Croce presents a menu that strikes a pleasing balance between meat and fish, always guided by careful respect for the seasons. Among the dishes most appreciated by the Inspector is the excellent octopus alla marinara: expertly cooked in two stages and full of flavour, it is served with cherry tomatoes, garlic, olives and capers, bringing out the character of the ingredient with both simplicity and skill.

Name: Etchemaite
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Deep in the mountainous Basque Country scenery, this disarmingly simple establishment, the repository of a family history that goes back four generations, couldn’t be more authentic. At the helm, Ximun conjures up hearty, polished fare, depicted by lavish portions and well-crafted sauces. Think comfort food founded on premium local produce: confit pork cheeks, risotto of “orzo” pasta, emulsion of smoky bacon and a gutsy jus; “Aldabia” poultry breasts, macaroni gratin and Albufera sauce… Meals are served in the recently revamped interior which commands a knockout view of the Pyrenees!

Name: Etna
Description: On its website, this modern restaurant describes itself as “the home of different flavours from the Karst region”. The cuisine here is generous and exciting, with a focus on top-quality ingredients that the chef skilfully transforms into delicious dishes. The pizzas are excellent; the Burger Gourmet and Tuna Burger, served with home-made beetroot bread, are superb; and the exquisite desserts simply cannot be missed!

Name: Eton
Address: 1-2F, European Asian Bank Building, 749 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Fung Shing, once a household name in Mong Kok, was reincarnated as Eton, in a space that oozes nostalgic Chinese flair with its red carpet and dragon and phoenix relief art. The kitchen is run by mostly the same team, and the menu remains broadly similar. Expect Shun Tak classics such as sautéed mandarin fish roll with silky flesh, and angled loofah in a lightly seasoned glaze. Scrambled egg white with milk in Daliang style is also an excellent choice.

Name: Euang Kam Sai
Address: 185/3 Wua Lai Road, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: Eung Kham Sai has been run by the same family for over a century and is still serving up classic Northern Thai recipes handed down the generations. The modest space has traditional decor; large windows frame the view outside. Try the freshly made khao bai, rice wrapped around a pork, fish or beef filling, or the spicy Northern-style curry, made from scratch with local beef brisket and exuding fruity acidity. Some ingredients come from local farms.

Name: Everett's
Address: 22 High Street, Waterford, X91 Y983, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This proudly run, welcoming bistro is set in the heart of Ireland's oldest city and occupies a building dating back to the 15th century. The ground-floor room boasts a lovely barrel-fronted bar, while the vaulted brick cellar has an intimate feel. The modern, sensibly priced dishes come with a degree of complexity, but the biggest strength lies in the natural flavours of the fine Irish produce. Fresh, snow-white hake is a perfect example, delicious on its own but enhanced nevertheless by piquant salsa verde and top-quality mash.

Name: Eximio by Fernando Martín
Description: If you’re visiting Alcalá de Henares, the birthplace of the famous writer Miguel de Cervantes, make sure you dine at this restaurant located just a stone's throw from Alcalá’s 'Catedral Magistral' (the restaurant’s name, meaning “eminent” in English, is a nod to the “magistral” status of the cathedral). It is run by local-born chef Fernando Martín, who learnt his trade at Le Cordon Bleu and some of Spain’s leading restaurants such as at Martín Berasategui in Lasarte-Oria. His updated take on traditional cuisine is showcased on an à la carte, a good-value lunchtime menu (Monday to Friday), as well as on two more elaborate tasting-style menu that change with the seasons (Corto and Largo). In the chef’s own words, his aim is to 'ensure that every guest who walks through the door has a different gastronomic experience.'

Name: Existe
Description: Following its move from Mosqueruela, this restaurant now provides the culinary inspiration at the Mas de Cebrián hotel, along the road leading to Puertomingalvo. In essence, Existe continues to act as a culinary showcase for the so-called “Empty Spain”, in a setting that is both rustic and contemporary. The couple in charge (with María acting as sommelier in the dining room, and Alberto in the kitchen), offer a single tasting menu that showcases locally sourced ingredients from the province of Teruel, alongside constant nods to the region and its culinary roots. The chef particularly enjoys working with local game and wild mushrooms.

Name: Eylan
Address: 500 El Camino Real, Menlo Park, CA, 94025, USA
Description: Chef Srijith Gopinathan has struck gold once again with this swanky Menlo Park sensation, drawing in crowds with his inventive blend of regional Indian cuisine with a fresh Californian twist. To illustrate this singular approach, take a flaky, paratha-like flatbread filled with Dungeness crab and paired with a rich, complex sauce featuring fennel, poppy seeds, and mint. Wood-fired grills add an additional layer of interest, providing a robust char to the likes of lemon-grass scented gulf shrimp, chili-glazed celeriac and pineapple kebabs, and whole sea bream, as well as lending a subtle smoke to sauces. The compelling balance of flavors makes each dish stand on its own, but an assortment of carefully chosen wines and clever cocktails certainly doesn’t hurt matters.

Name: FAGN-Bistro
Description: There are several things this simple bistro shares with its more formal sister FAGN downstairs. The warmth of the welcome for one, as well as the use of the same top-quality produce. Where it differs is in its more laid-back atmosphere and the fact that the cooking has an unadulterated Norwegian base. A combination of glass and wood gives the room a bright but cosy feel, and a long wood counter provides views out over the city. Rustic, boldly flavoured dishes are generously proportioned, offering the likes of herring and potatoes with sour cream, browned butter, dill and red onion.

Name: FOB Kitchen
Description: Janice Dulce is behind this popular Filipino restaurant that began as a pop-up. Tucked into the Temescal neighborhood, the space may be diminutive but it is ingeniously designed—with whimsical wallpaper and a relaxed, island vibe. Cozy up to the bar while you wait—a situation made infinitely more bearable with a stirring cocktail in hand. The menu is loaded with keepers, but keep your options open for tantalizing specials, like sweet and sour sinigang with pork, eggplant and daikon; or Janice’s Ribs, slow-roasted with coffee, coconut beer and banana ketchup. Suman, a steamed rice cake in a banana leaf, is then served with coconut crumble, coconut sauce and mango for a none-too-sweet treat.Weekends are brunch only.

Name: FT · Bak Kut Teh (Yuexiu)
Address: Wonderful Life Mansion, 36-48 Wenming Road, Yuexiu, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: You can't miss the long queue at the door, but that doesn't put avid foodies off coming here. Available in both Singaporean and Malaysian styles, bak kut teh is simmered for three hours with pork ribs, garlic, white peppercorns and herbs until the meat falls off the bone. You will even find Thai and Vietnamese classics on the menu – the sautéed Chinese violet buds in Vietnamese fermented shrimp paste taste floral and pungent at the same time.

Name: FUME
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: The latest opening from the Siigur restaurant group sits within the bustling Rotermann Quarter. One of the hottest tickets in town, it’s a big, bold, blingy space complete with colourful furnishings and an open kitchen, at the heart of which is the Vulcano Gres Grill, where the dancing flames add not just flavour but also to the atmosphere. The extensive menu offers a good choice of Mediterranean-inspired dishes but, of course, it’s the meats and grills cooked over the fire that are the stars of the show. Lunch is good value, and the capable team cater as well for large groups as they do tables of two.

Name: Fa Sing Garden (Jinsui Road)
Address: 5F, Grand Mercure, 62 Jinsui Road, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Since 2018, Fa Sing Garden has been serving home-style Cantonese fare to hotel guests and other foodies. The brightly lit space boasts a tasteful decor, and there are a number of private rooms of various sizes. Along with signature dishes such as double-steamed chicken, lotus root starch pancakes, and soy-marinated chitterlings, the fried pork ribs in Worcestershire sauce are a must – the tangy sauce perfectly complements the tender, juicy meat.

Name: Fa. Pekelhaaring
Description: Welcome to the urban canteen of many Amsterdammers. Behind the façade of this corner building lies an eclectic and characterful interior full of art and a relaxed atmosphere. The cuisine has Italian flair, but cannot be pigeonholed. Think of it more as a creative mix with Dutch influences. Like the al dente tagliatelle with creamy venison stew, rich in flavour and beautifully balanced by the addition of gremolata. Or an entrecôte that has been given the full smoky flavour of the Big Green Egg, accompanied by Parmesan cheese and rocket. Fa. Pekelhaaring stands for simplicity with substance.

Name: Fable & Spirit
Address: 3441 Via Lido, Ste. A, Newport Beach, CA, 92663, USA
Description: With its elegant design and backdrop of the sparkling sea, this "fabled" spot doesn't have to try very hard to win fans. And yet, it never rests solely on its good looks. The room is packed with an unmistakable hum of happy diners diving into delicious pub grub. The comprehensive menu offers up a handful of delicious, inventive vegetable items such as the roasted cauliflower with green harissa, curry caramelized onions and almonds. You'll want to order everything, but don't skip the ambitious but well-executed 12-hour Kurobuta porchetta with polenta, romanesco, Calabrian chili, chimichurri, and textbook-perfect smoked braising jus. Dessert is worth a look, especially when brioche bread pudding with blueberry compote and crème anglaise is on offer.

Name: Fakin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Since its opening several years ago, this restaurant has helped revitalize the village of Legrad in northern Croatia. Located next to the church and overlooking the main square, it features a spacious outdoor area that comes alive on summer evenings. The simple yet elegant and modern interior perfectly reflects the spirit of the cuisine: Croatian and Central European dishes made with local ingredients, authentic and clean flavors, a good dose of creativity and technique, all at very reasonable prices. Be sure to try the Royal Blade, the house signature: a sumptuous grilled selection of noble cuts of local meat – chicken, beef, pork, and veal – served with potatoes, roasted peaches, and a tomato and chili sauce. The adjoining rooms are highly appreciated by cyclists: Legrad is, in fact, the starting and finishing point of one of Croatia’s most popular and renowned cycling routes.

Name: Familjen
Description: It might be situated in an elegant residential neighbourhood, but the name ‘Family’ gives a clue as to what to expect here: friendly, down-to-earth service; a bubbly, laid-back atmosphere; and prices that won’t break the bank. Enter via the wraparound terrace and you’ll find yourself in a simple room that feels something akin to a pub, where seating is arranged around a central bar; pull up a chair and get ready to enjoy the likes of confit duck leg with Hokkaido pumpkin and Gotland lentils. The appealing wine, beer and cocktail list adds to the experience, making it the perfect spot for meeting friends.

Name: Famous 4th Street Delicatessen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The Famous 4th Street Delicatessen, a Philly institution since 1923, sits on the corner of 4th and Bainbridge Streets in Queen Village. Long known for its towering corned beef and pastrami sandwiches, the menu is a treasure trove of beloved Jewish deli classics, starting with a lineup of hefty sandwiches like Reubens, roast beef and pastrami, each served with a choice of sides like potato salad, chips or a potato pancake. It also stretches into appetizers, salads, soups, cheesesteaks, traditional dinners, smoked fish and a full breakfast spread. Everything is made with a sense of pride; the meat is generously portioned, well-seasoned and tender, and the sandwiches are stacked with care.

Name: Fan Shui Chang Yu Mian (North Jiefang Road)
Address: 2-57 North Jiefang Road, Guangling, Yangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This neighbourhood noodle shop rose to fame after appearing on a TV show. Wild-caught rice paddy eel is the main event here. In the noodles in milky eel bone broth, "dry" noodles tossed in sauces, or fried noodles topped with sautéed eel in a peppery glaze, the umami is pronounced and the textures well layered. The milky broth, which takes six hours to make, is also a highlight. Sample different cuts of the deboned eel for different textures.

Name: Fana
Description: It is clear to see that chef Gabriel Gras Fernandez and pastry chef Jorice Sardain are passionate about food. In their compact restaurant on a pedestrian street in Montmartre, they work in tandem to create intelligent and flavourful seasonal cuisine. Their meticulously made dishes include roasted leek with cockle and walnut vinaigrette, or chicken with fennel and a reduced jus. And how could we forget their iconic Paris-Brest, an absolute must-try!

Name: Fang Lao Da (Shangcheng)
Address: 629 Jiangcheng Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Born into a family of chefs, the young owner started as an apprentice and worked his way up. Exacting about his noodles, he has them tailor-made to the required texture. All the Hangzhou-style noodle dishes are made to order, featuring various toppings and sauces. His original recipe, noodles tossed in scrambled egg with a tangy sweet tomato sauce, stands out from typical pork sauces. The shrimp, eel and tomato sauce version is equally good.

Name: Fang Po
Address: 50 Wangfu Street, Qinhuai, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
Description: Since the 1970s, the owner has been treating customers to iconic Nanjing-style small bites at this no-frills shop. Black rice balls, the favourite breakfast for many, comprise black sticky rice with bilberry leaves and stuffed with meat. End on a sweet note with baby taro in osmanthus sweet soup thickened by lotus root starch. Glutinous rice balls in red bean soup with wine lees, and peppery beef broth are also popular.

Name: Fang Xiang by Detan (Zhonglou)
Address: 2-3F, Detan Hotel, 1 Xiaohe Yan, Zhonglou, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Detan is a local F&B brand founded in 1908. It expanded into the hospitality sector in 2000s and the on-site restaurant naturally perpetuates the brand’s legacy, melding Jiangnan traditions and modern touches. The menu focuses on classic Changzhou recipes passed down for generations. Qianlong crab roe and crabmeat soup seduce with varied textures and deep umami. Red braised black carp tail in a sweet soy sauce boasts firm, flavoursome meat.

Name: Farang
Address: 72 Highbury Park, Highbury, London, N5 2XE, United Kingdom
Description: It’s easy to understand why Farang is so popular; it’s an immensely likeable restaurant serving generous and heartwarming recipes from all regions of Thailand – and even with overly eager ordering, you finish up with a bill that isn’t too overwhelming. Each dish, be it the salted turmeric prawns or the whole sea bass with raspberry nahm jim, showcases the hallmarks of Thai cuisine: freshness, vibrancy and a lovely balance of the sweet and the sour. The ‘Feasting’ menus are great for groups, and you’ll find it hard to resist buying some of their homemade produce on the way out too.

Name: Faraya
Description: The Harika family has morphed the Faraya into an elegant restaurant, whilst retaining its home from home vibe (songbirds included!). True to Lebanese tradition, the authentic dishes are piled high in the middle of the table to be shared by all the guests. Smooth hummus, labneh, mixed grills rich in spices and baklava dripping in honey… Don’t miss the buffet (Saturday evening and Sunday lunchtime).

Name: Farmer & Sons
Description: In an expanding neighbourhood on the outskirts of the city, this white-tiled bistro is the perfect place to taste modernised, lightened versions of traditional Polish dishes that have lost none of their punchy flavour. A few prime steaks sold by weight are ideal for celebrating, but the real value is to be found in the likes of the ‘szare klunchy’ (‘grey ducks’) dumplings topped with melting beef cheek, sauerkraut and a rich demi-glace sauce thickened with bone marrow. Polite, helpful service is an added bonus.

Name: Farmer's Apprentice
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: With a decade of history behind it, Farmer's Apprentice is a true neighborhood gem. This tiny space with rustic appeal minds the seasons and makes the most of local ingredients and heirloom varieties. Under Chef Alden Ong, the cooking is inspired, and the constantly evolving menu pulls inspiration from across the globe. Longstanding classics include the egg yolk potato rosti sando with pickled jalapenos as well as roasted cabbage prepared with a Kerala-inspired coconut curry. Heirloom corn sourdough bread is baked daily. Those looking for a big night out should consider the dinner-only tasting menu.

Name: Farmgate Lismore
Address: Main Street, Lismore, P51 NH95, Ireland
Description: In the centre of a lovely County Waterford town, this nicely converted former pub stands in the shadow of the mighty Lismore Castle. The sensibly priced menu comes with a prevailing ethos of fuss-free cooking and prime, locally sourced produce; look out for dishes with a certain comfort-food quality, such as liver and bacon, deep-fried calamari, or braised lamb shank. The knowledgeable service comes with such engaging charm that, combined with the terrific dishes, you’ll wish you could come here every week.

Name: Farouche
Description: A stone's throw from Montrouge town hall, this place is a breath of fresh air on the local restaurant scene. At the helm, Cécile Farnier and Hélia Maouch, both trained at the Ferrandi hospitality school, have devised a short – and constantly evolving – menu: shredded fish with potato espuma, fish with a tangy sauce vierge, refreshing seasonal desserts. Quality ingredients, on-point cuissons, service with a smile… It's no surprise it already has a following of regulars.

Name: Farragua
Description: In this unusual bistro-style restaurant just a few metres from the Plaza Mayor and the ever-busy marina, the self-proclaimed aim is to create “inquisitive and evolving” cuisine. What is certain is that Farragua’s updated take on traditional dishes features plenty of fusion influences and nods to Extremadura, the native region of chef Ricardo Fernández Señorán, who is particularly at ease working with locally sourced and seasonal ingredients which he uses to create his signature escabeches. His cooking is firmly focused on his tasting menus: Asina, Mangurrino and Dejalamío (everyone has a pairing option). The restaurant has also developed a concept entitled “Arrieros” (named after the men who, in the past, would transport food from one community to the next), as part of which invited chefs help to create four-hand menus.

Name: Fat Kee
Address: No.2, Path J, Mu Dan Cun, Yi Jing Hua Yuan, 2003 Yijing Road, Luohu, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
Description: Guests are greeted by foo dog statues and tropical greenery in a courtyard, before entering this spacious restaurant. The signature roast goose has just the right level of spice and boasts glistening, crackling skin and firm meat. You may want to coincide with the time these highly prized birds come fresh out of the oven, at 11:30am and 5:30pm daily. Fatty, sticky and with a delicately milky flavour, the char siu is nicely charred on the edges.

Name: Fauna
Address: México 3 Km. #73, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
Description: Is this dinner or a party? The answer is both. Inside the Bruma Wine resort, this backyard celebration features communal tables and a buzzy crowd that never lets up. The kitchen keeps pace, delivering an eclectic Mexican menu that covers land and sea. Brimming with confidence and bravado, the rustic cooking is scaled such that sharing is essential while still delivering clear, punchy flavors. Have you ever seen cabbage grilled so fiercely? Carrots, bone marrow and warm flour tortillas make for an unexpectedly thrilling combination. Scallops with eggplant puree are a meal on their own, as is the stack of smoked quail paired with chili aioli. Should you have room for dessert, swing for the warm churro with guava and dulce de leche ice cream.

Name: Favorites Thai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This vibrant Thai hot spot hides in plain sight along Ossington Avenue. A quick walk through a tiny coffee shop to the very back leads to the actual dining room, anchored by a small kitchen fitted with binchotan charcoal grills. Sunlight bathes the airy, narrow dining room. All the while, guests dig into electric, vibrant Thai cooking that makes the most out of fresh herbs and fiery chilis. You could fill up just on appetizers, like sticky rice spring rolls, fried chicken wings and beef tenderloin tartare enlivened with fish sauce and fried shallots. A particularly clever fried calamari salad demonstrates the creative talents of this kitchen. From green curries with fish to red curries with duck, the curated menu offers wide appeal for groups.

Name: Fei Fei Roasted • Noodle
Address: Yuhua Village Market and Food Centre, #01-28, Blk 254, Jurong East Street 24, 600254, Singapore
Description: Popular stall for roasted meat and dumplings. Duck leg with shrimp wonton noodles is recommended. Come early before the food runs out.

Name: Feilmeiers Landleben
Description: Now run by the third generation, this traditional inn has been in the Feilmeier family for years. According to Johann Feilmeier (who goes by Hans), his "country-style" cooking is both a labour of love for his native terroir and a commitment to his culinary heritage – this regionally and seasonally inspired food is full of flavour. Choose from the various set menus or order à la carte. Extremely charming and cordial service, plus savvy wine recommendations. With a trendy yet cosy decor made up of modern lines, quality fabrics, pleasant colours and warm wood, the space is also extremely inviting. Tip: Delicatessen items can be purchased.

Name: Feine Speiseschenke
Description: This friendly restaurant is located in a small village in a quiet side valley surrounded by woods and meadows. It offers seasonal cuisine bearing regional and international influences. They even raise Scottish Highland cattle here. You can choose from various set menus (including a vegetarian one) or go à la carte and opt for one of the classic dishes.

Name: Feldman's Deli
Address: 2005 E. 2700 S., Ste. D, Salt Lake City, UT, 84109, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Looking for a classic New York City-style deli in Salt Lake City? This family-owned and operated spot has just the thing. Founded in 2012 by Michael and Janet Feldman and now overseen by their son, John, this deli doles out appetite-busting, half-pound sandwiches served on Jewish rye (though other bread is available if you choose to go off script). There is a long list of signature sandwiches, but you'll never go wrong with a Reuben. You won't leave hungry, either, especially if you happen to snag a slice of their homemade cake, which often sells out.

Name: Fellin
Description: This brightly decorated café-cum-bistro sits within a red brick building on the edge of the Old Town and has something of a bohemian air, courtesy of a tiled bar, an eclectic mix of artwork and a laid-back vibe. Carefully prepared European dishes have a homely style and burst with freshness and flavour; you can have anything from coffee and cake or a lamb sandwich to a full meal, with the house pasta coming highly recommended. Add to this a charming service team and it’s easy to see why this is a place that’s loved by guests both young and old.

Name: Felsenbirne
Description: This restaurant with a friendly atmosphere and a sleek modern interior is located on a cobbled street in the pretty old town, not far from the Elbe. Chef-patron Felix Mikulla uses seasonal ingredients – his dishes are fresh and delicious, as well as good value. The menu also includes vegetarian and vegan options. In summer, diners can make the most of the terrace in the inner courtyard.

Name: Feng Chi Goose
Address: 170 Pingxi Road, Shalu District, Taichung, Taiwan Region
Description: Now run by the fourth generation, this family business has consistently served delicious goose dishes and provided warm and friendly service. Freshly slaughtered local geese are used – they are never chilled or frozen but prepared daily to ensure quality and a bouncy texture. The hindquarters are especially prized for their high fat content. Sides such as goose offal and marinated meat are also popular. Best accompanied by plain noodle soup.

Name: Fenyal
Address: Crystal Walk, Gewen Island, Doha, Qatar
Description: In a lovely modern building nestled among a discreet complex of towers on Gewan Island is this simple and colourful restaurant cum café. A local favourite, with a terrace, the spot immediately attracts you thanks to the lovely aromas of the bread oven. Simple, fresh dishes are served from breakfast to dinner; you can expect falafel, tasty juices, lamb kofta, and qahwa (Arabic coffee) served in a dallah set at great prices. The elbah – a baked custard with saffron – is a sweet way to wrap up any meal here.

Name: Ferme des 4 saisons
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Frank and Caty have refurbished this farm which is almost on the doorstop of the Trappist abbey that brews the legendary Chimay beer. Wholesome family favourites continue to dominate the menu of this welcoming farmstead. Examples include Bigorre black pig: cutlets in a gutsy BBQ sauce, fork-tender cheeks and croquettes of leg, flanked by a velvety potato mousseline and a big-boned pork gravy. As well as championing premium produce like sole and calf’s sweetbread, the chef manages to keep his prices sensible. An enticing mix of authenticity and generosity depicts this country inn.

Name: Fezi
Description: A buzzy casual vibe and a bargain-priced lunch menu set the scene in this neighbourhood hangout. Fezi means "home-made" in Brittany's Gallo lingo. Cédric Bruneau crafts tasty, straightforward, market-fresh cuisine, with a soft spot for local ingredients. The resulting legible score unveils a genuine flair for savvy, mouthwatering combinations. Natural and biodynamic wines set the scene on the beverage side, alongside a number of alcohol-free options.

Name: Fi Glbak
Address: 3058 Prince Turki Bin Abdulaziz Al Awal Rd, Al Mohammadiyyah, Riyadh, 12362, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
Description: This is Chef Hisham Baeshen’s first restaurant. The cooking is inspired by five Saudi regions and sprinkled with some dishes from various Middle Eastern countries. The eatery, whose name translates as ‘in your heart’, is set in a large open room with an eye-catching tree trunk suspended from the ceiling. Be sure to come in a big group as portions are perfect for sharing. Recommendations include their samosas, seabream in molasses stew and the sharqawi rice topped with caramelised onions. Finish off the meal with the queen of Arabic desserts, the kunafah.

Name: Fiata
Address: GF, 2 Staunton Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: The divine smell of freshly baked pizza lingers in the air, as the chef – hailing from Southern Italy – devises his short menu of expertly crafted Neapolitan pizzas plus a handful of starters. Made to order using Italian DOP ingredients, his pizza boasts a light, chewy crust, gooey centre and perfectly charred edges. His proud creation of provola e pepe pizza features smoky, creamy mozzarella, juicy tomatoes and a sharp peppery kick.

Name: Fico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This white house styled after a masseria in Puglia is sited by the seaside within East Coast Park. The sprawling lawn, spectacular ocean views and sound of the waves all exude a soothing vibe. The chef is keen to bring authentic Pugliese cuisine to Singapore, with focaccina and pasta made from scratch as the highlights. Try his San Marzano tomato focaccina with mozzarella and fresh basil, bursting with intense flavours.

Name: Fidelis
Description: In the heart of Saint Malo, a professional couple whips up wholesome traditional cuisine crafted sincerely and at sensible prices: tacos of spider crab; scallops, parsley butter and Jerusalem artichoke; rice pudding, grapefruit and pistachios. A pleasant location, a cheerful bistro spirit and invariably packed to the seams!

Name: Filigrana
Address: Av. Veracruz 62, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: This colorful, sun-soaked address from Chef Martha Ortiz has looks and substance in spades. At the base of a residential building in Roma, find a concrete jungle with purple-cushioned chairs, soaring floor-to-ceiling windows, and fully grown trees woven throughout. And much like the space itself, the cooking is equally stylish with thoughtful, playful interpretations of familiar favorites. Start with the gordita, a delicate, crispy disc packed with tender, shredded tongue and garnished with fried epazote leaves. Is there a prettier tamal around? This one is presented as a toasted cube made with fried portobellos and set in a warm guajillo chili sauce. Another highlight is the pozole brujo, featuring superbly tender chicken and a soulful, spicy broth.

Name: Finca Alfoliz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant with a strong focus on sustainability is a dream come true for chef Xanty Elías. Located on a family estate surrounded by fields of crops and protected areas, Finca Alfoliz enables its guests to enjoy its stunning natural surroundings to the full. On the à la carte and Compartir Clásicos tasting menu, enjoy a modern take on traditional cuisine including a complete emphasis on seasonal organic products, although you’ll also find delicious rice dishes cooked in clay pots, grilled meats (including a choice of mature cuts), and fish from the local estuary. We can particularly recommend the intense hock of wild boar which is slow cooked for 18 hours and carved in front of you. An interesting brunch is also available at weekends.

Name: Fino Seppeltsfield
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Housed within the light-filled, heritage-listed former bottling hall of the estate winery, this restaurant effortlessly embodies the convivial charm of a leisurely Barossa lunch. Warm hospitality sets the tone, while the kitchen champions a thoughtfully concise sharing menu built around exceptional regional produce. The vast majority sourced from small-scale farmers and producers located in the surrounding countryside. To start, don't miss the blue swimmer crab with jalapeño and brioche, or the pristine Gazander oysters, freshly shucked and served with a squeeze of lemon! Dishes like impeccably fresh King George whiting arrive with crisp asparagus and a savoury bagna càuda, while wood-fired Abelsway chicken is expertly cooked, complemented by vibrant chimichurri and earthy parsnip.

Name: Fiorella
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: If you’re staying away from carbs, then you best steer clear of this restaurant too. But for everyone else, this tiny but mighty kitchen in South Philly is impossible to resist. Once a butcher shop that spanned three generations, the restaurant under Marc Vetri delivers a tight menu of handmade pastas. Think pitch-perfect cacio e pepe with tonnarelli or cloud-like orbs of ricotta gnocchi bathed in brown butter. Do you have room for mezzelune stuffed with sweetbreads and veal? Of course you do. End with a simple and satisfying scoop of ice cream.

Name: Fire And Slice
Address: 7 Wakefield Avenue, Sumner, Christchurch, 8081, New Zealand
Description: This simple shop in the seaside suburb about 30 minutes from the city centre is serious about pizza. Much time and effort go into making the dough with the freshest ingredients, mostly from Canterbury. Their hand-stretched, thin-crusted pizzas are made to order and baked to perfection in a wood-fired oven, boasting crispy, nicely browned edges and a satisfying chew. A wide selection of toppings is available, including many vegetarian options.

Name: Fischerstube
Description: Packed with flavour, craftsmanship and carefully selected ingredients, the menu at this long-established establishment is sure to impress. The man who makes it all happen is chef-owner Alain Koenig. Fish takes centre stage, but by no means will meat lovers and vegetarians be disappointed. Dishes such as "char, morels, potato and wild garlic purée" or "duck breast, rhubarb, honey, brioche dumplings" are particularly appetising examples. You can dine à la carte or opt for one of two set menus: "Menu Dégustation" and "Menu Terroir". The excellent wine list has a penchant for Switzerland, France and Italy. With its classic ambience of dark green panelling, wooden floorboards and elegant table settings, the interior is inviting. Service is attentive and friendly. Tip: For private dining or events, book the historical vaulted cellar.

Name: Fish Shop
Address: 3 Netherley Place, Ballater, AB35 5QE, United Kingdom
Description: From the genuine, professional service to the array of quality seafood, there is a lot to love about this smart restaurant decorated with a wicker shoal hanging from the ceiling and photos of fishermen on the walls. Fabulous produce, much of it Scottish, powers dishes that accentuate the flavours of their core ingredient with a few well-judged, finely made accompaniments – such as Shetland halibut accompanied by slow roasted tomatoes and salsa verde. As always with the best seafood restaurants, keep an eye on the specials board for more fresh delights.

Name: Fishmonger
Address: 674 N. Highland Ave. NE, Ste. A, Atlanta, GA, 30306, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: It's part fish market, part casual spot here, where a single communal table and stools lined up at the windows await guests. Order at the back counter from a compact, seafood-focused menu listing oysters, crudos, sandwiches and soups. This is not your typical fried fish shack, though, and many of the dishes have a Southern slant to them. Peel and eat shrimp is a good standby, while tuna melts are leveled up. Specials driven by the daily catch are always a good bet, but the house staple—the blackened grouper sandwich—is a winner. A thick piece of generously spiced, blackened grouper is draped over a buttered, toasted seeded bun with Florida sauce, pickled peppers, ripe tomato and lettuce for something far from fussy but totally spot on. Gumbo is flavorful and hearty.

Name: Fisholic (North Point)
Address: Shop 14, GF, Victor Court, 14-28 Wang On Road, North Point, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Famous for snacks and noodles made with fish, this stall sells playful items like deep-fried minced fish in the guise of French fries, or fish skin nachos. Fishotto, where minced fish is shaped like rice grains, is also good.

Name: Fitó
Address: Rua Cardeal Arcoverde 2773, São Paulo, 05407-004, Brazil
Description: It’s not by chance that this restaurant occupies a charming, whitewashed property with blue windows – an external decor that is reminiscent of houses in inland areas of northeast Brazil, a part of the country that provides the inspiration for the cooking here. Under the baton of chef Cafira Foz, the exclusively female team creates cuisine that combines traditional flavours with an international touch. On the menu, there are options such as the authentic “paçoca” (shredded sun-dried beef served with “baião de dois” and plantains), a simple dish yet one full of strong flavours. For dessert, the “pirangi” (whole cashews with apple jam and “requeijão de corte” cheese), showcases genuine Brazilian flavours that will certainly leave their mark. Why not round off the experience with one of Fitó’s innovative cocktails prepared by the skilful and talented hand of bar manager Renata Adoración?

Name: Floh
Description: Tapping into the region is the name of the game here. In the cosy setting of a traditional country inn, diners are served flavoursome dishes that celebrate local ingredients. Top-quality produce is prepared without fuss – the emphasis lies squarely on taste. There is a wide selection of vegetarian, meat and fish dishes, as well as the classics of this type of establishment. Highlights include salmon trout – pan-fried with white carrots and gnocchi, and Grammelknödel – a potato dumpling stuffed with cracklings and chilli, served with summer cabbage, Red Amposta onion and courgette. Choosing a wine is no mean feat either – the list boasts more than 2 800 labels! There is a separate menu for Veltliners, white wines, red wines, international wines and magnum bottles.

Name: Flora
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Do you fancy enjoying regional flavours prepared creatively in Viseu’s historic centre? Restaurant Flora is the ideal destination! Chef João Guedes, passionate about nature (hence the name of the house), presents an offer that captures the changing seasons, providing bold flavours and presentations brimming with originality. The offer is divided into three surprise tasting menus of 5, 7 and 9 courses that underline the quality of the product and can be enjoyed alongside a “selection of minimal-intervention, organic and biodynamic wines”. The minimalist, contemporary-bistro setting seats only fourteen people, so booking ahead is advisable!

Name: Flora's Field Kitchen
Address: Flora Farms, Ánimas Bajas, San José del Cabo, 23407, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally opened by Gloria and Patrick Greene as an organic farm, this ever-so-charming spot has evolved since the late 90s and now features a wine and coffee bar, as well as shops set among the mango trees and this restaurant. It's family run and all heart—they grow their own produce, raise chickens, have an onsite butcher program, and bake all the breads, too. The tempting menu features offerings such as Neapolitan flatbreads, salads, and lighter starters like a flavorful gazpacho. From there choose one of their sandwiches, or an entrée like the pork chop with crispy potatoes. Portion sizes are generous but save room for their sweet treats baked onsite, and house-made ice creams and sorbets.

Name: FnB
Address: 7125 E. 5th Ave., Ste. 31, Scottsdale, AZ, 85251, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: FnB is Chef/owner Charleen Badman's long-running flagship in Scottsdale's Craftsman Court. This is cooking rooted in Arizona's soil, transforming what local farmers deliver into vegetable-focused dishes that are comforting and intentional. Equally defining is the wine culture shaped by co-owner and beverage director Pavle Milic, whose early all-Arizona wine program helped legitimize the state’s winemakers long before it was fashionable. Dishes like grilled sweet potatoes drizzled with a thick mustard vinaigrette or a wedge of grilled cabbage glossed with a tomato-pomegranate glaze and artichoke provide a harmony of textures and flavors. Desserts, like a pecan tart piled high with whole nuts and caramel, lean wonderfully nostalgic.

Name: Folga
Description: Located in the trendy Plac Nowy square in the city’s historic Jewish Quarter of Kazimierz, this busy and buoyant restaurant adopts a chic brasserie-style aesthetic with high-top tables and a terrace that’s ideal for the summertime. The menu showcases appealing variety, with the globally influenced dishes ranging from oysters to arancini and tempura to ceviche. Whatever you choose, there’s a unifying theme of sensible pricing and quality execution from the kitchen team.

Name: Foong Lian
Address: 55 Jalan Yew, Pudu, Kuala Lumpur, 55100, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed
Description: A firm favourite with the locals, Foong Lian has been feeding hungry diners claypot rice cooked over charcoal since 1986. The experienced chef uses two kinds of rice and controls the heat meticulously so that every pot is perfect. Try the preserved meat option with pork and liver sausage that perfume the rice with flavourful grease or top up with chicken leg and salted fish. Soups and snacks like tofu skin roll are also recommended.

Name: Forentum
Description: In the heart of the historic center, this charming restaurant welcomes guests between a cool outdoor terrace and an evocative dining room created in a natural cave. The cuisine celebrates local traditions, with occasional forays into seafood. In the evening, the offering also includes pizzas, made with three different doughs: the classic Neapolitan, the thin and crispy “Papà Luigi”, and the one with vegetable charcoal. Surrounding the restaurant, simply furnished yet well-maintained guest rooms in the style of a scattered hotel complete the experience.

Name: Foresta
Address: Strada de la Comunità de Fiem 42, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: Situated in front of a dense fir wood, this restaurant comes as something of a surprise. The dishes are prepared with genuine local ingredients, resulting in food that is full of flavour. Don’t get up from the table without having tasted the pappardelle pasta with mushrooms and speck ham or the fillet of venison with a redcurrant sauce.

Name: Forma
Description: Not by the sea, but at the foot of a medieval quarter, the dining room is an elegant blend of old and new; you can’t go wrong with the cuisine: Gianluca Formichella is a truly talented chef who puts a modern spin on Italian classics with creative touches. The ingredients are at the heart of the dining experience, in both meat and fish dishes. Among the best are those cooked on the barbecue.

Name: Forst's Landhaus
Description: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is located by a small stream – tables on the terrace overlooking the water are in great demand! The seasonal menu uses plenty of regional produce, such as lamb from the Bavarian Jura. The vegetarian dishes are also appealing, imaginative and delicious! The friendly maître d' provides good service with a personal touch. There are simple but well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Forêt
Address: 8/9 Sussex Terrace, Ranelagh, Dublin City, D04 KN82, Ireland
Description: When you browse a menu and see words like ‘pâté’, ‘rillettes’, ‘vin jaune’ and ‘au poivre’, you know you’re in for a thoroughly French treat. The surprise at Forêt is that these Francophone delights are found above the M. O’Brien’s pub – which couldn’t sound more Irish if it tried. Nevertheless, thanks to the team behind Forest Avenue next door, here you have a delicious slice of France, with every authentic dish combining top-quality produce and skilled execution to flavour-packed effect. The tomato tart with piperade is a prime example, simply bursting with umami.

Name: Fossil
Address: Kellergasse 6K, Purbach am Neusiedler See, 7083, Austria
Description: The name "Fossil" was not simply plucked out of thin air: This restaurant is actually located in a Muschelkalk limestone wine cellar dating back to 1870. At the entrance on the historical Kellerplatz, you are greeted by a plant-filled Mediterranean-style terrace. Then take just a few steps down, walk past the open kitchen and into the bright and imposing barrel vault, which makes for an enchanting setting. Chef-patron Thomas Daniel Pugel has been cooking here since 2015. Between noon and 9pm, he serves up regional and seasonal cuisine that is rooted in Austrian tradition yet incorporates modern influences – wild pike-perch fillet with fermented beetroot, Jerusalem artichoke and gnocchi, or Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) served with a potato and lamb's lettuce salad. Choose à la carte or the set menu of four or six courses.

Name: Fossé Saint Ange
Description: Johann (front of house) and Collis (chef) spoil their diners rotten in this vibrant bistro established in a picturesque 17C village built by Cardinal Richelieu. The focus is on good food and good cheer. The chef keeps things simple with a regularly changing menu of wholesome patriotic fare that is firmly rooted in the seasons, albeit spiced up with the odd exotic note. The creative desserts are in a similar vein. Even better, the owner, a former opera singer, is known to burst into song on occasion…

Name: Fotografiska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Above the Fotografiska photo gallery sits an equally striking restaurant offering picture-perfect views out across the Old Town; be sure to make the most of this by either starting or ending your night with cocktails in the rooftop bar. A ‘leaf-to-root, nose-to-tail’ ethos leads the way, with each ingredient used to the maximum – be that in the dishes themselves or as a garnish in one of the drinks – and the highly original cooking could include the likes of rabbit agnolotti or apple pie with chanterelle ice cream. On summer Sundays they offer a themed brunch.

Name: Fox & The Knife
Description: The roots of Chef Karen Akunowicz’s pasta empire trace back to this welcoming restaurant in South Boston, where she draws inspiration from her time in Italy. Everyone from parents in for a quick meal with their kids to younger couples just getting their evening started take to the lively space fit with a long bar up front and banquettes further back. Meals must begin with warm pieces of focaccia stuffed with taleggio or, for something a bit lighter, gnocco fritto with mortadella. Broccoli Caesar is a classic starter too. Pasta, as expected, is the main attraction. The likes of raviolo carbonara with guanciale, tagliatelle Bolognese with wild boar, and braised beef agnolotti del plin with roasted carrot butter are enormously satisfying.

Name: Foxy Nişantaşı
Address: Harbiye, Mim Kemal Öke Caddesi No:1/D, Şişli, Istanbul, 34365, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Foxy takes its name from the musky flavour of the Concord grape, though it also suits the casual, playful spirit of this spot – where you might notice the house cat wandering around. Indeed, at Foxy, chef Maksut Aşkar of the MICHELIN-starred Neolokal, and wine specialist Levon Bağış have appointed a team that understands their philosophy. Sample wonderful Turkish wines – from natural wines to classic appellations – and savour a fresh, modern and sophisticated take on traditional local cuisine. For instance, cured tuna fillet, lightly salted and served raw, is accompanied by julienned red onion, pickled spring onion and beetroot, creating a powerful contrast. Keep in mind that the menu is more extensive in the evening than at lunchtime.

Name: Fracia
Description: After leaving your car in the car park and walking up a short slope through the terraced vineyards, you reach this charming restaurant, housed in an old stone building once used for wine-growing. The rooms retain the charm of old Valtellina, with a pleasantly rustic and romantic atmosphere, while in the warmer months the arbour offers a splendid view over the valley. The cuisine draws on local traditions to create a menu that combines classic recipes with contemporary interpretations: there is no shortage of bresaola, pizzoccheri and meat dishes, alongside more creative dishes that follow the rhythm of the seasons. The wine cellar is particularly interesting, showcasing the finest wines of Valtellina, with a selection of wines from the historic Nino Negri winery, which owns the vineyards of the same name, among which the restaurant is situated.

Name: Fragrant Kitchen (Chaoyang)
Address: 3F, Building 2A, Courtyard 16, Nanmofang Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The veteran chef-owner devises a menu of traditional home-style Shandong fare that showcases classic techniques – oil-blanching, quick-frying in soy-based sauces, flambéing… Start with pear soup or eight-treasure tea, followed by braised pork belly casserole – a stew that boasts deep umami. Do as the locals do and wrap the pork in fluffy shaobing. Sautéed free-range chicken, and sea cucumber braised with spring onion (pre-order only) are also great choices.

Name: Frances Vinbar
Description: One of three eateries housed in the former US Embassy building, this ground-floor spot occupies a space previously used for the rather less exciting purpose of issuing visas. It’s now been transformed into a café, wine bar and restaurant, serving a selection of Middle Eastern and Mediterranean-inspired sharing plates. The generous dishes catch the eye with their vibrant appearance, then satisfy the palate with their fabulous flavours; confit cauliflower with the colourful trio of tomato coulis, cashew cream and coriander oil is a prime example.

Name: Francesca
Description: Chef Lukas Botta champions Wanaka-style Italian cuisine rooted in tradition, but reinterpreted with super-fresh local produce. Handmade pasta is a definite highlight, especially the gnocchi with braised beef cheeks starring soft, chewy dumplings and fork-tender beef. Wood-fired, thin-crust Margherita pizza is another classic. The cosy room feels warm and vibrant, and the covered terrace is relaxing whatever the weather.

Name: Franklin Barbecue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This iconic barbecue oasis in the heart of Austin needs no introduction, even further evidenced by the lines snaking out the door. Inside is simple at best, with a corrugated metal ceiling and cement floors, but it's the board above the counter that has everyone's attention anyway. Pork ribs, sausage, turkey, and pulled pork, along with a handful of sandwiches and classic sides (think cole slaw salad and pinto beans) are what's on offer, but you won't ever go wrong with the brisket. Sliced to order, it's wrapped in butcher paper and weighed before being placed on the famous blue tray. Tender and smoky with flavorful marbling and a dark char, it's worth the hours-long wait. Pair it with a cold local beer and it's the perfect duo.

Name: Fratelli Bruzzone
Description: Great credit is due to the Bruzzone brothers, who have transformed the very premises where they once operated as a simple delicatessen into an authentic temple of Piedmontese cooking. Today, across two small dining rooms of homey character – where a reservation is indispensable, even at lunch – a sequence of dishes takes shape that pays homage to tradition with rigour and passion. The offering is a celebration of timeless flavours: acciughe al verde, onion with vermouth and Blu del Moncenisio fonduta, agnolotti of impeccable pastry, rabbit al civet, guinea fowl, through to the classic desserts such as bonet and vanilla panna cotta. Course after course, the cooking wins one over through its forthright honesty and depth, making departure a reluctant affair: this is one of those places from which one rises from the table already longing to return.

Name: Fred's Meat & Bread
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Krog Street Market, what this contemporary space lacks in size it makes up for in charm. The concept is straightforward: sandwiches of all varieties from burgers and oyster po'boys to bahn mi and cheesesteaks. Each one is messy-delicious and over the top in the best possible way, as in the pimento cheese club with house-made pimento cheese, roasted poblanos, fried green tomatoes and bacon sandwiched between bread and seared. Meanwhile, the Italian grinder with all the meats, melty provolone cheese, garlic aioli and cherry pepper relish knocks it out of the park. Of course, there must be fries, and the barbecue version, with barbecue seasoning and a white barbecue sauce for dipping, won't disappoint.

Name: Freigeist
Description: This place may have a resolutely relaxed atmosphere, but in no way does that detract from the high degree of professionalism in both the service, courtesy of friendly owner Bernd Mossmann, and Paul Hunger's cuisine. The chef turns out fuss-free dishes made using top-notch, mostly organic regional produce – the full-bodied beef broth with root vegetables is a delicious way to kick off your meal. The interesting decor featuring unique decorative elements makes for a charming vintage feel. When the weather is nice, head for the inviting terrace. A somewhat simpler, pared-back menu is served at lunchtime.

Name: Freilager La Trattoria
Description: A charming and lively trattoria that, along with La Cucina Colaianni, forms the exciting Freilager dual concept in the Albisrieden neighbourhood. With Marco Però and his team providing warm and attentive service, Antonio Colaianni whips up flavoursome Italian classics in the kitchen – from vitello tonnato and paccheri con gamberoni to filetto di branzino and the "Tiramisu Freilager", which is prepared at your table. The good range of pizzas is also worth mentioning. At lunchtime, the options are more limited but include the wallet-friendly three-course "Menu D'Affari", as well as daily specials and items from the evening menu. In fine weather, you can eaton the terrace. Tip for motorists: the adjacent multi-storey car park (entrance at Flurstrasse 116).

Name: French Kiss
Description: This bustling brasserie in Jette has been renowned for its warm welcome and first-class grilled repertory since 1988. By the the grill, the owner masterfully supervises the spot-on cooking of all types of meat. An example: rare hanger steak with a subtle shallot sauce and of course piping hot fresh fries. The enticing menu naturally stars a lineup of patriotic Belgian classics ranging from shrimp fritters to authentic Brussels waffles. A friendly vibe, generous helpings and a glass of wine in good company – hard to beat!

Name: Frisone
Description: Frisone’s change of location, albeit just a few metres from its original incarnation, has resulted in significant improvements, including a new brighter look created by its large windows, high ceilings, elegant chandeliers and a minimalist-contemporary decor dominated by a variety of white tones. Its local clientele is already familiar with the cuisine created by the Rivas brothers, who continue to focus on updated traditional cooking with a contemporary Mediterranean flavour that maximises the use of locally sourced products. Rice and seafood continue to fly the culinary flag here!

Name: Fromażeria
Description: As the name suggests, cheese lovers will be in heaven at this welcoming, rather unique dining spot. To one side is a smart, bustling little bistro; to the other is a cheese bar with an admirable display of global varieties. Heartily flavoured dishes provide great value for money and usually incorporate cheese in some form, such as parmesan grated onto the excellent beef tartare. Whatever you order, follow it, naturally, with a cheese course. If you’re just after a quick snack, pop in for a seasonal cheeseboard with alcohol pairings.

Name: Frontera Grill
Address: 445 N. Clark St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
Description: This linchpin in Rick Bayless’ empire is decidedly unique in its homage to regional Mexican cuisine and displays a cult-like devotion to local product. From the table-shaken margaritas and the molés to the warm, uplifting music, you'll likely feel you're in Mexico. The menu is ever-changing but begin with the classic Frontera ceviche, a vibrant and refreshing blend of Pacific albacore, lime, tomato, olive and cilantro. Don't miss the specialties, highlighting the flavors of Guerrero on the Pacific Coast, along with sides like roasted cauliflower with poblano crema and melted cheese. Do save room for the chocolate pecan pie.

Name: Frontier
Address: 2400 Central Ave. SE, Albuquerque, NM, 87106, USA
Description: Located across the street from the University of New Mexico, this longstanding, family-owned restaurant has always been a favorite of students looking for a comforting meal at a great price but it's not just a hotspot for hungry students. Everyone flocks here from 5 am to midnight for items like their endless coffee, burritos on house-made tortillas and cinnamon rolls, heated to order and slathered with rich and creamy frosting. The breakfast burrito, filled with hash browns, scrambled eggs and a choice of one of their featured proteins like carne adovada or their flavorful green chili stew is another fan favorite.

Name: Froschgrundsee
Description: This appealing country house lies above a small lake, in the town's Schönstädt neighbourhood. Hannes Scammell shows his culinary mettle, cooking up fresh and tasty seasonal dishes. In addition to the appetising à la carte menu, there is a four-course set menu (the "Genuss-Menü") in the evening. The outside tables are perfect for al fresco meals. The good food is complemented by friendly service courtesy of the owner. If you love a barbecue, look out for their regular evening "Smoker Events" dedicated to grilled meats.

Name: Fu Din Wang (Central)
Address: 560, Section 1, Taiwan Boulevard, Central District, Taichung, 400, Taiwan Region
Description: Diners flock to this semi-self-service shop for pork trotter, hock and leg – braised in a soy-based marinade for up to four hours, the meat is gelatinous, tender and flavourful. It tastes even better with the house-made chilli sauce, cleaner and less complex than with the typical marinade and its strong herbal undertones. The braised diced pork rice and braised fried tofu are also good options. The simple decor makes for a relaxed vibe.

Name: Fu Ding Zheng Zong Bian Rou (Jianxin Road)
Address: 1-27 Jianxin Road, Jiaocheng, Ningde, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Beloved by the locals, this simple shop hidden in an alley ticks all the boxes in the way of local snacks, including Fujian’s take on wonton known as bian rou, either served in a sour and spicy broth with laver and pork cracklings, or deep-fried until crispy. House-made xiaolongbao is steamed to order, stuffed with pork and is rich in mushroom and scallion aromas. Marinated pork diaphragm boasts a meaty flavour and chewy texture.

Name: Fu Juang Yuan
Address: 203, Section 1, Meicun Road, West District, Taichung, 403, Taiwan Region
Description: One of the most famous spots in town for braised pork trotters, this shop keeps the liquid gold – made with soy, rock sugar, chillis and shallots – on a gentle simmer all day, hence the comforting aroma. While trotters are prized for their gelatinous texture, upper leg cuts strike a fine balance between fat, skin and meat. Drizzle the steamed rice with a spoon of marinade. A dab of the house-made bird’s eye chilli sauce cuts through the richness.

Name: Fu Kuei Ting
Address: 31, Lane 18, Section 2, Sanmin Road, Central District, Taichung, 400, Taiwan Region
Description: Many Taichungians have fond childhood memories of this shop as it has been around for some 60 years. The goose noodle soup combines the Chinese herb Dang Gui, springy goose flesh and robust flavours. If the goose runs out, try the equally enticing duck version. Smoked goose uses adult birds weighing about 6 kg, smoked with cane sugar instead of wood chips. Those craving juicier and fattier meat may ask for the hindquarters when ordering.

Name: Fu Lin Xuan (Jiqingmen Street)
Address: 188 Jiqingmen Street, Jianye, Nanjing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The owner’s grandpa used to be a street vendor selling cold jelly noodles. In 2011, when the owner opened this restaurant, he decided to uphold this legacy and put them on the menu. The fine, velvety noodles are made with three types of starch, topped with dried radish and chilli and dressed in a sauce that is sweet, sour, savoury and spicy - all at the same time. Red-braised beef rib tips boast deep flavour and the cartilage adds a lovely texture. Reservations recommended.

Name: Fu Ming Cooked Food
Description: The carrot cake made fresh from scratch daily comes in black and white varieties. The former is seasoned with dark soy for richer, deeper flavours. They also sell sticky rice dumplings in Chinese and Nyonya styles.

Name: Fu Tai Table Third Generation
Address: 219, Section 2, Minzu Road, West Central District, Tainan, Taiwan Region
Description: Fu Tai Table began as a street vendor over 80 years ago, but not until 2015 did it have a permanent address.
