It's the perfect place to experience the unique fan zhuo zai culture – diners order a bowl of braised pork rice with several small plates that arrive at the table stacked on top of each other on a tray. Look for the menu on the blackboard. Made fresh daily, the soup with assorted meatballs is also worth trying for its bouncy texture and deep umami.

Name: Fu Xing Mian Wang (Hedong Road)
Address: 178 Hedong Road, Gongshu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This shop may lack a snazzy decor, and nobody gets a table to themselves, but there are always queues eager to be cooked for by the self-proclaimed "noodle king". The signature tomato sauce noodles with scrambled eggs are tangy and appetising, best enjoyed with a sprinkle of pork cracklings. All made-to-order, the delicious toppings are served piping hot – try the deep-fried carp. Those with a big appetite can even get extra noodles for free.

Name: Fu Yu Da Tong Ya Rou Zhou
Address: 166 Kaihe Road, Siming, Xiamen, Chinese Mainland
Description: This neighbourhood duck congee shop opened its doors in 1983. Locals come in droves 24-7 for a bowl of comforting porridge that warms the heart and soul. Those overwhelmed by the 20-plus toppings available can opt for one of the popular combos – ‘signature’ with duck meat and offal; ‘seafood’ with duck, oysters, and squid; or the ‘classic’ with duck, pork liver and marinated egg. Always order a deep-fried dough stick to mop up the broth.

Name: Fu Yuan Ju (Shangcheng)
Address: 35 Hefang Street, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This acclaimed eatery prides itself on its home-style dishes. Expect queues at mealtimes! The juicy chicken dressed in scallion oil exudes heady aromas. Steamed vegetarian chicken and bamboo shoots with dried pork marinated in soybean paste evoke childhood memories for many a Hangzhou local. Freshwater fish is another strong suit – check out the bream, eels and crabs in the fish tank at the entrance and ask the servers the best way to have them cooked.

Name: FuLu Mandarijn
Description: Expect aromatic spices, deep umami notes and the distinctive tingle of Sichuan pepper at this lively, atmospheric restaurant in the heart of Amsterdam. Authentic Sichuan cooking takes centre stage, with a few Cantonese specialities and dim sum also on the menu. The beef offal is well worth trying: lifted by dried chilli, Sichuan pepper, garlic and coriander, it retains a pleasing bite. Another tempting option is the whole sea bass in an aromatic stew with assorted mushrooms and a rich broth. The menu is extensive and portions are generous – this is food best shared around the table. With so much to try, there is every reason to plan a return visit.

Name: Fugaz
Description: Located in Roma Norte, the low-key vibe of this pleasant cafe belies some very serious and creative cuisine. Simple but attractive, the setting boasts a bright green facade, sandy-hued terrazzo flooring, light wood furnishings and pale unadorned walls.Chef Giuseppe Lacorazza studied in Buenos Aires and spent time in kitchens in Europe and New York City. The cuisine here has a faint Mediterranean accent to its Mexican foundation and is enhanced by vegetable-dominated preparations. The day's catch may be transformed into crudo tossed with white beans and set atop a creamy almond and brown butter puree, and gnudi are served in a light broth with tender slices of white onion and some Parmesan cheese. The Italian sausage sandwich is a meaty option as well.

Name: Fujian Cuisine (Dongsanhuan North Road)
Address: 110-111, Kaidexingmao, 26A Dongsanhuan North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The owner and chefs who hail from Xiamen insist on using produce and seafood from their home province to create authentic Fujian dishes, especially country recipes that were the staple diet of the commoners in olden days. Steamed red crab on sticky rice seduces with seafood umami and briny-sweet roe, while the ginger duck is an heirloom recipe passed down for generations, made with Muscovy duck for exceptional depth. Also try the creamy mashed taro dessert.

Name: Fujian Yu Shan Tang
Address: 3F, Bai Fu Yi Hotel, No. 19 Nan'erlizhuang, Dongzhimenwai Street, Dongcheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The live seafood tanks and marine specimens display resembles a miniature aquarium. The menu is predominantly Fujian, but with unexpected twists. Their signature spring roll is oyster omelette, reimagined in a crispy wafer-thin shell. Creamy textured, the "strange-flavour" pan-seared pork liver is complemented by sweet and sour sauce. The wine list is sorted into categories such as umami, dry, sweet and mellow for easy reference.

Name: Fullie's Seafood House
Address: 1-7 Jiazhi Street, Jiaojiang, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: At this spot with a model junk boat at its door and a name that is a wish for a bountiful catch, it comes as no surprise that the freshest local seafood and fish are its strong suit, alongside Taizhou home-style classics. The bouncy-textured signature shrimp patty boasts unparalleled umami, and the steamed roe crab seduces with its buttery, gelatinous roe. Their sautéed rice cake with sea anemone comes in an umami-loaded broth with a unique briny flavour.

Name: Fung Shing (North Point)
Address: 62-68 Java Road, North Point, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: This long-standing champion of Shun Tak cuisine sports traditional fixtures and fittings. Locals and tourists come for dim sum in the morning, while painstakingly prepared Cantonese favourites and Shun Tak specialities are served at lunch and dinner. Besides signatures like crispy fried chicken and Daliang-style scrambled egg white with milk, don’t miss their sugar egg puff doughnuts available at weekend lunchtime only. Hearty portions to share.

Name: Furancho La Zapatería
Address: Paseo Canarina 18, Icod de los Vinos, 38430, Spain
Description: A Galician restaurant on Tenerife that, despite its simple decor, is highly original. Behind its colourful façade, which recreates the glass frontage of an old shoe shop, the friendly couple running it (Emma is in the kitchen; Alberto in the dining room) focus on an unusual combination of Galician and Canary Island products, the former brought in fresh from Fisterra (La Coruña) every other day by the owner’s brother. Highlights on the menu here include the octopus empanadas, the entrecôte of Galician veal, grilled scallops, and mussels with a mojo sauce that are a must.

Name: Furbetto
Description: Gust and Jasper have established their friendly eatery a stone’s throw from Heverlee railway station in a smart town house. Their love of unfussy Italian cooking shines through as you watch them wield their magic in the open-plan kitchen. Homemade is the name of the game here, underscored by a constant quest for superlative local produce. After nibbling on a delicious focaccia appetiser, dig into homemade pasta and subtle dishes such as beef tartare jazzed up with cream of anchovies. You can’t go wrong with French toast and buttermilk ice cream to finish. Choose your wine from the bottles on the surrounding shelves. Furbetto hits the spot every time, all the more so due to its eater-friendly prices!

Name: Futura Osteria
Address: Largo Garfonda 10, località Abbadia Isola, Monteriggioni, 53035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Along the Via Francigena, just a few steps from Monteriggioni, stands the small medieval hamlet of Abbadia Isola, with its splendid Romanesque church and ancient buildings that once formed the monastery and its dependencies. Futura Osteria occupies the rooms that were once the monks’ cellars, where they stored their wines: here you can enjoy flavourful, Tuscan-inspired cuisine, simple and profoundly seasonal. The format offers three fixed-price tasting menus, with portions that are always generous; many of the vegetables come from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. In addition to the menus, there is always Florentine steak cooked over the embers, as well as the option of ordering the selection of cured meats made by hand in the osteria and cheeses matured in-house. Completing the picture are a refined wine selection, friendly service and a secluded, atmospheric terrace.

Name: Fuyacho Kuraku
Description: Names of dishes cram the menu. The menu is replete with fish dishes, so you can enjoy the ‘fruits of the sea’ to the full. Fish from Wakasa Bay, in the chef’s native Fukui Prefecture, is a point of pride. Whether served as sashimi, grilled with salt or boiled in soy sauce, their inherent flavours shine through. ‘Heshiko’, fish pickled in rice-bran paste, is a Fukui hometown favourite. Fukui sakes are ordered in, spreading the appeal of the Echizen and Wakasa regions. Standards such as potato salad and deep-fried horse mackerel are perennial hits as well.

Name: Fährhaus
Description: Practically right behind the dike and just a few minutes' walk from the ferry port, this restaurant serves distinctly local cuisine made with produce sourced from local fishers and farmers. Completely unpretentious and free from unnecessary frills, owner Gerold Janssen's dishes are brimming with freshness and flavour, as in the Helgoland crab cocktail or the crispy baked plaice fillets. Good to know: Well-kept guestrooms are available for overnight stays or holidays.

Name: Fürstenfelder
Description: This former monastery makes for a wonderful setting. In what was once the stables, the impressive Bohemian barrel-vaulted ceiling has been incorporated into the modern interior design, with a centrally positioned open kitchen. Out in the courtyard of the Cistercian monastery, there is a lovely terrace, slightly separated from the beer garden. On the varied menu: organic produce from the region goes into clever, exciting plates with a modern twist that are far from run-of-the-mill. Options include dishes from the Josper grill – such as grilled chicken breast with a thyme and honey glaze – as well as vegetarian and vegan options, such as "Duet of peas and carrots". Buffet at lunchtime.

Name: GASSENHAUR
Description: Despite looking quite unassuming from the outside, this first-floor bistro turns out to be a real little gem. Russet-red walls, beautiful hardwood floors and ornamental crystal chandeliers hanging from high ceilings make for a decidedly cosy ambience. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back, and that is in no small part thanks to the friendly and attentive service. Classic Viennese cuisine is the name of the game, offering the chance to try the original Wiener schnitzel made from veal loin – a freshly tapped beer is highly recommended to go with it. As an alternative to the à la carte selection, there is a three-course set menu. Tip: This place is very popular, so it's advisable to book!

Name: GINZA KATSUKAMI II
Address: 4F, Kojun Bldg, 6-8-7 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo, 104-0061, Japan
Description: Service at this tonkatsu restaurant is prix fixe only. Along with the familiar fillet and pork loin cutlets, you’ll find rare cuts such as rump and round tip, fried one slice at a time. Several name-brand pork varieties are available to taste and compare, each one tender and succulent. A few unexpected entries, such as minced pork burgers, add whimsy into the mix. It’s a concept that makes sense: unique prix fixe menus of tonkatsu, each item served piping hot from the kitchen.

Name: GaGa
Address: 566 Dumbarton Road, Partick, Glasgow City, G11 6RH, United Kingdom
Description: In the West End suburb of Partick, this brightly painted restaurant offers an enjoyable slice of Southeast Asian cuisine. One side is a former butcher’s shop with the original glazed tiles on the walls, whilst the other is more rustic with colourful pot plants dotted around. Grab one of the booths if you can and start with a cocktail, then dive right into the menu of vibrantly flavoured dishes that take inspiration from Malaysia, Thailand and beyond. Lively, delicious and great value, GaGa has all the ingredients for a fun night out.

Name: Gabbiano 1983
Address: Piazza Vittorio Veneto 10, Corte de' Cortesi, 26020, Italy
Description: Having successfully been in business for over 40 years, this restaurant continues to shine for its top-quality traditional cuisine, priding itself, as it has always done, on its love for local specialities. Goose dishes take centre stage on the menu (the area is famous for its goose), alongside an excellent selection of traditional boiled meats all of which are sourced locally. There’s also a good choice of wine, which is skilfully displayed and served from a trolley in the dining room from which wines are served by the glass.

Name: Gabrielle
Description: In an old building on a bustling street not far from Copenhagen City Hall you’ll find this French sister of Norrlyst and Theo. Set on the mezzanine floor, it has a comforting vintage feel courtesy of wooden bistro-style furnishings, ceiling fans and white clothed tables – and the packed room attests as to both its quality and its value. Carefully prepared, classically based dishes include the likes of confit duck and apricot purée croquettes; tarte Tatin with onions, olives, oregano and crème fraiche; and Gabrielle's signature garlic and thyme bread – all of which can be accompanied by exclusively French wines.

Name: Gaeseong Mandu Koong
Description: Set inside a converted traditional hanok, this restaurant is built around its signature gaeseong-style dumplings, a recipe passed down from the owner’s grandmother. The dough, fermented for three hours, yields wrappers with a pleasantly elastic texture and a subtle wheat aroma, while the filling—pork blended with generous vegetables—offers a clean, harmonious flavour. The clear, milky broth is simmered for eight hours with beef and ten kinds of fresh vegetables, resulting in a naturally savoury depth without heavy seasoning. The accompanying mul-kimchi and kkakdugi pair beautifully with the dumplings, completing a balanced and quietly refined meal.

Name: Gaijin Izakaya
Description: This place with a name that can be translated as "foreigner bar" is a cool spot that channels the style of a Japanese izakaya (casual bars that serve drinks and food). A team led by chef-patron Daniel Shu, who trained in Chicago and New York, and his business partner cook up creative Asian soul food – in the form of an omakase menu or à la carte. The lunch menu is more limited. Modern music plays in the background, fostering a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Gala
Description: Gala is considered a classic address in the Spanish capital, offering high levels of service to loyal customers since 1989. It boasts an attractive dining room plus a private dining space, both contemporary in style, where guests can enjoy updated traditional cuisine inspired by seasonal market produce on an à la carte that also offers half-plate options (the Alistano-Sanabresa breed of beef is excellent), alongside a daily menu and a more tasting-style option. The most popular specialities requested by its customers are its famous steak tartare, dishes featuring red tuna, and the rib of beef which is cooked at low temperature for 36 hours.

Name: Galanga Thai House
Description: There is a distinct tropical vibe at Chef "Ana" Somsri Raksamran's restaurant, set in a courtyard lined by towering bamboo and decorated with woven reed ceiling pendants and dangling vines.The menu features impressively prepared Thai cuisine with specialties from the country's northeast, central plains and the south. Peak freshness is guaranteed, as the team tends to their herbs and harvests to-order. Gaeng kiew wan is a luscious green curry with a bright hue, noticeable fresh chili spice, and a nice herbaceous quality; stocked with tender beef brisket, organic eggplant, sweet baby corn and chopped green beans, it's a delight best enjoyed with some freshly made roti canai. Save room for the khao niew ma muang, or perfectly ripe mango with sticky rice and coconut ice cream.

Name: Galea
Description: This corner charmer boasts a terrace out front, while inside, the use of wood keeps things firmly planted between the old and new worlds. There is an amiable, casual vibe to Galea, and with prices that don't break the bank, it's a favorite among locals. The focused Italian menu is concise but manages to present a varied selection all the same. Be sure to check the dishes of the day (and note the crudo specials, too) and always order a pasta, as it's made in house. All of the pasta dishes are also offered as half portions if you're tempted to try more than one. Focaccia made in-house starts things off, then a plate of gnochetti with ragu de mariscos feeds the soul. Fish of the day in a creamy beurre blanc is a hit, but save room for the panna cotta, given a bit of a Mexican slant here.

Name: Galvin Green Man
Address: Main Road, Great Waltham, Howe Street, CM3 1BG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Essex outpost of the Galvin empire is this big, busy pub, where there’s always something going on, from live music evenings to special events. The friendly team offer a warm welcome and the original 14th-century building provides all the rustic charm you’d expect, while a modern barn extension and a charming riverside garden complete the picture. The extensive menu offers an appealing mix of classic British and Mediterranean influenced dishes which are big on flavour, and the 'Bib Gourmand' menu is a steal.

Name: Gan Ji Fei Chang Fen
Address: No. 1-3, 18 Ma'an North Road, Jinniu, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: With over 30 years of history, this tiny gem is no secret to locals in search of a bowl of hearty glass noodle soup with braised pork intestines. The toothsome, springy noodles are made in-house. Choose between mala spicy soup and rich white broth. Optionally, order intestine knots on top for an extra layer of texture. And don't miss the piping hot guokui – crispy flatbread with pork and Sichuan pepper filling.

Name: Gao San Jie Dou Hua Dian
Address: 56-2, Shangmeilinxincun, Meicun Road, Futian, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
Description: It's been almost 20 years since this simple shop specialising in savoury tofu pudding and Sichuan cooking opened its doors. The spongy tofu, which takes hours to make every morning, is full of pores that soak up the chilli dip. Also worth trying are their Sichuanese dishes, such as pork intestine braised with soybeans. The broth is mildly spicy, while the lightly browned organ meat is soft and fatty, in contrast with the firmness of the soybeans.

Name: Garabato Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In the heart of the Núñez district, right next to the train station, there is a restaurant with a relaxed atmosphere that is gaining popularity and always has customers waiting. It offers a comfortable and bright dining room, with well-set tables (all of them have their own little lamp, which adds a romantic touch), a bar where you can also eat and the open kitchen at the back. This is the most lively part, as there’s also a large communal table there which doubles as a serving space. The couple in charge, chefs Clara Corso and Lucas Canga, like to define it as a ‘neo-bistro’ where they serve up traditional food with a modern twist, designed for sharing. Dishes include the ham and cheese tartlet, a pleasant trout salad, the hearty ribeye steak and marrow, the delicious combination of pears, white chocolate and tonka bean. The round tables placed at the entrance are reminiscent of Parisian terraces!

Name: Garbí
Description: A family-run restaurant named after a thermal wind from the southwest that blows across the whole of the Levante region. The owner-chef, who has taken over the reins following the retirement of his parents, is closely involved with the collective of “Cuina Vallès” chefs, and their straightforward approach to traditional Catalan cuisine. As a result, the menu is bursting with legendary classic dishes such as Mongetes del ganxet white beans from Can Casamada, tripe with chickpeas, crispy fried brains, and the delicious oxtail stew. The daily menu is particularly popular here!

Name: Garde Manger
Description: Picture a traditional Ardennes edifice in the Samson Valley whose interior is snug and homely… Garde Manger (“larder” in English) inevitably brings a smile to our lips, which is largely thanks to the inspired score of Christophe Durand, whose love of seasonal produce is paired with charismatic enthusiasm and consummate know-how. He subtly reinterprets authentic flavours whilst allowing their core character to shine through. Ballotine of guinea fowl is flanked by a powerful gravy and subtle sides. All that remains is to try and solve the dilemma of choosing between the enticing à la carte and set menus…

Name: Garden h
Address: 22 Zhiguang Street, Yonghe District, New Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: Thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows, diners can sit back and appreciate the beauty of a century-old camellia tree in the yard. The menu is mostly Hakkanese, with some Jiangzhe dishes, jazzed up by creative touches and elegant plating. The signature braised pork belly with dry pickled mustard greens boasts tender texture and succulent flavours, while pickled cucumber cuts through the richness. Also try braised napa cabbage with pork-stuffed tofu.

Name: Garden.V
Address: 136, Section 1, Dongda Road, East District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan Region
Description: For 20+ years, Garden.V has been valued by locals for its authentic Jiangzhe fare served in generous portions. The three-storey space feels airy and bright thanks to full-length windows. Certain items, such as cabbage rice with Jinhua ham, need to be pre-ordered. Be sure to check out the glass display case for cold appetisers and sides – the kao fu, or fried wheat gluten with mushrooms and bamboo shoot, is savoury-sweet and incredibly appetising.

Name: Gare aux Goûts
Description: Chef Vincent Seviller has come up trumps in this establishment near the railway station. He invites diners on a bistronomic journey in a tasteful, modern setting. An experienced and talented craftsman, each dish is artfully presented, flavoursome and balanced. The lunchtime menu is chalked up on a slate, but more elaborate in the evening.

Name: Gary’s
Description: It's easy to be won over by this convivial neighborhood spot, which owes its easygoing charms to the combined efforts of partners Bailey Hayward and Mathew Bishop (who oversee the service and the kitchen, respectively). To match the relaxed, friendly vibe, the cuisine is rustic and approachable, offering hearty dishes that draw inspiration from French country cooking, as in asparagus with saffron rouille, or pork collar with parsley sauce—and don't miss out on the fluffy, freshly baked rye rolls, served with green garlic butter. For a final slather of indulgence, do order dessert, like a rum baba soaked with chamomile-scented syrup and capped with a ribbon of decadent pistachio custard and a cloud of chantilly.

Name: Gaspar's
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: On the border of the Old and the New Town you’ll find Gaspar’s, a neighbourhood restaurant with a long history as an eatery – look out for the original Yiddish restaurant sign above the door (this was once the Jewish Quarter). Chef Gaspar Fernandes was born in Goa, India and is of Portuguese heritage, so his cuisine is an intriguing blend of the two countries. The menu is concise, driven by the produce available and subtle Indian spicing, and dishes are generous and beautifully presented. “My mum’s curry” is available in several varieties and the naan bread uses locally milled whole wheat flour, which adds a unique nuttiness.

Name: Gassenwirt
Description: Situated next to the village church, this restaurant has been serving excellent South Tyrolean cuisine since as far back as 1602. House specialities include canederli pressati (dumplings) and Buchteln (a type of sweet bun).

Name: Gasthaus Egertal
Description: The Rupprecht family keep things cosy in their pretty, traditional restaurant. Rustic details such as brick vaulted ceilings and natural stone walls combine with more modern touches to create a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere. There are two set menus and an appealing à la carte selection. The flavourful dishes take inspiration from both regional and classic recipes – think Label Rouge salmon fillet prepared confit-style in brown butter, with chives, lemon and Maldon sea salt. Somewhat simpler but no less tempting are dishes such as pork fillet with a peppercorn sauce or beef cheeks in vegetable broth. The terrace out front is inviting in summer.

Name: Gasthaus Fuchs
Description: After completing stints at renowned establishments, Thomas Fuchs has brought a breath of fresh air to his parents' restaurant in the middle of this Burgenland village. His delicious dishes range from classics such as schnitzel, Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth) and the like to "salmon trout fillet, chervil root, fregola" or "goose liver, fig, chocolate, Buchtel (sweet yeast buns)". In addition to an à la carte selection, there is also a three- to six-course tasting menu in the evening and a smaller set menu at lunchtime. The well-kept dining area (divided into rooms – some with a rustic touch, some more modern) is complemented by a pleasant terrace in summer.

Name: Gasthaus Goldener Stern
Description: Run with great dedication by the same family for three generations, this place operates as a traditional Gasthaus at lunchtime and as a casual-fine dining restaurant in the evening. The inviting interior is modern yet cosy, and the cuisine, inspired by contemporary trends, emphasises seasonal, regional ingredients. Local producers are proudly showcased, supplying the restaurant with meat, fish, eggs, cheese and more. A fine example of the meticulously crafted dishes is Böfflamot (Bavarian bœuf à la mode – slow‑braised beef in wine sauce) made with Wittelsbach ox from Hofmetzger Ottillinger, cold-stirred lingonberries, roasted celeriac cream, glazed vegetables and pretzel dumplings. Friendly and adept front-of-house team. The Eichen Loft can be booked for events, and the stylish wine shop can be reserved from October to April for celebrations (max. 12 people). The pleasant beer garden has a slightly shorter menu.

Name: Gasthaus Scherz
Description: Born in Vorarlberg, but no stranger to Cologne's restaurant scene, Michael Scherz showcases the cuisine of his home country. The menu is divided into Austrian classics, including Tafelspitz (boiled beef), Wiener schnitzel and Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake with raisins), and "new classics with a twist", such as "Drei-Käse-Hoch, corn soufflé, green asparagus and artichoke" – to be washed down with good wines from Austria. The pleasant and professional team provides speedy, friendly, laid-back service. There is also a nice bar. The terrace to the rear of the restaurant is another appealing spot. Good to know: the restaurant is easily accessible from the city centre by tram.

Name: Gasthaus Schupfen
Description: With a history dating back to 1455, this lovely half-timbered house is really something special. In an inviting atmosphere, food is served in three charming rooms and on the idyllic terrace overlooking the Rhine. The menu features Swiss classics such as fillets of perch with tartare sauce or Kalbsgeschnetzeltes Zürcher Art – Zurich veal ragout with rösti, alongside seasonal dishes such as asparagus salad with herb vinaigrette, served with smoked trout and fresh horseradish. If you are looking for a good location for a wedding or event, the premises can also be rented out.

Name: Gasthaus Schwanen
Description: This inn is everything you could wish for! Nestled in the heart of the sleepy hamlet of Schwaningen, the family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for three generations. Inside, a cosy ambiance awaits, while outside, the idyllic garden terrace with its shady chestnut tree beckons. The food is outstanding – their wild boar ravioli in sage butter is a house speciality. They make a point of using regional ingredients, some of which they produce themselves: They have their own chickens and eggs, hunt their own game, keep bees, bake their own bread, make juices, liqueurs and spirits… Both Gasthaus Schwanen and Villa Pfarrhus, which boasts a beautiful garden, have guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Steinberg
Description: If you want to combine a hiking trip with a really wonderful meal at a fair price, the Grafl family establishment is the place to go! In this typical regional inn in a wonderfully idyllic location, the cuisine is traditional, aromatic, and perfectly crafted. The Pressknödelsuppe (dumpling soup) and Almrindsülzchen (Alpine beef aspic) are full of flavour, not to mention classics such as beef goulash and schnitzel. In summer, the terrace boasting a view of the surrounding countryside and mountains is a joy. Overnight accommodation is also an option.

Name: Gasthaus Tante Liesl
Description: In the charming Servitenviertel – an area replete with small shops, eateries and lovely period architecture – this lively and cosy establishment has a rustic feel. It is right next to the Servitenkirche, a Baroque church that is certainly worth a visit. The neighbourly atmosphere is as much of a draw as the delicious Austrian food. The menu features dishes such as pork crackling dumplings with coleslaw or mushroom goulash with bread dumplings, not to mention classics like Wiener schnitzel with potato and lamb's lettuce salad. The traditional Sunday roast naturally has its place as well. Tip: Mon-Fri, there is a reasonably priced lunch special. Tables on the tree-shaded garden terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Gasthaus Waltz
Description: This fashionable and lively restaurant in Munich's Glockenbachviertel is run by a dedicated young team. The secret of its success lies in its modern Alpine cuisine – by turns creative and traditional, but always presented with flair and based on the finest regional ingredients. Dishes such as "breaded pork chop, mushrooms, nasturtium & potato and cucumber salad" or "Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings), pumpkin, hazelnut & Belper Knolle cheese" can be chosen à la carte or combined in a four- or five-course set menu. The well-curated wine list is also surprisingly extensive – another highlight. In summer, guests are drawn to the terrace in front of the restaurant. N.B. Parking options are limited – public transport is the best way to get here.

Name: Gasthaus Weißenbeck
Description: You will find plenty of satisfied customers here, and no wonder! The mother-daughter duo of the Weissenbeck family cook with a real sense of ambition. Excellent produce, often sourced from regional suppliers, is transformed into well-crafted combinations that showcase both technical skill and a clear culinary identity. The menu, which changes according to seasonal availability, features dishes such as "venison pâté, mushroom salad, grape-ginger jelly" and "Bavarian char, kohlrabi noodles, lemon butter and parsley purée". The charming, almost picture-postcard inn makes for a really cosy setting. In summer the attractive garden terrace is an added draw.

Name: Gasthaus Zum fröhlichen Arbeiter
Description: This spruce family-run inn has been welcoming diners for 100 years. Owner and head chef Hannes Tschida showcases his love for the Seewinkel region through dishes incorporating plenty of local ingredients. The wide-ranging à la carte options include Grammelknödel (potato dumplings stuffed with greaves), beef goulash, trout ceviche, dry-aged steak and Lake Neusiedl catfish. There is also a four- to six-course surprise menu. To complement the bold flavours of the cuisine, an impressive wine list dominated by Austrian labels is available. The restaurant itself has two indoor dining spaces: one oozing traditional charm, the other more modern with a conservatory feel. The friendly and attentive service is appreciated by regulars and newcomers alike.

Name: Gasthaus zur Kanne
Description: "The oldest inn in the Palatinate" has been around since 1160 – as it says on the façade. Given that the hosts are dedicated, the location is charming and the cuisine is excellent, it's no surprise that it's popular with many (regular) guests – and it's best to book ahead. The restaurant is divided into different rooms, which creates a certain intimacy. Historical and modern details have been successfully combined, including eye-catching features such as wonderful old tiled stoves and a brick fountain. Regional cuisine with international influences is served in the form of a lovely, seasonal à la carte selection featuring dishes such as "Palatina Trio – Saumagen, bratwurst, liver dumplings", "cod fillet, saffron foam, herb risotto, kohlrabi" or even charcoal-grilled rump steak. The selection of Palatinate wines is appealing – and there is also a wine bar. The terrace in the courtyard is truly charming.

Name: Gasthaus Ödenturm
Description: As if straight out of a picture book, this beautiful inn stands on the edge of the forest. Inside, a warm and welcoming atmosphere reigns; outside, there is a charming terrace. Ernst Hunger Jr and his wife Brigitte run this long-standing family business with great dedication, delighting diners with good food and friendly service. The cooking is regional but also features Mediterranean and contemporary influences – from steak and fish to locally hunted game and vegetarian options. The dishes are delicious and very reasonably priced. The bottom line: this is a place people love – so be sure to reserve in advance. Modern, cosy guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthof Adler
Description: This picture-perfect inn set on the village square occupies a wooden building dating from 1756, restored in keeping with its historic character and featuring warm wood from floor to ceiling for a cosy atmosphere. Felix Messner, who runs the establishment with his brother Florian, serves up fresh, flavoursome fare inspired by the culinary traditions of Austria and the Vorarlberg region. The cooking is stripped back to the essentials, allowing the excellent regional produce to take centre stage. Dishes include Backhendl (Austrian-style fried chicken), Tafelspitz (beef simmered in broth), schnitzel, lemon chicken and chanterelle ragout. For overnight stays, there are tastefully appointed guestrooms in a modern regional style.

Name: Gasthof Alpenrose
Description: This long-established inn by the church is always busy and much loved by its many regulars. Appearing in records as a tavern as early as the 16C, it has now been run by the same family for five generations. The cosy interior features an old tiled stove providing warmth in winter. In summer, a secluded beer garden, a veranda and even a rooftop terrace beckon. The Bavarian and Styrian cuisine includes appetising options such as venison goulash with butter spaetzle, red cabbage and aronia berries. Seasonal ingredients from the immediate area are used whenever possible. It is a real plus that on every day that it is open for dinner, the restaurant also serves lunch. Attractive guestrooms.

Name: Gasthof Berghof - Ursprung
Description: "Tradition meets modernity" is the theme here, both in the decor and the cuisine. Carefully selected ingredients go into flavoursome seasonal dishes. In addition to two appealing set menus, there are à la carte dishes including classics such as shashlik of hand-prepared pork neck and venison schnitzel, not forgetting the Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with vanilla ice cream and apple compote. Be sure to take advantage of the inviting courtyard terrace in summer! For overnight stays, there are well-kept guestrooms and a lovely modern holiday home.

Name: Gasthof Blumenthal
Description: A family business in its sixth generation, this is all you could wish for from a Franconian inn. The interior is cosy and the beer garden, which is largely sheltered from the elements, is fabulous. Served in a pleasingly laid-back and extremely charming atmosphere, the menu features down-to-earth, unfussy dishes that are big on flavour and showcase the kitchen team's craftsmanship and good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients. Tip: They breed their own char and trout!

Name: Gasthof Brink
Description: A place with charm! The traditional style that is cultivated here will evoke childhood memories for many diners. Family-run since 1880, the restaurant serves classic French cuisine that is down to earth and delicious. The pleasant setting has an elegant feel. The house-made pâtés and terrines are just as popular as the saddle of veal with Béarnaise sauce or the sole meunière.

Name: Gasthof Rössle
Description: Currently at the helm of this restaurant, once an inn (dating back to 1775), is Valentin Bargehr, the third generation of the family. On the first floor of this building next to the parish church, Pfarrkirche St Nikolaus, diners are welcomed in a number of inviting dining spaces (some wood-panelled), or outside on the pretty terrace shaded by trees. The menu features delicious regional cuisine made from seasonal, almost exclusively local ingredients. In addition to à la carte dishes such as "Rössle fish soup" or roast chicken, mixed salad, lingonberries, parsley potatoes, there is also a choice of two lovely three-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. These include mouthwatering veal cheeks, chanterelles and noodles or pumpkin capuns and grilled vegetables, respectively. While Valentin Bargehr takes care of things in the kitchen, his brother Martin provides charming service. Don't forget to book at this very popular place. Tip: They have cosy contemporary guestrooms for overnight guests.

Name: Gasthof Schäffer
Address: Hauptstraße 9, Neuberg an der Mürz, 8692, Austria
Description: A restaurant where you feel right at home, thanks to the cosy atmosphere, cordial service, and the food that is straight-up delicious! This is traditional, home-style cuisine – think Austrian classics such as Wiener schnitzel, Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) and Tafelspitz (boiled beef), as well as venison Beuscherl (lights) and freshwater fish from the region. Those who prefer something a little more elevated can opt for a surprise menu (three to five courses) in the evening, subject to advance booking. They also have seven cosy guestrooms.

Name: Gasthof zum goldenen Kreuz
Description: This restaurant is steeped in tradition, and much sought after for its excellent seasonal cuisine. The chef's expertise and his knack for preparing select ingredients with real flavour are evident in dishes such as spicy smoked trout tartare with dill mustard and marinated apple and beetroot salad, and braised veal cheek, Bramata polenta and green beans with dried bacon. At lunchtime, you can order à la carte or opt for one of four three-course set menus. In the evening, there is a tasting menu in addition to an à la carte selection. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-organised front-of-house team. Goethe himself was a guest here – the pretty Goethe-Stübli is named after him – and the well-preserved painted panelling from the 17C adds rustic charm. The terrace is a delightful spot, secluded from the street by abundant greenery. Modern, functional guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Tip for motorists: public car park behind the building.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This charming traditional inn with its striking red façade may be a little off the beaten track, but the flavoursome regional and Mediterranean cuisine served here makes the journey worthwhile. Be sure to set aside some time because Egbert Tribelhorn is the sole chef at work here, and he takes great pride in the quality and meticulous preparation of his creations. Your patience will be rewarded with impeccably crafted and bold classic dishes. Diners often opt for the "Sonnen-Menü" set menu, but the à la carte options are also very popular. The house-made ravioli are a must-try.The restaurant also has three simple but beautifully kept guestrooms.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This 500-year-old heritage-protected inn is now a hotel and restaurant run by Patricia and Cäsar Meyer, who represent the second generation of their family here. Cäsar has a penchant for fish caught in Lake Zurich, just a stone's throw away – you can't get any fresher or more regional than that! Meat and vegetables, too, are sourced from the immediate vicinity. Besides the whitefish and perch, the Stäfa venison is especially worth trying – it is served as the overnight-braised shoulder with Pinot Noir sauce. This cuisine is built on regional ingredients. Food is served on the first floor of the building, in cosy yet stylish rooms that exude historical charm. A wonderful terrace balcony affords stunning lake views. The staff are very attentive and cordial – you're sure to want to come back! Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Gaston Vouzote
Description: Gaston Vouzote is the sort of authentic brasserie that will bring a smile to your face. From the vintage, Parisian-inspired bistro interior to the cheerful table service, each detail is designed to ensure you enjoy every minute of your meal. A wide range of house-made family favourites oozing in rich, generous flavours is what you can expect ranging from perfectly cooked poached egg with Parma ham and parmesan to tomahawk steak grilled in a Mibrasa charcoal oven or steak tartare crammed with gherkins and capers and served with freshly-made, piping-hot French fries. Just the ticket for fans of no-nonsense tasty nosh that satisfies the appetite and the senses!

Name: Gaststube
Description: Housed inside Krone is this pleasant, cosy and down-to-earth restaurant that is also run by the Wölfelschneider family. The Gaststube menu will appeal to those who appreciate regional, home-style cooking, a case in point being the fillet of Odenwald trout on a bed of leek and chanterelle mushrooms with a cider and herb sauce. Mediterranean influences can also be detected on the menu. In addition to the delicious food, a highlight is the friendly service, which contributes to the congenial atmosphere. In summer, the terrace is idyllic!

Name: Gatherings
Address: Unit 5, 2 Papanui Road, Merivale, Christchurch, 8014, New Zealand
Description: In this intimate 20-seat restaurant, warm lighting and an abundance of reclaimed wood create a warm atmosphere where you feel right at home. The small menu changes weekly to make the best use of local, organic ingredients in season. When available, the Fiordland venison is a must-try for its tender, delicate meat that doesn't taste gamey. The 3-course set meal, which allows free combination of entree, main and dessert, is a deal.

Name: Ge Ji Mei Ji Xian
Address: 2F, Proudway Hotel, 15 Hongbao Road, Luohu, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: For over 20 years, this joint has been serving authentic Northern Guangdong fare, in particular recipes from Shaoguan, but with influences from the Hakka and Yao ethnic groups. The umami-loaded dishes tend to be sour and spicy. Popular with drinks, the signature "duck five cuts" is made with duck head, neck, wings, webs and chins – these are fried, then braised in a savoury sauce. Be sure to try the fermented bamboo shoot with beef or offal, too.

Name: Ge Jia Wu Farmer’s House
Address: 7-17 Gejia Cove, Shushan Village, Dashishan Road, Huqiu, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: Off the beaten track in Shushan Ecological Village, this restaurant is set in an idyllic landscape. Despite its distance from the city centre, locals flock here for authentic Suzhou cooking while on a day out in Suzhou's majestic nature. The signature braised goose is repeatedly steeped in an aged marinade with 16 spices so that the flavour penetrates deep into the bones. Clams with baby burr clovers are a classic with a unique grassy fragrance.

Name: Ge Lang Guan
Address: 2F, Hengchuandao, 9 Quzhou Street, Gongshu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: It's a bit out of the way, but that doesn't stop diners from coming here in droves for authentic Shaoxing dishes. The menu is written daily on the whiteboard. All ingredients are seasonal and shipped from Shaoxing. The free-range chicken marinated in aged distillers' grains has firm, flavoursome flesh with a hint of wine aromas. The stinky duo, or stinky tofu with fermented amaranth stems, exudes a stench that you'll either love or hate!

Name: Gebangsikdang
Description: Soy sauce-marinated crab and stylish décor don’t always go hand in hand, but at Gebangsikdang, they do. A collaboration between fashion marketer Bang Geon-hyuk and his parents, veterans of the soy sauce marinated crab restaurant business, Gebangsikdang caters to a trend-conscious crowd with its polished interior and its wide selection of raw crab dishes. For those who find it bothersome to eat crab on the shell, there are options that come with just the crab flesh and crab roe on a mound of hot rice.

Name: Gehrlein's Hardtwald
Description: Somewhat tucked away, the Gehrlein family's restaurant boasts a welcoming interior, as well as a lovely garden terrace. Meticulously crafted using the finest ingredients, the dishes served here are remarkably flavoursome. Chef-patron Martin Gehrlein has a penchant for fish – whether fried pike-perch with potato salad or sea bass with gnocchi. Led by the proprietress, the highly committed and friendly service team guarantees a seamless dining experience. The guesthouse opposite provides comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Gemma
Address: 2323 N. Henderson Ave., Ste. 109, Dallas, TX, 75206, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Gemma is a charming spot from the husband-and-wife team of Chef Stephen Rogers and Allison Yoder. The couple met while working at Napa Valley's Press and returned to Rogers's home state to open this intimate spot in Dallas that highlights contemporary American cooking with a seasonal focus.The evening begins with a simple sounding but sinfully delicious warm raisin scone. Fried Castelvetrano olives mixed with fragrant Texas pecans are a delight, but it's cooking like the roasted heirloom carrots or the Idaho trout almondine that make a meal here memorable. Meyer lemon tart with notes of lavender and kisses of toasted meringue is a perfect send off.

Name: Gemmayze Street
Address: Shop 16, St. Kevin's Arcade, 183 Karangahape Road, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: Chef-owner Samir Allen celebrates his Lebanese-Pākehā heritage here, where he rather cleverly takes over the tables in the arcade outside his tiny restaurant that the café opposite uses during the day. The sense of family is palpable, in the warm yet busy atmosphere, in the service which is both friendly and so well organised, and in the sharing of the keenly priced and delicious dishes. Start with homemade pide and the wonderfully creamy hummus; and you’ll be hard pressed to find juicier chicken thighs.

Name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
Description: Located along a main road in Sindang-dong, Geumdwaeji Sikdang can be easily spotted by its gold-on-white-tile signage and the queue outside the door long after peak dining hours. The establishment used to serve fine cuts of YBD pig and has recently upgraded the meat quality by switching to premium-grade cuts. The texture of the pork is firm and meaty, with a good balance of flavourful fat that renders the meat supremely juicy. Items are cooked on a cast-iron grill over coal briquettes that help keep the temperature constant.

Name: Ggupdang
Description: Situated right near Sinsa station, this restaurant specializes in grilled pork butt cured for 15 days before being quickly grilled on a specially made aluminum grate over Binchotan charcoal. Thanks to this method of cooking, the meat is fatty, tender, and juicy. As in the case of sushi, when it is eaten with rice (prepared with a recipe conceived by a Japanese consultant chef) and Korean horseradish, the meat juice is absorbed by the rice, making it even softer. The side orders are not to be missed.

Name: Ghee Indian Kitchen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Niven Patel’s smash-hit restaurant is bound to put diners in the mood for the team's smartly spiced food with warehouse floors, mango wood tables and a wall lined with rows upon rows of spice jars.The kitchen takes no cues from its suburban locale; in fact, it features a tight menu of flavor-packed dishes made with ingredients sourced from Chef Patel’s own farm. Ghost pepper-cheddar seed naan is a fiery, puff-pastry-like riff, while yellowfin tuna bhel with avocado makes for a zesty first course. Kerala lamb with tomato and coconut is a richly satisfying effort with layered notes, soft basmati rice and meltingly tender meat.

Name: Ghee Lian
Address: Lot No. 39, MBPP Kompleks Makanan Medan Renong Padang Kota Lama, 4 Jalan Tun Syed Sheh Barakhbah, George Town, 10200, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: They serve three noodle dishes: the signature green tom yum, noodle soup and fried noodles. The fresh green tom yum hits the right balance of sour and spicy. The fried fish topping has a crispy outer layer and a succulent centre; the large prawns have a moreish umami flavour.

Name: Ghin Khao
Address: 2128 W. Cermak Rd., Chicago, IL, 60608, USA
Description: The name is Thai for “eat rice,” and you’ll want plenty of it to mop up every last bite of this kitchen's perfectly spicy, salty, sweet and tangy Northern Thai dishes. Operated by chef siblings, Nova and Kami Sasi, this is a fun, lively spot, with graffiti-like signage, hip-hop in the background, and colorful murals bedecking the walls. Every item is perfectly balanced, from the crunchy and subtly spiced fishcakes with cucumber-herb salad to the glorious nam khao tod, featuring crispy rice with ground chicken, pork skin, plenty of fresh ginger, cilantro and green onion.As a bonus, it’s also BYOB, so bring along a crew of friends with a couple of six-packs, and you'll be able to conquer most of the small menu—along with a few specials listed on the board.

Name: Giant
Address: 3209 W. Armitage Ave., Chicago, IL, 60647, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Vibrant and easy-going, this clever restaurant takes familiar dishes like onion rings and crab salad and drums them up with delicious twists and turns. Such is the appeal of this longtime favorite in Logan Square where friendly servers keep close watch in a petite space that is rustic in design and relaxed in feel. From the patio to the chef’s counter, the cooking is constant, rolling with the seasons and bringing just the right amount of flair to each and every dish. Past highlights include gorgeous jalapeno biscuits with maple butter, hearty beef cheek ravioli and fine tangles of tagliatelle paired with crab.

Name: Gigio
Description: A trattoria where à la carte dining is encouraged with a comprehensive menu of regional cuisines. Pici served with tomato ragú laden with garlic and vegetable sformato are all flavours learned in the Italian countryside. A marble bar counter and Tuscan-style stone walls create a stylish space inspired by interiors in Tuscany. Steps from Shoin Shrine, this is Italian food culture with deep roots in daily life.

Name: Gilt Bar
Address: 230 W. Kinzie St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
Description: Doughnuts, dry-aged steaks, and house-made pastas—Hogsalt Hospitality certainly has the lockdown on this corner of River North, but it all started in 2010 with this moody and imposing retreat. The bar up front mixes cocktails to a metronomic rhythm, while the back feels more intimate with studded leather banquettes and nostalgic lighting.True to form, the restaurant excels at big plates and bold flavors. We're hooked on the fried chicken that arrives with a golden-brown crust and rich mashed potatoes. But, who then will order the beef cheek pot pie with bone marrow gravy? You won’t have room for dessert, but order it anyway. A towering slice of carrot cake with spiced cream cheese frosting and toasted coconut counts as a vegetable anyway, right?

Name: Gim Nguan Noodle
Address: 75/70 Soi Chom Thong 16, Chom Thong Road, Bang Kho, Chom Thong, Bangkok, 10150, Thailand
Description: This hidden gem, tucked away in a Bangkok alley since 1999, excels in fish ball noodle soup. They offer fresh, umami-rich fish balls, al dente noodles, and a savoury, aromatic broth. Optional toppings like cheese and poached egg, along with large servings and ample condiments, provide great taste and value.

Name: Gina
Address: 92 Station Road, Chingford, E4 7BA, United Kingdom
Description: Chef and TV personality Ravneet Gill is behind this smart neighbourhood bistro, along with her chef husband Mattie Taiano – after whose late mother the restaurant is named. The menu has a meaty basis, with a daily blackboard of prime cuts being the star of the show. Everything is well-priced, prepared with care and swaps fuss for flavour, such as well-judged onglet with a creamy peppercorn sauce. The whole team bring personality and infectious enthusiasm to their work, helping to make a visit here such a lovely experience.

Name: Ginza HARU CHAN Ramen
Description: The chef, known to all as Haru-chan, pours all her energies into her shio ramen. The clear broth of pork and dried sardines is poured to the rim of the bowl. The colours of green onion, nori and wheat bran ‘flowers’ floating in wisps of pork fat make a comforting sight. Noodles are pounded flat for a satisfyingly plump texture. Roasted pork fillet, simmered with the soup, brings the whole dish together. To stay close to the community it serves, the restaurant remains open even between lunch and dinner times.

Name: Gion Yorozuya
Description: When Gion Yorozuya was founded, its focus was on meal deliveries to teahouses and playhouses. The restaurant thrived thanks to a favourable reception from geisha and maiko, and today guests queue up at the door well before opening time. The dish of renown is the onion udon. Eager to use Kyoto foodstuffs, the chef smothers his plates in Kujo spring onion. The three pillars of the cuisine that keeps customers coming back are tender noodles, dashi and onions. “Mari”, a dish larded with pickled plums, and “Tsunoda”, enhanced with chicken meat, are named for the celebrities who favour these ingredients.

Name: Girl & The Goat
Address: 809 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
Description: Girl & The Goat remains a lively and consistently busy restaurant, with a dining room that hums from open to close. The energetic atmosphere is matched by a warm and welcoming tone, even as the space fills with a mix of groups, families and regulars. Appropriately rustic wooden pillars and beams connect a warren of seating areas, from elevated platforms to banquettes to dim private corner nooks. The menu is organized by primary ingredients, including a dedicated section for goat, and reflects the kitchen's signature style of bold, shareable dishes. Flavors are direct and satisfying. The kitchen's willingness to offer smaller portions for solo diners is a truly thoughtful touch.

Name: Gitane
Address: Jan Pieter Heijestraat 146, Amsterdam, 1054 MK, Netherlands
Description: Gitane immediately catches the eye with its pavement terrace, where you can soak up the trendy vibe of the Oud-West neighbourhood, as well as its large round windows overlooking the street and attractive period features such as stained glass. The place has something of a 1970s feel. From 10am every day of the week, you can drop in and soak up the relaxed atmosphere. The Mediterranean dishes have an appealing touch of Ottolenghi about them, with rich flavours taking centre stage. Take the kebab, for example, combining minced lamb and beef with a Mediterranean blend of sumac, pickled red cabbage and smoked aubergine. Then there's exceptionally fresh fish, enlivened with kefir and a nuanced fish broth. A real feast! The chef makes sure that there are plenty of vegetarian and vegan options on the menu, and he keeps his prices affordable. One of Amsterdam's gems!

Name: Glaz
Address: 9 place de la République, Pont-Croix, 29790, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: On the village square, Glaz – a Breton word evoking the sea's shifting hues of green, blue, and grey – strikes a balance between old and new: wrought iron, earthenware and rugs sit alongside wood panelling, copper and plants. Tanios Nakhlé Cerruti presides in the kitchen; Émeline Macé oversees the dining room and wine cellar. Born in Saint-Malo to an Italian mother and Lebanese father, the chef draws on his heritage and his travels to craft precise fusion bistronomy dishes with their roots in French culinary tradition. The menu showcases local ingredients, many organic, skilfully elevated with spices.

Name: Glen Ellen Star
Address: 13648 Arnold Dr., Glen Ellen, CA, 95442, USA
Description: The setting is charmingly quaint, but don’t be fooled—this humble cottage boasts a serious culinary operation that draws in crowds rain or shine. The cozy space hinges around a wood-burning oven, which in turn serves as the springboard for a compact menu of compelling, inventive Californian cuisine overseen by Chef Ari Weiswasser. Biodynamic produce sourced from nearby Glentucky Family Farm is a mainstay, from wholesome, vibrantly fresh salads, to lightly charred, smoke-kissed roasted vegetables like sugar snap peas with truffle-chili cashew crunch. More substantial fare ranges from seasonal pizza and pasta, to whole roasted branzino and brick chicken—all of it worthy of attention. So, too, are house-made ice creams in flavors like vanilla maple bourbon.

Name: Glo Noodle House
Address: 4450 W. 38th Ave., Ste. 130, Denver, CO, 80212, USA
Description: The location in a run of the mill strip mall belies the cool interior at this spot named for Chef/owner Chris Teigland's mother. Inside, dark charcoal and dark wood are offset by pops of bright colors, while overhead, vibrant lanterns of different colors and sizes draw attention. The kitchen delivers serious flavor on their noodle/ramen-based menu. Kick off with a sweet and savory skewer of marinated tofu skewer served with a miso peach jam and an almond and sesame candy crumble. Ramen options run the gamut from miso bacon and brothless versions to the death wish designed for spice hounds who want the heat without sacrificing flavor. Sweets worth saving room for include the sweet crispy rice cake with smoked caramel and kasu-lime ice cream.

Name: Glorious Cuisine
Address: 31-33 Shek Kip Mei Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Lined by multi-tier fish tanks, the entrance showcases live seafood from around the world – Hokkaido scallops, Thai marble goby, even Hanasaki crab if you're lucky. Chicken dishes are another strong suit. To avoid disappointment, it's best to pre-order signatures such as double-boiled chicken soup with conpoy and Yunnan ham, braised chicken stuffed with abalone and sea cucumber, stock-poached leafy greens with chicken liver or chargrilled suckling pig.

Name: Glou Glou
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The distinctive sound of fine natural wine “glug glugging” into a glass is the hallmark of this friendly eatery. Let yourself be guided by the expert insights of the sommelier. The chef, for his part, showcases his personal take on contemporary tapas, mingling French, Asian and Italian influences with enthusiasm and generosity. Full-bodied soy flanks aubergine, while fresh, spicy kimchi jazzes up beef hanger steak without forgetting the irresistible lost bread. Everything is impossibly tempting –don’t forget to book!

Name: Glug
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant in the Eixample district of the city, this is a name you’ll definitely want to jot down. Located opposite the Sant Jordi swimming pool, Glug is much more than a hangout for foodies as wine also plays a prominent role here (hence its name). The couple in charge, chefs Iván Garcia and Beatrice Casella (the latter, a native of Turin, is responsible for the wonderful desserts), offer cuisine that is informal, does not follow any set rules, and is designed exclusively for enjoyment. The menu, featuring delicious dishes such as onion soup and “buttons” of Comté cheese, works with seasonal ingredients, combining aspects of Catalan and Italian cuisine in a highly interesting and creative way. They also offer a tasting menu!

Name: Go Benz
Address: 163 Krabi Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: The constantly busy Go Benz has been serving its speciality pork with peppery broth and rolled rice noodles for over 20 years – and it's easy to see why. Many of the dishes often sell out, like the fragrant dry boiled rice with crispy pork and tender pork offal. Also well worth ordering is the crispy pork with sweet soy sauce, which is seasoned wonderfully and has a lovely charcoal-grilled crust. No need to queue: arrive at opening, grab any free seat and staff will come to take your order.

Name: Goat
Address: 12 Wyndham Street, Auckland Central, Auckland, 1010, New Zealand
Description: At Goat, chef Sid Chopra has brought 20+ years of culinary expertise to the table. He updates traditional Indian recipes with modern techniques and personal touches. His refined street food delivers flavours that taste both familiar and surprising. His signature dish, The Goat, is slow-cooked caprine in spices and aromats, rendering deep flavours emblematic of Bihar. Round off with thandai tres leches, or sponge cake in saffron-infused milk.

Name: Goat On The Roof
Address: 1 Bridge Street, Newbury, RG14 5BE, United Kingdom
Description: A former bank is now this bright and airy restaurant where plenty of natural light floods in through the large windows. There's an understated elegance to the décor and the counter is the place to sit if you want to discuss the concise yet quality wine list with the enthusiastic team. The appealingly varied cooking offers sharing plates that draw inspiration from multiple sources but are rooted in the British larder. The fish 'gilda' snack is a prime example, offering plenty of flavour in the harmonious combination of trout, quail egg and smoked haddock.

Name: Golden Boy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set across from the Botanical Garden, Golden Boy is a local favorite for its distinctive take and modern interpretations of Thai cuisine. Don't worry, though, as the familiar flavors are still here as they level up dishes like the unmissable salt and pepper squid. While it's à la carte at lunch, evenings feature "Tuk Tuk" style, with the kitchen directing the meal. It's ideal for groups to mix and match, sampling a variety of dishes from a menu that makes decision-making difficult with so many tempting choices. The wraparound terrace is almost always packed and reservations are suggested, as it's full almost every time of day.

Name: Golden Dragon
Description: The Asian restaurant at the Grischa hotel serves a combination of Chinese and Japanese dishes. Tip: Some dishes are designed for sharing. If you fancy the Peking duck for two, which is absolutely to be recommended, be sure to pre-order (at least 48hr in advance). You also have the option of taking your pick of many of the ingredients and having them put together as you wish. The sleek, authentic design of the restaurant is also appealing.

Name: Golden Horseshoe Barbecue
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Golden Horseshoe Barbecue, run by mother-son duo Doris and Andrew Golden, was sparked by a passion for barbecue developed during the pandemic. It began as a series of pop-ups and has since moved to a brick-and-mortar space where Andrew smokes the meat and Doris deals in desserts and cornbread. This is true Texas-style barbecue, specializing in the holy trinity of brisket, ribs and sausage (if you happen to swing by on a Thursday, you'll be rewarded with pastrami, though). While all eyes are trained on the meat, sides like charro beans with jalapeños and cotija cheese, and cornbread slathered in cinnamon butter, are far from a second thought.

Name: Goldenes Bründl
Description: This popular place set right by the Goldenes Bründl cycle path basks in beautiful verdant surroundings. In summer, it is wonderful to eat alfresco on the terrace. The food is regional and made with excellent-quality seasonal ingredients, much of which comes sourced in the immediate vicinity. The dishes are straightforward and delicious – think "fried pike-perch fillet, chorizo-pumpkin risotto" or "Powidltascherl (Austrian dumpling), plum sorbet". As well as the à la carte menu, there is a three- to five-course set menu. The excellent wine list encompasses over 800 labels, with a particularly superb Austrian selection, although France and Italy are also well represented.

Name: Goldfish
Address: Galleria Mall, Al Wasl Road, Jumeirah 1, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Vibrant, modern Japanese dishes – from sushi, uni and yakitori to sharing plates and Wagyu steak – are the order of the day at this funky, buzzing spot located in a smart mall. Keep an eye out for the daily chef’s specials and nice selection of mocktails! Prices are more than reasonable, and service is bright and keen; sit at the counter to watch the chefs at work.

Name: Goldie
Description: This restaurant housed in the long-standing hotel Nautilus, right in the historical city centre, exudes a sophisticated bistro atmosphere that blends the charm of bygone eras with a touch of glamour. In summer, the terrace giving onto Žižkov Square is a real draw. Go à la carte menu or opt for a four- or six-course tasting menu; a four-course vegetarian variant is also available. There is an additional, wallet-friendly lunch menu. The chef's specialities include "Sturgeon & Umami", traditional kulajda mushroom soup and fillet steak Rossini. Tip: Be sure to visit the city's labyrinth of alleys and passages (both above and below ground) and its historical buildings.

Name: Goldie
Address: 128 Oliver Plunkett Street, Cork, T12 X5P8, Ireland
Description: What a terrific, buzzing little place this is. The compact space is filled to bursting with happy diners delighting in Goldie's inviting combination of sensibly priced cooking, electric atmosphere and friendly service. The daily menu is based around the latest catch from the Cork coastline, with the top-notch seafood used with a 'fin-to-gill' approach and often enlivened by an array of international influences. Hake tail schnitzel or pan-fried John Dory with chicory chutney are prime examples of the ethos, which yields delicious results.

Name: Goli
Description: Set within the former Goldberger textile factory, Goli refers to the nickname the locals gave to this historic building. It’s a small place with a simple terrace and a colourful, cramped interior, but it’s gloriously friendly and positive vibes simply pour out of the kitchen. Sit at the counter to talk with the chefs, who are eager to guide you through the menu of fresh, tasty Middle Eastern favourites, from warm pita, vibrant salads, and green beans with chilli and lemon, to charred entrecôte with tahini. Deliciously fruity soft drinks and cocktails complete your meal.

Name: Gombei
Description: Fans of Gombei think immediately of udon or soba with kitsune (deep-fried tofu), but certainly not with tanuki (deep-fried tempura pieces). The menu begins with udon, showing how popular it is. Two types of kitsune are available, one with chopped tofu, the other with tofu simmered in sweetened soy sauce. ‘Keiran’ is a warm udon dish topped with a starch sauce of soft scrambled eggs and ginger. Noodles are boiled soft to soak up the dashi. A taste of Kyoto, beloved of kabuki actors, geisha and maiko.

Name: Gommerstuba
Description: Diners are assured of a pleasantly informal atmosphere and great food at this little inn run by Yvonne and Lars Dederscheck on the outskirts of Niederernen. Their dishes are inspired by modern culinary trends and made using the freshest select ingredients. Think lukewarm char, celeriac, apple and horseradish, or duck breast, pulled duck leg, Jerusalem artichoke and kale. A fine à la carte selection is available, along with a three- to seven-course set menu and a three- or four-course vegetarian set menu s. Valais wines are recommended as an accompaniment. The welcoming interior has a contemporary feel – as well as an attractive stone-clad counter, there are pleasing decorative touches including some lovely paintings that are also available to purchase. Last but not least, the inviting terrace overlooks the Rhone Valley.

Name: Gomtang Lab
Address: 10F, Hyundai Department Store, 517 Teheran-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06164, South Korea
Description: Gomtang Lab, newly reopened on the 10th floor of Hyundai Department Store, is Chef Jeong-sik Lim’s secret base for exploring gomtang and other broth-based dishes. The signature collagen gomtang is simmered for over 10 hours with beef bones, tendons, shank, and tail, resulting in a rich, gelatinous depth of flavour. The menu is broad, ranging from tripe gomtang and clam gomtang to Pyongyang-style cold noodles and beef ramen. Ordering the set brings an array of sides, such as tofu with pollack roe, kimchi pancakes, and dumplings. The slow-cooked beef pairs well with traditional Korean liquors.

Name: Gondola Gondola
Description: Find Gondola Gondola smack dab in the heart of Adelaide. Inside, its wood accents and colorful neon signs transport guests to Southeast Asia, as does the menu, with a blend of traditional Thai and Vietnamese dishes. Everything, from the small plates, appetizers, main courses and sides, is meant to be shared. Order one from each category and you'll leave feeling satisfied. Enjoy Thai street food staples such as grilled pork skewers, green curry and pad Thai, or savor Vietnamese favorites like banh xeo, a pasta dish packed with vegetables. Don't miss the Thai milk tea tiramisu, an intriguing twist on the Italian classic with Genoise sponge cake soaked in Thai milk tea with mascarpone cheese.

Name: Gong De Lin (West Nanjing Road)
Address: 445 West Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: When you see that sweet and sour pork and fried shredded eel are on the menu you may doubt if the food is truly vegan but fear not – all the mock-meat and fish is made with either veggies, soy product or mushrooms. This institution of Shanghainese vegan cooking has been serving plant-based dishes in disguise since 1922. Its annexed shop now sells cake and snacks freshly made in-house, such as the tasty mugwort rice dumplings.

Name: Gong Zhou · Ba Shu Wei Yuan
Address: No. 6, 64 Junlong Street, Jinjiang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: Gong Zhou was the ancient name of Chongqing, the home municipality of the owner and kitchen team. Since opening in a residential area next to Taikoo-li shopping hub in 1998, it has kept its fans coming back for its Chongqing dishes, such as "auspicious" home-style fish – blanched grass carp dressed in a tangy sauce made with spicy bean sauce, pickled chilli and ginger. Try the pork ribs coated in spiced ground rice, stuffed in pork tripe and steamed.

Name: Gongkham
Address: 259/22-23 Mu 1, Rim Tai, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
Description: Around 30 minutes from downtown Chiang Mai, this Lanna-style wooden house with a warm, relaxed vibe offers a peaceful escape that feels like dining at a local friend's home. Outdoor seating without air conditioning is ideal for enjoying the cool air. The menu sticks to local classics, from Kaeng Khae and Nam Prik Noom with deep-fried pork liver to Cho Phak Kat. Cooked to order, the dishes are simply presented, allowing the Northern Thai flavours to shine.

Name: Good Good Culture Club
Description: Stroll into this lush, happening spot and your eyes will quickly fall on neon blue letters scrawled above the lively open kitchen: "did you eat yet?" The correct answer is "no": an empty stomach will be amply rewarded by the vibrantly flavorful cooking here. Southeast Asian flavors find unique Californian expressions in dishes like a signature orange-mango glazed fried chicken wing filled with chicken egg roll stuffing, or a Lao-style sausage with tangy pasilla pepper jaew. A version of halo halo, featuring mango jellies, shiso shaved ice and seasonal fruit, is a particular treat. Reservations go quickly during peak hours, but if you walk in early (or late), you may find a perch to dine at the bar, where you'll also find an array of creative, tropically inflected cocktails—a match made in paradise.

Name: Good Thief
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Described as the rebellious younger sibling to next-door Anh and Chi, this lively bar and restaurant offers a more freewheeling, inventive take on Vietnamese cuisine, matched with equally inspired cocktails. The compact menu comprises small plates ideal as bar snacks, like juicy binchotan-grilled skewers, or impeccably fried, crunchy frog legs anointed with torn mint and a seductive sweet-tangy sauce glaze, as well as more substantial plates like humble garlic noodles enhanced with morsels of Dungeness crab. The excitement continues into dessert, as in a layered mousse cake featuring banana, peanut and Thai chili, paired with coconut sorbet and fish sauce caramel. Whatever you do, don’t miss out on the brilliant drinks—many of which can be made spirit-free.

Name: Goodbye Horses
Address: 21 Halliford Street, Islington, London, N1 3HB, United Kingdom
Description: There’s so much going for this former pub which has been transformed into a wine bar and restaurant with a young, on-trend vibe. The place is packed with East London’s coolest diners, many of them at shared tables and all delighting in a concise menu based around high-quality, seasonal British produce. The treacle tart makes for a wonderful end to the meal – and if your sweet tooth is still not satisfied, the same people run The Dreamery ice cream shop across the road. The eclectic wine list specialises in natural options, which the affable and knowledgeable team will happily guide you through.

Name: Gordo's Cantina
Address: 140 St. Nicholas Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11237, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There are some places that truly reflect the heart and soul of a neighborhood, and in Bushwick, it's Gordo's Cantina. Family-friendly and with something for everyone, this spot's name also ensures that portion sizes are mighty. Of course, nobody is complaining, thanks to the talents of Chef Reyna Morales, who hails from Mexico City and whose careful handling of familiar favorites goes a long way.Order the tacos tucked with crumbles of aromatic chorizo with a mild heat, while the chile relleno stuffed with creamy queso fresco and beans is a savory delight. This hangout also dishes out a satisfying mole, as seen in enchiladas stuffed with tender shredded chicken.

Name: Gorkhali Kitchen
Address: 10044 Cross Creek Blvd., Tampa, FL, 33647, USA
Description: Take the short drive from downtown for a taste of Himalayan cuisine at Gorkhali Kitchen. The mirrored glass exterior means the interior is kept a secret until you're through the door but come inside to experience this place's warm hospitality.The menu is large with a Nepalese focus along with some Indian elements. Of course, there must be momo, those iconic Nepalese dumplings that are seared, pan-fried or even in jhol (soup). Chili momo filled with chicken is tossed in a fiery sauce that's not for the faint of heart. Sweet at the start, the heat builds and then finishes with a very spicy kick—perfect for heat seekers. Chicken is a popular protein that appears often on the menu, but don't shy away from the goat specialties. They're falling-off-the-bone tender and savory.

Name: Gosari Express
Description: Tucked beneath a red awning in Sindang-dong Jungang Market, Gosari Express stands out among the neighbourhood’s long-established eateries. With the motto 'Vegetarian every day', it takes a playful approach to plant-based dining. Every dish features the restaurant’s signature gosari oil sauce, from spicy bibim noodles to Taiwanese pancakes topped with sweet and tangy gosari chilli sauce. This inventive spot demonstrates the boundless potential of gosari.

Name: Gostilna Francl
Description: With the castle of Celje dominating the valley and the river close by, this inn has been reborn with a cuisine of traditional character, played out through clean flavours and contemporary technique. Meats sourced mainly from nearby farms lie at the heart of the offering: venison is a constant presence on the menu, alongside dishes such as truffle carpaccio and less celebrated cuts including lamb and veal shank. The wine list is predominantly Slovenian, with select forays into Italy and a dedicated section of distinguished vintage labels.

Name: Gostilna Mahorčič
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: An unmissable restaurant in a small village in the beautiful Karst region, with a classic, beautifully kept dining room with the intimate feel of a private lounge. The owners here are friendly and welcoming and keen to showcase the best of their region. With enthusiasm and expertise, skilful owner-chef Ksenija Krajšek Mahorčič adds a personal, technical touch to Slovenian ingredients, resulting in dishes of the highest quality. Among the appetisers, the puffed wild garlic chip topped with a sea bass cream made from fish scraps shows her hands-on approach to using every part of the ingredient. Also recommended is the roast lamb served with cider made from home-grown apples and a garlic potato mash. Don’t forget to leave space for one of the exquisite desserts, such as the refreshing and delicious yogurt mousse with elderberry ice cream. The same care and attention to detail is found on the wine list.

Name: Gostilna Rajh
Address: Soboška ulica 32, Bakovci, Murska Sobota, 9000, Slovenia
Description: It is the fifth generation that now confidently stewards this small gem, one of the most interesting restaurants in the region. The cuisine is deeply rooted in the territory, reread with modern accents and elevated by raw materials of great quality, handled at times with elegance, at others with a more rustic touch.
