Description: Take the door on the left to a chic, cosmopolitan restaurant specialising in delicious fish and seafood. Or choose the door on the right for the more relaxed brasserie, where an extensive menu of boldly flavoured dishes – featuring plenty of fish – delivers on quality. The range includes classic cuisine and Mediterranean- or Asian-inspired creations. A pristine cod fillet with mashed potatoes and a beurre blanc, a generous bento box featuring sashimi and sushi, or vegetarian tortellini? The choice is yours!

Name: Kolae
Address: 6 Park Street, Borough Market, London, SE1 9AB, United Kingdom
Description: The cuisine of southern Thailand provides the inspiration for this bustling restaurant in the equally bustling Borough Market. It’s an extremely popular place and rightly so, with attractive pricing, efficient service and downright delicious cooking. The menu lends itself to sharing and each dish is packed with flavour, from the terrific snacks such as grilled mussel skewers or crispy prawn heads with nahm jim sauce, to the lip-tingling curries. If you can’t decide, opt for the set menu to share – which is also available in a vegan form.

Name: Kolun.h
Address: 110/1 Mahannop Road, Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Renowned for Hainanese-style rice noodles, Kolun.h has been serving locals since 1997. The signature dish comes with rich or clear broth, braised pork, radish and crispy pork belly. Don't miss the peppery-flavoured goat meat in an aromatic herb soup. Expect long queues at peak times.

Name: Komah
Address: Rua Cônego Vicente Miguel Marino 378, São Paulo, 01135-020, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The Komah restaurant is renowned for its Korean cuisine with a contemporary touch – a combination of traditional recipes, signature dishes and international culinary techniques. The chef here ensures a unique gastronomic experience that challenges the palate through a panoply of flavours, with a full range from spicy to sweet. The concise menu features ten savoury dishes and three desserts, as well as a tasting option created personally by the chef. Dishes include “yukhoe”, a Korean steak tartare with cured egg yolk and Asian pear, “japchae” (sweet potato pasta with assorted vegetables and honey), and “kimchi bokumbap” with omelette, the house's signature dish, featuring rice sautéed with kimchi with a creamy omelette.

Name: Komal
Address: 3655 S. Grand Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90007, USA
Description: In the bustling Mercado Del Paloma, Chef Fátima Juárez runs this little stall specializing in corn. Heirloom varieties sourced from Mexico and nixtamalized in-house form the heart of the menu. A quesadilla lined with squash blossoms and sweet corn bound with melty quesillo earns top marks. Golden-fried plantain balls set in a smoky black mole is another accomplished winner. From tlacoyas topped with cactus to tacos lined with short rib, be liberal with the salsa for extra punch and power.

Name: Kombu to Men Kiichi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: A fifth-generation kombu merchant turns his hand to ramen, hoping people will rediscover the appeal of kombu. Guests are first invited to taste cold-brewed infusions of three types of kombu: Rishiri, Makombu and Rausu, in that order. Oboro kombu shaved before their eyes offers another point of interest. Bringing these umami-rich flavours together, the “Kombu Ramen” is a bowl where Japan’s dashi culture meets ramen, a national favourite.

Name: Komedokoro Inamoto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The proprietor loves rice, so he named his establishment ‘Komedokoro’, meaning ‘Place of Rice’. Taste the freshly-cooked white rice and you’ll understand why it’s so famous. Dishes are served on small plates, encouraging you to try a variety. Order the platter of side dishes and you’re sure to eat more than intended. The chef sources seafood and citrus fruits from his native Ehime. Sake and nibbles served at this ‘place of rice’ vary by the day.

Name: Komfort
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An interesting option (with a name that pays homage to the current trend for comfort food) despite its location away from Calp’s main tourist haunts. Its facilities are part of the gastro-boutique Cook Book hotel and feature a modern bistro-style dining room with large picture windows, bare tables of differing heights, plus countless lamps which define its personality. Enjoy highly varied traditional and international cuisine, including delicious pizzas, cocas (a type of flatbread), grilled and rice dishes, plus a superb steak tartare. A tasting menu option is also available.

Name: Koneser Grill
Description: The Koneser Grill's location is one of its many appealing qualities, set inside the Centrum Praskie Koneser, an old vodka distillery that has been transformed into a mini walled village where apartments, shops, art venues and a museum now sit beside one another. The restaurant comes from the same owners as Butchery & Wine, and its grill-centric menu offers a range of steaks aged in-house served with textbook sauces, but everything on the list – from the salad to the ikejime fish – is equally enjoyable. Sharing provides the best value experience and the chefs aim to use every part of the ingredients for minimal waste.

Name: Konjiki Hototogisu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the second floor of the Mall of the Emirates is this very likeable restaurant which is a slightly simplified version of the original with the same name in Tokyo. Here, the menu offers ramen, including the signature shoyu ramen, along with other classic Japanese dishes: gyoza, tempura, and kushiyaki such as chicken skewers with yakitori and sesame sauce. End the meal with a light and sweet matcha mochi accompanied by coconut ice cream. Booking isn’t possible, but service starts before noon and there is usually space available at the counter.

Name: Konoba Malo Selo
Description: Situated near Buje, Konoba Malo Selo is an authentic Istrian tavern where genuine flavors of local tradition come alive. The interiors reinforce this authenticity: stone walls, rustic furnishings, and a commanding fireplace create a warm, inviting atmosphere. During the meal, the aromas of the grill, truffle, and mushrooms permeate the room enhancing the pleasure of dining. Don’t miss the house-made charcuterie, fuži with boscarino sauce, and excellent grilled meats.

Name: Konoba Mate
Description: In the small village of Pupnat, some ten kilometres from Korčula, this intimate family-run tavern has welcomed guests with warmth and authenticity since 2000. The whole family is involved in the running of the establishment, bringing forth a cuisine that celebrates natural flavours and tradition, reinterpreted with a contemporary touch. The menu is built around the property’s own produce: house-made charcuterie, goat’s cheeses aged on site, vegetables from the kitchen garden, local olive oil and wines. Among the most appreciated dishes, the handmade ravioli filled with goat’s cheese and served with a fragrant sage sauce, stand out. The covered terrace, lit by lanterns, with large solid wooden tables that invite convivial dining, is a particularly evocative setting.

Name: Konoba Pescaria
Description: Directly overlooking the small harbour of one of Kvarner's most romantic villages, from its small terrace this venue enjoys a splendid view: small boats, beach and sea compose a relaxing and evocative picture. As is natural, the cuisine is predominantly seafood, simple and tasty. What could be better than to start with a carpaccio of the catch of the day and then follow it up with scampi alla busara, a preparation that apparently originated in these very areas? Prices are generally fair, except, understandably, for the finest shellfish.

Name: Konoba Vinko
Description: As soon as you sit down – either on the terrace at the front of the building or in the well-kept dining room – you’re instantly aware of just how many customers are having something from the rotisserie. So don’t hesitate and go for the house specialty: the deliciously sweet suckling pig, along with some homemade fried potatoes. The menu offers plenty of other delights, such as veal risotto – and the cheese and ham plates are a great way to start. The restaurant is run with confidence and efficiency and there’s a palpable sense of authenticity to everything. Furthermore, the prices are terrific, which only adds to its popularity, so booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Koral
Address: Rua Barão Da Torre, 446, Rio de Janeiro, 22411-002, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Just a few metres from the Nossa Senhora da Paz park, in the heart of Ipanema, there is a restaurant that keeps winning new devotees — and with good reason, as it has Pedro Coronha at the helm, considered one of the most outstanding chefs on the contemporary Brazilian culinary scene. His credentials speak for themselves: he trained at some of the world's great establishments — in both Lisbon and Copenhagen — and has been recognised as one of the most promising young chefs in all of Latin America. In its dining room, with its modern feel and open kitchen, you can savour a cuisine that, without neglecting the meat dishes and delicious homemade pastas, gives special pride of place to fish and seafood — Grilled prawns, Catch of the day à la meunière, Chargrilled octopus — celebrating the art of smoking and live-fire cooking. What did we love most? The truth is, we were thoroughly delighted by one dessert in particular: a fantastic warm, flaky cheesecake served with guava and cheese ice cream.

Name: Kotori
Address: Rua Cônego Eugênio Leite, 639, São Paulo, 05414-011, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
Description: An innovative dining option in the trendy Pinheiros district of the city. The focus here is very much on Japanese culture, with cuisine inspired by yōshoku cooking which reinterprets Western-style dishes to Asian tastes. Chef Thiago Bañares offers just a single menu option, albeit with a cutting-edge touch and one that includes Brazilian ingredients in his dishes. The latter include a selection of hot options, such as the Eryngil mushrooms, which is combined with chicken broth, tucupi and mustard seeds, plus matured fish cooked on the grill. It’s worth saving space at the end of your meal for the “rabanada de shokupan”, a bread dessert served with a milk ice cream and toffee syrup. To round off the experience to the full, choose from the list of classic and creative cocktails, or the interesting array of sakes.

Name: Kotuwa
Address: New Bahru, #01-03, 46 Kim Yam Road, 239351, Singapore
Description: Moved to this spot in 2024, Kotuwa is named after the CBD of Colombo. From quintessential Sri Lankan street food to curries, every bite is loaded with big flavours. Seafood is their strong suit, especially crab prepared in myriad ways. With its balanced, layered flavours and the subtle warmth of cinnamon, the crab curry really stands out. Hoppers – crispy pancakes made with fermented rice – are perfect for mopping up the delicious curry sauce.

Name: Krachang Khao Lak
Address: 78/155 Mu, 5 Lam Kaen, Thai Mueang, Phang Nga, 82210, Thailand
Description: At a breezy, rustic location with a laid-back tropical atmosphere and modern edge, this seafood-forward restaurant serves fresh, mostly live catch in à la carte dishes that showcase natural flavours. The daily specials board highlights the day's top picks. Don't miss the aromatic shrimp-coconut soup with melinjo leaves or the turmeric-marinated grilled giant trevally, a rare local fish. Honest, warm service rounds off this relaxed, seaside-style experience.

Name: Kricket
Address: 12 Denman Street, Soho, London, W1D 7HH, United Kingdom
Description: Kricket now boasts four branches across London, but this Soho spot was its original permanent home after its pop-up origins. The counter in front of the open kitchen dominates the room and is huge fun, although the seating downstairs has something of a cool nighttime vibe. The generously priced menu leans towards India’s more southerly states in authentic dishes that burst with flavour. Highlights to look out for include Goan sausage croquettes, Keralan fried chicken with a delicious curry leaf mayo, and succulent Karnatakan pork neck.

Name: Krispels Genusstheater
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Krispel family's estate presents an appealing contrast between old and new architecture, with the Genusstheater and strikingly stylish winery forming an interesting whole. Both the attractive restaurant and the lovely courtyard terrace are inviting. The flavoursome cuisine is based on carefully sourced regional ingredients, including organic Mangalitsa pork from the family's own pigs. The impressive wine list comprises over 600 labels, with the estate's own wines naturally among the recommendations. Service is attentive and professional. A tasting menu is also served three days a week. It is worth checking the events calendar for seasonal specials, too.

Name: Krone
Description: The past retains its fascinating appeal in this traditional restaurant situated in a small mountain village, where modern trends are ignored in favour of authentic dishes from the South Tyrol. Originally opened as an inn, the restaurant still offers a few simple and discreet rooms furnished in traditional style, as well as a new and modern sauna.

Name: Krone Hittisau
Description: The town-centre hotel, Krone Hittisau, dates back to 1838. Today, the restaurant on its first floor serves regional and seasonal cuisine. Fantastic ingredients are showcased in delicious dishes such as fillet of char with coriander lentils, ginger and lemon foam, and ricotta gnocchi. Diners can also look forward to charming and attentive service in a thoroughly inviting setting. The tasteful blend of clean lines and warm wood finishings (all the lovely furniture is made by carpenters from the Bregenz Forest) can be found both in the guestrooms and the restaurant.

Name: Krua Apsorn (Dusit)
Address: 503-505 Sam Sen Road, Wachira Payaban, Dusit, Bangkok, 10300, Thailand
Description: This family-run stall is inevitably a hit with anyone who eats here, including patrons such as the Thai royal family. The simplicity of the exterior belies the gem of a Thai kitchen hidden inside. Some dishes are unique and feature the family's secret recipes. The stir-fried pork with bird's-eye chilli is tender and bursting with herbal aromas. The signature yellow curry with large prawns and crispy lotus root strikes the perfect blend of sour, spicy and sweet.

Name: Krua Baan Platong
Address: 167/1 Mu 5, Thepkrasattri Road, Si Sunthon, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: A rewarding local food hunt away from the tourist hubs, it occupies a townhouse with an open-air garden setting. The home-style cooking feels deeply authentic and rooted in local tradition. Quality local ingredients are used to produce intensely flavoured dishes that capture the essence of Phuket. Highlights include stir-fried banana stalk with plump shrimps and shrimp paste, and melt-in-your-mouth steamed pork belly with their signature southern Thai budu dipping sauce. Advance planning is essential, with both booking and pre-ordering strongly recommended to ensure a smooth visit.

Name: Krua Jay Sim
Address: 98/17 Mu 2, Soi Khun Kaeo 12, Khun Kaeo, Nakhon Chai Si, Nakhon Pathom, 73120, Thailand
Description: Four times in a decade, this Thai restaurant changed locations before finally opening on the chef-owner’s land in Nakhon Pathom. Each time, regulars followed along for its flavoursome local dishes, including some, like stir-fried sesbania with shrimp paste, that cannot be found elsewhere. The current digs are in an open-air pavilion on a country lane with tranquil lotus pond views. Try the stir-fried pork loin with jaew sauce and the spicy mackerel soup with madan fruit.

Name: Krua Kao Kuk
Address: 47/4-5 Phatthana Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The legacy of the original roadside stall lives on, thanks to the owner's granddaughter. Famous for its boiled rice with fish, this humble restaurant also serves a variety of other home-style dishes that are worth trying. The quality is clear in these bold-flavoured plates. The deep-fried meatballs, made to a family recipe, are a great start to the meal and go well with the fresh fish menu, which is cooked in a traditional Phuket style.

Name: Krua Khun Nid
Address: 64 Soi Nonnivet 1, Udon Dussadi Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: For over four decades, this restaurant has been a mainstay for locals. Focusing on freshwater fish and meat, it serves generous sharing portions. Seasonal options and occasional fish specials accompany typical Isan dishes and local specialities, including om sai taek, an aromatic herbal soup. Enduring classics, such as the flavourful deep-fried pla som and snakehead fish in flavoursome tom yam soup, are also worth trying. The friendly staff are happy to share their recommendations.

Name: Krua Laew Tae R-Rom
Address: 17/62 Mu 6, Paniad Chang Road, Pattaya, Na Kluea, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: With a limited menu, the kitchen excels in seafood, Thai food and home-made curries with bold, rich flavours. The crab, shrimp, clams and fish are served ultra-fresh at reasonable prices, with rare catches often appearing on the menu. The restaurant doesn't open if the line-catch on that day is not successful. Booking a week in advance is necessary.

Name: Krua Luang Ten
Address: 160 Mu 2, Phet Kasem Road, Khuekkhak, Takua Pa, Phang Nga, 82190, Thailand
Description: Krua Luang Ten makes for an unusual setting with its tables arranged on sand-covered floors. Check the whiteboard for the specials, which often feature the catch of the day and seasonal ingredients. The dishes masterfully balance robust Southern Thai flavours for authentic spiciness, and the complimentary vegetables come with tai pla sauce. As everything is cooked to order, it's best to place your full order at the outset. The restaurant is closed on the 10th, 20th, and 30th of the month.

Name: Krua Praya
Address: 216/19 Mu 3, Soi Hua Tha 1, Si Sunthon, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Krua Praya showcases Southern Thai, especially Phuket, cuisine. The menu features skilfully prepared dishes with bold flavours and enticing aromas. The standout pork belly dishes include the signature fried pork belly with curry paste and young coconut shoots, delivering a crispy, spicy delight. Alternatively, the Phuket-style stew offers a rich non-spicy option, served in a satisfying gravy. The food is cooked to order, so please expect to wait.

Name: Krua Suwimol
Address: 1229/9 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This simple, open-air restaurant serves Thai-Chinese fare. The food is distinctive for its simply cooking techniques yet quality dishes with extra-fresh ingredients and intense flavours. They offer a fantastic range, including several seafood and made-to-order options. Deep-fried chicken thigh with fish sauce and stir-fried spicy seafood are recommended.

Name: Kruk
Address: 213 Blenheim Grove Peckham, London, SE15 4QL, United Kingdom
Description: Enter into this railway-arch restaurant in Peckham Rye and you could convince yourself you’ve been transported to Bangkok. A pair of friends have turned their years of experience in Thai restaurants into an authentic slice of the country, from the bustling atmosphere to fresh, vibrant dishes like fried chicken ‘gai prik’. The chefs don’t hold back on the spice, yet their strong sense of balance ensures the central ingredients are never overwhelmed. Meat-free diners will be particularly delighted that every dish on the menu is matched by a vegetarian equivalent.

Name: Kuhara
Description: The friendly couple who run Kuhara—the chef a disciple of Japanese cuisine, the proprietress a welcoming figure in kappo wear—make us instantly feel at home. The signature fare is duck. In addition to salt-grilled duck, they offer chilled breast stew in summer, and a hot duck stew called jibuni in winter. Dried baby fish with soy and pepper on rice and Kokusho miso soup of root vegetables are must-try items. Unripe pepper is gathered by the couple and their children when they visit her hometown in Tochigi Prefecture. Kokusho miso soup brings back memories for the chef, who sampled it when he applied to a restaurant specialising in shojin ryori.

Name: Kulturhof Stanggass - Gasthaus
Description: The Gasthaus, which annexes the Kulturhof Stanggass located on the road between Bischofswiesen and Berchtesgaden, offers a culinary alternative to the restaurant Solo Du. Done out in light wood, the minimalist-style interior has a modern yet cosy feel. The glass façade affords views of the garden, which includes a children's playground. Book a spot at the "Stammtisch", a long handmade wooden table for 25 diners. The menu draws on the region and nature's bounty – the ingredients are locally sourced. The good food is complemented by friendly service.

Name: Kumba
Address: 92 Aguirre Avenue, BF Homes, Parañaque - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: With warm lighting, rattan chandeliers and wooden furnishings, this street-side restaurant offers a warm welcome. The chef, inspired by her mother's recipes and time working at a Chinese restaurant in Singapore, serves nuanced dishes from China, the Philippines, Taiwan and Japan. Seasonal specials appear often, so do ask. The cuapao ni cristina – fluffy buns with tender pork, crispy pig skin, peanuts and coriander – is a heartfelt, flavour-packed signature.

Name: Kung Fu Little Steamed Buns Ramen
Address: 811 Eighth Ave., New York, NY, 10019, USA
Description: Set among the neon lights of the Theater District, this gem is always packed. Everyone is here for the on-point cooking, though the friendly staff and an endearing, cartoon-style mural featuring diners enjoying the food are a close second. Hand-pulled and hand-cut noodles are stir-fried with mouthwatering accompaniments, while the dumpling variety is so great it’s almost impossible to pick. Herb-spiked pork and shrimp wonton soup is well worth the 20-minute wait, allowing diners plenty of time to devour pan-fried Peking duck bundles, scallion pancakes stuffed with sliced beef or even steamed buns full of mushroom.

Name: Kung Fu Shanghai Fish Ball
Address: 380 Zhongmei Street, West District, Taichung, Taiwan Region
Description: The push cart out front turns back the clock and the retro vibe is pursued indoors. For over 10 years, the owner-chef has been making fish balls, wontons and sauces from scratch. He orders his noodles from his favourite shop in Shuinan Market because of their bouncy texture. Purists should try noodles tossed in scallion oil for its simple, but addictive aromas. Marlin fish ball soup with salted potherb mustard is another best-seller.

Name: Kung Wo Beancurd Factory
Address: 118 Pei Ho Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Since 1893, this much-loved shop has been making its own tofu that exudes a deep, rich soy aroma. The tofu pudding is a must-try. With murals that depict tofu being made, the room is styled to attract a younger crowd.

Name: Kushi-Ya
Address: 14a Low Pavement, Nottingham, NG1 7DL, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Head through the arch of Enfield Chambers and you'll be transported to this uber-cool setting. The Japanese cooking revolves around small plates and skewers, cooked over a charcoal grill with consummate skill. Bright, authentic and generous, each dish is a joy to eat and sensibly priced too. If you're coming for lunch, get here early as they don't take bookings and the lunchtime offer is phenomenally good value. Efficient service, a dynamic atmosphere and a courtyard terrace all add to the already considerable appeal.

Name: Kushikatsu Gojoya
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The tempo in the kitchen is lively as cooks deep-fry these imaginative skewers. Order the omakase, which only ends when your belly is full. An amazing 25 types of skewers are normally available—you’ll want to see them all. Korean kimchi, Indian curry, Italian tomato sauce and so on take you on a journey from country to country. A fusion of Osaka’s fried foods with traditional cuisines of the world.

Name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodles
Address: Shop E, 1 Wing Lung Street, Cheung Sha Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: It’s inside a local market but easy to spot, thanks to the big yellow sign. Watch the kitchen at work through the glass wall as noodles are made the traditional way – with the chef seesawing on a bamboo pole to painstakingly knead the egg-rich dough for that stringy texture. Secret techniques are deployed to remove the soapy taste of lye and accentuate the eggy flavour. Don’t miss the signature noodles tossed in shrimp roe and oyster sauce.

Name: Kwan Kee Clay Pot Rice (Queen's Road West)
Address: Shop 1, GF, Wo Yick Mansion, 263 Queen's Road West, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: Its red sign, basic interior and traditional stir-fries all point to an authentic Hong Kong food experience. Claypot rice is only served at night and takes time to prepare, so order it first as soon as you’re seated. The three-rice blend results in a chewy texture and appealing fragrance; the bottom crust is always perfectly scorched. The white eel variety is especially popular; pair it with claypot dishes with excellent wok hei.

Name: Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-20, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: Though this stall is famous for incredibly sweet fish porridge and fried fish bee hoon, the fish head soup is also a crowd pleaser. Mackerel head is chopped and pre-fried, then cooked à la minute in a broth with scallion.

Name: Kwee Heng
Address: Newton Food Centre, #01-13, 500 Clemenceau Avenue North, 229495, Singapore
Description: With over 50 years of history, Kwee Heng makes boneless braised duck that is tender, juicy and flavoursome; it can be served with rice, congee or noodles. Other dishes such as Hainanese chicken and char siew are also available.

Name: Kwestia Czasu / NAGO
Description: Sitting within a residential district, but in walking distance from the city centre, this cosy bistro is tied together with a nod to nature and the vast forests of Podlaskie. The dining room is decorated in earthy shades from brown to terracotta, while branches and wood elements complete the effect. Flatbreads are a feature on the sensibly priced menu, which also includes the likes of saffron milk-cap mushrooms with an intense consommé or tender, subtly gamey roe deer – the overarching principle is quality ingredients treated with the care they deserve.

Name: Kyewol
Description: Located near hip Seongsu, this restaurant specializes in Korean-style chicken gomtang and has become especially popular with younger diners. Gently cooked chicken breast is served over warm rice with blanched young napa cabbage, then finished with a clear, refined broth for a clean yet deeply savory flavor. At lunch, diners can enjoy reasonably priced side dishes such as spicy chicken salad and torch-grilled chicken with doenjang, while cold noodles are available in the summer.

Name: Kyodaiya
Description: When one can hear the dull tap of a blade against a wooden board every time a customer places an order, it’s a telltale sign that the chefs are serious about their craft. At Kyodaiya, that craft is Sanuki udon. The thick noodles are always cut to order to preserve their characteristic elasticity and smoothness until the very last minute. In addition to the classic kake udon, flavored with dried and smoked sardines and seasoned with light soy sauce, the chef brothers also offer classics like tempura udon and chilled bukkake udon.

Name: Kyogoku Kaneyo
Description: This eel restaurant has been in business for seven generations, dating back to the Meiji period. Every day finds the shop crowded with customers, many seeking its signature dish of ‘Kinshi Don’: rice covered in dipping sauce and topped with Edo-style eel and a large Kyoto-style omelette. What makes this east-west marriage of flavours work so well is the dipping sauce, a staple since the restaurant’s inception. The Kanto-style kabayaki, which involves steaming eel before grilling and dipping it in sauce, is a technique from a cook recruited from Tokyo during the founder’s generation. In both looks and taste, Kyogoku Kaneyo bears traces of Japan’s east and west.

Name: Kyomachibori Nakamura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: A tonkatsu set menu allows diners to compare the flavours of different varieties of brand-name pork. The chef first presents the day's selection of meat, which is then deep-fried slowly in lard at a low temperature to draw out its natural sweetness and aroma. The tasting starts with the mild tenderloin, progressing to more richly flavoured cuts such as the shoulder and loin. Each cut is served by the slice, a welcome touch that allows guests to savour the meat while it is piping hot. Other fried dishes, such as prawns and minced-pork cutlets, are also tempting.

Name: Kyorakutei
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The queue forms before the doors open. The reason for Kyorakutei’s popularity is the extensive menu, with drinks and snacks to sample between bites of soba. It’s great to visit any time, whether day or evening. Tempura choices are also abundant, and guests can order combination platters or individual items according to preference. Buckwheat is sourced from the chef’s native Aizu, with a focus on delivering the flavour of cold inaka soba (thick soba made with whole buckwheat) with a pleasing finish. Tomato soba, the early summer speciality, is worth waiting for.

Name: Kàran Bistró
Address: Plaza de la Constitución 1, Pozoblanco, 14400, Spain
Description: In this restaurant, located in the heart of the Los Pedroches valley, they like to say that “you don’t just come here to eat, but also to have fun”. In this intimate and attractive setting, the high level of cuisine comes as a pleasant surprise. The cooking is completely centred on the renowned local Iberian pork, including the finest cuts of acorn-fed ham (pluma, presa etc) as well as produce from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. Chef Carlos Fernández is committed to showcasing the best possible flavours from the local area on a modern à la carte complemented by two excellent set menus: De Temporada and Nuestra Dehesa.

Name: Küisine (West)
Address: 1, Lane 24, Mofan Street, West District, Taichung, Taiwan Region
Description: This unpretentious joint, tucked away in a residential alley, feels homely and relaxing. Each guest is expected to order at least one set menu with a main, rice, and either soup or drinks. The Taichungese rice works well with Taiwanese, Southeast Asian and Japanese dishes. Popular mains include Kung Pao chicken with cashew nuts or golden curry omelette. Everything is sourced and certified from small local farms.

Name: L'800
Description: Period furniture, regional cuisine and a cheerful ambience are some of the characteristics of this old farmhouse which is named after the 1800s when it was built. Some of the ingredients used, such as snails and frogs’ legs, may come as a surprise: the restaurant specialises in these unusual delicacies, even offering a tasting menu totally dedicated to snails.

Name: L'AMITIE
Description: Apprenticing at a bistro in Paris, the chef was captivated by its lively energy. At L'AMITIE, he has put down roots in Takadanobaba with this intimate diner where you can feel like part of the daily life of France. Offerings include meat terrine À la campagne, cassoulet and beef cheek simmered in red wine. À la carte items are prepared for two, so you can enjoy sharing. Savour Gallic culinary culture and the ambience of the French countryside.

Name: L'AO - L'Aigle d'Or
Description: This family-run establishment with its pleasant, recently renovated contemporary interior continues to fete local produce and tradition (think: Alsace head cheese, frogs' legs, chicken cordon bleu with bargkass)… but the younger generation is coaxing it into the modern era with more contemporary recipes and presentation. Expect flavour, indulgence and attentive service! Well-maintained guestrooms make this the perfect place to stay, too.

Name: L'AS
Description: Simple yet refined fare, enjoyed in a casual setting. Keen to make French cuisine familiar to his clientele, the chef offers great taste at a reasonable price. Guests can enjoy their meals as if they were gathered around their own dinner tables. The chef changes the menu monthly, greeting diners with something different each time they visit. Cooks also bring dishes to tables for a seamlessly integrated dining experience.

Name: L'Acino
Description: In the heart of the Quadrilatero Romano, just a stone’s throw from the bustling Porta Palazzo market, this small, family-run restaurant embodies the very essence of Piedmontese culinary tradition. The simple, welcoming atmosphere provides the ideal setting for cuisine that is rich in flavour and generous in portion size, deeply rooted in the local area and traditional recipes. The menu, often enhanced by the day’s specials announced verbally, invites you on a journey through the great regional classics: from traditional starters to fresh stuffed pasta, right through to the slow-cooked dishes that are a hallmark of Savoyard cuisine. To round off the meal, there are some unmissable desserts such as bonet and hazelnut cake, served with zabajone. There are just a few tables and they’re in high demand: booking in advance is strongly recommended.

Name: L'Acquario
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele 69, Castiglione del Lago, 06061, Italy
Description: In the historic center of this charming village above the lake, this spot is a great place to explore Umbrian cuisine, particularly traditional dishes featuring freshwater fish. For example? The oven-roasted medallion of porchetta-style carp, which offers a rich and succulent flavor!

Name: L'Acte 2
Description: Before revamping this restaurant, Julie (restaurant floor and wine) and Lucas (kitchen) met at Restaurant Marcon, a benchmark if ever there was one. They are now welcoming customers of their own into this compact contemporary space. Veal prepared three ways, with polenta, carrots and cistre (wild Alpine fennel); almond sponge, cherry and fromage blanc-geranium ice cream: the chef goes all out in his endeavours to craft dishes that are both meticulously prepared and visually striking.

Name: L'Agape
Description: Red mullet, courgettes, peppers, artichokes and olive oil: chef Julien Gleize celebrates Provence on a picturesque square of the City of Popes, courtesy of drool-worthy dishes jazzed up with herbs and spices and a fondness for produce from the Atlantic. A seasonal score packed with flavour to be sampled in an urban interior dotted with vintage details or on a shaded terrace by a refreshing fountain.

Name: L'Agape
Description: A period tiled floor, wooden banquette seating, wall mirrors and a rather amazing light fixture made out of old copper pans, without forgetting a delicious summer pavement terrace set the scene in this tastefully renovated vintage-style bistro. The concise, carefully thought out menu will make your tastebuds drool with the likes of foie gras au torchon and the house signature, tournedos Rossini, ordered à la carte or as part of the succulent tasting menu. Virtuoso cooking, meticulous plating and a front-of-house team that goes the extra mile.

Name: L'Aghjalle
Description: This large farm in a somewhat remote and picturesque food-producing valley of Balagne is home to olive groves and a vegetable garden and also raises cattle. The owner, a fiery character, pulls out all the stops to make guests feel welcome in this simple, rustic restaurant, whose vibe is poised between a sheepfold and an open-air tavern. She puts all the farm's produce to good use: traditional Corsican cuisine is served here, packed in gutsy flavours (cabbage stuffed with veal; quenelles of brocciu and poached Swiss chard in tomato sauce; stufatu of veal with olives and roast polenta). The menu-carte is very good value and it is easy to see why the spot, a favourite with the locals, is always busy. The service is attentive and efficient.

Name: L'Aillet
Description: Mathieu in the dining room and Rémi in the kitchen have poured their love of produce and good vibes into this buzzy town-centre hangout. Whether it is beneath the shade of plane trees in summer or in the dinky dining room in winter, you will sample up-to-the-minute bistro nosh that stars local produce and well-judged creative notes, without straying too far from traditional roots as the textbook technique and whole roasts frequently confirm. The admirable selection of wines by the glass (and the bottle), which is both savvy yet affordable, goes down a treat with the evening carte blanche menu. A firm fixture of the local culinary scene.

Name: L'Air de Famille
Description: L'Air de Famille makes for an appealing place to eat with its period decor (vintage advertising posters, original counter) and unpretentious atmosphere. Tradition and the seasons dictate the menu here, with particular attention paid to flavour combinations and sauces. Calf's head with ravigote sauce and other classics regularly feature… and they boast a well-stocked wine list!

Name: L'Alchimie
Description: Picture a modern, buzzy hangout popular with local foodies for its sensibly priced honest food and its particularly enticing lunch menu, something of a bargain for Nice. Think pork in a tom kha kai stock, beef confit in peas and carrots or upside-down-style apple tartlet – good food that ticks all the boxes. Invariably fully booked for the first service, it is much easier to find a table come 2pm. Only open for dinner on Friday and Saturday.

Name: L'Alcôve
Description: This restaurant just behind the cathedral is known for its market-fresh cuisine that is full of flavour, flawlessly prepared and delivers on its promises. Examples include house-made ravioli with ricotta, spinach and mandarin beurre blanc; cacio e pepe-style celeriac "tagliatelle" with pecorino espuma and breaded egg. Ever popular, not least thanks to its eater-friendly prices.

Name: L'Algadir del Delta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Hotel Algadir del Delta, the first to be certified with the European Ecolabel in Catalonia... this spot has the quality to be the undisputed star of the business, located in the Natural Park of the Ebro Delta and with its famous rice fields just a stone’s throw away. Owner-chef Joan Capilla is committed to local products, conscious gastronomy and the most modern techniques to give shape to updated traditional cuisine with a marked regenerative philosophy. The proposal, which always reserves a special place for rice dishes, revolves exclusively around several set menus: the Bib Gourmand, another market menu called Som Gastronomía, one where the chef takes us on a gastronomic tour of the area called Sabors del Delta and, finally, Raíces del Delta, with more of a focus on vegetables (all need to be pre-booked). In the garden area there is a much more informal option (Lo Bistró del Delta)!

Name: L'Alicanta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: Perched on the banks of the River Jonte, in the exceptional setting of the Gorges du Tarn, L'Alicanta has been on our radar for a while. The chef demonstrates a sure hand, turning out meticulously composed dishes that showcase bold, well-defined flavours: black pudding and apple tarte fine, pike-perch fillet roasted skin-on, pavlova with caramelised pears… Everything is house-made and the menu changes with the seasons. You can also expect a warm welcome!

Name: L'Amandier
Description: Tomato and mozzarella puff pastry tart, green tomato sorbet and basil vinaigrette; fillet of sea bream, vegetable tian and a warm caper vinaigrette; apricot compote with vanilla, semolina biscuit and pistachio ice cream… The delicious dishes crafted by this charming couple are the epitome of Mediterranean. In a bid to maintain standards, they don’t take bookings for more than 16 diners (even if they have room for 26). It is thus recommended to plan ahead, all the more so because of the sensible prices.

Name: L'Angle
Description: This hidden gem is nestled in a village at the confluence of two rivers – the Aveyron and the Viaur. A contemporary take on an artists' bistro, it boasts artwork on the walls and affordable prices. Working solo in his small, glass-walled kitchen, chef Arnaud Ronxin crafts ingenious dishes with the mission of showcasing seasonal produce. Think oven-roasted veal with confit potatoes and chanterelles, or lamb trotters with a red wine sauce. The more ambitious multi-course evening set menu is different every evening.

Name: L'Angle Saint-Laurent
Description: On the corner of Rue Saint Laurent and Rue des Bouchers, Luc Catherine in the kitchen and Stéphanie Amy in the dining room have brilliantly preserved the soul of this establishment, following a warm, fashionable makeover featuring bare stones and beams. Top-notch ingredients, indulgent, nostalgic recipes and artful plating are the name of the game: gazpacho of green peas with an organic poached egg; smoked pork cutlet with saté-laced risotto of noodles and a cheesecake version of Breton shortbread. Slick service and sensible prices: what’s not to like?

Name: L'Antre Amis
Description: Courtesy of premium, seasonal produce, the chef-owner devises a concise menu in the zeitgeist, without forgoing the temptation to revisit more traditional registers (pâté en croute, duck foie gras; Breton sole meunière; Madagascan vanilla-laced flan), or even a tempting range of tapas to share. To be accompanied by your pick from a well-stocked wine cellar. Pleasant trendy interior and pavement terrace on a quiet street. Something of a favourite with foodies, so booking is highly advised.

Name: L'Araignée Gourmande
Address: 8 rue de la Paix, Laragne-Montéglin, 05300, France
Description: Breton-born chef, Thierry Chouin, knows the score and never messes around with premium, often locally sourced produce. His conservative French lineup stars hearty, forthright flavours, drenched in sunshine (gazpacho, mozzarella, raw tomato sauce, shallots and pesto). While he may avow a particular penchant for fish, illustrated by hake baked in a mustard-laced crumbly shell, he doesn’t snub patriotic, soul-warming dishes of the likes of calf’s sweetbread sautéed in butter or risotto with cèpe mushrooms. Chouin’s cheerful wife seamlessly and singlehandedly greets and serves diners.

Name: L'Arbre Vert
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The tree mentioned in the name of this restaurant could well be a genealogical one, so closely is its history bound up with that of the Koenig family. Now run by the fifth generation of this family, the restaurant serves specialities from Alsace, which are accompanied by good regional wines.

Name: L'Ardoise
Description: On the left bank of the Maine, the chef cooks up flavoursome recipes that blend tradition and the essence of the sun-drenched Mediterranean: croquetta di miale and a herby mayonnaise; shank of confit veal with Milanese risotto… A festive vibe, a crisp, enticing lineup and invariably packed to the seams. Meals are served in a trendy, industrial brasserie interior or alfresco, on the terrace.

Name: L'Artichaut
Description: Headed up by a chef whose enthusiasm is contagious, this place is an ode to the seasons. Dishes are crafted from market-fresh ingredients and the menu-carte changes regularly – smoked haddock terrine, burrata, herby beetroot and devilled eggs; steamed saithe, parpadelle, braised fennel and fish soup; white chocolate and yoghurt cream, rum-soaked banana pulp, almond cake and salted butter caramel ice cream. Fresh ingredients, recipes made from scratch, regional wines: a restaurant that cannot fail to win you over.

Name: L'Assiette au Jardin
Description: Near Noirmoutier Château, take a seat in a dinky bistro interior whose shelves are laden with gourmet deli produce, or in the pretty conservatory. You will sample tasty food in which tradition is cleverly paired with wayfaring influences, illustrated by the Fujiyama oyster (house specialty) or a bourride of monkfish with an aïoli.

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Xavier Giraudet, chef at La Robe, has opened a second establishment in a bistro vein. Diners know they are in safe hands here as they tuck into traditional, flavourful and generous cuisine: succulent and aromatic pâté en croûte, melt-in-the-mouth black pudding with mashed potatoes, and a dessert inspired by the Paris-Brest, which is as indulgent as they come. You get up from your table with a smile on your face and your finances intact, thanks to the affordable set menus at lunch and dinner. A bright and modern setting; friendly service from the cheerful waitstaff.

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Chef Fabrice Rodot is a food lover, and he proves it with his dishes, which feature local and seasonal ingredients. He has a perfect grasp of the classics, and this cosy restaurant with rustic touches is a lovely setting in which to eat: cauliflower in a brioche crust, mousseline cream; organic veal, peas and carrots, sauce Périgueux-style jus; crêpes Suzette flambéed on a pedestal table. Not forgetting the excellent house-made bread! In fine weather, head for a table by the fountain on the terrace.

Name: L'Atelier Flavien Valère
Description: After honing his talents around southwest France, Flavien Valère has decided to treat Langon to his culinary flair. He knows his stuff, no doubt about that: impeccable cooking techniques, perfect seasonings, premium produce and carefully crafted recipes – everything is from scratch, to our delight! Eater-friendly priced lunchtime menu. Bookings advisable.

Name: L'Atelier L'Art des Mets
Description: The chef rolls out neoteric instinctive cuisine, whose mainstay is wild herbs, which he learned to identify through a local herb picker. Goosefoot, wild lemon balm, purslane, mugwort add a poetic note and layers of flavour, while the mystery menu keeps track with market availability and the result of foraging excursions. Consider us smitten!

Name: L'Atelier Locavore
Address: 2 avenue de la Libération, Le Coteau, 42120, France
Description: On the banks of the River Loire, this restaurant is run by a local chef, whose trademark is delicious market-fresh cuisine. He serves an affordable set menu at lunchtime and a more elaborate monthly set menu. He carefully sources his ingredients, giving local produce pride of place: foie gras from Domaine de Limagne, trout caught in the Oron, beef from a farmer-butcher in Renaison, Roanne saffron and organic vegetables from Arfeuilles. A lovely cheese trolley is presented in the dining room.

Name: L'Athome
Description: In this picturesque village bistro complete with a wine shop, chef Lionel Cotentin (what a coincidence!) draws on his strong culinary background and premium local produce – organic market garden vegetables, small-scale fishing – to whip up a concise, seasonal menu. The cuisine is modern, meticulous and forthright: home-smoked mackerel, stracciatella and basil-flavoured olive oil sauce; loin of ling, Carnaroli risotto and beurre blanc. Cheerful, spot on service and sensible prices.

Name: L'Attanum
Address: 64 place de la Nation, Saint-Yrieix-la-Perche, 87500, France
Description: The ground floor of this 19C sous-préfecture is now home to a fashionably appointed restaurant that welcomes with a cheerful vibe. At the helm, Ludwik Crosnier, with stints in some prestigious establishments under his belt, signs a seasonal score depicted by local ingredients, stellar technique and delicately balanced flavours. Claire cheerfully and attentively supervises the front-of-house, adding a gracious flourish to this fine dining experience.

Name: L'Auberge
Description: Not far from Hazebrouck, this Auberge was once a tannery then a barroom in full-blown ‘ch’ti’ tradition, before it morphed into this friendly inn, with a focus on seasonal produce and Flemish roots courtesy of new takes on classic local recipes (Welsh, carbonade). The menu features some surprising combinations, like langoustine with haddock and green peas. Hats off to chef Antonin, who is also a wine buff and thus an excellent source of wine tips.

Name: L'Auberge
Description: Come for lunch beneath the vaults of Château Neercanne's old chapel – you cannot fail to be impressed by this charming historical setting that has been given a stylish makeover. The terrace affords spectacular views. The kitchen team serves up a repertoire of classic dishes, adding subtle modern accents and drawing inspiration from their own kitchen garden. House-smoked salmon accompanied by a generous potato salad with gherkins and capers, finished with an indulgent beurre blanc, perfectly captures the spirit here: comforting yet lavish. A gem worth discovering.

Name: L'Auberge des Gourmets
Address: 9 place de l'Église, Le Villars, 71700, France
Description: In a charming village above the River Saône, this restaurant has a traditional decor (exposed stones and beams, large colourful frescoes). Guillaume Laublanc, a native of these parts, sets about cooking his bistronomy-style cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and infectious enthusiasm. Cooked at low temperature, the Bresse chicken (from Johan Morand's farm) stuffed with morels and vin jaune cream is sure to win you over!

Name: L'Auberge des Montagnes
Address: 7 chemin de la Beauté, Pailherols, 15800, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: Perched in the Cantal mountains, this pleasingly rustic farmstead is the fruit of a beautiful family saga spanning six generations. Tuck into generous traditional cuisine rooted in the local terroir – featuring the legendary truffade, served with every dish, and the family recipe for tripoux à la tomate. All dishes are sincere and precise. And then there is the trolley of regional cheeses, with Salers, produced just a few metres away, taking pride of place.

Name: L'Auberge du Laminak
Description: In this charming inn on the edge of the forest, the Basque Country – where the chef is from – meets fine produce from the Ardennes. The result is delicious, skilfully made dishes, such as piquillo peppers stuffed with cod brandade and fish soup, or lamb confit with piperade. Generous and indulgent cuisine awaits!

Name: L'Auberge du Pas de Vent
Description: Authenticity is the name of the game in this Landes "inn" that specialises in hearty, wholesome food, far removed from fads and fashions. The menu shines a light on the local terroir – beef from the Fermes de Chalosse network of farms, fattened free-range duck, milk-fed veal, sheep's milk cheese from a village shepherd and additive-free house-made sourdough bread. An open sandwich with pork shank terrine and confit pig's ears, with an orange and endive salad, or their iconic veal sweetbreads in Jurançon wine served in a skillet: the generous portions are a throwback to a bygone era. Warm welcome and attentive, professional and efficient service. What's not to like?

Name: L'Auberge du Pont des Pierres
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant on the road to Monts Jura is invariably busy! Chef Romain Blanc, who hails from the region, has no shortage of talent or ideas when it comes to cooking seasonal local produce: fish from Lake Geneva or nearby fish farms, pork and poultry from the surrounding area, local market gardeners and a herb garden. He also demonstrates a flair for preparing jus and a mastery of cooking processes, and makes a lot from scratch (including ice cream and bread). Bargain prices and service with a smile from Chloé, who will guide you through the nice selection of wines from independent winegrowers.

Name: L'Aubépine
Description: L’Aubépine has been flourishing for a decade now in the capable hands of Manuel Raya Moreno, former research scientist turned chef. In his town centre HQ, he rolls out a modern, local, seasonal lineup with an eye on market availability and short supply chains. Concise appetising lunchtime menu; surprise menu in the evening. Distinctive, deftly crafted signature cuisine by a talented chef who believes in what he’s doing.

Name: L'Echappée Belle
Description: This quintessential Bib Gourmand eatery is embodied by Grégory and Camille’s warm friendly welcome, enhanced by the lovely terrace overlooking the market garden. The couple has created strong ties with local producers, such as Ferme d’Artagnan and Ferme Fourchette, who have become part of the family. The chef crafts their excellent ingredients lavishly and creatively. Examples include medium rare, crispy skinned duck breast with a gutsy gravy, grilled fruity peach and a subtle vibrant tarragon-laced mojo sauce. From time to time, the chef organises highly popular theme events, like a Spanish week. A splendid opportunity to taste authentic Liège fare.

Name: L'Embellie
Address: rue de la Station 115, Soignies, 7060, Belgium
Description: Home from home is the expression that comes to mind as you set foot in L’Embellie. Géraldine graciously welcomes diners into a pretty vintage interior, depicted by a handsome dining room and a peaceful garden terrace. Classically trained chef Pol rolls out a contemporary score without ever compromising on the quality of the produce, as you will notice right from the tempting appetisers. How about duck breast, cooked rare in a delicate jus with poultry stuffed morels, a fritter made with duck legs, Malines asparagus and a velvety celery millefeuille? A gourmet repertory crafted meticulously and deftly. Outstanding value for money – don’t forget to book!

Name: L'Empreinte
Description: Solid oak tables, custom-made tableware and a warm welcome… This snug restaurant is the domain of Manuel Godet, who harnesses his impeccable technical skills to craft creative dishes that shine a spotlight on local produce, sometimes with original flavour combinations. Examples include braised pork cheeks with Madiran wine and orange zest, served with textures of pear and purple sweet potato mousseline and finished with a rich, concentrated jus. Simple lunch deal, more ambitious fare in the evening.

Name: L'Entre D'Eux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of chef Caroline Druine and your master of ceremonies, Alexandre, is warm and inviting and exudes a lovely home-from-home feel. The small garden patio, near the pear trees, is ideal for alfresco summer dining. The culinary focus is on local produce, decadent flavours and painstaking craftswomanship. The chef may wrap a juicy ballotine of pheasant in a cabbage leaf, which she then stuffs with sweet chestnuts and pumpkin. A punchy cognac sauce and a few well-chosen side dishes add the finishing touch to this rich seasonal dish. The savvily curated wine list is definitely worth spending time over, all the more so as it stars a fine selection of organic vintages.

Name: L'Envers du Décor
Address: 23 rue de la Bienfaisance, Les Herbiers, 85500, France
Description: This old bakery has been transformed into a smart, contemporary restaurant that sports a minimalist vibe. Chef Aurélien Jousseaume earned his stripes in Michelin-starred kitchens with the likes of Etchebest, Guy Savoy and Guy Martin. To-ing and fro-ing between his open kitchen and the restaurant floor, the chef, who is clearly having a ball, takes the orders and presents the dishes himself. His delicious seasonal cuisine showcases his flair for creating tasty sauces and jus.

Name: L'Ermitage
Description: This restored old barn has retained a homely rustic feel. The chef, whose CV boasts establishments of the calibre of Jacques Maximin and La Grenouillère, orchestrates a purebred Gallic score, in which red meat enjoys a leading role. The meal often kicks off with a delicious country terrine and a selection from the cheese trolley is included in the menu. Finish with one of the house signature desserts: honey-laced crème brûlée or a meringue and verbena ice cream extravaganza, flambéed in Velay liqueur. Let’s not forget the open fire in winter and the inviting terrace in summertime. Ticks all the boxes!

Name: L'Espièglerie
Description: Since 1988, gourmets have been making a beeline for this romantic hideaway, whose old vaults and bare brick walls lend it masses of cachet and bags of elegance. Choose from the daily special or the menu to sample rich authentic food that has earned this eatery its fine reputation. How about a creative spin on a maki with gambas and smoked eel or cod in lemon breadcrumbs jazzed up with seaweed flavoured cabbage stock? The chef knows how to grab our attention and pamper our taste buds. Gloriously sensibly priced and a splendid selection of beers and Bordeaux wines.

Name: L'Esprit Bistrot
Description: In a trendy bistro interior, you will sample good food crafted by an enthusiastic chef. The long list of local producers with whom he works is emblematic of his mindset. A few examples: a salad of razor clams and lentils from Trept; mallard duck cooked two ways and garnished with braised chicory and an offal-flavoured gravy; Chartreuse-flavoured baba…

Name: L'Essentiel
Description: Tucked away at the foot of the castle, this beautiful tuffeau-stone house unveils charming dining rooms (parquet floors, exposed rafters and bare stone walls), furnished in a contemporary vein. Chef Anthony Vaillant crafts food in the zeitgeist, jazzed up with a scattering of creative and globetrotting touches: 65°C soft-boiled egg, shortbread perfumed with Indonesian vanilla and hollandaise sauce; lacquered duck breast in a sesame and wasabi crust with a gutsy jus; hot, coffee-laced soufflé and pineapple sorbet. Alfresco dining on one of the peaceful pretty patios is very pleasant when the weather is fine.

Name: L'IØDE
Description: A butcher's son born on the Île d'Oléron, chef Benjamin Girard has chosen to focus on fish and seafood. In this narrow modern dining space done out in white and blue hues, the delicious dishes with creative touches keep on coming: mackerel half-cooked with a blowtorch, grilled watermelon and tomato water; halibut with a langoustine foam and blackberries; black forest gateau-style "explosive cherry" dessert. Eater-friendly prices and an enticing wine list with plenty of organic options.

Name: L'Obélias
Description: In the Ségala region, nestling in a village that is famous for its Cistercian church, this recently renovated little restaurant is accommodated in a half-timbered house. Léonie and Guilhem, a well-travelled couple of industry professionals – pastry chef and chef, respectively – put a skilful spin on traditional fare such as roast chicken breast, Padrón peppers stuffed with smoked vegetables and bell pepper, or Mara des Bois strawberries with fir essence and pollen dust. They have come up with a well-balanced and appealing menu abounding with fresh and colourful dishes that vary with the seasons and market availability – plus it's excellent value for money. In short, they've got it all figured out. Delightful terrace laid out in the shade of an albizia and a magnolia.

Name: L'Ogustin
Address: 2 place de l'Ormeau, La Vacquerie-et-Saint-Martin-de-Castries, 34520, France
Description: Not far from the Cirque de Navacelles, in a small village on the southern edge of the limestone plateau that is the Causse du Larzac, Pricillia Lebon's restaurant is housed in a converted inn. Beneath the stone vaults, the inviting, cosy decor reflects the endearing personality of a chef who has come to this beautiful, isolated setting to cook. The surprise set menu celebrates the Larzac area, with ingredients sourced mainly via short supply chains (not least from local market gardens), as well as from mushroom and plant picking. Plants reign supreme in the intuitive, light and aromatic dishes. The dessert is a tribute to the chef's Malgasy origins, with a sweet potato cream spiked with vanilla. Vegetarian options are also available. A unique and authentic place.

Name: L'Olivier
Description: Chef Olivier Lamard crafts a modern culinary score that draws on the terroir of Alsace: house-made foie gras in gewurztraminer; guinea fowl with velvety parsnips and mushrooms; upside-down plum pie, tonka bean-laced mascarpone cream and vanilla ice cream. Savvy, deft craftsmanship and premium produce, some of which from the chef’s granddad’s garden: it ticks all the boxes!

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: 3 rue de la Marne, Menton, 06500, France
Description: This inconspicuous restaurant in the centre of town is actually home to a culinary powerhouse. The Japanese chef, who was sous-chef to Bruno Cirino at Hostellerie Jérôme, masterfully crafts his own addictive take on Mediterranean cuisine, putting a Japanese spin on locally sourced produce. Thanks to ultra-fresh ingredients, spot-on cooking and well-judged seasoning, everything comes together beautifully: eg artichoke hearts à la barigoule with prosciutto chips; salmon tataki with marinated vegetables, or sirloin steak with yuzu kosho. The terrace, partly covered by an awning, looks out onto a pedestrianised street.

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: 9 rue de la Prépoise, Pornic, 44210, France
Description: Trained by some of the best (Alain Dutournier, Jean-Michel Lorrain, Alain Ducasse), chef Julien Lainé crafts mouthwatering modern food from locally sourced ingredients. The menu changes regularly according to his inspiration, giving rise to unexpected combinations, such as oysters in a hollandaise sauce laced in peated whisky. This endearing eatery is a very welcome addition in a seaside resort such as Pornic.

Name: L'Ortone
Description: A bistro with a Tuscan soul overlooking the Sant’Ambrogio market: pared-back in décor and equally forthright in its culinary approach, alongside tributes to the territory, the cuisine focuses on imaginative preparations inspired by the great themes of Italian cuisine. Emblematic is the work with squab, interpreted according to the season, as in the agnolotti, a dish that speaks to technique and contemporary sensitivity. The wine list offers a focused selection of regional bottles at every price point, while a small terrace provides a handful of pleasant tables on milder days.

Name: L'Oste Dispensa
Description: Along one of the two strips of land that join the mainland to the Argentario is this contemporary osteria, minimal but comfortable and equipped with a pleasant veranda that opens in summer, always projecting toward a splendid view of the sea (don't miss the sunset if you can). The cuisine is based on local products, especially sustainably caught fish: not surprisingly, in keeping with this, the wine list features several organic labels. Highly recommended tasting menus that can range from 35 to 45 Euro. Better make reservations because they are extremely popular!

Name: L'Osteria della Trippa
Description: In the heart of Trastevere, a recent interior refurbishment has given the Osteria della Trippa a new look, while retaining its rustic, homely character. The cuisine passionately celebrates the traditions of Rome and the Lazio region, offering generous, meticulously prepared dishes, with a particular focus on offal. The undisputed star of the show is, of course, tripe, served in a variety of ways and featuring as the centrepiece of a dedicated tasting menu; another menu, meanwhile, pays tribute to the cuisine of Viterbo. There’s no shortage of the great classics, from artichokes alla giudia to coratella, right through to pasta dishes with the most famous sauces: amatriciana, carbonara, cacio e pepe and pajata. Rounding off the experience is the warm welcome from Alessandra Ruggeri, the heart and soul of the dining room, and a wine list with a focus on wines from Lazio and across Italy.

Name: L'Ostreria Fratelli Pavesi
Description: The menu is a journey through flavours that weave the traditions of Piacenza together with influences from other Italian regions. One of the highlights is their take on a Ligurian dish: Cappon magro di fiume, which combines sturgeon and trout with seasonal vegetables and salsa verde, creating fresh and lively contrasts. But the dish that won us over today is the charcoal-grilled pigeon: juicy meat, velvety liver pâté, a rich gravy and vegetables from the garden, in a perfect balance between technique and taste. The experience doesn't stop here: the wine list offers a wealth of rare and intriguing labels, ready to complete the delightful dining experience.

Name: L'Ouillette
Description: An enthusiastic young couple is at the helm of this family - run inn on the village square. In the kitchen, Simon hops between traditional (eggs in red wine sauce, marbled, seasoned ham, coq au vin) and more modern creations; Maude ensures that her guests’ every need is met in the dining room. Definitely to be recommended.

Name: L'Ourdissoir
Description: This modest establishment at a remove from the city centre, whose name is a nod to its past vocation as a weaver's house, boasts an inviting interior of exposed stone and wood panelling – the perfect backdrop for contemporary cuisine made with top-notch seasonal ingredients. The short menu is beautifully presented and original, with some unexpected combinations, such as pollock with a helianthus medley, grapefruit and watercress sauce. The food is truly delicious, and that goes for the desserts, too. Don't miss out!

Name: L'Échappée Belle
Description: On the ground floor of a contemporary hotel, the entrance framed by birch trunks leads to a stylish dining space done out with anthracite feature walls, red banquettes and white seats. The modern, refined and flavoursome brasserie cuisine includes dishes such as Dubarry velouté, focaccia croutons and peanut oil with Espelette pepper; sautéed prawns, piquillo pepper and chorizo risotto, sauce armoricaine; melt-in-the-middle moelleux au chocolat, Armagnac cream and caramelised hazelnuts. Pleasant terrace overlooking the main square.

Name: L'Éclat de Pierre
Description: This brasserie in the heart of the village sits just outside the indoor market, serving delicious traditional dishes that scrupulously respect the fundamentals of French cuisine. Made with seasonal produce, the set menu – available at both lunch and dinner – changes every week. The blackboard features mouth-watering dishes: pork and poultry terrine with pink peppercorns; pollock steak with potatoes dressed with parsley and a Parmesan sauce; a custard tart with Madagascar vanilla that won first prize for the "best flan pâtissier in France".

Name: L'Éden
Description: On a side street of one of the Côte Fleurie’s most iconic and most picturesque villages, the establishment of the Tougard couple, open since the early 2000s, sports an unassuming facade. In a snug stylish interior, the chef crafts a score that cleverly slaloms between tradition and modernity. If we were to cite a single example, it would be his virtuoso take on the ballotine of plump chicken. Flavours and aromas that hit the spot every time. Not to be missed!

Name: L'Émotion
Description: From one year to the next, local lad Michaël Ruat has been regaling the foodies of Puy-en-Velay. Natural materials and designer details, including a glazed wine cellar, depict the interior. The food forges a culinary course between regional Haute Loire ingredients (green lentils, Fin Gras du Mézenc beef, Monts du Velay red fruits) and a hyper modern slant. An example: tartare of seabass paired with crunchy veg, sorbet of rocket lettuce and sweet pepper-infused oil.

Name: L'Épicerie
Address: 1 chemin des Usages, La Borne, 18250, France
Description: Is the restaurant a grocer’s or is it the other way round? Whatever, this ebullient, two-in-one business quietly feeds us well, which is all that matters! Mathieu (in charge of savoury dishes) and Clémentine (desserts) curate a splendid, seasonal menu that stars regional produce: organic market garden veg from down the road, free-range meat and herbs from the garden. All the tableware (crockery, knife rests, carafes) is the handiwork of artisans established in this thriving pottery village. Their unpretentious eatery is a hit with the locals, which is always a good sign. Beware, 20 seats only, so book before you come. An affably French establishment offering a taste of rural life in times past!

Name: L'Épicurien
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Luck has nothing to do with the current reputation of this downtown venue, facing Jean Jaurès Fountain, as the darling of the town’s discerning epicureans. The stripped-back interior sports a distinctly Scandinavian feel, which given the chef’s Swedish origins is hardly a surprise. On the culinary front, he deploys his undisputed talent, adding a new twist to French classics and conjuring up enticing recipes in tune with the era: generous portions, well crafted and oozing with flavour. The intelligent wine list and crack table staff, as professional as they are friendly, add the final flourish.

Name: L'Épicurieux
Description: This spruce, endearing bistro on the main square of Illies is smoothly and passionately run by former Top Chef contestant, Christophe Pirotais and his partner Julie Dieudonné. Their gutsy indulgent cuisine is unveiled in an inspired, big-boned surprise menu, illustrated by a delicate pannacotta of white asparagus with radish-flavoured ice cream or a fillet of seabream escorted by chickpea fritters and a creamy jus of smoked herring roe. The welcome is warm and cheerful and the service is as smooth as a silky bearnaise sauce. Lovely rear patio for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: L'Épicurieux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant in a peaceful village in the Corrèze hinterland charms with its tranquil setting and view of the Corrèze valley (especially from the terrace). The bright dining room with a festive atmosphere is the playground of chef Thomas Ceaux and his partner Pauline Gane, who works front of house. The chef cooks up seasonal cuisine that showcases the local terroir: Limousin veal, creamy peas and chorizo; crispy puffs with red berries, vanilla mascarpone cream, and strawberry and raspberry sorbet from Tulle. A place with a loyal following.

Name: L'Épicurieux chez Luc
Description: After many years with the Bocuse group, chef Luc Abadie has set up shop in this restaurant with a partially open kitchen that allows him to interact with his customers. His traditional cuisine is perfectly crafted and bears the hallmarks of the late Paul Bocuse – namely an absence of contrived creativity and unnecessary convolutions. The culinary offering, which is the same for lunch and dinner, is based on an excellent-value weekly set menu – eg carrot royale with cumin, roast rack of pork with herbs and white beans – and an à la carte menu on which the dishes are just as classical, but made with more refined ingredients: seasonal pâté en croûte, sole meunière, Charolais beef rib with a green peppercorn sauce, and Norwegian omelette flambéed with Cointreau.

Name: L'Épine
Address: 19 place de la République, Azay-le-Rideau, 37190, France
Description: The name of the restaurant refers to the blackthorn, a spiky shrub commonly found in France's countryside hedgerows and whose shoots are used to make a fortified wine. Tasteful elegance reigns in this former schoolhouse (dating from 1866) with an exposed beam ceiling, large windows letting light flood in and opening onto a terrace planted with trees, designer light fixtures and artwork. The chef's seasonal cuisine, infused with Asian influences, fêtes local artisans and their produce.

Name: L'Équilibre
Address: 10 place de la Libération, Balma, 31130, France
Description: Run by an enthusiastic couple who believe in hearty, wholesome food, this restaurant fully deserves its resounding success. The chef skilfully works with fine market produce, illustrated by a perfectly cooked egg with a runny yolk, onions confit in white wine and shredded pork in wild garlic… Outstanding value for money and hits all the right buttons.

Name: L'Évidence
Description: After honing his skills in top houses, Julien Burdin now rolls out a modern, seasonal score rich in crisp, legible flavours, illustrated by creamy Jerusalem artichoke soup with Murcia pepper and finely diced chorizo, or free-range Burgundy poultry in a vin jaune sauce. The à la carte lineup highlights more upmarket produce, like seared slices of duck foie gras, truffles and mashed potato.

Name: L'Ô à la Bouche
Description: At the head of this pleasant restaurant is a foodie couple who travelled to faraway lands and seas before dropping anchor in Cahors. Jean - François concocts gourmet dishes such as: salmon marinated in fennel or wild seabass, pan - fried chard and Lautrec pink garlic cromesquis. Enough to make your mouth water!

Name: LA BETTOLA da Ochiai
Description: ‘La Bettola’ is Italian for ‘the dining hall’. With its casual atmosphere and fare that is good value for money, this trattoria draws throngs of guests day after day. The menu is crammed with regional cuisines and seasonal dishes. The prix fixe selection allows a choice of items—you’ll find it hard to make up your mind. For the appetiser, we recommend the combination platter, generous in both portions and variety. Sea urchin spaghetti is a perennial favourite.

Name: LA Mahzen
Address: Kuşçuburun Mahallesi, Başmimar Sinan Caddesi No:81, Yazıbaşı, Torbalı, Izmir, 35860, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Domaine Lucien Arkas vineyards are well worth a visit. Take some time to stroll among the vines – highly romantic if you have that special someone by your side. The same romantic feeling prevails whether you dine outdoors overlooking the vineyard or indoors with a view of the wine cellar beneath you (bottles are for sale at the entrance). The chef tempts you with unfussy Mediterranean dishes that perfectly complement the quality wines produced here. Charcoal-grilled leg of lamb with a bold lamb jus enriched with mustard, then a wonderfully sweet strawberry magnolia for dessert – honest flavours are paramount, both in the glass and on the plate.

Name: LALÚ Bistro
Description: In the heart of the old town, this simple, no-frills restaurant focuses all its efforts on the quality of its cuisine, which is also reasonably priced. The menu is à la carte. Starters include a selection of charcuterie, while the main courses feature traditional Slovenian dishes alongside more exotic ingredients and recipes, from ramen to poke, via bao burgers and falafel.

Name: LAMM
Description: A really cosy place, where you will also eat very well: seasonal Swabian-Baden cuisine, with an emphasis on regional produce; some of the meat comes from the restaurant's own highland cattle. Some dishes are labelled ‘Naturparkwirte’ (nature park hosts). There are good wines to accompany your meal, as well as a special whisky offer. In summer, try and bag a spot on the terrace. Pleasant guestrooms also available.

Name: LANBRoA
Description: The menu lists dishes from every corner of Spain, every one a precious memory of the chef. The preponderance of Basque dishes reflects her attendance of a cooking school in San Sebastián and apprenticeship at a restaurant there. We start with pintxo (pinchos), an apt choice for the Spanish pub atmosphere. Piquillo pepper stuffed with dried and salted cod, squid simmered in its ink and other Basque-country favourites are faithfully reproduced here. Experience the food culture of Spain.

Name: LAUBURU
Description: The number ‘64’ on the door refers to France’s 64th department: Pyrénées-Atlantiques, in the Basque Country. A devotee of pork culture, Shinichiro Sakurai is a lover of all things Basque, especially its pork cuisine. Having learned from charcuterie, Chef Sakurai places pork dishes front and centre: pâté and pig’s-head terrine as appetisers, boudin noir as a main dish. The Basque spirit lives and breathes in this back alley off Kotto-dori Street.

Name: LENZ
Description: Lenz Leslie Himmelheber pours his heart and soul into his cheerful, modern restaurant and his style of hosting has a distinctive personal touch. In season, the self-proclaimed "duckman" carves his signature Vierlande duck at your table. The menu also includes regional, seasonal and cosmopolitan cuisine with dishes such as salmon tartare with ponzu beurre noisette, pear and avocado, or "Wiener schnitzel deluxe" with cucumber salad, truffle chips and truffle mayonnaise. A separate lunch menu featuring simpler and more affordable dishes is another highlight. The food is complemented by an appealing wine list, service is attentive, and the bright conservatory can be opened up in summer!

Name: LEV by Mike
Description: LEV occupies the first floor of a former bathhouse, with wonderful views of the natural pond and the inviting decor of a modern brasserie. Mike Vrijdag's concept is irresistible: an extensive selection of mid-sized dishes ranging from comfort food to more contemporary creations. The chef has the technical skill and playfulness to keep diners interested from start to finish. One example is succulent cod accompanied by al dente green beans, pan-fried gnocchi and a delicate fish sauce with subtle notes of vanilla. This cooking is all about flavour.

Name: LOLA
