FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a district of Caramanico, this typical stone house is home to an attractive restaurant that is the perfect choice for anyone keen on typical Abruzzo specialities. Prepared from regional ingredients, the dishes are delicious and substantial.

Name: Locanda delle Grazie
Address: Via San Pio X 2, Grazie, 46010, Italy
Description: A long-established family-run concern, opened many years ago and today a cornerstone of traditional Mantuan cooking: forthright, generous and of consistent quality, in the heart of the small and evocative village of Curtatone. Here the classic repertoire is never found wanting: tortelli di zucca, local cured meats, pike in salsa verde, long-braised meats, sbrisolona, zabaione... simple and fragrant dishes of genuine homely character, served in abundant portions at prices that are more than reasonable.

Name: Lohmayr Stub'n
Description: This place is popular for good reason! Sebastian Oberholzner puts his heart and soul into his cooking, and his flavoursome dishes are much in demand. He favours seasonal, regional ingredients, and knows both his suppliers and exactly where their produce comes from. You can choose from several set menus and à la carte options. Tempting dishes include "Lohmayr's Vorspeisenetagere" (a tiered selection of starters), Sicilian prawn stew with toasted bread, and oven-cooked veal Tafelspitz (rump cap) on a bed of chanterelle ragout, served with lemon-infused potato purée. There is also a good selection of wines. Hostess Tanja Oberholzner and her team provide charming, attentive service in this beautiful historic building. Tip: Be sure to book!

Name: Loiseau de France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Inside Institut Français de Tokyo, time flows slowly, the bustle of the city forgotten. The chalk-white building, designed to suggest a small village in the south of France, gently enfolds a courtyard. Poached eggs in red wine sauce and beef simmered in red wine bring a taste of Saulieu, in Burgundy’s Côte d’Or. Desserts are classic sweets selected from a trolley, as tradition dictates.

Name: Lok Kei Noodles
Address: 1-D Travessa da Saudade, Macau, Macau, Macau SAR
Description: This busy shop next to the Chun Lei pier still kneads the noodles with a bamboo pole like in bygone days. The owner’s wife then cooks them perfectly, thus explaining their bouncy texture. The broth simmered with an array of seasonal fish boasts depth and sweetness. Dried prawn roe sprinkled on tossed noodles is toasted by the owner himself, imparting umami and aroma. Also try the crab congee and deep-fried wontons with crispy dace balls.

Name: Lokanda Devetak
Address: Via Brezici 22, località San Michele del Carso, Savogna d'Isonzo, 34070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A historic and rightly famous restaurant. The same family – now in its sixth generation – has been celebrating the flavours of the region since 1870, just a stone's throw from the Slovenian border, where traditions and aromas blend seamlessly together. Authentic emotions are brought to the table: Palatschinke lasagne with mushrooms and pumpkin béchamel sauce, veal tripe à la Carsolina flavoured with bay leaves and pecorino cheese, and the traditional “Kraško pecivo”, a soft cake with raisins and walnuts, accompanied by cinnamon ice cream. The wine cellar, lovingly curated by the owner, boasts 1,000 labels and a rich selection of wines by the glass, with local wines taking centre stage.

Name: Lola Gaspar
Address: 211 W. 2nd St., Santa Ana, CA, 92701, USA
Description: This gastropub in downtown Santa Ana isn't new but a post-pandemic reset and a trip to Mexico changed Chef Luis Perez's mindset—and menu. It's all about quality over quantity here, so expect a tightly edited menu featuring tacos, quekas, and churros, but it's all very good. Happy hour discounts make sampling it all a tempting proposition. Tacos are made with handmade flour tortillas topped with a grilled tomato and dried chili salsa and filled with everything from sauteed shrimp to pork shank carnitas and suadero. Quekas feature hand-pressed masa and are served with a habanero salsa. While the vegan mushroom queka is worth ordering by itself with nicely sauteed mushrooms, confit potatoes, and guacamole, you can also opt to add cheese for a wonderful addition.

Name: Lom Wong
Address: 218 E. Portland St., Phoenix, AZ, 85004, USA
Description: After years of running a pop-up, Chefs Alex and Yotaka "Sunny" Martin opened this brick-and-mortar in downtown Phoenix. Lom Wong delivers fiery, regional Thai dishes, all served family- style. There is a clear respect for traditional techniques and ingredients, from hand-pounded curries to fresh coconut milk. Hoi shae nam la, a subtly sweet scallop crudo, is a refreshing opener before naem khao tawt, a classic dish of crispy rice and cured pork sausage. Turn up the heat with kaeng phet charinda, a spicy mix of beef shank and tendon with curry paste, coconut and makheua eggplant. Cool down with a banana split with creamy coconut sorbet, fish sauce caramel and Thai chocolate sauce.

Name: Londo
Address: Unit 6, 2 Papanui Road, Merivale, Christchurch, 8014, New Zealand
Description: Good things come in small packages – and Londo is a very good example. This tiny wine bar has just three tables and a few counter seats; everyone is treated like a friend and you really feel the love from the passionate young chef, Robert. The short menu changes often, with the dishes – as big on flavour as they are in size – designed for sharing. Beef tartare made from Canterbury grass-fed beef aged for 55 days is always worth ordering. Along with a short selection of local natural wines are cocktails and craft beers.

Name: Long Sen Yuan (Qingyang)
Address: 60 Qintai Road, Qingyang, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: For over 20 years, this no-frills restaurant has had a single item on the menu – authentic Chengdu hotpot. Diners have never get bored because of the 18 soup bases and the stunning variety of dipping sauces, meat, offal, and sea and river fish on offer. Don’t miss the pencil-width strips of crisp, juicy Emei eel. The mala soup base is infused with Chinese herbs, perfect for blanching celtuce or pork cracklings. Their appetisers and snacks also hit the spot every time.

Name: Long Story Short Eatery & Bakery
Description: This on-trend, modern bistro concept – including a chef's table and open kitchen complete with Jopser grill – lies within the historical walls of a military bakery with lofty vaulted ceilings. The flavoursome cuisine is creative and seasonal, with an appealing à la carte menu, plus an extra dish at lunchtime. It's not easy to choose between dishes such as "Grilled oyster mushroom, cream cheese, bread chips", "Chickpea tofu, hoisin, yuzu, chard" and "Venison, rosehip, brussels sprout, semolina". Tip: The dishes also lend themselves to sharing, so you can try different things. Don't miss out on the terrific sourdough bread and sweet pastries. Café bar and hostel on the premises, too; public car park 100m away.

Name: Longkushan Eatery
Address: 24 Xiyuan Road, Jin'an, Fuzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: In business for over 10 years, this restaurant has become part of the collective food memory of Fuzhou citizens. Despite the remote location and lack of ambience, locals come in droves for well-made home-style dishes and seafood at wallet-friendly prices. The deep-fried Bombay duck in peppered salt seduces with velvety meat and a crispy crust. Drunken spare ribs in sweet and sour sauce feature layers of textures and subtle warmth from the spices.

Name: Longman & Eagle
Address: 2657 N. Kedzie Ave., Chicago, IL, 60647, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit cards not accepted,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Since opening in 2010, this gastropub has defined what it means to look like one thing but cook like something else. A long bar stocked with a breathtaking whiskey selection and excellent draft beer anchors a dimly lit dining room fitted top to bottom with wood; its tiny kitchen relegated to a corner. And yet, what lands on the table is far from ordinary bar food. Think terrines made of rabbit and pork or stroganoff paired with sweetbreads. The daytime menu is especially enticing. Cured salmon with crispy potato pancake is a meal unto itself, while the omelet has few equals, a singular triumph folded around mushroom, sweet leeks, and melted brie. Neighbors wander in from morning until night, happy to be back at a place that feels like home.

Name: Longo Seafood
Description: The parking lot is likely full, and you may have to wait for a seat, especially on weekends, but this Cantonese parlor in Rosemead is more than capable of handling its crowds. Open since 2017, the restaurant earned its success without the familiar dim sum carts and through plates big and small that arrive freshly prepared, carefully seasoned and appropriately hot. Golden-brown skewers of sugarcane shrimp, plump orbs of pork siu mai and fluffy steamed buns filled with char siu all delight. Best of all may be the rice noodle rolls flecked with barbecue pork.

Name: Loquita
Address: 202 State St., Santa Barbara, CA, 93101, USA
Description: Loquita is located just blocks from the beach and inside a cream-tinted building with a red-tiled roof. Small and stylish, the space oozes with creative flair—picture colorful tiles, a humming bar framed by soft pink stools, and starburst light fixtures. Find a perch at the beloved wood counter or outside in the inviting and attractive patio. Servers know the menu by heart, so follow their lead and start with tapas like crusty pan con tomate, before digging into hearty chorizo y pollo paella. An homage to the El Bullí olive is a contemporary signature, while carpaccio garnished with pickled mustard seeds and aged sherry vinegar is fittingly popular.A separate gin and tonic list, complete with iterations of the classic, makes a great kickoff (and sendoff).

Name: Lore Bistroo
Description: The sister restaurant to neighbouring UMA is a characterful modern bistro which sits in a cavernous warehouse overlooking the harbour at Port Noblessner. Steel girders, hoists and concrete pillars provide the backdrop, while an open kitchen adds to the buzz. Assured, modern dishes are inspired by the owners’ travels, ensuring you'll always find something that appeals. Go for the Lore Experience menu if you fancy sharing dishes served family-style – and if you see crêpes Suzette on the menu, be sure to give them a try! Friendly service rounds out the experience perfectly.

Name: Loreto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The López sisters, with Irene in the kitchen and Eva in charge of front of house and wine, surprised us in this centrally located aristocratic property, the former family rooms of which been transformed into comfortable, classic-style dining rooms. The chef, who previously studied chemical engineering, has taken advantage of her knowledge in this field by applying the principles of molecular reactions to her recipes, which are unsurprisingly based around local ingredients. On the à la carte, which is complemented by two tasting menus (Origen and Inspiración), you’ll find unmissable dishes such as the confit artichoke, roasted onion hollandaise sauce and murcian lamb bresaola. As you would expect, the wine list is heavily focused towards wines from Jumilla and... they've got a great selection of artisan breads!

Name: Los Camellos
Address: C. 24 Sur 703, Azcarate, Heróica Puebla de Zaragoza, 72501, Mexico
Description: This colorful taqueria can do it all. Away from the historic center and close to the ecological park, this quiet spot has a small but focused menu that delivers wonderful tacos made with soft, plush, flatbread-like pan árabe. Both the tacos arabe and taco pastor variations are worth trying, each one waiting to be dressed up with a fiery salsa. Not to be missed are the excellent cemitas, which arrive hot, toasted and filled with melty queso. A side bowl of charred, sweet onions is a nice touch to any bite.

Name: Los Carnalitos
Address: 30200 Industrial Pkwy. S.W., Hayward, CA, 94544, USA
Description: From the symphonic blend of top-quality flavors in the kitchen to the brightly hued dining room walls decked with Aztec-inspired figures, this family-run spot delivers a taste of Mexico City. The two brothers behind this operation, which started as a wildly popular food truck, present delicacies like huaraches and quesadilla de huitlacoche that rarely appear on other menus in town. Here, quesadillas are made from house-made tortillas, so try the one filled with squash blossom, queso fresco and tomatillo salsa. Tortas are a draw at lunch, while the pambazo—with bread dipped in guajillo sauce and then seared—is divine at all times.The $2 tacos featuring tender suadero and al pastor are a delightful surprise, not unlike their selection of agua frescas.

Name: Los Consentidos del Barrio
Address: Manzanas 27-B, Tlacoquemecatl del Valle, Benito Juárez, 03200, Mexico
Description: Climb the stairs to this second-story restaurant with a large dining room with wood tables and black chairs. The built-in charcoal grill keeps things toasty in the dining room, so you may want to grab a seat on the spacious patio with tall tables and chairs. The house specialty is tacos al carbon, with thinly sliced meat that is skillfully cooked on the grill, then diced. Proteins are the focus here, but vegetarian tacos aren't forsaken. Sliced poblano, nopales and mushrooms are among the top choices. Another can't-miss menu item? Their arrachera, or skirt steak, with its perfectly pink center.

Name: Los Fueros
Description: This typical Bilbao “botxero”, a classic feature of Bilbao’s restaurant scene, opened its doors in 1878 under the name Bar Colón. Today, following its impressive renovation which has seen it retain much of its authentic character, it is one of the most interesting restaurants in the city’s old quarter. Its beautiful bistro-style interior provides the backdrop for an impressive à la carte (including “media ración” options) that features Bilbao’s most representative and typical dishes, all presented with a contemporary flair, alongside two enticing tasting menus: “Gourmand” and “De Bilbao de toda la vida”. Don’t leave without trying the legendary grilled prawns!

Name: Los Reyes Magos
Description: The second-generation chef passes on the Catalonian cuisine that the first-generation chef acquired in Barcelona. Salad of sardines and egg like grandma used to make honours the memory of this couple’s mentors. Dried cod and parsley sauce and homemade sausages convey the flavours of Catalonia, while the well-worn pots attest to the popularity of the paella. Cuisine interwoven with warm memories echoes the journey this restaurant has traced.

Name: Los Sentidos
Description: Los Sentidos occupies a restored house with an imposing stone façade in the centre of town, behind which the contemporary design of its dining rooms comes as something of a surprise (the main room stands out, in particular, as it is brighter and overlooks an internal patio). Owner-chef Juan Pablo Gámez is strongly committed to contemporary cuisine that showcases the bygone flavours and history of Jaén, adapting regional recipes with his modern culinary techniques. The à la carte, which always features plenty of daily suggestions, is complemented by two tasting menus: “GastrÓleO”, which extols the virtues of extra virgin olive oil; and “Un guiño a la TIERRA” (literally, “A Nod to the Land”), the latter only available by booking ahead.

Name: Los Tacos
Address: UGF, One Uptown Residences, 36th Street, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig - Metro Manila, 1214, The Philippines
Description: This casual space featuring glass walls, concrete and soaring ceilings has a simple yet sophisticated modern feel. The buzzing open kitchen sets the stage for bold Mexican flavours. Try the Wagyu beef cheeks and chorizo campechano tacos with house-made tortillas crafted from a blend of Mexican corn types. Vibrant ceviche with leche de tigre and seafood tostadas round out a menu rooted in tradition yet full of personality.

Name: Losange
Address: 100 rue Saint-Germain Ouest, Rimouski, G5L 4B6, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Tommy Roy's restaurant is a unique place. The decor and food have all the makings of a regional bistro, with the long counter that is perfect for watching the chefs at work in the semi-open kitchen. The apparent simplicity of the food belies the explosion of flavours to come. Each bite paints a vivid picture of the countryside: a simmered and braised split pea and lentil soup – reminiscent of an Indian dal; roast pork, confit potatoes, root vegetable purée and jus. Be sure to save room for dessert: the scrumptious tarte à la farlouche (traditional Québec pie filled with molasses and raisins) surpasses even the best home-made versions! Special mention for the cocktail selection.

Name: Lotters Wirtschaft - Tausendgüldenstube
Description: Hotel Blauer Engel not only offers lovely guestrooms, it is also home to this restaurant. With 360 years of tradition to its name, it oozes historical charm. Warm wood panelling lends the space a cosy atmosphere, and the old tiled stove is a quaint detail. Added to that is service with a personal touch and very good food – to be sampled à la carte or in set menu form. Lotters Wirtschaft brewery is also pleasant with its rustic-style vaulted ceiling.

Name: Lou Kei
Address: Shop H&M, GF, Vang Kei Building, 12 Avenida Da Concõrdia N, Macau, Macau, Macau SAR
Description: Though slightly out of the way, Lou Kei is a firm favourite among locals for a simple, good value supper. For over 20 years, its sizeable selection of tasty noodles, congee and Cantonese dishes has won the hearts of countless diners. With heaps of crispy fried garlic and chilli bits, the typhoon shelter-style deep-fried Bombay duck is delicious. Claypot rice with eel in black bean sauce boasts firm, oily fish on crispy scorched rice.

Name: Lou's (Nantun)
Address: 65, Section 3, Xiangshang Road, Nantun District, Taichung, Taiwan Region
Description: Sesame oil lover alert: this no-frills shop is famous for cooking with the earthy, nutty oil. Simmered for a whole day, the sesame oil chicken leg soup exudes intoxicating aromas of wine and herbs. Another must-try are their egg noodles tossed in Taiwanese dried shrimp sauce. Sun-dried shrimps from Keelung are ground and slow-cooked in scallion oil for 10 hours producing rounded flavours rich in nostalgic charm, alongside savoury umami.

Name: Louyau
Address: 15 Xiaoyun Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The retro Hong Kong-style interior with a double-height ceiling and a mezzanine feels cosy thanks to warm wood tones and lighting. Specialities are showcased in the Cantonese barbecue corner and live seafood tanks; other highlights include their hand-crafted dim sum and hearty soups that take up to six hours to make. The sugar-coated Chinese doughnut is made the traditional way, for a crisp golden crust and moist custardy centre.

Name: Lu Bo Lang
Address: 115 Yuyuan Old Street, City God Temple, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: After a makeover in 2019, the room now boasts wavy silvery panels on the ceiling and recessed lights emitting a subtle green glow. Despite the update in décor, the menu stays the same so expect food that is as tasty and reasonably priced. Shanghainese dim sum is still the key draw - turnip pastry, osmanthus glutinous rice cake and ‘eyebrow’ pastry are the must-try items. Private rooms on the 2nd and 3rd floors can cater to parties of various sizes.

Name: Lu Niang Zi (Huli)
Address: 161 Jiangtou West Road, Huli, Xiamen, Chinese Mainland
Description: This simple shop is famous for beef noodle soup and noodles dressed in beef ragout. The signature beef noodle soup with pickled cabbage is a must – the beef long loin is perfectly cooked to be tender but firm. The beef bone stock is flavoursome, and the pickle cuts through the richness. The red-braised beef noodle soup, and the marinated meat platter with dried tofu, hard-boiled eggs, beef tripe, intestine and shin are also popular.

Name: Lucali
Address: 1930 Bay Rd., Miami Beach, FL, 33139, USA
Description: Although it's located in sunny South Beach, Lucali exudes a charming rusticity that calls to mind its original Brooklyn locale. The greenery-adorned, umbrella-shaped sidewalk is ultra-tempting; or beat the heat and find a seat inside—outfitted with plank floors and chunky tables. The wood-fired brick oven at the rear is sure to stoke the appetite. The 18-inch pizza is lusciously charred and sports a light crust crowned with fresh pomodoro sauce, a combination of cheeses and fragrant sprigs of basil. Various toppings are offered to embellish the pie, and one may even choose to have just half dressed with say, meatball crumbles and green chili slivers.

Name: Lucie Cocina
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Lucie Cocina exudes Spanish charm without resorting to clichés. Set on a street corner, the restaurant has been decorated with an eye for detail, from the mosaic floor and wall panelling to the wooden cabinets and counters displaying fish and seafood on ice. A love of Southern Europe is immediately apparent. Chef-patron Will Ermens translates that passion into familiar, mid-sized dishes prepared without unnecessary frills and with a clear focus on the ingredients. Boquerones in a bright, tangy marinade with cherry tomatoes and dill are a fine example. Raw sea bass is equally impressive, its delicate texture complemented by a bright, sweet calamansi vinaigrette, avocado cream and ají amarillo. Desirée expertly guides you through this vibrant menu, which is excellent value for money, encouraging you to sample widely.

Name: Lucky
Address: 452/90 Thathong Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This well-established, low-key local favourite serves Southern Thai food in a relaxed setting. As well as seafood and freshwater fish, the Thai-Chinese-leaning menu features several pork dishes and a few with chicken or beef. Bold Southern curries sit alongside wok-fried classics; begin with a spicy yum salad and ask for local fish prepared to your liking. Enquire about the daily specials – the kitchen's confident touch ensures vibrant, comforting fare.

Name: Lucky 8
Address: 1812 S. Osprey Ave., Sarasota, FL, 34239, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The spirit of New Orleans is alive and well in Sarasota’s Southside Village. Open for lunch and dinner, the restaurant draws inspiration from a range of Cajun and Creole classics. Chicken and andouille sausage gumbo with pickled banana peppers is a comforting effort, as is the barbecue shrimp with superb French bread. Crispy suckling pig with herbs dressed in nuoc cham honors Louisiana’s Vietnamese community. The colorful dining room leans kitschy and vintage and is run by a friendly team that’s always happy to help.

Name: Lucky Indonesia
Address: 46 Tung Ming Street, Kwun Tong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: For over 30 years, this tiny gem has been famous in the neighbourhood for its authentic Central Javanese cooking. The room feels cosy and youthful after a facelift and the food is as tasty as always. For chargrilled satay exuding an addictive smoky aroma, choose from lamb, pork and chicken varieties. Lontong capgome is sticky rice balls with several side dishes such as beef rendang, opor ayam and pindang egg. Pair with an iced longan drink.

Name: Lucky Leek
Description: "Fine Natural Dining" is the concept here at this inviting restaurant. Charming staff serve up vegan cuisine in the form of a three- to seven-course tasting menu – it's also possible to order à la carte. The buckwheat gnocchi, beetroot and sesame cream serves as a fine example of the intriguing dishes available. Made with seasonal vegetables, the creative, plant-based dishes are packed with flavour, and they are popular with international visitors and locals alike. In summer, the best place to dine is on the terrace out front.

Name: Lucky Seafood
Address: 28/1 Phran Nok-Phutthamonthon 4 Road, Bang Phrom, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: This gem of a place serves fresh seafood with Thai flavours, featuring house-made curry and chilli paste. Order in advance or call to check availability. Try the stir-fried crab with bird's eye chilli or the non-spicy stir-fried squid with curry powder.

Name: Lufu Nola
Address: 301 Saint Charles Ave., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
Description: Two friends with a passion for food and respect for their roots. That's the origin story of Lufu, or "let us feed you," Nola. Aman Kota and Sarthak “Shan” Samantray originally did pop-ups but after adding partner and chef Sachin Darade, the three opened this brick-and-mortar in the Central Business District. This is craveable Indian cooking. Tandoori-grilled naan, charred and puffy, wafts with the scent of garlic and butter. Then, if you only get one thing, let it be the dosa. Golden and crisp, it's served with a side of sambar masala and a light green sauce. Chase it with a drink like their Curry Nola-da, a nonalcoholic twist on a pina colada with garam masala and curry leaves.

Name: Lugya'h
Address: 4301 W. Jefferson Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90016, USA
Description: Chef Alfonso Martinez's tlayudas are the star of the show at Lugya'h, tucked inside Los Angeles's Maydan Market. It's a food market, so expect a casual experience where you'll order at the counter and find a seat, but do come hungry, as the portions are hearty. You can also expect a bit of a show, as the hand-pressed tortillas are cooked in comals over a live fire. Filled with beans, cheese, shaved cabbage and salsa, they're exceptionally well prepared. Add protein, especially their standout moronga (blood sausage), and it's easily a meal for two.

Name: Luk Lak
Address: 4A Le Thanh Tong Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 000084, Vietnam
Description: Spread over three floors, chef Madame Binh's venture in Hanoi opened its doors in 2018. It serves a similar menu to its sister establishment in Da Nang, but with a bigger selection plus seasonal offerings. The chef excels in imbuing traditional Vietnamese fare with unique character. Try her Sapa's pork belly dipped in herbal sauce, grilled to perfection and served with mắc mật leaves that cut through the richness and enliven the flavours.

Name: Lula Cafe
Address: 2537 N. Kedzie Ave., Chicago, IL, 60647, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: This neighborhood gem is just as it’s always been and regardless of whether you're squeezed into the main dining room with friends or seated solo at the spacious bar in the adjacent space, the charm of this mainstay endures. The evolving menu focuses on fresh, seasonal, and original fare, keeping it slammed from morning to night. The potato 'nduja tart with cheddar and caramelized onions is spot on, as is the house-made spaghetti tossed with seasoned pancetta and a sweet and spicy chili bean “salsa rosa." Finish over a tall slice of double-layered carrot cake, complete with crème anglaise and a luxurious spoonful of strawberry preserves.

Name: Lulu Baobao (Wong Chuk Hang)
Address: Shop 102, 1F, Metro South Tower 2, 39 Wong Chuk Hang Road, Wong Chuk Hang, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: With custom-made crockery and retro marquetry on the walls and tables, the space feels stylish and spacious. Noodles and buns are handmade à la minute in the glass-clad kitchen, so expect a wait during peak hours. Try their noodles in "gentle" scallion oil – bouncy noodles dressed in the perfect amount of infused oil. The xiao long bao are also exquisitely made with beautiful pleats and soupy pork filling. The combo sets are great value.

Name: Lulu Fusion Bistro
Description: Steps from the historic center, this intimate bistro (a few tables, so reservations are advised) welcomes guests in a contemporary setting anchored by a convivial bar where cocktails can be enjoyed while awaiting dishes. The creative, playful cuisine draws on Asian flavors, skillfully balanced by the chef through the use of local ingredients. In warmer months, a few tables are available outside.

Name: Lum Lai Duck Meat Koay Teow Th'ng
Address: Pasar Lebuh Cecil, 24 Lebuh Cecil, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
Description: For 40+ years, they have been making their kway teow soup the same way – with duck, pork and fish cake. The broth bursts with umami, the duck is silky, and fried garlic and shallot bits add aroma. Expect to queue at peak hours.

Name: Luminosa
Address: The Flat Iron Hotel, 20 Battery Park Ave., Asheville, NC, 28801, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
Description: Luminosa is located at the recently reopened Flatiron Hotel, originally built in 1926. It's an elegant space, with an L-shaped marble bar counter and a dining room that unfolds into several areas with an open kitchen, brass fixtures, black leather seating, and windows dressed with cafe curtains.Executive Chef Graham House and his team strive for zero-waste, butchering whole cows in-house, and sourcing from local farmers' markets. Theirs is a crowd-pleasing menu of wood-fired pizza (perhaps topped with lemon, smoked mozzarella and arugula), impressive pastas (bucatini with summer squash, ricotta salata, chili breadcrumb); and hearty main items like bone-in pork chop with cherry mostarda. Basil poundcake with grilled peaches and honey caramel seals the deal.

Name: Luna Mexican Kitchen
Address: 1495 The Alameda, San Jose, CA, 95126, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Chef/owner Jo Lerma-Lopez's love for food is clear in every morsel that emerges from this kitchen. The name, which means "moon" in Spanish, doubles as an acronym reflecting the team's ethos of "L(local) U(unrefined) N(natural) A(authentic)" cooking. Ingredients are carefully sourced: Rancho Gordo beans, Mary's free range-chicken and house-made staples like chorizo, stocks and sauces all play a role. Fresh tortillas are pressed in-house, and the results shine across the menu, whether in crisp Baja-style fish tacos or sizzling parrilladas served with handmade nixtamal corn tortillas and deeply flavored charro beans. The cooking feels vibrant, generous, and rooted in tradition. The lively cantina setting features a full-service bar and an open-air patio. Having earned its stripes as a neighborhood favorite, it's no surprise that a second location is thriving in nearby Campbell.

Name: Luna Rossa
Address: Via Marconi 18, Terranova di Pollino, 85030, Italy
Description: Nestled in the heart of the Pollino National Park, Luna Rossa is an authentic local trattoria that makes tradition its hallmark. The cuisine is based on traditional recipes handed down from generation to generation, prepared with meticulous care and enhanced by carefully selected local ingredients. From charcoal-grilled carchiola to strascinati made with local flours, each dish reflects the traditions, flavours and culture of these mountains. The experience is made even more engaging by the presence of the owner, a passionate storyteller who knows the local area and its culinary traditions inside out.

Name: Lunasia Dim Sum House
Address: 500 W. Main St., Alhambra, CA, 91801, USA
Description: Few kitchens can prepare a noodle roll quite like this local Alhambra favorite. Rice wrappers filled with gently cooked lobster and finished with a subtly sweet soy sauce arrive on a platter set with the lobster shell itself for a presentation that draws attention from all corners. Indeed, this kitchen puts a fine edge on the area’s dim sum scene. There is not a single cart roaming this elegant dining room, which in turn is managed by a team of fast and friendly servers who will ensure that you never leave less than stuffed. Traditionalists will want to end with a rich egg tart, but for a more soothing finale, order the minced pork congee.

Name: Lunch Lady
Description: Chef Nguyen Thi Thanh's legacy continues at this beloved East Vancouver spot. The menu is endlessly enticing and inspires immediate decision paralysis. One could fill up fast on starters like fried black tiger prawns with fish sauce or beef carpaccio buried under a blanket of fresh herbs, pickled onions and lime vinaigrette. Garlic fried noodles are another big hit, but then will you still have room for the wagyu beef noodle soup?

Name: Lune Siamoise
Description: The spicy scent of lime leaves and curry tantalises your nostrils as you enter this spruce, street-corner edifice, which sports soft lighting and a warm buzzy vibe. The name is a reference to the book written by the chef’s partner. Authentic Thai cuisine is crafted with an intelligent blend of spices, fresh herbs and noodles that are cooked on the spot. An example: spicy green curry of beef, bamboo shoots, spring onions and an impossibly tempting unctuous sauce of lime leaves and spices that are crushed just before serving so that they explode in the mouth to reveal their full flavour. A banquet of exotic generosity.

Name: Lung Khajohn Wat Ket
Address: 109 Charoen Rajd Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: Located opposite Wat Ket Karam, this humble gem of a shop specialises in khao kriap pak mo – steamed rice dumplings with a truly generous drizzle of fresh coconut milk – and neatly wrapped tapioca dumplings brimming with sweet and savoury pork and peanut.

Name: Lung Shall Kitchen
Address: 50 Mu 7, Nongmaikean Road, Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Simplicity and quality go hand in hand at this hidden gem with an intimate atmosphere. Experience food in its most authentic form thanks to skilfully prepared fresh ingredients. The bold yet nuanced stir-fried black squid ink delivers an intense, textured exploration of the sea's flavours.

Name: Lungi
Description: Chef/co-owner Albin Vincent, who hails from Kanyakumari, India, draws on the cooking of South India and Sri Lanka at this Upper East Side restaurant. The expansive menu moves from short eats and kothu to dosas, biryanis and an especially tempting selection of karis. Curry leaves appear throughout, bringing their distinctive fragrance to dishes like chicken Chettinad, where juicy pieces of meat arrive in a deeply flavored sauce rich with black pepper, coconut and warm spices. Hoppers are another highlight, their bowl-shaped form crisp and lacy around the edges and pleasantly chewy toward the center. Tear off a piece and put it to work scooping up curry, pol sambol or the deeply caramelized onions served alongside.

Name: Luo Ji Mian Xian Hu
Address: 56 Xianhou Road, Licheng, Quanzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: By the fading sign and vintage enamelware, it’s not hard to believe this noodle shop opened its doors 40 years ago. It focuses on mee sua gou – a wheat vermicelli soup of porridge consistency. Feel free to jazz it up with toppings like vinegar pork, pork intestine or oyster. Suck up the broth with a fried dough stick. Sautéed pork liver is another must-try: lightly coated in sweet potato starch, the liver has a burnt crust and a juicy centre.

Name: Luscious Dumplings
Address: 919 W. Duarte Rd., Monrovia, CA, 91016, USA
Description: It’s hard to order poorly at this delightful retreat. The menu is concise, with half of the items dedicated to the eponymous specialty. Indeed, this narrow hot spot has been a city-wide favorite since it opened in 2001 and continues to draw lines so long that servers leave a sign-in sheet outside. The secret to their success? Discipline. While many spots make dumplings ahead of time and freeze them, this kitchen starts fresh every morning.It’s best to begin slowly with a tray of boiled pork and celery jiaozi—the wrapping smooth to the touch and boasting just the right amount of bite. Anything pan-fried, though, is the main draw. From juicy pork to fresh chives, these little parcels of goodness have few equals.

Name: Lynx
Address: 427 S. Hewitt St., Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Lynx may be a newcomer, but fans of Joshua Skenes' pizza will recognize this spot's focus. The streamlined menu pulls no punches, focusing on well-crafted pizza with thin, crisp centers and puffy, skillfully cooked edges. Toppings are plentiful but carefully balanced and refined, including options like grilled and thinly shaved raw mushrooms set with stracciatella, mascarpone and buffalo mozzarella. Their Hello Satan V8, with guanciale, soppressata and pepperoni with firebird tomatoes, basil, fermented chili and a drizzle of black and white truffle honey, is especially memorable. There's just one dessert — fantastic soft serve ice cream, perhaps tiramisu if you're lucky — and the strong cocktail program is on point.

Name: Là-Haut
Description: On the top floor of the Parc des Artisans, this contemporary restaurant affords a view over the rooftops and the mountains beyond. The chef homes in on the essentials with his tasty, no-nonsense cuisine. Top-notch ingredients, generous dishes, intense sauces – it all conspires to ensure a pleasant time is had by all. At lunchtime, in particular, there is an affordable set menu.

Name: Là-Haut
Description: Julien and Morgane Ostertag's winning combination of good produce and no-frills, expressive, gourmet dishes creates a moment of indulgence, enhanced by the view over the lake. From the terrace or behind the bay windows of the elegantly decorated dining room, bistronomy is at the heart of the chef's offering: Valentin Chappuis' caramelised pork belly, patatas bravas and crispy sucrine; Mediterranean-style scorpion fish, taggiasche olives, tomato marmalade with basil and panisse. The service is friendly and charming. Don't hesitate to head upstairs!

Name: Léonie
Description: The name is a tribute to the founder of this modest eatery, which opened in the late 1940s. It has since morphed into a pleasant contemporary bistro under the impetus of an enthusiastic young couple who are no strangers to the business. Originally from Deux-Sèvres, the chef fell in love with the Basque Country and its produce and his slate menu stars an updated interpretation of Gallic classics, often with game taking the limelight in season, illustrated by roasted fillets and crispy confit legs of woodpigeon, paired with mashed potatoes and a big-boned jus.

Name: Lê Gia Khang (Ngũ Hành Sơn)
Address: 19 Le Quang Dao Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This shop specialising in Huế-style bún bò makes its robust, savoury broth fresh every day. Pick from four toppings including the signature xí quách: the large L-shaped beef bone lends deep flavour and a wealth of textures – meat, cartilage and fatty edges. For a more varied bowl, try the thập cẩm, which comes with beef blood curd, pork loaf and tendon; the thinly sliced beef tongue is tender and delicate. Arrive early as beef bone availability is limited.

Name: Löwen
Description: With chef-patron Roman Pfaff at the helm, this traditional restaurant is now in its fourth generation of family ownership. He uses carefully selected ingredients, many sourced from the Lake Constance region, to create flavoursome, thoughtfully prepared food. Details of their provenance are provided on the menu. Modern-inspired dishes include matjes-style salmon trout from Lippertsreute with pickled cucumber, apple, spring leek, caper yoghurt and almond and egg white, or straw-bedded pork saltimbocca with courgette and pepper vegetables and potato gratin. Meals are served in charming dining rooms or on the inviting garden terrace, where you can unwind and enjoy the view of the greenery. Tip: The restaurant is popular, so booking is advisable! There are also two rather simple but attractively furnished holiday flats right next door.

Name: L’Abbaye Caladoise
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Old-world charm meets contemporary comfort in this tastefully renovated 15C abbey built entirely of honey-coloured stone. The uplifting cuisine celebrates local recipes and classics: pâté en croûte, pike quenelles, volaille de Bresse with morels, scallop mousse, Rossini pigeon and praline tart. In summer, reserve a table on the pleasant terrace overlooking the courtyard garden.

Name: L’Ardente
Address: 200 Massachusetts Ave. NW, Ste. 100, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Many diners walking into East End's shiny Capitol Crossing development already know what they’re ordering. Chef David Deshaies' 40-layer lasagna has captivated the city’s attention and rightfully so (though it's only available on the dinner menu and at lunch on weekends). Tender short rib, truffled mornay, and razor-thin sheets of pasta make for a delicious trinity that tastes as good as it looks.With soaring ceilings and windows to match, this Italian kitchen has plenty more to offer. A wood-burning grill and pizza oven allude to its other strengths—sit at the counter to watch them fly out. Bucatini cacio e pepe or gnocchi with meaty lamb ragu are just a few of the dishes that satisfy. Do save room for dessert, especially the lime mousse with black currant sauce.

Name: L’Hostal de Ca l’Enric
Address: Carretera Camprodón N 260, La Vall de Bianya, 17813, Spain
Description: This bright, welcoming restaurant just 100m or so from its elder sibling, the award-winning Ca l'Enric, is run by chef Isabel Juncà, who shares her passion for seasonally inspired traditional cuisine through affordably priced day-to-day cooking that definitely does not skimp on flavour. The à la carte, featuring savoury rice dishes, grilled fish and meat, and delicious cannelloni, is complemented by different seasonal suggestions plus an inexpensive yet well-crafted weekday menu. One dish that we can highly recommend, the finishing touches to which are added at your table, is the ajoblanco with a tartare of anchovies and strawberries.

Name: M Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: A cocktail of vitamins! Julien Gautier’s cheerful establishment adds a whiff of exuberance to Lyon’s well-heeled, tree-lined Avenue Foch. The smart interior sports a muted blue and flashy orange colour scheme, felt grey designer armchairs, linen tablecloths, a bar and a wine cellar encircled by a conservatory… The similarly charismatic service is as smooth as a silky béarnaise sauce. In the kitchen, the veteran and talented chef, formerly of Léon of Lyon, rustles up an appetising, market-sourced menu, combining flawless technique and know-how in a bid to pamper our tastebuds with delicate flavours tailored to modern appetites. The honey-flavoured madeleines served with a fromage blanc sorbet are awesome!

Name: MAKfam
Description: What began as a pop-up back in New York City, where owners and married couple Doris Yuen and Kenneth Wan first met, and then became a stall in a Denver food hall, has its own proper space, complete with bar and counter service. The cozy, winsome room and the compact menu both celebrate the pair's Chinese American roots, both having been raised by immigrant families who worked in restaurants. Fried crab and cheese wontons and hand-shaped chicken and chive potstickers are inspired by Chinatown favorites and takeout staples, made with particular care and big flavor. Chicken wings with a spicy, tingly málà seasoning are favorites with good reason, and larger dishes, like the familiar-yet-inventive corned beef fried rice impress as well.

Name: MAMA Oakland
Description: Opened by a husband-and-wife team, this alluring spot has its simple yet chic look down pat, with dark green ceilings, brass-and-glass chandeliers and live plants scattered throughout. The premise is straightforward, offering a reasonably priced, three-course dinner with no reservations. Choose one of two options for each course, like a soup or salad tailed by pasta and dessert. Items change often, but one constant is house-made pasta dressed with a hearty tomato sugo featuring braised pork and beef, which also served as the inspiration behind this establishment. The wine list is full of interesting labels and employs symbols for easier navigation.

Name: MAST Weinbistro
Description: Set in a historical town house, this trendy place is a winning combination of modern wine bar and upscale bistro. It is very popular for its great food, is made with seasonal ingredients sourced from local producers – and at fantastic value for money. Organic and biodynamic wines are recommended to accompany your choice of dishes. There is an appealing outdoor dining area, too.

Name: MASTAN
Description: What a charming place! The classic bistro feel of this compact restaurant in Kreuzberg is inviting. Cordial, attentive and professional service also contributes to the pleasantly relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere. In the kitchen, chef-patron Yann Mastantuono, who hails from southern France, gives expression to his passion for French bistro cuisine. Be sure to try the charcuterie, eg the "Bauernterrine". The "gambas tartare, citrus fruits and bottarga" or "veal tongue in charcutière sauce, grenaille potatoes in butter" are unfussy and delicious. In summer, head for the secluded terrace.

Name: MEIER
Description: This restaurant with a delightful garden and terrace enjoys a fabulous countryside location. Traditional and modern elements are combined to winning effect. Run by the Meier family, the attractive HILZHOF is home to chic guestrooms and the small fine dining restaurant HIO, as well as MEIER. Their flavoursome cuisine places the quality and provenance of the ingredients centre stage – it follows the seasons and uses organic ingredients sourced locally, if not from the family's own vegetable plot and herb garden. Local producers are credited on the menu. The staff are exceptionally charming.

Name: MIURA
Description: The interior design of this restaurant is sleek and modern, in keeping with the futuristic look of the hotel that houses it on its first floor. Diners sit in an airy, high-ceilinged room lit by chic designer pendant lamps – large floor-to-ceiling windows afford magnificent views of the surrounding countryside. Choose from an appealing selection of regional and international classics, or opt for the tasting menu. Full of flavour and depth, the dishes are testament to the skill of the kitchen team.

Name: MN Santa Inés
Description: The first thing that strikes you in this simple, unpretentious restaurant, somewhat tucked away in the Buenos Aires district known as “the island” of La Paternal (so called because it is partially enclosed by train tracks and the Chacarita cemetery), is its unique bohemian charm, despite occupying the former premises of an industrial bakery. From this period in its history it has preserved an old oven, some of the large tables used to knead dough that are now used by guests, and countless vintage items (old TVs, bread shovels, antique crockery, weighing scales etc) which add a genuine touch to the decor. Here, chef Jazmín Marturet showcases her cooking on a concise and contemporary à la carte featuring eclectic details and a hint of fusion which changes regularly but retains a strong commitment to her taste for spices and the tangy flavours she has discovered on her travels around the world. The ambience here is both relaxed and authentic, and the restaurant is popular with a local clientele.

Name: MOLÁM
Description: A fun evening out is on the cards at this lively spot inspired by the night canteens of Bangkok. An open kitchen and vintage vibe contribute to the party atmosphere, which is helped along by a range of Thai-inspired cocktails. The authentic menu covers all four regions of Thailand, with vibrant dishes delivering the hallmark blend of sweet, sour, spicy and salty. Sharing is encouraged and the dishes are well-priced, so don’t hold back when ordering.

Name: MOUT & HOUT
Description: Beer and fire are at the heart of this establishment, whose name translates as "Malt & Wood". Next to the Beerze family brewery, which is steeped in history, there is an American-style bar with a stone pizza oven at the front. The back of the restaurant has a raw industrial feel. The chefs like to work with the Josper charcoal oven, parrilla grill and Oklahoma smoker to infuse their dishes with smoky flavours. For example, they put a unique twist on vitello tonnato by searing the veal on charcoal. Of course, meat takes centre stage in these generous and ingredient-led dishes, but there are also vegetarian and fish options on the menu to whet your appetite.

Name: MP Thai (Vision Exchange)
Description: This simple shop may not be the most atmospheric, but its tasty food in generous portions at affordable prices always attracts a crowd. With a Thai owner and all Thai kitchen team, rest assured that the food is as authentic as can be. The tom yum soup strikes a fine balance between sour, sweet, spicy and salty tastes; the BBQ squid is nicely grilled and loaded with umami, perfect with the hot and sour sauce. Reservation recommended.

Name: MTR 1924
Address: 69 Jalan Thambipillay, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur, 50470, Malaysia
Description: This international chain, which began almost 100 years ago, now has branches all over the world. This outpost has been a popular dining spot among the locals since 2017. Idli is a soft, fluffy steamed cake made out of fermented rice batter, paired with green chutney and lentil sambar. Masala dosa, or crispy crepe with potato curry, packs a real kick. Uddin vada, or black lentil fritter, is also a good choice. Check out the daily specials and mini meals for combos.

Name: Ma Cuisine
Description: Ratatouille, cassoulet, beef cheek simmered in red wine: familiar regional fare covers the blackboard menu. Special attention is paid to Tokushima pork, which stars in numerous menu entries. Taking pride in the ingredients’ flavours, the chef shares a passion in common with the producers he relies on. A full range of pork cuisine is available, including cutlets and charcuterie. Ingredients are lightly salted to bring out their flavour, and portions are generous. The traditions of French food culture on full display.

Name: Ma Er Si Fang Cai
Address: 159 Fengshan Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant started out as a noodle shop some 20 years ago. What hasn't changed is the authentic and affordable home-style Hangzhou food it serves. Browse the photos on the wall or pick something from the live fish tanks. The oil-blanched live river shrimps are fried until crispy and tossed in a sweet savoury sauce with vinegar and scallions. The steamed pork-filled tofu skin roll with dried fish is another timeless umami-laden classic.

Name: Ma Lu Qiao Jiang Tang Mian
Address: 306 East Zhongshan Road, Jiaojiang, Taizhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This shop specialising in ginger broth has been going strong for more than half a century. Every morning at 5 am, the owner makes the broth with ginger that is marinated in yellow wine and sun-dried for a rounded flavour. For starch, order hand-rolled noodles, rice noodles, rice cakes or even steamed rice to go in the broth. Feel free to top up with an assortment of seafood like shrimp, razor clam, mantis shrimp, mud crab or Bombay duck.

Name: Ma Poule
Description: The chef opened a small restaurant, Ma Poule to celebrate the appeal of Jura, in eastern France. This region, with its beautiful forests, valleys and wetlands and its wonderful ingredients and people, made a profound impression on the chef. Chicken and morels in sauce vin jaune is a Jura dish in which the chef takes great pride. This dish is paired with specially produced yellow wine. The façade and interior, and even proprietress’s clothing, are yellow as well. A restaurant filled with love of Jura.

Name: MaMi's
Description: Having gained many years of experience in the fine dining sector, Marcel and Miriam Hertrampf have opened this laid-back little restaurant. For starters, the location is lovely: the street lined with tall trees and buzzing with a lively atmosphere has a charm all of its own – the terrace on the wide pavement is especially inviting. In the kitchen, patron Marcel serves up aromatic modern fusion cuisine, drawing on a wealth of culinary influences from Spanish to Asian. The cuisine is predominantly vegetarian, with fish and meat used sparingly. Flavoursome dishes are served as an eight- or 10-course sharing set menu or à la carte. "MaMi's Bolo" is especially delicious: a spicy beef bolognese wonderfully refined with Asian spices and served on crisp little gem lettuce with sour cream and crispy onions. The service team led by hostess Miriam is charming and professional. As a trained sommelier, the chef's sister provides very sound wine recommendations; the list features over 200 labels.

Name: Maan Muang
Address: 165/6-7 Soi Ramkhamhaeng 112, Ramkhamhaeng Road, Saphan Sung, Bangkok, 10240, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: For 30 years, Maan Muang has been offering Northern Thai cuisine in a rustic, wooden Lanna‐style setting. Celebrated for traditional recipes and seasonal dishes, the restaurant serves steaming soups made to order. One highlight is the bamboo shoot with crab paste soup and pork ribs, in which tender bamboo meets umami‐rich flavours. Complimentary fresh vegetables are served to each table. The go-to eatery for anyone craving a true taste of Northern Thailand!

Name: Mabel’s Gone Fishing
Description: Charm is in abundant supply at this popular gathering place, from the name and décor (both of which honor an owner's beloved dog) to the easygoing, friendly staff. But it's more than just window dressing that draws in the crowds. A focused menu highlights excellent local seafood with a simple-yet-satisfying approach that blends Californian and Iberian cuisine, and the results are undeniably delicious. Case in point is the crispy, meaty swordfish schnitzel, served with salsa verde and creamy tonnato sauce alongside a salad of caper berries and shaved fennel, for a winningly bright, briny combination. Raw items like oysters and simple crudos are a great way to start, and an assortment of natural wines and gin-based cocktails provide top-notch accompaniments.

Name: Macarraca
Address: Navegante Juan Patiño 78, Villanueva de la Serena, 06700, Spain
Description: Under this intriguing name, which is a celebration of an almost forgotten dish from Extremadura, this simple restaurant attempts to revive traditional regional flavours from a modern perspective. The young duo at the helm, Josemi Martínez and Mercedes Rincón, are embarking on their own personal project here after working in some of the finest establishments, some even outside Spain. Both chefs, who throughout their careers have always been ambassadors for the products of their home region, uphold traditional Extremaduran recipes using modern techniques and the best local seasonal produce, bringing them to our palates through their à la carte menu and two tasting menus (Corto and Festival). Standout dishes? Don't miss the unique grilled Extremaduran ensaimada, the boneless Verato-Retinto kid and, above all, their multi-award-winning smoked cheese tart.

Name: Macauda
Description: Fish dishes are the pride of this Italian restaurant, helmed by a chef who apprenticed at a trattoria that specialised in seafood. As he travelled through the various regions of Italy, he became fond of fish cuisine, going on to work in areas near the sea such as Puglia and Sicily. Today he interprets the rural cuisine and homemade pastas he studied in southern Italy through the marine products of Japan. ‘Macauda’ is the name of the house in which he stayed in Sicily that won his heart.

Name: Maccheroni Republic
Address: 332 S. Broadway, Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
Description: With its tall mirrors, tiled walls and tin ceilings, this rustic Italian eatery is every inch the classic trattoria. Hidden in plain sight just across from Grand Central Market, it is a known quantity with the local crowd, who fill these tables at all times of day. A few bites, and you'll be ready to pledge allegiance to the Republic, too.The array of excellent handmade pastas is seemingly endless, like long, tubular strands of bigoli della nonna, headlinng an impeccably balanced angus-and-sausage ragout. Then, try to pry yourself away from the noodle nexus and savory tomato-based sauces to savor freshly baked olive oil bread, deliciously paired with bites of polpettine di gamberi. Be sure to finish with a creamy affogato and be on your merry way.

Name: Machado
Address: Rua Doutor António José de Almeida 467, Maia, 4475-456, Portugal
Description: Quality and quantity are both guaranteed at this restaurant occupying an old house in a small village close to Maia. Several separate dining rooms, all with a similar rustic decor, simple table settings and lots of typical decorative details hanging from the walls. Here, it is impossible to leave hungry given the copious portions on the traditional home-cooked menu which teems with local flavours. Make sure you try Machado’s house speciality, the Lafões-style roast veal.

Name: Macok Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Set on a cobbled street in the Old Town, alongside the castle walls, this bright, colourful bistro is known by food-lovers across the country – and it certainly deserves its reputation. It’s family-owned and professionally run by a friendly team, and the menu is an appealing mix of colourful Hungarian and Mediterranean dishes. While classic flavours are in abundance, presentation is decidedly modern; the wild boar soup is not to be missed, as is the beef cheek goulash. As well as a wine shop, they also have bedrooms, and in summer you can sit in the courtyard beside the working water wheel.

Name: Madame B
Address: Hôtel Burdigala, 115 rue Georges-Bonnac, Bordeaux, 33000, France
Description: At this chic brasserie in the Hotel Burdigala, particular care has gone into the decor, which sports a slightly vintage feel: oak parquet flooring, banquettes and armchairs, black tables and a pale wood console covered with black marble. The chef does an authentic job of turning out skilfully crafted dishes in a similarly nostalgic vein (confit of pork belly, venison stewed in red wine, stuffed cabbage), dotted with contemporary touches and wickedly addictive sauces. The dessert lineup of pastries is equally irresistible, illustrated by a soufflé of sweet chestnut purée and yuzu sorbet.

Name: Mae Malai Thai House of Noodles
Address: 5445 Hollywood Blvd., Unit A and B, Los Angeles, CA, 90027, USA
Description: Just a short walk from their original food stall, this restaurant's strip mall digs are simple but it's a comfortable, welcoming spot with a tempting menu to boot. As the name suggests, their specialty is noodles, particularly boat noodles with a thick, intense broth and your choice of pork or beef, noodle type, and spice level. Fret not if you can't decide, as the bowls are small and ordering two or more varieties might just be the perfect compromise. Don't skip out on their stir-fried dishes, such as the boldly spiced chili holy basil with ground pork, bell peppers, and green beans. For dessert, choose from coconut ice cream or kanom tuay, a two-layer custard featuring a green layer infused with fresh pandan leaf, and a white layer with coconut.

Name: Magari by Oca
Description: Although there may be a number of Italian-leaning restaurants and pizza spots scattered around Vancouver, this simple pastificio invites diners to pull up a chair and savor authentic, well-prepared dishes. They have bistro charm down pat, with black-and-white tiled flooring, a chalkboard emblazoned with the daily specials and a window onto an open kitchen. Consider the specials, then peek into the pasta rolling station and watch as your meal is made. The kitchen's singular devotion to the craft of pasta-making is evident in dishes of studied simplicity, like a single spiraled raviolo with a creamy filling of ricotta, mascarpone, and green garlic with sage butter sauce. The facciamo noi tasting option allows diners to sample an assortment of off-menu pastas.

Name: Magazzino 52
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The dining room, defined by characteristic brick ceilings, retains the memory of its warehouse origins, while the numerous labels displayed on shelves – available for retail purchase at a modest discount – attest to a broad and carefully curated selection, justifying the establishment’s self-description as “wine and dishes.” The kitchen presents a concise yet thoughtfully composed menu built on the quality of its ingredients: nods to Piedmontese tradition, select seafood offerings, and creative touches in the accompaniments, all designed to showcase the principal components. Dishes may be ordered individually or as part of generous and flexible mini-tastings, customizable to the guest’s preference. An excellent address in one of the city’s most elegant neighborhoods.

Name: Magnagallo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a minute’s drive from the Campogalliano motorway exit, this ultra-classic restaurant has made a name for itself over the years thanks to its excellent price-quality ratio, which has remained surprisingly stable even at times when inflation has been high. The menu features numerous traditional Emilian dishes — gnocco fritto, tortellini, and Emilian-style “fritto misto” — alongside some of the great classics of Italian cuisine. The finale is left to the cake counter, situated right at the entrance to the restaurant: a riot of homemade desserts that invites you to choose whatever takes your fancy, following the inspiration of the moment and ending your meal on a truly indulgent note.

Name: Magnolia Café
Address: 131/70, 131/82 Rattanakosin Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 503200, Thailand
Description: With just four large communal tables, Magnolia Café is a simple, cosy spot enlivened by bold colours, vintage décor, and chandeliers. The owner-chef’s exquisite personal collection is on display, and she pays meticulous attention to sourcing high-quality ingredients, some from overseas. Their à la carte menu offers tasty, well presented fare from across Thailand. Dishes are distinguished by vivid, gutsy flavours; fried sun-dried squid with peanut sauce and fresh watermelon with desiccated salmon are exemplars. A complimentary pandan pudding is offered, making for a sweet and satisfying finish.

Name: Mahaniyom
Description: Childhood friends who grew up north of Bangkok end up in Boston for college. It's not the plot of a cinematic hit; it's the story behind Mahaniyom. This Brookline Village spot, with seating for just two dozen, packs a punch with a highly original menu of Thai small plates and creative cocktails (sip the Mahaniyom Sazerac with Thai tea-infused rye). Dishes to consider include yum som-o, or pomelo salad, a seasonal treat featuring grilled tiger prawns arranged with diced citrus segments, roasted cashews and toasted coconut. Kang pu is a decadent bowlful of house-made red curry in rich coconut milk with crabmeat and rice vermicelli, as well as shredded cabbage and bean sprouts for a lovely contrast of freshness and crunch.

Name: Mahir Lokantası
Address: Cumhuriyet, Tavukçu Fethi Sokak No:28/B, Şişli, Istanbul, 34380, Türkiye
Description: The long queue of locals that forms before opening time speaks volumes – this bustling place is hugely popular. So, be sure to arrive on time and you will be handsomely rewarded with a generous menu featuring expertly prepared Turkish classics. Options include an intense lahmacun with lamb, black Urfa chilli and fresh herbs, a salad that balances spicy, zesty and sweet nuances, and dolmasi with a filling of lamb, beef, rice and herbs. Deciding will not be easy, but you are bound to leave sated thanks to the outstanding value for money. A cherished spot that has truly earned its praise!

Name: Mai Mien Yen Tsai
Address: 106 Anxi Street, Datong District, Taipei, 103, Taiwan Region
Description: Nestled in the Dadaocheng area, this family business is now run by the third-generation owners. It opens at 7am for traditional Taiwanese breakfast – egg or rice noodles served in a flavoursome stock made with pork bones, offal and chicken, or dressed in a sweet sauce. Side dishes like pork offal, boiled chicken and blanched squid are also worth trying, but their signature crispy skin braised pork is only available after 10am.

Name: Mai Yu Lao Sha Guo Zhou
Address: 28-5 to 28-8, Shangmeilinxincun, Meicun Road, Futian, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
Description: The owner used to be a fishmonger, which explains why he is so picky about the seafood he uses in this rustic restaurant. His signature mud crab congee is cooked with dried scallops and dried squid for a burst of umami. Deep-fried Puning tofu is crispy on the outside and creamy inside; dip in chive-spiked brine for extra fragrance. The menu also features other nostalgic Cantonese home-style dishes. Go with a posse because the portions are huge.

Name: Maison Brume
Address: 2 place du Marché, La Chaize-Giraud, 85220, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of a charming village in the Bocage Vendéen, chef Tanguy Rattier cooks up contemporary cuisine rooted in his terroir, underpinned by brilliant finds sourced from local producers. The hearty dishes are packed with bold flavours: hake steak with aubergine pulp and artichokes, a full-bodied jus; peach and blueberry tartlet with a sweetly tart flavour.

Name: Maison Cachée
Description: In the heart of this village with no shortage of medieval charm, this half-timbered house decorated with sculpted faces tells a story. Dating from 1478, it was an inn, then a crêperie and is now home to an inviting restaurant. Alban Chartron and Sarah Alba have brought with them the expertise they acquired in prestigious Michelin-starred establishments (Ducasse, Pic, Crillon), ploughing it into a menu they describe as "pastoral". Their cuisine is generous, well-crafted and often enhanced by just the right amount of peppers and spices. The dishes are run through with authentic accents: juicy pork ribs, melt-in-the-mouth beetroot and tuna; and rice pudding sprinkled with roasted seeds. Wallet-friendly bistronomy in an original and eclectic setting.

Name: Maison Vidal - Le Bistrot de Justin
Description: Le Bistrot de Justin pays tribute to the grandfather of chef Aurélien Vidal (that's him in the mural). Justin and Odette Vidal opened a buvette (bar, café, restaurant all in one) on the village square in 1954, which has since morphed into this friendly, inviting bistro. Enjoy indulgent and hearty traditional cuisine that is reasonably priced and draws on the local terroir. Rest assured: the pâté en croûte, which can also be found on the fine dining menu, is still a mainstay on the menu!

Name: Maison Wessman par Thierry Marx
Description: Forming the heart of the stunning Les Verdots wine estate, this detached building in the local architectural style looks out over the vineyards; a travertine-paved terrace is laid out in front. Inside, the comfortable interior is done out in chic bistro-style decor. Chef Thierry Marx has devised a menu that turns tradition on its head: open-field tomatoes with fresh goat's milk cheese, vanilla oil and strawberries; duck confit served with lentils with carrot and dressed in a mustard vinaigrette; floating island with raspberries and custard. The short wine list, of course, highlights the estate and the region.

Name: Maiz De La Vida
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Fans of the food truck can now head to the Gulch for this restaurant’s first brick and mortar location. The vibrant space features colorful artwork and pottery, a chef’s counter and a stunning wall of heritage corn kernels behind the bar. As the name suggests, corn is a point of pride here, and the restaurant works with both imported and domestic varietals to make their own tortillas. From enchiladas doused in salsa verde to quesabirria packed with tender beef, flavors and portions alike are generous. First timers should ask about the wonderfully complex and refined mole negro.

Name: Majchapasuk
Address: 166 Mu 8, Udon-Nong Khai Road, Mu Mon, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: A serene pond encircled by wooden pavilions is Majchapasuk's tranquil setting. Each spot in the expansive seating area has a soothing atmosphere, ideal for savouring local seafood steeped in over 40 years of Isan culinary heritage. Standout mains showcase Isan tradition with seabass and snakehead fish. Don't miss the crispy deep-fried spring rolls stuffed with minced pork and pork skin. Evening promises optimum weather conditions and idyllic pond views.

Name: Mak Man Kee
Address: 51 Parkes Street, Jordan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: No one is here for the no-frills interior, typical of any noodle shop in Hong Kong. This 60-year-old establishment is all about Cantonese wonton soup noodles – firm and bouncy prawns, visible through the paper-thin translucent skin, with springy duck egg noodles swimming in a flavourful broth. The noodles taste equally great when simply tossed in oyster sauce or shrimp roe, the latter also available as a pre-packaged condiment to go.

Name: Maketto
Address: 1351 H St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: Credit to chef-owner Erik Bruner-Yang and his team for keeping it fresh, as it were. On ever-changing H Street, this long-favored restaurant at first looks like a clothing store with its glittering display cases lined with chic merch. More impressive, though, is what’s on the menu: A diverse, ambitious, and consistently satisfying roster of dishes inspired by flavors from across Asia. Everything here is designed to share, starting with the sourdough scallion pancake; or the chicken soup dumplings with peanut chili vinaigrette. What’s next? That should be the crispy fried chicken drizzled with five-spice caramel. There are no rules, no borders, in this house, and diners wouldn’t want it any other way.

Name: Mala Pata
Address: 2431 Crabtree Blvd., Ste. 102, Raleigh, NC, 27604, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: Mala Pata brings a taste of Mexico to Gateway Plaza. This upbeat spot has a lively vibe that spills over to the cocktail bar next door. Plan to start or end your evening with a mezcal mule or pisco sour.As for the food, Mala Pata takes ingredients quite seriously, importing corn from Oaxaca and grinding it in house to make their own tortillas, tostadas and chips. Sip a cocktail and order one of the botanas (snacks) like guacamole or Colombian bunuelos. Of course, tacos are a must and include fish and meat varieties. Whole market fish and beef to share are also available.

Name: Mala Sichuan Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: From Katy to Sugarland to Montrose, this Sichuan restaurant has spread its wings across the Houston area and beyond. The story begins at the original location, which opened in 2011 in Bellaire’s Chinatown. Whereas many Sichuan restaurants submerge everything in pools of chili oil, this kitchen takes a more measured approach. And true to its name, dishes boast a distinct thread of tangy bitterness and tongue-numbing heat but never so much that you’ll sweat. Don't ignore the classics like wonderfully balanced kung pao with soft juicy chicken, pork belly with broccoli or lotus root with a truly delicious sweet and sour sauce. Be sure to bring an appetite, as the portions are very generous.

Name: Malabar Bistró Nómada
Address: Real 14, Becerril de la Sierra, 28490, Spain
Description: Occupying a townhouse in the mountains around Madrid, this restaurant features a patio-terrace at the entrance and a rustic and unpretentious bistro-style interior. Choose between a concise à la carte (including “raciones”, half-portions, and even quarter-portions for some dishes) with no little creativity and a strong focus on dishes designed sharing. These dishes change regularly (on this visit we thoroughly enjoyed the red tuna with a pepper-flavoured butter, and the succulent meatballs made from 7-year -old ox from Buitrago de Lozoya) and are usually based around ingredients sourced locally or from the nearby region, and enhanced by an exotic touch. Excellent technique and meticulous presentation add to its appeal.

Name: Malerwinkl
Description: Whether you prefer traditional Styrian cuisine or more sophisticated fare with a modern touch, this restaurant caters to your tastes. Almost exclusively regional ingredients are used in the set menu and à la carte dishes, eg char with kohlrabi, peas and vegetables and a truffle hollandaise sauce. The wine list with a focus on Austria is appealing, and the selection of wines by the glass is also good. You can opt for a table in the main dining area, in the bright winter garden or on the beautiful terrace. The restaurant is located in an "art hotel", which has 10 individual guestrooms and a holiday apartment. Take a look around the garden with its sculptures by Peter Troißinger Sr – chef, sculptor and painter.

Name: Maligne
Description: The name means “clever” or “cunning,” but you don’t have to be a particularly sharp tool to appreciate the ample charms of this hip, easygoing Seaside gem. The staff is effortlessly hospitable, and the breezy space has a chic loft aesthetic, but it’s the cooking that really makes this place a coup de coeur. The menu draws on Italian-American and French classics (think chicken parm and asparagus with hollandaise), but the feel is thoroughly Californian, with a light, contemporary touch and spectacular local ingredients that make even all-too familiar dishes like Caesar salad memorable—a testament to Chef Klaus Georis’s extensive experience in fine dining. To drive home the point, finish with a spot-on tarte tatin, served warm with softly whipped cream.

Name: Mamak
Address: Shop 082C, East 1 Street, B1 Level, Fashion Tianhe Plaza, 299 Tianhe Road, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Named after hawker stalls in Malaysia, this cheerful little spot in a shopping mall occupies a bold yellow room with Malaysian flags everywhere. With years of history, this is their only shop. The owner also rolls up his sleeves to prepare the country's national dishes, such as laksa (seafood noodle soup) and nasi lemak (coconut rice) served with juicy fried chicken and house-made sambal. For drinks, try the teh C special (three-layer milk tea).

Name: Mambow
Address: 78 Lower Clapton Road, Clapton, London, E5 0RN, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Malaysian Heat + Juicy Wines’ is the strapline of Vanessa Fernandes and Abby Lee’s restaurant – that means exhilarating dishes inspired by Abby's family recipes, alongside natural wines. Start with the terrific '100+ Sour' cocktail and then order plenty of the delicious food to share. While the menu changes frequently, expect eminently satisfying dishes like Otak-Otak prawn toast or squid stuffed with pork belly mince – and don’t ignore the Kerabu section. There's a great atmosphere around the room and there are also a few seats on a semi-covered terrace at the back.

Name: Mammom
Address: 23 Phan Dinh Phung Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Built on devotion, this kitchen pays homage to the traditional home cooking of Vietnamese mothers. The chef brings a decade of experience to bear in a repertoire of nearly 100 dishes covering Southern, Central and Northern specialities, each gently cooked with authentic seasonings that preserves their rustic character. In the clam broth, brightened with tomato and pineapple, the clams are deliciously tender, and sweet and sour flavours are expertly balanced.

Name: Man Heng Ji
Address: 14 Ping'anli West Street, Xicheng, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This brand established on the Niujie halal restaurant strip is famous for instant-boiled mutton, a traditional Beijingese charcoal hotpot dish. It is prized for its premium lean lamb from the Mongolian grasslands without a gamey taste, alongside beef from around the world. The bite-size flatbread goes well with the hotpot. Round off with sweet flatbread covered in sesame sugar. Rows of copper steamboats set the scene indoors.

Name: Manam at the Triangle
Address: Restaurant Arcade, Ayala Triangle Walkways, Makati - Metro Manila, The Philippines
Description: Manam's flagship restaurant in Ayala Triangle elevates the brand with its minimalist lines, vibrant Filipino pop art and airy, polished aesthetic. It feels welcoming despite its spaciousness. The extensive menu fetes Filipino flavours – try the Tagalog beef cheeks with calamansi, the spatchcock chicken inasal or the standout lechon manok with tutong longganisa rice with a playful choice of gravy: Red Horse beer or Sarsi.

Name: Manat
Description: This old building with thick stone walls a stone's throw from Saint-Jean-Baptiste Cathedral has been appointed in a minimalist vein with an open kitchen, a large corner counter and pale wood tables; it is regularly packed to the rafters and with good reason, so be sure to book. At the helm are Franco-Japanese couple Yuka and Marc Meya, a highly inventive pair whose seasonal cuisine designed for sharing brings together Catalan and Japanese ingredients, drawing on the culinary techniques of both countries. Mainstays on the menu include the iconic karaage, boneless chicken deep fried in oil, served with fresh shiso leaves and spring onions; or a tasty tataki of locally fished bonito, leeks and wild garlic.
