Rustic décor adds to the welcoming feel, as do the polite, helpful service team. The sharing plates offer great value and have a playful streak, as evidenced by the pig's cheek glazed in Henderson's Relish, the cult condiment from nearby Sheffield. The wine list is concise but, refreshingly, it’s all available by the glass – and the local ales are understandably popular.

Name: Norrlyst
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: If you’ve been wandering Strøget – one of Europe’s longest shopping streets – you’ll do well to stop off at this intimate basement bistro: a cosy neighbourhood spot with a bubbly atmosphere and a laid-back feel. At lunchtime it’s all about smørrebrød and schnapps, aquavit or local beer, while in the evening they serve a set four-course menu. Local ingredients lead the way, with some produced organically or biodynamically, and all freshly picked or caught. You might find ‘fish of the day’ royale with trout roe or duck breast with smoked marrow, cherries and black trumpet mushrooms – and they offer vegetarian menus too.

Name: North Street Kitchen
Address: 55 North Street, Fowey, PL23 1DB, United Kingdom
Description: In the busy months you might have to queue at this simple, trendy boat house conversion – but it’s well worth the wait. The menu is constantly changing as it’s informed by the freshest catch from nearby waters, with the array of seafood allowed to shine with a delicious purity thanks to the simplicity of the preparations. Fowey oysters are often a favourite, as is the lip-smackingly delicious brown crab rarebit. There’s an endearingly rustic, no-nonsense feel to the place and the chefs cooking in an open kitchen adds to the buzz.

Name: Noto
Address: 47a Thistle Street, Edinburgh, EH2 1DY, United Kingdom
Description: Following the success of aizle, Stuart Ralston took inspiration for his next restaurant from time spent in New York, naming this small plates spot after his NYC roommate, Bob Noto. It’s been a hit ever since, offering well-conceived dishes at sensible prices that are ideal for sharing. The culinary influences span the globe, with a particular focus on a range of Asian cuisines, be that through duck bao buns or a luscious chocolate and miso dessert.

Name: Noto Toto Teuchisoba Tabiki
Address: 1-3-6 Horyuji Nishi, Ikarugacho, Ikoma-gun, Nara, 636-0114, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Pets not allowed
Description: Seiji Matsushima grows crops and makes pottery. He doesn’t just knead earth, though, he also kneads soba. The thin juwari soba set out on dishes he made himself exudes rusticity and the way of life of a self-described farmer. He grows the buckwheat berries for the sobagaki himself. Basil picked in the field in the summer is served with soba topped with a thick dashi-rich sauce, and winter yuzu is served with hot soba. Grated daikon is used in place of wasabi.

Name: Nova
Description: Surrounded by the trees of the tranquil Hoge Bergse Bos, with an intimate terrace and jetty overlooking the River Rotte, and a cosy, luxurious interior, Nova is a truly wonderful place. Your elegant hostess extends a warm welcome, and chef Vaandrager presents an enticing set menu with options for each course. His modern cooking draws on French traditions, highlighting pure flavours and refined presentation. Expect dishes such as lightly seared Argentine prawns with melon, curry and a sesame crisp, or medium-rare lamb fillet accompanied by ratatouille and succulent lamb neck. Seasonal asparagus dishes further demonstrate his flair for generous, comforting flavours. Excellent value for money makes Nova all the more appealing, as does the opportunity to explore the Rotte by boat while enjoying a few delicious bites.

Name: November Brasserie
Description: This Japanese brasserie in a bustling neighbourhood of Prenzlauer Berg entices diners with an interesting range of Japanese specialities in the evenings – including sushi and sashimi, of course. The flambéed toro nigiri, for example, is a treat. Other draws of this place include competent service courtesy of a friendly and down-to-earth front-of-house team, and the pleasingly bright and modern minimalist-style interior, complete with a small sushi counter, where you can see the chefs at work. In summer, the outdoor tables shaded by trees are highly coveted.

Name: Nub
Address: 642-644 Chomphon Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: The owners, originally from Suphan Buri, specialise in beef and offal noodles simmered over charcoal in a smoky, clear broth. The mixed beef luak chim features braised beef, beef slices, beef balls and offal tossed with dark soy and a squeeze of fresh lime, creating a distinctive flavour combination.

Name: Nulle Part Ailleurs
Address: rue de la Gare 10, Couvin, 5660, Belgium
Description: The Corman brothers have been at the helm of this vintage looking restaurant for over 25 years. In the Absinthe bistro, the accent is on soul-warming fare such as Chimay-flavoured cheese fritters, duck cassoulet and veal stew. We also recommend the Bib Gourmand menu that is more polished, but equally Gallic in leaning. For example, the chef might pair salmon marinated in herbs with different textures of red beetroot, green apple, a gherkin mousse and a few dabs of balsamic vinegar. This delicate feast can be washed down with one of the fine bottles that come from the next-door wine shop. To finish your evening in style, spend the night in one of the establishment’s pretty guestrooms.

Name: Nung Wei Hsiao Chu
Address: 56, Lane 92, Section 3, Jingguo Road, Xiangshan District, Hsinchu City, Taiwan Region
Description: With a career in Chinese cooking spanning more than 40 years, the chef opened this family-friendly restaurant a decade ago. The small menu captures the greatest hits of Hakkanese cuisine, but classics such as braised pork belly with shredded bamboo shoot are given a healthy spin thanks to the low-fat, low-salt recipe and a lighter sauce. Portions can be tailored to your party size; booking is recommended due to the limited number of seats.

Name: Nuré
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden down a narrow street in the city centre, this is one of those venues that genuinely surprises. A tiny bistrot with just four tables, welcoming and with a relaxing atmosphere: a small gem made special by a kitchen that reflects the international background of a Korean family that arrived in Zagreb after significant fine dining experiences across Europe and Asia. The dishes, only lightly influenced by their origins, express a precise and creative personality. Among the most requested, the unmissable hummus with broccoli, smoked scamorza, crispy onion and paprika powder, and the excellent rack of lamb with smoked mashed potato, harissa sauce, roasted pepper and green goddess sauce.

Name: Nußbaumerin
Description: In her cosy restaurant, Johanna Nußbaumer recreates a little bit of Austria in the heart of Berlin. Ensconced in a side street off Kurfürstendamm (aka "Ku'damm") since 2008, it has become an institution and an essential fixture. "Authentic... Traditional... Austrian" is the motto here. Tafelspitz aspic on a shallot vinaigrette, Viennese beef goulash with bread dumplings, or apricot dumplings with sweet buttered breadcrumbs are some shining examples. The good selection of wines also originates in the chef's homeland. The restaurant is popular and doesn't have an excess of tables, so be sure to make a reservation! Tip: There are also excellent options to be had at Nussbaumer Heurigen on Breitenbachplatz in Zehlendorf.

Name: Nyonya
Address: 199 Grand St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: Nyonya flaunts a comfy setting composed of brick walls and basic wood tables, but really, everyone’s here for their outstanding Malaysian food. Speedy servers steer diners through the varied menu—and perhaps even away from such delicacies as prawn mee, an exceptionally spiced and sour shrimp broth with noodles, pork, vegetables and bean sprouts floating in its goodness. Some know to stick to such faithful and deeply satisfying dishes as nasi lemak, which is a delightful combo of coconut rice, pickled veggies, crispy anchovies, curried chicken and hard-boiled egg. The chow kueh teow, with stir-fried noodles, tiger prawns and squid, is a go-to dish, while coconut batter-fried jumbo prawns are another winner.

Name: Nénu
Description: It is neither its sober contemporary décor nor its casual vibe that set Nénu apart from the many restaurants in the Avenue Louise neighbourhood, but its anh nhau concept. This Vietnamese culinary tradition involves sharing good food and a glass (or two) of something with friends and family. Start by sipping a delicious cocktail as you discover how the team adds a modern twist to traditional flavours, creating a mouth-watering menu (choose at least three dishes). House-made lamb wontons in a rice wine and pimento oil sauce, with smoked eel, duck’s tongues in pimento and lemon, etc… Superlative Vietnamese fusion cooking…

Name: Nüman
Description: History oozes from the walls of this inviting building, which has housed everything from a butcher’s shop to this discreet little restaurant. Inside it has a charming, understated feel and it's run with genuine warmth, so everyone feels welcome. The seasonal menu offers dishes that are full of flavour; if you like duck then hope that either the duck dumplings or the roast duck breast with wild carrot are on the menu; and who can resist a doughnut for dessert? Prices are more than fair but if you're looking for something special go for the ‘Six Plates Dinner’. Wednesday is Roast Night.

Name: O Castiço (Taipa)
Address: 65B Rua Direita Carlos Eugénio, Taipa, Macau, Macau SAR
Description: This cosy hangout has long been attracting a loyal following for its tasty, homespun food at affordable prices. Now run by the late owner’s son, it continues to welcome diners like family, offering carefully crafted, authentic Portuguese fare. Their signature stewed pork with clams delivers balanced flavours and a pleasant kick due to coriander and a secret sauce. The made to order salted cod fritters are served piping hot.

Name: O Javali
Address: Quinta do Reconco 6 - Estrada Nacional 103-7 KM 5 Nº 6, Bragança, 5300-672, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-oriented establishment near the Montesinho Natural Park, where the virtues of the local Bragança cuisine are showcased. The place, easy to spot as it is right by the road, features a large car park, a public bar and two rustic-style dining rooms, both displaying hunting-themed decorations. The menu showcases regional Trás-os-Montes recipes and game dishes, always in hearty servings and based on fresh produce. Don’t miss the stewed wild boar with chestnuts, hare rice, Bragança-style lamb... or the wonderful grilled wild boar sirloin.

Name: OBBO
Description: Antoine Gaudin, previously Alexandre Couillon's pastry chef, and his associate, sommelier and front-of-house manager, Guillaume Claireau, have opened this feel-good restaurant-cum-wine bar, where good food and good wine (over 200 labels) go hand in hand. The chef rolls out a banquet of cheerful recipes and punchy sauces: grilled green beans with almonds and garlic, a verbena emulsion and samphire. The dessert lineup is decisive proof that the chef has not lost his touch. In the evening, the menu focuses on dishes to share.

Name: OMA
Address: Rua De Oliveira Monteiro, 183, Porto, 4050-442, Portugal
Description: This establishment is run by chef Luís Moreira and his partner Ana Silveira, who left the small village where they began the project to embark on a new urban adventure in Porto. In a welcoming space distinguished by thoughtful décor and soft lighting, they seek to share the experiences gained in the different cities where they have lived, including in Germany (hence the restaurant’s name, which means ‘grandmother’ in German). The chef offers cuisine that combines local produce with contemporary techniques, evolving constantly with the seasons but always seasoned with a dash of personality. Here, a journey of flavours is guaranteed: it begins in Asia, with an appetiser inspired by a destination the chef dreams of visiting, continues through French-inspired dishes such as Foie crème brûlée, and revisits Portuguese flavours in creations such as John Dory served with courgette, jalapeño and pine nuts.

Name: ORA | Taverna & Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: ORA is the kind of place where time seems to stand still. With its Southern European chic and its warm, convivial feel, this trendy restaurant invites friends and family to share dishes evocative of sunnier climes. Full-flavoured wines from around the Mediterranean accompany a feast in which Greek flavours take centre stage. The chefs have a flair for fresh twists – their ceviche, for example, strikes just the right balance between acidity and spice. But you could simply come for the tzatziki with smoked yoghurt and pita straight from the oven, or beautifully tender beef cheek with creamy orzo. This is vibrant, aromatic and rich cooking that instantly transports diners to a summer holiday by the water. A word of warning, though: choosing from the extensive menu is no easy task.

Name: OTHER
Address: 32 Cannon Street, Bedminster, City of Bristol, BS3 1BN, United Kingdom
Description: If you were to ask Chef Zak Hitchman what kind of food he cooks, you may not get a clear answer, such is the variety of influences that he skilfully adopts across the playful, constantly changing menu served inside this small, modish bistro with bright orange walls. Dishes like barbecued trout with a fragrant chive butter sauce are fresh and flavoursome, while the sourdough doughnut is a great way to end for sweet-toothed diners. Everything, including the wines, comes with an appealing price tag and the friendly service is the icing on the cake.

Name: Odd Duck
Address: 1201 S. Lamar Blvd., Austin, TX, 78704, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
Description: Odd Duck began as a food truck and has grown into a lively South Lamar fixture, offering a casual, come-as-you-are atmosphere with seating at a large counter and surrounding tables. The space is relaxed and eclectic, matching the spirit of the kitchen. The menu draws broadly from a range of culinary influences, combining Southern ingredients with global flavors in dishes designed for sharing. Offerings may shift frequently, but often include a mix of Texas seafood, meats and vegetables prepared with a focus on seasonality and bold combinations. With its energetic setting and consistently engaging cooking, it remains a popular destination for diners seeking generous, flavor-driven fare.

Name: Odeon
Address: 165 Gloucester Street, Christchurch Central City, Christchurch, 8011, New Zealand
Description: In an area of the city awash with dining choices, Odeon offers a taste of Andalusia, with sharing plates that look to the Mediterranean and Middle East for inspiration. Much of the produce used comes from the wider Canterbury region, with Akaroa salmon and Lumina lamb the standouts. If you come for dinner consider the ‘Just Feed Me’ menu, a selection of dishes chosen by the chef. The wine list is big on organic and biodynamic wines, while the layout and style of the room make it equally suited to large groups or couples.

Name: Ofício - Wine & Dining Room
Address: Rua Nova da Trindade 11, Lisbon, 1200-301, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This restaurant, located in the heart of Chiado and close to the Jesuit church of São Roque, was born under the philosophy of a contemporary taberna (tavern), however… it is now taking a new path! The starting point is the recreation of Portuguese recipes in the light of current knowledge, always respecting the product and its origins, but without setting limits. The chef at the helm, Maurício Varela, champions a fluid proposal that seeks balance between cold and hot cooking, with constant references to the memory of Portuguese cuisine, spanning from traditional churrasco (barbecue) to conservas (preserves), as well as escabeches and smoked preparations. For them, in pursuit of a living offering, proximity and freshness of raw materials are fundamental to the creative process.

Name: Ogimachi Udonya Asuro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: At this eatery, just off the bustling Tenjinbashi-suji shopping street, lunchtime queues are an everyday sight. The signature dish is Toriten to Taichikuwaten to Ontama Bukkake (udon with chicken tempura, sea bream paste cake tempura and soft-boiled egg). To savour the broth and noodles in their purest form, the hiyakake (udon served with cold broth) is recommended; curry udon topped with an egg yolk is also a popular choice. Any leftover curry broth is best enjoyed with a bowl of rice. With a wide variety of udon and toppings on offer, discovering a favourite combination is all part of the fun.

Name: Oilje
Description: The regulars at Oilje return for one dish: the perilla seed miyeok-guk. The clean broth and nutty perilla seeds pair perfectly to create a flavourful soup. Simple banchan—such as soy sauce for dipping miyeok, nakji-jeotgal, and gat kimchi—round out a well-balanced meal alongside freshly cooked rice. Diners can view the soup and rice being cooked in the gamasot in the spotless open kitchen. The restaurant offers special birthday meals every Friday to guests celebrating their special days.

Name: Oishi
Description: Located in the heart of the city center, Oishi offers a comprehensive tribute to Japan in an intimate, minimalist yet colorful dining room that has been recently renovated. This homage to Japan is evident both in the interior design and – above all – in the numerous and ongoing classic Japanese references throughout the menu. Sometimes reimagined with local ingredients and flavors, the dishes range from crudo and marinated preparations to sashimi and nigiri, rolls, some tempura, and more. The wine selection is respectable, featuring Italian craft beers with flavors consistently oriented toward the East.

Name: Oito
Description: The name comes from the nickname of the first proprietress. Today the fourth-generation chef stands at the counter, preserving the flavours that define Oito. The broth, infused with the savoury richness of the ingredients, has a deep, lustrous colour. Daikon is prepared in several ways, each absorbing flavour differently, while eggs are simmered for days. Items are plated to complement each other, making a beautiful presentation. The broth, handed down from the founder, is truly irreplaceable.

Name: Okane
Address: 669 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA, 94103, USA
Description: Can’t afford to indulge in the exquisite sushi at Omakase? Consider heading to its next-door little sib, where the fish is still top-notch (it’s all sourced from Japan) but the atmosphere is more laid-back. Okane draws lots of nearby Adobe and Zynga employees at lunch and big groups at dinner, all sharing bottles of sake and making the most of the small-plates menu. Sushi is, of course, a must: the nigiri is pristine and delicious. But don’t sleep on the non-sushi dishes—cod marinated in sake lees is grilled to perfection, and broiled salmon aburi with avocado and ikura is delicious too.

Name: Okdolhyunok
Address: D Zone, 1F, Songpa I-Park, 55 Beobwon-ro, Songpa-gu, Seoul, 05841, South Korea
Description: Taste the deeply savory broth and the nutty flavor of the noodles made from 100% buckwheat that intensifies the more you chew at Okdol Hyeonok. The restaurant is fairly new, but it has gained a solid following among Pyongyang naengmyeon connoisseurs. Some of their most popular dishes are mandu with a nuttiness that comes from plenty of tofu in the filling, eobok jaengban, and gajami shikhye. You can also have your favorite wine with your meal for a corkage fee. Enjoy the mild flavors with incredible depth.

Name: Okdongsik
Description: Okdongsik has defined its own refined take on dwaeji gukbap, offering a light, clean broth reminiscent of gomtang. Made from the ham and foreleg of native Korean black pigs raised on Jirisan Mountain, the broth is subtle yet elegant in flavour. Prepared using the toryeom method—repeatedly pouring hot broth over the rice—each grain comes alive, enhancing the dish's depth. The house dipping sauce complements paper-thin slices of pork beautifully. Delicately crafted kimchi dumplings complete the comforting dining experience.

Name: Okàn
Address: 71 Calhoun St., Ste. 100, Bluffton, SC, 29910, USA
Description: In quiet Bluffton, Chef Bernard Bennett cooks from the heart. Sunlight beams through the handsome dining room’s many windows and across cushy banquettes, dangling greenery, and colorful works by local artists. A large bar anchors the center of the space. Celebrating West African, Caribbean, and Lowcountry traditions, dishes are rife with bold spicing and vibrant flavors. Think tender jackfruit fritters with berbere aioli, jerk oxtails with djon djon rice, and curried goat with Carolina gold rice. Generous in both portion and in taste, this is food that radiates comfort and is best shared with friends.

Name: Olaias
Address: Rua Abade Pedro 2 - Centro de Artes e Espectáculos, Figueira da Foz, 3080 081, Portugal
Description: In this restaurant you will have reason to return at any time of year, as the house speciality, Carolino rice from the Mondego — a Portuguese variety grown on the Mondego river — varies with the seasons, so you will always have a new option to savour. From chef Mónica Gomes’s hands, besides the rice dishes made in a clay oven, come house‑baked breads served still warm, the delicious Rissol da Tia Fernanda (Portuguese croquette)… Among the rice options — duck, fish or octopus — you will always make a sound choice, and to finish, our strong recommendation is the Tiramisù made to order with excellent texture. The restaurant is located in the Centro de Artes e Espectáculos (Arts and Performances Centre) and presents careful décor, with large panoramic doors offering lovely views, as well as a comprehensive garrafeira (wine cellar/collection) under sommelier Pedro Ferreira, who is always ready to advise you!

Name: Old Friend
Address: Via Giuseppe Cesare Abba 51, Cagliari, 09126, Italy
Description: Tucked away a little off the beaten track from the main shopping streets, this restaurant charms diners with its contemporary, relaxed atmosphere, featuring stylish design touches, good background music and attentive, professional service. The cuisine strictly follows the rhythm of the seasons, creating original dishes that are deeply rooted in local identity, such as the delicious spiced aubergine with almonds and fig leaves. Beyond individual creations, the common thread is the pursuit of flavour and balance. As well as the à la carte menu, guests can choose from three different tasting menus, which also include dishes created specifically for these menus.

Name: Old Greek House
Address: Davutlu, Şahin Caddesi No:12, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, 50420, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Yes, this is indeed an old Greek house from the 19C, and what a beauty it is! The striking façade with its distinctive traditional balcony, the arcaded courtyard adorned with old frescoes and the open dining area under a canopy of vine leaves make you feel as though you've wandered onto a 1970s film set. Brimming with charm, this is also a true family-run establishment – several members of the Özturk family were even born within these walls. In the kitchen, the matriarch prepares dishes that blend Turkish tradition with Greek influences. A crisp seasonal salad with just enough vinegar and the gentle sweetness of tomato, succulent sac tava, rich baklava with candied nuts… Every bite is a joy. Consider booking an overnight stay in one of the guestrooms – Old Greek House is a perfect base for discovering the region.

Name: Olea Comedor
Description: Honesty is raised to a new level here thanks to the open-view kitchen which is a clear demonstration that this restaurant has nothing to hide! Chef Eduardo Albiol creates cuisine that is both personal and different, adding a modern take to traditional recipes through the use of culinary touches and ingredients from other parts of the world, hence his dishes inspired by the Mediterranean, Asia and South America. His customers are his only benchmarks, so he is constantly attuned to their reaction with the hope that his cuisine will receive their full blessing! Excellent value for money!

Name: Olijfboom
Description: This restaurant is nothing if not nostalgic and traditional, as the exposed rafters and tables laid with crisp white tablecloths and silverware all bear witness. Chefs Jean Vandenberghe and Nick Debeir champion no-nonsense Franco‑Belgian nosh with a focus on the ingredient, sauces and gutsy flavours. Heartwarming, honest food and a back-to-basics, old-school ethos. Order frog’s legs sautéed in a garlic-parsley butter or melt-in-the-mouth Aubrac steak served with freshly whisked velvety béarnaise sauce and piping hot crispy fries. Generous helpings and a truly jaw-dropping wine list add the final touch in this timeless eatery. Pleasure before all else.

Name: Olive & Artichaut
Description: Originally from Nice, the chef moved back to the region with his Breton wife after several stints abroad. He showcases local ingredients in knockout recipes, inspired by the sea and the mountains: pissaladière-style wafer-thin tart with roast black pudding, braised chuck veal with creamy chickpeas and a chocolate and hazelnut praline pie to finish.

Name: Olmo
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Olmo has a true neighborhood feel, where communal tables encourage new friendships, and light wood and plenty of white create a soothing ambience. The food is inspired by Mexico City with a focus on nostalgic, approachable flavors. Find everything from chicharrón preparado and eggplant milanesa to lacto-fermented crudités on this menu. There are so many winning dishes, but the grilled branzino over a bed of stewed beans with a colorful circle of morita salsa is surely one to consider. Carne asada is another can't miss, with a 12-ounce steak topped with a bright salad of verdolaga greens and shaved fennel, but it's that smoky chipotle bearnaise that steals the show. The flan paleta drizzled with caramel hits all the right notes.

Name: Omnivore
Description: Two minutes from Pau Château, on the picturesque Place Gramont, imagine a nostalgic bistro with a zinc-topped counter, wood panelling and upholstered seating. Pau's foodies flock here, sharing good vibes as they tuck into fish fresh from the fish auction or 24hr shoulder of pork. The slate menu features traditional nosh served generously and sometimes enhanced by touches of citrus fruit or well-balanced smoky notes. The jovial front-of-house staff are an added bonus.

Name: One Chun
Address: 48/1 Thep Krasatti Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Merging the owner's fashion design flair and passion for fine fare, One Chun offers a vintage-toned dining experience in a 19C building. Diners still enjoy the family recipes, which have been passed down the generations. Among the specialties, the fresh crab meat with yellow curry and coconut milk stands out for its rich, creamy curry and generous pieces of naturally sweet crab. Be sure to try "Mu Hong" for its bold flavours and soft, tender pork belly.

Name: One More Noodle House
Address: 3370 S. State St., Ste. N5, South Salt Lake, UT, 84115, USA
Description: This family-owned spot in Chinatown Plaza is a come-as-you-are place for a satisfying meal. Order at the counter, then get ready to tuck into appetizers like wood ear mushrooms seasoned with soy sauce and vinegar as well as a variety of noodles with a bevy of broths. Consider their signature braised beef noodles or if you're able to handle the heat, their numbing spicy beef noodles (if you're used to Sichuan peppercorn, opt to go heavier on the spice level here).

Name: Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: This family has been serving onigiri in Asakusa for three generations. Ingredients are arrayed inside a glass case, as at a sushi shop, to be formed into onigiri on the spot. Offerings range from salmon and dried plum to rarer items such as herring roe pickled in sake lees and opossum shrimp preserved and simmered in sweetened soy sauce. Offering a wide range of ingredients allows customers to choose based on their physical condition; the area was once home to numerous bars and pubs, so customers would drop in for morsels to soothe constitutions punished by a night on the town.

Name: Onslow
Description: Onslow, a buzzy landmark in the peaceful Sint Anna district, is depicted by casual dining, a vintage vibe and a terrace that oozes Mediterranean charm. The concise culinary lineup of regularly renewed, playful dishes is designed to share and to entice you to try out new combinations. Lieven Vynck works with familiar ingredients, to which he adds an international spin. An example: succulent, meaty, melt-in-the-mouth mussels in a spicy tom ka khai sauce or a tribute to Italian flair with cacio e pepe pasta. A festival of flavour awaits you at Onslow: “Food with Drinks, Drinks with Food” is their baseline!

Name: Oníric
Description: Under this name, which automatically takes us into the world of dreams, we have found one of those establishments that we would all like to visit; it illustrates that the most longed-for and unattainable projects can become reality. The tandem at the helm, with Jonatan Izquierdo behind the burners and Laura Humanes in charge of everything in the dining room, champions a proposal of modern cuisine built from common sense, with a small menu and three interesting menus: Herrén (executive-style, only at midday during the week), Oníric and Somni. One dish that we loved? The risky but convincing conger eel buñuelos, green curry, coconut and tamarind.

Name: Open Smile
Address: 441 Zhuangjing Road, Xinyi District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: Living up to its name, Open Smile delivers simple pleasure through food. The bright, stylish setting lends an air of relaxation. With braised dishes at its core, the menu highlights Taiwanese-style braised pork, glazed pork belly and deep-fried braised ribs. The pork, slowly braised, is tender with a gentle chew and a balanced sweetness, and goes well with both rice and noodles. Beyond pork, options like chicken with scallion sauce or Sichuan peppercorn oil provide additional variety. For an extra kick, try the house-made chilli sauce.

Name: Oren
Address: 89 Shacklewell Lane, Dalston, London, E8 2EB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The appealing, Eastern Mediterranean-influenced menu at Chef-Owner Oded Oren’s bustling little bistro is made up of enticing sharing plates, with many ingredients cooked over charcoal, such as lamb loin, succulent chicken skewer and hispi cabbage with muhammara. Start with the delicious stone-baked flatbread and then around five dishes between two should suffice. The prices are kept fair and that includes the well-made cocktails, while the service team are delightful. There’s lots of fun to be had here.

Name: Oreno Ramen
Description: Oreno Ramen blends its broth just before serving, creating a frothy soup that pleasantly coats the palate. The paitan, made by boiling a whole chicken, is a milky broth with a nutty flavour and creamy texture. House-made noodles, melt-in-your-mouth chicken, kelp, and egg complete an exceptional bowl. For an extra kick, opt for the spicy broth, and take advantage of complimentary refills of noodles, rice, and broth. Though the restaurant often has a long queue, turnover is quick, so waits are usually short. A side of chilli peppers is also recommended and provided free of charge.

Name: Organization South
Address: No. 209, Block 1, Pebble Walk, 669 Wanxiang South Road, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: The playful, vintage décor with fake tree trunks and red lanterns is aptly matched by a menu disguised as a martial arts instruction book. In addition to famous Sichuanese wok-fried dishes such as green chilli ‘ruthless’ chicken and braised swamp eel, we also recommend the daily specials up on the whiteboard. Seasonal offerings like bitter bamboo shoot and milk cap mushroom are worth a try. Inevitably packed to the seams, book ahead and arrive early.

Name: Oribe
Description: French bistro and teppanyaki cooking are the draw at Oribe. The impressive range of appetisers includes items inspired by French standards such as paté and smoked salmon. Its famous cabbage steak was dreamed up from the essential ingredients of okonomiyaki. Speaking of okonomiyaki, the meal ends with Osaka’s famous savoury pancake, a popular item here. The restaurant was named for the chef’s penchant for Oribe ware, and this style of pottery inspires the green theme for its décor.

Name: Oriental Chao
Address: No. 03-27/62, 3F, South Zone, Suzhou Center Plaza, Xinggang Street, Suzhou Industrial Park, Suzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant in a conveniently located shopping mall serves modern Chaozhou dishes alongside live seafood from Guangdong and Cantonese barbecue dishes grilled in-house. The angled luffa with Chaozhou beef balls, fish balls and pork sausage has a bouncy texture and the sweetness of cucumber. The sachima with olive kernels is an exclusive sweet with fluffy egg-fried batter bits. The set menus are great value. Booking recommended at peak times.

Name: Origen
Description: Located on the ground floor of an old stone building (the same one that houses the two-Michelin-star Molino de Urdániz), Origen showcases the cooking of award-winning chef David Yárnoz, albeit in a much more informal and relaxed format. Directly accessed from the street, it features a rustic-contemporary dining room, bare wood tables and a fixed-price menu (where you choose a starter, main course and dessert), including dishes such as the delicious glazed and baked organic trout with pickled beetroot and parsnips, that adopts a contemporary take on traditional and regional dishes. The continual focus here is on seasonal and locally sourced ingredients, with the option of ordering half-portions.

Name: Oryori Amenimomakezu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: ‘Ame ni mo makezu’ (Be not Defeated by the Rain) is a poem by Kenji Miyazawa about caring for others, unbowed by hardship. Feeling deep affinity for this attitude to life, the owner-chef declares through this naming his intention to live for others through his cooking. Having apprenticed at an izakaya run by a liquor shop, the chef stocks an impressive range of sake from all around Japan. Focusing on how well dishes pair with sake, the omakase-only service also uses fermented seasonings. No-nonsense Japanese dishes mixed with bar snacks express the owner-chef’s unaffected personality.

Name: Ose
Description: After stints in top establishments from New York to Paris, two veteran chefs now swap places every fortnight, taking turns in the open kitchen and the dining room. 100% bistronomic cooking from scratch using local, fresh, seasonal ingredients is the backbone of this bistro in the Abbesses neighbourhood. The menu, chalked up on a slate daily, is bang-on confident with a strong French bias and showcases deceptively simple recipes. ‘Ose’ means to dare – so what are you waiting for?

Name: Osobano Kouga
Description: Taste sake and snacks while dining on soba. Think of the culture of the soba shop, the beloved essence of Edo popular culture, plunked down near Nishi-Azabu Intersection for the modern generation to enjoy, and you have the atmosphere of Osobano Kouga. Evenings bring prix fixe presentations that encourage you to linger over cups of sake. Tensui, tempura soba with the soba removed, is an old-timey snack. Soba in season and appetisers of vegetable or fish of the day are a delight.

Name: Ostaria Pignatelli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A stone's throw from the neoclassical Villa Pignatelli, with the municipal gardens in front and the sea just beyond, lies a haven of authentic charm: you can sit outside or inside, where the décor is reminiscent of an elegant tavern. “You only live once, so eat well” is the motto here, and when you see the dishes arriving at your table, you can't help but agree. Neapolitan classics executed to perfection and served in generous portions: from “mozzarella in carrozza” (fried mozzarella sandwiches) to cuoppo of fried anchovies, from mixed pasta with potatoes and provola cheese to “candele alla Genovese” (pasta with beef ragout), Neapolitan-style cod and “Pastiera”, all of which are truly unmissable. Reservations? Absolutely! Even for lunch.

Name: Ostaria Tyrol
Description: In the heart of this picturesque mountain resort, this contemporary restaurant is situated on the ground floor of the Post Hotel, within the restricted traffic zone. The simple, cosy interiors offer a contemporary take on traditional mountain taverns, featuring extensive use of wood and understated elegance. The cuisine follows the same philosophy: straightforward, authentic and deeply rooted in the region, with a strong focus on meats, cured meats and cheeses. Standout specialities include beef tartare with brioche and cranberries, canederli, polenta with venison goulash and the unmissable strudel served with whipped cream, as well as our own homemade ice cream. Please note that the venue does not accept bookings, but its particularly long opening hours make it easy to visit.

Name: Osteria Bar Sport
Address: Strada Alessandria in San Germano 85, Casale Monferrato, 15033, Italy
Description: In what was once a typical sports bar, the friendly owner-chef serves home-style cuisine featuring traditional dishes from Monferrato and further afield. Don’t miss his plin pasta served with a roast meat sauce and a delicate cream of leeks, cotechino sausage and raw Mazara prawns. The atmosphere here is pleasantly informal and relaxed.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Address: Via A. Boito 26, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Having already proved a success at its Cesenatico and Bologna branches, this modern seafood restaurant has found a particularly picturesque location here, on the ground floor of a building situated between the beach and the small harbour. The cuisine pays homage to Adriatic tradition through simple, comforting dishes, ranging from sardines sautéed in oil and lemon to tomato risotto enriched with fish, served ‘the old-fashioned way’, as the menu puts it. A great deal of attention is paid to fried dishes, the restaurant’s true speciality, while the daily specials are determined by what’s available at the Cesenatico fish market, ensuring freshness and seasonal variety. Rounding off the range are desserts, ice creams and baked goods made in our own bakery, further evidence of our commitment to quality and craftsmanship.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Description: The sister restaurant of the Bologna and Milano Marittima restaurants of the same name, this osteria serves fresh fish with an excellent choice of delicious and generously portioned dishes. As the restaurant doesn’t take bookings, make sure you get here early in high season or during busy periods.

Name: Osteria Bartolini
Description: Under the majestic vaulted ceiling of Palazzo Dondini Ghiselli and in the shade of an old plane tree, this restaurant combines a simple ambience with an innovative concept. Here, guests can enjoy typical seafood dishes from Romagna – don’t miss the delicious sardines sautéed in oil and lemon, which are a real treat!

Name: Osteria Bolognese
Address: rue de la Paix 49, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: Giacomo’s mission is to redress the hackneyed image of ‘spag bol’ and his mouth-watering tagliatelle con ragù alla bolognese does just that! All his ingredients are sourced direct from Emilia Romagna, ensuring an explosion of flavour in the mouth. Our inspectors were treated to taglioni with flash fried bresaola, a syrupy balsamic vinegar packed in bitter-sweet flavours and spicy rucola. A buzzy, vibrant vibe depicts this delightful osteria that will introduce you to the authentic cuisine of Bologna.

Name: Osteria Borsò Gambrinus
Address: Via Capitello, 20, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
Description: Casual and relaxed, the atmosphere is just like that of a typically traditional tavern, consisting of a series of pleasant little dining rooms, while the menu combines local specialities with fresh seafood dishes.

Name: Osteria Didù
Description: A small establishment in the heart of the historic centre, where simple and genuine cooking pays homage to the flavours of the sea and the Ligurian tradition. Quality ingredients, dishes executed with care and a decidedly competitive bill make it an ideal port of call for those in search of authenticity without affectation. Among the most accomplished offerings, the stoccafisso accomodato alla ligure stands out, a great classic interpreted with respect and taste.

Name: Osteria Expanificio
Description: Situated in the historic centre between the Pirandello theatre and the belvedere, this former bakery has been transformed into a modern, welcoming restaurant that has recently been expanded to include an evening cocktail bar (the Buvette del Panificio). The menu features a superb selection of some of the island’s most famous dishes, including stuffed sardines, Robiola goat’s cheese, Palermo-style sword fish and ricotta cassata.

Name: Osteria La Cicerchia
Description: Kumiko Muraji hopes to serve as a bridge between Osaka and her beloved Marche region of Italy. The town where she stayed is renowned for its cicerchia beans, known in Japanese as renriso. Noting that the character for ‘ren’ is the same as her surname, she felt the hand of destiny. A area of foothills and mountains, Marche is a region distinguished for its vegetables and meats. Majolica pottery adorned with cicerchia flower-and-bean motifs complements the shop’s honest fare.

Name: Osteria La Pimpinella
Description: Situated in the historic centre but near a square with a car park, this modern inn serves Piedmontese cuisine which is contemporary in style yet still firmly anchored in local traditions. The generously portioned, well-presented dishes on the menu include vitello tonnato (excellent – we tried it!), tajarin pasta, Bra sausage and casseroles (the soft suckling pig cheek was delicious), all of which are as much a feast for the eyes as for the palate. The restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, aided by proficient and courteous staff with a feminine touch.

Name: Osteria La Solita Zuppa
Description: In the heart of the historic centre of Chiusi, the authentic spirit of a true Tuscan trattoria pervades the air, between evocative barrel-vaulted ceilings and a cool terrace that invites one to linger. Here a love of regional cooking finds expression in the revival of ancient recipes, presented with the generous richness of flavour that characterises the local tradition. Among the dishes recommended by our Inspector, the fragrant artichoke and mint soup and the refined rabbit with ginger, inspired by an ancient medieval preparation, stand out.

Name: Osteria La Torre
Description: To get to this welcoming restaurant, it’s best to leave the car in one of the convenient car parks just outside the town walls a short walk from Cherasco’s quiet, picturesque historic centre with its two perpendicular streets. At Osteria La Torre, the friendly female staff will happily guide you through the menu, which features traditional dishes prepared in contemporary style – we particularly enjoyed the egg, cardoon and fondue dish, followed by breaded veal rump as our main course. If you’re a fan of snails, you really must try them here as Cherasco is renowned for this speciality. The extensive wine list demonstrates the same high quality as the cuisine.

Name: Osteria Le Panzanelle
Description: Just outside Radda, in a small hamlet, a rustic little house welcomes guests with a territorial cuisine that is solid and full of flavour. Handmade fresh pasta, seasonal produce and a well-considered wine list – anything but predictable, and firmly rooted in the local area – contribute to an authentic and satisfying experience. Much appreciated by both tourists and local regulars alike, the restaurant is often full: booking is therefore strongly recommended.

Name: Osteria Madonnetta
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the square with its famous chessboard, this authentic trattoria boasts a warm, inviting dining room and an outdoor space shaded by wisteria. Run by the same family for 120 years, the restaurant serves regional specialities such as tripe soup, bigoli pasta with various sauces, Vicenzo-style bacalà (salted cod), Venetian liver and desserts such as zaeti biscuits and macafame bread pudding. As there are just a few tables and the restaurant is very popular, booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Osteria Magona
Address: Località Vallone dei Messi 199, SP 16/b km 2,400, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Amidst vineyards and the renowned cypress avenue, Osteria Magona is a must-visit for meat enthusiasts and Tuscan regional cuisine aficionados. Impeccable are the famous soups, from ribollita to pappa al pomodoro, alongside gnudi and fresh pastas. The wine list offers ample room to various Bolgheri labels.

Name: Osteria Mondo d'Oro
Description: The osteria as envisioned by celebrated three-Michelin-starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini: a place, indeed, a “world,” where guests can savor fragrant Italian classics and vegetarian options in a relaxed atmosphere at remarkably honest prices, complemented by an excellent selection of wines by the glass. The inspector enjoyed: pasta reale in capon broth, Amarone-braised beef cheek with potato purée and fried leek. Right in the city center, tucked along a side street off Via Mazzini, diners may choose between the intimate indoor dining room and the alfresco terrace (weather permitting!).

Name: Osteria Numero 2
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Fefa is the perfect place for lovers of authentic flavours from the Emilia region. The Inspector sums it up like this: “Flicking through the menu you want to try everything!” - and this really is the case. Start your meal off with a selection of the finest charcuterie, in which an outstanding Culatello di Zibello, accompanied by a “Gnocco Fritto” not to be missed reigns supreme. Continue with excellent homemade, fresh-egg pasta followed by main courses made up exclusively of meat, in keeping with local tradition. The dessert page is deliciously tempting, offering an extensive selection of sweet treats: trifle, biscuits served with warm zabaione, “taccolenta degli Estensi” cake and lots of other specialities that evoke memories of the region’s cuisine. Fragrant and generous flavours, served in a simple but charming dining room featuring a splendid wooden ceiling recovered from an old country haybarn.Great attention is also paid to the winelist, which boasts impressive vintages and a meticulously curated selection, skilfully put together by talented sommelier Edoardo, that completes a rich, sincere and profoundly Emilian gastronomic experience.

Name: Osteria Ophis
Description: Situated in the beautiful historic pedestrianised centre of Offida, this restaurant with a brick-vaulted ceiling is housed in the former stables of an old palazzo with a modern, inviting and intimate feel. Here, owner-chef Daniele Citeroni Maurizi skilfully reinterprets regional cuisine to create precise, imaginative dishes that are full of flavour. The stuffed cannelloni cooked on the barbecue grill are delicious, as is the veal tartare served with a warm meat, herb and vegetable jus on the side. We should also highlight the “low cost” tasting menu available for guests aged under 25.

Name: Osteria Piazzetta Cattedrale
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Ostuni’s 15th-century co-cathedral, dedicated to Santa Maria dell’Assunzione, a husband and wife passionately run this refined and cosy gourmet gem. The interiors, adorned with mirrors and ceramics on the walls, evoke the atmosphere of an elegant private drawing room, enhanced by floors and chandeliers of remarkable quality. In the kitchen, Mrs Marilea offers a selection of regional recipes featuring both land and sea fare – simple yet prepared with great care. There is also a significant range of artisanal produce, including fresh pasta, bread, baked goods, cakes and ice cream. Among these, the ricotta ice cream with fig compote and toasted almonds, served on a sponge cake as a unique take on the zuccotto, is particularly worth mentioning. As well as the menu, the excellent value for money of the small traditional tasting menu is a real draw. Given the limited number of seats, particularly during busy periods, it is advisable to book in advance.

Name: Osteria Platzegg
Description: This comfortable and informal “Gasthaus” with a simple yet welcoming and contemporary feel is run by talented chef Herbert Hintner, the undisputed master of Alto Adige cuisine. Housed within a historic building in the town’s pedestrianised centre, the restaurant serves simple cuisine with a focus on regional recipes and ingredients (such as potato ravioli filled with speck ham and spleen crostini in broth) alongside a few Mediterranean-influenced dishes such as arancini in a gorgonzola sauce. The wine list, on the other hand, focuses uniquely on the Alto Adige.

Name: Osteria San Giulio
Address: Via Dulzago, Badia di Dulzago, 28043, Italy
Description: A timeless atmosphere lingers in this hamlet, a former rural abbey that speaks to the region’s deep ties with agriculture and its enduring traditions. Those same roots are reflected in the menu of this humble, almost austere osteria: agnolotti with roast meat sauce, local cured meats and cheeses, panissa, and bunet. Prices are very fair, especially with the Menù dell’Oste (under €40).

Name: Osteria Uno
Address: 140 Hinemoa Street, Birkenhead, Auckland, 0626, New Zealand
Description: The pasta machine in the dining area is a clear visual cue as to the main offering at this osteria – handmade pasta, made from scratch. Among the variety of pasta types with vegetable, seafood and meat sauces, the prawn and Fraser Isle spanner crab cappelletti stands out for its deep umami. The crusty and fluffy house-made focaccia is also a must; rather than balsamic vinegar and olive oil, it is served with a decadent balsamic butter.

Name: Osteria Veglio
Description: With a convenient reserved parking space and an expansive terrace overlooking the Langhe panorama, the 1920s-built house greets guests with stylistic minimalism but gastronomic enthusiasm in its sincere regional cuisine proposal. The minimum selection à la carte comprises two courses excluding desserts.

Name: Osteria Zanchetti
Description: In the heart of Fossombrone’s charming historic centre, at the top of a picturesque narrow street, this superb contemporary osteria makes a striking first impression: as soon as you step inside, the medieval charm of the village gives way to interiors inspired by the elegance of the Roaring Twenties. Here, head chef and owner Luca Zanchetti draws on the experience he has gained in prestigious restaurants – many of which have been awarded Michelin stars – to create his own personal and creative take on regional cuisine. His dishes range from traditional classics, such as vanilla ice cream ‘drowned’ in Fano’s Moretta coffee, to original creations crafted from the excellent produce of the surrounding valleys. An authentic, contemporary dining experience that wins you over with its balance, character and warmth: the sort of trattoria that, as the inspectors agree, everyone would love to have on their doorstep.

Name: Osteria da K. [káppa]
Description: An osteria presented by a sushi shop. After apprenticing in Italy, the chef helped out at a sushi restaurant before taking charge here. Seafood, procured from the chef’s personal sources, catches the eye. Cut ends of abalone and fish make a seafood ragù for pasta, born from meals prepared for employees. Acqua pazza is enhanced with kombu water for an even more delicious dish. Cuisine that brings out the best in the ingredients, backed by the skills of Italy and Japan.

Name: Osteria dal Moro
Description: A lively fish and seafood restaurant on the seafront, which is always busy thanks to its excellent value for money – booking ahead is highly recommended! Fish-based dishes only, all of which are announced at your table and which change regularly depending on market availability. The dishes are simple, rustic but full of flavour, which is why it’s easy to forgive the rather restricted choice of wine.

Name: Osteria de Börg
Description: In the characteristic Borgo San Giuliano so dear to Federico Fellini, with its narrow streets and colourful houses that were once home to the local fishermen, this excellent osteria celebrates the most typical Romagna cuisine, including the finest charcuterie, fresh homemade pasta (the traditional cappelletti in chicken broth are excellent) and meats, including Mora Romagnola pork, which is used in a variety of dishes. Inside, you'll find a setting that you would traditionally associate with a trattoria, complete with check cotton tablecloths and bottles on display.

Name: Osteria dei Maltagliati
Address: Via Regina Margherita 37, Torano Nuovo, 64010, Italy
Description: Run by Maicol and Federica, this cosy, rustic-style restaurant wins you over with its cuisine, which has its roots in tradition and is enhanced by the use of a wood-fired oven and a grill fuelled by its own embers. The cooking methods evoke authentic flavours and time-honoured traditions, reinterpreted with a contemporary sensitivity and a focus on the ingredients. In the warmer months, the wooden tables on the small, cool outdoor terrace offer a pleasant spot to relax, while the rooms above the restaurant allow you to extend your stay and enjoy the very best of Abruzzo’s authentic hospitality. Among the specialities not to be missed are the hand-rolled pasta dishes, prepared with artisan care, including the flavourful wild boar cappelletti with olives and sage, a true expression of the local area.

Name: Osteria dei Segreti
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated amid hills in a secluded and panoramic location, this farmhouse offers guestrooms, a spa and a restaurant, where meat (often cooked over the grill) takes pride of place on the menu, alongside various local specialities such as stuffed pigeon, roast goose and “coniglio in porchetta” (stuffed rabbit).

Name: Osteria del Boccondivino
Description: Access is via the inner courtyard of an elegant period building, where, on sunny days, the outdoor tables buzz with conversation and delicious smells. Upstairs, there is a large, bright dining room flanked by two cosy side rooms that are perfect for conversing. In the main room, a climate-controlled wooden display case catches the eye: inside are precious bottles, from the intense reds of Langa and Roero to wines that tell stories from every corner of the world. The menu is a journey through the flavours of Piedmont: dishes that exude tradition, such as “Gobbi di Nizza Monferrato” (cardoons drenched in velvety bagna cauda), or persimmon mousse paired with sweet chestnut cream. Every mouthful is a memorable encounter of textures and aromas. We recommend booking ahead, even for lunch!

Name: Osteria del Gallo e della Volpe
Address: Piazza Umberto I 14, Ospedaletto d'Alpinolo, 83014, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of this small town is run by the Silvestro family (father and son). In summer, book one of the tables in the charming outdoor space overlooking the square. The menu focuses on local traditional cuisine with the occasional personalised twist, such as the pork-belly kebab with a papacelle reduction (short, pulpy peppers with a sweet flavour) and stracciata sauce, while the wine list features labels from the Irpinia region (and elsewhere) with a good choice of vertical wines and top-quality names such as Aglianico and Taurasi.

Name: Osteria del Mare già il "Votapentole"
Address: Via IV Novembre 15, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: In the city center, there's a small but lively restaurant with cheerful colors and a charming outdoor area on the pedestrian street. The atmosphere is always relaxed, even in summer when dining is only in the evening and tables are in high demand (reservations are essential). The menu is a journey through the sea: always featuring raw seafood, tuna amatriciana, cacciucco, and other classic dishes with imaginative touches.

Name: Osteria del Miglio 2.10
Address: Via Patrioti 2, Pieve San Giacomo, 26035, Italy
Description: A pleasant (and excellent) provincial restaurant with a modern feel and a traditional brick-vaulted ceiling, where owner-chef Samuele Miglioli pays tribute to local traditions in his cuisine (don’t miss the marubini pasta in three broths and the famous pumpkin tortelli). The dishes here focus on seasonal ingredients which are carefully transformed into generous dishes full of flavour, as demonstrated by the rice timbale served on a delicious beef ragù and topped with beef carpaccio. There’s also an excellent selection of wines, with a particular focus on sparkling wines.

Name: Osteria dell'Accademia
Description: Within an evocative medieval hamlet dating to the thirteenth century, with breathtaking views extending to the sea, this is an authentic osteria where the pleasures of local and regional home cooking may be savoured: the cappelletti with cream sauce and Grana are not to be missed, nor are the excellent gelati among the desserts. For a particularly memorable visit, reserve a table on the welcoming summer terrace, which enjoys wide-ranging views over the surrounding hills.

Name: Osteria della Bottega
Description: This lively restaurant is located on a steep little street in Geneva's old town. Against a chic industrial-style backdrop with an open kitchen, diners are treated to modern, seasonally inspired Italian cuisine and fine wines, plus attentive and friendly service. It's best to book, as Osteria is very popular!

Name: Osteria della Villetta
Description: A bastion of tradition for over a hundred years, Art Nouveau furnishings and a retro atmosphere are the accompaniment to Brescian classics and familiar recipes: always based on seasonal ingredients, as in the case of the many vegetables from their own garden, from which the Evo oil also comes. The wine list offers a wide selection of labels from Franciacorta, Barolo and Barbaresco: true passion of the owner Massimo!

Name: Osteria la Fefa
Address: Via Trento e Trieste 9/c, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description: A beautiful farmhouse not far from the town, with a friendly, welcoming and colourful feel, where the menu features Italian dishes alongside a few local specialities, such as an excellent "bagna caoda". Special mention goes to the superb selection of beers chosen by owner Moreno, which ranges from local craft beers to labels from across the globe. There’s even a beer-themed dessert, the Birramisù. Offering excellent value for money, it is extremely popular, so booking ahead is recommended.

Name: Otantik Ocakbaşı
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The barbecue and wood-fired oven will catch your eye as soon as you enter this congenial establishment, which has a cosy terrace in the lane to the rear. The chef expertly tames the open fire to cook delicious dishes, such as kebab and grilled dry-aged steak. The mixed grill is a signature dish here: a variety of juicy meats, oven-fresh bread and a judicious sprinkle of sumac. This restaurant offers great value for the money, serving delicious food without pretensions.

Name: Otoro
Address: Al Qana Marina South, Al Maqta' Street, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,No alcohol served,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This friendly, contemporary Japanese spot is perfect for a bite to eat when visiting the nearby National Aquarium in Al Qana. The space has a relaxed, funky feel and is dominated by a large open kitchen to watch the team in action. The experienced chef, under the aegis of consultant-chef Akmal Anuar from 11 Woodfire in Dubai, has a diligent brigade supporting him. Ingredients are flown in from various prefectures of Japan, like wagyu from Kagoshima, otoro from Tokyo and uni from Hokkaido. Signatures include yellowtail with green chili and leche de tigre, wagyu striploin with truffle jus and wasabi and of course, the titular otoro nigiri.

Name: Otto's High Dive
Address: 2304 E. Robinson St., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This tiny but oh-so-sweet space recalls the charm of Old Florida with its whitewashed brick walls and white tile floors. Billed as a neighborhood rum bar, Otto's High Dive is on point at every turn, from the genuine service to the unfussy but well-executed food. The kitchen delivers a concise edit of Floridian/Cuban fare with oodles of tropical elements. Begin with oysters before moving on to an array of cold and hot plates ranging from a shrimp cocktail that's all grown up with its thick "Bloody Mary" sauce to chicken mojo and ropa vieja with sides like rice and beans. Cinnamon bread pudding topped with a delightfully tangy cream cheese whip is a memorable sign-off. Rum is all around, from the Cuba Libre on tap to the daiquiris available by the pitcher.

Name: Ou Yue Zun Xian
Address: Shop 605, 6F, Crystal Galleria, 68 Yuyuan Road, Jingan, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The owner is a seafood vendor himself, so only the freshest catch makes it to the table. Without bells and whistles, the food is traditional Wenzhou fare that highlights natural flavours. Wild-caught marine fish, steamed and served chilled with salted potherb mustard greens and Puning soybean paste, imparts layers of flavour. A Wenzhou street-food classic, the pork wonton soup brings back childhood memories. Certain items need to be pre-ordered.

Name: Oudon Yomogi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only - lunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: This à la carte udon shop is a project of the proprietress of the Japanese restaurant Miyamoto. The plain-wood counter and bamboo accents lend the restaurant a kappo feel. À la carte dining is available for both lunch and dinner, while dinner service generally begins with a set offering of appetiser and hassun. Udon noodles are house-made, their broth light and clear like Japanese soups. Sake and side dishes end with a serving of udon; closing with udon rather than soba is one of the restaurant’s charms.

Name: Ouroboros
Address: 135 rue Saint-Joseph Est, Québec, G1K 3A8, Canada
Description: The name Ouroboros, like the mythological snake that symbolizes an eternal circle, reflects the way this restaurant works: from market to plate (and even composting), their approach forms a perfect cycle. The cozy bistro has comfortable seating at tables and a counter, and a concise menu that prioritizes fresh seasonal and regional ingredients, such as delicious pork gyozas served with a stout beer sauce, flavorsome chicken, Jerusalem artichokes and salsify, and an excellent apple strudel. There is no wine list here; ask owner Daniel for recommendations.

Name: Outerlands
Address: 4001 Judah St., San Francisco, CA, 94122, USA
Description: On the fringes of the city, this charmingly rustic salvaged wood retreat is a beloved neighborhood stalwart. Noteworthy above all for baking some of the best bread in the city, sourdough devotees are known to make the pilgrimage from far and wide to partake in the crusty, mahogany-hued levain, served in thick slices with house-cultured butter (loaves are also available to purchase). Beyond the obligatory bread, the small seasonal menu features commendable ingredients served in a simple, hearty style that allows their quality to shine, whether its roasted chicken with market vegetables, or a slow-cooked ragu Bolognese with springy tagliatelle. On weekends, brunch follows a similar formula, with the addition of excellent pastries like a signature sticky bun.

Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Address: Hong Lim Market and Food Centre, #02-17, Blk 531A, Upper Cross Street, 051531, Singapore
Description: In business since 1953, this hugely popular stall specialises in fried kway teow with egg and cockles. The piping hot noodles impress with deep smoky flavour. Consider ordering extra cockles or eggs.

Name: OvenBird
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: From the parking lot, you can smell the sweet smoke that billows out of the restaurant’s two roaring, wood-burning ovens. In what feels like a backyard oasis fit with a spacious patio, find a hazy, sun-lit dining room where Chef Chris Hastings pulls inspiration from Spain and Latin America. Much of the food is cooked in cast-iron skillets. From Spanish omelets dotted with chorizo vinaigrette to charred empanadas to finely-seared scallops set in ajo blanco sauce, the tapas-style menu does not shy away from flavor and is fully designed for sharing. For dessert, spiced molasses crème brûlée makes for a sweet send-off.

Name: Ox and Finch
Address: 920 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow City, G3 7TF, United Kingdom
Description: Now in its second decade, this hugely likeable bistro is becoming something of a Glasgow institution – the first in a small group of restaurants offering brilliant value and a buzzing atmosphere. After a refurbishment in early 2025, it's got a fresh new look and menu, but the ethos remains: Mediterranean dishes that are ideal for sharing, showcasing skilful use of simple ingredients so that their flavours really shine through – such as cod cheeks with chorizo, tomato and morcilla. The attentive service team run the place like a well-oiled machine.

Name: Oxalis
Address: 2 place de la Fontaine, Marcolès, 15220, France
Description: This bistro is the more casual sibling of the iconic Auberge de la Tour, which is even more reason to stay overnight in the medieval village of Marcolès deep in the Cantal countryside. Whether it is in the vaulted dining room or on the pleasant alfresco terrace, you will sample deftly crafted regional recipes with a fondness for local produce: trout from the volcanoes, free-range poultry, Auvergne cheese, cottage garden veg… Examples: seed crusted trout, roast quail in Auvergne blue cheese, or a citrus fruit réligieuse pastry.

Name: Oyamel
Description: This well-liked mainstay of DC Mexican cuisine comes courtesy of Spanish Chef Jose Andres, whose typical dedication to flavorful cooking and high-quality ingredients still draws brisk business. Snag a seat at the entertaining ceviche bar and sip thirst-quenching drinks while snacking on small plates.The kitchen's dedication to technique and ingredients is clear, with a particular penchant for regionally inflected Mexican cuisine like huevos enfrijoladas, crispy chilaquiles, and gorditas topped with Hudson Valley duck confit. Don’t miss the tarasca estilo pátzcuaro though, an otherworldly black bean soup with avocado leaves, swirls of crema, and crumbled cotija. A special hora feliz menu makes the early evening hours very happy indeed.

Name: P'tite Pomme
Description: A stone's throw from the Cité des Congrès events venue and the lively rue Fouré, this concrete-clad neo-bistro has an industrial edge. A couple made up of chef Ruddy Maisonneuve (P'tite Pomme was his childhood nickname) and Juliette Jovelin (front of house) are the driving force behind this venture! Trained as a pastry chef and formerly sous-chef at Lulu Rouget, the chef cooks up ultra-fresh seasonal cuisine, elevated by local produce – some of the vegetables are supplied by his brother, a farmer and baker. In all their vibrancy, his refined, precise dishes are testament to the work of a true professional: aubergine, blue lobster and cherries; fish from the fish auction, (pulped) bell pepper and courgette; chocolate and hazelnut choux bun.

Name: PERILLA Fare
Address: 401 N. Milwaukee Ave., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: This prime location welcomes diners with a mural of former First Lady, Michelle Obama, dressed in a hanbok. Inside, the vibe is cozy with an urbane simplicity. Imagine a smattering of artwork, greenery, and edgy light fixtures. Large windows with views of a buzzy street and a semi-open kitchen reinforces that sleek city feel. Chef Andrew Lim's forte lies in his contemporary take on familiar Korean food. Here you will find tables spread with delicious banchan, tailed by Wagyu beef tartare accented with Asian pear. Kimchi stew with glass noodles; fire chicken with Chihuahua cheese; and even that classic fried chicken gets a spin in this kitchen—the latter with ranch and pickled radish.In lieu of dessert, go for the special and thoughtful tea cellar menu.

Name: PILI PILI
Address: 54 Muhak-ro 33 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48268, South Korea
Description: PILI PILI may seem a bit rough around the edges, but its unmistakable Thai restaurant aesthetic is hard to resist. The menu presents Thai classics reinterpreted for local palates while staying true to their roots. Its signature pu phat phong curry features creamy crab meat folded into a rich, aromatic curry sauce that pairs wonderfully with warm white rice. The vividly acidic and spicy tom yum soup is tasty, but the khao pad tom yum fried rice steals the show. The deliberately vintage interior recreates the feel of a local Thai dining eatery in Busan. Now, add a cocktail, and you have a miniature Thailand at your table.

Name: PINOT
Description: The location in the side wing of the modern Klinik Gut private hospital may be a little unusual, but the food here is excellent… thanks to Sebastian Titz (previously at Verve by Sven in Bad Ragaz), who cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine that cuts to the chase. Lunch is the main affair here: dish of the day, a small à la carte selection and set menus (fish/meat or vegetarian), as well as a weekly special and "Our House Speciality". A tasting menu is served on Thursday evenings. The decor is trendy and minimalist in style, with an open kitchen; the view of the mountains and the surrounding area is fabulous – tables on the terrace are understandably coveted.

Name: PITAK GOHAN
Description: Chef Pitak from Bangkok offers food from his native Thailand. Exotic aromas of herbs, spices and fish sauce thrill our souls. Temptations include salad of ground pork and glass noodles, a Thai-style grilled chicken dressed with coriander known as gai yang, and curry stir-fry with seafood and egg. The generous portions of the à la carte dishes encourage diners to share. The everyday flavours of Thailand live and breathe down this Nakazakicho alley.

Name: PIZZERIA TRATTORIA MAGAZZINO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only - lunch,Pets not allowed
Description: The pizza here is prepared true to how it’s done in Naples, with chef Hironori Noda reproducing those authentic flavours. What Naples has that Nara doesn’t is an ocean so, in response, he came up with the idea of a restaurant that’s all about the fields. He grows the vegetables himself and makes them the main ingredients. The garden is his mother’s, and he harvests the vegetables himself, meaning that the bounty of Kashiba proffered here truly springs from ‘Mother Earth’.

Name: PODA
Description: It is in the tranquil streets and historic setting of Montemor‑o‑Novo that you find PODA. This restaurant occupies a former agricultural warehouse, fully restored, and presents an elegant ambience that preserves the rustic details of its past life. Chef João Narigueta and sommelier Miguel Dominguinhos, long‑time friends, joined forces in this project to create a space where traditional Alentejo cuisine is revived and presented with decidedly pronounced flavours. The offering includes a tasting menu (5 courses) and a concise à la carte menu, which offers, among the options, the soup of the day — such as the comforting Sopa Fatia Azeda (regional sour‑bread soup) made with cured sausages and poached egg — or a sweet hard to find outside this region, Enxovalhada, a spongey pão‑de‑ló filled with pieces of walnuts, honey and dusted with cinnamon. The wine list is composed mostly of local producers!

Name: PRESTAU
Description: The husband takes charge of the cooking, while his wife handles the desserts. Valuing a sense of the seasons, they strive to create Italian cuisine unique to Japan. Seeking out high-quality domestic ingredients, they present regional Italian dishes in a modern style. Their top priority is to bring out the best in each ingredient, layering flavours and textures. Drawing on his experience working in Kobe, the chef serves his dishes on Tambayaki pottery, further enhancing their Japanese character.

Name: Pa Lek Boat Noodles
Address: Bang-Ain Road, Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This third-generation family-run street food joint has been offering tasty boat noodles for over five decades. Try their pork or beef boat noodles for great value — it comes in a small bowl, so more than one may be needed to truly enjoy it.

Name: Pa Pleung Mhee Kratok
Address: 1 Mu 8, Chok Chai, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30190, Thailand
Description: Simple and always busy, this spot is renowned for phat mi krathok, which the owner cooks over the wok herself. Go for the fresh prawn or classic with egg, both served generously with bean sprouts and garlic chives on the side, plus lime to squeeze on. Closed on Buddhist holy days.

Name: Pa Ting (Don Sak)
Address: 1/8 Mu 5, Don Sak, Surat Thani, 84220, Thailand
Description: Established in 1967, Pa Ting is now run by the founder’s daughter. This simple, open-air spot overlooking the Don Sak River serves seafood rooted in local tradition. The spicy salad with salted Kulao fish bursts with fragrant Thai herbs, while the southern-style sour curry with fresh Kulao fish is spicy, rich, and boldly flavoured. You can choose the vegetables you prefer — whether it’s taro stem, coconut shoot, or bamboo shoot.

Name: Pacífico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This classic family-run restaurant founded in 1975 by the grandparents of current owner Francisco Domínguez has moved with the times and now presents a much more appealing modern feel that showcases the evolution of this renowned eatery. The café-bar at the entrance leads to a bistro-style dining room with an open-view kitchen. Here, the focus is on a single, contemporary-style tasting menu that changes every two months approximately and is centred around seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. An added option here is the extensive brunch available at the weekend. One dish that we particularly enjoyed on our last visit was the sea bass escabeche with carrot purée, a garlic refrito salsa and dried fruits.

Name: Pad Thai Bua Dang
Address: 7/27 Soi Assawin, Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This modest roadside shop is known among locals for its pad thai with prawns, not overly sweet and full of wok aroma. They offer variations with seafood, meat, or other toppings. Indoor seating is air-conditioned, service is friendly, and an English menu is available.

Name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
Address: 115/5 Dinso Road, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: The tempting scent of sizzling pork greets you at this vibrant restaurant by chef Andy Yang. Their signature dish features nicely char-grilled pork loin slices atop savoury Pad Thai. Another recommendation is the Pad Thai with fresh prawns, stir-fried in their shell for sweet, delicious meat. For top-notch Pad Thai and skilled wok-based cooking at a fair price, this is your spot.

Name: Padella
Address: 6 Southwark Street, Borough Market, London, SE1 1TQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: It's not hard to see why this perennially popular pasta spot is so busy. The chefs make their pasta fresh every morning ready for a new wave of hungry customers to enjoy, then cook it with admirable precision and add a range of mouth-watering accompaniments – whether that be cavolo nero with the the cavatelli or regional specialities like a delicious Tuscan gorgonzola sauce with stacci. Don't forget the equally impressive tarts for dessert, too. Arrive in plenty of time to scan the QR code and join the virtual queue, then have a wander round the neighbouring Borough Market.

Name: Pae
Address: 80/1 Rahaeng Market, Rahaeng, Lat Lum Kaeo, Pathum Thani, 12140, Thailand
Description: This hidden eatery in the 100-year-old Rahaeng Market has been serving traditional Thai-Chinese dishes for over 50 years. With a focus on quality ingredients from the market, their homemade dishes like minced featherback fish and pork in tofu sheets are recommended. Arrive early for spicy stir-fried featherback fish and fried sun-dried snakehead fish.

Name: Pae Brass Pot Porridge 38 Years
Address: 320 Pracha Rat Sai 1 Road, Bang Sue, Bangkok, 10800, Thailand
Description: Don't let the name mislead you – "38" is a nod to the founder's lucky number. This porridge hotspot has been simmering since 1962, serving up porridge in its signature brass pots for three generations. Our favourite is the mixed rice porridge option.

Name: Paesàno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Down a charming cobbled street in the trendy Nørrebro neighbourhood, where you will find a number of artisan food producers, lies this thoroughly fun restaurant run by a Neapolitan Chef.
