Description: Don’t be perplexed if certain items on the menu seem familiar – this all-day dining bistro is from Paul Pairet of Ultraviolet and Mr & Mrs Bund fame. Some dishes echo the signatures from those establishments, albeit rendered in simpler forms. Onion soup is recommended – rich and well-balanced, with a nice contrast of textures. The classic Parisian décor with an industrial twist works perfectly. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Pondus
Description: The little sister to Michelin-Starred Substans is a simple place set beside the canal in a historic part of the city. Glasses and wine bottles grace the shelves, and exposed brickwork and unfinished floors set a relaxed, unpretentious mood. The food is a perfect match for the surroundings, with the colourful dishes showcasing organic Danish produce and representing great value – you might find cured hake with capers and relish, followed by spice cake with figs, ice cream and caramel sauce. In summer, you can dine alfresco on the pavement terrace.

Name: Ponta Honke
Description: Since its inception in 1905, this Western restaurant has been run by four generations of the same family. The chef’s famous cutlet is deep-fried in lard carefully trimmed from the pork he will fry. Everything is done by hand, as it has been from the first generation. The youthful energy and practiced skill of the chef is evident in every detail, even down to the hand-chopped cabbage. Traditional flavours and skills testify to his mettle. Delicious fare and the gentle ambience of a family enterprise make everyone feel at home.

Name: Poppenborg's Stübchen
Description: This is the more relaxed alternative to Poppenborg's more traditional eatery. Try the Atlantic sea wolf with mustard sauce or the Westphalian-style boiled top-side of veal. Pretty garden terrace.

Name: Post
Address: Horwood House, High Street, Newnham, GL14 1AA, United Kingdom
Description: A striped canopy strung with fairy lights beckons you into this delightful bottle shop and bistro where you can feel the joy and passion of the team coursing through their work. A concise, regularly changing à la carte is chalked up on the blackboard – and it makes great use of ingredients from the team’s own smallholding. With produce and cooking this good, along with sensible pricing, every penny spent brings with it bucketloads of flavour. Straightforward is the name of the game, with the likes of homemade pasta and a terrific tarte Tatin on offer.

Name: Posto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A former barn, this warm and welcoming spot in the dynamic neighbourhood of Jeżyce has been renovated in a chic style that feels elegant, yet still with a rustic touch. The cooking is all about the French classics, from pâté en croute to decadent chocolate ganache with sour cherries cooked in red wine. There’s a wonderful generosity to the food that chimes with the enthusiastic service; the prices are sensible and the added extras include a drink on arrival and freshly baked madeleines with your coffee.

Name: Poststuben
Description: It is hardly surprising that this restaurant is so popular. As well as charming and attentive service, diners are drawn by the regionally influenced cuisine conjured up by chef-patron Sven Molitor. Made using carefully selected ingredients, his dishes reveal talent and good craftsmanship. They are down-to-earth, but also show a certain finesse here and there. On the menu, for example, the delicious spinach and cheese dumplings will whet your appetite. The likeable traditional family-run hotel Die Post offers well-kept, contemporary guestrooms for overnight stays – an ideal base for exploring the beautiful surroundings of the village, which is located in the Meerfelder Maar volcanic crater.

Name: Potluck Club
Address: 133 Chrystie St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
Description: Chrystie Street wins big with this high-energy Chinese restaurant that is always down to have a good time. The stylish room leans on a Hong Kong cinema motif, with posters and stills from classic films and a glowing marquee above the chef’s counter. Looks aside, the cooking offers a fresh, generous take on Cantonese American favorites using top-rate products. Pan-seared pot stickers get their boost from a Berkshire pork and chive filling, while fried tiger shrimp slicked with Calabrian chili aioli are piled high and deeply satisfying. The XO fried rice is a standout: a hefty mound packed with shrimp, Chinese sausage and savory seafood richness. Also worth an order is the salt and pepper fried chicken, served with fluffy scallion biscuits and a chili-plum jam that should be bottled and sold.

Name: Pouwe
Description: In the sleepy village of Hoeven, Walter and Vivian Pouwe greet diners with true Brabantian hospitality. Their modern, intimate restaurant boasts a striking open kitchen and a rear terrace that provides a pleasant setting for relaxed dining. The chef incorporates ingredients such as yuzu, tandoori and vadouvan into creative dishes that pack a punch. One highlight is the carpaccio of red and yellow tomato, lavishly adorned with artichoke, roasted pine nuts, confit Padrón peppers and a silky emulsion of oil and grated Manchego. After all those rich flavours, be sure to sample something from the cheese trolley – an intriguing selection of international cheeses personally presented by the chef with infectious enthusiasm. A Bib Gourmand restaurant with a cosmopolitan twist!

Name: Pranakhon
Address: 88 University Pl., New York, NY, 10003, USA
Description: The name may reference Bangkok's original name, Phra Nakhon, but this busy spot is all about the now. The yawning, two-story dining room leads with a long bar and is a constant whirl of energy. It’s not uncommon to arrive to find a completely full house. A wide range of Thai dishes prepared both classically and with contemporary touches feature an abundance of herbs, spices, heat and zeal. The yum kai salad makes for a refreshing, invigorating start before delving into richer specialties like tender mussels stuffed with curry paste custard or marinated pork jowls coated in an electric Thai chili-lime dressing. Other hits include crab fried rice, pad see ew and, for lovers of pork belly, the kang tae po.

Name: Prandtauerhof Gutshofrestaurant
Address: Prandtauerplatz 36, Weißenkirchen in der Wachau, 3610, Austria
Description: A centuries-old wine farm has been transformed into the beautiful Holzapfel winery estate, featuring a small boutique hotel, an inviting restaurant and a gorgeous terrace set within an arcaded courtyard. The kitchen team serves up dishes with a strong regional character that are distinguished by excellent craftsmanship and flavour. Opt for the set menu or order à la carte. The estate's own wines are available to pair with your meal. The front-of-house team is friendly, attentive and always on hand.

Name: Pranom Shredded Chicken Noodles (Tha Wasukri)
Address: 47/9 Mu 4, Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayuthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: On Ayutthaya-Ang Thong Road, near Wat Phanom Yong, the shredded chicken noodle soup needs no extra seasoning. The tom yum broth is perfectly balanced; chicken is tender, while slow-cooked chicken feet are an option. Available for breakfast and lunch only.

Name: Praprai
Address: 345/1-2 Airport Road, Ban Pet, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Arrivals and departures are better with a stopover at this simple restaurant in front of Khon Kaen Airport. For more than two decades, Prapai's friendly owners have been serving authentic Isan dishes made with fresh local ingredients that change with the season. To experience traditional Isan cooking, try the deep-fried sour fish or mok khai mot daeng – red ant eggs steamed in banana leaf.

Name: Prashad
Address: 137 Whitehall Road, Drighlington, BD11 1AT, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Set over two floors of a former pub, this colourfully decorated, family-run restaurant offers interesting, original Indian vegetarian cooking inspired by the owners' Gujarati heritage. After a warm welcome from the team, you can choose between set sharing menus, a full tasting experience or picking a few dishes from the extensive à la carte. Dishes such as the 'Chole' chickpea curry are substantial in both size and flavour and the spicing is well-judged. The bread selection stands out, with excellent naan and rotli.

Name: Prasit
Address: 44/4 Ammart Road, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The inviting smell of charcoal-grilled sausages wafts from the kitchen at the front of this shophouse restaurant. This family-run business has been serving traditional Isan pork and beef dishes since 1972, in line with their motto: ‘using the best cuts of beef to create flavoursome Isan dishes.’ Dishes like their fried sun-dried beef slices, pork sausages and sliced beef shank in spicy and sour soup live up to the ideal, are reasonably priced and served with a smile.

Name: Prik-Yuak (Phya Thai)
Address: 108 Pradiphat Road, Phaya Thai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Garden or park
Description: Housed in a renovated former school building, the restaurant retains the calm and welcoming atmosphere that has marked its place in Bangkok's dining scene for over 30 years. Home-style Thai dishes are served in generous portions on clay plates lined with banana leaves, adding a rustic touch to the presentation. The cooking shows respect for the ingredients, and the stir-fried squid with yellow chilli and basil stands out for its balance. With a garden, café and small boutique, it caters to a variety of occasions.

Name: Prime Barbecue
Address: 403 Knightdale Station Run, Knightdale, NC, 27545, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Pitmaster Christopher Prieto relocated from his native Texas to North Carolina, setting up Prime Barbecue just outside Raleigh in Knightdale. You'll need to arrive early, be prepared to wait and know that once they've run out of food, they'll close for the day. Expect all of the classics, including brisket and ribs plus pulled pork, all sold by their weight or ordered as a "meat and 2" with two scrumptious side dishes. Keep an eye out for their daily specials, especially on Saturday when they serve their chopped whole hog lechon. You won't be hungry, but a slice of pie or a banana pudding never hurt anyone.

Name: Primeur
Address: 116 Petherton Road, Canonbury, London, N5 2RT, United Kingdom
Description: There's something so appealing about the simplicity of a restaurant like Primeur. A proper neighbourhood operation, it comes with stripped-back décor, a handwritten blackboard menu and a relaxed, bustling atmosphere. Diners can sit around large communal tables or up at the counters around the edges of the room. The cooking, for its part, avoids overcomplication and puts the ingredients first, as evidenced by grilled pork chop with roquefort butter. Ensure you save room for dessert, too, especially if the textbook custard tart is on the menu.

Name: Prof Chan's (Western District)
Address: 420-424 Queen's Road West, Western District, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: The kitchen team of Hunanese natives boasts solid skills, especially in quick-fried dishes that sport exceptional wok hei. Ingredients such as chillies and smoked pork are sourced directly from farmers in Hunan. The speciality braised pork elbow involves four complicated cooking steps spanning over 10 hours to develop layered flavours and the right texture. Stir-fried pork with Youxian beancurd and spicy organic cauliflower are also worth trying.

Name: Promessa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: With "Food is art" as their motto, the chefs at this trendy and laid-back restaurant treat their plates like canvases, placing a strong emphasis on aesthetics. But fear not: these visually stunning dishes are also packed with flavour. Koen van den Kerkhof's creativity draws on the culinary traditions of the Netherlands, France and more far-flung locations, with his refusal to be constrained by any single style reflected in a wide-ranging menu. A yellowtail tartare paired with an intense mushroom dashi perfectly illustrates how refinement and expression come together here. A beautifully cooked entrecôte, served with a mustard-seed jus and various preparations of salsify, follows the same path while adding an extra touch of generosity. They have the art of indulgence down to a T!

Name: Prosper
Description: Not far from Cours Julien, this old Marseille bar, spruced up but pleasingly unfussy, has retained its heart and soul: white and bottle-green walls, exposed stonework, and a terrace on a lively square. At the helm is a French-British duo who trained at Frenchie (Paris and London). They serve up bold and fiery Mediterranean dishes that look to Spain for inspiration. On the dinner menu on this occasion: skate wing terrine with pepper sauce; aubergine, smoked yoghurt, caponata, plum and sumac flower… and squid-ink rice with grilled octopus and aioli. Two sittings in the evening in summer. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Provender
Address: 17 High Street, Redbridge, London, E11 2AA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: ‘A little piece of France in Wanstead’ is the tagline at this busy and welcoming neighbourhood bistro – and it certainly delivers on the promise. The extensive menu is a roll-call of classic French dishes from escargots and soupe à l’oignon to coq au vin and steak frites. They prove to be impressively executed too, providing satisfying flavours at fair prices. A startlingly good value 'prix fixe' is available throughout the day Tuesday to Thursday and for lunch only on Friday and Saturday.

Name: Psomi
Address: 701 N. Howard Ave., Tampa, FL, 33606, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Owned and run by second-generation Greek American Chef Christina Theofilos, this daytime eatery and bakery epitomizes warmth and comfort. Strangers become friends in no time, noshing on breakfast and lunch during the week and brunch on weekends. The menu is laced with Greek items ranging from flavorful and tender octopus ceviche to house-made dolmades that display an added level of care. Their take on a French dip with feta-brined organic roasted chicken, kefalograviera cheese and skordalia aioli on a crusty baguette is a hearty and delicious meal. Of course, with a name that translates to bread, there must be baked goods, and you'll find it all here. Don't skimp on dessert and order bougatsa, baklava or baklava coffee cake (an impressive marriage of the two).

Name: Puchegger-Wirt
Description: The Puchegger family's country inn, well-loved by its many regular patrons, features a rustic yet elegant restaurant and a charming wine cellar. Regional cuisine.

Name: Pueblo Pibil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Nestled in Tixkokob in a converted 18th-century mansion, Pueblo Pibil is a charming spot spotlighting authentic Yucatecán dishes and utilizing the al Pib technique of cooking in an underground hearth-style pit. The meat, buried for more than 15 hours on fire with chukum and catzín wood, plus oak leaves and jabín, is the reason you're here. Chef Silvio Campos, widely considered the "mastro of the pibil," is perhaps best known for his cochinita pibil, or slow-roasted pork. It's marinated in citrus, then braised and wrapped in banana leaves before being roasted over the fire for an impossibly tender and flavorful result. Cheesecake with pumpkin seed and topped with tomato marmalade rounds out the meal.

Name: Puerto Bravo
Address: 1425 Gerrard St. E., Toronto, M4L 1Z7, Canada
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Blink and you'll miss this quaint little spot on bustling Gerrard. Drawing inspiration from Mexico, the menu is equally compact and leans heavily on seafood in the form of crisp tostadas and generously built tacos. Indeed, this little kitchen doles out bold flavors like the wera tostada, a riot of colors and textures featuring octopus, shrimp and spicy macha mayo. The tuna tostada, meanwhile, leans Asian with soy sauce and sesame oil. For tacos, consider sautéed shrimp jolted with salsa brava or charbroiled octopus tossed with onions and poblanos. Finish with something sweet, like the classic carlota made with soft biscuits, condensed milk and cream cheese.

Name: Pulpo Negro
Address: 28 Broad Street, New Alresford, SO24 9AQ, United Kingdom
Description: Standing outside this whitewashed Georgian townhouse, you’re in a Hampshire market town; step inside and you’re in the heart of Spain. Barcelona-born Andres Alemany has brought all the authentic flavours of his homeland to the UK, along with a terrific buzz that’s entirely befitting of a popular tapas bar. The classics like boquerones and tortillas are executed with great skill and offered at a sensible price, while the likes of barbecued Cornish monkfish tail show the kitchen's talents to the full. A good choice of Spanish wines serves to enhance the experience.

Name: Punta Corcho
Address: Av. Rafael E. Melgar, SM01, MZ6, Lt. 01-01, Puerto Morelos, 77580, Mexico
Description: You’ll have an excellent vantage to see the nearby shore from this second-floor perch, whose thatched roof and open-air plan allow the welcome ocean breeze to circulate. Better still, you can enjoy the view alongside a bountiful menu of memorable seafood offerings and tropically inflected cocktails. Shareable starters include puffy gorditas filled with roasted octopus, salsa verde, and melty quesillo, as well as an assortment of vibrant and inventive ceviches and aguachiles. Mains are likewise not boxed in by tradition, with typical Mexican flavors alongside the likes of Provençal butter and horseradish aïoli. With so many options to choose from, decisions can be a challenge, but the friendly staff will be only too happy to steer you in the right direction.

Name: Purple Poppadom
Address: 185a Cowbridge Road East, Upper Floor, Cardiff, CF11 9AJ, United Kingdom
Description: Enter via the glass door between the shop fronts and head up to this bright, sleek Indian restaurant where flashes of purple ensure it lives up to its name. Abstract murals, exposed brick walls and blonde wood chairs complete the look. The interesting menu showcases recognisable dishes like lamb rogan josh, but it’s worth keeping an eye out for the chef's signature tiffin sea bass too. Throughout, the subtle spicing and quality produce ensure layer after layer of wonderful flavour comes through in each bite. Warm, welcoming service is the chutney on the poppadom, so to speak.

Name: Putien (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop A, 7F, Lee Theatre Plaza, 99 Percival Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR
Description: The original restaurant was founded in Singapore in 2000 and named after a coastal city in Fujian province – the owner’s hometown. This branch comes with an easy-going atmosphere and its Fujian cuisine is respectful of tradition, with a focus on natural flavours. New items are added to the menu from time to time. Don’t miss their themed offerings that feature a particular seasonal seafood, such as razor clams or oysters.

Name: Pyeongyangjip
Description: Pyeongyangjip serves North Korean-style mandu and nokdujeon. The house-made dumplings, filled with kimchi, glass noodles, tofu, and vegetables, are encased in silky wrappers and served with a clear broth of beef brisket and shank. The nokdujeon, made from mung beans finely milled on a stone metdol, is airy and crispy, accented by crunchy bean sprouts. Prepared by the owner and family in this intimate, spotless space, the mandu-guk here is sure to warm the heart.

Name: Pythouse Kitchen Garden
Address: West Hatch, Tisbury, SP3 6PA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You'll struggle to find a lovelier all-round experience than having lunch at Pythouse Kitchen Garden. Set inside a red-brick former potting shed within a Victorian walled garden, it's a gorgeous setting with elegance and country charm to spare – and it's perfectly matched by the warm, friendly team who welcome you inside. The cooking is a joy too, with great value to be had in the generous fixed-price offering built around cooking over fire. Ingredients from the titular kitchen garden are a feature, such as the beetroot served with Dorset yoghurt.

Name: Pàng
Address: 181 Wenchang Street, Da'an District, Taipei, Taiwan Region
Description: Orange tables add a pop of colour to this simple room done out in wood tones and neutrals. An Americanophile, the owner-chef worked in a Latam fine dining restaurant before opening this casual joint to realise his culinary vision of refined Mexican fare with Taiwanese ingredients. His grilled spinach taco boasts layered textures and flavours with crispy grilled Ceylon spinach, diced sweet pepper and house-made salsa macha. He even makes his own soft corn tortillas.

Name: Pátio 44
Address: Passeio De São Lázaro, 44, Porto, 4000 508, Portugal
Description: A restaurant that proves a delightful surprise, both for its technical prowess and the quality of its produce, as well as for its understated façade. Conceived by three friends whose paths crossed behind the scenes on an earlier project, this venture has chef Simão Soares at the helm in the kitchen and focuses on traditional Portuguese cuisine, enriched with modern techniques and distinctive flavours. In a space that reflects the same philosophy — simple, welcoming and largely unadorned — diners are presented with a concise yet characterful menu, with stand-out dishes including Sweet Potato with Beetroot, Ox Liver served with potato millefeuille, and the delicate Rum and Sultana dessert. There is also an outdoor terrace, perfect for sunny days and for enjoying one of the creative cocktails on offer!

Name: Qi Cun Da Tou Hui
Address: 2F, 20 Haiwen Road, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe, Guangzhou, Chinese Mainland
Description: The collaborative effort of two local restaurant brands focuses on local flavours and myriad techniques to make Cantonese food even better. Many diners come for the soups, which are double-boiled for at least four hours – expect deep umami but little grease. The steamed fish jaw with pickled young ginger and sweet soybean paste, and deep-fried chitterlings are also popular. Most seafood dishes are not on the menu – ask the server what is available.

Name: Qiang Ye Fan Dian
Address: 636 Changbai Street, Qinhuai, Nanjing, 210000, Chinese Mainland
Description: This restaurant comes from humble beginnings as a street hawker stall. Thanks to the unrelenting support of the city's foodies for over 30 years, it has expanded into a two-storey restaurant serving Jiangsu cooking alongside Cantonese favourites. The juicy frog's legs with duck tongues in sizzling claypot are a must – their smoky aroma is intoxicating. Some find the fragrance imparted by the stinky tofu and pork intestine pot addictive!

Name: Qiantang Garden (Shuangyushu North Road)
Address: 59 Shuangyushu North Road, Haidian, Beijing, Chinese Mainland
Description: The owner opened this joint in 2006 to serve food from his hometown of Ningbo, especially seafood – his close connections with fishermen back home mean he gets daily shipments of the freshest catch. Pick something from the fish tank or try specialities such as oil-blanched river shrimps tossed in vinegar and grated ginger. For a sweet finale, go for Ningbo sticky rice balls with a runny black sesame filling that boasts lardy aromas. Book well in advance.

Name: Qiao Ai Lai Lai Xiao Long (Huangpu)
Address: 506 Tianjin Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, Chinese Mainland
Description: This simple little shop tucked away in a bustling alley has been packed with hungry diners ever since it opened its doors 20 years ago. The chefs are always busy in the kitchen making xiao long bao, the crab roe variety being the most popular. Brace yourself for an even bigger crowd in hairy crab season, when wontons, spring rolls and soups are generously loaded with crabmeat and roe. The classic soupy pork buns are another must-try.

Name: Qing Chun Perma
Description: The Zen-inspired, wood-rich room overlooks a serene Japanese rock garden. It serves an eclectic plant-based menu that draws on both Chinese traditions and global influences, featuring top-notch organic produce and combinations that spin with the seasons. In the open kitchen by the entrance, hearty soups are simmered over charcoal – try their hazelnut burdock soup. Dim sum like dark rye wontons are best enjoyed with silky hazelnut-brown rice milk.

Name: Qing Lang Xuan Shui Jiao (Hongqiao)
Address: Building 1, West District, Milan Hongli Yuan, Zhaqiao, Tianjin, Chinese Mainland
Description: Since 2012, this no-frills shop has been serving handmade halal dumplings with a range of fillings: beef, lamb, seafood and veggies. Their signature lamb and pear dumplings seduce with a crisp texture and fruity edge that underscores the gamey, fatty side of lamb. Fermented tofu adds a unique savoury depth to the classic Tianjin veggie dumplings. Also try hot dishes like deep-fried garlic-scented beltfish - crispy, juicy and umami-laden.

Name: Qing Tao
Address: 226-1 Siyanjing, Hupao Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: The owner with almost 30 years of cooking under his belt still gets hands on in the kitchen at times. Check the blackboard for no-frills, wok hei-laden dishes, most of which star local, seasonal produce. The sautéed pork kidney is crisp in texture and mildly hot in flavour. Soft and chewy, the sautéed rice cake is the staple of choice. House-made pork sausage and rice wine brewed by the owner’s father are some of the unique items available only here.

Name: Qing Wa Xiang (Tianning)
Address: 130 Xiejiatang, Xintang North Road, Tianning, Changzhou, Chinese Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: This is the flagship of a local restaurant chain famous for traditional Changzhou cuisine cooked over clay wood stoves. The three-storey historic mansion was restored to retain its early 1900s charm and the friendly staff also dresses the part. Steamed before presented in a clay pot, the must-try bamboo grove chicken is prized for its juicy, tender meat. Sensible prices and a vintage vibe make it routinely packed with diners.

Name: Qu Kou Zhou Jia Rou Bing
Address: 14 Sudi Road, Nankai, Tianjin, Chinese Mainland
Description: This brand from Hebei is famous for its paper-thin Xianghe flatbread stuffed with savoury meat filling. Their acclaimed signature pork and leek filling provides the perfect ratio of lean and fatty meat and bursts with juices and flavours. The beef and leek version stands out with robust meatiness that works magically with the sweet leeks. Feel free to order hot dishes to go with the flatbread – deep-fried river shrimps are a best-seller.

Name: Quai 17
Description: Don't hesitate to try out this establishment set up within a charming hotel in a wonderful location on the canal. Diners take their seats in a plush space lit by droplet chandeliers to enjoy modern cuisine with plenty of Mediterranean flair, in which fish from Sète's market takes pride of place. Examples of dishes include mussels escabeche and oysters from the lagoon (Étang de Thau); monkfish with peas, cured pork belly and pork jus, not to mention bourride and Sète-style rouille… All the magic of Sète on a plate.

Name: QuarantunoDodici
Description: 4112 are the naval coordinates of the location, and the choice is no coincidence: we are in the vicinity of a shipyard, just a few metres from the Tiber, looking out onto the moored vessels. Chef Lele Usai (the same hand behind the starred Il Tino on the floor above) prepares here simpler and more traditional cooking, with seafood classics such as spaghetti alle vongole lupini and grilled fish, yet always with the same exacting attention to the quality of the catch, in an informal and relaxed setting of an almost holiday atmosphere, particularly at the outdoor tables.

Name: Quarter Sheets
Address: 1305 Portia St., Los Angeles, CA, 90026, USA
Description: Aaron Lindell and Hannah Ziskin's Quarter Sheets Pizza has nailed that haute hipster vibe with its casual styling and vinyl and cassette collection. The word is out on this Echo Park spot, so expect a wait, but one bite of their inch-thick, pan-style pizzas makes it all worth your while. Baked to order, they're prepared with flavorful sauce and quality ingredients. Pepperoni is a classic choice, or opt for the pimento grove, a vodka sauced pizza topped with olives, 'nduja and cheese. And, while you might not expect to get serious pastries at a pizza shop, don't leave without trying at least one of Hannah Ziskin's pastries. There are a few offerings that rotate often but the signature Princess cake is a staple that's worth every bite.

Name: Quatre Vins
Description: Put on your rose-tinted spectacles and bask in the warm, cosy interior of Quatre Vins, steeped in the vibe of a stylish private sitting room. An open kitchen adds a joyful note, in echo of the chef’s buzzy personality. The menu features a lineup of international dishes prepared with premium big-boned ingredients. How about slices of raw scallops paired with morcilla (Italian black pudding) and a creme of Jerusalem artichoke? Or crunchy wontons filled with chopped turkey and an expertly crafted sweet-sour seasoning? Pure unadulterated pleasure, a relaxed, feel-good atmosphere and a fine range of biodynamic and natural wines.

Name: Queen of Cups
Address: 10-12 Northload Street, Glastonbury, BA6 9JJ, United Kingdom
Description: This deliciously different restaurant sits within a rustic 17C inn in the heart of Glastonbury, and comes with numerous seating areas, including a cosy courtyard for sunny days. Menus showcase West Country produce and the resulting Middle Eastern and Mediterranean small plates burst with colour and flavour. Grab a friend, go for the chef’s selection entitled the ‘Queen’s Feast’ and accompany it with the ‘sharing ciders’.

Name: Queen’s English
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Greeting diners at this tiny Columbia Heights retreat is a yellow neon sign. The interior design, however, exudes all the understated feels, by way of white floors, blue banquettes, an intricately decorated counter and sleek metal stools. Nooks framed by geometric screens ensure the utmost privacy.The menu reveals a modern take on Hong Kong plates. These high-heat wok dishes show a blend of fresh ingredients and balanced flavors. Lotus root salad with anchovy dust and a charred tomato vinaigrette; or cured hamachi spiced with cumin, brushed with seaweed oil and set atop watermelon make for a great starting point. Not far behind, Wagyu rosettes gently poached in a "mala" broth are crowned by duck egg yolk and soy foam for a flourishing finish.

Name: Quinqué
Description: Having worked in various prestigious restaurants such as Nacho Manzano’s legendary Casa Marcial, chefs Carlos Griffo and Miguel Ángel García do their utmost to combine the skills they have learnt to create “comida de casa” – traditional home cooking based around seasonal ingredients, albeit in an updated format, but one that still respects their full flavours. The interior, which is now more elegant and features an open kitchen, provides the backdrop for an à la carte (including dishes such as hake tortilla with pil-pil and chilli peppers, shoulder of rabbit escabeche, rice with pigeon, etc) and a tasting menu. You’ll also find frequent daily suggestions, featuring fish sourced direct from the auction, plus some half-plate options.

Name: Quán Nhân
Address: 83 Phan Tu Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: People flock here for its famous duck porridge. A local duck breed from Cẩm Nam Island, rice, mung beans and coix seeds are slowly simmered in duck broth for a creamy, hearty meal. Poached duck and duck salad are also available.

Name: Quê Xưa (Hòa Cường)
Address: 165-167 Nui Thanh Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Spread across two floors, you may need to share a table at this lively local spot – a testament to its authentic Vietnamese fare. Straw chandeliers and local-style paintings add charm. The menu focuses on two dishes: Mỳ Quảng, a local speciality made with soft, fragrant flat rice noodles and varied toppings; and Bánh Thịt Heo, boiled pork belly wrapped in rice paper and herbs, served with a tangy dipping sauce made from fermented anchovy and tropical fruits.

Name: R&D
Description: In a match made on primetime, Chef Alvin Leung was one of the judges who declared Eric Chong the winner of "MasterChef Canada’s" first season, before taking on the younger chef as his protégé. Smack dab in the middle of Chinatown, this hip, unconventional eatery is the product of their partnership, serving up just the sort of freewheeling fusion cuisine that made Chong a TV hit. The assortment of decidedly untraditional dim sum serves as a prime example; foie gras sou draws upon a grab bag of international flavors. Popcorn shrimp fly in the face of the bar staple, while yellow curry rigatoni with braised short rib, snow pea and curry leaves is the mashup you didn't know you needed.

Name: RAGÙ Restaurant
Address: Unit 25, Cargo 2, Museum Street, Wapping Wharf, City of Bristol, BS1 6ZA, United Kingdom
Description: Like most of the restaurants occupying the reclaimed shipping containers in Wapping Wharf, this authentic Italian eatery is cool, compact and totally irresistible. Coming from the same team as nearby COR, what it lacks in size it makes up for in flavour, with each simply prepared dish utilising the well-sourced seasonal ingredients to maximum effect. The menu’s designed for sharing and the prices are generous, so order in abundance and revel in everything from the moreish garlic and rosemary focaccia to the fish and meat cooked over fire. Finish with their creative take on tiramisu.

Name: RAMEN MATSUI
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The husband boils the noodles; the wife garnishes them with spring onion and fermented bamboo shoots. Between them, they bring alpha and omega together to complete each bowl of ramen. Flavours are based on soy sauce, salt and dried sardines. To bring out the aroma, pure rice sake is added to chicken or seafood dashi soup stock. Several types of fragrant oil are used, deepening the flavour experience. Kombu kelp, scallops and wheat flour, all from Hokkaido, infuse the husband’s love of his homeland.

Name: REI
Description: The concept is ‘neo-machichuka’, ‘machichuka’ denoting an unpretentious neighbourhood Chinese restaurant and ‘neo’ referencing an upgrade for modern tastes. A culinary tune-up, so to speak, with the accent on changing aromas and textures. Red sea-bream salad, for example, is dressed with scorched rice for a smoky fragrance. Mouth-watering chicken, prepared in black vinegar to deepen the flavour, accentuates red pepper and nutty texture. Menu items are reassuringly familiar, yet each recipe harbours a novel twist.

Name: REIF Japanese Kushiyaki - Dar Wasl
Address: Unit 70, Dar Wasl Mall, Al Wasl Road, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,No alcohol served,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the residential neighbourhood of Al Wasl, away from the city’s impressive skyscrapers, is a kushiyaki-inspired but friendly restaurant, offering far more than just grilled skewered meats and vegetables. The contemporary Japanese menu also covers a wide range of well-priced snacks, sushi and ramen, like their Tantamen ramen, raw salmon with crispy black rice and Wagyu steamed bun. Be sure to also save room for one of their creative desserts.

Name: REIF Japanese Kushiyaki - Dubai Hills
Address: Building 3, Dubai Hills Estate Business Park, Dubai Hills, Dubai
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This second branch, opened in 2023, is located in the emerging Dubai Hills district. Similar to the original in Dar Wasl but with a few subtle differences, the eatery offers a wide range of colourful Japanese favourites, from kushiyaki (as the name suggests), to fun classics with an international twist, such as their escargot teriyaki and beef gyoza. The restaurant blends contemporary, sleek design with pops of colour.

Name: ROSE
Description: For the Tress family, everything revolves around organic food, with a focus on vegetarian and vegan cuisine. The complex, carefully considered dishes win diners over with their depth of flavour and aroma – the pea and broad bean tartare, for instance, makes a lasting impression. Meat can be ordered as a side dish – here, they follow the principle of nose-to-tail eating. The portions are kept on the smaller side, so sharing is a good option if you would like to try a variety of dishes. All the wines to accompany this regional cooking are Demeter-certified. It's lovely to sit on the terrace in the shade of a chestnut tree. Tip: Should you wish to stay over, there is the guesthouse opposite.

Name: ROZZO SICILIA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: The largest island in the Mediterranean, Sicily has flourished for centuries as a hub of trade, so the cuisines of many lands have been passed down here. The unique local dishes that sprang up on this island captured the heart of ROZZO SICILIA’s chef. Authentic recipes are valued, including aubergine caponata, fennel and sardine pasta and seafood couscous. Lemon as an essential accompaniment is another traditional touch. The chef’s cherished goal is to craft flavours that remind Sicilians of home.

Name: RPM Bakehouse
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Serving bread and pastries from their bakery, produce from their farm and wine from their vineyards, this charming cafe in Jordan cuts no corners. The daytime relative of Pearl Morissette offers a casual, evolving menu that never fails to delight. To complement a vibrant salad, sourdough grilled cheese with golden beets and aged cheddar is the move to make. If still available, swing for the quiche, a custardy indulgence that has few equals. A cup of hot coffee, a buttery danish, a seat on the sunny patio — is there a better way to start the day? The line often stretches to the front door, especially on weekends when customers make the drive from other parts of Ontario.

Name: Racine
Description: Nestled in a discreet cul-de-sac, Racine creatively explores local ingredients, without excluding a few more exotic touches. This large, modern bistro serves seasonal cuisine at affordable prices. Meticulous work can be seen in the pineapple tartare with satay ice cream, black pollack confit with coconut milk, or Holstein sirloin with celeriac mousseline. This down-to-earth, friendly and contemporary place is ideal for an accessible, well-executed meal.

Name: Racines
Description: A stone's throw from Étaples marina, Pierre Chavatte's restaurant sports a contemporary decor with wood details, and the kitchen as a backdrop. Generous and precise, particularly when it comes to sauces, the cuisine is a hit. The prawns with spinach, black garlic and cashews are a pure delight; the oh-so-tender red mullet is elevated by a bouillabaisse-style broth. For dessert, the pear in spiced wine sees an interplay of textures. A sincere, warm and indulgent spot.

Name: Racines
Description: The roots of this bistro are tied to the family history of the young couple who own it: on one side of the family, a butcher's shop specialising in choice cuts of meat (especially milk-fed veal from Limousin) and on the other, chickens and orchards. The chef’s fondness for fine produce can be tasted in dishes like egg parfait, tagliatelle of celery cacio e pepe, fillet of trout, ravioles, shrimp jus and curly kale. Cheerful front-of-house team.

Name: Racines by Daniel Gallacher
Description: This self-taught chef with Scottish roots rustles up inventive and exuberant cuisine that flies in the face of convention. He changes his menu every month according to what produce is to be had at the market. His fresh and meticulous dishes, such as Atlantic monkfish with carrots, satay and passion fruit, are dependably delicious. Recently redesigned, the restaurant is always busy.

Name: Racinette
Description: She is Canadian and he’s Belgian and they have set up shop in Lectoure in a steep street near the cathedral. Half-café, half-bar, it is busy all day long for a drink, a snack or a meal. The concise menu is a savvy mix of tradition and contemporary notes: medium rare slice of roast veal with girolles and confit potatoes, fried aubergines with a Japanese twist and a creamy cheese, or figs in red wine delicately laid on a hazelnut cake and mascarpone mousse. Pastel tones and stone set the scene in the large dining room, the mezzanine area is eminently friendly and the terrace invariably bathed in sunshine. A hit with pilgrims and regulars alike.

Name: Radio
Address: Julius Thomsens Gade 12, Copenhagen, 1632 V, Denmark
Description: The name comes from its location opposite the old offices of The Danish Broadcasting Corporation, but it could easily refer to the lively buzz of the atmosphere too. Its moody décor encompasses black low-hanging lights, a black chandelier made of metal desk lamps and dark panelled walls hung with large slates decorated with chalk-drawn vegetables. Full-flavoured dishes use organic ingredients grown in the restaurant’s nearby fields and feature well thought through combinations such as salmon sashimi with crunchy kohlrabi and hot horseradish sauce or caramelised pork belly with pumpkin and spices.

Name: Raedthuys
Description: With its own bakery, patisserie and even a smokehouse, Marion Thus's bustling, inviting restaurant, formerly a café, is a place where nearly everything is made from scratch. Her enticing à la carte and set menus always include vegetarian options. There is no mistaking the generous, traditional character of her cooking. Think ribeye cooked rare, accompanied by an aromatic antiboise, a mustard jus with mustard seeds and a bitterbal (small Dutch croquette) filled with beef and mushroom stew. The chef does not hold back when it comes to delivering bold flavours. Be sure to check out the beer list and try something on tap.

Name: Rafales
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In Royan, a breath of fresh air is blowing across the restaurant scene, brought not by an up-and-coming young chef, but by a couple in their fifties from Toulouse. Laurence and Philippe left Le Tire Bouchon, their Toulouse wine bar-cum-eatery, to set up shop where she grew up. As they embark on the last decade of their working lives, the exuberant and enthusiastic pair has created a spirit reminiscent of Parisian bistros. Philippe takes care of the restaurant floor and cellar (over 200 natural and biodynamic wines); Laurence crafts fresh, generous dishes that smack of home cooking: puff pastry tart with spring vegetables; sautéed pork cheeks in Welsh onions and soy with mashed sweet potato; strawberry shortbread and mascarpone.

Name: Raieü
Address: Via Milite Ignoto 23, Cavi di Lavagna, 16033, Italy
Description: After over 60 years in business, this trattoria, which started out in a warehouse that was once used to store fishing nets, is still a reliable choice in terms of quality and price. Located in the centre of the little village, simple and old-fashioned, with outdoor seating overlooking the characteristic narrow street, it still serves the same deliciously tasty and generous Ligurian seafood cuisine it did when it first opened. The fish soup is a great classic, but is rivalled by some delicious versions of fish tartare.

Name: Rajarani Thosai
Address: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre, #01-33, 137 Tampines Street 11, 521137, Singapore
Description: This stall serves thosai and appam made from scratch. Their thosai comes in nearly 20 different fillings such as crispy cereal, or cheese, egg and butter – everything tastes better with the sambar and chutney dips.

Name: Ramen & Tsukemen TAO
Address: 10488 Valley View St., Buena Park, CA, 90620, USA
Description: Ramen & Tsukemen TAO is tucked away in an easy-to-miss corner of an open-air mall, but the humble setting quickly fades once the steaming bowls arrive. The compact dining room is strictly no frills, though the focus here is squarely on deeply comforting ramen crafted with passion and dedication. A concise menu keeps attention on the essentials, from rich and creamy spicy red miso ramen to a lighter but equally satisfying chicken ramen built on a classic, Tokyo-style broth. Custom noodles from Kobayashi Noodle Factory are tailored to each preparation, ranging from firm Sapporo-style noodles designed for the hearty miso broths to thicker, more robust tsukemen noodles made for dipping. Pork buns and a handful of small plates round out a meal that easily inspires repeat visits.

Name: Ramen Break Beats
Description: The chef was a DJ in a former life, and the technique he applied in that calling, break beats, informs both the name of the restaurant and the music piped through the dining room. The signature dish is soy-sauce ramen, which owes its beautiful presentation and clear soup to careful preparation of the noodles. The purity of the broth delights the palate from the first mouthful. With rhythmic tempo, you’ll reel in the noodles and drink every drop of soup before you know it. A beat-driven bowl that hit big in Meguro.

Name: Ramen Gaijin
Description: With more than a decade of history behind it, this Japanese favorite is a must-visit in Sonoma County. Fusing local ingredients with traditional technique, the kitchen delivers a range of top bites, starting with superb chicken karaage with miso ranch as well as crispy tofu with Calabrian chili and toasted sesame oil. Featuring house-made noodles, ramen is the main event. The light shoyu ramen is as impressive as the richer, spicy tantanmen, highlighting pork belly chashu, Sapporo noodles and woodear mushrooms. The best seats at this expansive restaurant are at the counter, where you can watch the chefs in action.

Name: Ramen Hayato
Description: This long-serving ramen shop is loved by Japanese people for its “Three Great Ramens”: soy-sauce, salt and miso. First-time visitors are recommended to order the soy-sauce ramen, but once you learn that the Hokkaido-born chef studied in Sapporo, you might be tempted to go for the miso ramen. The soy-sauce ramen is served in a double soup of meat-based stock and seafood-based stock. “Ura-Shoyu”, the ‘hidden soy-sauce ramen’ not listed on the menu, uses meat-based stock only. If you’re having trouble deciding, start with the ‘official’ menu.

Name: Ramen Kitanoya
Description: This cosy ramen restaurant is tucked away on a narrow side street in the heart of The Hague. Take a seat at the dining counter by the open kitchen to soak up an authentic Tokyo vibe. At lunchtime, the air is thick with the aroma of the simmering broths. The menu offers a wide range of options, including house-made gyoza with a succulent minced meat filling, or fantastic chewy ramen in an intense chicken broth bringing together layers of umami, spice and subtle sweetness. This is made-to-order cuisine that honours the richness of authentic Japanese culinary tradition. Reservations are not accepted, so be sure to arrive early!

Name: Ramen Kuon
Address: B2F, Semba Centar Bldg Sangokan, 1-4-3 Sembachuo, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0055, Japan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: The chef takes pride in his “Shio Soba” (salt noodles), his quest for a bowl of perfection. Taste the seaweed—sea lettuce and nori—and you can feel the rustle of sea breezes. Triple soup of fish, shellfish and chicken is prepared using Pi-Water, a water that is said to be extremely similar to water in living tissue. High hydration ramen noodles, prepared with a blend of three types of wheat flour, produces a texture similar to noodles kneaded by hand. Three types of chashu are served as well, combining pork and chicken. Bringing out the best in soup, noodles and chashu for a triple treat.

Name: Ramen Touhichi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: Ramen that’s all about the goodness of chicken, imparting its flavour in purest form. Ramen Touhichi’s signature soy-sauce ramen uses dashi made only with locally raised free-range chicken and water, mixing it with raw soy sauce kaeshi. Other offerings include richly flavoursome chicken boiled in plain water, cold noodles soaked in kombu dashi soup served with dipping sauce of chicken soy sauce, and chicken-oil noodles served without soup. ‘Touhichi’ is named after the house where the chef was born. See him at the counter full of pride in his native Kyoto.

Name: Ramenya Fujitora
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
Description: ‘Fujitora’ is a blend of the chef’s name and that of the shop where he apprenticed, created to bring luck. It was his mentor’s ramen that inspired him to embark on his current path. The techniques he cultivated and his inquisitive mind shine in his chicken-and-pork soup. The chef prepares this soup in a large stockpot in the kitchen, patiently teasing every drop of umami from the ingredients. Sauce for soy-sauce ramen is created from a medley of soy sauces to harmonise with the soup.

Name: Ramenya Toy Box
Description: The chef’s starting point is the ramen his grandmother cooked for him when he was a child. He added ‘Toy Box’ to the name because he wanted to create ramen that holds the same excitement for his guests as a box of toys does for a child. Soy sauce ramen, the shop’s flagship offering, is constantly tinkered with to improve it. In search of a depth of gustatory experience, over 10 types of soy sauce are combined in the broth. Yet the ramen is a dish of simple happiness; noodles from the good old days.

Name: Rang
Address: 384 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Rang is the Hindi word for colour and splashes of colour adorn the room, including colourful curries in white, yellow, green and red. The owner-chefs are two brothers, born in India and raised in Australia. They received formal training in Western culinary arts and champion a nouvelle cuisine with international influences. Start with chicken tikka, tailed by dal tadka yellow curry with roti or naan. Rice lovers should try their biryani.

Name: Rao Shi Fu Da Xian Shui Jiao
Address: No. 105, Building 4, Shuangfeng Lane, Shuangfeng Road, Nankai, Tianjin, Chinese Mainland
Description: This spot offers an authentic local experience and the no-frills interior buzzes with a down-to-earth vibe. Dumplings are cooked to order and the mantis shrimp version explodes with seafood umami. The veggie trio filling is generously stuffed and bursting with juices. Other best-sellers include Spanish mackerel, pork and veggies, and ark shell clam – a delicacy rarely found elsewhere. Stir-fries and cold appetisers are also recommended.

Name: Rasa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: Weekly visits to this gastropub might not be enough. Truly, few restaurants feel this relaxed and cook with so much gusto. Are you curious about those chickpea fritters with lemon mascarpone and wasabi or the truffle gnudi with pesto? You should be. Sea bream ceviche with chili oil is as bold as lamb vindaloo dumplings. In the end, no one cuisine can claim this endlessly tempting menu that delivers hearty, unfussy flavors in abundance. And yes, the burger is as good as it looks, the tender patty made with beef cheek, grilled, and served on house made brioche smeared in gochujang mayo. In total, the portions are generous so bring friends; the flavors are big so bring an appetite; and the satisfaction is high so count on a return visit.

Name: Rasa Rasa
Address: 59 Gat Lebuh Chulia, George Town, 10300, Malaysia
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: A decor of raw brick walls and industrial accents is softened by potted plants. Alongside the concise à la carte menu, the Nyonya combo set, built around pandan nasi lemak with your choice of toppings, is a crowd-pleaser. For a small bite, the tender, juicy meat of the five-spice chicken roll is wrapped in tofu skin and imparts layered aromas. Those with a sweet tooth should try the tub tim krob. Open until afternoon only, so plan accordingly.

Name: Rasarumah
Address: 3107 Beverly Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90026, USA
Description: Expect to be greeted with an array of sambals as well as Malaysian classics on Chef Johnny Lee's Chinese-Malaysian menu. Don't let the slightly higher price point steer you away, as these large plates are designed for sharing. Pork jowl or chicken satay skewers start things off right, as do ulam bendi with charred okra, and steamed eggplant with sambal and dried shrimp. There are plenty of main dishes to choose from, but beef rendang in a rich and creamy curry accompanied by a buttery roti is a sure thing. To finish, look no further than the cendol sundae with coconut and pandan ice cream with pandan jelly noodles, red bean, gula melaka syrup, and toasted buckwheat.

Name: Rasik Local Kitchen
Address: 44/3 Sridonchai Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: This thoughtful take on Thai cuisine unfolds in a casual, wood-accented space. The chef adds a personal touch to seasonal Thai ingredients in three menus: "Special", "Seasonal" and "Classic". We recommend asking about the catch of the day. Start with crispy rice crackers and Thai tomato salsa and pair your meal with Thai draft beer or aromatic alcohol-free drinks. Booking is required, as there are just 14-16 seats per service for each of the three daily rounds.

Name: Rathauskeller Bistro
Description: Dating back to 1497, this historical townhouse in Zug's old town is a lovely location. The friendly service and relaxed atmosphere here are appreciated by locals and tourists alike. Diners can choose from the selection of classics such as cordon bleu, Lammhacktätschli (lamb patties) and beef roulades, and there is also a seasonal menu. The tables on the gorgeous terrace in front of the building in the cobbled pedestrian area are coveted. Tip: Just a stone's throw away, the lakeside is perfect for a stroll.

Name: Rauch & Rebe
Description: The vibe here is pleasantly down to earth – and that goes for both the modern decor and the food at this place, which is run by a dedicated pair, chef Christian Bernhard and sommelier Michael Stafford, who also provides attentive service. In the evening, take your pick from an array of delicious à la carte dishes, such as "chestnut and Jerusalem artichoke foam soup, winter truffles, brioche croutons, chervil" or "miso cod, wok vegetables, pak choi, Everest basmati". At lunchtime, there is an affordable two-course set menu, plus a selection from the evening menu. In summer, there are also sheltered outdoor tables. The restaurant is located just behind the Augarten Art Hotel, just outside the Old Town.

Name: Ravi's Famous Apom Manis
Description: Since 1920, this stall has been selling its famous apom: their crispy crêpes with a soft, puffy centre cooked in claypot over charcoal are fluffier and more coconutty than most. Come early – they tend to sell out by 9:30am.

Name: Raíz
Address: Schiller 331, entre Horacio y Presidente Mazaryk, Polanco, Miguel Hildalgo, 11570, Mexico
Description: Located on the ground floor of a residential building, this restaurant could easily go unnoticed, but one bite of their contemporary Mexican cooking and you won't soon forget its address. A welcoming staff invites you to take a seat and peruse their menu or opt for one of two tastings. A plantain molote with a bit of pickled onion is a nice opener before savoring the flavors of an aguachile in a cuttlefish ink broth. Tostada de camarón is a spot-on treat, then pescado zarandeado delights with its crispy skin. To finish, arroz con leche is comforting and classic.

Name: Re Hai Fan Zhuang
Address: 141 Guangrong Dao, Hongqiao, Tianjin, Chinese Mainland
Description: The room may not be the epitome of trendy, but a pop of lime green adds a vibrant, playful edge. The veteran chef offers Tianjin classics, ranging from wholesome family favourites to meticulous recipes that require pre-ordering. Sautéed shrimps are delicate and lightly seasoned to highlight their natural sweetness. Braised winter melon in chicken oil unveils exquisite knifework, which is further enhanced by the deep, rich notes of the crystal-clear chicken stock glaze.

Name: Rebel
Description: It’s not just the streets that bustle with life at this city centre location – behind a glass façade, this contemporary bistro is equally animated thanks to its open kitchen and the buzz of contented diners. The décor might come down on the slightly shabbier side of shabby-chic – and the tables are compact in their arrangement – but that’s all part of Rebel’s charm and the locals love to come here all the same. Go for the tasting menu or choose from the list of small plates, which include the likes of chicken confit with portobello, onion, ramson oil, sauce blanquette and black truffle.

Name: Redheaded Stranger
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: There is typically a line out the door at this Cleveland Park spot. Named for a Willie Nelson song and album, the vibe is laidback and slightly quirky (think diner style with chili pepper lights strung above). It's a small spot but great care is taken with everything from house-made hot sauces to tortillas. Watch the chef making those terrific flour tortillas in the main dining room or sit outside on the patio to savor Chef Bryan Lee Weaver's Tex-Mex menu. Tacos run the gamut from simple (bacon, egg and cheese) to creative (poblano with whipped feta and crispy rice). Main dishes include a burrito and a green chili cheeseburger, and the menu includes a section devoted to crunch wraps (the pork green chili version is a glorious, messy delight).

Name: Regadera
Description: Situated along the pleasant avenue skirting a bend in the Guadalquivir river between the Roman and Miraflores bridges, this restaurant boasts a youthful ambience and a rustic-contemporary decor that definitely made an impression on us (the bed of aromatic flowers in the middle of the dining room is a particularly attractive feature). The cuisine here is equally modern and very much market influenced, and includes dishes ranging from the traditional (mazamorra, salmorejo, oxtail etc) to more globally and fusion-inspired options (such as wild sea bass ceviche with apple, cucumber foam and marinated carrot gazpacho). Fine textures, distinctive flavours and impeccable presentation are all to the fore here.

Name: Regional Friesoythe
Description: "Regional" is more than just a name; it's a guiding philosophy in this tradition-steeped town-centre restaurant, run by Timo Plenter and Ina Stuke since September 2022. The chef-patron draws on locally sourced seasonal ingredients, and partners with regional suppliers to craft his flavourful dishes. There is a four- to six-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. A cheese course can be added on. The interior decor marries modern and rustic elements. Warm and attentive service. In summer, a few tables are set up in front of the restaurant for al fresco dining.

Name: Reliquia
Address: Angel Justiniano Carranza 1601, Buenos Aires, C1414COQ, Argentina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: There’s a palpable sense of authenticity in this friendly restaurant, where the young owners have created a warm and welcoming ambience perfect for a romantic supper. The service is attentive without being excessively formal, while the soft colour scheme contributes to Reliquia’s warmth and intimacy. The menu is equally attractive with options for every taste – the chef has a perfect command of flavours and textures and uses techniques such as escabeche to raise the level of his dishes further, many of which showcase vegetables in a more rustic, home-style manner. We suggest starting with the delicious brioche-style bread with smoked butter, followed by the beetroot, “alcauciles” (artichokes) and the Brussels sprouts (“repollitos”). The agnolotti is a very popular main course with guests, although meat-lovers will also be keen to order the lacquered pork steak (“churrasquito de cerdo laqueado”). Everything possible is done here to avoid waste.

Name: Remi
Description: This urban-cool restaurant in the building of publishing house Suhrkamp-Verlag has a sleek design with its floor-to-ceiling windows, and the open kitchen in the middle is the defining feature of the space. The seasonal dishes prepared in view of diners are pleasingly intelligible and without unnecessary flourishes. The affordable lunch deal is also very popular. Their true feel-good dishes range from "fennel risotto, radicchio" to "mackerel, corn, tomatillo". In summer, the lovely terrace is a real draw. The restaurant has many regulars, so it's best to book.

Name: Ren Ren Shui Jiao
Address: 24 Ruisheng South Street, Wuhou, Chengdu, Chinese Mainland
Description: The owner-chef honed his skills in a famous local dumpling shop for eons before starting his own business. A stickler for tradition, he aims to deliver authentic Chengdu flavours. His signature dumplings tossed in red oil sauce are rich in garlic and house-made chilli sauce, striking a balance between savoury and sweet flavours. Dumpling soup with laver and peppercorns on the vine and spun mung bean cold noodles are other best sellers.

Name: Renée
Description: Dunkirk-born Charles Bruneval completed stints at some top establishments before opening this restaurant, the name of which pays tribute to his grandmother. In an unpretentious setting, he cooks up traditional, hearty and meticulous fare: skate wings à la grenobloise, pâté en croûte, shrimp croquettes. Precise cooking and rich sauces – every bite reveals the touch of a seasoned chef.

Name: Resident Taqueria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
Description: Chef/owner Andrew Savoie brings experience from acclaimed kitchens, channeling those influences into a menu that blends Mexican traditions with touches of Texas barbecue and global flavors. House-made flour tortillas serve as the foundation for a range of creative tacos, including pork belly burnt ends with salsa macha, Texas short rib with Morita barbecue sauce, and picadillo accented with raisins, green olives and pepperoncini. Breakfast tacos, quesadillas and a variety of sides make this a popular destination throughout the day. Thoughtful combinations, bold flavors and generous portions reflect the kitchen’s creativity, while the relaxed atmosphere and welcoming service reinforce the restaurant’s neighborhood appeal.

Name: Residents Cafe & Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A large greenery-donning patio out front greets diners to this "cafe," set within a black-painted row house. The space, spread over two levels, is thoroughly charming, thanks to a bar lined with mid-century modern stools, exposed brick and plush seats. Edison bulbs and white hexagon floor tiles simply enhance the vintage vibe. The menu underscores an array of contemporary plates with Middle Eastern and European elements. Imagine Turkish eggs at brunch; sweet potato croquettes with pickled fresno chile and maple aioli; and chicken schnitzel with a salad of romaine hearts, charred corn and tomatoes in a herb dressing at night. Their spin on Basque cheesecake features ras el hanout and passion fruit coulis.

Name: Restaurant Blauw Utrecht
Description: Tradition, street food influences, authenticity and integrity are among the words that best sum up this popular restaurant, which showcases the full array of Indonesian cuisine. The rijsttafel (a medley of dishes with rice – also available in a vegan version) provides an excellent insight into the chef's talent for seasoning and balancing intense flavours. With such an extensive à la carte menu, the diner really is the king. From the succulence of the lamb, the distinctly nutty flavour of the peanut sauce and the delicate spiciness of the gado gado, you can see that this is a chef who knows how to combine generosity with subtlety. Be sure to try the roasted goat meat as well!

Name: Restaurant Coquo
Description: Corentin Lonnoy, affectionately known as "Coco," has realised his childhood ambition by transforming his family abode into a delightful restaurant adorned with nostalgic photographs of Bierwart. Having honed his skills alongside Pierre Résimont, his genuine enthusiasm for high-quality ingredients shines through in his culinary creations. One standout dish features Anjou pigeon fillet complemented by intriguing accompaniments such as potato millefeuille, confit beetroot, blackberries, and a robust jus. The tempting set menu offers the perfect opportunity to savour this approachable yet refined cuisine.

Name: Restaurant Corona im Hotel zur Post
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sergio Corona's cooking is pure fun! His straightforward yet meticulous approach is always based on classical foundations and uses top-quality, exceptionally fresh ingredients. Dishes of note include saffron risotto with prawns and octopus, marinated salmon trout with rocket, and braised beef cheek, broad beans and Parmesan rösti. The two four-course menus, "Méditerranée" and "Corona", are priced very reasonably indeed. In the classically styled restaurant, hostess Kerstin Corona heads up a friendly, attentive and adept front-of-house team.

Name: Restaurant Dimofski
Address: 2 quartier de la Gare, Wœlfling-lès-Sarreguemines, 57200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant housed in an imposing 1950’s edifice a dozen or so kilometres outside Sarreguemines is just the ticket for a slap-up meal with all the trimmings. Wholehearted and single-minded, Julien Dimofski’s enthusiasm can be tasted in delectable, carefully crafted dishes overflowing in ambition (snails in potato nests, langoustine gently seared in butter or free-range roasted squab in a simple parsley sauce). The infectiously cosy, voluntarily rustic interior is further enhanced by the warm welcome and service proffered by Véronique, Julien’s mum.

Name: Restaurant ET
Description: The setting ticks all the boxes: an elegant 19th-century house with a peaceful terrace located in a charming cobbled courtyard, and a location close to Aarhus Harbour yet also within easy rich of the city’s main streets. Regional ingredients are to the fore in generously proportioned, good value dishes that lead with a Gallic edge. Alongside the likes of grilled entrecôte and crème bûlée you’ll find their own reinterpreted version of Danish stjerneskud – a hot and cold open breaded fish, salmon and shrimp sandwich. Wines from their exclusively French cellar include around 70 options by the glass.

Name: Restaurant Frank
Description: After eight joyful years spent at its former premises, Frank moved just a hop, skip and a jump away to this spacious spot inside a beautiful historic building. Sporting a minimalist style, the room keeps its focus on the open kitchen, where Chef Ander Strier cooks up well-balanced modern dishes with a subtly creative edge. The attractively presented, good value plates could include octopus with grilled pineapple, sobrassada, potato and aioli or cannelloni stuffed with confit rabbit, pine nuts and ceps. To accompany, choose something from the particularly extensive wine list.

Name: Restaurant Litoral (Taipa)
Address: No. 53-57, Block 4, Wai Chin Kok, Rua do Regedor, Taipa, Macau, Macau SAR
Description: The simple space has a vaulted ceiling with exposed wooden trusses, roughcast walls and irregular flagstone floor for a casual vibe. Portuguese and Macanese classics are served in portion sizes meant for sharing. Carne Alentejana marries the umami of fresh clams and pork cubes with bold seasoning; the African chicken is coated in shredded coconut and caramelised onion then browned under a broiler. Finish with the light and fluffy serradura.

Name: Restaurant Schlüssel - Schlüsselstube
Description: A feel-good spot through and through, this bistro run by the Kalberer family owes much of its appeal to the unmistakable warmth of its hospitality. The elegant historical setting and attentive service provided by staff in traditional dirndl attire add to the charm. And then there's the wonderful food, which is both sophisticated and fairly priced. Classics such as braised veal cheeks and Hacktätschli (meat patties) are delicious. Highly recommended: the seasonal set menu featuring three to four courses. Impressive wine selection. Tip: The cosy garden restaurant opens in summer.

Name: Restaurant VIE
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Only service animals permitted
Description: Close to the imposing UN campus, you’ll find a new red-brick development and, within it, this contemporary bistro with concrete walls, exposed ducting and an industrial feel. The cooking has a direct, no-frills approach, with generously proportioned dishes paying great attention to seasoning and cooking times. You might find onion bread with Iberico ham; kalix roe with sour cream, herbs and potato bread; or an indulgent take on a kro dessert – almond cake with salted caramel and vanilla ice cream. Glass-fronted coolers line the room, giving a clue as to the range offered on the top-notch wine list.

Name: Restaurant du Dauphin
Description: In the old town, at the foot of the Porte St Julien, this restaurant in a pretty 16C building serves cuisine for the modern palate. The chefs incorporate a smattering of exotic touches, but always have a handful of classics up their sleeve. The chicken supreme with quince, accompanied by mashed potatoes with walnuts and an amaretto-infused carcass jus is a good example. As for dessert, it is a pleasure to find a vacherin, a rum baba or a moelleux – always a failsafe option! Fine selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Restaurant du Pont
Description: Overlooking the little Canal de Goulaine, this white building with a contemporary interior boasts a lovely garden terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Having cut his teeth abroad, chef Mathieu Corbineau bridges the gap between traditional recipes and modern influences: braised pork shoulder, thyme jus and vegetable tarte Tatin; fillet of pollock, shellfish marinière and a medley of Nantes carrots. Affordable lunch set menu and a wine list that zooms in on Muscadet.

Name: Restaurant élevé
Description: The 11th floor of WTC Hotel is home to a rooftop bar and restaurant with a cosmopolitan feel. Lounge seating, soft atmospheric lighting and windows all around the dining space affording views of the city make for a stunning setting. Chef Mike Kalkman presents modern cuisine that blends Dutch accents with international influences. Think hand-cut Frisian Black Angus beef tartare with a celeriac and mature cheese sorbet, or flawlessly cooked cod with pumpkin risotto, a vibrant Champagne mousseline and a sweet-and-sour pumpkin soup. Élevé is refined yet approachable, all in a decor that never ceases to impress.

Name: Restaurant ñ
Description: The yellow façade already hints at a Mediterranean vibe. Inside, the atmosphere is lively and informal, with closely set tables – a perfect space in which to share delicious food. Start, for example, with Spanish tapas such as boquerones, Ibérico ham or pimientos de Padrón, before moving on to Mediterranean dishes that pair fish and meat in unexpected ways – for example, tender pork belly topped with a thin slice of raw sea bass and leek oil. The tasting journey highlights freshness, simplicity and nuanced fermentation.

Name: Restaurante Casareyna
Address: Hotel Boutique Casareyna Puebla, Privada 2 Ote. 1007, Centro, Heróica Puebla de Zaragoza, 72000, Mexico
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: For almost two decades, this restaurant has stood as a standard-bearer for classic Pueblan cooking. Open at all hours, the spacious dining room features high ceilings, modern art and a host of attentive servers ready to swoop in. The menu is large, but locals know which specialties to focus on. When in season, chiles en nogada is a must. Another essential is the sizeable sample platter featuring mole poblano, verde, rojo and blanco – each one finely layered and bursting with personality. Everything has to be shared, including several endlessly tempting and fiery salsas. The restaurant is connected to a boutique hotel as well.

Name: Restavracija Jožef
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: Located just outside the UNESCO-listed old town, the restaurant offers a classic, welcoming setting, with a bright and inviting first-floor dining room. The menu, which includes starters, soups, main courses and desserts, is varied and sure to satisfy both meat and fish lovers. The three-course lunch menu, inspired by traditional recipes from the Idrija area, is not to be missed. If you happen to stop by on a cool autumn day, warm yourself up with a delicious and flavoursome traditional soup called smukavc.

Name: Restavracija Majerca
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Majerca is the intimate restaurant of an elegant boutique hotel nestled in the valleys of the Julian Alps, a short distance from the bucolic Lake Bohinj. The chef-patron, a native of the area, combines international techniques with a contemporary vision, expressing them with balance and sensitivity. Ingredients from the surrounding valleys take centre stage: the trout, offered in several preparations; the daily soups, typically rich in flavour; and the meats, among which the duck breast stands out as one of the most appreciated dishes. The wine list shows a clear preference for Slovenian labels, which account for approximately 90% of the selection.

Name: Resumé by 6&24
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: A glass of crisp rosé with fine charcuterie in the wine bar or on the canal-side terrace, a few small plates or a complete meal in the restaurant, with its floral, slightly tropical-looking decor – you have plenty of options here. This inviting establishment is open throughout the day, making it the perfect place for a leisurely lunch, drinks or dinner. The cooking is just as spirited, rooted in French traditions while embracing both Dutch specialities and influences from around the globe. Whether serving succulently pan-fried pike-perch with sauerkraut and buttermilk foam or pairing scallops with a beurre blanc given extra depth and vibrancy by kimchi, the chefs cook with confidence and curiosity. In short: delicious, inspired and generous!

Name: Reua Thai
Description: Reua Thai has a rather rough-hewn feel, with wooden ornaments adding to the unique character of the space. Pattama Simons is an aficionado of authentic Thai cuisine but adds a touch of finesse. She often works with produce from her own garden or local suppliers and takes the time to create depth in her cooking. For example, she infuses beef stock with cinnamon, lemongrass, peanut and coriander to achieve a vibrant and subtly spicy flavour profile. This broth serves as a rich foundation to elevate chopped beef, rice noodles and daikon. With a choice of options for each course, the set menu is recommended to fully appreciate this aromatic cuisine.

Name: Revelry
Address: Building 1, Dubai Hills Estate Business Park, Dubai Hills, Dubai
Description: Little sister to avatāra, which is directly next door, this Indian 'tapas bar' is more casual and informal in style, with a particularly good range of cocktails inspired by India’s vastly differing seasons. Inside the L-shaped room, the atmosphere is very relaxed with three TV screens showing sports games, including, unsurprisingly, cricket! The appealingly priced menu comprises a good range of well-crafted, balanced, and gently spiced contemporary Indian dishes, which combine tradition and modernity. Three ‘tapas’ and a main course should do the trick and will arrive when ready. Do leave room for the creative desserts, such as Bailey’s tiramisu with Kahlua rasmalai.

Name: Rex Shan Shui Chang Fen
Address: 1F, Building 31, Shatoujiao Baoshuiqu, Haijing 2nd Road, Yantian, Shenzhen, Chinese Mainland
Description: This long-standing neighbourhood store is famous for its rice roll, or chang fen. Made with spring water, the soft and translucent skin encases your choice of filling from a range of over 30 – including ground pork, shrimp, egg, beef, abalone and mushrooms. All are priced reasonably and come in generous portions. The mildly sweet soy sauce perfumed by garlic oil and chilli sauce complement all varieties. Try the eel balls, fish balls and marinated chicken.

Name: Richmond
Address: 43 Richmond Street South, Dublin City, D02 X499, Ireland
Description: Despite its discreet exterior, you'll be able to spot this charmingly run neighbourhood gem thanks to the warm glow of its red neon sign. Inside, the restaurant has an intimate, relaxing feel, with the exposed brick walls and red leather banquettes bathed in soft light, while smooth jazz plays in the background.
